heading: Introduction
content: In our daily life, mobile devices became a very important part of  our daily lives. Mobile devices are used to perform daily tasks. Mobile devices use advanced cloud services to complete the tasks at maximum level due to limited storage constraint on mobile devices. IOS allows users to put in application solely offered within the iTunes AppStore whereas Android-based mobile devices allow putting in  applications from several sources, consisting of Google Play Store, torrents, or direct downloads etc. [1]. Android system is more prone to malicious activities. It provi des developers more access to its working compared to IOS. Due to more access, as there are more customized and variety of apps in Android, it also has variety of threats. Hackers develop new ways of breaching device’s security every day. Android users can allow their device to install applications from third party developers. Applications on Google Play cannot be deemed safe. It needs some amount of scanning to check its intent. Mobile devices are permitted to spare documents, photographs etc. in the cloud . Mobile devices are the ideal method to associate with each other. Many mobile devices have important limitations presented to them due to the value and worth of smaller sizes; bring down weights, and different highlights. Cloud computing enables devices to avoid these limitations by enable the more resource complete tasks to be performed on systems without these requirements and having the outcomes sent to the device [2]. Applications can need a number of different hardware and software to run them. It can be quite difficult and complicated. With the use cloud, it is easier to run and manage things on your device. It can provide users with processing po wer and can fulfil their storage needs. It can be cost efficient. Users don’t need to own the infrastructure to use it. They can just pay when they need to use it and there is also less need to manage it. You don’t need to buy it or keep it up to date.

More and more companies are moving their software to clouds rather than the tradi tional way. It makes sense storage wise and other resources wise to keep the software in cloud. In malware detection, it is suitable to run an application on a remote device rather than your own, to check for malware. It keeps your device secure. Stolen devices, disabling security features and malware come under mobile security incidents. Malware has become a concern for users. It has grown up to 19% from 2012. Since there is a strong connection of human beings to mobile devices , which can be personal in na ture. Mobile devices are faster than laptops. Concerned departments are not able to put same security features on smart devices as they are on many other devices. Cyberattacks on smartphones have become too common in our daily life. In addition, over the last year, we have seen cybercriminals deploy all sorts of strategies  to overcome system’s security . Privacy has become a big question mark, as so many of these mobile applicati ons contain big amount of data and store them on the cloud. This has been experienced by many prominent people in the media who were storing their personal data on iCloud.  Data was then leaked online and threatened people’s personal information. Apps request too many permissions, which gives them access to various information from user’s device. Sometimes there are legitimate look alike applications. They tend to act like genuine apps which makes them even more dangerous. Data loss and theft is most commonly caused by malware attacks. Emails, suspicious links, websites and downloads from incredible sources can infect user’s device with malware. Most users do not pay attention to small details which can alert them to suspicious material. Sometimes they are c leverly hidden and cannot be detected before running them.

heading: 1.1 Malware types found in Mobile Devices
content: Malware is short for malicious software. It’s harmful for the mobile device in   many ways like, for instance breach of data, unauthorised access or danger to the host of mobile device. We will discuss a few of them here.

heading: Rootkit
content: It is a type of malware which is designed to remotely access or control a device without being detected by involved parties. Once it is installed, the device is under the full control of an attacker. Attacker can further manipulate and use any information or data from the device.

heading: Ransomware
content: It is a form of malware which can stop you from accessing data on your device by some form of encryption. The attacker can then demand ransom in any form and until its paid you cannot access your device. It can be installed by clicking on a fake locked screen on a mobile device, or by using a pretend anti-virus software.

heading: Trojan Horse
content: This kind of malware normally disguises itself and appear as a legitimate application or software, and on downloading the application, they will infect the mobile device. Once its installed, the attacker can modify, delete and steal information and can monitor your activities.

heading: Virus
content: It is capable of copying itself quietly and spreading to other mobile devices. They can spread through files, documents and websites. They are used to steal information, damage host computers and networks, create botnets, and more. They depend on human activity to spread.

heading: Worms
content: They are among the most common types of malware. They spread over mobile devices by abusing operating system weaknesses. They are very similar to virus but can be separated from them from the fact that they can self-replicate and spread independently.

heading: Adware
content: Adware (short for advertising -supported software) is a type of malware . It automatically shows advertisement which, include pop -up ads on web and advertisements shown by software. Most
applications have two versions. One is “free” version that comes with a number of ads which are sponsored by companies, to generate revenues. The second version costs money.

heading: Static Detection Techniques
content: Static techniques are based on classification of an application through the inspection of source code without having the application being executed. Static  detection techniques are classified as: Signature-based and Permission-based.

heading: 2.1 SIGNATURE-BASED ANALYSIS
content: Signature based malware detection methods are used commercially for anti -malware software. It gets the semantic patterns from the source code and recognize a unique signature for each malware [3]. For a program to be classified as a malware, its signature is matched to any previous existing signature of malware. It is a very fast and accurate method for detecting the malware. It can only recognize the existing malwares and fails against the unseen variations of malware. The malware database needs to be immediately updated as detected. The major downside is that it cannot detect the malware that is not in the database yet. in that case malware will remain undetected, using this method. Technology is evolving f ast and new ways of infecting devices with malware are devised every day. Signature matching is a good and accurate method of detecting malware, but malware can be hidden or encrypted in the code in  different forms. New malwares are not detected by it. It alone cannot new attacks.
Figure 2.1 Signature -based Analysis

heading: 2.2 PERMISSION-BASED ANALYSIS
content: According to [4], permissions requested by any app plays a vital role in its access to its ri ghts. When an app is installed, it does not get any access to data storage by default. It can do no harm the device’s security by itself.  APK files have an AndroidManifest.xml file, which contains permissions requested by the app. Any application can ask f or any permission. It does not mean

that it is essen tial for the app to work. They are over -privileged applications. The problem with this method is that it only focuses on the Manifest files and does not consider other. And also, apps can be over-privileged, does not necessarily mean it has harmful intent. Advantages of Static Analysis: ▪ Cheap and Fast. ▪ Not very resource consuming Disadvantages of Static Analysis: ▪ Malware patterns or signatures in patterns should be known for it to detect them. ▪ Code can be coded differently just to make it harder to match patterns with any previous detected malware. ▪ Malware can be easily obfuscated in the code somewhere with encryption.

heading: Dynamic Analysis Techniques
content: Dynamic analysis is performed after the exe cution of a program and evaluating the data [5]. The main thing is to find problems in a program while it is executing, rather than by inspecting the code offline. Its main objective is to evaluate malware after executing an application, to monitor its behavior. Dynamic analysis consumes more device resources than static analysis.  Dynamic detection techniques are classified as: anomaly based, taint related and emulation based.

heading: 3.1 ANOMALY-BASED ANALYSIS
content: Anomaly-based analysis utilizes machine learning algorithms to detect any suspicious behavior. It extracts different features from already  known malwares and then uses these features to train a model, which can then classify unknown malware. Analysis in su ch cases can require a lot of resources. For deep analysis for detection of malware, app should be installed on the device. The limitation to this approach is that it may even classify a benign application as harmful if it detects the application is making unusual number of system calls.

heading: 3.2 TAINT ANALYSIS
content: It is quite a popular technique. It checks which values are modifiable by un authorized user. User input can be harmful in such cases if they are not monitored carefully.  TaintDroid follows this approach. It uses a technique called "dynamic taint analysis". It labels information which can be useful with an identifier. The tag allows us to track the influence of the tainted object along the execution of the program. System tracks the movement of this iden tifier. TaintDroid tracks information flow system -wide, for Android. It tracks several sources of sensitive data  at once and can catch any data loss from third-part developed apps. It can tag sensitive data automatically, and when that sensitive data exits from the system through any network, it is logged by TaintDroid. It marks the app involved in
sending data, due to which sus picious apps can be identified. The limitation to this technique is that it does not track data that exits the system but returns any reply.

heading: 3.3 EMULATION-BASED
content: DroidScope is an emulation -based tool. It is used to analy ze applications dynamically based o n Virtual Mac hine Introspection. It observes the whole system from outside by being out of execution environment. As malwares will not be able to detect existence of anti-malware installed on the device, they will be easier to detect. Another emulation -based tool is provided by Blaising et al. It’s called Android Application Sandbox (AASandbox) [6]. This tool makes use of both dynamic and static analysis for the detection of malicious applications. The effectiveness of the tool is limited to sandbox for some of the security reasons. The tool observes the behavior of the user dynamically, such as touches, clicks and gestures etc. Its drawback is that the tool cannot detect new malwares. Advantages of Dynamic Analysis: ▪ Detection of unknown attacks. ▪ It determines the app behaviour during execution and loads marked information. Disadvantages of Dynamic Analysis: ▪ Its highly resource consuming, not feasible for battery devices.

heading: 3.4 HYBRID DETECTION TECHNIQUES
content: It is an amalgamation of static and dynamic analysis techniques. It is a method that can assimilate data extracted dynamically, during run time, and then combine it with a static analysis algorithm, for distinguishing malicious behavior of an application.
Tools with hybrid analysis approach:

heading: Application Sandbox:
content: Application Sandbox was the first framework combining static and dynamic analysis. It first extracts the .dex file  from the application  and then performs static analysis  by scanning the software for patterns without executing it. In the dynamic analysis the appli cation is executed in the Sandbox with the traced system calls and corresponding reports for the further analysis.

heading: Mobile Sandbox:
content: Mobile sandbox uses hybrid analysis. In this, it analyses APK file of the system for static analysis. And for dynamic analysis, they run application on an emulator to observe suspicious behavior.

heading: Andrubis:
content: In Andrubis [7] framework, static analysis is done first, so that dynamic analysis can use the result of static analysis, which increases system’s efficiency . In static analys is, it focuses on byte code and manifest file. All the material static analysis is then utilized for dynamic analysis.

heading: 4.2.1 Decision Tree
content: It is a classifier. It represents a supervised learning approach. It is a graphical model where leaf nodes give result and non-leaf nodes characterize tests on one or more attributes. Tree co nsists of one root, branches, internal nodes and leaves. They use rules that are easily understandable by humans and used in knowledge system such as database. The strengths of using decision tree learning include: ▪ Easily understandable rules. ▪ It performs classification without slowing the computation. Saves time. ▪ It works well with categorical variables. ▪ It provides clear classification. The limitations of decision tree learning are: ▪ This learning tool is not suitable for prediction of continuous attribute. ▪ It does not perform well with small amount of data and multiple classes. ▪ Training decision tree is computationally costly.

heading: 4.2.2 k-Nearest Neighbour
content: This is also known as k -NN which is a kind of directed learning calculation. It works by simply storing in memory existing preparing dataset, when another inquiry is fired, an arrangement of related cases that display associates are saved from memory. k-NN deals with multiple neighbour at any given moment even as ordering thus it is known as K-Nearest neighbour.

content: It is a machine learning technique. It was proposed by Vladimir Vapnik and colleagues at AT&T Bell laboratories in 1992 [9]. It is the condition of artwork in system learning strategies. heading: Cross-Validation
content: It is an assessment of model that how well it will work on an unseen data. It is used when one wants to find out the accuracy of a model. The objective mainly is to accurate prediction using statistical analysis. In a predictive problem, there are two sets of instances, one is training set in which the class of instances is known. Training set, as the name suggests is used to train a predictive model. The other data set is test set, also known as validation set. In this set classes of instances are unknown. It is used to validate our model by predicting classes of test set, hence the name validation set.

The objective of cross-validation is to check the trained model’s capacity to predict classes of new instances that was not used in estimating it , so that we can check for problems like overfitting or selection bias  and can predict how well the model will work on an unknown dataset  (i.e., an independent dataset, for example an actual problem). For instance, we have a model with unknown classes, and we also have a data set which we can fit to our model. The fitting process improves the model to make the it fit the training data. If then we use our unknown dataset to check how will it work on independent sample, we will find that it does not work that well on an independent dataset as it worked on our training set. It doe s not fit as well as on training set. It is most probably because the training data was small and there were not enough variations in the set to make it fit to generalize it on other datasets. Cross-validation can be u tilized to compare the accuracies of d ifferent predictive modeling algorithms. For instance, we are interested in classifying malware applications from benign ones and we are considering k-nearest neighbor and Random Forest to predict the intent of an apk file. Using cross -validation, we could  compare both algorithms in terms of a ccurately classified instances and false positives.

heading: Proposed Methodology
content: In this chapter we describe the methodology we have proposed to perform analysis for the mobile devices to protect them from malware. Our aim is to design efficient malware detection system to achieve high accuracy using permissions of an APK, battery statistics and system calls. For better accuracy and efficiency, we will check both the benign and malicious applications. We will check the APK in two divisions, statically and dynamically.

heading: 7.1 STATIC ANALYSIS
content: We are using static analysis to extract the most indicative permissions, without executing the file, which in turn save device from any harmful intent. We have chosen permission analysis for static phase of our method. Application needs access to device resources, in order to complete its task, which a user c an only allow.  We are chec king an application’s Manifest file for specific permissions. We are using Android ( adb) for getting desired information. Manifest file has xml extension. It has package information, which consists of application components activi ties, broadcast receivers, permissions etc. It protects the device by providing permission to access protected resources. It also gives information about the Andr oid APIs an application is going to use. Most frequently requested permissions according to [1].

Figure 7.1 Most common permissions used by malicious and benign apps [17] We will check the permissions given below specifically for the behavior of an application. Figure 7.2 Requested permissions by APK

heading: READ_PHONE_STATE
content: It allows access to phone s tate, phone number, cellular network and status of ongoing calls. Its categorized under dangerous permissions. It transmits a user’s sensitive data such as device ID and phone number to an outside URL without the user consent.

heading: SMS PRIVILEGES
content: SEND_SMS, RECE IVE_SMS and READ_SMS. As the name indicates, app can read any incoming texts. Many services send SMS to user to change their passwords use the key in the SMS. App can send that data on outside server and can hack your account easily.

heading: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
content: External doesn’t necessarily mean SD storage. The primary purpose of external storage is to provide a place to put files that are meant to be shared between apps or that are too large to fit on the internal storage. Your external storage has your data backups and if they are not encrypted, it can be easily be accessed by malicious apps.

heading: INTERNET
content: This permission lets an app have access to internet. It allows the application to open network sockets. ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE allows the application to know whether an application in connected to a network. Some applications have no use of internet connecti on, asking for these permissions can suggest the application has a malicious intent.

heading: RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED
content: It allows an application to receive a broadcast after t he system finished booting. It doesn’t affect the system itself, but application can start working in background after system is restarted.

heading: VIBRATE
content: It allows application access to the vibrator. Application can make your device vibrate unnecessarily, causing the battery to deplete and also scare the user.

heading: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
content: It allows the applicat ion to access precise location of a device. Its categorized under protection level, dangerous.

heading: 7.2 DYNAMIC ANALYSIS
content: In some cases, permissions alone may not be able to classify application as malware. For instance, Careem is a utility app. It asks for all such permissions as shown in Fig 2.7, which we are using to classify an application as malicious. So, in order to increase the accuracy of classifying application as malware, we are also going to perform dynamic analysis. As the time passes, malware writers find new ways to hide malware in code or code them in some form which makes it hard to detect using static analysis. Dynamic analysis is widely used to analyze the behavior of applications. The files are executed in virtually controlled environment so as to not affect the device. Applications are installed and tested on Android emulator. It’s virtually same as an actu al android device. It has some pre -installed software. We are using two attributes for dynamic analysis:

heading: 7.2.1 BATTERY CONSUMTION
content: This is one of the difficult symptoms to notice as most mobile users have experienced some kind of battery issues in their devices. Malwar e drain resources faster than benign. Battery statistics include CPU usage, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and screen usage. This is because malware usually carries on its activities in the background effectively, and are able to make your device work double than usual.  If you notice, your battery draining much quicker than normal, then your phone might be carrying out malicious activities without your knowledge. As an APK runs, we will check its battery statistics i.e. how much the app is using CPU resources. Malicious applications drain device’s battery quicker than any benign application. Malware hide its activities in the background, without the user ever knowing. So, CPU usage is a good indicator of differentiating between the two. We will check the  CPU behavior of b oth the benign and
malicious applications to get data , to train our model to be efficient.  Benign applications don’t consume battery as the infected ones does.

heading: 7.2.2 SYSTEM CALLS
content: Android platform has multiple layers, in the form of a stack. Layers on the lower level provide service to the upper layer.  Application Layer: Application run at this level. Third party a pps are also included. Kernel Layer: Android runs on top of a Linux 2.6 kernel. Apps communicate with the system hardware through this layer. It provides core functionalities and resources to the apps. System calls acts as an interface between application and device. Apps can invoke a function or a method to do a task. Application pass these system calls to get access to hardware devices. As we can not get to know the behavior of an application just by analyzing permissions, so for better accuracy we will monitor battery statistics and also consider system calls. There are some system calls which are called by both malicious and genuine applications.  We will monitor the frequency with which some system calls are being made. If an application is continuously making those system calls then by combining them with above mentioned attributes we can declare if the application is malicious or benign.

Figure 7.3 Mostly occurring system calls among applications according to [18]. In the above figure there is graph shown the black bar is show the percentage of system calls. If an application calls the mentioned system calls again and again frequently then that application could be infected with malware.

heading: Discussion
content: This chapter explores the role of machine learning and data driven approach in the first part.

heading: 10.1 ROLE OF MACHINE LEARNING IN MALWARE DETECTION
content: We have trained three separate models on machine learning algorithms. Machine learning is great technique for detecting malicious file and threats to the devices. It helps to predict missing values and identify patterns. These algorithms depend on dataset pro vided to them. Our method shows promising results for malware detection. For effective model training, we need to have large dataset. With the work being done in data analytics, it is easier to collect and access data. As our method is data driven, we need to have the right attributes and in sufficient amount. We selected specific permission based on data collected from application and same for system calls. System calls, in total are very large in number. We reduce them to a few for our checking. But it c an vary from data source to data source. Our purpose was to detect malware in android device effectively. Our trained model shows that it accurately predicted more than 90 percent of the data. FP, short for False Positive, for malicious class is less than 0.13 which is considerably a good number. FP is an important attribute as it tells us if an instance is wrongly classified as benign. It can be quite dangerous as it will allow the system to run an application that can inflict harm to the system or data. Limitations of Machine Learning Machine Learning is helpful in  identifying patterns which makes it able to handle security incidents. New versions of Android come every year. Mobile devices are progressing rapidly in technology. With the advancements, every year new kind of malware are m ade too. People find new ways to injecting malware to devices. Hackers are quite skilled as researchers. They can easily confuse the algorithm with different malware modifications.  It is impossible to train your model for all kinds of attack. We monitored 100 application for malware an d benign each. Machine

Learning ideally needs a large amount of training data. It can be quite cumbersome to extract these features manually and label them accordingly. Another limitation of Machine Learning is lack of variability. It is difficult to prove  that predictions made by Machine Learning models are appropriate for all scenarios. Limitations of our methodology Our data which, we have collected is not enough to properly train a model and predict accurately. Increasing our dataset will enhance the ability of the model to classify applications. We selected pe rmissions and system calls on the basis of [17] and [ 18] respectively.  These attributes were selected on the basis of a dataset. This means attributes can vary depending on the dataset. We monitored applications for one minute each. Some malwares remain do rmant for quite some time or they need some specific triggers or a set of commands to activate malicious behavior, which cannot be detected at early stage of use. Our testing was emulator based. In certain cases, malicious apps crashed emulator. According to [19], tests done on real devices gave far more efficient results than emulators. Moreover, during testing of application on emulator, malware can act artificially as a genuine applicatio n to affect the efficiency of the result.

heading: 10.2 CONCLUSION
content: In this project, we devised a method to efficiently classify android based application as malicious or benign. We performed static analysis by extracting permissions and dynamic by getting battery consumption and system calls. We used machine learning techniq ue for classification. We performed malware detection analysis by means of Simple Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes and KStar. Our method generated promising results for malware detection.

heading: 10.3 FUTURE WORK
content: In future, we will aim to increase our dataset to  further increase the efficiency of the system. It could also investigate, in additional, battery consumption and system calls. Which system calls or their frequency with which they occur,  can predict the behavior of an application with more precision. A comparative battery analysis between malicious and benign applications can be done in future, to estimate the role of battery drain in identifying malware.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: In every local organization, tracking of employees work, performance and their attendance on daily basis is a general and an important task for the betterment of an organization. Because it helps an organization to make important decisions like promotion, devotion and suspension of employees, moreover it also helps them to make salaries as per the work done by the employees. The purpose of this project “smart incident report” is to track employees work and generate their daily, weekly, monthly and annually basis performance reports by analysing their work hours, their arrival and departure time from the work field and their attendance. Moreover it also generate employee’s salaries by analysing their working hours on daily basis, and can perform actions of deduction and add bonus on salaries as per organization defined criteria. A web app that will provides local organizations, industries, offices, banks to track their employee’s performance and generate their daily, weekly, monthly and annual basis reports by keeping in view of their performance and working hours, which help organizations to become efficient, boost their work and help them to minimize the man force which they had hired to mark  attendance, keeping record of employees arrival and departure from the work field and generate hand written reports which is time consuming and less efficient. So, it is very mandatory to develop such system that can help organizations and high authoriti Ses of them to find and differentiate the lazy and faineant employees from the workforce, which helps to make organization resources optimize and efficient.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The main objective of this system is to track and analyse the employees performance within a local organization, and generate reports on daily, weekly, monthly and annually basis by keeping in view of their working hours and their performance. This will ultimately help to differentiate the lazy and faineant employees  or workers from the organization and helps organization to make strategies and plans to get efficient results from the employees by analysing their performance. This system will help to maintain the log files of workers and employees work, which later can  be analysed and help to generate reports. As in many organizations they have to hire people for keep tracking or examining the workers performance, activities, their attendance and even their arrival and leaving time from the work field or office, which increase the organization resources and budget and also is not very efficient and fast. So this system will help the organization to minimize their work force and make their processes efficient by keeping track record of their employees and it also help or ganization to take decisions about employees or workers promotion and devotion or even also help them to make better and good strategies to get efficient work.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: This is the modern era of technology which help people to reduce human effo rts and minimize the workforce. In Pakistan, most of the organizations still not adopt efficient systems which track or analyze their workers and employees performance. As technology is growing very rapidly, so local organizations are now turning to automa te systems which minimizes their workforce and help them to get a work of ten employees or workers from a single efficient system. The organizations are hired workers to maintain the records of employees work, their performance, their attendance, their arrival and leaving time from the working field, and also for to generate their reports. As these all tasks are performed by manually so they are not so much efficient and even they are time consuming. It also sometimes give favour to other employees who are lazy and faineant. Hence, it is very mandatory to develop such system that can help organizations and high authorities of them to find and differentiate the lazy and faineant employees from the workforce, which helps to make organization resources optimize and efficient.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions and Constraints
content: It’s assumed that the admin is already created in the system and system require the backend database server for storing the records for different types of the employees or workers as well as various databases regarding the attendance and working hours of employees which later help to generate reports. The admin will enter the record and attendance of employees and workers after verifying or analysing the authenticity of work which is done by the employee through process of verification.A centralized database system will be designed for generating daily, weekly, monthly and daily basis reports. The main constraint here would be the checking and the genuineness of the admin who is using the system, which is done by verification method like password or finger print scanner. There can be no security risks involved.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: In local organizations many workers and employees spent their time by doing nothing, and there are no such systems are available which can analyze the employees and workers are working or not, so the organizations have to are hire more employees to observe and monitoring th e workers and employees in the work field and maintain the records of employees work, their performance, their attendance, their arrival and leaving time from the working field, and also for to generate their reports. As these all tasks are performed by ma nually so they are not so much efficient and even they are time consuming. It also sometimes give favour to other employees who are lazy and faineant. Hence, the scope of this project is so important for organization growth and employees monitoring and generating reports that can help organizations and high authorities of them to find and differentiate the lazy and faineant employees from the workforce, which helps to make organization resources optimize and efficient.

heading: Abstract:
content: Crime activities have become a major issue in our country. It ’s increasing/growing day by day. We have to play a role in order to overcome this issue. We noticed that our security departments are still using old technologies like CCTV footage for event surveillance, which is very time consuming and leave a blind spot for anyone to utilize, to overcome this problem from this point of view, we developed a system that will reduce terrorism from our country. The system which we built uses the profits of this field to find the suspect trying to flee or to hide in our environment. This system proposes a prototype product of a quadcopter which uses a camera integrated within to get the real-time video feed of the environment. We process that live feed to recognize person based on image that we stored in concerned system. It also shows the real-time location using navigation system. This method shows appropriate range assistance for security purpose with better performance as well as efficiency.

heading: 1.1 Overview:
content: Suspect Monitoring and tracking system is an aerial surveillance system, which uses quad copter at its base, while our security departments are still using old technologies like CCTV footage for event surveillance which limits its use. The growing need of today ’s world is to provide sense of security that will be beneficial in the development of the society. As regulation of attention is selectively focused on discrete aspect of information from surroundings, our system will continuously monitor the environment using camera as its eyes thus generate live report.

heading: 1.2 Introduction:
content: Within mind about the security issues in Pakistan, we have developed a product to provide assistance to our society. This product will help us identify the suspected person with the help of a quadcopter attached to it a camera whose responsibility is to monitor the environment to capture live video feed as to synchronize with our databases in backend to identify that specific person’s identity. Lawlessness is increasing day- by-day, we live in a society where people using resources (bribery, political power) can easily exit the suspension, crime rate is gradually increasing, and our security departments are still using old technologies like CCTV footage for event surveillance, which is not sufficient, because after suspect passed through CCTV camera it doesn’t provide further location and monitoring of the suspect. Suspect Monitoring and tracking system is an aerial surveillance system, which uses quad copter at its base, since the quad copter used by professionals cost a great amount of money we build on our own which is cost efficient and highly customisable, it includes many other features which are not covered by many other quad copters, a raspberry pi device is attached to it for the live streaming process which can be accessed over IP address on any device, it ’s like a computer flying through the air cause raspberry pi itself is a powerful computing device, an algorithm works in real time when ever live streaming is initiated which identifies the facial properties of objects shown in the video, this algorithm works on the desktop application which accesses the video from quad copter ’s attached raspberry pi. There is a GPS device installed on the quadcopter which sends the current location of the quadcopter to an application.

P a g e The advantage of this surveillance system is that it covers all possible angles in a given environment and keeps you updated with the current location. That makes it time efficient and cost efficient.

heading: 1.3 Objectives:
content: The main objective is to monitor and survey the local area for any possible unnatural activity. With the power to save and analyses the live video stream with constant working on recognizing the facial expressions simultaneously. One of its goals is to provide its current real time location.

heading: 1.4 Problem Statement:
content: When training a set for face recognition, height, distance and angle is very important for the algorithm of face recognition to work properly, for example, if the distance is too great, the picture will be small and algorithm will be unable to identify, the size of image do impact on the result so does the resolution and compression of camera, or if angle of drone is too steep, it reduces the successful working of both face recognition and detection.

content: Efficient planning of a project depends on the correct statements of project assumptions and constraints. content: Literature review and related work is the key base for every project. You can brainstorm many different aspects from it, in simple words you can create your own path by following the steps (previous work) or you can follow the same way just by adding some more twists into it (modifications).In this chapter, we have discussed some systems related to detections, identifications, surveillance and some elements related to UAVs that is unmanned autonomous vehicles so that we can have a more detailed discussion on what we have developed in the followed chapters.

heading: 2.2.1.1 Overview
content: The increase in the number of vehicles on roadway networks has led transport management agencies to allow use of technology advances resulting in better decisions. The mission of roadway transportation agencies is to evolve from solely providing roadway infrastructure to focusing on the needs of the traveling public, management and operations, and improved performance of the surface transportation system. Traditional technology for traffic sensing, including inductive loop detectors and video cameras, are positioned at fixed locations in the transportation network. It is not possible to move detectors; further, they cannot provide useful information such as vehicle trajectories, routing information, and paths through the network. Aerial view provides better perspective with the ability to cover a large area and focus resources on the current problems.UAVs may be employed for a wide range of transportation operations and planning applications: incident response, monitor freeway conditions, coordination among a network of traffic signals, traveler information, emergency vehicle guidance, track vehicle movements in an intersection, measurement of typical roadway usage, monitor parking lot utilization, estimate Origin- Destination (OD) flows .

P a g e UAVs are classified as either rotary-wing or fixed-wing. Fixed-wing vehicles are simple to control, have better endurance, and are well suited for wide-area surveillance and tracking applications. They have high maneuverability and hovering. Rotary wing vehicles have short range radars and cameras to detect traffic movement. They can work at altitudes up to 100,000 feet. Fixed-wing aircraft use to collect congestion and traffic information [1].

heading: 2.2.1.2 Critical Analysis
content: Now coming to the feedback about this product, The Aerosonde UAV is a fixedwing vehicle made in Australia and operated by Aerosonde Pty Ltd (AePL). It flies for over 32 hours, at an altitude of between 300 to 20000 feet above the ground, where it will be largely invisible during daylight hours. The Aerosonde employs a Sony XC555 video camera, which captures video of the traffic on the highway; and a pair of Vaisala RSS901 weather sounds to gather freeway surveillance and RWIS data for transmission to the FDOT microwave towers.

heading: 2.2.2.1 Overview
content: Similarly like a flying helicopter, quadrotor or quadcopter have the ability to take off a nd land vertically, can move in any way at any time with the stability in air. Due to the increasing demand for UAVs, quadrotor has gained popularity in this modern era. In terms of mechanism quadrotor technology is much easier than a helicopter as it has four motors that all having a stable intensity, also those rotors can be enfolded with a frame body, provide protection from any

P a g e collision and allow secure flights in an obstacle-less and hurdle-full environment. Those problems can be settled out by unique effective tools to handle their inconsistency in unknown environments as well as increasing their payload capacity and low continuance. Our focused approach is ‘’Parrot AR Drone technology version 2.0 ” quadrotor to elaborate search and tracking operations, that involve mobility target searching and then tracking if found.

heading: Figure 2.2:  Perrot Drone 2.0
content: Computer vision promotes object detection field these days. Precisely recognize an image of the object is the main part of object detection. Those systems having such kind of applications like image recognition or search apply detection of the object as its core part. Lim in 2012 says that the detection of an object is still a huge issue because of image resolution or object itself. Commonly each frame from a stream observed to get the object is the only approach used to date, but this type of analysis has chances of high error rate. That ’s why Mohong in 2012 concluded that high error rate can be reduce using temporary values that have been calculated by the sequence of frames from a video stream. Tracing an object is just like the detection of the object is one of the prime fields of computer vision because of the need of time. The process of tracking the object from images or fra me sequences is termed as object tracking.  Issues while tracking an object relies on movement of the object, background material like color, pattern changes, some changes in the object structure, occlusion by two phase ’s object-by-background or object- by-object or in any phase of camera movement. Coming to our point of concern, a person or any kind of object that seems like moving at the speed that well matched with the speed of AR Drone according to some specific purpose.

P a g e By following a preset path in any indoor or outdoor environment the target wants to reach some calculated destination that is well known. It should be understood that the target doesn ’t want to do any kind of imprecise action to play its features in any situation for hiding. Probably we can assume that the target might show cooperation with quadcopter or may be unaware of AR Drone presence. Some sort of noisy sensors can become the major cause that a drone might miss leading the target of a specific tag so face recognition plays an important role here. So we use some facial recognition techniques over there to overcome such kind of problems we are facing that might be useful in future as well [2].

heading: 2.2.2.2 Critical Analysis
content: A drone has the capability of following lines and is known when to turn or not near to corners especially. That phenomenon is very helpful in future research's to produce intellectual applications. One of them is an auto guided application or you can say a system for the clients in a mall or such businesses. Different color lines pattern can be drawn on the ground or according to customer demand so quadcopter will follow that set pattern, which allows the quadcopter to fly according to the preset corners or colors. Except for these entire possibilities still required recognition element to trace more objects. Developing such kind of drone robots is also counted as one of the biggest challenges in future proceedings. Hope to have success in such kind of projects in future.

heading: 2.2.3.1 Overview
content: In this particular project for the purpose of developing a system of robust tracking, we distributed the task of tracking and detection in different phases of operation. In other words it means that with the use of face detection algorithms the drone has to find out its field of view for any type of human faces which we implemented in this Drone to identify if a particular person is present in a close range. Additionally in the different human faces our algorithms have developed a database. In this following algorithm we applied the Eigenface recognizer algorithm. The face identification algorithm based upon Eigenface was projected to reside in this AR drone. Other

P a g e algorithms such as SURF detection algorithm is also an important algorithm. The resulted output from the detection and recognition algorithms is our central controlling of the drone. Allowing the robot to regulating its position towards the level of tracked object, which including the following tasks firstly going in the direction or towards him, secondly maintaining an optimal distance (backward motion as well) and finally by keeping the specific target in its field of vision by rotating its movement in the environment. By using the wireless connection the data was transmitted between the AR drone and computer Figure 2.3: AR Parrot Drone 2.0 This project suggests a system for tracking of objects by using Speeded up Robust Feature (SURF) detection and by using Eigenface recognizer for the human face identification. In this following paper the combinations of algorithms such as Haar-Cascade classifier, modified Eigenface, and SURF resulting in an additional robust system for face recognition and object detection. On AR drone 2.0 this type of proposed system was executed by utilizing the Microsoft Visual Studio 2010 platform along with the OpenCV. The proposed system analysis was carried out in an enclosed environment for evaluating its performance in terms of angle, accuracy and distance of detection. From four different detecti on distances at least 132 images of various people were utilized for the purpose of face recognition. Approximately 92.22% the best resulting average was obtained by the detection distance ranging from 50cm to 75cm. We are using the Eigenface recognition algorithm which was projected effectively on the Eigenface recognition algorithm. It was also used in Haar-Cascade library,
P a g e Eigenface values and PCA etc. The final results obtained through testing revealed that the most effective algorithm was the Eigenface recognizer algorithm [3].

heading: 2.2.3.2Critical Analysis
content: It was observed that by increasing the detection distance the detection accuracy was decr eased. In addition improves proposed algorithm, AR drone strengths and other various limitations. Point to be pondered on is the Haar-cascade feature that relies on algorithms of face detection on robots till now, correct face importance belongs to images having proper face detections by nature of that algorithm. To detect face correctly from a flying robot like quadcopter integrated with camera need stable face detection to improve results by maintaining the balance between image resolution and distance between object and quadcopter so location is also one of the premium parameters to balance equation. Face detection requires images in the data base to be compared with the current faces getting from each frame for matching the real-time image with the image that we have in our database, so we required a training set of targets in our database to find out, which we are looking for. AR Drone helped us getting live stream so we can apply ou r calculated algorithms to find out the results we required to get the target in our pocket.

heading: 2.2.5 Automatic detection, classification and tracking of objects in the ocean
content: surface from UAVs using a thermal camera

heading: 2.2.5.1 Overview:
content: Quadcopters or in other words UAVs are becoming popular these days because of their autonomous behavior in a high-risk operating and dynamic environment. An operation like this kind requires classification and detection of objects along with specific tracking to achieve their goals. In some past years, the establishment of hardware on UAVs played a vital rule in data processing and observance because of the small and powerful hardware integration with the quadrotor. Their ability to process live stream or saved video feed with the help of fast and accurate providence algorithms for object detection, identifications, and tracking. In this article, they have discussed the development of a machine with the implementation of a vision system for a low budget UAV having fixed propellers with a flying weight no more than 4kg.The main focus of the system is to use those algorithms along with an integrated camera that will provide thermal images for object detection, identifications and tracking in the ocean surface [5].

heading: 2.2.5.2 Critical Analysis:
content: Data from test flight has been collected and observed under the developed system and surprisingly 99.6% of objects were located according to the interest from the ocean surface. Only 5% were declared as false positives from the collected data at the end of observations. Moreover, it classifies almost 93.3% objects that it has been trained to find out correctly. The kind of objects and their characteristics have already been set to train the classifier so that it can easily identify the object from a thermal image. But the point to concern is it doesn ’t allow the classifier to predict only it can give results on matching even if an object has some characteristics changed by nature, at this point we might miss out some of the major objects.

heading: 2.2.6.1 Overview:
content: Life of every person has the first priority to save in any case. In this research, we are focusing on to the system that is capable of human detection and geo-location if they have faced any kind of

P a g e disaster using quadcopter with integrated systems to rescue them. For this purpose, we have included the characterization of humans so that the system can determine if a human is found at such place by the help of thermal and the optical images for true or false accuracy decisions. The geographical location of that human is found with the help of GPS data that is calculated from triangulated-adjustment of G.P.S module with integrated Google maps [6].

heading: 2.2.6.2 Critical Analysis:
content: Some tools used in this system have some pros and cons such as creating human detection with geographical location programs and V.C.D ’s that is video capturing devices. As the focus is on survivors so sometimes the devices attached to UAV ’s not functioned properly at some altitude and because of their attachment to the autonomous behavior we can’t fix it out immediately due to distance. Another factor that is crucial is the nighttime, at night thermal images accuracy is decreased because of many factors one of them is heat, on the other hand, optical detection is suitable at daytime so we have used the combo to provide day and night rescue facility to those who faced any kind of disaster using Drone Technology to save lives as much as we can.

heading: 2.2.7.1 Overview:
content: Duo to the constant increase in the devastation of environment, we need to monitor the changes in the environment constantly, but usage of ground based travelling devices are very consuming in every aspect, that ’s why we need aerial based devices. There is a large development in the airborne engineering, it costs very little to have a simple device following you around, these are known as, quad-copters. The focus of this study is to manufacture a low cost and low weight device that helps in the surveillance of environment and research. A multirotor concept was created which was based on the assumptions that it could hover, analyze environmental data and generate GPS location. On the ideas frame, drivers and software was selected for successful presentation.  During the testing some custom hardware was made to complete the current need.

heading: 2.2.7.2 Critical Analysis:
content: Quad copter ’s available configuration are very versatile, this engineering allows this field to provide a multiple number of different types of platform. Number of hardware parts used is the
P a g e first most distinguishable quality, e.g. like the types motors used on the quad copter. Like the configuration of both its arms is also very important feature.

heading: 2.2.8.1 Overview:
content: Quad Copters is the most enjoyable platform because of its agility, simplicity, and a large number of applications. Many research quad copters have large frame which can carry cameras and other accessories, but cost increases with the size and hardware, because they have to carry  a huge weight. But for the usage of large numbers of this machine like a swarm, small is the best, the small size of this product motivates different system design choices, here we are using 49 small quadcopter for an indoor swarm, and they use a motion-capture system and share or communicate over shared radio. We uses custom made hardware and do work on board. Till date, the described system is the largest overall in terms of indoor swarms, and quadcopter controlled by radio.

heading: 2.2.8.2 Critical Analysis:
content: The shown system is architecture for stout, synchronized and dynamically controlled large scaled indoor quadcopter swarm till date. Our system uses on machine solving problem capability, which gives us flawless control over machine movement and great communication over radio. This also improves the overall radio bandwidth. For the swarm which includes 49 quad copters, only requires 3 radios to fully control all machines at latency of 30ms and below.

heading: 2.2.9.1 Overview:
content: This research uses an algorithm for abnormal people ’s behavior data and produces real time surveillance applications. This method is based on pixel density modeling. By the use of static methods we obtain pixel density in normal behavior by using data sets available in literature. While in the case of anomaly, we run an imitation of people ’s motion and save the data for future. We record the algorithm ’s execution time for motion detection and confirm its approach
P a g e in fast applications. Lastly we confirm the method with respect to other approaches in the literature [9].

heading: 2.2.10.1 Overview:
content: Unmanned aerial vehicles are getting popular among the community. Fast growing technologies like LTE 4G/5G networks will broaden the use of drone. In this article we discuss about the UAVs, prepared with IoT devices to deliver IoT services from heights. This article demonstrates how UAVs can be used for crowd surveillance based on face recognition. To evaluate it, we study the offloading of video data processing to a MEC node compared to the local processing of video data onboard UAVs. To perform face recognition, we used LBPH method from the OpenCv library. The obtained results reveals that the efficiency of the MEC based offloading approach reducing the processing time of face recognition and rapidly detecting suspicious persons in time [10].

heading: 5.1 Overview:
content: System Architecture is a skeleton of every project. If the base of each part is strong enough to get proper functionality and outcome then we can say that system is stable and reliable. In this chapter, we have discussed the quadcopter assembling in detail, and then we have a brief explanation of how we have managed to achieve live streaming and the geographical location. Apart from that, we have also mentioned the details of Raspberry Pi and the algorithm we choose to find out the suspect along with prototypic demonstrations.

heading: 5.2 System Architecture:
content: Nowadays Drone technology becomes increasingly popular to explore and observe behaviors in indoor and outdoor environments respectively. This technology can be used as a lifesaving element in many cases like finding the suspect through embedded high-resolution cameras that provides live streaming, pictures and aerial views of several events. In our project, we have developed a system that is capable of finding the suspect through an embedded high-resolution camera that provides live streaming and aerial view. Our target area is to reduce the unethical and unlawful activities during a particular event by providing surveillance to that particular event. The main objective of our project is to find the suspect and notify the concerned person in security checking area of that particular event by making the face of the suspicious person prominent with his/her name also providing the location of the suspect. We have searched out the market and concerned area to find a quadcopter that is capable of uplifting weight to some height with the stability and within the budget and time as Drone flying is prohibited in Pakistan and due to a ban on its flying we can ’t purchase a drone and shipped it to Pakistan. We found some but they are either incapable of uplifting some weight or out of our budget as we have already mentioned that we are providing surveillance to event level so we have decided to build a drone that has the capabilities and functionalities to fulfill our requirements, we searched out the required parts and purchased it, then assembled the quadcopter.

heading: 5.3.1 Quadcopter frame:
content: It’s a carbon fiber 4 axis flexible frame with nylon touch to provide the frame some flexibility and strength to hold the connected weight. 17.7inch/450mm wheelbase provides the multi-rotor the required base to stand and bear the weight. Model of frame is f450 (see figure 5.3.1). The frame comes in parts we have to assemble it by self, using the provided guideline that comes with the frame. Figure 5.1: Quadcopter frame

heading: 5.3.2 Landing Gear for Flame wheel Quadcopter:
content: Quadcopter stand or landing gear is basically 4 legs made of nylon bind with the quadrotor frame to provide smooth takeoff and landing. Hard nylon provides the leg ability to bear the quadcopter weight and to maintain the balance of the connected components (see in figure 5.3.2).

heading: 5.3.3 Quadcopter Motors
content: We have use 4 brushless motors because brushless motors have almost no brushes this m eans fewer parts need to be changed in case of any breakage or wear out as compared to the brushed motor. Th e motor we used is of type 22 x 12mm with 920rpm (KV) and 7-12V D.C voltage needed and 53g in weight. 2 clockwise and 2 counter clockwise motors with a size of 22*12mm. Black nuts represents clockwise while silver ones are clockwise motors (see in figure 5.3.3).

heading: 5.3.4 Quadcopter ESC
content: Electronic speed controllers in quadcopters play vital role as they allow the control the speed of the motors according to the information they get from the flight controller they are like communicators between motor and flight controller working as third party component to deliver flight controller message that comes from the receiver. Each ESC ’s with a current of 30A and output of 5v or 2A.

heading: 5.3.5 Quadcopter Flight Controller with G.P.S module
content: We have used Arducopter Amp 2.6 flight controller as it is easily available and great repute for videos and photography kind Drones. It ’s an FPV flight controller (first person view) provides a great pilot eye view through a camera attached as we have implemented it with our own ca mera so it works only a flight controller for our quadcopter. Along with flight controller, there is a built-in G.P.S module that provides constant location this is another reason that we have chosen this flight controller model using 3M double tape G.P.S module is attached to a stand for enhancing signal strength. An application name Mission Planer provides the longitude and latitude values for the specific location. The G.P.S module comes along with compass to easily adjust to new area just by configuring it using that application.Mission Planner allowed us to visualize not only the location but also the some other particular terms too such like flight time, ground speed, vertical speed altitude and many other factors. We can easily configure flight controls using this application and some other factors too like if battery level is below quadcopter will auto land to save it from any consequences.
P a g e Figure 5.5: Quadcopter Flight Controller with G.P.S module

heading: 5.3.6 Quadcopter Controller and receiver
content: For quadcopter model f450 we use the FLYSKY fs-iA6 controller along with its receiver that is connected to Arducopter flight controller to control the flight parameters like takeoff, landing, and speed variations according to the given signals. It also shows the battery life of quadcopter as well as the controller itself. Figure 5.6: Quadcopter Controller and receiver

P a g e The controller has two joysticks embedded the left one controls the flight speed usually termed as throttle and the right one is used to move the drone towards any direction. There is a power on & off button that provides the controller power to functioning properly. We can configure the controls on mission planner for quadrotor flight. To start the motors the left joystick first push downward then move towards the right side, when motors start, moving that joystick quickly upwards to takeoff and to turn off the motors simply move that joystick towards the right and use the right side joystick to turn around in any way.

heading: 5.3.7 Quadrotor propellers
content: Quadcopter propellers also play a vital role. Stronger the propellers will provide greater stability and flight by crossing the wind in an appropriate manner so we chose the carbon fiber material rather than nylon material. We have 2 pairs of propellers with a size of 1045 that means 10inch long and 4.5inch width, 1 clockwise pair and 1 counter clockwise to maintain balance at some height. Both the propellers already have their selected motors to be fitted on. There are two types of propellers present self - tightening and nut bolt screwed. We choose the bolt screwed type because self-tightened sometimes misplaced the nut that can damage the motor tightening part. Figure 5.7: Quadcopter propellers

heading: 5.3.8 Quadcopter battery
content: A Battery is a core component of any flight motor either it ’s a quadcopter or helicopter. Your flight time, flight performance and safety from any flight damage totally depend on battery material and lifetime. We choose LIPO 5200mah battery that provides consistent 12V power to maintain stable flight up to 20 minutes without live streaming. We can ’t use a higher battery because of weight issue higher the battery will increase in weight and requires related changed components as well as powerful motors, requires increased propellers length and ESC ’s etc. Battery charge and discharge time sometimes counter a problem that leads towards battery lifetime. Figure 5.8: Quadcopter battery

heading: 5.4.1 Raspberry pi
content: To get live stream from quadcopter we have embedded a raspberry pi 3 model b. we have installed a raspbian Jessie flavor of Ubuntu as an operating system on pi along with 1 GB of RAM and 8 GB of ROM. The idea behind using the pi is to send the live stream using a network over an IP address to get that easily while connecting with the same network. You can have at any display by just accessing that IP. Pi is an updated technology that allowed us to use it according to the need of the project it works like a compact pocket size P.C.

P a g e Figure 5.9: Raspberry pi We have set those configurations for motion start (webcam start when pi boot) in motion.config file along with some changes like frame rate, width, height etc. Figure 5.10: motion.conf

heading: 5.4.2 D.C to D.C Converter
content: As quadcopter battery supplied 12V parallel current and pi just needed 5V so we have used a D.C to D.C converter to supply the required power to raspberry pi to save it from any damage. The converter is directly connected to battery and converting continuously to supply forward to pi. There is a nob on that converter to easily set the required voltage to be converted we have set it on 5V. Figure 5.11: D.C to D.C converter

heading: 5.4.3 Camera
content: As we are using the cam for recognition and detection so the camera should be of high resolution with focused pixels and clear images from a distance so we can have some better results. For capturing and streaming live environment we decided to go with Logitech c270, an I.P based webcam.

heading: 5.4.4 Final Product
content: We assembled all the parts and finally have a quadcopter that is capable of uplifting weight along with pi and camera. Figure 5.13: Final product After assembling drone, let’s discuss about system that we proposed and how it works:

heading: 5.5  Live Stream:
content: Raspberry pi is connected to the internet connection which provides us with its IP address, we have adjusted the setting on the pi boot service which gets the pi camera to auto start when power is given and gets the live stream rolling, These configurations were set up in a motion.conf file that relies in \etc\motion directory, Because of which when we put IP address in our application it access the camera of raspberry pi directly and the video starts streaming.

heading: 5.6 Face Detection and Recognition:
content: The very first step is to find the number of faces in environment. We used live streaming and face detection algorithm to find faces. For face detection we use “haarcascade_frontalface_default.xml” classifier. This classifier is already trained with front faces of different people. So when we run code that we written in python, it starts detecting persons face.
P a g e Figure 5.14: Face detection Figure 5.15: Face detection using drone As we can see above, there are total three faces, it successfully detect all three faces.

P a g e Next step is to find the suspect in real time environment. Here comes face recognition which is most important part. For face recognition we use “FisherFaceRecognizer”. It’s actually a model that is used to train data that we have in our drive. First we have to train recognizer (suspect images) so, for that feed that face data and respective names of each face to the reco gnizer so that it can learn. After training recognizer, it starts recognizing people from live stream. How it works? It actually use principal components of persons face (like eye, nose etc) to match with images that stored in our drive. Here comes recognizer that helps to recognize face. Now the question is why we use FisherFaceRecognizer instead of other recognizers? Because FisherFace recognizer algorithm extracts principal components that differentiate one person from the others. In that sense, an individual's components do not dominate over the others. Figure 5.16: Face recognition using recorded video We test our face recognition code with recorded video; we take the video as sample from shuttertsock, it’s slow motion video that is recorded as 20fps. Why would we take slow motion video? Because when person walk slowly, it ’s easy for face recognizer to recognize face of suspect correctly. Also make easy for observer to see suspect face properly. Otherwise person move fast and face recognizer unable to recognize face properly.

P a g e As we can see in above image, one person is recognized successfully, because we have images of that person in our drive. And on other persons face, it shows unknown because it does not recognize those faces and we don’t have images of those persons in our drive. (See figure 5.6.4) There are few things that would make face recognition fast and accurate:  Train maximum images of suspect. The more images we have, the more accuracy we will achieve.  Images should be clear not blur.

heading: 5.7  GPS:
content: After recognizing suspect, next step is to find the location of suspect. Quad copter provides the precise current location to the application, to get balanced with the environment so that the location sent is properly transmitted; “Mission Planner” an external environment is used to fix its axis and its location. Mission planner is already made software that is using for configuration of custom made drone. We used that software to configure drone and its location. It provides real time location of drone.

heading: 10 of 70  14 May 2018
content: RDF (Resource Description Framework) originally designs as metadata model. It has come to be used as a general method for conceptual description or modelling of information that is implemented in web resources. It also facilitates data merging even if the underlying schema differ, and it specifically supports the evolution of schema over time without requiring all the data consumers to be changed. This framework is used for describing resources on the web. RDF is designed to be read and understood by Computers. XML language is used for it, by using XML RDF information can easily be exchanged between different types of computers using different types of computer using different types of operating system and application languages. Protégé is a free, open source ontology editor and a knowledge management system. It provides a graphic user interface to define ontologies. It also includes deductive classifiers to validate that models are consistent and to infer new information based on the analysis of an ontology. The purpose of protégé in our project is that we can upload structured data on web so it can be retrieved in structured format. Web Ontology Language (OWL) is a semantic Web [2] language designed  to represent rich and complex knowledge about things, group of things and relationship between things. OWL is a computational Logic based language such that knowledge expressed in OWL can be exploited by computer programs. OWL documents known as ontologies can be published in World Wide Web and may refer to or be referred from other OWL ontologies. OWL ontology is built by following steps:  Create the ontology.  Create classes, subclasses and provide information about them.  Create properties and provide information about them.  Create individuals and associate domain and range. SPARQL[3] is a procedure/system to generate quires. The queries are used to perform different operations and functions on the data that is semantical ly arranged. T he data would  then be accessed and retrieved using SPARQL instead of SQL because in Semantic Web SPARQL can make data collection of data in one big database where we could get information from different websites and different enterprise database. Semantic web is beneficial because it provides user with the accurate results.  Semantic web means a web with meaning. It searches, and combines the web information and provides with accurate results. It is a smart web which retrieves only the required results.

heading: 1.6.1 Implementation
content: We have created ontologies using the symmetric approach  [4]. The focus of our project revolves around the merging and mapping of ontologies, there are tools to perform this task but we are manually merging and mapping the concepts. Ontology merging, as its name implies, merges the concepts that match semantically with each other into a single concept. In the symmetric approach, data of the ontologies is fetched via SPARQL  query, and the query merges the data of both the ontologies, resulting in merging of ontologies. The web and android interfaces ar e designed to facilitate the user in viewing and purchasing different products. The interface will allow the user to register their profiles and login the application. Ontologies are created in protégé which does not allow every SPARQL query to be processed. SPARQL queries are used to process the RDF datasets, for this purpose we devised a solution in Jena Fuseki[5], which process the range of SPARQL queries to fulfil our requirements. We researched and then developed SPARQL queries to perform the required functionalities. To connect J ena Fuseki server datasets with web, we have built a new API which will receive and send requests to connect web with Fuseki server and with android. Fuseki server cannot work alone. To solve this problem, we used Ubuntu linode server so we can upload fuseki on linode. We used linode to get data on web server which will be connected to web easily. API will send and receive requests to web server and then server will send JSON[6] data to android. OWL ontology is built by following steps:  Create the classes, subclasses and provide information about them. All the classes will be subclass of owl:Thing.  Create data properties and provide Domain which will be the class in the ontology. Enter range of the data property which will be the int, double or string. All the data properties will be the subclass of owl: topDataProperty.

heading: 13 of 70  14 May 2018
content:  Create object properties and provide domain and range in this case both will be the class. Object properties are used to define the relation between two objects also called individuals in OWL ontology. All the object properties are subclass of owl: topObjectProperty. Provide the characteristic of object property and check the appropriate option.  Create individuals in the individuals tab. Individuals are the instances of class which is set in the “type” description. heading: 2.1 Literature review
content: In this project, we will work to produce a centralized application for nurseries and registered clients who need to avail gardenin g activities, facilitated by the system administration using our knowledge regarding semantic web and merging ontologies. In Pakistan we have no projects working on such centralized system of gardening currently but we will design a product that will not only benefit the clients but also the associated nurseries. Our project will be using the web application and Android application services so that the co -ordination between both  web and mobile app is well synchronized and the records are updated and maintained quickly and efficiently so the clients faces no difficulty. The details are as follows:  A web and Android interface will be provided for application services. Through log-in system we will differentiate between admins and other users of the application. Admins have the authority to monitor and control every service offered by the application. Admin can provide a direct communication between clients and nursery owners.  A client can register through web interface or by the application itself. The basic information of client will be if searched, can be selected and the application will show all the nurseries available to the client in specific radius. The client is provided with the facility of search, select and purchase of product from list.  Nurseries of different areas or locations can get registered through this application to facilitate the clients. Nursery owners make repository which they update periodically. They can make sure that the product demanded by the client is available to them. There are some website working in the field of botany, they provide with the facilities such as planting seeds, plants, providing them to the user, but none of the available websites’ are centralized and accommodate the essential needs of people all over the country.
