heading: 4.2 Unit Testing
content: Unit testing is a technique in which small units or modules of the system are tested individually. Unit testing can be done manually. Unit testing refers to testing of each module that has been built against functional requirement collected in software requireme nt specification, each module is built and tested. Following are the techniques of unit testing:  Black Box Testing: Input is provided and output is generated against an interface of the system module.  White Box Testing: The behavior and the patterns of the functions are tested.  Gray Box Testing:  This is used to tests risk and the assessment methods.

heading: 4.2.1 Integration Testing:
content: Integration testing focuses on the interface of the system. It is performed on the individual modules and units, integrated together to check their errors, reliability and interactivity with each other. Integration testing is important because the individual function or sub -functions when combined do not produce the desired results. Therefore, we apply integration testing to check the working between the modules after integration. We created different modules individually, first module was building of ontologies. This module consists of classes, sub-classes, data properties and object properties of our project. Ontology defines the main hierarchy of the project. The next module was creation of SPARQL Queries in Jena Fuseki. After the creation of SPARQL queries, we created merging queries which merged the ontologies. Later web they were integrated with our web and android application.

heading: 5.1 Project Working
content: We have created ontologies using the symmetric approach. The focus of our project revolves around the merging and mapping of ontologies, there are tools to perform this task but we are manually merging and mapping the concepts. Ontology merging, as its name implies, merges the concepts that match semantically with each other into a single concept . In the symmetric approach, data of the ontologies is fetched via SPARQL query, and the query merges the data of both the ontologies, resulting in merging of ontologies. The web and android interfaces are designed to facilitate the user in viewing and purchasing different products. The interface will allow the user to register their profiles and login the application. Ontologies are created in protégé which does not allow every SPARQL query to be processed. SPARQL queries are used to process the RDF datasets, for this purpose we devised a solution in Jena Fuseki, which process the range of SPARQL queries to fulfil our requirements. We researched and then developed SPARQL queries to perform the required functionalities. To connect Jena Fuseki server datasets with web, we have built a new API. For web we have used PHP/Laravel which will send requests to API, and API will process requests for both web and android. Fuseki server cannot work alone. To solve this problem, we used Ubuntu linode server so we can upload fuseki on linode. We used linode to get data on web server which will be connected to web. OWL ontology is built by following steps:  Create the classes, subclasses and provide information about them. All the classes will be subclass of owl: Thing.  Create data properties and provide Domain which will be the class in the ontology. Enter range of the data property which will be the int, double or string. All the data properties will be the subclass of owl: topDataProperty.  Create object properties and provide domain and range in this case both will be the class. Object properties are used to define the relation between two objects also called individuals in OWL ontology. All the object properties are subclass of owl: topObjectProperty. Provide the characteristic of object property and check the appropriate option.  Create individuals in the individuals tab. Individuals are the instances of class which is set in the “type” description. Create the object assertion properties and data assertion properties  Set disjoint sets where two classes cannot contain same instance.

heading: Abstract
content: This project aims to develop an intelligent vehicle assistance and safety system by integrating advanced technologies across multiple domains. The primary objectives include real-time object detection and frame annotation using YOLOv8, facilitating obstacle and hazard identification, and enhancing driver awareness through annotated video frames with bounding boxes, labels, distance estimates, and safety warnings. An automatic braking system uses additional sensors and image processing to reduce opposite collision risk. Automatic wiper activation, as well as rain detection, are considered to utilize rain sensors that are interfaced to an Arduino microcontroller so that visibility is clear during bad weather conditions. The proposed system is a fingerprint- based security system for biometric vehicle access, along with IoT enabled GPS monitoring to increase security by way of real time alerts and access logs. IR and ultrasonic sensors are employed by blind spot detection and parking assistance systems to enhance safety during such moves in limited space. Moreover, conceptual research is inherited to attempt to improve the speed and energy efficiency of solar powered vehicles with provided insights and the suggestions. Together, these innovations seek to make for a safer, more efficient and technologically superior way of driving. Table of Contents

heading: 1. Introduction
content: Solar powered cars are fast becoming the revolutionary concept in transportation, largely thanks to the growing demand for sustainable and eco-friendly solutions in transportation. These cars take the benefit of renewable solar energy to help diminish fossil fuel dependence and greenhouse gas emission. Yet, solar powered cars aren’t yet widespread because they confront several challenges. The problem of this project is related to these challenges, which can be minimized by integrating image processing and Internet of Things (IoT) into solar powered cars, which would improve them in functionality, efficiency and user experience. This project  provide the most ideal performance of solar powered vehicles as long as they are practical and easy to be utilized. Using image processing, the car achieves more advanced safety features than what is available today such as obstacle detection which also increases road safety by allowing autonomous breakage. The second advantage is that IoT based systems provide vehicle security systems as well as a user-friendly interface. Road safety is one of the most important global issues, as evidenced by the startling data that almost 5 million vehicle accidents occur each year and result in about 1.3 million fatalities globally. The majority of human mistakes and negligence including distracted driving, and disregard for fundamental safety precautions. Conventional cars, which depend entirely on human control and attention while in motion, frequently serve as the unfortunate setting for accidents in which human error is a major contributing factor. This project focuses on innovation, implementing systems on state-of-the-art technologies to solve real world problems. Another core system developed is object detection and frame annotation using the state-of-the-art computer vision model YOLOv8. This system takes raw video frames, and in real time is capable of detecting and annotating objects, outputting bounding boxes, labels, distance estimates, and safety warnings. This is a great road safety feature because it alerts the driver of what to stay out. The project is also critical to the integration of a rain detection system using rain sensor, Arduino microcontroller automatically activating wipers. It guarantees optimal visibility under adverse weather conditions and make it more convenient and safer. The system is made with fingerprint dependent unlocking systems coupled with an IoT enabled monitoring platform for security. With this system, not only is it ensured that only authorized users can access the vehicle, but should an invalid fingerprint attempt be made to use the vehicle, receive GPS location alerts as well. In addition, the vehicle comes with a blind spot alarming system and parking distance warning system. Infrared and ultrasonic sensors detect obstacles in the car’s blind spots and in proximity and provide real-time alerts to the driver to avoid collision. Finally, the project contains a detailed report on how strategies can help in increasing the speed and efficiency of solar powered vehicles so future research and development in this area can be laid down. This project shows how renewable energy combined with advanced technologies can be used to help address critical sustainable transportation challenges. This work integrates safety, security and energy efficiency features onto a solar powered vehicle and contributes to the creation of smarter, safer and a sustainable mobility solution. This report will enable readers to look at the different ways that these enhancements can make the ride safer, more energy efficient and more interactive with users. Ultimately this project hopes to create a more sustainable and interconnected future in the field of transportation.

heading: 2.1 Project Background
content: Since the addition of renewable energy and advance automation technology, the global transportation sector is experiencing a transformation. Solar-powered vehicles currently possess the potential to play a role in providing a sustainable means of decreasing the greenhouse gases produced by vehicles while dealing with the rising energy demands of the future. More than this, modern vehicles are combining features for safety and convenience that are intelligent and powered by IoT, machine learning and microcontroller systems. It consists of this review of latest developments in solar powered vehicle along with fingerprint door locking system, door fingerprint security system, GPS module for real time tracking and servo motors based automatic rain wipers. Microcontrollers like Arduino and ESP have a pivotal role in achieving all these functionalities which include processing sensor data, image recognition and so on and actuation. In addition, autonomous braking systems present a major step forward from typical sensor-based approach to systems based on image processing and computer vision. Though these modern approaches revolutionize efficiency and reliability, sensors remain indispensable in everything from rain detection to blind spot monitoring, and to so many other important systems. This review is extended further to include automatic rain wipers that are provided using servo motors that dynamically respond to precipitation in order to provide greater driver safety and comfort. In this review, we analyze the evolution of these technologies and their combined effects on vehicle automation together to illuminate research gaps and opportunities for future advances.

heading: 2.2 Automatic Braking
content: Automated systems in the automotive industry are intended to promote passenger safety, improve driver comfort, reduce traffic congestion and optimize energy efficiency. The goal of these technologies is to assist drivers by replicating human driving behavior, and overcome the problems of distractions, limited field of view, and delayed response time. Taking a top-down approach, the proposed system adjusts the intensity of braking proportionally to available stopping distance, ensuring that the vehicle can modulate speed for a successful stop and still provide a level of control to the driver during lane changes. Real time data on braking performance has been gathered on vehicles with sensors and then comprehensively tested on those vehicles. These tests characterize and analyze braking conditions through application of image processing techniques to characterize the pressure on the brake system and provide accurate automated assistance for driving under dynamic conditions [4].

heading: 2.2.1 Object Detection
content: Deep learning has propelled object detection that have been revolutionized over the past decade. Real-time object detection has seen the rise of YOLO (You Only Look Once) models, most recently YOLOv8, in recent years. Based on the convolutional neural networks (CNN’s), this model processes the video frames, and the objects are very accurately and quick detected[5]. Annotation of detected objects works on-the-fly with bounding boxes, labels, and distance estimates helping build situational awareness for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and assisted autonomous vehicles.

heading: 2.2.2 Innovations in YOLOv8
content: Additional improvements for detection accuracy and inference speed were gained by the YOLO(v8) based on its predecessors (e. g., YOLOv3, YOLOv4, and YOLOv5). The model makes use of a more efficient backbone architecture and features dynamic label assignment, which allows for training on real world datasets more efficiently. YOLOv8 is thus very well suited for such missions where reliable and fast object detection is necessary for safety — such as automatic braking [6]. Comparative Analysis with Previous Techniques However, ensuring both high accuracy and high speed of operation for object detection has remained an open problem since earlier models, including YOLOv3 and Faster RCNN, demonstrated that real-time object detection is possible. For example, Faster RCNN is very precise but has slower processing time and cannot be used in real time applications [7]. Instead, YOLOv3 compromised between speed and accuracy, but fell short in small object detection in difficult scenes [5]. Traffic rule violations by drivers are a significant global concern, particularly in urban areas, as they contribute to increasing traffic accidents. This study proposed a novel approach to identifying vehicles involved in such violations by building prediction models using image processing and machine learning techniques. The research focused on three key vehicle characteristics: type, colour, and brand. The study employed a transfer learning mechanism as the machine learning method to generate the prediction models. The results revealed that the YOLO V8 achieved the highest accuracy in predicting vehicle type and colour, with an accuracy of 98.9% and 93.2%, respectively. Comparatively, YOLO V7, V6, V5, V4, and V3 achieved lower accuracies. In terms of predicting vehicle brand, the YOLO V8 achieved an accuracy of 89.8%, surpassing the accuracies of the YOLO V7, V6, V5, V4, and V3. These findings demonstrated the potential of image processing and machine learning techniques in accurately identifying vehicles involved in traffic violations and highlighted the opportunity to develop effective strategies to reduce the number of traffic accidents caused by rule violations. This research has significant implications for enhancing road safety and promoting advanced technologies to address real-world problems [5]. These problems are tackled by YOLOv8 using state-of-the-art feature extraction methods to enhance the detection of both small and large objects in varied environments.

heading: 2.3 Security System
content: Modern vehicles have long been using secured systems to deal with the alarming situation of theft, unauthorized access and driver safety concerns. As urban vehicles are getting used at a rapid pace, video security solution such as physical locks and standalone alarms are not enough. IoT, sensors, and smart technologies have entered their advanced level and have integrated into advanced security systems for safety and convenience. These systems utilize IoT devices such as door-locking mechanisms equipped with IoT devices, used to remotely control and monitor vehicle access via the use of biometric authentication, or through mobile applications. The second important part of the safety package is blind spot detection systems, which increase safety by locating and warning drivers of vehicles or objects that are not within the view of normal mirrors. GPS tracking systems also assist with real time location tracking, preventing theft and locating a vehicle [8].

heading: 2.3.1 Door Locking Systems using IOT:
content: Yet, IoT-based door locking systems have revolutionized traditional security by introducing greater convenience, remote access as well as advanced user authentication via internet connectivity. These systems allow mobile app control, real time monitoring, and personalized access making them a more secure and easier to use. Vehicle door locks have evolved from mechanical locks using physical keys to state-of-the-art RFID and biometric based locks. A key fob with a chip that communicates with the vehicle when in range using RFID based systems will automatically unlock the doors, as biometric systems, like fingerprint or facial recognition have higher security, as they rely on unique biological traits. These modern systems are integrated with IoT and provide secure, user friendly and remotely manageable vehicle and home access control, which enhance vehicle and home security [9]. Biometric (Fingerprint) systems are chosen for door locking because of their higher security and the use of unique personal characteristics for unlocking. They have higher protection against unauthorized entry as compared to RFID, which is a requirement in secure environments. RFID systems use key fobs or cards to automatically unlock doors when within range, while fingerprint sensors provide access based on unique biometric traits. Both systems, when paired with IoT, enable remote management, allowing users to lock/unlock doors and receive notifications via mobile apps. This combination offers improved security, flexibility, and user convenience, making them ideal for modern access control solutions [9].

heading: 3.1 Conceptual Framework
content: This develops an intelligent vehicle safety system based on a fusion of advanced techniques, methodologies, and philosophies. Image processing and sensor-based automation are integrated into the system to achieve safer driving, less human error and greater convenience. The system is broken down in more detail below using the project objectives to guide it and discuss existing techniques and methodologies that relate to each function.

heading: 3.1.1 Image processing framework
content: In this system, advanced computer vision techniques, paired with robust object detection models form the image processing framework, providing precise real time analysis of video frames. Embedded underside perspective provides valuable objective information of surrounding, including object identification, distance estimation, and contextual annotations for environmental awareness and safety. This relies on use of the powerful combination of Python libraries [25]and algorithms to process and analyze the video data and annotate its contents.

heading: 1. Video Frame Extraction
content: OpenCV (cv2) is used to capture video frame by video frame and save each video frame as an image for sequential analysis. This step allows the pipeline to keep working on videos (rather than just frames) by keeping data frame integrity/configuration ensured, and synchronizing pipeline video states.

heading: 2. Object Detection With YOLOv8
content: I use the YOLO (You Only Look Once) model from the ultralytics library that allows to detect objects at high speed with high accuracy pay of frame. With its ability to classify objects and report them as bounding boxes along with confidence scores, the system is able to reliably identify possible hazards in real time.

heading: 3. Distance Estimation
content: We leverage YOLOv8 bounding box dimensions to perform distance estimation. The proximity of detected objects to the camera is estimated via a mathematical formula, based in the focal length, real-world object height, and bounding box height. The functionality is critical for the ability to issue "danger" warnings when objects are within unsafe distances.

heading: 4. Frame Annotatios and Warnings
content: Using OpenCV functions like cv2.rectangle and cv2.putText, annotated frames is generated. The annotations have to do with bounding boxes, labels, distance values and warnings in case of dangerous proximity. This is ensured by providing annotations so that the resulting processed frames provide actionable insights that increase awareness.

heading: 5. Logging ad Danger Flaming
content: All detection results are logged systematically where annotated objects that violate safety thresholds (i.e., vehicle pose within 4 meters) are flagged. This is a record of detections, as well as an auxiliary safety mechanism.

heading: 6. Output and Storage
content: Raw and annotated frames are saved in specific originated folders for raw and annotated images while having a log file that logs detailed detection data.

heading: 3.2 High Level Design
content: Its high-level design considers hardware, software and connectivity components interdependence to provide real time process as well as data accessibility.

heading: 1. Portability and Scalability
content: The system is built with a modular architecture that can be easily integrated into current vehicle models of any given make or model. The system's scalability means that the system can be used on high end vehicles as well as economy vehicles and little needed modification to the system is required. Its portability is enhanced by the usage of commonly used components similar as fingerprint sensor, IoT platform integration and GPS for alerts. The design of this provides a solution that can be applied to a wide variety of vehicles with its modularity and each module tailored to meet specific vehicle types and user requirements ensuring broad compatibility.

heading: 2. Customization and Adaptability
content: The safety system is designed so that each module of it is customizable enough to allow adaptation to different types of vehicles and users’ preferences. For example, the rain detection system can be calibrated so that wipers activate at different intensities of precipitation, allowing for a personalized experience for drivers. Similarly, the object detection system can be trained to detect a range of obstacles and hazards, given vehicle environment and purpose. The adaptability of the system makes it applicable to both the urban and rural driving grounds resulting in the utility of the same in diverse conditions

heading: 3. Reliability and Robustness
content: A system based on proven image processing algorithms and robust sensor systems is tested to meet reliability as one of the key targets. Based on real time object detection and automatic braking system is able to detect the obstacle and take proper safety actions with a high accuracy. The automatic wiper system and rain detection rightly demonstrate reliability, as it responds to wet weather conditions without manual input commanding wiper speeds to manoeuvre. IR sensors and ultrasonic technology is used by the blind spot detection system to ensure a clear and consistent alert in the most frustrating situations, boosting driver confidence and minimising risk.

heading: 4. Advanced Functionality with Reduced Complexity
content: It offers you safety system with simple design and operation while containing advanced features such as biometric security, IoT monitoring and GPS alerts in a single system. The car is protected through secure access by a fingerprintbased security system and integration with IoT allows real time monitoring and tracking. If there are any unauthorized access attempts, the IoT platform automatically delivers the GPS alerts, so you are immediately alerted of the potential threats. With user friendly features and unnecessary complexity removed the system remains easy to use, easy to use and easy to access with advanced security yet at the same time providing the convenience.

heading: 5. Seamless Integration and Ease of Adoption
content: The system design aims for seamless incorporation into existing vehicle systems with minimal hardware changes or expensive retrofits. Image processing, fingerprint-based security, IoT platform integration, and GPS alerts in the form of combined provide an individual an opportunity to install and use each module with much ease. The ease of adopting this technology is important to make advanced safety technology widely accessible to all market segments including drivers of new as well as older vehicle models.

heading: 6. Comprehensive Safety and Driver Support
content: With real time object detection, automated braking, blind spot detection, rain sensing and biometric security, this project brings a whole safety solution through which multiple layers of driving can be addressed. They all work together to help the driver, increasing situational awareness, reducing the probability of accidents and decreasing the brain load consequent to driving. The system seeks to perform with consistent performance across different driving environments, so as to provide drivers at all ability levels with a safe and confidence inspiring driving experience.

content: any other parameter Through some relevant performance parameters such as efficiency and sensitivity among others, the performance of the intelligent vehicle safety system is evaluated. These parameters help the analysis of the object detection, obstacle avoidance, rain detection, security and functionality of the system. The following outlines the key performance parameters and their calculation methods:

heading: 1. Efficiency
content: In this case, we refer to the efficiency of the system being able to identify and respond to real time driving situations, such as obstacle detection and object classification, with minimal computation resources. The efficiency of the system can be assessed based on the following:

heading: Frame Processing Rate:
content: The number of frames the system processes per second (or FPS). The speed of detecting objects from video streams  by the system is measured by this parameter. A better system efficiency is better shown by higher FPS values [27]. Computational Load = System  Resource Usage (cpu/gpu) / Total System Available

heading: Computational Load:
content: How much system computational resources the system, reports (e.g., CPU/GPU usage to perform object detection, object annotation, etc). Better efficiency is one where you use lower resource for the same level of performance.

heading: 2. Sensitivity
content: System sensitivity measures its capacity to understand and recognize what is around it, including objects, hazards and obstacles in the operational environment. Fps = Total Number of Frames Processed / Total time Taken for Processing True Positive Rate (TPR): Measure of the ratio of correctly detected objects (true positives) to all existing objects in the scene (true positives and false negatives). Its measurement shows the system’s ability to identify objects well. Object Detection Sensitivity This is for YAML configuration file, which measures the accuracy of system’s object detection module (using YOLOv8), which is to detect various objects such as vehicles, pedestrians and other obstacles in the frame. Rain Detection Sensitivity: This means it’s showing how well the rain detection system can spot different intensities of rain. Higher sensitivity True Positive Rate= True Positive / True Positive + False Negative means that the system reacts to very fine rain — the lightest of rain — and turns on the wipers when it should [28].

heading: 3. Precision and Recall
content: The performance of the system for detecting obstacles and other objects is measured with these two metrics to balance both true positives and false positives. Rain Detection Sensitivity = Detected Rain Events / Total Rain Events

heading: • Precision
content: Checks how many of the objects detected actually are correct. More precision means less false positives. Precision = True Positive / True Positive + False Positives

heading: • Recall
content: It measures [28] system's capability to correctly identify all possible objects in the scene. Fewer [missed] objects (false negatives) means a higher [recall]. Recall = True Positive / True Positive + False Positives

heading: 4. Specificity
content: Specificity represents the crystalline property of the system to correctly inform that no obstacles or hazards exist so that no false alarms or unnecessary interventions occur.

heading: • Specificity
content: True negative proportion (correct identification of safe space among all actual negatives (true negatives + false positives)). Specificity = True Positive / True Positive + False Positives

heading: 5. Overall Detection Accuracy
content: Overall detection accuracy metric is a measure of the total success rate of the system in correctly identifying all objects (obstacles, pedestrian, vehicles, etc.) and hazards in multiple frames across varying conditions.

heading: • Detection Accuracy
content: The proportion of correctly detected objects (true positives) to the total number of detected objects (true positives + false positives + false negatives). Detection Accuracy =     True Positive / True Positive +

heading: 6. False Alarm Rate
content: This parameter gives the false alarm rate of the system, i.e., determines the rate at which the system generates false alarms, e.g., misidentifying a non‐hazard as obstacle. We would like a lower false alarm rate.

heading: • False Alarm Rate
content: Ratio of the false positives (false hazard alerts) to all alerts the system issued. False Alarm Rate = False Positive / True Positive + False Positive

heading: 7. Security System Performance
content: Security system performance of a fingerprint-based system is evaluated based on the ability of the system to accept authorized users authenticates and deny unauthorized access. Moreover, the performance of IoT and GPS based alerts for unauthorized access attempts is measured.

heading: • Authentication Success Rate:
content: A fingerprint authentication, success/failure) out of total authentication attempts.

heading: • Unauthorized Access Alert Rate:
content: Total number of unauthorized access attempts, as a percentage of unauthorized access attempts which result in an IoT and GPS alert. heading: Components:

heading: Functionality:
content:  The camera continuously captures video footage from the environment.  The YOLOv8 deep learning model processes the frames in real time to detect and classify various objects.  Objects are annotated with bounding boxes and labels and if distance estimates or safety warnings are detected, do so.  This information is shown on a screen or via audible alerts, so the system improves the driver's situational awareness.  It also integrates with the braking system to let you avoid potential collision timely.

heading: Components:

heading: Functionality:

heading: 3.3.3 Software implementation on PC before implementation on Microcontroller
content: Image Processing Implementation on PC: • YOLOv8 Model: On the PC, the YOLOv8 model can be implemented using Python and TensorFlow/Keras. The model will be trained or fine-tuned on a dataset (such as COCO or custom dataset) to identify relevant objects such as pedestrians, vehicles, and other hazards. • Image Processing: OpenCV will be used for image pre-processing (resize, normalization, etc.) and post-processing (annotating frames with bounding boxes, labels, and safety warnings). • Object Detection Workflow: The PC will process video frames from the camera or a video stream. YOLOv8 will detect objects in real time, and annotations (bounding boxes, distance estimates) will be drawn on the frames. • Testing: The system's accuracy, object detection speed, and annotation accuracy can be evaluated on a variety of video inputs (such as simulation or real-time camera input). Once the PC version is working correctly, the code can be adapted for the microcontroller. The microcontroller will process input from the camera and handle object detection in real-time, but due to limited computing resources, it may require a lightweight version of the model or optimization techniques like TensorFlow Lite. Automatic Braking System Implementation on PC: • Obstacle Detection: Using the annotated video frames from the object detection system, depth estimation algorithms (like stereo vision or monocular depth estimation) will be implemented on the PC to determine the distance of obstacles [31]. • Braking Logic: The braking mechanism logic can be simulated on the PC. If an obstacle is detected within a certain distance threshold, the braking system will be activated (simulated with a software "brake" signal). • Communication: Simulate communication with a mock actuator (software simulation) to apply the brakes once an obstacle is detected. The microcontroller will simplify object detection and depth estimation, with optimized algorithms for real-time performance. The microcontroller will use data from the camera and other sensors to trigger the braking mechanism (via GPIO or other control signals). Rain Detection and Automatic Wiper Implementation on PC: • Sensor Simulation: Since IR and impedance sensors are hardware components, the rain detection logic can be simulated on the PC by using artificial sensor data. For example, a range of simulated rain intensities can be inputted, and the system should adjust wiper speeds accordingly. • Control Logic: Use the sensor input data to control wiper speed, and simulate the wiper motor response (in the form of a visual representation or log outputs). For the microcontroller implementation, the same logic will be applied, but the sensors' inputs will come directly from hardware components (IR or impedance sensors). The microcontroller will control the wiper motor based on real-time data from the sensors. Fingerprint-Based Security and IoT GPS Monitoring Implementation on PC: • Fingerprint Sensor Emulation: On the PC, you can simulate fingerprint scanning using a predefined database of fingerprint templates and a simulated scanner. For testing purposes, biometric data can be substituted with pre-stored sample data. • IoT Platform Integration: Implement the IoT communication protocols (MQTT or HTTP) using Python or other suitable libraries. This will allow for real-time alerts and communication between the system and a cloud or IoT server. • GPS Simulation: Use a simulated GPS location (hardcoded or from a GPS simulator) to send alerts via IoT if unauthorized access is detected. The microcontroller will interface with the actual fingerprint sensor and GPS module. The IoT communication can be handled by a Wi-Fi or GSM module (e.g., ESP8266, ESP32), and alerts will be sent via an IoT platform like MQTT. The fingerprint authentication will directly interact with the hardware. Blind Spot Detection and Parking Assistance  Implementation on PC: • Sensor Data Simulation: Since ultrasonic sensors and IR sensors are hardwarebased, simulate their data on the PC using predefined or randomly generated proximity data for blind spot detection and parking. • Detection Algorithm: Implement algorithms to calculate the distance to objects in blind spots and during parking maneuvers. The system can provide simulated alerts when obstacles are detected. • Audio Feedback Simulation: Simulate audio feedback or visual warning messages on the screen when an obstacle is detected. On the microcontroller, real sensors will be used to detect objects in the blind spot and provide real-time alerts via audible signals or visual indicators (LEDs, for instance). The system will be integrated with the vehicle's hardware setup.

heading: 1. Object Detection and Frame Annotation Using YOLOv8
content: The object detection subsystem processes video frames to identify obstacles and hazards in real time. The YOLOv8 model detect objects and outputs bounding boxes, labels, and confidence scores for each detected object.  Process: Video frames are captured and fed into the YOLOv8 model. Detected objects are annotated with bounding boxes and labels, and the system calculates the distance to obstacles using bounding box dimensions. Safety warnings are overlaid on the frames to assist the driver. The system is tested on a PC to ensure the YOLO model correctly identifies objects and produces annotated outputs with minimal latency.

heading: 2. Automatic Braking System
content: This subsystem leverages real-time video data to detect obstacles and initiate braking when necessary. It employs edge detection, object classification, and distance estimation algorithms.  Process: The video feed is analyzed to identify objects and measure their distance from the vehicle. If an object enters the pre-defined danger zone, the system triggers a braking signal.Simulated scenarios are used to test the object detection accuracy and the response of the braking mechanism to ensure reliable obstacle avoidance.

heading: 3. Rain Detection and Automatic Wiper Activation
content: This system uses rain sensors (IR and impedance-based) connected to an Arduino microcontroller to detect precipitation and adjust the wiper speed.  Process: The sensors measure water droplets or changes in impedance caused by rain. The Arduino processes the sensor data and adjusts the wiper speed accordingly. Various levels of water exposure are simulated to verify the system's ability to detect rain intensity and adjust wiper speeds without delay.

heading: 4. Fingerprint-Based Security System with IoT GPS Monitoring
content: This security system ensures vehicle access is restricted to authorized users through fingerprint recognition. IoT capabilities monitor access attempts and provide GPS alerts in case of unauthorized attempts.  Process: The fingerprint sensor captures and verifies a user’s biometric data against a stored database. Upon successful authentication, the system grants access. For unauthorized attempts, the IoT platform logs the event and sends GPS alerts to the owner’s device.The fingerprint sensor is tested for recognition accuracy and response time, while the IoT platform is validated for seamless logging and alert delivery during unauthorized attempts.

heading: 5. Blind Spot and Parking Distance Warning Systems
content: The blind spot detection system uses IR sensors to detect obstacles in areas not visible through mirrors, while the parking assistance system uses ultrasonic sensors to measure distances to nearby objects.  Process: The IR sensors scan blind spots and alert the driver when obstacles are detected. The ultrasonic sensors emit and receive sound waves to calculate distances, providing warnings during parking. The IR and ultrasonic sensors are calibrated and tested in controlled environments to ensure accurate detection and warning delivery.

heading:  Camera:
content: o Reason for Selection: Captures real-time video input from the vehicle's surroundings for YOLOv8 processing. o Chosen Component: A high-definition camera (e.g., 1080p webcam or dashcam) with wide-angle capability to cover a larger field of view. o Why this Component: It is cost-effective, readily available, and compatible with deep learning models.  YOLOv8 Software: o Reason for Selection: It is a state-of-the-art object detection model with superior speed and accuracy. o Why YOLOv8: It outperforms earlier versions (like YOLOv3) and other models (e.g., Faster R-CNN) in terms of real-time processing, making it ideal for safety-critical applications.

heading:  Arduino Microcontroller:
content: o Reason for Selection: Processes data from the rain sensor and adjusts the wiper speed. o Why Arduino: It is highly compatible with basic sensors and actuators, making it suitable for this application.  DC Motor with Wiper Mechanism: o Reason for Selection: Powers the wipers to clear the windshield. o Why this Component: A cost-effective solution that supports variable speed control based on microcontroller input.

heading: 4. Fingerprint-Based Security System with IoT GPS Monitoring
content: Components and Selection Justification:  Fingerprint Sensor (e.g., R305): o Reason for Selection: Provides secure biometric access to the vehicle. o Why this Component: It is affordable, reliable, and easy to integrate with microcontrollers.  Microcontroller (e.g., ESP32): o Reason for Selection: Processes fingerprint data, manages IoT functions, and communicates with GPS. o Why ESP32: It combines low power consumption with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities, making it ideal for IoT applications.  GPS Module: o Reason for Selection: Tracks vehicle location during unauthorized access attempts. o Why this Component: Modules like NEO-6M are cost-effective, accurate, and widely used for GPS tracking.  IoT Platform (e.g., Firebase): o Reason for Selection: Logs access attempts and sends real-time alerts. o Why Firebase: It is reliable, scalable, and offers free-tier plans for small- scale projects.

heading: 4. Conclusion
content: The creation of this project shows a thorough strategy for improving vehicle security, driver support, and road safety while fostering accessibility and cost. In order to ensure driver awareness and obstacle avoidance, the project reaches a major milestone by using state-of-the-art technologies like YOLOv8 for real-time object identification and frame annotation. This is further enhanced by the automated braking system, which uses sensor integration and image processing methods to proactively avoid crashes. By automating wiper controls to lessen driver workload and increase safety, the rain detection and automatic wiper activation module tackles vision issues during inclement weather. In addition to offering real-time location alerts for improved vehicle security, the fingerprint-based security system with IoT GPS monitoring adds  biometric verification to prevent unwanted access. By employing infrared and ultrasonic sensors to identify obstructions and alert drivers, blind spot detection and parking assistance systems improve situational awareness in situations that are typically difficult. These characteristics enable drivers to confidently maneuver through confined spaces and steer clear of possible hazards. In order to maximize the speed and energy efficiency of solar-powered cars, the project also involves conceptual research, which will provide important information for future sustainable transportation options. All things considered, this project effectively combines cutting-edge technologies with useful applications, accomplishing its goals of efficiency, security, and safety. It bridges the gap between high-end automotive advances and mass-market accessibility thanks to its modular construction, cost-effective components, and scalable design. This work lays the groundwork for future developments in the sector and marks a major advancement in intelligent vehicle safety systems.

heading: Abstract
content: As every domain around us is getting upgraded daily whereas some essential domains are losing the race due to less attention. One of them is the education sector and most importantly their management. So metimes it becomes tedious to handle a heap of students in the (SSC) Student Service Centre. With the artificial intelligence we can deal with this problem, introducing intelligent machines that could work alongside humans can increase the efficiency of wo rkplace. IHSAS is a step towards making the life easier for students and their manageme nt where we are developing  Bio Inspired Socio Cognitive Assistive Agent  that would work alongside humans in a student service centre and capable of listening, understand ing and adequately answering the problems of students within the territory of a university and online as well. Making a machine, intelligent enough to provide a whole Student Service Centre into a virtual humanlike bot, is our purpose. IHSAS would be intel ligent enough to answer the queries by students and learn with its experiences in real time. Having a 3D virtual face on a tablet mounted on a human mannequin  with a printer and movement circuitry attached to it, that can interact with students by talking and some gestures, and respond within seconds would provide ease, time saving and resource saving. heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: This study aims to propose a social cognitive robot for a  SSC-Office (Student Service Centre) to serve as an assistant. The design of this agent required the utilization of concepts, tools and techniques from various domains. Therefore, literature review is interdisciplinary. The main objective of the research in robotics and cognitive artificial intelligence is to make computationally equivalent human -like mind. Broadly speaking, cognitive computing is defined as the simulation of human manners of thinking in an automated model. The corresponding relationship between cognitive science and robotics defines the characteristics of cognitive robotics research, which focuses on giving robots with advanced cognitive abilities in order to observe, reason, and behave separately in a similar intelligent manner to humans A cognitive agent that ch ooses actions to be performed based on complex processing which simulates various mental functionalities at a certain level in order to general insight, cognition and reactions under regulation of cognitive cycle(s) [3]. Cognitive architectures [4] are used in the construction of cognitive artificial systems which can perform cognitive activities like knowledge organization, attention, learning, reasoning etc. The problem in cognitively inspired arti ficial systems is concept representation for this we have theoretical and computational cognitive sciences [5]. As cognitive tasks involve different brain activities and neural impulses so it is important to describe the conceptual information representation. Moreover, for the concept representations the proxy type theory of concepts [6] can be combine with heterogeneity approach [7] [5]. In this regard BICA [8] is very important to create humanoid cognitive agents that serve the humans , reduce their  burden, solve complex problems and will be acknowledged as a member of a society. The cognitive agents are modelled with certain level of independence which allows the agent to take senso ry input from its environment and try to assign meanings to it; this is called perception phase. After assigning meaning it tries to understand the perception. The analysis and understanding of perception allows the agent to decide what actions are there t o be performed. This process includes complex cyclic processes based on current goals. By design these agents can be self -regulated by the agent itself [11], [1]. Consider the perception of differen t colours in different agents. The nervous system of an agent constructs the sense of colour on the basis of cone classes [3]. The modules involved in cognition process are memory, attention etc. After perception, Attention is the next phase which acts as a filter of the perceived information. External or perceptual attention selects and modulates information incoming from various senses and internal attention modulates internally generated information, such as the contents of w orking memory or a set of possible behaviours in a given context. The episodic memory provides information based on past experiences and events, to the rest of cognition. The Attention codeless interacts with the episodic memory to recall episodes of simil ar perception and also encodes new patterns. Memory is an essential part of any systems -level cognitive model, regardless of whether the model is being used for studying the human mind or for solving engineering problems. Similarly, perception is evolved a fter every cycle of similar episode, known as perceptual learning. On contrast, procedural memory is the memory of actions and behaviours of a system; it stores the procedures of learning behaviour. Cognitive agents always either learn new behaviours or im prove and evolve old ones. This procedural learning is defined as non -declarative memory, which refers to “how to” kind of information. It is a set of internal processes that changes the capability of the way to respond to sensory inputs on the basis of pa st experience and practices. Perception, procedural learning, and episodic learning are based on association of things. An object is associated with its features and categorization in perceptual

Therefore, attention also reinforces the procedural learning at every cycle. This reinforcement may be a result of positive or negative effe ct of the behaviour and performance [3]. heading: 3.4.2.1 Input
content: First a user comes to the interface and either inputs in the form of a text or speech. If the input method is the speech, then the speech first converted to text and then goes for further processing. IBM Watson’s speech to text API is used for this purpose.

heading: 3.4.2.2 WORDNET
content: After the input is converted into text it is checked for the keywords like ‘bus challan’, ‘course registration’, ‘course drop’. WORDNET NoSql database has collection of all English language words and their synonyms. These keywords are linked to their synonyms so no matter user enters the text in what every form, bot will be able to recognize the keyword.

heading: 3.4.2.3 C# Functions
content: If a keyword matches, there are certain C# functions will be executed. For instance, if the keyword of ‘bus challan’ matches, the function for bus challan printing will execute. S ame goes with the course add/drop and other functionalities.

heading: 3.4.2.4 AI BOT
content: If the keyword does not match it means it’s a ‘general query’, for some textual information is been required e.g. information about university. For the bot AIML language is used.  AIML stands for artificial intelligence markup language and is used to create conversational systems using natural language based knowledge representation based as discussed earlier in above section. Aiml possess the following pros.  Simple to program  easy to understand  highly maintainable Knowledge base in AIML is further consists of following tags.

heading: Basic:
content:  <aiml>: this tag defines the beginning of AIML file.  <category>: it is a basic knowledge unit contains for input and output response along with optional context  <pattern>: here we define the pattern/question which user may ask.  <template>: it contains the response against the user queries.

heading: 52 of 73  22 May 2018
content:  <srai>:  It is used for 4 main reasons (i) Symbolic Reduction: It reduces the complex grammatical patterns into simpler ones. (ii)  Divide and Conquer: Sentences are reduced into sub -sentences and formed a common reply. (iii) Synonyms resolution: Helps the bot to reply in identical manner for similar words. (iv) Keywords Detection: Helps to reply a standard reply whenever that specific keyword occurred.

heading: CONTEXT:
content:  <that>: it is used to respond according to context. *One thing should be kept in mind while using this tag i.e. everything placed within the tag must be in capital alphabets.

heading: General:
content: : It is used to capture the wildcard character. : It allows the chatbot to respond differently to a same question. : It is used to store the value of variable. and : Used to set and get the value of variable respectively. All the above mentioned tags has been used in developing the chatbot for iHSAS For making knowledge base in AIML simply open a notepad, add knowledge in the file by using the above discussed tags and saved the file by (.aiml) extension. heading: 5.1 Problems Faced
content: The major problem faced so far is that it requires a large number of data set in order to work properly. No doubt it works fine on limited dataset  but in future when it would be implemented on large databases of big universities like COMSATS then its performance can be a question for which it also requires huge computing resources. The difficulty of the task depends upon the functiona lity of the project the more we ask the more it takes to do. It depends upon our quest how deep we want to go with this project. We are not going for our own natural language processing module where as we are using off the shelf module for this purpose whi ch till now is working fine and if we make our own, that would require extra time and resources. The face morphing and lip synching are also off the shelf modules where as our major focus is on the functionality of the brain of iHSAS.

heading: 5.2 Lessons Learned
content: There were so many lessons in the journey of this project. Working first time with artificial intelligence was itself quit challenging and interesting. As this field is very immature and every project needs out of the box approaches and immense hard work. The approach for this project was not used before in artificial intelligence world as it covers a lot of different integral parts and combines in a project. All these parts are completely different domains in themselves but combining them into a project like this is really a piece of art. In the beginning we thought to go with the deep learning and implement neural networks with the project for its adaptive behaviour but it came to the knowledge down the road that it requires large realistic datasets to tra in the model and large computing resources also require to process that information in real time.

heading: 5.3 Project Summary
content: By the advancement in the fields like Artificial Intelligence and machine learning, the development of abovementioned robots/agents is now possible because the machines are made capable to solve issues on their own, through learning and interacting with th e environment. The literature review abovementioned motivated the construction of such a cognitive agent that will engage with students in social interaction; thereby leading towards kindlier and more agreeable student relationship. It will recognize people by their name, record their preferences by analysing their previous data maintained in the database. This agent will provide relevant information of students with different natures , it can  answer the queries of the s tudents, through social interaction.  This agent would be able to do complex tasks like add/drop courses and many more. This project can revolutionize the management of a university and the course of managerial actions can be changed. Once trained properly it can mitigate the need of manpower in a student services centre.

heading: 5.4 Future Work
content: Future developments that we intend to add into this project are as following: The architecture represents the complete cognition process in virtual agents, which can be accomplished. It is complex to complete it at once; this is one reason why it is broken down into separate modules. The robot being developed will move manually, it will not have navigation or map construction. Therefore, in the future it can have a human like body that would allow it to work on these walking modules. This robot can be extended to various proposes depending upon the dataset provided it can be trained on different grounds. In the future we are looking forward to create different and large dataset to implement learning process in the robot. Also, this robot would solely be focused on the student’s services and interaction with the students and try to solve their queries however the emotion  and gesture recognition will be handled in future.

heading: 2.3.2.7 Glossary
content: Clinix: A system designed to provide ease to doctors as well as to patients to automate the manual system of Appointments and Meditation by the doctors to patients. Patient: A person who is not feeling well as wanted to see a doctor or a person who is conscious about his/her health and visits for regular checkup. Doctor: The specialist to deal with Patient’s diseases. Receipt: The print out of the total bill of the treatment. Admin: A person who can control the Patient appointments as well as Doctor’s schedules. Treatment: Any curing of the disease will be Treatment. Virtual Appointment: Appointment by video calling between doctor and Patient.

heading: Software Development Life Cycle Model
content: The software development process model that we plan on using for the development of this application is the agile model. The agile model is a blend of iterative and gradual process models. In the coordinated model working item is conveyed after every emphas is; this is the essential explanation for picking this model. It is additionally most appropriate in light of the fact that it will be generally speedy and as we have time imperatives to complete this undertaking we might want to have working rendition accessible. By utilizing this model we would build up our application in stages with each working form having a bigger number of highlights than the past one. This would to a great extent decline the multifaceted nature of the task and after every emphasis we would have the capacity to get input from client on any conceivable inadequacies which we would then have the capacity to enhance in the following cycle. By doing this the item that we would get at our last emphasis would be one that would have every one of the highlights at first got ready for and any varieties that would emerge while getting criticism from clients. Because of the way that we will be getting working forms after each emphasis it safeguards that at no time in time would we be totally clear or have nothing to appear for our endeavors. As we are building up an application it is most extreme significance to make it profoundly accessible as feasible for client else they would have numerous different alternatives to browse as opposed to our application so a consistent input from them would help us in accomplishing this.

heading: Abstract
content: Digital devices such as desktop computers, laptops and mobiles have become an essential pa rt of our lives. With the boom of the digital devices everyone is spending a lot of  time on computers that can cause serious strain on body parts. Staring at computer screens for hours has bec ome essential requirement for most of the jobs. Jobs require people to continuously int eract with the computer screen for at least 5 hours a day [1]. Some of the offices take care about  computer ergonomics (science of designing a job, workspace or equipment to fit the worker [2]) but most of the employers and employees are unaware about it. The usage of these devices without prope r orientation of body can lead to eye, backbone, and neck and head strain. The users are unaware of the side effects such as musculoskeletal problems, obesity, vision problems and stress di sorders that long term usage of these devices are causing on our body. This can be avoided by sitting in a correct posture and practicing exercises for eyes and back at regular intervals. Our project aims at monitoring the user ’s posture, eye and neck strain. The user will be shown exercises and tips to practice at regular intervals. The software will keep a record of the statistics of the user ’s posture that will be shown in the form of charts. heading: 2.1.8 Technologies for Monitoring Students Body Posture and Physiological
1 Introduction
content: Good posture helps to do everyday tasks with more energy, less strain and fatigue. It helps to reduce chances of obesity, diabetes, heart, breathing and digestion problems. In the present era, usag e of computers has increased dynamically which is giving rise to computer vision and digital strain issues. The eye problems due to computer usage fall under computer vision syndrome (CVS). While u sing computer the eye muscles have to continuously focus and refocus. Moreover screen adds flicker, glar e and contrast that require more effort from eye muscles. It makes the eyes dried, r ed and causes blurred or double vision. Major symptoms of CVS are shown in the figure below:

heading: Figure 1 Computer Vision Syndrome
content: The neck and shoulder strain is caused due to forward head and shoulder posture as shown in fi g 1. According to [1] when the head is 3 inches forward from the neck the spine receiv es 30 times more weight of the head. The poor neck and head posture leads to kyphotic posture that is excessi ve forward curvature of the spinal cord. This happens due to dropping shoulders and tensed back. Figure 2 ErikDalton, Forward Head Posture and the 42 Pound Head. There is a separate field of study named computer ergonomics that deals with the post ure and orientation of body to reduce body strain. The user is prone to develop bad posture and eye strain issues wi th regular usage of computers. The application targets to remind the user to correct his posture whene ver he is slouching and recommend exercises to overcome eye and back stress. Page 12 of 52  14 May 2018

heading: 1.1 Objectives
content: Our aim is develop a software that would be performing the following tasks:  The software will monitor user’s posture.  It will check user’s dizziness and eye strain by tracking eye movement and eye blinking rate.  The software will give reminders for posture and usage.  It will generate charts for average time spent on work and exercise that wi ll help user to assess working patterns.  It will check distance of user from the computer screen and prompt whenever di stance is too short.  The software will prompt for exercises, provide tips and facts, when required.

heading: 1.2 Problem Statement
content: The usage of computers has reduced the time people used to spend on exercising, playi ng etc. This has increased the risk of various health related problems that are being induced slowly  in our living patterns. The motivation of this project is to minimize the risks associated with comput er usage. According to [3] slouching causes the muscles to bear more burden to keep spine stabilized and prote cted. This effects in changing the curvature of the spine and destroys posture. We plan to develop an environment w here the user can work and know when to relax. This will enable the user to work effect ively and maintain a healthy lifestyle at the same time.

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: The applications that are currently available are:

heading: 2.1.1 MacBreakZ
content: MacBreakZ, a desktop application developed for Mac OS and works only for posture bui lding and recovery from poor posture, as mentioned in [4]. It works by providing break r eminders at intervals fixed by the user. In the break, application provides simple stretches and exercises. The app lication does not monitors if the user is actually following the exercises or sitting in correct posture.

heading: 2.1.2 Posture Man Pat
content: Posture Man Pat is another Mac OS application that uses accelerometer of the mobile phone as in [4]. It only gives alert when the Y-axis of webcam is below the defined target. It dim s the screen and a small window is shown to user. The application only works to correct the neck positio n.   There are wearables available too that get synchronized with mobile apps. The wearables can either use m ultiple cameras or accelerometers to check posture. Cameras are expensive and not applicable in daily l ives but accelerometers are small as compared to cameras and quite cost-effective.

heading: 2.1.3 LumoBack
content: LumoBack is a small wearable device that is worn near collarbone. It uses a single acce lerometer embedded in belt to correct slouching posture. It slightly vibrates whenever you slouch. The data is transferred to a mobile application via Bluetooth that shows statistics and allows cus tomization. The idea proposed in paper [5] uses 6 accelerometers placed on lower back, chest, right  and left thighs, right and left leg. The sensors send data to mobile application via Bluetooth which per forms calculations. It can distinguish between 4 postures i.e. sitting with bent knees, standing, lying fac e up and sitting with legs laid straight.

heading: 2.1.4 Zikto Walk
content: Zikto Walk is another device that contains a gyroscope and accelerometer to monitor walking patterns [6]. The mobile centric sensing as in [7] uses built-in sensor in mobile phones such as a ccelerometer, gyroscope etc. The computations are performed using the capabilities of the mobile and no external storage is used. The drawback is that a single accelerometer cannot clearly dis tinguish between standing and sitting. The mobile centric applications require mobile to be placed near the waist for best results. The paper [8] presents an idea of wearable vest that contains accelerometers at di fferent places. The idea is to make elderly people wear the vest and enjoy life without the need of car etakers. The idea is efficient as compared to tele-surveillance and continuous monitoring by a person. Similarly the sol ution presented in [9] uses a pressure sensing mattress. The mattress is used to check whether the patient is lying in correct position and comfortable. The mattress send the data to computer workstation which evaluates the results. It alerts the related hospital staff whenever the patient ’s posture is incorrect. These solutions widely depend upon the external hardware resources for computations and storage. The major disadvantag e is low availability of the wearables.

heading: 2.1.5 BeUpright
content: BeUpright [10] is a mobile application to benefit targeting the users retain the precise sitting posture. BeUpright senses two kinds of bad sitting postures which are leaning backward and leani ng forward. In order to sense the position of a user BeUpright works on a slight sensor Bluetoot h wireless. The sensor is worn on the user ’s shirt with the help of magnet. When the connection is built in between the sensor and Page 15 of 52  14 May 2018 the application, BeUpright starts monitoring. And when the user has bad position for mor e than 20 seconds, BeUpright gives an alert. After receiving the alert if the user doe s not alter the posture within 10 seconds, BeUpright locks the mobile of the user’s helper. 2.1.6 A Surveillance System Designed for the Correction of Sitting Posture in Writing A right sitting position for writing can be described with one of t he most significant aspects is the distance D calculated from head to desk-plane. The systems proposed early only make the user atten tive when his head is much closer to the pen but the proposed system moreover alerts the user when his head is far-off from the pen. This development can defend the user from sitting in the  improper positions such as bending over the desk, head tilt etc. The proposed system consequently digitizes the production voltage of the sensor and inputs the data to a programmable regulator to check whether the D is in the safe series or not. Subsequently, the proposed system is composed of an infrared signal sensor, a prog rammable controller, an alert device, and a touch-switch [11].

heading: 2.1.7 Recognizing Posture in Pictures with Successive Convexification and Linear Programming
content: The approach presented in [12] made a posture detection technique grounded on local imag e structures and successive convexification image matching. Image matching built on successive convexif ication functions is exact contrarily to the earlier approaches for example graph cut , belief propagation, iterative conditional modes (ICM), relaxation labeling, and additional convex programming-based opt imization systems. The system denotes target points for each pattern point with a small basis set. Successive convexification slowly makes the trust region for each template site small er and alters the original difficult problem into an arrangement of easy and simpler convex programs. This hurries up the searching process, creating the technique suitable for large-scale matching and posture-recognition difficulties.

heading: Learning
content: Real Automóvil Club de España (RACE) has done research according to which 30% of tra ffic mishaps occur due to drivers ’ exhaustion. It is possible to recognize from visual structures (actions, eye sig ht) or physical constraints (heartbeat, brain actions and pulse). If we can measure the dr iver’s situation each second and practice that statistics in the car embedded system then it is possible to build a driver assistant system that will decrease the road accidents. The symbols of tiredness look are: degree of eyelid opening, person's head place and blinking frequency of eyes. This system comprises of two core devices. One of which converts information from analog to digital. The other one gathers and m odifies the information received, and directs it to the processing center. The central part of the system is the capability to evaluate and manages the symbols of driver tiredness in the real time. The system interferes in the form of alarm or signal and make driver attentive. Previously exists technologies for noticing persons with their features (hands,  foots, head, eyes). These are some options for detecting humans: • Approaches for identifying persons using video. • Using keyboard or mouse for tracing information. • Sensors embedded on the body or seat. Context Aware Posture Recognition in Offices (CAPRIO) is a system which build s a smart monitoring system. That is for worker postures in office location. They used sensors which are embedded in the seats of workers. They uses pressure sensors and set them in back pane. With the help of these sensors it can be clear if the worker is sitting in correct posture or not. Research is being  done to develop more effective systems. heading: 3.4.2 Description
content: In pipe and filter style, each filter has a set of inputs and outputs. The connectors  are pipes which take output of one filter and pass it as input to next filter. The architecture follows sequential flow of information. Source filters produce only output and sink filters only have inputs. The pipe and filter architecture is the most widely used architecture for computer  vision applications. The video stream acts as data source as it produces data that is passed t o filter. The posture detector filters the data stream and passes the results to next filter i .e. statistics generator. This filter passes its outputs to sink as input. The data sink stores the overall results generated by the system.

heading: 5.1 Conclusion
content: “FitAssist” will be a trend maker if published with all the goals and objective as mentioned. Despite of the fact that there are already many running fitness gadgets and applications doing  a massive business, “FitAssist” with the help of its compact size and features will provide ease to user, wher e the people would find it more attractive and comfortable to keep themselves fit while working. This methodology has been wanted since ever by the people who have more interaction with computers and want to be fit at the same time. The basic purpose of our project was to develop a system that would monitor th e posture of user while he is working on computer. The application regularly alerts user about his posture, blink rate and usage limits. Wherever any of these measures are out of threshold values, the syst em alerts the user. This continuously reminds user to sit in correct posture and take regular breaks from work. Consequently, it helps computer user to know more about his activities while he is working and improv e them over time.

heading: 5.2 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: Developing “FitAssist” was a big decision made by all of us. Though we were aware of how complex it could be to develop a system capturing real time posture of user. At first , the plan and the idea we initiated with was that the basic purpose distinguishing our system would be to  develop a system that will work using webcam of the user ’s system. The idea was to use the webcam to monitor user continuously. All the processing would be done in user’s system. But after making too many searches and studying the related researches, we came to a conc lusion that it is far more complex to do this task using a simple webcam. Therefore we thought t o use external webcam with a better resolution. The continuous processing of user ’s computer for monitoring would cause high battery strain so we decided to make it as a standalone device. We then planned to use Raspberry pi 3 for making a standalone posture monitoring  device. It could help to reduce battery consumption of user ’s system. We planned to make it an interactive and attractive device for user. A standalone device would not had been much feasible for every computer user as it cost s around Rs.10, 000 to build a single unit. We decided to build a system tray application for desk top as well. The functionality in the desktop and raspberry pi module are almost same. We planned to use the desktop version for analysing the accuracy of our system. We had planned to use simple text files to store user ’s settings and statistics. This approach was making data retrieval slower as we had to parse sequentially through the whole f ile every time something was needed. We then planned to shift to a JSON database called tinyDB. It provided us a small database that we could use to store data in a well-structured manner. This reduced data retrieval and updating time to quite extent. We had some issues implementing the activity monitoring module. The purpose of thi s module was to find the applications that the user was using and then check stress according to the  type of application. We searched for a 3 rd party application that could extract the applications being used. Finally we were able to find an application that could extract application information as we wanted. In going through all of these methodologies, we came to learn about python, im age processing, OpenCV, Dlib, activeTCL and tinyDB databases. We got to know about the tools l ike pyCharm, CMake, and Visio. In order to transfer files between laptop and raspberry pi, we learnt about command line application pscp and PuTTY (terminal emulator for file transfer) .The k nowledge of using these tools would make us develop, complete, and enhance our application to even wider environment.

heading: 5.3 Project summary
content: “FitAssist” is an innovative project that would be a big introduction to the ergonomics mar ketplace. The project has been developed with the help of 2 people. The design, the interface, t he backend programming, all of this has been done with the effort of the 2 group mat es. It took different tools to develop the application. And not only the tools but the techniques, algorithms and the methodol ogies in developing this application are in a good count of number. Despite of facing many pr oblems in developing this project, we still have managed developing a unique product in the mark et of ergonomics. But with time, this product would further grow and attract the computer users.

heading: 5.4 Future work
content: The future work includes adding more features to the posture monitoring device . The application can be extended to give alerts for water intake. Posture monitoring can be improved by using 3D head pose estimation techniques for better analysis. The application can be extended to detect user facial expressions and emotions to predict stress and fatigue. We can develop a mobile application that can show posture related notifications and  reminders on user’s mobile.
