heading: 2.2.3 Comparative Analysis with Previous Techniques
content: However, ensuring both high accuracy and high speed of operation for obje ct detection has remained an open problem since earlier models, including YOLOv3 and Faster  RCNN, demonstrated that real -time object detection is possible. For example, Faster RCNN is very precise but has slower processing time and cannot be used in real time applications [7]. Instead, YOLOv3 compromised between speed and accuracy, but fell short in small object detection in difficult scenes [5].  Traffic rule violations by drivers are  a significant global concern, particularly in urban areas, as they contr ibute to increasing traffic  accidents. This study proposed a  novel approach to identifying vehicles involved in such violations by building prediction models using image processing and machine learning techniques. We were aimed to figure out to which extent we could correctly guess the type of car, its color, and brand and we chose to use a transfer learning framework with Yolo V8 as a machine learning backbone. Upon carrying out the experiments, we noticed that YOLO V8 achieved 98.9 % accuracy in guessing the type of the vehicle and 93.2 % accuracy on guessing vehicle color.  Comparatively, YOLO V7, V6, V5, V4, and V3 achieved lower accuracies. Regarding determining which car is on the road, the accuracy percentage of YOLO V8 was 89.8%. It is more than all the YOLO V7, V6, V5, V4, and V3 truth tables we have witnessed so far. This implies that image processing and machine learning solutions are quite useful in terms of revealing the vehicles that provoke traffic offences, and it makes room to wiser approaches that would reduce the amount of accidents caused by the rule breakers. Anyone interested in increasing road safety would care about this work using YOLOv8 because it demonstrates the effectiveness of current feature extraction when it comes to detecting tiny and large objects in virtually any environment.

heading: 2.3 Security System
content: Since the invention of the first vehicle all the way down the first automobiles produced off the assembly lines, designers and engineers have been working day and night to ensure they are secure. A modern car has been developed to use a combination of defenses to prevent theft attempts, unauthorized access, and ensure the safety of a driver.  As urban vehicles are getting  used at a rapid pace, video security solution such as physical locks a nd standalone alarms are not enough. IoT, sensors, and smart technologies have entered their advanced level and have integrated into advanced security systems for safety and convenience. These systems utilize IoT devices such as door -locking mechanisms equipped with IoT devices, used to remotely control and monitor vehicle access via the use of biometric authentication, or through mobile applications. The second important part of the safety package is blind spot detection systems, which increase safety by locating and warning drivers of vehicles or objects that are not within the view of normal mirrors. GPS tracking systems also assist with real time location tracking, preventing theft and locating a vehicle [8].

heading: 2.3.1 Door Locking Systems using IOT:
content: Yet, IoT -based door locking systems have revolutionized traditional security by introducing greater convenience, remote access as well as advanced user authentication  via internet connectivity. These systems allow mobile app control, real time monitoring, and personali zed access making them a more secure and easier to use.  Vehicle door locks have evolved from mechanical locks using physical keys to state-of-the-art RFID and biometric based locks. A key fob with a chip that communicates with the vehicle when in range using RFID based systems will automatically unlock the doors, as biometric systems, like fingerprint or facial recognition have higher security, as they rely on unique biological traits. These modern systems are integrated with IoT and provide secure, user friendly and remotely manageable vehicle and home access control, which enhance  vehicle and home security [9]. Biometric (Fingerprint) systems are chosen for door locking because of their higher security and the use of unique personal characteristics for unlocking. They have higher protection against unauthorized entry as compared to RFID, which is a requirement in secure environments. heading: 3.2 Conceptual Framework
content: This develops an intelligent vehicle safety system based on a fusion of advanced techniques, methodologies, and philosophies. Image processing and sensor-based automation are integrated into the system to achieve safer driving, less human error and greater convenience. The system is broken down in more detail below using the project objectives to guide it and discuss existing techniques and methodologies that relate to each function.

heading: 3.2.1 Image processing framework
content: In this system, advanced computer vision techniques, paired with robust object detection models form the image processing framework, providing precise real time analysis of video frames. Embedded underside perspective provides valuable objective information of surrounding, including object identification, distance estimation, and contextual annotations for environmental awareness and safety. This relies on use of the powerful combination of Python libraries [25]and algorithms to process and analyze the video data and annotate its contents.

heading: 3.2.1.1 Video Frame Extraction
content: OpenCV (cv2) is used to capture video frame by video frame and save each video frame as an image for sequential analysis. This step allows the pipeline to keep working on videos (rather than just frames) by keeping data frame integrity/configuration ensured, and synchronizing pipeline video states.

heading: 3.2.1.2 Object Detection With YOLOv8
content: I use the YOLO (You Only Look Once) model from the ultralytics library that allows to detect objects at high speed with high accuracy pay of frame. With its ability to classify objects and report them as bounding boxes along with confidence scores, the system is able to reliably identify possible hazards in real time.

heading: 3.2.1.3 Distance Estimation
content: We leverage YOLOv8 bounding box dimensions to perform distance estimation. The proximity of detected objects to the camera is estimated via a mathematical formula, based in the focal length, real-world object height, and bounding box height. The functionality is critical for the ability to issue "danger" warnings when objects are within unsafe distances.

heading: 3.2.1.4 Frame Annotations and Warnings
content: Using OpenCV functions like cv2.rectangle and cv2.putText, annotated frames is generated.  The annotations have to do with bounding boxes,  labels, distance values and warnings in case of dangerous proximity. This is ensured by providing annotations so that the resulting processed fram es provide actionable insights that increase awareness.

heading: 3.2.1.5 Logging ad Danger Flaming
content: All detection results are logged systematically where annotated objects that violate safety thresholds (i.e., vehicle pose within 4 meters) are flagged. This is a record  of detections, as well as an auxiliary safety mechanism.

heading: 3.2.1.6 Output and Storage
content: Raw and annotated frames are saved in specific originated folders for raw and annotated images while having a log file that logs detailed detection data.

heading: 3.2.2 Automatic Braking System
content: An automatic braking system leverages image processing and sensor-based automation to avoid a collision. The vehicle’s surroundings are captured by cameras, and algorithms analyzing the video feed detects obstacles. The distance estimation techniques, depth perception, defines the distance of objects. The braking system turns on autonomously when an obstacle is within certain safety threshold. It also gives us real time responsiveness, which helps with safety among other things, especially in emergency cases. Figure 7:: Output warnings from object detection

content: The rain detection and wiper activation module detect the amount of the rain to guarantee The  detected precipitation on the windshield is the best visibility in adverse weather conditions.

heading: 3.2.4 Rfid-Based Security System with IoT  Monitoring
content: In our case, we have a Rfid-based security system such that the vehicle can only be unlocked and operated by authorized users. This system sorts out IoT technology for logging access attempt alert  in case of unauthorized access. It is  this dual layer of security which ensures high level of protection against theft and real time monitoring gives added level of protection.

heading: 3.2.5 Blind Spot and Parking Distance Warning Systems
content: This blind spot detection system makes use of IR sensors to detect obstacles in regions which are not visible through normal mirrors. heading: 3.4 Sub system design
content: The intelligent vehicle safety system is composed by a few subsystems, with the purpose of resolving each specific functionality which contributes to increase vehicle safety, the automation and providing convenience to the driver.

heading: 3.4.1.1 Real-Time Object Detection and Frame Annotation Subsystem Components:
content:  Camera: Records live video feed of the surroundings surrounding the vehicle.  YOLOv8 Model (Deep Learning Model): Its a state-of-the-art object detection model what reads video frames, detects objects like pedestrians, vehicles, and other obstacles.  GPU/CPU: Used for running the YOLOv8 model and performing the computational tasks involved in object detection and annotation.  Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino/Raspberry Pi): Camera interfaces to processing unit handle system control and task management as well as data flow.  Display Unit (Optional): Annotates frames and shows including bounding boxes, labels and warnings to the driver.

heading: 3.4.1.1.1 Functionality:
content:  The camera continuously captures video footage from the environment.  The YOLOv8 deep learning model processes the frames in real time to detect and classify various objects.  Objects are annotated with bounding boxes and labels and if distance estimates or safety warnings are detected, do so.  This information is shown on a screen or via audible alerts, so the system improves the driver's situational awareness.  it also integrates with the braking system to let you avoid potential collision timely.

heading: 3.4.1.2 Automatic Braking System Subsystem Components:
content:  Camera: Provides the visual input necessary for the detection of obstacles.  Edge Detection Algorithms: Algorithms that process images to detect edges and shapes of objects.  Depth Estimation Algorithms: I studied how to estimate the distance to detected obstacles, allowing the system to decide when to activate braking.  Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino): Interfaces with image processing system and controls the braking mechanism.  Braking Actuator (Electronic Braking System): Physical actuator responsible for applying brakes according to the system commands [30].

heading: 3.4.1.2.1 Functionality:
content:  The camera captures video frames of the surrounding environment.  Edge detection and depth estimation algorithms analyze the video to identify obstacles and measure the distance to these obstacles.  An obstacle is detected when it falls within a predefined safety distance and triggers the braking actuators to brake.  This system lessens the chances of collisions as well as increases safety by automatically breaking during times when the driver cannot act quickly enough.

heading: 3.4.1.3 Rain Detection and Automatic Wiper Activation Subsystem Components:
content:  IR (Infrared) Sensors: Detect the presence and get the intensity of the rain or other precipitation on the vehicle wind shield.  Impedance Sensors: The resistance or impedance changes on the presence of water on windshield should be measured.  Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino): It interfaces with the sensors to process the data and to control the speed of wiper accordingly.  Wiper Motor: Speeds and operates wipers based on sensors.

heading: 3.4.1.3.1 Functionality:
content:  Rain or precipitation is continuously monitored with the IR and impedance sensors.  Sensor data is processed by the microcontroller to decide the amount of rain.  The wiper motor controls the speed of the wipers according to rain intensity detected, ensuring best possible visibility without human touching.  This subsystem enhances driving safety and reduces driver distraction during adverse weather conditions.

heading: 3.4.1.4 Fingerprint-Based Security and IoT GPS Monitoring Subsystem Components:
content:  Fingerprint Sensor: Captures and scans the fingerprint of the person attempting to unlock the vehicle.  IoT Platform (e.g., MQTT/Cloud): It is a Monitor that logs all access attempts and integrates with GPS tracking for unauthorized access.  GPS Module: gives the real time position of the vehicle when unauthorized access is made.  Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino): Controls the access control system, manages fingerprint data, and interfaces with the IoT platform and GPS.  Actuator (e.g., Lock Mechanism): Controls the vehicle’s lock mechanism, unlocking or locking the vehicle based on fingerprint authentication.

heading: 3.4.1.4.1 Functionality:
content:  The fingerprint sensor scans the fingerprint of the user attempting to access the vehicle.  If the fingerprint matches an authorized user, the lock mechanism is triggered to unlock the vehicle.  If it recognizes the fingerprint, all is good. If the fingerprint does not match, the system triggers an alert via the IoT platform that also passes on a GPS location of the vehicle to the owner's device.  The vehicle access real time monitor ensures secure vehicle access and enabling real time monitoring of any unauthorized access attempt.

heading: 3.4.1.5 Blind Spot Detection and Parking Assistance Subsystem Components:
content:  IR Sensors (Infrared Sensors): Emit infrared light to detect objects in the vehicle’s blind spots and measure the reflections.  Ultrasonic Sensors: During parking maneuvers, measure the distance of the vehicle from objects in close proximity.  Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino): They process data by interfaces with the sensors and provide alerts accordingly.  Audible Alert System: Alerts the driver through an alert (e.g., beep, sound) when an obstacle is detected within the blind spot, during parking.

heading: 3.4.1.5.1 Functionality:
content:  The IR and ultrasonic sensors monitor the areas around the vehicle, detecting objects in the blind spot and during parking.  The microcontroller processes the sensor data and determines the distance to obstacles.

content:  YOLOv8 Model : On the  PC, the  YOLOv8 model can be implemented using  Python and TensorFlow/Kera’s. The model will be trained or fine-tuned on a dataset (such as COCO or custom dataset) to identify relevant objects such as pedestrians, vehicles, and other hazards.  Image Processing: OpenCV will be used for image pre-processing (resize, normalization, etc.) and post-processing (annotating frames with bounding boxes, labels, and safety warnings).  Object Detection Workflow: The PC will process video frames from the camera or a video stream. heading: 3.5.2 Automatic Braking System Implementation on PC:
content:  Obstacle Detection: Using the annotated video frames from the object detection system, depth estimation algorithms (like stereo vision or monocular depth estimation) will be implemented on the PC to determine the distance of obstacles [31].  Braking Logic: The braking mechanism logic can be simulated on the PC. If an obstacle is detected within a certain distance threshold, the braking system will be activated (simulated with a software "brake" signal).  Communication: Simulate communication with a mock actuator (software simulation) to apply the brakes once an obstacle is detected. The microcontroller will simplify object detection and depth estimation, with optimized algorithms for real-time performance. The microcontroller will use data from the camera and other sensors to trigger the braking mechanism (via GPIO or other control signals).

heading: 3.5.3 Rain Detection and Automatic Wiper Implementation on PC:
content:  Sensor Simulation: Since IR and impedance sensors are hardware components, the rain detection logic can be simulated on the PC by using artificial sensor data. content:  Fingerprint Sensor  Emulation: On the PC, you ca n simulate fingerprint scanning using a predefined database of fingerprint templates and a simulated scanner. heading: 3.5.5 Blind Spot Detection and Parking Assistance Implementation on PC:
content:  Sensor Data Simulation : Since ultrasonic sensors and IR sensors are hardware based, simulate their data on the PC using predefined or randomly generated proximity data for blind spot detection and parking.  Detection Algorithm: Implement algorithms to calculate the distance to objects in blind spots and during parking maneuvers. heading: 3.6 Working of Each Subsystem Before Integration
content: a) Object Detection and Frame Annotation Using YOLOv8 The object detection subsystem processes video frames to identify obstacles and hazards in real time. The YOLOv8 model detect objects and outputs bounding boxes, labels, and confidence scores for each detected object. Video frames are captured and fed into the YOLOv8 model. Detected objects are annotated with bounding boxes and labels, and the system calculates the distance to obstacles using bounding box dimensions. To ensure that everything on the road takes place smoothly, the safety warnings are overlaid to the image stream. In order to ensure that all this is working, the entire arrangement including the YOLO model is also tested on a PC. This way, we will be able to tell whether the system is actually detecting things and marking them correctly and maintain low latency nice and low. b) Automatic Braking System The theme of our group project is the development of a self-driving subsystem with the input of live video that would notice the possible obstrole and engage the brakes when necessary. To make this happen we have piled on edge detection, object classification and distance estimation techniques. The first helps us isolate boundaries in the scene, the second picks the kind of object, and the third determines the distance of the object. All of them combined provide the vital data in collision avoidance. When you are analyzing video feed you will be able to identify objects present on the screen and be able to measure the distance between each and the vehicle. In case an item veers or floats into an area you have determined to be dangerous, the system gives a signal of braking. You want to be certain that it all works, so you may have to run through simulated situations and see how well the system identifies the objects then there is whether the braking system behaves as per your expectations so you will be confident that you can count on it to avoid obstacles. c) Rain Detection and Automatic Wiper Activation This system uses rain sensors (IR and impedance-based) connected to an Arduino microcontroller to detect precipitation and adjust the wiper speed. Water nodes are attached on the windshield and when there is rain pelting on the water sensor, the gadget becomes aware of a difference in impedance. Arduino reads that information and changes the speed of wiper motor on the fly. We tested the system with different amounts of rain at the bench to check the accuracy of the system in detecting the intensity of rain and respond to the rainfall sensations without any lapses. d) Fingerprint-Based Security System with IoT GPS Monitoring Consider this arrangement as a deterrence of unwanted individuals, only individuals with their fingerprints stored in the database will be able to enter the car. Behind the scenes, IoT technology is monitoring all the attempts and the red flag warns the GPS that someone conspicuously does not belong. The embedded fingerprint sensor extracts a biometric data and then compares it with data in the database of the device, in our case it is a fingerprint. Where the match is strong it gives the system access. When they do not match, then the sensor records the event and sends a alert on the GPS that appears the owners device. In order to check the accuracy and speed of the sensor, I set a number of trials, monitored the time of authentication as well as the frequency of the mis- detection of the fingerprints of the user. Meanwhile, I ensured that the IoT platform at the other end of the connection was transmitting the logged event and the GPS alert in a hitch-free manner whenever the unauthorized attempt caused a spike of the log. e) Blind Spot and Parking Distance Warning Systems The blind-spot detection system will be composed of infrared transducers to detect the presence of an object in front of the vehicle within a range that cannot be accessed by the lateral mirrors and the parking assistance system will have ultrasonic sensors to perform the calculations of the spatial distance between the vehicle and the obstacle. f) Process: The IR sensors scan blind spots and alert the driver when obstacles are detected. The ultrasonic sensors emit and receive sound waves to calculate distances, providing warnings during parking. The IR and ultrasonic sensors are calibrated and tested in controlled environments to ensure accurate detection and warning deliveryjhdjhefhsdh

heading: 4.1 Development Stages
content: A single printed circuit board (PCB) was designed in order to enable an integration of a heterogeneous system comprising of normally more than one microcontroller and sensors to help in minimizing physical footprint as well as the number of wires that needed to be used. Th e microcontrollers were only given specialized tasks, and the inter -module communication was established using standard protocols, such as the I2C, SPI, and UART, whereby the Raspberry Pi was a central element.

heading: 4.1.1 PCB Development
content: The hardware development process for the autonomous vehicle assistance and safety system was conducted in a structured and iterative manner, focusing on accuracy, modularity, and electrical safety. To ensure that all components functioned together seamlessly, the entire design was first prototyped and tested using breadboards. This allowed early detection of compatibility issues and simplified debugging. Once the breadboard model functioned reliably, the design was transferred to Proteus Design Suite for schematic development, l ayout planning, simulation, and eventually fabrication. The following stages outline the complete hardware development procedure: Stage 0: Breadboard Prototyping and Testing The initial phase involved assembling all core components—Raspberry Pi, ultrasonic sensors, IR modules, servo motors, OLED display, ESP8266, and RFID reader —on a breadboard. This allowed manual wiring and real-time testing of signal compatibility, voltage behavior, and microcontroller response. Modules were connected through jumper wires, and power was supplied from a regulated DC source. Each module was independently tested for response accuracy and communication stability. This stage was essential for identifying connection errors, pin mismatches, and cross -talk between sensors before moving to PCB development. Stage 1: Schematic Design in Proteus After successful breadboard validation, a detailed circuit schematic was designed in Proteus. The schematic was created by logically dividing the system into functional blocks:

heading: 1. Core System Wiring and Power Management
content: The power supply system was designed to deliver 5V and 3.3V outputs using step-down voltage regulators to meet the requirements of Raspberry Pi, ESP8266, IR sensors, OLED display, and other peripherals. A dedicated power module was included with buffering capacitors and diode protection to prevent back - current or voltage spikes. Analog-to-Digital Conversion (ADC) and PWM signal control for servo motors were integrated using GPIO-compatible modules.

heading: 2. Blind Spot and Parking Assistance Module
content: IR sensors were positioned at the sides for blind spot detection, while ultrasonic sensors were used for rear parking detection. Each sensor’s signal output was routed through protection diodes and resistors to reduce noise and false triggering. Signal conditioning components were added to improve reading accuracy. heading: 3. ESP-RFID Interface with Optocouplers
content: The ESP8266 Wi-Fi module was connected using UART communication. An RFID reader (using SPI protocol) was integrated with optocoupler protection to isolate the logic level difference between ESP and RFID module. Figure 18:pcb schematic of Rfid locking System

heading: 4. Display, Communication Buses and rain wiper control
content: An OLED display was added using I²C communication, and wiring was tested to ensure address match and real-time update capability.UART, I²C, and SPI buses were properly labeled and isolated to avoid crosstalk during simultaneous communication. An LM393 rain sensor connected to an Arduino UNO read analog moisture levels. The Arduino processed the data to determine rainfall intensity and controlled the wiper motor through PWM signals. This Arduino was mounted on the PCB and communicated the sensor readings to the Raspberry Pi over the I2C bus, allowing centralized monitoring and logging. heading: 1. Footprint Design
content: Custom footprints for Arduino, ESP8266, voltage regulators, and screw terminal blocks were created to match real-world component sizes. Standardized headers were used for sensor connections to support easy troubleshooting or replacement.

heading: 2. PCB Layout and Tracing
content: A two-layer PCB layout was designed for compactness and modularity. Traces were routed with a standard width of 80 (80 mils) for power lines and 30-50 mils for signal traces, ensuring low resistance and heat dissipation. Careful attention was given to ground plane design and trace separation between analog, digital, and power lines.

heading: 3. Routing and Optimization
content: Proteus auto-routing tool was used initially, followed by manual optimization for signal integrity and trace efficiency. All connectors and modules were logically grouped to reduce wire clutter during assembly. Test points and jumper pads were added for debugging. Stage 3: 3D Visualization and Fabrication After layout finalization, a 3D visual simulation of  the PCB was generated in Proteus to inspect spacing, component alignment, and overall physical footprint. This visualization helped identify mechanical constraints, potential overlaps, and clearances for connectors and headers. Once the design passed this stage, Gerber files were exported and sent for fabrication to a local PCB manufacturer. The final fabricated board was delivered with solder mask and silkscreen layers for ease of assembly. Figure 21: PCB 3D visualization Front Figure 22: PCB 3D Visualization Back Stage 4: Soldering and Continuity Testing Upon receiving the fabricated PCB, components were manually soldered in -house. In installing the hardware installations, care was taken to avoid cold joints, over heat or bridges. After soldering was complete, all the critical traces were then tested by co ntinuing a multi meter, to ensure that there were no open circuits, or shorts. The individual modules have been tested and powered before connecting them to the major Raspberry Pi. The integrated system that was done easily showed that it could be able to deliver power and communicate with the Raspberry Pi 4 indicating successful assembly. Functional reliability was not the sole attribute of the synthesized hardware development process: electrical safety and physical compactness were also guaranteed during  it. Moreover, modular blocks, signal - protection measures, and organized way of design allow upgrading and maintenance activities in the future. heading: 4.1.2 power system development
content: Power system is a key component of architecture of the autonomous vehicle assistance and safety system, as it ensures consistent and suitable voltage in each of the mutually supporting modules. Given the fact that the hardware is modular by its very nature, and that various components that constitute it require dissimilar voltage conditions, namely: sensors, controllers, and microprocessors, the custom power -distribution approach was a necessity. A 12-V 7-Ah lead-acid battery is used to power the whole system, because of its strong output, being portable and coordinate to automotive-grade electronics. Multi-buck converter topology was incorporated to control the conversion and distribution of 12V input power to have several load -specific voltage levels. It was set up in a series of four free  buck converters, three using LM2596 module and the other using XL4016 module. Every converter was optimized separately to suit its target load and not to add an instability, overheating, or high current consumption.

heading: 1. Buck Converter 1 – 5V for Arduino Nano Modules
content: The former buck converter converts the battery 12 V to controlled 5 V. In this arrangement LM2596 module and the 7805 voltage regulator transist or are used coupled with a multi -turn potentiometer. With the potentiometer you can manually adjust the output voltage in tiny steps and 7805 provides the other level of protection that eliminates any chance of voltage offsets. The converter has current rating of up to 2 A which is suitable to power up the two Arduino Nano microcontrollers and their low power peripherals.

heading: 2. Buck Converter 2 – 4.3V for ESP8266 Wi-Fi Module
content: The maximum supply voltage of ESP8266 Wi-Fi module is 4.3V which is by far very low voltage compared to that handled by most conventional microcontrollers (5V). So within the scope of protecting ESP8266 against overvoltage the second converter based on LM2596 on the prototype system is set in a manner that it provides 4.3V. The reduction of supply voltage just slightly helps not only prevent any overheating or possibility of permanent damage, but also provide stable performance of the module in normal use. The filtering capacitors and a special heat sink are also added to maintain a consistent performance even in case of a long-read data transfer or when working under high-current demands.

heading: 3. Buck Converter 3 – 5V for Peripheral Sensor Modules
content: LM2596 converter (version 3) can produce 5 V, which means that it will provide the necessary voltage of the sensor modules used in the project. The modules are an IR sensor, an ultrasonic distance sensor, an OLED display, a rain sensor and a RFID reader which operate on a 5 volt logic level. The decoupling between the sensor power supply and the control boards will increase the dependability of the system, works well in decreasing the voltage level of the noise, and lessens cross -interference between logic and analog signal lines.

heading: 4. Buck Converter 4 – 5V for Raspberry Pi 4 (XL4016)
content: The fourth and strongest power-supply design is based on the XL4016 module, the integrated circuit which could be used to control the currents with the maximal value of 8 A. The duty of this unit is to take the higher 12 V supply and halve it down to a 5 V controlled sup ply with a 3 A rating. The Raspberry Pi 4 as the major processing part of the system also has high power consumption demands due to the inclusion of an embedded CPU, USB peripherals, and camera input. Therefore, the XL4016 delivers power energy reliably and thermally efficient to meet these requirements. In installation, adequate heatsinking and thermal products in terms of pad were used to ensure safe operating temperatures. Additional Protections and Design Considerations  Capacitors and Inductors were added to each converter output to smooth voltage fluctuations and minimize EMI.  Diodes were used at critical junctions to prevent reverse polarity damage.  Each converter output was measured and calibrated using a multimeter before being connected to modules.  Fuses were included at the 12V input stage for short-circuit and overcurrent protection. The architectural design structure of the suggested power distribution system is devised with the aim of encouraging the safe, continuous operation of all the elec tronic constituents and at the same time uphold the set design codes. This is attained through physically separating the spheres of power, trying to reduce the chances of ground loops, and creating overall stability of the entire system. Moreover the use o f independent, adjustable and modular power supply would provide flexibility as well as the capability to expand or modify scheme of potential future expansions.

heading: 4.1.3  Power Distribution on PCB
content: The next important activity on the development of power supp ly system was on the performance after calibration processes had taken place; it had to do with the effective supply of current throughout the specially-designed printed circuit board (PCB). The PCB was carefully routed in order to ensure that all functional blocks e.g. microcontrollers and communication modules, different sensing registers were fed by the correct voltage value and with the least power dissipated, observable noise, or likelihood of component damage. Power traces were separated and categorized based on their voltage level and current requirements to maintain electrical isolation and system stability.

heading: 1. Main Power Entry and Isolation
content: The 12V input from the battery is fed into the PCB via a high -current screw terminal block. This input is immediately filtered through bulk capacitors and a reverse polarity protection diode. From this entry point, the 12V line branches out to four individual buck converters mounted on or near the PCB board surface. These converters serve as the core voltage regu lators, stepping down the 12V to multiple lower -voltage lines based on module-specific needs. Each converter’s output is then routed into the PCB through separate terminal points or pin headers. Proper decoupling capacitors are placed at each voltage input  point on the PCB to ensure that transient currents and voltage ripples are suppressed before reaching sensitive ICs.

heading: 2. 5V Line for Arduino Nano Modules
content: The 5V output from the first LM2596 converter (regulated with a 7805) is routed through wide copper traces to the sockets designated for two Arduino Nano modules. These traces are sized to handle up to 2A of current and are routed directly without vias to minimize resistance. Each Arduino module is isolated from the main 5V line using a Schottky diode and bypass capacitor to prevent back feed and voltage noise.

heading: 3. 4.3V Line for ESP8266
content: A separate 4.3V trace is dedicated to powering the ESP8266 module, entering the board through a designated pin header. Since the ESP8266 is sensitive to voltage spi kes, the power line is buffered with both ceramic and electrolytic capacitors and includes a TVS diode for surge protection. The UART and I²C connections from the ESP are optically isolated where needed to avoid ground potential issues when communicating with 5V logic systems.

heading: 4. 5V Sensor and Peripheral Power Line
content: The third 5V line, dedicated to peripheral components, is distributed across the PCB using a star topology. This ensures that each module—such as IR sensors, ultrasonic sensors, OLED display, RFID module, and rain sensor —receives a stable and clean 5V supply from the same central node. Inline resistors and decoupling capacitors are placed at each connection point to prevent voltage dips caused by simultaneous sensor activation. Each sensor module  has a clearly labeled header on the PCB for plug -and-play functionality.

heading: 5. 5V Line for Raspberry Pi (via XL4016)
content: The most current-demanding module—the Raspberry Pi 4—receives power through a thick trace connected to the XL4016 buck converter. To handle the higher current (up to 3A), this trace is widened (80 mils or more), and thermal reliefs are used on the copper plane. The Pi’s input trace is further supported by a solid ground plane and ground loop breakers to ensure noise-free operation. An inline polyfused  is included for overcurrent protection.

heading: 6. Ground Plane and Return Paths
content: A continuous ground plane was implemented throughout the bottom layer of the PCB to provide a low - impedance return path for all components. Special care was taken to isolat e analog and digital grounds where necessary, particularly between motor drivers and logic circuits. Ground vias were strategically placed to connect the top and bottom layers, reducing voltage differentials and improving EMC performance.

heading: 7. Test Points and Debugging Headers
content: To facilitate debugging and safety checks, multiple test points were added for each voltage rail (12V, 5V, 4.3V, GND). These allow for quick verification using a multimeter or oscilloscope during prototyping or post-deployment maintenance. Additionally, status LEDs are included for visual confirmation of voltage presence.

heading: 4.1.3 Software Implementation
content: The software development phase of this project focused on implementing distributed logic across multiple microcontrollers and integrating real-time cloud connectivity to support autonomous assistance and safety features in the vehicle. Each functional objective —such as object detection, parking assistance, anti -theft locking, rain sensing, and mobile control—was implemented through independent controllers working in a synchronized architecture. The system was programmed using a mix of Python (Raspberry Pi), C++ (Arduino and ESP8266), and block -based programming (MIT App Inventor), ensuring compatibility and flexibility across hardware.

heading: 1. Arduino Nano 1 – Blind Spot and Parking Sensor Integration
content: The first Arduino Nano was programmed in C++ via Arduino IDE to interface with both IR sensors for blind spot detection and ultrasonic sensors for parking assistance. The following libraries were used:  NewPing.h – for reliable distance measurement using ultrasonic sensors  SoftwareSerial.h – for UART communication with Raspberry Pi

heading:  Sensor Logic:
content:  The ultrasonic sensor measured distance in cm using the ping_cm( ) method. Any value ≤ 50 cm triggered a buzzer using digitalWrite(buzzerPin, HIGH) to indicate a potential parking hazard.  The IR sensors monitored the vehicle’s blind spots. When an object was detected via reflection, the Arduino activated a warning LED using digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH).  Sensor readings were filtered using moving averages to reduce false positives and were sent to the Raspberry Pi through UART serial communication.

If value equals "OK is report", it updates a label (used as system health status or acknowledgment).  Firebase Integration: Uses MIT’s Firebase DB blocks to: StoreValue for commands GetValue to read back data Handle success/failure via notifier blocks

content: App reads RFID status from /access_log/status Displays “Authorized” or “Unauthorized” status accordingly 5.Raspberry Pi 4 Programming – YOLOv8 and Motor Control The Raspberry Pi 4 was responsible for real-time image processing and motor control. The system used the Ultralytics YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once version 8) model, implemented in Py thon with support from opencv-python, torch, and ultralytics libraries. YOLOv8 was chosen for its lightweight, single-stage detection pipeline capable of providing bounding boxes and class probabilities in real time.  The YOLOv8n (nano) variant was selected to balance speed and accuracy on edge hardware.  The model achieved an average mAP of 50 –60%, and inference time remained below 100 ms per frame, suitable for responsive decision-making.  Detected object classes and proximity data were used to control a L298N motor driver, connected through GPIO PWM signals using the RPi.GPIO library.  Multithreading was implemented to separate video capture, model inference, and motor control, improving responsiveness.

heading: 4.1.4 Hierarchy of Microcontrollers and System Modules
content: The embedded system architecture of the project is based on a hierarchical microcontroller design, where the Raspberry Pi 4  serves as the central command unit. This controller is tasked with the most computationally intensive operations such as real -time object detection using the YOLOv8 deep learning model, distance estimation, PWM -based motor control, braking system management, sensor data processing, and user interface feedback. In addition, the Raspberry Pi maintains all network -level communication, inc luding Firebase database connectivity for remote command reception and system logging. The Pi directly interfaces with peripheral modules such as IR sensors, ultrasonic sensors, motor drivers, OLED display, brake lights, and the onboard camera. It also com municates with the Arduino and ESP8266 over I²C and UART respectively, thereby acting as the master node in the system hierarchy. Assisting the Raspberry Pi is the Arduino UNO, which is responsible for environmental sensing and mechanical control of the ra in wiper system. The Arduino continuously reads analog signals from the LM393 rain sensor and calculates the moisture levels. Based on this, it generates PWM signals to operate the wiper motor accordingly. This division of labor allows the Raspberry Pi to offload analog processing tasks and maintain its processing focus on the object detection and motor control logic. Communication between the Arduino and Raspberry Pi is managed through the I²C protocol, ensuring reliable and low - latency data transfer. Third essential subcomponent of the suggested architecture is ESP8266 microcontroller which only serves to act as a standalone wireless authentication device only. It communicates with an RFID reader module over SPI so as to access information in the RFID card and authenticating an authorized entry. Optical isolation, enacted via the implementation of optocouplers, necessitates to block the desire to electromagnetic interference generated by the ESP8266 circuitry and monitor compatibility as well, at the logic-level. Then the module sends the information about user identification using UART to the Raspberry Pi central hub. Another development of the design can be to incorporate a direct Wi-Fi connection between the ESP8266 and Firebase resulting in a complete decentralized verification procedure. Multi-controller architecture thus proposed has the potential of increased modularity, parallelism, and reliability. The Raspberry Pi hosts a higher level of logic and inference roles, where special real-time analog work is delegated to the Arduino and authentication to the ESP8266. The respective power path feeding each controller to the structured power management system is designed with the independent power path, protection of the power management system consisting of the voltage regulator, supplemental capacitors and protection diodes circuits. The schematic also has the careful routing and isolation to ensure the noise is minimized, interference is mitigated and that analog, digital, and power signals paths through the circuitry travel in well-defined domains. Figure 26:Hierarchy of Microcontrollers The design of the aimed system is carefully pivotal, which allows the separate parts to be confirmed, reused, and advanced on versus the rest of the system. Such design approach does not only support the maintenance but also provides opportunities to scale in the future. The system is prototyped on a breadboard in early stages of development (proof of concept) and later edited to obtain a two-layer printed circuit board that is compact and efficient. Inter-module communication facility is passed through APIC-dedicated buses (I 2 C and UART/SPI) and these are distinctly labeled buses to facilitate trouble shooting in case required. The last step that  was performed in integrating the systems indicated that the controllers were synchronized and the Raspberry Pi as the coordinator. The modular design had resulted in a simple hierarchical structure that simplified the system and system performance as well as safety.

Inter -module interaction is achieved through the coordination of Firebase, in which communication between al l hardware pieces is synchronized and maintains an undisturbed user-experience between devices. Real VNC Server In this current project, the Raspberry Pi 4 will operate as the central processing machine, and will run an object detection program based on a YOLOv8 algorithm where an integer input will be fed to it based on an actual video stream being recorded and streamed, by an integrated camera module. heading: 5 Evaluation
content: This chapter contains the outcomes of the conducted implementation of the proposed design methodology along with the discussion of the performance of each of its components. The main determinant of the evaluation process was to confirm that the system had the capability to accurate ly carry out its intended operations under game/real-life environments. The evaluation took place in two phases, namely, unit and functional (integrated) testing which imply the assessment of not only each subsystem separately but also the efficiency of th e combined vehicle assistance and safety system. Important performance spots were real-time object detection, automatic braking response, RFID-based access control, IP-based security alert, rain detection and blind spot assistance. Testing was done in a nu mber of environmental conditions and scenarios to check the robustness of the system, response time, precision and reliability of the system.

heading: 5.4 Comparison
content: The project under consideration does not have manual intervention as the only attribute involved; it uses automation and intelligent response in low-cost automobiles. The real-time AI-driven object detection, RFID-based access control, and automated rain and blind spot systems mimic high-end automotive safety features, making them accessible and customizable for a broader market.

heading: 5.5  Socio-Economic and Environmental Impact of the Project
content: This project aims to make smart vehicle safety systems affordable and scalable, particularly for countries like Pakistan where road safety  and theft prevention are growing concerns. By integrating low -cost yet highly effective technologies such as RFID, IR sensors, and camera-based AI, the system can be installed on older or economy vehicles, thus democratizing access to advanced road safety . This can lead to a reduction in road accidents, vehicle thefts, and manual driving errors—directly benefiting society. From an environmental standpoint, the vehicle system is designed to operate on solar power, reducing dependence on fossil fuels and minimizing carbon emissions. Additionally, all selected components—like the Raspberry Pi, IR sensors, and RFID modules —are low-power devices that align with energy-efficient principles. The use of an IP -based alert system instead of GPS reduces hardware comp lexity and energy usage, making the entire system both cost -effective and environmentally sustainable. As the world shifts towards eco -friendly transportation, this project sets a solid foundation for solar -based smart mobility solutions.

heading: 5.6.1 Introduction
content: Solar-powered vehicles are gaining momentum as an eco -friendly alternative to fossil -fuel-based transportation. However, one of the critical challenges in the development of su ch vehicles lies in optimizing speed and energy efficiency without compromising system reliability or safety. This research explores strategies that improve the operational performance of solar -powered vehicles, particularly in terms of speed management, energy harvesting, drivetrain efficiency, and control logic.

heading: 5.6.2 Factors Affecting Speed and Efficiency
content: The speed and energy efficiency of a solar-powered vehicle depend on multiple interlinked factors:

heading: 5.6.2.1 Solar Panel Efficiency
content: a) The efficiency of photovoltaic (PV ) cells directly impacts the amount of power available to the vehicle. b) Use of monocrystalline panels (20–24% efficiency) is preferred for compact systems. c) Techniques such as Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) ensure that solar panels operate at their optimal power output under changing light conditions.

heading: 5.6.2.2 Vehicle Weight and Aerodynamics
content: a) Reducing vehicle weight by using lightweight materials (carbon fiber, aluminum) lowers the required propulsion power. b) Streamlined, low-drag vehicle body designs reduce air resistance and allow higher speeds with less energy. c) The drag force can be modeled by: Fd=(1/2)⋅ρ⋅Cd⋅A⋅v2

heading: 5.6.2.3 Motor and Drivetrain Efficiency
content: a) Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are commonly used for their high torque-to-weight ratio and low energy loss. b) Efficient drivetrain design, such as direct drive or single -speed gear reduction, reduces friction and power loss.

heading: 5.6.2.4 Battery Management and Storage
content: a) Energy harvested by the solar panels is stored in Li-ion or LiFePO₄ batteries. b) Smart Battery Management Systems (BMS) re gulate charging, discharging, and temperature to avoid energy loss and prolong battery life. c) Regenerative braking systems can recover kinetic energy during deceleration and feed it back to the battery.

heading: 5.6.2.5 Control Algorithms for Speed and Load Balancing
content: a) Real-time control systems monitor speed, battery status, solar input, and road gradient to dynamically adjust motor speed. b) Fuzzy logic and PID controllers can optimize motor performance based on current load and energy availability. c) Speed vs. power trade-offs must be continuously evaluated by an onboard microcontroller or Raspberry Pi unit.

heading: 5.6.3 Optimization Strategies
content: Based on the above parameters, several conceptual and practical strategies were studied and recommended for future implementation:

heading: 5.6.3.1  Maximum Power Utilization
content:  Implementing MPPT algorithms in the solar charge controller maximizes solar input utilization under varying sunlight conditions.  Adaptive duty-cycle control ensures the battery is charged at the most efficient rate.

heading: 5.6.3.2  Hybrid Energy Strategy
content:  Combine solar power with auxiliary energy sources (e.g., regenerative braking or supercapacitors).  Use dual -mode operation where solar energy powers motors under light loads and batteries supplement under high load.

heading: 5.6.3.3 Speed Scheduling Algorithms
content:  Pre-define speed limits based on terrain and sunlight availability.  Use GPS and weather forecast APIs to dynamically plan speed limits and routes that optimize sun exposure.

heading: 5.6.3.4 Machine Learning for Efficiency Prediction
content:  Implement lightweight ML models on the R aspberry Pi to predict energy consumption and recommend speed adjustments.  Input parameters: current draw, solar intensity, historical energy usage, terrain slope.

heading: 5.6.3.5 5. PWM Optimization for Motors
content:  Vary the PWM signal supplied to the L298N motor driver based on real-time distance (from object detection) and energy availability.  This allows speed throttling during low sunlight to conserve energy and prevents over-speeding in obstacle-prone zones.

heading: 5.6.4 Results & Future Recommendations
content: Initial simulation and testing of these concepts revealed that speed optimization without sacrificing efficiency is best achieved through a combination of lightweight design, real-time control logic, and energy prediction models. Some actionable insights include:  Maintaining a cruise sp eed where the motor operates at peak efficiency (usually 60 –70% of full throttle) gives the best range-per-watt.  Using MPPT along with predictive control gives up to 15 –25% improvement in energy harvest under dynamic lighting.  Implementing regenerative bra king saves up to 10% of kinetic energy per braking cycle under urban conditions.

heading: 5.6.5 Conclusion
content: Efficient speed and energy management in solar -powered vehicles is a multi -disciplinary challenge requiring coordination between hardware, software, and energy systems. By incorporating real -time sensing, predictive control, and energy-aware speed algorithms, solar vehicles can achieve both speed and efficiency without compromising safety or range. This conceptual research lays the groundwork for building intelligent, self-adaptive solar vehicles suitable for real -world application and scalable for future development.

heading: 6. Conclusions & Future Work
content: In this project, we have researched and created a coordinated Autonomous Vehicle Assistance and Safety System, which is aimed at improving the areas of safety, security, and functionality with respect to small - scale intelligent transportation scenarios. Various innovative technologies such as real-time object detection using YOLOv8, automatic braking, access control using RFID with IP tracking, rain detection and the automatic control over wipers, and blind spot monitoring using IR are present in the system. The design of all the modules was based on low -cost, low-power components including Raspberry Pi 4, Arduino Nano, IR and ultrasonic sensor, ESP8266, and RFID modules, so the cost of the system could be very reasonable, and it could be scaled. We managed to prove in the process of development the possibility of using embedded systems and microcontrollers in such a way that both of them will share the tasks of visual and sensor data processing and will make real-time decisions which will help the vehicle to navigate and increase the awareness of the driver. RFID access system enhances security through authentication of users and recording of all attempts of access with an IP based monitoring system. Basic integration and testing demonstrated the reliability and responsiveness of the individual modules as well as the entire system , proving the usability of a modular and yet centralized system in small platforms of autonomous vehicles. This project will form a good ground to build affordable and intelligent vehicles safety systems in particular during academic, prototyping and experimentation settings where reliability and real time behaviour is vital. It emphasizes the possibility of integrating machine vision, microcontroller programming and IoT connectivity into small-sized, practical solutions. There could be several improvements possible in the future As technology evolves, various improvements can be incorporated into the system to expand its capabilities and improve efficiency. Some of the ideas for future development are mentioned below: Idea 1: Optimize Object Detection for Night-Time Conditions At the moment, the object detection system is most effective when there is a good light. To improve the system in situations of low-light or at night, infrared (IR) or thermal imaging Vision cameras may be used that allows seeing in the dark. Also, YOLOv8 can be trained using low-light datasets, as well as synthetic brightness increase filters can be run on the camera feed prior to detection. Such upgrades would make the system operate safely in tunnels or at night. Idea 2: Develop a Mobile App or Voice-Based Access Interface The existing access control solution relies on the RFID tags. In subsequent versions, the ability to communicate with a specific mobile application or Voice assistant (such as Google Assistant or Alexa) might unlock the possibility of remote vehicle operation, RFID control of the allowed users and driving behavior surveillance. This would provide conveniences to the user and could provide access control in a lesser intelligent form in terms of fleet or shared vehicle situations. Idea 3: Implement Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) Communication In order to enhance safety in areas with heavy traffic or other cooperative driving scenarios, a V2V communication system may be established based on protocols (such as Wi -Fi Direct, LoRa, or ZigBee). The latter would enable vehicles to share essential information including a warning about sudden brakes, warning about danger or indicating that the road is clear, which would result in improved situational awareness and safer automatized or assisted driving. Future Research Actions on the Project to Enhance Its Social and Environmental Impact Future Research Proceeding regarding the Project in order to make it have more Social and Environment Impact In order to enhance even more the value of society and sustainable potential of this system, further directions to be considered by future research should include the following areas:

heading: 1. Integration Smart City
content: By incorporating this system into smart city infrastructure, e.g. traffic light global systems, centralized car park, or emergency warning, it may be possible to create collaborative intelligence between traffic and environment. This would enable safer intersections, improved route planning and on -urban-scale car orchestrating.

heading: 2. Battery Management and Energy-efficient Hardware
content: Although the existing one has not been solar-powered, it can be possible to optimize batteries and manage the energy distribution, which might be the topic of further versions. This involves low power sensors, the ability to put in power saving features and batteries health monitoring systems to guarantee long operation lifespan particularly with systems with mobile or robotic vehicle platforms.

heading: 3. Universal Mobility and Accessibility Features
content: The system may be strengthened to serve the elderly users or disabled users better by including: voice - based control, automatic lane change, or vibration/haptic mechanism invoking warnings.

heading: 4. Informed Safety Road-Based Enhancements
content: The system could be used lo ng term to accumulate access logs, object detection statistics, sensor events (with the user and owner consent). The anonymized data would then be appropriate to use in making road safety policy, enhancing better urban design, and coming up with accident-prone areas to plan accordingly on the side of public planning.

heading: Final Remarks
content: Creation of the Autonomous Vehicle Assistance and Safety System embodies a considerable success in the conceptualization, development and fabrication process of modern embedded systems, real time processing, and intelligent automation into one micro-module that is functional. Using object detection with YOLOv8, automatic braking, RFID-based security, rain-responsive applications and blind spot monitoring, we have shown that inexpensive hardware and open technology can be used to overcome the problem of transportation safety in the real world. The project reflects both technical competency as well as practical design of engineering, where hardware and software have to work tog ether reliably in a real -time, in real conditions. It highlights modularity, responsiveness, and the user in safety-critical systems. Every module developed was thoroughly tested and streamlined to operate in an autonomous fashion as well as any fully integrated, centralized control system. Finally, the project offers a basis of future innovation in autonomous and semi -autonomous vehicles technology. It is scalable, adjustable and capable of being further developed in the future, although this may be as clever sensing, as being further integr ated into the cloud, or even as being extended to full automatisation of vehicles. An understanding of intelligence and experience demanded in this task will come in handy as a powerful foundation going forth into other intensive studies or actual implemen tation in the intelligent transport system.

') stop_motors(pwm_a, pwm_b, led_pwm) elif direction == "rwd" and distances.get("back", float('inf')) < threshold: if uart: uart.write(b'Ultrasonic back stop

') stop_motors(pwm_a, pwm_b, led_pwm) elif direction == "right" and distances.get("right", float('inf')) < threshold: if uart: uart.write(b'Ultrasonic right stop
') stop_motors(pwm_a, pwm_b, led_pwm) elif direction in ["fwd", "rwd", "left", "right"]: speed = 60 if distance_buffer: avg_dist = sum(distance_buffer) / len(distance_buffer) if avg_dist < 90: speed = 0 elif avg_dist < 100: speed = 20 elif avg_dist < 125: speed = 30 elif avg_dist < 150: speed = 40 elif avg_dist < 175: speed = 50 elif avg_dist < 200: speed = 60 elif avg_dist < 225: speed = 70 elif avg_dist < 250: speed = 80 else: speed = 90 print(f"[DETECTION] Distance: {int(avg_dist)} cm | Speed: {speed}%") move_motors(pwm_a, pwm_b, direction, speed, led_pwm) else: stop_motors(pwm_a, pwm_b, led_pwm) fps = 1 / (time.time() - start) cv2.putText(frame, f"{fps:.2f} FPS", (10, 25), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (255, 0, 0), 2) cv2.imshow("Optimized Detection", frame) if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'): break cv2.destroyAllWindows() def cleanup(pwm_a=None, pwm_b=None, led_pwm=None): try: if pwm_a: pwm_a.stop() if pwm_b: pwm_b.stop() if led_pwm: led_pwm.stop() except: pass GPIO.cleanup() def main(): global uart try: model = YOLO("yolov8n.pt") model.overrides['conf'] = 0.5 if torch.cuda.is_available(): model.model.half() pwm_a, pwm_b, led_pwm = setup_motors() initialize_uart() if uart: uart.write(b'UNLOCK

heading: Abstract
content: The problem of patients having misplaced medical records, how to access patient’s previous medical history when they change their hospital or doctor, how to find best  doctor according to their work experience on yearly basis and also doctors are unable to k now their complete history (previous medication), is a serious issue for effective trea tments. Therefore, we intend to aid such an online health care system where we are providing facility to patients where they can have their complete medical records saved also doctors can view all thei r medical records. Our system will integrate all the stakeholders of Online Health Care System that are major part of our system such as (hospitals, doctors, receptionist, patients, nurses, fam ous laboratories, and famous pharmacies of Pakistan). In diagnose disease functionality pat ient will tell doctor their symptoms what the patient is actually feeling; doctor  type those symptoms using doctor’s diagnose disease panel to diagnose the disease of the patient in a modernized and calculated way. By typing those symptoms on doctors diagnose disease panel the system show disease names in the form of probability chart against those symptoms using Ma chine Learning technique because in this system we store 40 to 50 common disease symptoms in our sy stem’s database. The result produced by those symptoms may or may not 100% accurate but shall  be close to those symptoms which then help doctor to make final decision that fr om which disease the patient is actually suffering from before prescribing any medicine to pa tient. This system assists doctor to diagnose patient ’s disease. Admin panel is the platform where admin can add, delete, view, and update any particular registered members or the overall register ed members within the system. Admin is able to view the disease rate of particular dis ease of any city of Pakistan. Admin just select the city from the dropdown menu on the admin pane l and then a graph depending upon the number of patients belonging to the common disease appear on the screen, which will help in controlling the disease in that area by generating alert of precautions in that area in the form of an email to all the doctors of the city belong s to high rated disease area or city. Admin can also view the graph of yearly new registered users at the bottom of the admin panel window, which will help admin to evaluate results on yearly basis. Instead of carrying reports and test prescriptions to every doctor, doctor is res ponsible for uploading the recommended test prescriptions on respective patient panel and the  laboratory staff is responsible for uploading patient test reports on respective patient panel. Doctors, laboratories, and pharmacies can view patient ’s previous medical history, test reports, prescriptions of patient by typing patient ’s CNIC number on their panel. The system serve many purposes for example Patient Management System where all the current and previous medical records of the pati ent are managed such as Patient ’s previous disease, previous medication reports along with the doctor ’s details who diagnose particular patient ’s disease, the medicines recommended previously etc. In Doctor’s Management System, doctor ’s details are managed such as doctor ’s qualification, area of specialization, which helps in finding the best doctor for specific area of speci alization and a diagnose disease panel where system assist doctor to diagnose disease of the patie nt. In Laboratory Management test reports of the patient developed, after test reports of the patient developed lab attendant first send them to respective doctor of the patient, doct or carefully examine the reports, then send them again to the laboratory with remarks, after t hat laboratory upload those reports to respective patient ’s panel using the CNIC of that patient. heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: The purpose of designing such platform is that patients are unable to provide their complete medical history such as prescriptions, test reports and the details of the doctors who diagnose their disease previously. Due to which doctors find it difficult to correctly diagnose the disease of the patient in a better way because they do not know their previous medical history. Moreover, the busy schedule of doctors needs this type of system, which assists them in diagnosing disease of the patient in a modernized and calculated way. In order to resolve this issue we provide a solution in the form of an online health care system that will assist doctor in diagnosing the disease of the patient. Because we store symptoms of 40 to 50 commonly occurring diseases using machine learning approach that will assist doctor to diagnose the disease of the patient. In addition to that, doctor can view previous medical history of the patient such as prescriptions and their dosage, prescribes test and their reports and the details of the doctor who diagnose the patient previously without any ambiguity or redundancy in the data. Retrieving of data without any redundancy is because doctor will use the patient CNIC no in order to view the patient previous medications and obviously every patient has unique CNIC No against their previous medical history, so there will be zero chance of data redundancy.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: This project is designed to maintain the medical records of patients along with details of their respective doctors. There are many areas around the globe where there is a lack of such automated system. The system assists doctor to diagnose the disease of the patient in a calculated way using machine learning approach. The system provides many services for patients, which includes; daily treatments, registration of patients, maintain records for patient’s medical history, search best hospitals or doctors according to their needs within few seconds respectively. This system contains:  Login and registration forms for (patients, doctors, receptionists, pharmacist, laboratory and hospitals)  The system shall allow (patients, doctors, receptionists, pharmacist, laboratory and hospitals) to edit their information like name, contact number, address, etc as identified in the introduction of the report. The following languages used within the system to enable development and implementation: PhpMyAdmin is used for keeping records about all the registered members of the system for security, accuracy and reliability each patient record shall kept against their CNIC number (backside we use SQL Server for databases development). Server side scripting shall do with java, php, embedded in html and java web server will facilitate simultaneous processing. This system is implemented using the languages PHP, HTML, CSS, BOOTSTRAP, Javasrcipt, Laravel framework, and SQL server management for databases and PhpMyAdmin only. We are not using any other programming language for the implementation purposes like Java, C sharp etc. It’s a complete web based application implemented by web-based components. Other than that we are not providing any rating feature to all the doctors because it might possible that the doctor which has more experience than other doctors have the lowest rating in the system as compared to the doctor who have less experience because of patients reviews.

heading: 2 Existing System Study
content: There are many hospital management systems where patients can register themselves and al l the details of the patients are online (no paperwork) but this type of system only  used in some departments of the hospital such as in Mayo Hospital Lahore, Pakistan, NHS (National Health Services) and Bayano System but they are not successful in many ways which includes:

heading: 14 of 90  15 May 2018
content: 1. Lack of immediate retrievals of patient ’s background medical history with 100% accuracy. Like if the patient has changed the hospital or doctor, the new doctor don ’t know anything about the patient ’s previous medical records, what medical tests, and medicines the patient had previously taken and from which doctor the patient diagnose him/herself previously. On the other hand if the laboratory or pharmacist wants to see the previous medical history of particular patient, like test reports and presc riptions both laboratory and pharmacies has to go through various registers. This results in inconvenience and wastage of time. 2. Patient Registration. For registration purpose patient has to go to hospital and registe r him/herself by waiting in line and passing through a lot of paper work, whic h is very frustrating and time-consuming task. 3. Booking Appointments. This is the main issue faced by patients to book appointments with those doctors that are actually according to their needs because are unabl e to see the details or search for particular doctors. 4. Getting hospital details and services provided by the hospital. 5. Diagnosing a disease in a calculated way.

heading:  Proposed System
content: Like in our system that integrate all the stakeholders of Pakistan (hospitals, doctors, receptionists, laboratorist and pharmacies) under one umbrella that is Online Health Care System. Such systems are not currently implemented yet in which all the major stakeholders of the hea lth care system can integrate with each other. Our system includes all the stakeholders as one syst em. The systems currently implemented are separate for each stakeholder such as Hospital Managem ent System, Laboratory Management System, and Pharmacy Management System etc. The patient can view the availability of doctors, details of doctors and hospital a nd the previous medical history of him/herself. Like area of specialization of doctors, from  which hospital particular doctor belongs to, address of hospital, how many doctors, nurses, receptionist, patients, laboratory and pharmacies the particular hospital have. Patient can also view his/her details on the patients respective homepage like previous test reports, prescriptions, previous doct ors and hospitals where the patient went for check-ups. The server side of the system has added doctor ’s details such as availability of doctors, consultation-hours, and specialization etc. Admin also add the patient details against their CNIC no that will be asked from patient during their registration process, the details include information files, test reports, prescriptions, and visiting history along with the detail s of the doctor where the patient has been previously checked. Retrieval of patient’s complete medical records in few clicks and with 100% accuracy that can be accessible using one platform is not currently implemented, but we implement this fea ture and to make each patient record unique we use patient ’s CNIC number. Doctor, pharmacist, and laboratories just have to enter the patient ’s CNIC number on their respective panel and the medical records against that CNIC number will be displayed on their screen with 100% accuracy. Moreover, patient’s data is secured using secured internet transmission and secured databases to make overall system secure and reliable.

heading: 15 of 90  15 May 2018
content: In addition to that, our system will assist doctor to find the disease of the patient in a modernized and calculated way using Machine Learning algorithms. Patient will tell doctor  their symptoms what the patient is actually feeling; doctor type those symptoms using doctor ’s diagnose disease panel to diagnose the disease of the patient in a modernized and calculated way. By typing  those symptoms on doctors diagnose disease panel the system show disease names in the form of probability chart against those symptoms using Machine Learning technique because in thi s system we store 40 to 50 common disease symptoms in our system ’s database. The result produced by those symptoms may or may not 100% accurate but shall be close to those symptoms which then help doctor to make final decision that from which disease the patien t is actually suffering from before prescribing any medicine to patient. This functi onality is currently not implemented in the existing systems. Other than that our system also generate precaution alert in the form of emai ls to doctors where the disease rate of common disease increases depending upon the number of patient ’s suffering from the common disease. Admin just select the city from the dropdown menu on the admin panel and then a graph depending upon the number of patients belonging to the common disease appear on the screen, which will help in controlling the disease in that ar ea by generating alert of precautions in that area in the form of an email to all the doctors of the ci ty belongs to high rated disease area or city. Advantages of proposed system:  Improve patient satisfaction with this web application  Improve security and accuracy rate in retrieving and storing patient informatio n in the databases.  Previous medical records along with the details of doctor and hospital.  Making appointments with those doctors that are according to patient’s needs.  No time consumption and frustration. For example patients don ’t need to stand in queue for registration purposes, patient don ’t need to take help from admin for adding him/her into the system unless the patient is uneducated. In case the patient is uneducated then the patient can take help from the receptionist of the hospital where he wants to regi ster him/herself as identified in the abstraction section of the report.  Diagnosing disease in a better and quick way.   Calculation of disease rate graph form particular area. Moreover, our system is made for the whole country Pakistan, not for only one hospit al all the hospitals, doctors, patients, pharmacies nurses, receptionist and laboratories that belongs to Pakistan.

heading: 2.5 Software development life cycle model (justification on why this
content: particular model is considered) We are using agile methodology for developing our system because of the following reasons.  Stakeholder Engagement . This software development model provides us multiple opportunities for stakeholders and team engagement before, during and after each sprint. It provides us high degree of collaboration between the clients and project t eam by involving the clients in every step of the project, which provide us way to better understand the client ’s vision. Delivering working software early and frequently increases stakeholder’s trust in the team’s ability to deliver high quality working software and encourages them to be more deeply engaged in the project.  Transparency: This approach provides a unique opportunity for clients to be involved throughout the project development and designing phase, from prioritizing feature s to

heading: 45 of 90  15 May 2018
content: iteration planning and review sessions to frequent software builds containi ng new features.  Early and Predictable Delivery. By using fixed schedule strategy that is 1-4 weeks, new features are delivered quickly and frequently, with a high level of predictability. This also provides the opportunity to beta test the functionality if needed.  Predictable Efforts and Schedule.  Because each sprint/module is a fixed duration, so the cost is predictable and limited to amount of work that can be performed by the tea m in the fixed schedule time-box. Combined with the estimates provided to the client  prior to each sprint, the client can more readily understand the effort of implementing ea ch feature, which improves decision making about the priority of features and the need for further iterations.  Allows for Change.  This methodology provides opportunity for development team to modify the sprint according to the needs of the stakeholders or customers. New or changed backlog items can be planned for the next iteration providing the opportunity to introduce changes within a few weeks.  Improves Quality.   By breaking down the project into manageable units, the project team can focus on high quality development, testing, and collaboration. Also by producing frequent builds and conducting, testing, and reviewing each iteration, improves the quality by finding and fixing the defects quickly and identifying expectations mismatches early.
