heading: 4.2 Unit Testing
content: For testing purposes we use unit testing approach, we test each functionality at the en d of its implementation so that if the functionality required any changes it can be implemented as early as possible. Other than that we test each module as well when it is completely developed i n order to verify that all the functionalities are successfully implemented and are accordi ng to customer needs and expectations. We use unit testing approach due to the following advantages:  Unit testing increases confidence in changing/maintaining code.  Codes are more reusable when unit testing approach is used in the development of application  The cost of fixing a bug/defect during unit testing is lesser in comparison to  that of defects detected at higher levels.  Debugging is easy. When the test fails only the latest changes made to the functi onality needs to be debugged.

heading: 5.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: In our journey until now, we faced many problems in the area of designing, implementa tion, and data collection phase. Those problems help us in learning our system complexities and functionalities in a better way. We propose solution for every problem we face during our journey until now by discussing those problems with our supervisor and with the help of som e tutorials. Overall, our experience until now is amazing in fact; we observe that those prob lems were beneficial for us. Problems related to designing are almost solved now but the pr oblem of patient personal data collection is a huge issue because no hospital, clinic agreed on giving us per sonal data of patient because it is against their authority to give personal data of patient to third user. So in our system we use machine learning techniques to implement diagnose disease functionality.

heading: 5.2 Project Summary
content: In short our project online health care system is a platform where all the stak eholders of health system (Hospitals, laboratories, pharmacies, doctors, patients, and receptionists ) can integrate with each other under one umbrella that s Online Health Care System. Patient  reports, prescriptions, previous medical history is stored in Online Health Management System database against patient’s CNIC number. So the issue of handling test reports, prescriptions etc. in hard form are resolved using this system. Our system assists doctor to diagnose the dise ase of patient using machine learning approach. Patient can search doctor and hospital according to their needs. Patient can make appointment with their desired doctors with the help of receptio nist. Admin can generate high rated disease percentage graph of particular city/area and a lso send precaution alert email to all the doctors of affected area. Online health care system provi des all the necessary features to patients, doctors, pharmacies, laboratories, hospitals, and receptionist as identified in the above sections.

heading: Abstract
content: Color plays a crucial role in our perception and interaction with the world, en- hancing object visualization and recognition. This project aims to revolutionize color mixing technology by automating the process with precision and accuracy. Leveraging image processing techniques and IoT (Internet of Things) technology, the system identifies colors in real-time and adjusts the ratio of primary colors to achieve the desired shade. The project begins with an exploration of various color models, including RGB (Red, Green, Blue) and CMYK (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black), elucidating their significance in digital displays and printing applications. It then delves into the HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) color model, crucial for color detection in the pro- posed system. The core of the system lies in its ability to convert input images into the HSV color space and analyze the Hue component to identify colors accurately. Commands are sent to an Arduino microcontroller based on color detection, enabling precise manipulation of an industrial robot for pick and place tasks. Real-time monitoring and control are facilitated through IoT integration, optimizing resource utilization and minimizing waste. The project addresses challenges in traditional color production methods, offer- ing a solution that streamlines the process, reduces human error, and enhances efficiency. Through algorithm development, sensor integration, and user-friendly interface design, the system aims to set a new standard in automated color recog- nition and mixing technology. iii Table of heading: Introduction
content: Color is the fundamental aspect of our perception and interaction with the world. Color improves the visualization and recognition of an object. These colors are the shades of three basic primary colors Red, Green, and blue. Different Color models mix these colors in a specific ratio to make various shades. A few Color models are RGB, CMYK, and HSV . The basic purpose of this machine is to improve the color mixing technology to form these shades with precision and accuracy. It uses image processing techniques to recognize the color and then applies different algorithms to set the ratio of each primary color to form the required shade.

heading: 1.1 Color Models
content: [1]Color models are designed systems that allow us to create a wide range of colors using numeric values or specific color components. These models serve as a conceptual framework for discussing, viewing, and working with color in various contexts, including art, design, advertising, and digital media. These colors are used in the paint industry, Textile industry, and other aspect of daily life.

heading: 1.1.1 RGB Color Model
content: RGB color model is anadditive color model that uses three basic primary colors Red, Green, and Blue in different Proportions to make other colors [2]. The white color contains the presence of each color and black contains the absence of these three colors. This color model is used in Digital displays like TV, Cameras, and other devices. The Figure1.1 shows different colors in RGB model.

heading: 1.1.2 CMYK Color Model
content: The CMYK color model is a subtractive color model , which means it works on the principle of reflecting light. The primary colors that it uses are Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, and Black. If certain colors combine and layer, darker hues of red, green, and blue will appear. Likewise, layering all three primaries (cyan, magenta, and yellow) will result in the darkest color combination (very dark brown or black) or filter out the lightest reflection [3].

heading: 1.2 Image Processing
content: Image processing is a process in which information about an image is extracted. These pieces of information are present in the form of pixels, which are the ba- sic units of an image. There are two types of image processing Digital Image processing and Analog image processing. In Digital Image processing computer algorithms are applied to extract information from images [4].

heading: 1.3.1 IOT
content: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of interconnected devices that can col- lect, transmit , and process data. [5]An operating system (OS) is essentially the brain and central nervous system of any computing system, including laptops, servers, smartphones, and sensors, and is available in both commercial and open- source varieties. The OS manages all of a system’s hardware and software and allocates all resources, including processing, memory, and storage. An IoT oper- ating systemis an OS designed for the particular demands and specifications of IoT devices and applications. It is critical for connectivity, security, networking, storage, remote device management, and other IoT system needs. Some IoT op- erating systems also have real-time processing capabilities and are referred to as a real-time operating system, or RTOS .

heading: 1.3.2 RTOS
content: A Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) is an IoT operating system that works under strict constraints of IoT devices with limited memory and processing power. RTOS is designed to operate in real-time to transmit and process data. Many IOT devices use RTOS to run small hardware such as Micro-controllers in automation

heading: 1.4 Problem Statement
content: In traditional color production, colors are created by manually mixing primary colors in specific ratios based on color codes. However, this manual process is prone to human error and sometimes results in incorrect proportions. Additionally, there may be instances where the ratio of a particular color component exceeds the desired amount. Hence, there is a need to develop an automatic machine that minimizes human effort to proceed with the process of color production.

heading: 1.5 Objective of the Project
content: The objective of this project is to design and implement an IoT-based real-time color recognition and mixing machine, aimed at automating and optimizing the color mixing process. The primary goal is to develop a system that accurately identifies desired colors, mixes primary colors in the required ratio to achieve the desired hue, and enhances precision in color production. By integrating with IOT technology, the system will enable real-time monitoring and control, ensuring timely adjustments and minimizing waste during the mixing process.Key objec- tives include the development of algorithms for precise color recognition, integra- tion of sensors and actuators for automated color mixing, and implementation of a user-friendly interface for easy operation and monitoring. Additionally, the

heading: Color Production Machine
content: system will focus on optimizing resource utilization, reducing material waste, and ensuring consistency and accuracy in color production.

heading: Literature Review
content: Since the early 1970s, color has played a pivotal role in our daily lives. However, during that era, the process of obtaining colors was laborious, requiring manual mixing of primary colors. This process causes many errors [7]. To streamline the resultant color in production, we embarked on an extensive research journey, exploring diverse methodologies. This comprehensive review has unveiled several promising avenues for automating color production. Our project comprises two primary components: image processing and color mixing using primary colors. In this literature review, we will delve into various techniques and strategies aimed at realizing the automation of this machine.

heading: 2.1.1 RGB Model-based approach
content: [8]The RGB (Red, Green, Blue) model is a fundamental color model used ex- tensively in digital imaging and displays. In this model, colors are generated by combining varying intensities of the primary hues: red, green, and blue. Each color component is represented by an 8-bit value, ranging from 0 to 255, where 0 signifies the absence of the color and 255 indicates maximum intensity. By ad- justing the intensity of each primary color, a wide spectrum of secondary colors and shades can be produced. For instance, mixing full-intensity red and green light results in yellow, while mixing all three primary colors at full intensity yields white light. This additive color mixing principle forms the basis of RGB color representation in electronic displays, such as computer monitors, televisions, and smartphone screens. Furthermore, the RGB color model is device-dependent, meaning that the per-

heading: Color Production Machine
content: ceived colors can vary between different devices due to differences in hardware and calibration. To address this issue, color spaces like sRGB (standard Red Green Blue) have been developed to standardize color representation across de- vices. Additionally, RGB values can be represented in various formats, includ- ing hexadecimal notation (RRGGBB), which condenses each color component into a two-digit hexadecimal number, facilitating color specification in web de- sign and digital graphics. The RGB model’s versatility and widespread adoption make it indispensable in various fields, including photography, graphic design, and multimedia production, where accurate color reproduction and consistency are paramount [9].

heading: 2.1.2 CMYK Model-based approach
content: [10]The CMYK (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Key/Black) color model serves as the cornerstone for color reproduction in printing applications. In this model, col- ors are generated through the subtractive process, wherein each primary color subtracts certain wavelengths of light from the white background to produce a desired hue. Cyan, magenta, and yellow are the primary colors, representing dif- ferent portions of the visible spectrum. Cyan absorbs red wavelengths, magenta absorbs green wavelengths, and yellow absorbs blue wavelengths. By combining these primary colors in varying proportions, a wide array of hues can be achieved, covering most of the visible spectrum. The ”Key” or black component is introduced to improve color depth and contrast in printing. Unlike traditional RGB models used for digital displays, CMYK is optimized for the absorption characteristics of printing inks on paper. The addi- tion of black ink, which absorbs all visible wavelengths, enables richer blacks and enhances details in printed images. This black component also aids in reproducing true black without relying solely on the combination of cyan, magenta, and yellow, which may result in a muddy or darkened appearance. Overall, the CMYK model revolutionizes color reproduction in printing by offering a versatile and efficient

heading: Literature Review
content: method for translating digital images into vibrant, accurate prints [11]. Figure 2.1: CMYK Color Model

Central to their methodology was the utilization of the HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) color model for color detection. This model offers a perceptually uniform representation of colors, crucial for accurately dis- cerning hues, saturation levels, and brightness. The algorithm developed for this system initially transformed the input images captured by the web camera into the HSV color space. Subsequently, the analysis primarily focused on the Hue component within this space, which denotes the type of color present in the scene. By interpreting the Hue values, the system could effectively identify specific colors, such as blue or green, which were pertinent for object classification. Upon color detection, corre- sponding commands (’G’ for blue and ’B’ for green) were dispatched to an Arduino microcontroller. The Arduino, in turn, activated a relay mechanism, interfacing with the DSQC I/O CARD, thus facilitating precise manipulation of the indus-

heading: 2.2.1 Image Segmentation
content: Image segmentation divides images into regions or objects for annotation. Tech- niques include region-based, edge-based, thresholding, and feature-based cluster- ing. [14] Region-based segmentation divides images into regions with similar prop- erties, suitable for noisy images. Edge-based segmentation focuses on abrupt inten- sity changes, providing accurate edge detection. Thresholding converts multilevel images into binary images based on intensity thresholds. Feature-based segmen- tation involves clustering methods like K-means and Fuzzy C-Mean for grouping similar objects.

heading: 2.2.2 Image Classification
content: Image classification extracts information, labels, and pixels from images based on user needs. Various approaches like artificial neural networks, expert systems, and fuzzy logic are used. Classification can be per pixel, sub-pixel, or field, de- pending on the required resolution. Techniques include supervised (using spectral signatures) and unsupervised (machine-driven) classification.

heading: 2.2.3 Image Compression
content: Image compression reduces data redundancy for efficient storage and transmis- sion. Lossless compression maintains image quality, suitable for medical imaging and technical drawings. Lossy compression sacrifices some image quality for faster transmission. Common lossy compression techniques include JPEG, which uses

heading: Literature Review
content: discrete cosine transform, and Wavelet transform, which divides data into fre- quency components for analysis

heading: 2.2.4 Image Restoration
content: Image Restoration aims to obtain a clean image from a noisy or corrupted one. Techniques include inverse filtering, Wiener filtering, wavelet-based restoration, and blind deconvolution. Restoration addresses degradation caused by sensor noise, misfocus, or atmospheric disturbance. Methods like Wiener filtering offer a balance between denoising and inverse filtering for optimal results.

heading: 2.2.5 Image Enhancement
content: Image Enhancement improves image quality using filters and restoration models. Spatial domain enhancement adjusts pixel values based on surrounding intensity. Frequency domain enhancement involves techniques like intensity transformation and histogram processing.Image acquisition is the initial step in any visualization scheme, commonly performed in real-time for 3D data.

heading: 2.2.6 Image Transformation
content: Image Transformation involves arithmetic or mathematical operations to change image representation. Popular transformations include Fourier, Hough, and Radon transforms, along with arithmetic operations. Feature detection and image match- ing are crucial in machine vision and robotics. Scale Invariant Feature Trans- form (SIFT) is popular for matching features across images.SIFT addresses rota- tion, scale, and affine transformations for feature matching. Despite its efficiency, SIFT’s computational complexity poses challenges for real-time applications

heading: 3.1 Overview
content: The IoT-Based Real-Time Fully Automatic Color Recognition and Pigment Mix- ing Machine operates through a seamless workflow integrating image processing, IoT, and automation. The process begins with image acquisition using a high- resolution camera or sensor to capture the target object, ensuring accurate RGB data extraction. The system converts these RGB values into the CMYK model for precise pigment mixing and the HSV model for perceptual color understand- ing. [15]IoT integration enables real-time monitoring and remote control, allowing operators to adjust and supervise the process via a user-friendly interface. Finally, automated actuators and motors dispense exact amounts of cyan, magenta, yel- low, and black pigments, ensuring precise color matching and minimizing waste through a closed-loop feedback system. This workflow enhances efficiency, accu- racy, and resource optimization in color production.

heading: 3.3 Block Explanation
content: The IoT-Based Real-Time Fully Automatic Color Recognition and Pigment Mix- ing Machine operates through an integrated system involving a mobile application, image processing, cloud communication, micro-controller ESP32 dev module, an industrial flow meter (932-9521-A Hall Effect), and real-time feedback through sensors to produce the desired color. First, the user uploads an image of the color through the mobile application. The image is enhanced and its RGB (Red, Green, and Blue) values are extracted using various image processing techniques, such as bilateral filtering to remove noise and improve clarity. Then, the K-means clustering algorithm determines the optimal number of color clusters. A Homomorphic Filter is applied to brighten the image, and the RGB values are mathematically converted into CMYK values using relevant equations. This conversion is essential for pigment mixing and is done in real-time for accurate color matching. Once the CMYK values are determined,

heading: Color Production Machine
content: the mobile application sends this information to a cloud server, which connects the application and the system’s hardware components. The cloud server then transmits the real-time CMYK values to the ESP32 micro- controller. The micro-controller processes these values and triggers the relay mod- ule, which controls the air pump responsible for dispensing the correct amounts of each pigment (cyan, magenta, yellow, and black) into the mixing container. The air pump is activated through the relay module by the ESP32, ensuring that the required amounts of pigment are released accurately. The industrial flow sensor (932-9521-A Hall Effect) is used to measure the flow of each pigment as it is dis- pensed. This sensor ensures that the correct amount of pigment is released by measuring the liquid flow and providing feedback to the micro-controller. If the sensor detects that the target volume has been reached, it sends a signal to stop the air pump. Once all the pigments are added to the mixing container, the mixing motor is turn on. The mixing time and speed depend on the amount of pigment used, ensuring they blend properly to create the desired color. The system works automatically in real-time, needing little human effort, to ensure accurate and efficient color mixing. With the help of IoT, the system keeps everything monitored and controlled, reducing waste and making the process smooth and reliable.

heading: 3.3.1 Mobile Application
content: The application used in our project ”Internet of Things Based Real-Time Fully Automatic Color Identification and Paint Mixing Machine” allows users to upload images of desired colors and monitor the entire color mixing process. The ap- plication provides instant updates, displays RGB and CMYK values of extracted colors, and allows users to directly control or adjust the combination. To inter- act with applications with Python code, we can create a back-end server that runs Python-based imaging algorithms using a web framework such as Flask or Django. heading: 3.3.2 Image Processing
content: The image processing techniques used in our project include a combination of ad- vanced methods to ensure accurate color detection. Noise cancellation is applied using techniques such as bilateral filtering, which removes unwanted distortions while preserving edge details, ensuring a clear and precise input image for analy- sis. K-means clustering is employed for color segmentation, grouping similar pixel colors to identify dominant shades in the image. RGB values are extracted from the processed image and converted into CMYK for precise pigment mixing. Addi- tionally, transformations are used to analyze color attributes for better detection accuracy under varying lighting conditions. These image processing techniques work together to provide reliable and efficient color recognition for the system.

heading: 3.3.3 Cloud Server
content: we will use the Firebase Cloud Server which acts as a bridge between the mobile application and the ESP32 microcontroller, it enabling communication and data exchange. The mobile app extracts the RGB values from the user’s input, such as an image, processes them, and then sends the data to Firebase. The cloud server stores and manages this information in real time, ensuring it is accessible to the ESP32 module. The ESP32 retrieves the RGB values from Firebase and uses them to perform the required operations, such as controlling the relay module and air pump for pigment mixing. This integration ensures reliable and efficient data flow, allowing for accurate color matching and automated system control.

heading: 3.3.4 Micro-controller
content: In your IoT-Based Real-Time Fully Automatic Color Recognition and Pigment Mixing Machine, the ESP32 microcontroller plays a crucial role for performing tasks. It facilitates the real-time exchange of data between the app, cloud server, and hardware components. The ESP32 receives commands from the app via the cloud server, such as adjusting pigment ratios or starting the color mixing pro- cess. Simultaneously, it collects data from sensors, such as feedback from the color recognition module, and transmits this information to the cloud for monitoring and analysis. The ESP32 also controls the motors and actuators responsible for dis- pensing the pigments by using precise signals to ensure accurate mixing ratios. Its built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities enable seamless IoT integration, allowing remote control and real-time system monitoring through the app. Additionally, the ESP32 ensures synchronization between image processing outputs and phys- ical pigment mixing operations, making it a vital component for automating the workflow efficiently and reliably.

heading: 3.3.5 Flow Sensor
content: The 932-9521-A industrial water flow meter is a precision device used for accu- rately measuring the flow rate of water in industrial settings. It typically operates by monitoring water flow through a pipe using advanced sensors and this sensor support digital or analog output. Its ability to deliver real-time flow data makes it essential for processes requiring precise fluid control. In a real-time color recogni- tion and pigment mixing machine, this flow meter plays a critical role by ensuring the accurate measurement of water or other liquid components needed for mixing pigments. By providing real-time flow data, it helps maintain consistency in the pigment mixture, ensuring the correct concentration and color quality in the final output. This integration enables the automation of pigment mixing with high accuracy and reproducibility.

heading: 3.3.6 Relay Module
content: The 2-channel relay module in my project acts as a switch to control the air pump using the low-voltage signals from the ESP32. When the user presses the push button, the ESP32 sends a HIGH signal to the relay, closing the circuit and allowing 12V power to flow to the air pump, turning it ON. The pump helps pressurize and push liquid through the system. Once the desired amount of liquid is dispensed, the ESP32 sends a LOW signal to the relay, which opens the circuit and stops the air pump. The relay allows the ESP32 to safely control high-voltage devices like the air pump without directly handling high-voltage power.

heading: 3.3.7 Air Flow Pump
content: In the project, the DC 12V water pump is used to help press and push the liquid through the system. This self-priming air pump is connected to the power supply, receiving 12V DC from the system. When the user presses the push button, the ESP32 sends a signal to a relay, which activates the pump. The diaphragm design of the pump allows it to draw liquid and push it through the tubing, making it ideal for moving liquids in a controlled manner. It ensures a steady flow of liquid, which is essential for precise measurements and mixing in the pigment mixing process. Once the required volume of liquid is dispensed, the relay deactivates the pump, stopping the flow.

heading: 3.3.8 Mixing Motor
content: The mixing motor is connected to the final container where all the pigments CMYK are combined. This motor is responsible for thoroughly blending the dis- pensed pigments to achieve a uniform and consistent final color. The mixing process ensures that the pigments are evenly distributed, eliminating any streaks or uneven shades that could occur due to insufficient mixing. Powered by the ESP32, the mixing motor operates based on the completion of the pigment dis-

Once the calculated amounts of each pigment are added to the container, the motor is activated to spin at a specific speed for a predetermined duration, ensuring optimal mixing. The motor speed and duration can be adjusted depending on the volume and viscosity of the pigments. heading: 4.1 Bilateral Filter
content: The bilateral filter is an advanced image processing technique used to smooth images and remore the noice in the picture and preserving edge details. This is particularly important in tasks like color recognition for our project , where clarity of the image is essential for accurate color extraction. In this report, we will explore the functionality of the bilateral filter, its parameters, the steps involved in applying it to an image, and the mathematical foundation behind it. The bilateral filter helps reduce noise and maintain high fidelity in color details, crucial for accurate RGB and CMYK extraction.

heading: 4.1.1 Overview of Bilateral Filter
content: The bilateral filter is a non-linear, edge-preserving, and noise-reducing filter that smooths an image while retaining sharp edges. Unlike traditional smoothing fil- ters that tend to blur edges, the bilateral filter takes into account both the spatial proximity of pixels and the intensity differences between them. This makes it par- ticularly useful in image processing tasks where you want to reduce noise without losing important details, such as edges or boundaries within an image. The bilateral filter operates based on three key components: d (Diameter of the Filter ) This is for the diameter of the pixel neighborhood used during filtering. Effect:A larger d considers a larger neighborhood for each pixel, potentially in- creasing the smoothing effect.Normally we select the value from 5 to 10.For larger image we select hight values. A smaller d restricts the filter to a smaller area, which can preserve details more effectively. Special Cases: If d is set to a non-positive value (e.g., d ¡= 0), it is computed from sigmaSpace.

heading: Color Production Machine
content: SigmaColor (Filter Sigma in Color Space) This parameter determines how sensitive the filter is to differences in intensity or color values. A larger sigmaColor allows the filter to consider a broader range of intensity differences as similar, leading to more aggressive smoothing.A smaller sigmaColor ensures that only pixels with very similar intensity values are smoothed together, preserving edges and fine details. SigmaSpace (Filter Sigma in Coordinate Space) This parameter specifies the ex- tent of the spatial smoothing (how far the filter considers neighboring pixels). A larger sigmaSpace leads to a smoother result over a larger area.A smaller sigmaS- pace ensures that only nearby pixels are considered for smoothing.

heading: 4.1.2 Function of Bilateral Filter
content: In our project, the bilateral filter is applied to the input image to enhance the clarity of the color details. The raw image captured from the camera may contain noise or distortions, especially in low-light conditions. Applying the bilateral filter to the image helps to: Reduce noise: By smoothing out the random variations in pixel values while preserving sharp edges. Enhance edge preservation: The filter ensures that important features such as boundaries between different colors or areas of high contrast are maintained. Improve color clarity: In the context of color recognition, clearer color separation is essential for accurate extraction of RGB values and their subsequent conversion to CMYK values. These improvements allow the system to better identify and extract the correct color components, ensuring that the pigment mixing process is precise and efficient.

heading: 4.1.3 Understanding the Bilateral Filter’s Parameters
content: The bilateral filter is governed by three main parameters that control its behavior: d (Diameter of the neighborhood): This parameter defines the size of the neighbor- hood around each pixel used for filtering. A larger value means that a larger region of neighboring pixels will influence the result for each pixel, leading to smoother

heading: Image Processing And Details
content: images but potentially blurring fine details if the value is too large. In contrast, smaller values will focus on smaller neighborhoods pixels, add more details but potentially leaving noise. sigma-color (Color Intensity Sensitivity): This parame- ter controls how strongly the filter considers the color intensity difference between pixels. Higher values of sigma-color allow pixels with larger intensity differences to influence each other, leading to stronger smoothing. Lower values cause the filter to add more color details but it result in less smoothing. sigma-space (Spatial dis- tance sensitivity): This parameter determines how much the filter is influenced by the spatial distance between pixels. A larger sigma-space value means that pixels further apart from each other in the image can influence the filter’s result, lead- ing to broader smoothing. Smaller values restrict the influence to nearby pixels, preserving more local features but potentially leaving noise.

heading: 4.1.4 Advantages
content: The bilateral filter is particularly beneficial for tasks in our project, such as color detection and noise removal. By preserving edges and smoothing regions with minimal intensity variation, the bilateral filter ensures that the important color features of the image remain intact. This is crucial when the system needs to accurately recognize and extract the RGB values to convert them into CMYK values for pigment mixing. Additionally, the bilateral filter is effective in scenarios where the image may contain noise due to factors like low lighting, camera distortion. By applying this filter, the system ensures that the noise is minimized without compromising the clarity of the edges, which is vital for achieving precise color matching in the pigment mixing process. In the bilateral filter enhances the quality of the image, making it suitable for further processing tasks such as segmentation, color extraction, and recognition, all of which are essential for the success of your color mixing machine. Recommended Parameter Values ranges When applying the bilateral filter, it’s important to select

heading: Color Production Machine
content: appropriate values for the parameters: d (Diameter of the neighborhood): Typical values range from 5 to 15. Larger values will result in broader smoothing but could lead to edge blurring. sigma-color (Color intensity sensitivity): Recommended values range from 50 to 150. Higher values allow more smoothing but may blur fine details. sigma-space (Spatial distance sensitivity): Values between 50 and 150 are typical, with larger values allowing the filter to consider a larger neighborhood of pixels.

heading: 4.2 k Clustering
content: K-Means Clustering is a method used to group data into k clusters based on how similar the data points are. It works by placing points into clusters so that each group is as tight and uniform as possible. The process repeats by assigning points to the closest cluster center and adjusting the cluster centers until they no longer change. This method is often used in tasks like image segmentation (grouping pixels by color), color reduction (simplifying the number of colors in an image), and customer grouping. It is a simple and effective technique, but user need to decide the number of cluster(k)in advance.

heading: 4.2.1 Function of K cluster
content: This code uses in K-Means clustering to group an image’s pixels into k color clusters. It is often used for tasks like reducing the number of colors in an image (color quantization) or dividing the image into different regions (segmentation). The function takes two inputs: the image and the desired number of clusters (k). First, the image is reshaped from its original 3D format (height, width, color channels) into a 2D array where each row represents a pixel’s RGB color values. This format is required for clustering. The pixel values are converted to float32 to ensure accuracy. The K-Means function from OpenCV is then applied to group the pixels into k clusters. The algorithm stops when either 100 iterations are completed or the cluster centers stop changing significantly (less than 0.2). Once clustering is done, the cluster centers (dominant colors) are converted back to integer RGB values. Each pixel in the image is then replaced with the color of its cluster center, resulting in a segmented image. This output image has only k distinct colors, making it useful for simplifying images or identifying the main colors present. The function returns the segmented image and the dominant color values.

heading: 4.2.2 Advantages
content: K-Means Clustering is a simple and easy-to understand algorithm, making it ideal for beginners and practical applications. It works quickly on small to medium- sized datasets, especially with a small number of clusters (k). The method is versatile, finding use in tasks like image segmentation, color reduction, and data grouping across different fields. It performs well when clusters are distinct and evenly distributed. Additionally, K-Means is adaptable to various types of data by adjusting the distance metric or scaling features. It also serves as a prepro- cessing tool by reducing data complexity, making it useful for further analysis or processing.When the k vlaues is increase then the cluter is increasing and at last the RGB values provide to user increase.

heading: 4.3 CLAHE filter
content: The filter used in this code is CLAHE (Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization), applied to each RGB channel of an image separately. CLAHE designed to improve the contrast of images while avoiding the amplification of noise.

heading: 4.3.1 Working
content: CLAHE enhances image contrast by dividing the image into small blocks or tiles (in this case, 8x8 tiles) and performing histogram equalization independently within each tile. This ensures that the contrast enhancement is localized, making CLAHE particularly useful for images with varying brightness or regions that need different levels of enhancement. To avoid over-amplifying noise in homogeneous areas, CLAHE introduces a clip limit to restrict the height of the histogram peaks. When pixel intensities exceed this clip limit, the excess is redistributed evenly across the histogram, preventing extreme brightness variations that could result from standard histogram equaliza- tion.

heading: 4.3.2 Application
content: In the code, CLAHE is applied to each of the Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) chan- nels independently. By enhancing each channel separately, the method preserves the color balance while improving overall contrast. After enhancement, the chan- nels are merged back into a single RGB image, resulting in an image that is visually more detailed and vibrant, particularly in regions with initially poor lighting or low contrast. In real-world scenarios, the input images of pigments may have uneven lighting, shadows, or low contrast, which can distort color information. CLAHE enhances the contrast of the RGB channels while maintaining the color balance, ensuring that the detected colors are closer to their true values. This is critical for a pigment mixing machine, as accurate color recognition is necessary to create precise color blends. By applying CLAHE, the RGB values become more distinguishable, even under challenging conditions, which improves the performance of the color recognition algorithms.

heading: 4.4 Gaussian Blur Filter
content: The filter is a low-pass filter.It is commonly used in image processing to minize the noise, smooth an image, or prepare it for further processing like edge detection. A Gaussian Blur applies a convolution operation to the image using a Gaussian kernel. The kernel is a matrix generated based on the Gaussian function, which gives more weight to the central pixels and less weight to distant ones, creating a natural blur effect. The size of the kernel and the standard deviation () determine the degree of blurring. Larger kernel sizes and higher values result in stronger blurring effects.

heading: 4.4.1 Application
content: The Gaussian Blur filter has versatile applications in image processing due to its ability to smooth and reduce noise while preserving essential features. By attenuating high-frequency components, it minimizes the impact of random noise and sharp, unwanted details, making images appear smoother and cleaner. This is particularly useful in reducing visual artifacts or distractions that can interfere with subsequent analysis. Gaussian Blur is also commonly used in image preprocessing. It prepares an image for tasks like edge detection or segmentation by eliminating small, insignif- icant details that could confuse algorithms, while maintaining larger, significant features. Additionally, Gaussian Blur is employed in visual effects, such as creating soft-focus or dreamy aesthetics in images, enhancing their artistic or professional appeal. These attributes make it a fundamental tool in fields ranging from pho- tography and graphics design to computer vision.

heading: 4.5 Homomorphic Filter
content: The filter implemented in this code is called the Homomorphic Filter. It is com- monly used in image enhancement techniques, particularly to correct non-uniform

heading: Color Production Machine
content: lighting conditions and enhance details. Homomorphic filtering operates in the frequency domain and is effective in separating and enhancing the high-frequency components (representing details and edges) while suppressing low-frequency com- ponents (representing smooth variations like lighting and shadows).

heading: 4.5.1 Working
content: The homomorphic filter begins by transforming the image into the frequency do- main. Before applying the transform, a logarithmic function is used to convert multiplicative intensity variations (caused by uneven illumination) into additive variations. This makes it possible to treat the lighting and reflectance components separately in the frequency domain. In the frequency domain, a Gaussian high-pass filter is applied. This filter em- phasizes high-frequency components (fine details and textures) and attenuates low-frequency components (gradual intensity variations like lighting). The filter’s parameters, such as gammaL, gammaH, and d0, control the extent of suppres- sion and enhancement. After filtering, the modified frequency data is transformed back to the spatial domain using the inverse Fourier Transform. Finally, an ex- ponential function reverses the earlier logarithmic transformation, reconstructing the enhanced image.

heading: 4.5.2 Application
content: Homomorphic filtering is widely used in scenarios where images suffer from poor or uneven lighting, such as in medical imaging, satellite imagery, and photographs taken in challenging lighting conditions. By enhancing details and normalizing illumination, it improves image quality and makes features more discernible for both human observation and computational analysis. The filter also retain the natural and origial look of image.

heading: 6.1.1 Introduction to Control System
content: The control system for our project is designed to automate the pigment mixing and dispensing process with high accuracy and real-time monitoring. The sys- tem is centered around the ESP32 microcontroller, which serves as the brain of the operation. All input and output components are interfaced with the ESP32, including the push button, relay modules for controlling motors, flow sensors for measuring liquid volume, and an I2C-based 16x2 LCD for user feedback. The architecture follows a sequential execution pattern. Once powered on, the system initializes all components and waits for user interaction through the push button. Upon activation, the ESP32 begins a series of dispensing operations by triggering each motor (associated with specific pigment colors) one by one through relay control. As the liquid flows, flow sensors measure the exact amount dis- pensed, and this information is constantly monitored and updated on the LCD. The process continues until each motor has dispensed a predefined amount of liq- uid (e.g., 50ml), after which the system stops the respective motor and moves to the next. The architecture is modular in design, allowing for easy scaling and debugging. Each component performs a defined function, and the ESP32 ensures centralized decision-making. This structured approach not only simplifies hardware integra- tion but also allows the control logic to be flexible and adaptable for future im- provements. Control System and ESP32 Algorithm

heading: 6.1.2 Role of Automation in Dispensing Mechanism
content: Automation plays a central role in enhancing the efficiency, accuracy [16], and reli- ability of the dispensing mechanism in our project. In manual systems, controlling the flow of liquids such as pigments requires continuous human supervision [17], which can lead to errors in volume measurement, inconsistent results, and in- efficiency. By introducing automation, these challenges are minimized through precise electronic control and sensor feedback. In the designed system, automation is achieved through the integration of the ESP32 microcontroller, which controls the relay-operated motors, reads input from flow sensors, and manages the user interface via the LCD. The system automati- cally starts dispensing when the user presses the push button, measures the exact quantity of each pigment being dispensed, and stops each motor once the desired volume (e.g., 50ml) is reached. This level of automation ensures that each pigment is dispensed accurately without the need for human intervention during the process. [18] It not only improves re- peatability and reduces human error but also enhances overall productivity. More- over, the real-time LCD feedback allows the user to monitor the process visually, making the system more interactive and user-friendly. In summary, automation transforms the dispensing mechanism into a smart sys- tem that is self-regulating, precise, and scalable, which is especially beneficial for applications requiring consistent and reliable mixing of multiple liquids.

heading: 6.1.3 Importance of Real-Time Monitoring
content: Real-time monitoring is a crucial aspect of any automated system, especially in applications involving fluid dispensing where precision and timing are essential. In this project, real-time monitoring is implemented through an LCD that con- tinuously displays the system’s current status, the motor in operation, and the volume of liquid dispensed from each motor. This ensures that the user remains

heading: Color Production Machine
content: informed about the system’s progress at every stage. The primary benefit of real-time monitoring is that it enables immediate feedback. If a motor fails to operate, a sensor stops responding, or the volume being dis- pensed does not match the expected amount, the issue can be detected instantly. This prevents wastage, avoids mixing errors, and enhances the reliability of the system. Additionally, by displaying the actual quantity of pigment dispensed through each motor, the system helps maintain consistency across different batches. Once the dispensing is complete, the LCD displays “Complete,” signaling the end of the process. This clear visual communication allows the user to operate the system confidently without needing technical intervention during every cycle. In short, real-time monitoring enhances system transparency, improves fault de- tection, and ensures high operational accuracy—making it a vital component of the overall dispensing mechanism. subsectionHardware Configuration and Com- ponents

heading: 6.2.1 ESP32 Microcontroller Overview
content: The ESP32 microcontroller is the core processing unit of the pigment dispensing system, responsible for handling all control logic, signal processing, and component coordination. It is a powerful, low-cost microcontroller with integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities, making it ideal for real-time embedded applications like this one. The ESP32 features multiple general-purpose input/output (GPIO) pins, digital and analog interfaces, and high-speed processing capability [19], which allows it to manage multiple sensors, actuators, and communication devices simultaneously. In this project, the ESP32 is used to control the relays connected to the motors, read signals from flow sensors, receive input from the push button, and update

Its dual-core processor and fast clock speed enable smooth multitasking, which is essential for time-sensitive operations such as measuring the exact volume of liquid being dispensed in real time. The microcontroller runs a programmed algorithm that governs the sequence of motor activation, monitors fluid flow, and determines when to stop each motor based on sensor feedback. Moreover, its compatibility with the Arduino IDE makes the ESP32 programmer- friendly, allowing efficient testing, debugging, and updates to the system. Due to its versatility, small form factor, and reliable performance, the ESP32 was chosen as the brain of this dispensing system.

heading: 6.2.2 Sensor Integration for Liquid Flow Measurement
content: Accurate measurement of liquid flow is essential for a precise and controlled pig- ment dispensing system. In this project, flow sensors are used to monitor the quantity of liquid dispensed by each motor. These sensors generate pulses based on the flow rate, where a fixed number of pulses corresponds to a specific volume of liquid (e.g., 50 ml). This pulse-based feedback allows the ESP32 microcontroller to track how much liquid has passed through each line.

heading: Color Production Machine
content: Each flow sensor is directly connected to a dedicated GPIO pin on the ESP32. As the liquid passes through, the rotating mechanism inside the sensor produces electrical pulses, which are then counted in real-time by the ESP32 using interrupt routines or polling methods. Once the pulse count reaches the threshold value representing the target volume, the ESP32 deactivates the corresponding motor, ensuring that no excess pigment is dispensed. This integration not only enhances the accuracy of the dispensing system but also provides essential data to be displayed on the LCD screen [20], allowing the user to visually monitor the flow. The sensor data plays a crucial role in achieving consistent and repeatable results across multiple dispensing cycles.

heading: 6.2.3 Relay Module for Motor Control
content: In this project, the relay module acts as an essential interface between the low- power ESP32 microcontroller and the high-power DC motors used for liquid dis- pensing. Since the ESP32 cannot directly drive motors due to its limited current- handling capability, a relay module is used to safely switch each motor on or off. Each motor responsible for dispensing a specific pigment (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black, White) is connected to the output of a relay channel. The relay’s input control pins are wired to designated GPIO pins on the ESP32. When the ESP32 sends a HIGH signal to a relay control pin, the relay activates, allowing current to flow to the motor and initiating the dispensing process. The relays used are of the Normally Open (NO) type, meaning the motor remains off by default. Only when the ESP32 triggers the relay will the motor receive power. This ensures precise control and energy efficiency, as motors only operate when required. The relay module plays a key role in automating the flow sequence. As each flow sensor detects that the desired amount of liquid (e.g., 50 ml) has been dispensed, the ESP32 turns off the corresponding relay, immediately stopping that motor. This ensures reliable, timed operation of the entire system.

heading: 6.3.4 Control Based on Flow Sensor Data
content: The pigment dispensing system uses real-time flow sensor data to precisely control the amount of fluid dispensed by each motor. This approach ensures that each pigment (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black, and White) is delivered in the exact quantity required to achieve the desired color mix. Each pigment container is equipped with a flow sensor connected to the ESP32

Control System and ESP32 Algorithm microcontroller. These flow sensors generate pulses as liquid flows through them. The number of pulse rate is directly proportional to the volume of fluid that has passed through the sensor. By counting these pulses using interrupt service routines (ISRs), the system continuously calculates the flowed volume. Working Mechanism Pulse-to-Volume Conversion: Each sensor has a prede- fined pulses-per-milliliter ratio (e.g., 7.5 pulses/ml). This ratio is used to convert the total pulse count into the volume dispensed in milliliters. During the dis- pensing process, the system checks the flowed volume approximately every 100 milliseconds. This allows for responsive control and real-time updates to the user via the LCD. As soon as the flowed volume for a given pigment reaches the target volume, the corresponding relay is deactivated, stopping the motor. If the sensor fails to reach the desired volume within a maximum time limit (e.g., 30 seconds), the motor is stopped to avoid overflow The control algorithm ensures that only one motor runs at a time, preventing electrical overload and ensuring accurate volume tracking for each pigment individually.

heading: 6.4 Control Based on Flow Sensor Data
content: Effective communication and precise data handling are critical. The ESP32 micro- controller is responsible for managing communication between various hardware components, including flow sensors, relays, LCD display, and the mobile app. Sen- sor readings, control commands, and system status updates are managed in real time to ensure accurate pigment mixing and a smooth user experience. Data flow begins with input received from the user interface, continues with real- time sensor feedback during the dispensing process, and concludes with visual output to both the LCD and the app interface. The system architecture supports reliable data transmission and synchronization among all components.

heading: 6.4.1 Sensor Data Acquisition
content: Sensor data acquisition plays a vital role in the real-time monitoring and control of pigment dispensing. Each of the five flow sensors (C, M, Y, K, W) is connected to a specific pin on the ESP32. These sensors emit digital pulses as fluid flows through them. The ESP32 is configured to detect and count these pulses using interrupts for high-speed and accurate response. Acquisition Process: Interrupt Configuration: Each flow sensor pin is attached to an interrupt routine. This ensures that every pulse generated by the sensor is captured without missing data, even if the main program is executing other tasks. Pulse Counting: For each pulse detected, a global counter variable is incremented. This value represents the total number of pulses received since the start of dispensing for a particular pigment. Volume Calculation: Using a predefined calibration factor (e.g., 7.5 pulses per ml), the system converts the pulse count into an accurate volume measurement in milliliters. Real-Time Monitoring: Every 100 milliseconds, the system checks the flowed volume against the target volume. Once the required volume is reached, the sensor stops contributing to the count, and the motor is turned off.

heading: 7.2.1 Overview of multimodule system
content: General introduction to using CMYKW In the complete pigment mixing system, five hardware modules are used corresponding to the colors Cyan (C), Magenta (M), Yellow (Y), Black (K), and White (W). Each module consists of a motor connected to a pigment container, a relay for switching, and a flow sensor for volume monitoring. These modules work together in a sequential process controlled by the ESP32 microcontroller to ensure accurate dispensing of each pigment. The transition from a single-module prototype to a five-module system was neces- sary to achieve full-color mixing capabilities. Each module is independently wired but controlled through a unified program logic. The ESP32 manages motor acti- vation based on input signals and monitors flow sensor data to stop each motor precisely after dispensing 50ml of pigment. This multi-module integration allows

Hardware and Computational Analysis the system to replicate colors extracted from images with high accuracy, forming the foundation of the automated color mixing solution. Overview of Multi-Module System The primary objective of the multi-module sys- tem is to accurately reproduce desired colors using the CMYKW (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black, and White) color model. This model is widely used in printing and other physical media because it can generate a broad spectrum of colors by com- bining different proportions of these base pigments.

heading: Figure 7.3: Multi-Module System
content: In the system, each pigment is handled by a dedicated hardware module equipped with its own motor, relay, and flow sensor. The motor dispenses the pigment, the relay enables controlled activation, and the flow sensor monitors the quantity of pigment released. Once the target volume is reached, the system automatically stops the motor, ensuring precise and consistent color mixing.

heading: 7.2.2 Relay, Motor and flow sensor Integration for All Modules
content: In the multi-module system, each module is equipped with its own motor, relay, and flow sensor. The motor is used to control the flow of each color from its container, while the relay acts as a switching device that turns the motor on or off based on the system’s signal. The flow sensor is used to measure how much color has been dispensed. When the required amount of pigment is released, the sensor sends a signal back to the microcontroller to stop the motor. This setup is repeated for all five modules, which include Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black, and White [21]. The system uses the same logic for each module to make sure every color flows in the correct amount. By using this method, the system ensures accurate and automatic color mixing for any desired shade based on the CMYKW color model. Overview of Multi-Module System To control the five motors for Cyan (C), Magenta (M), Yellow (Y), Black (K), and White (W), five separate relays are used. Each relay is connected to one motor and also connected with there corresponding flow sensor . The relays act like automatic switches which turn on and off according to the flow sensor requirements . Each relay is connected to a specific GPIO pin of the ESP32. When the ESP32 sends a HIGH or LOW signal to a pin, the corresponding relay gets activated or deactivated. This starts or stops the motor attached to it. This setup helps to control the flow of each color individually, ensuring the correct color quantity is dispensed during the pigment mixing process. Mention relay pins and control logic In our project, five relays are used to control five motors for the CMYKW color model. Each relay is connected to a specific GPIO pin on the ESP32. The pin numbers are: D15 for Cyan, D2 for Magenta, D4 for Yellow, RX2 for Black, and TX2 for White. These pins are used to send signals from the ESP32 to control the relays [22].The sensor output is connected like C is connected with GPIO 32 ,M is connected with 33 ,y is connected with 25,k is connected with 26 and w is

Hardware and Computational Analysis connected with 27 pin. The control logic is very simple. When the ESP32 sends a high signal to the relay pin, the relay turns ON and allows current to flow to the motor, starting it. When the required amount of color is dispensed, the ESP32 sends a HIGH signal, which turns the relay OFF and stops the motor. This logic is applied to each color module to ensure accurate color flow for the pigment mixing system.

heading: 7.2.3 Flow Sensor Setup and Monitoring
content: Each flow sensor in the system is connected to a separate GPIO pin of the ESP32 and is assigned to a specific color module. The purpose of these sensors is to measure how much color has been dispensed by each motor. As soon as a sensor detects that the required amount of liquid (e.g., 50ml) has passed through, it sends a signal to the ESP32 [23], which then stops the motor by turning off the relay. The pin assignments for the flow sensors are as follows: Pin 32 for Cyan, Pin 33 for Magenta, Pin 25 for Yellow, Pin 26 for Black, and Pin 27 for White. These connections help the system monitor each color individually and ensure the correct amount is released from each module during the color mixing process.

heading: Monitoring
content: Flow sensors work by generating pulses as the liquid flows through them. Inside each sensor, there is a small turbine or mechanism that rotates when liquid passes. Every rotation produces a digital pulse on the sensor’s output wire. These pulses are sent to the ESP32 through GPIO pins, and the ESP32 counts how many pulses are received. The number of pulses is directly related to the amount of liquid that has passed through the sensor. For example, a certain number of pulses might equal 1 milliliter of liquid. By using this method, the ESP32 can calculate the total volume of liquid dispensed by each module. When the pulse count reaches the desired value (like 50ml), the ESP32 sends a signal to stop the motor by turning off the relay. This monitoring system ensures precise control over how much of

heading: 7.2.4 Push Button Triggering System
content: The push button triggering system is used to manually start the entire pigment dispensing process. A normally closed (NC) push button is connected to a specific GPIO pin on the ESP32, typically D13. When the button is pressed, it changes the input signal at that pin, which the ESP32 detects as a trigger to begin the color mixing operation. Once the button is pressed, the ESP32 activates the relays one by one, turning ON the motors for each color module. The flow sensors monitor the amount of liquid being dispensed, and the system turns OFF each motor automatically after the required volume is reached. This push-button setup gives the user a simple way to control when the system starts running, making it user-friendly and efficient. Explain how pressing the button starts the full sequence. When the user presses the push button, the ESP32 detects a change in the input signal on the button’s GPIO pin (like D13). This signal tells the microcontroller to begin the entire dispensing sequence. The ESP32 first turns ON the relay connected to the Cyan motor, allowing the pigment to flow. At the same time, the flow sensor for Cyan starts sending pulses to the ESP32. The microcontroller counts these pulses, and when the required amount (like 50ml) is reached, it turns OFF the relay and stops the Cyan motor. After that, it automatically moves to the next color (Magenta), and the same process repeats for Yellow, Black, and White. So, by pressing the button once, the full cycle for all five modules runs one after the other without needing any more input from the user.

Along with the motor status, the LCD will also show the quantity of liquid being dispensed, helping the user monitor the flow in real time. heading: 8.1 Goal 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure
content: Goal 9 of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals focuses on building resilient infrastructure, promoting inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and fostering innovation. Our final year project directly contributes to this goal by developing a smart, automated pigment mixing machine that integrates real-time image processing, RGB to CMYK conversion, and sensor-controlled motor dis- pensing using ESP32 microcontroller technology. The innovation lies in its ability to analyze an image [21], extract dominant color values, and control the flow of pigments precisely, minimizing human error and material wastage. Our project promotes sustainable industrial practices by automating what is tra- ditionally a manual and error-prone process in printing, painting, or textile indus- tries. By implementing flow sensors that stop each pigment after dispensing ex- actly 50ml, we introduce precision engineering and smart feedback systems, which are key components in modern industry. Additionally, our system leverages the power of IoT (Internet of Things), which is central to the digital transformation of infrastructure in both developing and developed countries. To achieve this goal on a larger scale, industries should invest in automated systems that reduce reliance on manual labor, enhance accuracy, and decrease resource consumption. Encouraging research and supporting student-led innovations — like this project — can help scale such technologies. Furthermore, partnerships between academia and industry are crucial to accelerate the adoption of these intelligent systems in real-world scenarios.

heading: 8.2 Goal 12: Responsible Consumption and Production
content: Goal 12 emphasizes ensuring sustainable consumption and production patterns. Our project supports this goal by reducing pigment waste through automated color mixing based on calculated RGB and CMYK values. Traditional methods of pigment mixing often lead to overuse, human error, and leftover materials, all of which contribute to environmental damage and economic inefficiency. Our machine dispenses only the required quantity of each pigment using calibrated flow sensors, thus minimizing resource usage and eliminating unnecessary waste. By integrating sensors that detect the exact amount of fluid dispensed, we ensure optimal use of raw materials, which is a core principle of sustainable production. The automation of the process further ensures that each operation is repeatable and consistent, reducing errors and helping maintain quality standards without overconsumption. To promote Goal 12 on a wider scale, industries must shift toward data-driven production systems that are guided by real-time feedback and automation. Public awareness and education about sustainable manufacturing methods also play a vital role. Projects like ours demonstrate that smart design and technological innovation can directly lead to more sustainable practices in production.

heading: 8.3 Goal 13: Climate Action
content: Goal 13 of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals calls for urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. Our project contributes to this goal by promoting energy-efficient automation and minimizing material wastage, which indirectly reduces the carbon footprint associated with pigment production and industrial processing. By ensuring accurate color dispensing using flow sensors and ESP32 microcontroller control, our system avoids excess use of pigments, reducing the environmental burden caused by overproduction, chemical runoff, and improper disposal.

UN Sustainable Development Goals In addition, by integrating smart technology into traditionally manual systems, our project supports a shift toward sustainable, low-emission practices. The reduced need for reprocessing due to human error, and the precise handling of materials, means fewer resources are consumed and less energy is wasted. Projects like this highlight how innovation at even the student level can contribute to climate- resilient solutions in industry and manufacturing.

heading: 1. Introduction
content: Software-defined networking (SDN) is a term in which we can make our network more flexible as compared to our traditional networks. The SDN help us to respond quickly to changing business requirements. Software Defined Networking provided us an approach in building, designing and managing network. It enables us to separate forwarding plane and control plane. Also, it provides us the ability to directly program the network thus giving us an impression of underlying structure for network services and application. In SDN, we can change the flow of traffic without touching the switch and routers of network. Now, the question is why SDN still not implemented in Lahore or Pakistan? Because our infrastructure is not ready yet for SDN technology because if we use SDN then we have to change our hardware and software as well which is not possible or it costs too much. Also, our organizations still not ready for this and also because of insufficient SDN support skills. In this final year project, we aim to design an SDN Network for COMSATS’s different campuses. First of all, we will make a COMSATS’s network of two or more than two campuses and then we will generate security threats like DDoS attacks. DDoS is short for Di stributed Denial of Service.  DDoS is a type of DOS attack where multiple compromised systems, which are often infected with a Trojan, are used to target a single system causing a Denial of Service (DoS)  attack. After generating the attacks, we will first s tudy the attack patterns and then generate some prevention scheme for blocking the attacks. We have proposed a new algorithm for prevention of DDOS attack. We will be identifying user types. It will detect if a user is an attacker or not. If the user is attacker, then we block it else it is allowed access.

heading: 3. Hybrid
content: In our case we are using hybrid approach because our network is consisting of 4 switches and 12 hosts so it would be difficult for them to ping each other.

heading:  Proactive:
content: The proactive methodology is a decent methodology as it introduces flows dependent on the present network environment before the packet arrived at a specific switch. The proactive is great methodology as it introduces flows dependent on the present system condition before the packet came to at a specific switch. In Proactive methodology, flows are populated early, i.e., before the packet of another stream arrives. Loss of control association does not disturb traffic.

heading:  Reactive:
content: When the new flow of packet came in to the switch, the OpenFlow switch looks for that flow into the flow table, if flow matches, then packet is allowed to pass. However, if the switch doesn’t recognize the flow, it creates a packet -in message and send it towards the controller for further instructions. As it is a reactive approach so a new flow is installed in switch for that flow via packet -out message from the controller. At the point when the new flow of packets reaches the switch, the OpenFlow switch searches for that flows into the flow table, in the event that flow matches, packet is permitted to pass. In any case, if the switch doesn't perceive the flow, it makes a packet in message and send it towards the controller for further directions. In reactive if another flow is introduced in switch for that flow from the controller.

heading:  Hybrid
content: Hybrid flow method is the combination of both proactiv e and reactive approaches. This approach is considered to be very flexible approach as compare to other approaches, because, it has the functionality of both approaches. It installs basic flows even before communication is started like proactive approach a nd when communication starts it also installs flows for those hosts whose flows are not installed proactively, providing great flexibility, robustness and reduce delays. For hybrid approach, spanning_tree module is utilized which has a capacity of running  l2_learning, topo_proactive and disclosure module inside it. As the modules of proactive and receptive methodologies are running inside a similar module, thus, it gives the usefulness of hybrid approach. First topo_proactive and disclosure modules introdu ce streams before correspondence and after that l2_learning introduces streams when communication begins.

As proactively installed flows take space in TCAM but their expiry time is low because in need reactive flows can be installed so there should be enough space for reactive flows also. 2. Rolling out improvements to the directing of information through the network before usage turns out to be too high can moderate potential execution issues.

heading:  DDOS
content: DDOS (Denial of Service) attack is a cyber-attack in which the attacker tries to make the network or machines unavailable to its user by generating unnecessary traffic  using host or devices connected to that network. They do this by creating congestion and consuming the available bandwidth. Large amounts of traffic are sent using botnets. Botnets re number of intern et connected devices that are used to steal data, send spam and perform DDOS. We used hping3 for ra ndom packet generator. It is used for testing of networks. W e used it for DDOS attack on our network. We launched hping 3 attack between h1 and h12. It flooded the controller with packets. Switches started to receive random ip address. Following was the result of DDOS attack.
So we purpose a solution against these attacks to secure our network and we discussed the algorithm below:

heading: Valid User:
content: User is part of database mean it is a member of network and sen d no of request and packets in a defined range.

heading: Invalid User:
content: User is not part of database but send no of request and packets in a defined range.

heading: Zombie User:
content: User is part of database mean it is a member of network but does not send no of request and packets in a defined range.

heading: Normal Zombie User:
content: User is not part of database mean it is not a member of network also does not send no of request and packets in a defined range.

heading: CALL GETINFO()
content: If (getInfo() matches with database entries && check()==true) Print “user is valid”, assign him Ip, connect him to network and add him in flow table. Else if (getInfo match with database && check() ==false) CALL CheckRequest() CALL CheckPackets() If (checkRequest()>3 && CheckRequest()>10) print “user is zombie”, block him from the network and also delete this user from database. Else if (getInfo not match with database && check()==true) print “user is new but valid’, assign him new ip from database and add him into flow table. Else if (getInfo not match with database && check()==false) print “user is normal zombie”, block him from the network.

heading: Functions
content:  CheckPackets() It checks the number of packets from host and switch. Checks the flow of packets and returns output as no of packets in integer. It will help us in identifying the user type and categorizing it.

 CheckRequest() It counts and checks the number of requests from host. If requests from host are larger than the defined range, then it puts the user/host under suspicion. It returns number of requests as output integer.

heading:  Check()
content: This function checks if number of requests and packets are within the range of a normal user then it will be a normal valid user else the user will be under suspicion. It returns true or false as output.  GetInfo() This function gets the following paramete rs from user and make makes decision using these parameters. These are getSource-Ip , getDestination-Ip, getSource -Port, ge tDestination-Port, getTCP - No(6).

heading: SDN SCENERIO:
content: In our SDN Scenario, we used Mininet and POX controller platform for the implementation and evaluation of our work in Windows and Ubuntu-based operating systems. Mininet network emulator is usually used for experimentation purposes as well as learning, testing, development, prototyping and research. All of these benefits can be achieved on a PC or any laptop. Different network topologies along with virtual controllers, switches, hosts and links have been created by using Mininet. We start by creating Mininet’s default topology. Mininet’s default topology is known as minimal topology that includes two hosts connected to a single OpenFlow kernel Switch and a Controller using OpenFlow reference. We created our own custom topology through Python file containing custom topology code written in python. The objective of the proposed work is to give a custom topology structure
which empowers the formation of any custom network topology of client's decision, including numerous IP systems.

heading: Project Abstract
content: Finding a quality tailor on economical rates in the city is a difficult task to do, we (CandS) are solving this problem by making the service of quality stitching available for you 24/7. We are taking an innovative step to solve this problem by launching Android & IOS Stitching service Application. By using this Application, You can place your order anytime online and will also get to know the Latest designs and trends of Fashion at home on this mobile App. Collection of designs will be also available for all seasons’ fashions, so that customers can select any of that as well to order. User just has to give your measurements in the app and place the order, and then our rider will pick the fabric from mentioned location and will deliver back within the defined Time.

heading: Introduction

heading: Abstract
content: Report elaborates the project where the analysis of user behaviour is done with the help of social data mining approach. Our goal is to see how the data on social media sites can enable us to create a pattern of events and the behaviour a user exhibits. The data is extracted from social sites such as Twitter using a web scraper and stored in databases. That data is processed through many steps i.e. data cleaning, data classification, sentimental analysis and visualization. In data cleaning phase, unwanted data is cleaned through different cleaning techniques. Then data is classified for analysis. Then sentimental analysis is performed a ccording to negative and positive remarks. The results of sentimental analysis are then visualized in the form of graphs. At last, a web front end is used where all phases are integrated to provide ease in use to the users. Different data mining algorithms are used to identify the patterns to analyse the data. Brief history events are elaborated to show the difference present in the previous development and that provided by the project. More over, project defines a new era where the ease for studying behaviour using huge data without surveys takes place.
