This diagram includes the architecture of phases from start to end i.e. from extraction of tweets to its visualization. This architecture shows connection between each phase with each other and with the HDFS. Tweets are first extracted through scrapper and then stored in JSON format to HDFS. The data is then loaded to hive data warehouse. After the data is store, data is cleaned by noise exclusion and English expansion. After getting clean data, tweets are then classified and visualized. Figure 3-16 : Complete architecture

heading: 3.6.2 HDFS Architecture
content: This architecture represents Hadoop which can store huge chunks of data and easily retrieve data from it. This architecture shows the connection of name node and data nodes with the client. Figure 3-17: HDFS Architecture

heading: 3.6.3 Hive Architecture
content: This architecture represents hive links with the map reducer and HDFS. This also shows the connection of SQL with hive warehouse.

heading: 3.6.4 Scrapper Architecture
content: This architecture represent the architecture of scrapper tool we used for extraction purpose. In it, working of each part is shown clearly. When a request query is made, it process the requested data and then use parser to parse data. The data sets are sent to feed exporter through a processing pipeline and then stored that data into JSON file.

heading: 3.6.5 MapReduce Architecture
content: MapReduce architecture represent the MapReduce tool we used in cleaning process of tweets. It has two parts:

heading:  Mapper
content: It maps the key value pairs from the input data it gets. Mapper receives  the (key, value) and give the output (key, value)

heading:  Reducer
content: The work of reducer is to merge the processed data with that actual data which was generated by the mapper.  Reducer gets the (Key, Iterating [Value]) and gives the output (key, value). Figure 3-20 : MapReduce Architecture

heading: 3.6.6.1.1 Noise Exclusion
content: The following figure shows the architecture of noise expulsion process where Mapper takes data i.e. tweets from HDFS and makes its (key, value) pair and then send it to reducer. Reducer then process the (key, value) and remove user names, hashtags and links in the tweets step by step and then return the value to HDFS to store.

heading: 3.6.6.2.1 Slangs Expansion
content: The following figure shows the architecture of slang expansion  process where Mapper takes data i.e. tweets from HDFS and makes its (key, value) pair to send it  to reducer for further work . Reducer then  read the file and check single tweet at once. If it found any slang, replace it with its full form and return the file back to HDFS to store.

heading: 3.6.6.2.2 Alpha Numeric Exclusion
content: The following figure shows the architecture of Alphanumeric exclusion process where Mapper takes data i.e. noise free English expanded tweets from HDFS and makes its (key, value) pair to send it to reducer for further work. Reducer then read the file and check single tweet at once. If it found any slang which is not present in the slang dictionary , reducer remove it from that tweet and return the file back to HDFS to store.

heading: 4.4 Phase 4: Data Cleaning
content: The raw data we extracted from twitter contains many unwanted things in it which must be removed before analysis phase. Those unwanted things can be usernames, hashtags, slangs etc. Mainly there are two stages of data cleaning:

heading: 4.4.1 Filtration
content: This phase contains noise exclusion process through java programming. We filter the noise in the tweets extracted and make it cleaner and properly understandable.

heading: 4.4.1.1 Noise Exclusion
content: Tweets are meant to be incomplete without using hashtags but it is an unwanted things in case of analysis. Tweets from all over the world on social media contain many unwanted things in them like hashtags, usernames and links. When tweets are extracted, images used in the tweets are converted in the form of links which

are unwanted in analysis phase. These unwanted things are noise which are removed from tweets to get clear text. MapReduce is the major source used for data cleaning. In this phase, MapReduce is checking for the key and value pair it has just like in the hash table. It picks up the file containing the tweets and read the whole file line by line. By using delimiter |token|, tweets are tokenized i.e. tweet number is made the key and text of tweet as its value. Mapper maps this input to reducer which then takes the tweets one by one to remove all the unwanted things in it like user name, hash tags, links. Figure 4-14 : Noise exclusion code

heading: 4.4.1.1.1 Hashtag Exclusion
content: Hashtags represent different types of labels in a tweet to let reader get idea of the content of the tweet. Hashtags contains ‘#’ symbol following text representing the tweet content. No space or special characters other than ‘#’ are used in hashtags of tweets. In order to remove these unwanted hashtags, we used regex which first detected the hashtags following English alphabets and remove them from it.
Figure 4-15 : Hashtag removal code

heading: 4.4.1.1.2 User name Exclusion
content: People all over the world talk to each other through tweets. Some people mention the person who they want to let them know they are specified to see their tweet. For this purpose, people use user names of person they want to notify. This notification to other people does not belong to text of the tweet. So these user names are to be removed from the tweets to just get the required text. User names starts from ‘@’ symbol following English characters or numbers sometimes. If we want space in two or more words in user names, we put ‘_’ symbol. Similarly this removal of UserNames is done through regex. Figure 4-16 : Username removal code

heading: 4.4.1.1.3 Links Exclusion
content: As twitter is a social media platform where people from different places all over the world read tweets of people and get to know each other. They start sharing their media like images, videos etc with each other through this electronic media. But when tweets are extracted from twitter, these images and videos turn into links they carry. Those links may start by ‘http’, ‘https’, ‘ftp’ etc followed by English

characters. Other than images and videos, people also share site links from some online source. Thos e links start with ‘www’, then ‘.’ And then some english characters. We use regex in order to remove these links as they are of no use in analysis phase. Figure 4-17 : Links removal code

heading: 4.4.1.2 English Expansion
content: In this phase of data cleaning, all the abbreviations used in the tweets are expanded to their original words. We also check the incorrect or missing spellings of the words in the tweets to make it represent correct essence of the tweet. There are three works to do in this phase:

heading: 4.4.1.2.1 Slang Expansion
content: As twitter is a social media platform where people tweet from all over the world. Tweets are limited to only 140 characters so everyone tries to complete once tweet in limited characters. For this people use slangs like abbreviations of some words may be used in a tweet. From example ROFL is the slang for rolling on floor laughing. Therefore, for the purpose of analysis, these slangs must be expanded to original words to properly understand a tweet.

The following code represent the main working of slang expansion method. File paths are defined to get output file in desired location and format. Figure 4-18 : Slang expansion assigning paths Figure: 46 shows the method of splitting the tweets and comparing them with slang library to match each slang and replace it with its actual form. At the end output file is created and saved to desired location.
Figure 4-19 : splitting of tweets

heading: 4.4.1.2.2 Alpha Numeric Exclusion
content: As people worldwide talk to each other on twitter in different languages. These tweets may contains slangs people use by their own slangs. These slangs are custom made by people all over the world. These slangs confuse other to understand the meaning of whole tweet because some may create their own slangs too which may not be understood. These slangs are removed to get text of tweets for use in analysis phase. MapReduce is used again for this. The mapper, which generates key and value pair of the tweets, send tweets to reducer which then calls AlphaNumericExpulsion ( ) to check tweets containing slangs like digits and then remove it from the tweet.

heading: 6.1.1  Problems
content: As we were first timers to work on Big Data, so much effort and time  was consumed in learning the techniques and use of tools. Our project is Linux based which is totally different from Windows. It took much of our time while working on Hadoop eco system. Hadoop is a complete package containing many tools and frameworks li ke MapReduce, Hive Spark etc. We learnt these tools in order to perform project tasks.

heading: 6.1.2  Challenges
content: With great advantages challenges and hurdles exist. heading: Abstract
content: Diabetes is a very common disease which refers to insufficient production (Type 1 Diabetes) or mismanagement (Type 2 Diabetes) of insulin by the body. Over the years, there has been a drastic increase in the number o f diabetics globally. From 108 million in 1980, the number has risen to 422 million as of 2014. Diabetes causes severe problems such as lower limb amputation, heart attacks, stroke, kidney failure and blindness. Unfortunately, many diabetics do not realiz e the gravity of their disease or fail to acquire sufficient knowledge and succumb to horrendous consequences. Before we even begin to highlight the ways in which diabetes is countered, it is essential to spread awareness among diabetics and educate them about diabetes. As researchers try their best to find a permanent cure, the only viable solution available to date is managing and controlling body vitals regularly to avoid complications caused by diabetes. Diabetics need to keep daily, weekly and yearly track of their blood glucose levels, insulin levels, blood pressure, cholesterol, carbohydrates and exercise routines. If these vitals are not managed, it may cause damage to vessels supplying blood to important organs. Therefore, diabetes should be taken very seriously. Traditionally, diabetics have used diaries to log their readings which has turned out to be a very inconvenient and tedious activity. MedShare is a web application that makes the lives of diabetics much easier. Not only does it aim at improv ing the way in which medical readings are logged, it provides additional tools such as diabetes unit convertors and calculators. It provides detailed infographics and charts spanning over different time spans showing an overview of the readings. These logged readings can also be shared among others, especially doctors, within MedShare, by e-mail and on social media platforms such as Facebook. Diabetics are provided with a social platform including blogs and forums within MedShare where they can communicate with other members and doctors as well. They can read others’ blogs and also write personal blogs to raise awareness and other issues in the community, providing a better chance of getting relevant and informed responses.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Diabetes has grown drastically over the last few decades. As researchers strive to find a permanent cure, currently the best way to dea l with diabetes is managing it. In order to avoid t he complications of diabetes, patients are required to manage their blood glucose levels, blood pressure levels, carbohydrates and other vitals  to minimize the risk of hyperglycaemia – a condition where glucose levels increase to dangerous thresholds . This monitoring is to be done on a daily basis in order to adjust the insulin intake. Glucose level log maintenance is a necessity.  Carelessness or mismanagement can prove to be fatal. Consequences include lower limb amputation, heart attacks, stroke, kidney failure and blindness.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: We provide a Data Logging Web Application namely MedShare which allows its users (mainly diabetics) to log their medical readings to a log book in order to better track th eir health conditions. Our aim is to allow diabetics to realize their full potential in life and bring them closer to as normal a life as everybody else in the society. The application provide s users with Info graphics of health history, personal blog s, di abetes calculators, nutritional calculators, educational materiel, meal plans & exercise plans and the ability to export their data. Moreover, for consultants, the ability to view their patients’ history. The social platform for diabetics and consultants is dedicated to raising awareness about diabetes globally.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: Patients either log  their readings manually or currently available online solutions are not free. They do not allow users to share their data with consultants from within the platform. Diabetics are also concerned about how society perceives them and some are just not fond of the extra attention. Logging data using a notepad in public can feel uncomfortable for them. With MedShare, they can simply log on to the website on their phone and log their readings without anyone around them noticing. This would give them a great deal of confidence in their everyday life. Currently diabetics do not have a go-to website which provides them with the “All-in-one” experience. MedShare solves the problem by bringing together diabetics and consultants from all over the world on a social platform allowing them to share their knowledge, experiences, success stories and much more. The possibilities are endless. With useful Calculators and Convertors, we try our best to provide the most comprehensive experience to diabetics.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions and Constraints
content: 1. The platform will be mainly used by diabetics of all ages, consultants and nutritionists. The platform will support tens of thousands of users. 2. Users will use the platform for purely productive intentions. 3. Some modules may be added, changed or removed as progress is made into the project depending on changing requirements. 4. The project is limited to using Laravel Framework version 5.5 and may or may not be supported for later versions.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: This project has built  an online platform for diabetics and concerned professions such as consultants and nutritionists. The platform is to be utility oriented and also cater its users socially. Users can log t heir readings, view them, change them and generate reports. Users can communicate among themselves through forum threads, share data and also write blogs.

heading: 3.4 Software Architecture
content: For this project we are using Laravel PHP Framework which follows the MVC structure. Figure 9 software architecture diagram It comprises of three major components; Controller, Model and View. The controller manages the Http requests, using the model to load any necessary data from the database and passing it onto the view. The view usually consists of HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Users only interact with the view to achieve their objectives. The most important advantage of using this architecture is ‘the separation of concerns’. It separates the data, logic and the visual interface explicitly.  Other than that, it allows a more modular approach for developers; allowing them to work on multiple aspects of the web application at the same time without disturbing another. It also allows the flexibility for future enhancements as there is low coupling among models, views and controllers. It leaves more room for changes. For this project we have used PHP Laravel 5  MVC Framework as it provides a comprehensive boilerplate  which can be used as a foundation and built upon. It provides the BLADE Templating engine for the front end enabling amazing dynamic frontend UIs. It also includes a lot of pre -loaded powerful libr aries such as Carbon (for date time objects management), Guzzle (make HTTP requests) and a powerful Eloquent ORM (Object Relation Mapping) and a Query Builder which makes fetching and filtering data from the database much easier. Laravel also allows defining relationships between models e.g. assigning posts to users. This allows efficient model relation management and takes out the repetitiveness of joining tables again and again to find relevant data models. The architecture of Laravel also provides migrations which can acts as a ‘Version Control System’ for database structure.

heading: 4.2.1 Unit Testing
content: We have used Laravel Dusk; a PHP Package which allows the simulation of a browser window and can test the application as per the browser experience.

heading: 4.2.1.1 Website Live Test
content: This test determines if the website is live by going to the base URL and checking the status code of the response. public function websiteLive() { $response = $this->get('/'); $response->assertSee("Diabudy"); $response->assertStatus(200); }

heading: 4.2.1.2 Login Test
content: This test determines if a user can successfully view a page which needs authentication by logging in a new user with a random name, going to the base URL and checking the status code of the response. It also checks if it finds the name of this newly created user on the page. public function login() { $user = factory(User::class)->create(); $response = $this->actingAs($user) ->get("/user/$user->slug/myaccount"); $response->assertStatus(200); $response->assertSee($user->slug); }

heading: 4.2.1.3 Auth Middleware Test
content: This test loads a URL as guest which requires a logged in user. If the response status code is 301, it means the test is successful and the guest user has been redirected to the login page. public function authMiddleware() { $response = $this->get('/user/anyusername/myaccount'); $response->assertStatus(302); }

heading: 5.1.1 Dependency Management
content: We faced problems relating to dependency management  for frontend components. Initially, it was done manually installing components. However, that caused a massive inefficiency transferring the software from one computer to another. We decided to use bower for frontend dependency management and a single command now gets the job done.

heading: 5.1.2 Keeping up with updates
content: Laravel launches new versions every few months and sometimes the changes can cause incompatibility between different modules. Therefore, we decided to stick with a single version of Laravel for development.

heading: 5.1.3 Push Notifications
content: Initially, we tried implementing user notifications using AJAX requests and polling the server every few minutes. We learnt that this is bad practice and puts extra load on the server side. Therefore, we looked for a better alternative and found Pusher API which allows the server to push information to the client using socket programming. This helped optimize our notifications system.

heading: 5.1.4 Code Management
content: As our code base grew, it became more and more tedious to manage for our group members to collaborate and work on it at the same time. We used VCS (Version Control System) to work on different branches and merge later on.

heading: 5.1.5 Media Management
content: Managing media can get unorganized especially in an application where a lot of it is involved. We used Laravel Plank/Mediable package to manage our media items. It stores the media and mediables to media relations in the database and makes media management much easier. Also allows us to add tags to the media uploaded so we can group it together by tags.

heading: Abstract
content: The project is about developing an android application for providing assistance to the rescue organizations working in Pakistan. It would also provide quick menu for usability to complainants/victims with which the victims of an accident or the complainant (people reporting from the spot) can send rescue request which would be attended by an organization nearby (Rescue 1122 currently). The system that is currently being used by rescue is wireless system. Rescue teams communicate with hospitals through wireless system and rescue teams then communicat e to ambulance that is sent to place of disaster. The basic flaw in this system is that we do not have any real time monitoring of ambulance (We do not know exactly where the ambulance is). So such system is needed that can give real time monitoring of amb ulance. Recently applications are developed to rescue wild life in case of disaster. “IFAW Wildlife Rescue App” is an application that connects people to nearest rescue team or organization at the touch of a button to help native wildlife [1]. Similarly “EMNet findERnow” is an application that locates near hospital with respect to need of a patient [2]. The process of requesting and GUI of application would be simple for the complainants/victims and organizations. The rescue team can also install such appli cation on touchpad’s of vehicles, tables or smart phones through which they would be guided regarding location of the complainants/victim and hospitals near to them after attending complainants/victim.

heading: 1.1 Introduction:
content: The rescue 1122 is currently working in Pakistan using wireless system. This application would facilitate their work so they could perform their jobs in a more efficient and precise manner. Accuracy is very important especially in hour of calamity or sudde n accidents. This application would assure accuracy (in terms exact location, movement tracking) and moreover it would guide regarding hospitals nearby which will obviously save time and most importantly save someone’s life. This application is non -profit and the only purpose of it is to provide ease to our rescue organizations. On the other hand, the victim/complainant could also use it or a person nearby can make an urgent request by which request would be broadcasted and most nearby rescue team would attend the request with which it would ease some pressure on well-known organization i.e. Rescue 1122. System will also be integrated in associated hospitals so that facilities will be checked by rescue teams that hospital can offer. This feature will ensure efficiency so complainants/victim can directly be rescued to the hospital where space is available. The application would also include offline feature in case of no internet facility. The basic purpose of developing such application is to serve the commun ity and assist the organizations that provide rescue services. Such an application would serve the country in making things more manageable or at least ‘come abreast of salt’.   The idea of the project was discussed with Public Relation Officer of Rescue 11 22 service and the officer guided us about their day to day task handling and the issues being faced. In Pakistan  currently there is no application which can provide such facility and most effective part is the most nearby team could provide help to complainants/victim which would lessen the pressure on a specific team. Although in abroad applications like IFWA wild life rescue app is used to rescue wildlife as discussed above. But this app combines the idea of “IFAW “app[1] and “EMNet findERnow” app[2] to facilitate recue 1122.

This project is being developed using Android Studio. The major theme for application would be the easiest and most user-friendly. People who have difficulty in reading could also use it with an easy interface provided by icons. Scam calls Security would also be considered so no fake requests would be generated. This application will perform its task by just click of button. No long menus will be developed so that it can be simple and efficient in use.

heading: 1.2 Goals and Objectives:
content: • To provide help to complainants/victims of accident or some natural calamity. • To provide facility to rescue organizations in their operations. • To save someone’s life. • To save time. • To provide accuracy. • To provide efficiency. • An advertisement free application. • Assumption: Go Rescue (Discussed above). • Broadcasting of help request to nearby teams.

heading: 1.3 Motivation and Scope:
content: The main scope is to provide facility to every android user to guide rescue teams about victims or victims themselves regarding their position  and major form of injury. On severity of injury and nearest position the services would be given to complainants/victim. Only motivation of working on this project is to serve our nation as nothing before done on this schema. This need has pushed us to work on this project so we can make some betterment in our society. The assumption which is made ‘Go Rescue’ feature which would allow a local person to help the complainants/victim of an incident.

heading: 1.4 Problem Statement:
content: In Pakistan, our major departments are using out dated systems like wireless communication. The major change that we want to make is to upgrade the systems and provide features like real -time tracking facility by which rescue team and the complainant would know about the current location of complainant and ambulance respectively. The rescue team is also facing record management issue and we are providing them solution by which they would spend less time in making incident reports also after picking the victim from incident there will be a hospital communication by which availability of the staff would be determined.

heading: 1.5.1  Constraints:
content: • The system will provide live monitoring,  record management and communication between complainant/victim, control unit, ambulance driver and hospital.

heading: 1.5.2  Assumptions:
content: • No such system is existing in Pakistan. • The system will meet with high acceptance from its users. • The system will be usefull for everyone including ambulance staff,complainant and worker. •  We’ll add an additional feature by which volunteers (registered) would deal with the request broadcasted on the timeline. • It would become a proper disaster management system for Pakistan including other organizations.

heading: Distance Calculator:
content: public double distance(double latitude, double longitude, double e, double f) { double d2r = Math.PI / 180; double dlong = (longitude - f) * d2r; double dlat = (latitude - e) * d2r; double a = Math.pow(Math.sin(dlat / 2.0), 2) + Math.cos(e * d2r) * Math.cos(latitude * d2r) * Math.pow(Math.sin(dlong / 2.0), 2); double c = 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a)); double d = 6367 * c; return d; }

heading: 4.2 Unit Testing
content: Unit testing is a software development process, in which the smallest testable parts of an application (units) are exclusively and freely examined for appropriate task. All the modules of the project have been individually tested.

heading: 4.3 Acceptance Testing
content: Acceptance Testing is the phase of software testing where a system is tested for accessibility. Purpose of this test is to ensure that the system’s requirements meet business/user needs and verify whether it is acceptable for deployment or not. In our case, all the requirements are meet at the end as our system - Complainant details are sent (offline/online). - Availability of nearby hospital is ensured. - Ambulance is assigned to complainant. - Ambulance and admin have real time access. - E-Report saves time.

heading: 5.1 Problem faced and lesson learned:
content: • First challenge faced was how to handle a complaint at server end of our system. We used clicks to assign a complaint to an ambulance and hospital. • Another challenge was to get the complainant’s location and make the complainant-end’s interface user friendly so that a lay man can also use make request. • In order to find that a hospital can take any patient. Our system required a hospital end that can give us the information that either a hospital can a patient or not.  To overcome this

challenge hospital end will be notified whenever a new complain comes into our system and an interface will be opened through which the status of hospital can be send. • Our system requires maps as its ambulance -worker end function is to provide direction towards the complainant and then to the hospital. Maps are also a part of server side as the location of the complainant is to be shown. For maps we used Google maps and APIs. • Fake requests were also a big problem and to overcome that problem our system uses the permission from the user to get its phone data (IMEI, GSM, Network Type, Phone Number etc.) at the time of installation. When a complaint is sent along with the user’s location, user’s phone data is also sent.

heading: 5.2 Project Summary:
content: The basic purpose of developing such application is to serve the community and assist the organizations that provide rescue services. Such an application would serve the country in making things more manageable or at least ‘come abreast of salt’.   The idea of the project was discussed with Public Relation Officer of Rescue 1122 service and the officer guided us about their day to day task handling and the issues being faced. In Pakistan  currently there is no application which can provide such facility and most effective part is the most nearby team could provide help to complainants/victim which would lessen the pressure on a specific team.

heading: 5.3 Future work:
content: Every great nation thinks about future. Nations falls but the great nation is one that knows how to prevent it from happening again. Every nation that is successful believes in better system. There is always something better. Our system is good but we should always look for better. Every system has some weaknes ses and strengths just like our system. Every disaster leaves some questions about the system. Those questions should be answered to prevent disaster from happening again. Our system should be centralized to make the intercommunication of departments strong. That is what we are proposing. Our system is not bound for ambulances and Rescue1122 but it is whole system that will eventually act as automated disaster management system. It will be a system in which common people will also work side by side to save more lives and serve humanity. Registered user can help the victim in case of ambulance delay. The application

will show helper nearest hospital or health care facility according to help needed. This will also be helpful in case of disaster. It will give power to the common people so they can make Pakistan a better place. According to the survey,we conducted, many victims of head injury die because of no proper first aid. Sometimes helper do not know how to deal with that particular situation. System will provide visual aid to helper in case the ambulance is late or delayed due to some reasons. Visual aid will show simple steps that can save the life of victim. Helper just have to select from common injuries and application will guide helper. It can save many lives. Our system will provide a feature for missing people. Victim will report the picture of missing one and it will be broadcasted by our system to users around that specific area. By this user can help in finding the missing one. Our system can also be helpful in catching a wanted criminal. With increasing rate of terrorism, it can be helpful for police departments. Police departments will broadcast picture and related information of criminals using our system. So, users in that area can help identifying the criminals. This system is better because sometimes there are some threat due to which people cannot report to police departments. Our system will make police to citizen communication stronger than ever. Our system will provide a forum where users can make groups to serve the society in some way. It will encourage other people to do something constructive for Pakistan. Users can make group about cleaning the central park of local society etc. Our system will provide a platform where user can easily communicate to the departments and complain about anything it will make communication efficient and easy. In case of War it will act as disaster management system where citizens can communicate to departments and departments can communicate to other departments. This system insures better future of Pakistan. This system believes in” United we stand divided we fall”.

heading: Abstract
content: Emotions are part of everyday life of a person. With day -to-day life, automatic emotion detection is becoming part of modern era computer science. Emotion detec tion can be used  in many applications such as crime interrogation, online interviews, and improving online gaming experiences. In addition to this, emotion reco gnition can also be used for educational purposes to perceive students' interest in a course and make it better so that students can understand well a nd much more. Most of the facial images are captured using normal digital cameras however, the main problem with the normal cameras is that they take a lot of effect from Illumination that eventually affects the picture being processed. Every single emotion affects your face with different amount of heat on your face and heat can easily be captured using therm al camera, which is helpful for emotion recognition even in bad Illumination conditions. This work used thermal ima gery for emotion recognition. We have used Histogram Oriented Gradient (HOG), a feature extraction technique to extract face features from th ermal images followed by Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier for recognition of different emotion types. With this  handcrafted technique, we achieved 70% accuracy on thermal infrared images and 75% on visual images using Natural visible and infrared facial expression database. Furthermore, to improve accuracy an experiment is done on deep neural network using transfer learning for feature extraction and classification as well. We achieve an accuracy about 90% on thermal infrared images and 95% on visual images. Afterwards, another experiment is done using hybrid approach that is transfer learning to extract features and passing these features to Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier for recognition of different emotions. We achieve an accuracy about 99.34% on thermal infrared images and 99.8% on visual images using a benchmark natural visible and infrared facial expression database.

heading: 2.1  Literature Review
content: Emotion Recognition is an important field of study traversing various disciplines. The progress in this domain has advanced to a level that Emotion Recognition systems are being manifested in real world i.e. security monitoring, identification systems, defence systems etc. The rapid growth and development in this discipline is due to a variety of factors which includes the development of efficient algorithms, the accessibility of databases consi sting of facial images and the methods for evaluating the efficiency and performance of different Face recognition algorithms. This section gives an overview on the major human emotion  recognition techniques that apply mostly to frontal faces, advantages a nd disadvantages of each method are given. The methods considered are Eigen faces (Eigen features), Hog and SVM, neural networks (transfer learning and SVM).

heading: 2.1.1   Non-intrusive car driver's emotion recognition
content: This system was used to create betterment in the Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS). This system uses thermal emotion detected by a single thermal camera. Image acquisition in this very case was done through the thermal camera which makes this even more s evere in no or low light environments. The more thermal sensor will be added to enhance the experience and safety of the user. [8]

heading: 2.1.2 Thermal spatial-temporal data for stress recognition
content: Stress is now being treated as a major disease, but it is very difficult to know that if a person is in a state of stress or not. This research used thermal videos of by subject to measure the amount of stress on the subject’s faces. This can be further used to control the amount of medication according to the stress levels [5]. In the future more, complex pattern can also be recognized.

heading: 2.1.3 Eigen Faces
content: Eigen Face is one of the most deeply investigated technique of Face Recognition. They proposed that face images could be reconstructed by a collection of weights and a face picture known as Eigen picture. For this purpose, different face images of the same person ar e collected so that variation can be obtained. Each image from this collection corresponds to an eigenvector using a covariance matrix. The representation of these eigenvectors is known as eigenfaces. Weights are calculated by projecting the image of face onto the Eigen picture [8] [9]. Classification is the last step of this algorithm. The M eigenfaces that are the best ones constitute an M dimensional space which is also known as the face space. The match face image is determined by evaluating the face class image that gives the minimum Euclidean distance.

heading: 2.1.4 Histogram Oriented Gradient and Support Vector Machine
content: HOG is a feature descriptor used in image processing and computer vision for object detection. It makes use of direction and gradients magnitude to describe all parts of an image.  This algorithm reduces the impact of light on the image. It then performs gradient computation by applying a derivative mask. In simpler words, it calculates the directional changes in intensity of image. A histogram using magnitude and direction is then build from where the algorithm gets its name. SVM Classifier looks for an optimal hyper plane  which separates matching objects with non - matching ones. In our system, we have used Multi-class SVM for classification of HOG features.

heading: 2.1.5 Neural Network
content: The feature extraction of neural network is more efficient than other face recognition techniques. WISARD was the first neural network technique used for face recognition or emotion recognition. It maintains a separate network for each stored person [12]. Successful recognition is based on the way you construct a neural network structure that is almost dependent on the application you want to develop. Convolution Neural Network [14] are used for face detection whereas Multi-resolution pyramid structure is used for face verification [17]. Support Vector Machines (SVM) are also used for emotion recognition [4] [18]. The training time is as long as 2 hours whereas the classification time is less than 10 second. The Back-Propagation Network (BPN) is the most widely known and best algorithm in Multilayer Perceptron’s training. The BPN provides an efficient computational method where it changes the weights in feed forward network with differential units of activation function through which learning of training set of input and output data can be obtained. However, its drawback is that it is a slow technique.

heading: Viola Jones Algorithm
content: Face Detection is done through Viola Jones Algorithm. This is the first object detection algorithm which performs object detection in real-time. It was proposed in 2001 by Paul Viola and Michael Jones. It is mainly used for face detection. This is a four-step algorithm:

heading: 4. Cascading Classifiers
content: Reason to choose this algorithm: We chose this algorithm for face detection in our system because of its following good characteristics:  Robust Nature: This algorithm has very high positive detection rate and very low false detection rates.  Face Detection:  This algorithm performs face detection and distinguishes faces from non-faces.

heading: 3.2 Feature Extraction
content: Transfer Learning (ALEXNET) The next step after face detection is the feature extraction for which Transfer Learning (AlexNet) is used. AlexNet is a feature descriptor used in image processing and compu ter vision for object detection which is trained on millions of images of thousands of objects. It contains 8 layers from which we can trim last layers according to our desire to train our dataset on it. We trim last four layer according to our dataset need. Features are extracted from dataset images and stored in the hidden layers then these are pass to the classifier SVM for further classification.

Figure 9 AlexNet Architecture A fully trained AlexNet on ImageNet data set can not only be used to classify Image Net data set but it can also be used without the output layer to extract features from samples of any other data set [19]. As shown above last four layers are used to train our NIVE data set and extract features. Reason to choose this algorithm: We chose this algorithm over other algorithms that is  LeNET, because of some key points which are mentioned below: • The main reason to choose this algorithm is weights allocated to edges between the neuron. It is really hard to weight your own deep neural network. It might even take days in some cases. LeNet is an efficient network but the deeper the network is the better the result are. Since, AlexNet is deeper than LeNet so we have used AlexNet. • The non-linearity used in the feature extractor module of the AlexNet is ReLU whereas LeNet has logistic sigmoid. • AlexNet uses dropout whereas no such concept is used in LeNet.

heading: 3.3 Classification
content: Support Vector Machine (SVM) Classifier SVM Classifier looks for an optimal hyperplane that separates matching objects with non-matching ones. In our system, we have used Multi-class SVM for classification of features. Reason to choose this classifier: We chose this classification technique from other techniques because of the following key features:  Training of face images through SVM is relatively easy than that of Neural Networks.  Training of face images through SVM is computationally less extensive than that of Neural Networks.  SVM is robust to noise and works well in high dimensional spaces even when the training set is small. In our system, four images are used for training.  Independent Component Analysis (ICA) consumes more computational time than SVM. Moreover, SVM has the highest accuracy rate of 99.3% on NIVE database.

heading: Abstract
content: In this project, we aim to develop an informative Website and Android Application to provide people of Pakistan with a fast and reliable platform so that, they can contact with different pleaders. In this quick and modern world, it is challenging to find accurate lawyer regarding any issues in life. Websites and Android applications have evolved so much that they are now a part of every day’s business life. So, with the help of these, we will develop a complete system that will enable lawyers to contact with clients remotely and vice versa. Thus, we will be able to resolve their problems in a faster and reliable way. The societal effect of this project is that it will be a very first step to dematerialize paperwork of lawyers in Pakistan. Usually, in daily life routine, many questions arise regarding any law issues , but we cannot ask lawyers as many of us do not have any direct relation with lawyers. So, we leave those questions unintended and cannot take any proper actions accordingly. Hence, using our App, anyone will be able to ask any legal questions publically and can get appropriate answers by registered lawyers that will make their life easier. This project will make work easy for lawyers and clients because clients can hire lawyers from anywhere around the globe witho ut any time limitations. Also, the pleaders will not be in need to open big offices to attract clients because their portfolio will show what services they offer and their ratings regarding those services.

heading: 1.1.1 Structure of Android Application
content: Attorney of Law main purpose is to relieve the lawyers from paperwork and to handle their clients remotely. Attorney of Law provides the feature of hiring the best lawyers according to the client’s needs. As in today’s busy world, everyone is busy enough in their daily routine so, it is challenging for someone to personally go to the court and different locations to find some appropriate lawyer to handle their cases. So, we made an effort to develop some system so that we can fill this gap between the clients and lawyers. Attorney of Law provides a single platform for Lawyers to register their profiles from their home using Android Application. It is a very agonizing period to wait for some good lawyer to come up and handle your case. Also when you as a client know nothing about the Law. So, that is the time when our Attorney of Law will come in handy. You can view the profiles of lawyers at any time sitting at home and find out the best lawyer in the area you are searching for. Our filter search will give yo u the ability to search the Lawyers by City-wise or category wise. Once you have found a suitable lawyer, you can easily review the profile of that lawyer. You will also be able to see the ratings of different clients about any specific lawyer which you ar e going to hire. Also, it is a very common practice that we as users have many questions in mind that we are unable to ask any legal person because of not knowing any lawyer personally. We cannot go to the office of any lawyer every time if we have any questions in mind because of the busy schedule and also the availability of lawyer matters. Hence, Attorney of Law provides easy access to ask any question from any lawyer sitting in the home at any time without any constraints. This will help the public to get knowledge of any legal question or law of Pakistan without any effort. The Android App will provide the main basic functionalities to contact with the lawyers. Clients can also rate lawyers on the basis of  Appointment. Lawyers can register on the basis of their specialties and work experience. The Android Application will be an alternative to the users that feel more suitable to use mobile apps due to their fast and quicker functionalities. We will focus on developing complete Android Application first t hen we will go towards developing an informative website, and by the end of this year, we will have the complete system of Attorney of Law in Pakistan.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: In this modern world of technology, Pakistan is still dependent on manual work, especially for lawyers. All the lawyers have to do the paperwork and maintain the records of their clients and appointments manually. So to improve this manual system to auto system, a group of lawyers had a meeting with the project manager in which they decided to develop an android application and website naming “Attorney of Law.” Then the project manager arranged a meeting with the experts, and they decided primary measurable objects for this project that are listed below:  To relieve the lawyers from paperwork.  To facilitate lawyers to handle their multiple appointments and to keep records of their clients at the same time.  To help lawyers improve their relationship with clients and to get hired by clients.  To help clients ask any legal question from all the lawyers publicly to act accordingly.  To help clients understand the constitutions of Pakistan.  To help clients find top lawyers in a specific category in their city.  To facilitate clients so that they do not have to go to courts or lawyers manually but, they can find and hire the required lawyer remotely.

content: Pakistan is becoming one of the progressive country day by day, but still, we have to face many issues in this modern world. Such as, we have no automated systems. They have to maintain a lot of paperwork only to keep the information of their clients save. Also, keeping in mind appointments of different clients especially when there are multiple different clients with multiple cases, this becomes so hard. So, there should be a system to help them maintain their records and contact with their clients remotely. Also, clients in Pakistan have to face many issues finding the accurate and authenticate lawyer for their cases. They have to go to courts and visit many law firms only to find a best and affordable lawyer. So, we are trying to develop a complete system containing an Android Application and website that will help not only lawyers to maintain records a nd lessen their paper works but also will help the public to find out a best and affordable lawyer and discuss their problem remotely within no time.

heading: 3.4 Software Architecture
content: MVC stands for Model, View, and Controller. This is a commonly used pattern in developing software and application. From the day it was presented it gained high renown in building web applications mostly. It divides applications into three different parts. Model is linked with a database. The view gives user GUI to present information and controller acts as a bridge. It sends a request to model to change the data in the database if required and then send the request to view to present new information.

heading: 3.4.1   Model
content: Model is the basic component of the pattern also known as a central part of a pattern. It is used to model the behavior of applications as problem domain. It also separates the database or data storage from Graphical User Interface. Its main task is to manage the database, check logic, and formulas or rules of application. The model receives information from a controller that tells when to change or update data.

heading: 3.4.2   View
content: The view is commonly treated as Graphical User Interface that is visible to common users. The view may contain any information that needs to be presented. As in our traditional approach we, write view and model in the same file that makes it very difficult to do any changes. So, MVC here comes to our aid. The view is used to separate data from presentation. The view may contain different information, tables, graphs, images, videos or anything. There is a possibility that one information may have many views. The view will present data or information in the specific format given by the developer.

heading: 3.4.3   Controller
content: A controller is a middleman. It acts as a bridge between View and Model. Controller basically gets input from both Model and View, and it performs any certain action that is required. If any request of change comes from GUI, the controller sends a command to model to update its data and then when a change request is handled  the model responds to the controller and then controller sends a request to View, and new data is presented. heading: Abstract
content: In this project, we aim to propose a real-time Hybrid application to take students attendance using QR code. This is an innovative and unique advancement concept to automate the currently used attendance system. In majority o f the educational institutions,  the mostly  used way to mark attendance is on attendance sheet, which is very time consuming and a cumbersome process. We are in an era where there is a serious threat of global warming. We should focus on sustainable development. The proposed idea will not only eradicate the effort and time wasted in taking attendance but also help in reducing the paper resources used in managing attendance data.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Even today it is witness that manual attendance system is carried out in most of the educational institutions. Beside being time consuming, it is also an inefficient and sloppy method as the average attendance of each student is calculated manually and the re is always a chance of marking forged attendance of a student. We belong to a generation where we should not need to carry a paper and ballpoint along with us.  In regard of the following assumption, we have proposed an attendance marking system through Quick Response (QR) code scanning using a Hybrid application. Though many advancement have already been made in the field of attendance management system using radio frequency identification (RFID) technology, face recognition, iris recognition, barcode sc anning, Bluetooth etc. Along with being expensive and difficult to maintain, all of them had some types of limitations and flaws. However the proposed system besides helping the faculty to easily take the attendance of the students, maintaining, managing a nd manipulating the record of student attendance, it will also assist in overcoming all the current imperfections. QR code is a machine -readable code consisting of an array of black and white squares, typically used for storing URLs or other information for reading by the camera on a smart phone [1]. Hybrid smart phone application w ill be used to scan the QR code . Hybrid Applications are developed using HTML5, CSS and JavaScript. These are fast and simpler to develop and easier to maintain [2]. The biggest advantage of Hybrid application is that it is consistent and has a cross platform user interface (UI) that is compatible with most devices [3]. The teacher on entering the class will login the portal on the desktop pc in the classroom. After inputting minimal relevant details regarding the particular class and course for marking attendance, a QR code based on specific parameters will be generated; this will then be visible on

heading: 10 of 75  28 December 2018
content: the projector screen. A simple and user friendly application will be installed  on the smart phone of every student. The students will have to login into the application and simply scan the QR code visible on the projector screen. The concept of digital image processing will provide the mechanism to successfully scan the QR code bein g displayed on the projector screen.  On successful scanning of the QR code their attendance will be marked  as present which will be saved into the database. The student will have to wait for at least 1 hour before they can scan another QR code, preventing the students to mark false attendance for their fellows.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The goal of this project is to replace the currently used unsystematic, disorganized and time wasting attendance marking system with an automated system in all renowned educational institutions across Pakistan. Our target is make a convenient, user friendl y methodology to provide faster way to mark attendance to save the time of the teachers and students. This will not only help in solving the ongoing problem faced by the faculty in marking the attendance but will also help in reducing the burden on natural  resources. We further aim to assist the students to have complete track of their attendance through the application aiding them to avoid any kind of inconvenience caused by short attendance at the end of semester. Our foremost objective is to play our role in moving the country towards digital world.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: In the modern era where everything is being digitalized to ease the lives of people, marking attendance still hinders technological advancement. The faculty usually has to call out the name  of each student to mark his or her attendance, which besides being time consuming, is also a cumbersome process. Another problem that needs to be addressed is that maintaining the record of attendance on the sheets of papers is not a secure and advisable method because there is always a chance of sheets getting misplaced. One more issue with the current system is that marking attendance cover almost 10 minutes of the lecture time which again is not liked by majority of the faculty.  Further difficulty in t he contemporary system for marking attendance is that the students are unaware of their attendance in each course and not able to keep the record of their attendance. This sometimes causes them to suffer from short attendance.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions
content: Our assumptions are based on the problems faced by the faculty in using the current system. Though we still have to conduct surveys and polls, but our supposition is that our system will be appreciated by all the institutes of Pakistan and they will like to implement it in their universities.

content: Constraint in the project are that modules will be limited in the starting, like unable to upload fee payment challan, semester feedbacks etc. Work on it will be done in later time.

heading: 2.3 Requirements Elicitation
content: The functional and non -functional requirements are introduced using the Unified Modelling Language (UML) which is an open method used to specify, visualize, construct and document the artefacts of an object -oriented software -intensive system under development. UML offers a standard way to write a system's blueprints, including conceptual components. Functional requirement defines a function of a software system or its component. A function is described as a set of inputs, the behaviour, and outputs. Functional requirements may be calculations, technical details, data manipulation and processing and other specific functionality that defines what a system is supposed to accomplish. Behavioural requirements describing all the cases where the system uses the functional requirements are captured in use cases. Non-functional requirement is a requirement that specifies criteria that can be used to judge the operation of a system, rather than specific behaviours. This should be contrasted with functional requirements that define specific behaviour or functions.

content: Software development life cycle model

heading: 2.4.1 MVC Model
content: The MVC Model stands for Model -View-Controller. MVC Model  is a software d evelopment cycle model in which is used to separate application's concerns. Model - Model represents an object or JAVA POJO carrying data. It can also have logic to update controller if its data changes. View - View represents the visualization of the data that model contains. Using the prototype, the client can get an actual feel of the system. Therefore, this case of model is beneficial in the  case when requirements are not described initially. This prototype is developed based on the currently known requirements. Development of the prototype obviously undergoes design, coding, and testing, but each of these phases is not done very formally or thoroughly. By using this prototype, the client can get an actual feel of the system, because the interactions with the prototype can enable the client to better understand the requir ements of the desired system.

heading: 1. Faster development process:
content: MVC supports rapid and parallel development. If an MVC model is used to develop any particular web application then it is possible that one programmer can work on the view while the another can work on the controller to create business logic of the web application. Hence this way, the application developed using MVC model can be completed three times faster than applications that are developed using other development pattern.

heading: 2. Ability to provide multiple views:
content: In the MVC Model, you can create multiple views for a model. Today, there is an increasing demand for new ways to access your application and for that MVC development is certainly a great solution. Moreover, in this method, Code duplication is very limited because it separates data and business logic from the display.

heading: 3. Support for asynchronous technique:
content: The MVC architecture can also integrate with the JavaScript Framework. This means that MVC applications can be made to work even with PDF files, site-specific browsers, and also with desktop widgets. MVC also supports asynchronous technique, which helps developers to develop an application that loads very fast.

heading: 4. Modification does not affect the entire model:
content: For any web application, user interface tends to change more frequently than even the business rules of the company. It is obvious that you make frequent changes in your web application like changing colors, fonts, screen layouts, and adding new device support for mobile phones or tablets. Moreover, Adding new type of views are very easy in MVC pattern because the Model part does not depend on the views part. Therefore, any changes in the Model will not affect the entire architecture.

heading: 5. MVC model returns the data without formatting:
content: MVC pattern returns data without applying any formatting. Hence, the same components can be used and called for use with any interface. For example, any kind of data can be formatted with HTML, but it could also be formatted with Macromedia Flash or Dream viewer.

heading: 6. SEO friendly Development platform:
content: MVC platform supports development of SEO friendly web pages or web applications. Using this platform, it is very easy to develop SEO-friendly URLs to generate more visits from a specific application. This development architecture is commonly used in the Test Driven Development applications. Moreover, Scripting languages like JavaScript and jQuery can be integrated with MVC to develop feature rich web applications. Thus, MVC design pattern is a surely the great approach to building software applications. The MVC framework is easy to implement as it offers above given numerous advantages. Projects that are developed with the help of MVC model can be easily developed with lesser expenditure and within less time too. Above all, its power to manage multiple views makes MVC the best architecture pattern for developing web applications. As a result, today organizations are looking for development of web applications based on MVC architecture for cost and time benefits. There are many web developmen t companies providing MVC development services to develop web applications that satisfy every requirement of the clients. Brainvire is one such web development company that provides most desire output to their clients by offering fast and highly interactiv e web applications using MVC 6 development architecture.

heading: Views:
content: A view is a visual representation of the MVC model. This level creates an interface to show the actual output to the user. However, a view will not display anything itself. It is the controller or model that tells view what to display to the user. It also handles requests from the user and informs controller. A view is connected to its model and gets the data necessary for the presentation by asking certain questions. Sometimes, it also updates the model by sending appropriate messages. All these questions and messages are sent back to the model in such an easy terminology that it can easily understand the information sent by model or a controller.

heading: Controller:
content: Controller is a level which acts like a brain of the entire MVC system.. A controller also acts as a link between a user and the system. It provides the user with input by providing appropriate views to present it appropriately on the screen. The controller understands user output, converts it into the appropriate messages and passes the same to views.

heading: Abstract
content: In this final year project, we have developed an automatic statistical machine translation system that  translates English language text to U rdu language and vice versa. As machine translation (or MT) becomes increasingly desired for more and more language pairs, these systems become a necessity. However, the current state -of-the-art research on English-Urdu statistical MT is quite bleak due to the unavailability of large-scale good quality parallel corpora. Such data is important for the development and evaluation of a reliable MT system. Therefore, one of the main contribution of this FYP work is the de velopment of a freely available and  large-scale parallel corpus for English-Urdu language pair. We have also performed statistical MT experiments using the Moses open source toolkit and report ed competitive evaluation results using  Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score. heading: 1.1 Machine Translation
content: Machine Translation (MT) is a self-operating system in which a computer software translate s a text from one natural language to another.  A computer based MT system automatically learns to translate large text in a brief time without  the need o f human translators . As this is the age of internet, everyone is sharing their knowledge, reviews or  opinions in their native language or in the language they understand. On the other hand, a great dea l of information on the internet is in English language, which unfortunately is not very useful for people who don’t understand English. This has raised the demand for accessibility to English content available online  in foreign languages and vice versa . Consequently, the research in  automatic MT systems is continuously improving to produce systems to meet the demands of these users. MT  is one of the most interesting research area in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP) [1]. At present , there are several techniques used in automatic MT : (1) Rule-Based Machine Translation (RBMT) is the initial approach used in the field of automatic MT. The structure of this system is based on the knowledge of lingual information present in the language. It is more useful in translating languages that highly supports grammatical rules along with good quality lexicons. The translation is usually performed on the basics of grammatical rules of the languages involved. However, formulation of these rules is a tedious process and requires years of effort and linguistic analysis [2]. (2) Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) uses parallel corpus to define the meanings of both seen and unseen structure for translation. Different statistic models and algorithms are applied to transfer or aligned the parallel corpus from source to target language. It translates the input text and then transfer into probabilistic models for determining the correct output translation. It is further categorized into two-parts Word Base Translation and Phrase Base Translation. In Word Base Translation, word-to-word translation is performed which is quite simple and efficient while in Phrase Base Translation, collection of words or sentences are used as separate phrases to translate from source language to target language. It usually gives better results than W ord Base Translation. (3) Example-Based Machine Translation (EBMT) is the part of data driven model in automatic MT. This system usually relies on the existing or available bilingual data. It is based on

heading: 10 of 41                                                                                                                                                                             18 May 2018
content: three parts a) Phrase Fragment Matching b) Translation of S egments and c) Recombination that generates new translation by reprocessing the existing translation. (4) Neural Machine Translation is relatively new machine translation method that works on the basis of large neural networks and deep word embedding. It’s not much different than SMT but uses vector based word embeddings for continuous representation of words as translation units. (5) Hybrid Machine Translation refers to single main system that comprises by reprocessing all the methodology of multiple translation system. The working on this technique is to get desired accuracy results with in single main system.

heading: 1.2 Statistical Machine Translation
content: Statistical Machine  Translation (SMT) has been the leading method of research in automatic machine translation [ 3]. In SMT, first a word -to-word alignment is computed using a parallel corpus [4]. In the second step, these translated words are sequenced using n-gram language model. An open source toolkit, Moses [5], is used for SMT experiments. To build a translation model, Moses requires substantial amount of good quality sentence aligned bilingual parallel data. SMT gives more accurate and desired results once properly aligned parallel corpus is developed. Moreover, it does not need knowledge of grammar rules  as RBMT. However, for best results, it requires large amount of high quality parallel data to learn and translate properly. Furthermore, it manages and handles large data in an efficient manner. Unfortunately, such bi-text resources are very limited for resource-sparse languages (e.g. English- Urdu language pair). Moreover, automatic bi-text alignment is a challenging task because English follows SUBJECT -VERB-OBJECT (SVO) structure whereas Urdu follows the SUBJECT - OBJECT-VERB (SOV) structure (See Figure 1).

heading: 1.3  English-Urdu Statistical Machine Translation
content: The focus of our FYP work is to build an English-Urdu SMT system. The proposed system is trained using a large-scale gold standard English-Urdu parallel corpus which is also developed as part of this project. There are 163 million [6] Urdu speakers around the world that need access to online content in their native language. Similarly, U rdulibrary.org has a lot of books in Urdu language but they are not useful for English speakers. To fulfill this gap, there is a need for English- Urdu MT system to make such material useful for everyone.

heading: 1.4 Problem Statement
content: The main aim of this FYP is to build an English-Urdu SMT system.

content: Urdu ranks 19th among 7,105 languages spoken in the world [7]. However, when it comes to NLP, it has very limited resources available. The major hindrance in MT research in English-Urdu language pair is the unavailability of large- scale and accurate parallel corpus. Thus, our major contribution in this  FYP is to develop large- scale parallel corpus to increase the accuracy of the translation system. Moreover, the purpose of building such a tool is to promote NLP research in our native language.

heading: Resource Requirement
content: SMT demands  good quality and large amount of parallel data in both languages. However, Urdu is an under -resourced language with limited amount of parallel data available. So acquiring large amount of English- Urdu parallel data is a tough tas k. The parallel sentences were collected from different novels, books and online news websites. Manual translation is also performed to increase the amount of data. Punctuation Issues Urdu is a loose written language and has no standard punctuation markers to end the sentence. A  script is developed in java for both English and Urdu that deals with different sentence delimiters such as comma, semi- colon, question mark and full-stop. Alignment Issues Due to the difference in  morphological structure of both languages, and not a single good automatic sentences aligner available for English-Urdu language pair, the sentence alignment is not a straight forward task . To deal with it, first partial alignment was performed using a script written in Java and then manual correction was done to remove noise.

heading: 2.1  Related Work
content: In this section, we have  describe the related work that has already been done  on English-Urdu SMT. In 2016 [2], the authors investigated different MT approaches for Indian languages including Urdu. The corpus used in experiments is EMILLE dataset [ 8]. There are 8,245 English -Urdu parallel sentences in the corpus which were divided into train and test set for training and evaluation. The relatively low BLEU score (0.14) reported after experiments was supported by the reason that the corpus is too small for realistic experiments and the sentences in the corpus are not properly aligned. In 2014 [ 9], the authors presented a baseline  for English -Urdu automatic MT system. They investigated phrase-base MT (PBMT) and hierarchical MT (HMT) for English -Urdu language pair. Their parallel corpus  was collected from AFRL (50,313 sentences), EMILLE (8 ,245 sentences) [8], IPC (7,478) [10], QURAN (6,364 sentences) and PENN (6,204 sentences) [11]. On all datasets, it was found that HMT (BLEU 21.35) performed better than PBMT (BLEU 18.30). However, the AFRL corpus used in the experiments is not publicly available. In another study [1 2], the authors highlighted the issues of development and sentence alignment of English-Urdu parallel corpus. The parallel corpus used was collected from Ahadeeths of Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. 7,275 Ahadeeths from Sahih Bukhari and 7,190 Ahadeeths from Sahih Muslim were used in this study. The authors used MOSES toolkit and BLEU  score reported was 8.39 before training and 9.03 after tuning. heading: 3.1 Parallel Corpus
content: Parallel corpora are defined as a large collection of texts in two languages that are translations of each other . They are  an essential resource for bi-lingual and multi-lingual NLP research and especially for training an automatic MT system. For SMT, large-scale good quality parallel corpus is required to get useful results.

heading: 4.1  Design and Architecture
content: The basic architecture diagram of a English-Urdu SMT system. Figure 2  Architecture of SMT System The three major phases are used in building the SMT namely Translational Model, D ecoder Algorithm and Language Model. We use English and Urdu parallel corpora for training in the Translational Model while for language model training only one language is needed. So therefore, we used the English language as target language. In Decoder Algorithm  phase, after performing the language and translation model  training, the most match string which has highest probability generate an output of target language.

heading: 4.2 Pre-Processing the Data
content: In pre-processing stage, we firstly clean the data by removing incorrect and out of vocabulary words from both languages. From Urdu language we remove different "؁", "؎", "٭", "؛  " characters from the text.

heading: 26 of 41                                                                                                                                                                             18 May 2018
content: And from English language we convert the English sentences into lower cases. Then we split the sentences into words in both languages that called tokenization.

heading: 4.3 Tools for Training Data
content: Moses is the collection of tools in SMT, which is written in Perl with some in C++ [15]. We provide parallel data to Moses to perform the translation process. We installed following different tools that need for our system.

heading: • Installed Ubuntu:
content: To run Moses, firstly we need the Linux environment to train the system. We installed ubuntu as dual boot in our system.

heading: • Installed Moses:
content: The two models are the basic requirement for the Moses are Language Model and Reordering model.  By using these two models, the decoding process is implemented.

heading: • Reordering Model:
content: It is used to find out the appropriate translation of one another which should be based on Statistics on providing parallel corpus. We installed Giza ++ as reordering Model.  Giza ++ is a toolkit of SMT. It is the execution of IBM model. It is used to perform world- alignment for parallel corpus.

heading: • Language Model:
content: The main function of language Model (LM) to evaluate the probability of each part of sentences and paragraphs. It is usually the most time taking process. We installed the KEN- LM as the. Language Model.  We target the English language in LM. It is used to provide the assurance of fluent results. Moses use it to get the most matched sentences or those sentences which has the highest probability factor of target language by providing the set of possible translations. After the completely Installation, finally we come to the main event - training the translation model.

content: we run word-alignment (using GIZA++), phrase extraction and scoring, create lexicalized reordering tables and create your Moses configur ation file, all with a single command. Therefore, we run different commands for training the translation system.

heading: 4.4 Tuning Process
content: Tuning requires a small amount of parallel data, separate from the training data. The tuning process translates thousands of source language phrases in the tuning set with a translation model, then it compares the model's output with a set of reference human translations. This process occurs into many iterations. At each iteration, it repeats the steps until it reaches to the best optimized translation quality. We provide the results with tuning and without tuning.

heading: 4.5 Testing and Evaluation
content: Testing usually needs 10% of data which is to perform the suitable translation. And for     testing we run Moses with a command and type favorite Urdu Sentence to see the result. For Evaluation, To measure this we use another parallel data set (the test set) distinct from the ones we've used so far. And evaluate its performance in the form of BLEU Score. we get the 23.45 value result of BLEU score.

heading: 5 EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS
content: Data collected and prepared for experiment is 1,56,203 parallel sentences. Moses is used for training the English -Urdu automatic MT system. BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy Score) score is used to evaluate the results of the trained MT system. It is a score used for evaluating a machine translated sentence to the reference senten ce. A score of 1.0 indicates that it’s a perfect translation while a score of 0.0 shows a complete opposite. The whole corpus was used in the experiment, but it is divided into three sets. 75% of the data is used for training the system, 15% for tuning and 10% for testing.

heading: 8.1 Project Summary
content: Urdu language is a resource poor language when it comes to NLP research. Due to its highly rich morphological structure, it is hard to find basic NLP tools for the Urdu language . In this FYP project, w e developed a large  English-Urdu parallel corpus to train a Statistical Machine Translation System. We accomplished to collect and save a large  parallel corpus from different sources. The size of the dataset is 1,56,203 sentence pairs. The corpus is then preprocessed, cleaned and saved in standard format. We then performed  the experiment on Moses SMT toolkit to report the results. We have reported both before and after tuning results  on our parallel dataset, with a maximum value of 23.45 of BLEU score.

heading: 8.2 Future Work
content: The low BLEU score of our system can be improved by using transliterations module to handle the OOV words problem. Furthermore, we also plan to increase the size and quality dataset.
