heading: 2.1.7. A PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS OF CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK
1.1. Introduction:
content: Detection and monitoring of calories is trivial, not an easy task. It is very difficult to track daily calorie intake manually and not every person has knowledge about how many calories each food contains. People are facing health problems because of increase in weight and less exercise. By using calorie detector they can easily track their calories and can keep a proper chart of their meals. There are others scenarios in which we need calorie detector suc h as a people working in such companies or institutes where most of their time is spent sitting on the chair they have very less time for a workout and result in being overweight. So, if they want to keep track of their daily calories they can easily do th is and remain healthy. It can be used by someone conscious about their health and want to keep themselves fit.  And an old person who can’t do any exercise but wants to stay fit and healthy. Women are more conscious about their weight and they don’t have time for any kind of exercise especially for working women. it becomes very difficult for them to manage their work and health at the same time. So an application is required to solve above problems. The proposed system will tell the estimated calories by r ecognizing the food added by the registered user. Food can be entered manually and is saved in a specific category. Design and Development of calorie detector app to automatically recognize the food and tell its estimated calories. For this purpose, we have collected a dataset of six food categories i-e Burger, pizza, samosa, rolls, cupcake, and donuts and then train this dataset by using A.lexNet. This trained model will recognize the food by a picture and tell estimated calories and make a chart of daily calories intake by the user. The system will also make graphs of users weight and calories which will change according to their increase or decrease in weight or calories. The implementation of such a system will provide with a calorie detector which will help people to keep track of their daily consumption of calories and this system will automatically recognize the food the user just have to click a picture. It will also keep a record of daily, weekly and monthly meals and estimated calories.

heading: 1.2. Objectives:
content: To develop a calorie detector application that informs the user about estimated calories by taking a picture of food and  their daily intake of food and increase and decrease in weight and calories. The user can use this information to improve their diet plans. Our objectives are depicted below:  To facilitate people who don’t have time for any workout and are health conscious.  To automatically recognize the food added by the user.  To estimated calories form meal pictures.  To keep a record of user’s weight and calories by graphs and charts.

heading: 1.3. Problem statement:
content: People are facing health and fitness problems. Especially those who don't have time for exercise and are very busy to keep a manual record of their diet plans. So, for this purpose, an app is required which detect the calories in food and keep a record of daily calories and food intake. We are developing a calorie detector app for this purpose. This will detect the food automatically just with a picture and will provide estimated calories. This app will also keep a record of daily calories intake and will provide weight and calories graph. Graphs will increase or decrease according to daily calories taken by the user. Moreover, a user can edit information and can set their target weight app will help them to keep track of their weight.

heading: 2.1.5. Optimization of Convolutional Neural Network Parameters for Image Classification
content: Generic approach adapted: CNN has a large number of parameters and they can produce different classification accuracy based on diverse parameters including input window size, filter size, number of layers and number of neurons. They investigated the impact of these parameters on CNN accuracy in image classification. Two datasets were i -e CIFAR-10 and road-side vegetation dataset for real -world applications was selected. Experimental analysis has shown that changing the number of layers and input window size has a significant impact on classification accuracy of CIFAR -10, whereas for roadside vegetat ion dataset input window size and filter size have maximum impact on classification accuracy. The proposed optimization approach achieved higher accuracy (81%) than the accuracy obtained by Alexnet (77.75%) and PSO-CNN (80.15%) on a CIFAR-10 dataset.[5]

heading: Handwritten Character Recognition
content: Generic approach adapted: Two states of the art deep learning architectures were used which includes Caffe AlexNet and GoogleNet models in NVIDIA DIGITS. The frameworks were trained and tested on two different datasets for incorporating diversity and complexity. One of them is the publicly available dataset i.e. Chars74K comprising of 7705 characters and has upper and lowercase English alphabets, along with numerical digits. While the other dataset created locally consists of 4320 characters. The local dataset consists of 62 classes and was created by 40 subjects. It also consists of upper and lowercase English alphabets, along with numerical digits. The overall dataset is divided in the ratio of 80% for training and 20% for the testing phase. The time required for training phase is approximately 90 minutes. For validation part, the results obtained were compared with the ground truth. The accuracy level achieved with AlexNet was 77.77% and 88.89% with Google Net. The higher accuracy level of GoogleNet is due to its unique combination of inception modules, each including pooling, convolutions at various scales and concatenation procedures.[6]

heading: MODELS IN SAR TARGET RECOGNITION
content: Generic approach adapted: In this paper, the representative convolution neural network models such as AlexNet, VGGNet, GoogLeNet, ResNet, DenseNet, SENet  and so on are applied to SAR image target recognition. According to the accuracy, parameter quantity, training time and other indicators, the performance of different CNN models are analyzed and compared on MSTAR data set, the superiority of CNN model in SAR image target recognition is verified, and it also provides a reference for the follow- up work in this field.[7]

heading: Introduction:
content: Convolutional Neural Networks are just like the ordinary neural networks but they are made up of neurons that have learnable weights and biases. Each neuron receives some inputs, performs a dot product and optionally follows it with a non -linearity. The in puts to Convolution network are images, which allows us to encode certain properties into the architecture. Unlike the regular neural network which takes a single vector as input, the ConvNet takes an input in 3 dimensions such as width, height, and depth.  And transforms 3D input volume to 3D output volume of neurons activation.[8] The convolution neural network uses 4 main types of layers to build the architecture.  Convolution Layer: In this layer, we will take the Kernel/filter (piece of the image) and takes the dot product with the input image. The size of kernel and stride value will decide the output feature map size. And each filter is mapped on to each feature map. Such as if we have 10 filters then we have 10 feature maps  Pooling Layer: This layer will downsample the image. This layer is basically used to reduce the size. This layer is just after the convolution layer and takes convolution feature map as the input and prepare a condensed feature map. We have two types of pooling: L2-pooling, max-pooling. In max-pooling, we will take the maximum activation of the filter whereas in L2-pooling we will take the square root of the sum of the squares of the activations of the filter.  RELU Layer: RELU layer will apply the element-wise activation function and will update all the negative values of the feature map to zero. Such that the size of the volume remains unchanged.  Fully Connected Layer: FC layer will compute the class score just like the ordinary neural network. each neuron in this layer will be conne cted to all the neurons in the previous layer. This layer is basically used to predict the class label.

heading: Deep Learning:
content: Deep learning is the most advanced form of machine learning for classifying the objects. The architecture of deep learning is such that first, it will extract the features from the object and then what features are used to classify. Whereas simple machine learning will only use to classify the objects and we will extract features manually using other techniques such as SIFT.[9]

heading: Transfer Learning:
content: Transfer learning is the type of learning in which we use pre -defined models to solve our classification model. This will help us not to make the model from scratch and save s our time. There are a lot of models made on different types of problems and shared with the public on CAFFE MODEL ZOO, From where the people will take the model related to their problem and started working on it. As if they try to build the model from scratch it takes a lot of time to converge such as in days or weeks. But the weights of these pre-defined models were adjusted in such a way that they converge very fast. We have two types of transfer learning:  Modify the input and output layer.  Modify the internal layers also. There are several most common architectures in the field of deep learning [11] such as:  LeNet. The first successful convolution neural network was developed by Yann LeCun in 1990's.  AlexNet. The first neural network in the field of computer vision was developed by Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoff Hinton in 2012. And is the winner of imagenet ILSVRC 2012 challenge.  ZF Net. This architecture was developed by Matthew Zeiler and Rob Fergus. And is the winner of imagenet ILSVRC 2013 challenge. It has some improvements in the architecture of AlexNet.

heading: 87 | P a g e
content:  GoogLeNet. The ILSVRC 2014 winner was a Convolutional Network from  Szegedy et al. from Google. Its main contribution was that it reduces the number of parameters as compared to AlexNet. AlexNet: Structure of AlexNet is very simple than other architectures. It has Five convolutional layer and three Fully Connected Layers. After each Convolutional layer, we will use an activation function RELU in the Relu layer and all the negative values will be changed to zero. The output of the layer is calculated by the formula: image size – filter size/ stride +1. [10]

heading: Input Layer:
content: We will take the input in AlexNet  in [227x227x3]. Where 227x227 is the image pixel size and 3 denotes the depth of the image such that it denotes the RGB channel of the image.

heading: First Convolutional Layer:
content: Input from the input layer is transferred to the CONV1 Layer. We will apply the 96 filters each of kernel size 11 and stride of 4. So the output of this layer is [55x55x96].

heading: First Pooling Layer:
content: The output of CONV1 layer is transferred to POOL1 Layer. Where we can apply the filter of size 3 and stride of 2. So it compresses the image size and the output of this layer will be [27x27x96].

heading: Second Convolutional Layer:
content: CONV2 layer takes input from POOL1 Layer. Where we can apply 256 filters each of kernel size 5, stride of 1 and padding of 2. So the output of this layer will become [27x27x256].

heading: Second Pooling Layer:
content: The output of CONV2 layer is transferred to POOL2 Layer. Where we can apply the filter of size 3 and stride of 2. So it compresses the image size and the output of this layer will be [13x13x256].

heading: Third Convolutional Layer:
content: CONV3 layer takes input from POOL2 Layer. Where we can apply 384 filters each of kernel size 3, stride of 1 and padding of 1. So the output of this layer will become [13x13x384].

heading: Fourth Convolutional Layer:
content: CONV4 layer takes input from CONV3 Layer. Where we can apply 384 filters each of kernel size 3, stride of 1 and padding of 1. So the output of this layer will become [13x13x384].

heading: Fifth Convolutional Layer:
content: CONV5 layer takes input from CONV4 Layer. Where we can apply 256 filters each of kernel size 3, stride of 1 and padding of 1. So the output of this layer will become [13x13x256].

heading: Third Pooling Layer:
content: The output of CONV5 layer is transferred to POOL3 Layer. Where we can apply the filter of size 3 and stride of 2. So it compresses the image size and the output of this layer will be [6x6x256]. Fully Connected Layers (FC6,FC7,FC8): In these layers, every neuron in the previous neuron is connected to all the neurons In the next layer. They use softmax activation function for classification in the output layer.   The f eatures from the POOL3 layers is transferred to FC6 layer for classification. FC6 and FC7 have 4096 neurons in each layer and the FC8 layer will predict the class label. heading: Abstract
content: The aim of this project is to offer quality smart restaurant services and to decrease the effort for providing these services in Pakistan. This project, the Smart Restaurant Service, involves development of two systems, the Restaurant Service Automation Sy stem and the Online Food Ordering System. One system will be used by restaurant customers to directly place their food order and send notification of that order to restaurant kitchen staff through a smartphone/tab device placed on each dining table of the restaurant While the other will be used to let the online customers to order food online from different restaurants. Both these systems will contain a common administrator interface which will be operated by the restaurant manager who will also be able to generate food order receipts at both Kitchen interface (only a receipt printer device) and Restaurant Manager’s interface.The whole system will have a user friendly GUI interface which can be operated even by users who are interacting with it for the first  time. The thought behind this project is to promote application development in Pakistan. Deployment of Smart Restaurant Service will involve development and installation of Smartphone application , the Restaurant Service Automation System for the restaurant and development of a web application, Online Food Ordering System.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: There are several issues which we face in both providing and receiving restaurant services in Pakistan like when we go to a restaurant (and specially when we are with a group of people), we search through a list of food items on a menu card for what we want to order, at the same time the restaurant attendant will arrive at our table and ask us what we would like to order. The restaurant attendant will wait for us and this fact might force us to quickly give an order and we may end up selecting something we do not want. Mostly in Pakistan we order food home delivery from restaurants through a call. When we explain to the receiver what we would like to order it is possible that he/she might misunderstand a food item or it’s quantity for another. Another issue is that when we go to a restaurant sometimes there are already a lot of guests present. We have to wait a bit until the attendant arrives at our table and takes our order. And the attendant has to go to the kitchen every time he takes an order and gives the order receipt to the staff at kitchen. This whole process will consume a lot of time. The aim of our project, Smart Restaurant Service is to provide a solution for these above mentioned issues and take res taurant services in Pakistan to the next level of ease. These issues are a bit similar to each other but at the same time are also different. Therefore to tackle them our project, Smart Restaurant Service will involve the development of two separate systems. The first system, Restaurant Service Automation System will be used to deal with providing and receiving restaurant services within a restaurant. The second one is Online Food Ordering System which will be used to order food online by selecting desired restaurant and placing  an order from a selected restaurant’s menu and ordering food through home delivery. Both these systems will contain a common administrator interface which will be operated by the restaurant manager who will also be able to manage restaurant records, view change activity log, receive customer order notifications and generate food order receipts at both Kitchen interface (only a receipt printer device) and Restaurant Manager’s interface. Most of the functionalities we have mentioned ab ove for both systems are already present in existing systems like Foodpanda and McDonald’s touch interface ordering system etc. What is unique about our project is that it holds two different systems and each will encounter different challenges of the same  domain. Both systems will have a common administrator interface which will make the management of records a lot easier. The administrator interface will be connected to the kitchen interface to generate and print food order receipts directly in the kitche n. The Online Food Ordering System will  also have the feature to make table reservation and to book a food order in advance if a table is reserved. The Smart Restaurant Service will also be able to manage discounts according to the needs of every restaurant. Due to an always increasing demand of new and easy to use services, it is now even more important to become skilled at developing applications for new computer technologies. The thought behind this project is to promote application development in Pakis tan. Introducing new services through modern tools and technologies will certainly help in taking Pakistan one step closer in becoming a better developed country. Once the system is deployed across different restaurants, it will also motivate people to develop such more applications related to the domestic

content:  In a restaurant, when guests are going through the menu of food list, the restaurant attendant /server arrives at the guest’s table, the attendant/server waits for the guests to give an order, at the same time the guests will feel a bit under pressure (because of the attendant/server waiting for them) and may not end up selecting what they really w ant. Whenever we like to order food from a restaurant we choose different items from the brochure and make a call to restaurant contact number. The receiver as ks us about what we would like to order? We explain to him/her about our order but sometimes the receiver might misunderstood a food item for another or may not be able catch the correct required quantity of food item. The prices of food items on the broch ures do not remain the same forever; this also often misleads the customer (the caller) about prices and total bill of food order. Smartphone applications like Foodpanda are solving this issue but are still not very popular among Pakistanis. Our goal here is to promote the use of Smartphone applications for ordering food online even more.  Sometimes when we go to a restaurant there are already a lot of customers present in the restaurant and we have to wait a lot until our order gets prepared. With our proje ct, the Smart Restaurant Service, we can solve this problem by placing an order online to start preparing our order right after we arrive at the restaurant.  No popular system exists which synchronizes both online food ordering system and restaurant service automation system with each other. heading: 1.5 Project Scope

Both these systems will have a common administrator interface operated by the restaurant’s manager to view and manage the contents of both systems. In the Restaurant Service Automation System, users, guest/restaurant customer who will order food inside the restaurant, will be provided with a smart phone application, installed on a device placed on each dining table in the restaurant, to select desired menu. The complete menu of the restaurant will be displayed on the tab along with the price and an image of the food. The customer will select the desired food and/or drink which he/she wants to order. When the customer has selected all the desired food and/or drink items with quantity to order, the app will display the total bill. The guest can then select the option to “place ord er”. After an order has been placed, the notification of order details will be transferred to a restaurant manager’s interface and a receipt will be generated through receipt printing devices on both restaurant manager and restaurant kitchen end. The system will calculate order preparation time and display a message on the restaurant customer’s interface e.g. your order will be ready in almost 15 minutes. A countdown will begin on the guest -side interface, and the food will be served to the guest in or before the timer ends. After placing an order the restaurant customers will be able give feedback about restaurant interface through their interface. The system will also be able to manage discounts according to the needs of every restaurant. Right now, this S martphone application is planned to be developed for just android devices. In the Online Food Ordering System, user, who will order food online, can view a  the list of different restaurants with details like food menu, restaurant deals, give review etc, op tion for home delivery and option for booking table along with location of table in the restaurant. heading: 2.1.1 McDonalds touch interface ordering system
content: McDonalds is one of the most famous fast food restaurant chains across the world. They have planned to change their manual restaurant services into automation, by introducing the emenu and provide a touch interface for food ordering. With this system restaurant customers will not have to go the counter or place their order in old fashioned way rather then they will be provided a touch interface o r a machine that will take order. Customer’ s will place their order by a touch screen and their table number will be recorded after placing order, then customer’s order will be brought to their table by waiter. In most of the major outlets of Pakistan and  USA McDonalds are using this advance technology for the restaurant customer easiness.

heading: 2.1.2 Foodpanda
content: It is the mostly used online food ordering application now a day’s which connects the people with the best restaurant around them using GPS system. There webs ite version also provides the facility to order and live chat with their team for customer satisfaction. Food panda is currently active in 40 countries globally.

heading: 2.1.3 Supermeal
content: It is also an online food ordering application which provides a portal for the peop le of Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, and Hyderabad. It has almost same features like all apps have, provide menu details, menu prices, discount details of different restaurant’s and the customer can earn the discount and points when the order is p laced online. The application also provides the rating system for the customer’s so that they can review the restaurant services, food quality.

heading: 2.1.4 Zomato
content: It is a restaurant finder app currently active in 10,000 cities in India, USA, Qatar, Ireland and many other countries. It lets you search for or discover the restaurants from viewing restaurant menus, photos, customer reviews and ratings. It also gives you map feature which guide you to the restaurant location. The website version shows the same features that the customer can search in the city and restaurant which he wants to go. The application currently has more usage in India and USA.

heading: 2.6 Software Development Life Cycle Model
content: The SDLC model which is used in our system is the Waterfall model. We have considered this model best suited for our project because:  It is very simple to understand and easy to use.  Because our requirements are certain (requirements are well understood) therefore this model is best suited for our project.  Because we have less human resources and have only a development time period of one year, therefore using Waterfall model will be the ideal choice. This decision will let us avoid performing activities like risk handling and te sting in multiple phases which will consume time.  It will be easier to manage our project with Waterfall model.  The waterfall model will force us to be extraordinary disciplined in our design and structure.

heading: 3.3.1  MVC Architecture
content: Our project contains two modules as:

heading:  Online Food Ordering System
content: So the system architecture that we are using for (Online Food Ordering System) is MVC. Figure 15 MVC Smart Restaurant Service is a complex system, its first module is based on web application and second module is based on android app version. The system basically provides customer easiness, customer satisfaction and clarity of their order by using latest technology of online food ordering services. MVC consists of three basic components model, view, and controller. Model usually contains the state (data and logic) of overall application. View is used to display the data and act as a presenter. Controller act as an interface between model and view, it stores all the logic on which model and view will work whenever an input is received.

heading: 104 of 167
content: Our pro ject model contains our database, view contains all the displaying interfaces and controller will contain all the controlling logic. This separation will make our work easy, flexible and more secure. MVC framework is easy to maintain, easy to test.

heading: 3.3.2  MVP Architecture
content: For the second module of the project (Restaurant Service Automation System) we are applying MVP architecture. Figure 16 MVP MVP stands for (model, view, presenter) basically it is an advance form of MVC, and it is used a lot in android projects. In MVP there are also three basic components model, it is a data layer and its role is to access the data (database) and handles the business logic and communication with the network. View, it is a user interface layer it represents the data and notifies the presenter about it. Presenter, fetch the data from model and apply the UI logic and update the view. Our second module is based on MVP framework as we are developing the android app version of our web

heading: 105 of 167
content: application, so MVP is suitable for it. Android allows you to develop your app the way you want and that is its key factor. MVP design provides you separation of concern, dividing the code separately so that each code is easily understandable and modified and used. It provides the testability of the code by performing unit testing; you are able to know your code behaviour, function, input and output. Most of developer’s prefer unit testing in MVP design.

heading: 5.1 Problems Faced and Lessons Learned
content: Developing the two modules of our project carry different technologies to learn as working in a framework for developing our system was new to us. Implementat ion of “Restaurant Service Automation System” using android studio, IDE was new to us but it helped us a lot in the implementation of our project. The Work break down structure created many levels of details which took time to analyse it. But at the end it helped us to achieve our system requirements and the flow of work that we need to follow for the completion our application. We faced some difficulties while implementing Online Food Ordering System as a system unique for every restaurant; therefore, we de cided to make Online Food Ordering System a common system for all restaurants registered in our database. We directed our attention to APIs and PHP framework SLIM which we think is better (compared to framework laravel) at handling the development/implemen tation of projects which comprise of systems of different platforms, like our project, which includes an android application and a web application (and in the future may also require an iOS application or implementation on some other platform).  We faced some problems with back end implementation because in the initial development phase our database was complex and was not normalized. Our database was causing data redundancy; therefore, with proper guidance we redesigned our database and normalized it.

heading: 5.2 Project Summary
content: The proposed system provides quality restaurant service to generic public and also to decrease the efforts required in providing restaurant services for restaurant staff and also to let the guests to select the desired menu with ease. Our system  will provide restaurant customer satisfaction, restaurant customer convenience, flexible menu management, effective productivity. The customer’s now don’t have to stand in the queue or wait so long for their order, they will be provided with new touch interface ordering system/tablet on respective restaurant’s table to improve the efficiency of restaurant table ordering.

heading: 5.3 Future Work
content: This project is vast and regarding future needs it is flexible enough to expand even more. The future work planned for this project is:  To develop an Android and an iOS version of Online Food Ordering System (which is currently only a web application).  To also provide smartphone device(s) (along with the smartphone application for the restaurant), specially designed for restaurant service providing purpose.  To target other domains as well and to add features related to those domains in our software system.

heading: Abstract
content: The world of retail industry is growing at a rapid pace in the current times of data-driven revolutions. The competition here is based solely on the strategies formed by the experts and their ability to predict the future trends, only then can be an efficient and profitable working module be guaranteed. Big Data is considered to be an asset for these predictions and planning processes. Useful patterns are extracted from the data to foresight the production demands. In our project the factors impacting these trends will be put into consideration and data would be extracted to predict the expected future sales of the product for ensuring accurate production and better decision making.

heading: 1.1  Introduction
content: The trend of paying by cash is gradually vanishing from the society with the passing time as credit cards and other payments methods are now available for the ease of customer and a Point of Sale software for handling all these payments. A point of sale is also used when payments are made by cash. Besides that, we do know that at present times the world feeds on ‘Data’, it is data that is making websites and companies operate on such large scale, similarly social websites use data such as the location of the user and his/her interests and then use that extracted data to filter out people and find groups with common interests. This information is used by them to improve their advertising techniques. A particular subject is showed to specific people. We have developed a module of data entry  that will keep a record of the  sale purchase being made of a product. The data entries  made are to be saved and backed up on the server, this data will be available for us to fetch and app ly forecasting algorithms. ARIMA for Time Series Forecasting, Simple Linear Regression, Multivariant Linear Regression are used for forecasting. The factors  under consideration are temperature, fuel, CPI (Consumer Price Index) and unemployment rate. The technologies we have used are C# for the Data Entry Module and Python Jupyter Notebook for the forecasting algorithms.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: • To record the units sold of a product according to our need as the forecasting is being made based on it. • The module can be mo dified, and functionalities could be added to put it into use, that would be generating data values which will be used by us and meet the basic requirements of the point of sale system. • Data Visualization to find data behaviour. • Forecast Sales using time patterns. • Improve the planning process for organizations by saving time and effort. • Production planning to be made easier. Our model  will use sales  data to forecast the measures with time patterns. This will help in improving planning process for organizations. Amount of production of a product and its marketing can also be affected by this. The planning procedure will be a lot mature once you know the demand and expected sales.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: The industry is growing at a rapid pace. In this era of competition, entrepreneurs are establishing innovative ideas to give them the competitive edge. • In this process of succeeding from others, the production has enhanced. But the amount of production of the article has not been specified rather entrepreneurs are looking for promotions and providing discounts to the customers to sell their product. Still, the waste of resources is mighty huge. As not every person is looking to buy an article of a particular brand. People are more satisfied with the products they are using on a regular basis. So, our system provides a value that how much a particular product should be manufactured to avoid financial variation and waste of resources. • In this global village, the market strategies are playing a vital role in retail business. The problem lies as the entrepreneurs do not have sufficient data to make such strategies. By using our module, we can collect necessary data for application of machine learning algorithms on them to forecast sales. • Entrepreneurs develop plans, but uncertain situations may occur that creates ambiguity. Some of such situations are temperature variations and festival holidays. Hence, to create such strategies that include weather factor is quite of the scale. Our system includes one best feature of temperature forecasting and by including this factor predicting best trends in the market. • New entrants are often unsure where to invest and are unable to meet their expected sales despite putting good marketing efforts for it. If they would have better knowledge regarding the trends and future demands of similar products as compared to theirs t hey will stand at a better position.

heading: 1.6 Project Scope
content: The concept of an e-wallet is gaining importance on daily bases. Applications such as SIMSIM , i.e., a mobile wallet application developed by Finja, allow the user to m ake real-time payments through multiple methods, such as P2P payments, QR based payments, card-based payments and even allows the user to transfer money to bank accounts. These applications are becoming popular day by day , and they will frequently be used in the near future . Our motivation is to provide them with POS software that is free of cost and in return keeps a record of their daily sales. In this way, we could use their data for data sciences and business intelligence algorithms that could yield information valuable to large organizations. The procedures of data mining, data warehousing, data analysis, data sciences and business intelligence would be performed . Our System will have following key features:

This data could be used by companies to target specific advertising of products knowing the demand for specific products in specific areas and making sure that the need of a product is identified in the market, so no material is  wasted due to overstocking of product and no product goes short in the market due to customer demand turning out to be more than the expected demand. New entrants in the market can use this analyzed data to have a deeper  look at the marketing trends to make decisions about their product launch and its demand in various regions of interest.

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: “Big data is high -volume, high -velocity and high -variety information assets that demand cost - eﬀective, innovative forms of information processing for enhanced insight and decision making” [1] The world in the present times feeds on Data, it's because of this data that companies are being able to operate on such large scale. The  buying pattern and analysis of the changing demands of the customer play an important role in planning and launching different products for the company. Similarly, social websites extract data by capturing interests of the user and their locations to filt er them and find groups with similar interests ; this can be used for advertising strategies. Beaver, Kumar, Li, Sobel and Vajgel [2] report that Facebook processes up to one million photographs per second. Other estimates suggest that Facebook stored 260 billion photos using storage space of over 20 petabytes. Given the increasing importance of big data, companies can leverage on these data to exploit new opportunities and gain an in -depth understanding of the hidden values. Companies in many industries are increasingly interested in their potentialities since they c an generate high revenues [3]. According to International Data Corporation [4] “Big data and business analytics worldwide revenues will grow from nearly $122 B in 2015 to more than $187 B in 2019, an increase of more than 50% over the ﬁve-year forecast period”. Big data can be obtained  from within and outside companies, in the form of structured and unstructured data, and it can generate diﬃculties for co mpanies in capturing, aggregating, analyzing and extracting value from them. [5] Businesses are collecting more data than they know what to do with. [6] It's not been long that people realized that this data could be of any use for their business or industry, special skills are required to turn this raw data into useful data and take advantage from it and companies devote significant financial and human r esources for this purpose. As stated in [4] “Big Data is worthless in a vacuum. Its potential value is unlocked only when leveraged to drive decision making”. Decision making based on trends and forecasting helps companies to make sure that a specific product exists there at the right place and the right time. There are many positive aspects of big data, but companies do hesitate as capital is required for processing of data and extracting meaningful findings from it. The key contribution of this paper would be to demonstrate and provide evidence of how big data can be helpful in decision making. In third world countries  like Pakistan and many others, the importance of data sciences is yet to be acknowledged by the small-scale businessmen. Large organization and retail chains do realize the benefits of big data and how valuable their everyday sales record is, thus they ar e moving with the pace of the western world and putting it into full use.

heading: 5.5 Conclusion
content: The results are not 100% accurate.  Only one year worth of data isn't that much, whereas having multiple years data could have helped us improve the acc uracy quite a bit.  This shows that there are multiple factors that affect  the sales of a product. The project scope of evaluating seasonal effect is covered  efficiently. The results are based  on real-time values. If we do not have values of other factors l ike temperature etc, then we conclude that ARIMA model provides the optimal results. The regression is used  where we are evaluating the results by other factors like CPI, Humidity, etc. In the model that we defined to retrieve data from the Point of Sale and apply Machine learning to predict sales of a product. The Point of sale does not store temperature. Hence, if the data is directly gathered from POS the best model to predict sales is ARIMA time series model. But the flaw is that we should have a large dataset to maintain the accuracy of prediction.

heading: Abstract
content: Considering the current scenario of Pakistan, millions of students each year are compelled to pick their study program without legitimate direction. Ignorant of critical deadlines, scholarships, alternative options in terms of institutes for same study program and internship opportunities. Career opportunities are not well exposed to students per their study programs. There are no discussion platforms where crucial matters like above can be discussed and seek guidance from people who already faced them. The idea is to propose a system, an all-in-one platform to cater all above-mentioned issues. Student and institute profiling are maintained, to guide students choose for a better option. Utilities like guidance literature for admissions, scholarships and career development plus merit calculator are provided. Interactive discussion forum adds more value to our product as it allows people to discuss issues starting from general questions about academia to research questions. A tier system is maintained, grading students and institutes into different levels, restricting their access over our system. The system is smart enough showing students exact scholarship/internship opportunities, they can really opt for. Data mining and analysis techniques plus student’s rating of our system suggest institutional options for them. Smart phone application is developed to provided push up notifications to keep students updated more efficiently.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: With the passage of time, amelioration in web and mobile technologies have projected extraordinary solutions. Education, itself is a challenging process but people opting for it with no proper guidance makes it more complex. The change in people behaviour, finding themselves more comfortable with e-products raise the need of an educational portal, manoeuvring people around in search of better opportunities. In our country, students confront a considerable amount of issues in their educational career. They are the most unguided students on the planet. Neither the parent because of their obliviousness nor the instructors because of lack of professionalism, guide them properly. Absence of direction is intense issue which student confront. In Pakistan education is incredibly dearly-won owing to the shortage of public institutes. Most of our students belong to the middle class and have terribly restricted resources. Parents can’t simply afford the expenses. Numerous students need to work half time to sponsor their studies themselves. In student life, nearly each student typically faces money crisis. The existing solutions in market are providing study program guidance and scholarship updates in a diffused way. ScholarHub provides information in a legitimate way, all under one roof. Proper guidance is provided. Scholarships are published per student’s previous interaction with the system. Students ought to get basic knowledge concerning any profession before deciding to require it as their future profession. For this purpose, they must consult the persons that are already in that profession. Discussion platform in ScholarHub provide discussion forums to cater this issue. Interactive discussion forums divided into different disciplines is created, permitting students to discuss their queries. Profiling of students and institutions are maintained over some criteria, grading them into different categories. Internship opportunities per disciplines and institute are published recommending students keeping in view their study background and rating over web site. Important dates and events are published to keep students updated.

heading: 1.2 Objective
content: Major goals we are tried to achieve through our product are listed below: • To exploit market gap in educational portal field. • Provide service to students searching for information related to educational system. • Discussion forum for students to interact and discuss questions. • Scholarship and internship opportunities for students. • Breaking down longer, lengthy processes of scholarships into step. • Factors to consider institutes. Key points to consider while opting an institute for a study program. • Deadline notifications of various admission, scholarship and internship opportunities.

heading: 2.6 Software development life cycle model
content: We are using an evolutionary model that is Incremental Model for our project. It includes four steps:

heading:  Test
content: We chose this model because we need increments at every stage if changes are required then we will make the desired changes and go to the next increment. We can repeat this process following the delivery of each increment, until the complete product is produced. If the customer demands delivery by a date that is impossible to meet, we will suggest delivering one or more increments by that date and the rest of the Software later. Figure 2: Software development life cycle

heading: 2.6.1 Analysis
content: In this phase, we gather the business requirements for our project.

heading: 2.6.2 Design
content: In this phase requirements that we identified in the Analysis Phase will be transformed into a System Design Document that will accurately describe the design of the system and that can be used as an input to system development in the next phase.

heading: 2.6.3 Code
content: In this phase after software application is designed properly and requirements are gathered accurately, the coding process is more streamlined. It will include implementation of the design specified in the design document into executable programming language code. We will be better able to meet software coding deadlines when the correct information is gathered upfront from the customer.

heading: 2.6.4 Test
content: In this phase, the code will be tested and mapped against the design document created in the design phase. The output of the testing phase will be a test report containing errors that occurred while testing the application.

heading: 3.4.1 MVC Framework
content: MVC(Model-View-Controller) is an architecture which divide your application into three logical parts: Model, View and Controller. Each one them handle certain aspects of the application. MVC is one of the most used web application development framework. It is used to make scalable and extensible projects.

heading: 3.4.1.1 Laravel
content: Laravel is a powerful framework, designed for developers who needs a powerful, simple and elegant toolkit. It’s an open source framework with rich features which really speedup the process of developing websites. Its built-on core PHP which even makes it easier to use for new developers. ScholarHub is built on Laravel 5.4.36. Laravel provides features like: Modularity, Testability, Routing, Configuration management, Query builder and ORM (Object Relational Mapper), Schema builder, migrations, and seeding, Template engine, E-mailing, Authentication, Radis, Queues, Event and command bus. Figure 5: MVC Diagram

heading: 3.4.2 Machine Learning
content: Machine learning is a field which brings humans and machines nearer by enabling humans to “teach” machines. Machines learn by process a legitimate coaching set that contains the options necessary to tune associate rule. The rule allows machines to execute specific tasks, like classifying email, building catalogue, identifying diseases and suggesting solutions. ScholarHub uses Apache’s PredictionIO [11]. Suggestions and recommendations are given to users after monitoring users activity on website. ScholarHub is made intelligent and unique using Machine Learning and Predictive techniques.

heading: 3.4.2.1 PredictionIO
content: Apache PredictionIO an open source Machine Learning standalone server which is bundled with Apache Spark, MLlib, HBase Spray and Elasticsearch which enables you to create predictive engines for any machine learning task. It lets you:  Quickly build and deploy an engine as a Web-service with customizable templates.  Responds to dynamic queries in real-time  Deploy multiple engines variants at a time.  Support machine learning and data processing libraries such as MLlib and OpenNLP  Implement your own machine learning model and incorporate them into your engines. Figure 6: PredictionIO Architecture

heading: 3.4.2.2 PredictionIO Deployment
content: PredictionIO constitutes on two major parts: Event Server and Engines. Event Server is used for continuously storing data from our ecommerce platform. PredictionIO uses PostgreSQL to store the data send from our ecommerce platform. The dataset is trained and deployed. The engines receive queries from the ecommerce platform and returns the predicted results. The engine is responsible for making predictions.

heading: Abstract
content: In our daily life we use cloud storage for backing up our data to minimize the chances of data loss in case of disk corruption or any other hardware failure. Usually, the storage capacity these cloud services provide is not sufficient to store large amount of data of end user. This leads the user to make multiple accounts of different cloud services. With large amount of data stored in multiple locations, data management becomes difficult.  Additionally, to replicate critical data, files have to be manually copied to multiple locations. This project proposes a system that manages multiple cloud storages by providing a single platform to users from where they can upload, retrieve and replicate data according to its criticality. heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: With the advancement of technology, personal devices have become very common and all personal and official data of a user is stored on these personal devices. These personal devices, like all hardware, are prone to failure. Most of us have faced situations where at the time of critical need, our hard disk crashes or our personal devices start to malfunction. If the data was not backed-up, then we have to start from scratch. Over recent years, big technology companies like Google, Microsoft and Dropbox have started to provide free public cloud storage services. We use these online storage systems to store our data so that we can access it anywhere, at any time, without having to worry about hardware failure or unavailability of our personal devices. Usually, the storage capacity provided by the cloud services, at free of cost, is not sufficient to store large amount of data of the end user. To store all or most of the important data on cloud storage, the end user makes multiple accounts on different cloud serv ices. Most common cloud storage services include “OneDrive” by Microsoft, “Google Drive” by Google, and “Dropbox” by Dropbox Inc. Each service provides a directory that serves as an interface between the personal device and the cloud storage. All data that  is placed in those directories are synced and updated to the cloud storage through the Internet. With large amount of user data distributed manually by the user in multiple directories, data management becomes difficult. A user might have multiple accounts and does not know how much space he is left with in each account, or on which account the specific file is stored. Therefore, handling and keeping track of data is a hectic problem. Additionally, for some reason, if a cloud service is down at the time of  need of a critical file and the file is not backed-up, we can face severe consequences. In this regard, we propose a system that manages multiple cloud storages by providing a single platform to users from where they can upload, retrieve and replicate da ta according to its criticality. In this project, we are developing a desktop application which will allow user to store maximum data by efficiently managing the cloud space. End user will be able to manage number of accounts like “One Drive, “Google Drive ”, “Drop Box” etc.  at a time , and through  our application interface, user will be able to do all the management, operation on files. It will be the task of our application to look for available spaces and upload it according to placement and memory management algorithms, and update the database that will be keeping track of all the files uploaded. If the user tries to upload same file again, database will inform the user that the file already exists. Based on the criticality of the data file, specified by t he user, our application will replicate the data file in multiple clouds, so that if one of the cloud services is down, the file is still accessible through another cloud service. Page 9 of 47

heading: 1.2 Motivation
content: Unlike hard disk, we can store limited amount of data in cloud storage which is mostly comprised of our important documents, files, software etc. To store more data on the cloud, we have to acquire a number of cloud storages from different service providers. With multiple accounts, it becomes difficult to rememb er the details like how much space is left in our drives, on which drive a specific file is uploaded, which file is no longer need  but is occupying space in the drive, and which critical file needs to be replicated in more than one drives. To provide ease to the users, some web based applications are providing assistance to perform some of these functionalities, but not all in a single application. Additionally, all of these applications are available as paid products.

heading: 1.3 Scope
content: Our motivation is to develop a desktop application that deals with all of the above mentioned functionalities in a single interface and provide it to users free of cost. For our project, we will be dealing with three major cloud storages i.e. “One Drive”, “Google Drive” & “Drop Box”.

heading: 1.4 Objectives
content: Following are the Goals and Objectives of our project:  Our basic objective is to facilitate cloud users by tackling the problem of managing numerous cloud resources due to lack of provided storage. As soon as the storage capacity of a cloud reso urce is full, user needs to have another account to get additional storage for his data. As the number of accounts increases, so does the complexity of managing them. This application will provide an efficient system to manage all those cloud-based accounts.   To provide the users an efficient platform to manage their cloud resources.   To minimize the user’s involvement in managing their data to ease them.   Saving the users from the headache of keeping record of multiple cloud accounts.   To provide the users  a friendly interface to manage their multiple cloud resources from a single place at a same time.  Page 10 of 47  Our objective is to develop such a free of cost application which will help us in our daily life to save our time.

heading: 1.5 Problem Statement
content: Users have to manage bulk of data through different cloud storages, and have to deal with all the storages manually. Keeping the record of different cloud storages separately increases their headache. Which cloud storage has how much space left? Which file or document is locate d at which cloud storage? Which file or document is located at more than one [1] cloud storages? If a file or document is located at more than one storages, then which should be deleted to make room for the new data? These are some of the problems that use rs have to deal with on daily basis, which causes a lot of trouble for them. Our application is designed to tackle these problems. It will lessen users’ worries by providing them a platform through which they can manage all of their data without directly d ealing with the cloud storages. Our application, through specially designed algorithms, will automate the above mentioned tasks and keep them away from the users.

heading: 2.1.1 Jolicloud:
content: Jolicloud is a LINUX -based tool that links all of our cloud services at one place and allows access to multiple cloud services using a single web -based interface. It can handle cloud services like “One Drive”, “Google Drive” and “Drop Box”. Some of its [2] functionalities include file searching, file removing and file uploading. All these operations have to be carried out manually by the user. It does not support file transfer between cloud storages in its unpaid version. Moreover, it just allows one cloud service in its free version.

heading: 2.1.2 MultCloud:
content: MultCloud allows the user to work on 26 different cloud services at a single time. Being a paid app, in its free version, MultCloud only provides some basic functionality to users. It uses Google’s document viewer to view f iles which sometimes becomes an issue when user tries to modify a Microsoft Word Document. [3] MultCloud doesn’t let the user transfer individual files to cloud. It also gives user a schedule feature in its paid version. The interface of MultCloud is not user friendly and also lacks mobile apps version. Page 11 of 47

heading: 2.1.4 Unifyle:
content: Unifyle is a manager for Android and Android devices. It can be used for Windows OS but with web browsers. Although the files can be searched by the content, name and date range  (created and saved). Unlike our application Unifyle charges for its services. Only 10 accounts can be attached in free version [3].

heading: 2.1.5 OwnCloud:
content: OwnCloud is an open source cloud service that allows the users to access each of their cloud accounts smoothly and continuously. However, it is only for the people with a strong background of Computer Science field as it must be coded a certain way to work with different cloud accounts which isn’t possible for every user. So it’s not user friendly and can’t be used by novice people [2].

heading: 2.1.6 Cloudii:
content: Cloudii is an [2] android base cloud management service. Like our application its services comes for free, but the files are managed manually unlike our application.

heading: 2.1.7 Odrive:
content: Odrive is a desktop based service that provides a folder interface to connect all your online files on your computer, as if they are stored on your hard drive. It [4] integrates various services, and provides the users a platform to view and manage all of the cloud bases from a single space. It works as a folder on users’ personal computer. Files are managed manually though, unlike our application.

heading: 2.1.8 Air Explorer:
content: Air Explorer is a platform that enables users to access different cloud services through a single place. It works as a [5] FTP client, and allows you to exchange files between your Page 12 of 47 server and your computer or any other cloud services. It is not a freeware,  and offers only 1 account per cloud. It’s manual working is what differentiate it from our application.

heading: 2.1.9 Cloud Mounter:
content: Cloud Mounter is a cloud storage manager that enables the Mac users to use Dropbox and OneDrive from a single platform. Files will get access from your hard drives only when you decide to reach them from the cloud, hence local storage space doesn’t get wasted. Unlike our application, it can only be used for the  Mac systems  [6]. Furthermore, it only works with Dropbox & OneDrive, whereas, our application can handle multiple drives. All of the tools mentioned above basically perform a similar function. They only link different cloud services to one place and then allow users to perform tasks on them manually. But the major tasks like which files in our cloud storages needs to be updated, which file needs to be in more than one drives, how much space is left in our drives etc. remains cumbersome task of the user. Our app will not only work as a linker to all of our cloud services, but also ac t as an automation platform through which all of the essential functionalities will be performed from a single place. Instead of going to and checking every cloud service one by one manually, users can access upload, update, remove, search, check & transfe r their files through our application, free of cost.

heading: 2.5.1 Iterative development life cycle:
content: It’s a framework wherein we create modules or piece of modules in a single generation then improve this product in subsequent generation and many others unless it’s finished. Using this development lifestyle cycle on the grounds that flexibility in between modules is essentially the most normal standards of this hub. The iterative model  [7] presents a complete agenda of constructing a procedure and creates a medium of communique be tween important modules. Via using this iterative life cycle, checking out can be stronger considering the fact that the option to issues will also be compiled at the checking out time. And through making a loop of checking out and progress, modules can be made flexible. It contains six steps: Requirement Gathering and System Analysis: In this section, all viable requirements of the developing process are captured, documented in requirement specification documentation.

heading: System Design:
content: This phase includes the  gain knowledge of requirement necessities from the primary phase and design of the procedure is all set. Procedure Design helps in specifying procedure standards and also helps in defining total process architecture. If some problem occurs in this phase, then by using utilizing iterative methodology we will take a step again to the primary segment which is requirement gathering and analysis.

heading: Coding:
content: This is the core area of software development process as  it consists of writing the segments and the program which will be coupled together in the shape of complete system. Each and every segment is developed and demonstrated for its functionality basis which is then referred to as Unit testing. An implementati on may work flawed many times then we can alternate approach design by taking a step again. Integration and Testing: This segment includes the units developed in the implementation phase is built -in right into a process after the trying out of each unit. The whole procedure is proven for any bugs until final integration. Deployment of System: Once the functional and non - functional testing is finished, this section includes the product deployed into the market. Page 19 of 47

heading: Maintenance:
content: The last phase adjusts and improves the system by considering the user’s evaluation, feedback and enhancements based on their due recommendations. in this phase, due maintenance and help is also provided to the users against their queries, problems and ambiguities.

heading: Justification:
content: In iterative model, we can split the stages in smaller time frames. Then divide work in half so each of us put effort in the building of the system. Start is a little time taking but when the product is developed to some extent, to add new features, and overrid e the old version with the new one is easy. It allows us to develop system in partial fragments. But the complexity of the system increases as does the stage completes. Also, it allows us to use the inherent property [8], which is we build new features on older version of system. Page 20 of 47

heading: Chapter 3: Methodology
content: We have developed our own algorithms as the available were not very much helpful.

heading: Memory Management Algorithm
content: Memory management is the core of our project. We have designed and implemented our algorithm in a way, that in future when we would like to add more cloud storage drives like Amazon or any other than we’ll have to add just few lines of code and it’ll be up and running. Our algorithm is pretty simple, we are placing the f iles on the remaining percentage of space left in drives.as we know there are limited amount of storage space, so to deal each drive as equal space, we are converting the remaining memory to percentage and then comparing each one of them to find the least filled and place the file in it. That’s level 1 or criticality = low. At level 2, criticality level = high. We are placing the file in each drive. If that file is already present, there then it will be updated.

heading: 6.3 Project Summary
content: Cloud storage services are application software which is made for everyone’s use. These services are very essential for modern day computer user as they provide them additional storage as well as a remote backup for their important data. Different cloud st orage services offer different amount of storage spaces but perform a similar action i.e. to provide remote storage, other than the users’ hard drive, to the public. These storages are internet based services connected with users’ e-mail accounts. Cloud based management systems are the applications that provides a platform to sync all of the users’ cloud storages on a single place. Cloud based management systems that are currently available in the market works as a third party software to give users’ an acc ess to all of their cloud storages through a single screen. These software provides functio nality like connecting our all cloud storages and providing us the access through single interface. They do lessen the users’ burden of keeping record of multiple st orages at one time, but they still work manually and users do have to upload, search, and delete the files separately in every storage. With this application we have  reduced the users’ involvement in above mentioned functionalities. Our application automates the basic actions of a cloud storage management system that are uploading, searching, updating, & deleting the data. The main focus of our application is to reduce users’ headache to keep the record of their data. Our system  have the key specifications of being interactive, user friendly interface with less complexities and one the most important, secure to use.

heading: Abstract
content: Neurological disorders are frequently reported all across the world. The particular reasons for neurological issues fluctuate, yet can incorporate hereditary issue, inherent anomalies or clutters, diseases, way of life or ecological medical issues including ailing health, and cerebrum harm, spinal string damage or nerve harm.  The patient affected from neurological disorder simply gets frustrated from life and cannot d o anything productive. The sufferer of neurological disorder has the strength to live a normal life but the communication between brain and nervous system eradicates. Hence messages cannot be transmitted to other parts of the body to perform desired functi ons. To improve the condition of patients, an intelligent health care system is required which can help patients to rehabilitate through different procedures such as progressive m obilisation, training and occupational therapy. The proposed heath care syste m revolves around the occupational therapy using kinetic sensor for neurological disabled persons. The rehabilitation process will take place through the process of signal transmission along axons. The technique used to transmit signals is known as conduct ion where neuron interacts with its own terminal through axons. The proposed system would intelligently detect the signs and help in the occupational therapy of the patient using kinetic sensors. This project is being done with the collaboration of Pakista n Society for Rehabilitation of the Disabled (PSRD). This interactive purposed support system will be a major breakthrough for neurological disabled patients.

The proposed  system will improve day -to-day health care flaws in hospital across Pakistan and overcome poor health condition which is due to lack o f ICT infrastructure and time consuming procedures. heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Quibid is an online auction system quite different then the regular auction system, where user provides the auction product with the minimum price tag to purchase for a specific time and the interested buyers can bid amount they are willing to pay for that produ ct and the highest bidder qualify to purchase the product. eBay is the perfect model of the regular auction system but our presented model “Quibid” is different our company itself present items up for bid in this business however the key difference is the logic behind bids. Our business model is based on “all -pay auction” every bidder must pay regardless of winning or losing the contest. We sell our bids to our registered customer, each time they participate in a contest by placing a bid one is deducted fro m their account and to win the contest they have to stay as the last bidder. To do so they have to place a bid whenever else one places a bid. That’s not all that separates us from the conventional auction system we also introduce the “penny auction” syste m. The initial price of the product is set to zero, whenever someone place a bid the price of the product rise by one penny and a bid cost you around half a dollar. so, the final price at which product is sold is extremely lower than the product actual price, on average user can save up to 60-70% on item. Quibid also provides a “buy now” feature to the customer if they want the product at its actual cost listed at auction, to maintain a good relationship with the customer, this feature work differently it subtracted the amount that user invest in the auction via biding from the actual price. So, user have a sense of security that they never have to pay more than the actual retail price Also, they have the security that if they invest too much on a product via bidding and they lose they still have a chance of purchase that product. “Buy now” feature work till two hours of the product sale and within this time you can purchase product for its retail price minus invested money. This feature is available if and only if a customer place at least a bit on that product.  This is the framework of our business model we aim to develop. Quibid is a web -based application which implements this frame work by performing the required functionalities such as: • Manage the customer’s data • Register new customers • Manage the product store • Manage the product sales procedure include time management and bids management • Manage payment processes2

content: In Pakistan, there are many auction stores selling the products by adopting the methodology of auctions. In this way, customers are able to purchase quality products at the minimum cost. Our project aims to target the market and selling products by adopting the same methodology but in the different process. Quibid.pk provides a faste r way to sell the products by auction method online which is much faster and safer than the traditional methods. The project aims to provide accuracy, efficiency and security to the auction process. The project targets the potential customers and secures  their information in an encrypted database. The main goal of the system is to reduce the human effort and computerizing the whole auction process thus reducing the time and cost of the whole process while reducing the paper work after purchasing the product. The objectives of the system are to provide accessibility, flexibility and portability to the auction system. The project handles the risk effectively. The project analysis the statistical data regarding the sales and individual winnings. The project also provides the data in a much faster and accurate manner.

heading: 2.1. Literature Review/ Existing System Study
content: The concept of auctions has existed for many years, but the research literature on auction theory Expanded dramatically after the seminal paper by Vickrey (1961). Auctions use the market mechanism to solve the most difficult business problem, that of pricing the product. With an auction, there is no guesswork for setting up a right price for the product or service, since the price is set by the market (above some minimum). Auction-based pricing is sometimes referred to as "dynamic" or "fluid" pricing, in contrast to set or static pricing mechanisms.

heading: Related Work
content: Huge amount of work has already been done on online auction,  lots of online auction site available across the globe follows traditional auction system hierarchy like eBay, they provide framework for buyers and seller to interact and do business. Swoopo.com, BidCactus.com, Beezid.com, BigDeal.com these applications provide the services that we aim to provide, they also use the Quibid provided business framework. In Pakistan currently, no state of art system is available that provide the functionality that we wanted to provide there are lots of onl ine auction sites available in Pakistan but they follow traditional auction system and none of them get any success quiet yet.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: The aim of our project is to explore the field of business process management. In this field, we will be emphasizing on discovering the ways to evaluate the similarities among the process models that are present in the process repository. The business Process Management(BPM) is comprised of various methods and entire range of techniques that  supports analysis phase, enactment, the design and lastly management of operational business processes [1]. The BPM is a discipline in the form of a life cycle. It involves mixture of designing, modeling, execution, monitoring and lastly optimize stage fo r activity flows of the business considering supporting goals of enterprise and system spanning  [1]. In order to find the correspondence between process models, process similarity technique is introduced. Process similarity is the technique we apply on the  repositories to find out the processes that bear a resemblance to each other. To find the similarity among these process models similarity metrics were introduced that queries on the process metrics  [10]. Process model similarity query is a term used for such queries that we will apply over the process model repositories. There are three similarity metrics that are used to find the process similarity [10]. Structural Similarity metric is used for comparing labels of element including topology of process models [10]. The metric is defined by us based on the graph edit distance of business process graphs. Various operations could in fact be considered for evaluating this metric like Node deletion or insertion, Node substitution and Edge deletion or insertion  [10]. Graph Edit Distance is used to measures distance between graphs g1 and g2 by measuring distortion which is expected to change g1 into g2. The essential distortion operations of this can adapt to subjective names on both edges and nodes and in additio n with coordinated or undirected edges [13]. The second similarity metric, Behavioral Similarity metric takes the behavior of the business models as input  [10]. It compares labels of element including the unpremeditated relations that are captured in a mod el. The third and last similarity metric, Node Matching Similarity works on a principle and that is pair wise comparing of labels otherwise it can be attributes attached to the process model elements  [10]. The elements we compare include the value of the node that it contains and its attributes.

heading: 1.2 Research Problem
content: The need for finding the similarity between the process models arrived when the process analysts discovered new problems. These problems occurred when a new process model was inserted in the repository and there was no such technique available to check if any previous process models were similar to it. Also, the same problem occurred again when the company P a g e  | 10 mergers took place, where the process analyst desired about the similar process that were available in the process repositories of the two organizations.  To solve this problem, we discovered many people have published theories on ways we can accomplish that. Some of them were very promising like the work of Remco Dijk [10]. A comparative survey of business process similarity measures by Michael Becker and Ralf Laue  [14] also provides a very good insight on evaluating the similarities in the process models. Up to now, there is a notable research gap on comparing different approaches to this problem and on evaluating them in the same setting. As of now some researchers have worked on Node matching technique, but there was no proper implementation was found on the structural similarity technique. As a part of our FYP, we will be exploring the structural similarity technique , by considering all three operations for the similarity measurement, discussed earlier.

heading: 1.3 Objective
content: 1- Create a data set that constitutes of all the structural variations that are present and maintain them in a repository. 2- Compute all the 26 metrics values for the data set. 3- Development of a n application to check the correspondence of process models implementing the technique of structural similarity.

heading: 1.4 Research Flow
content: Entire 900 business process models will be present in our process repository archive each bearing an XML format acquired by utilizing CAMUNDA modular. As a part of our project first we are going to calculate the 26 -structural metrics. We will start by discovering the ways to calculate their values. These methods can be discovered by consulting different research papers. Once we have gathered enough information then we will start by learning the XML files we are being provided in the process repository. In this process, we will discover the tags that are used, to extract the relevant data that is required by us. Then we will move  on to developing phase, where we will compute each and every one of them by introducing an algorithm for each metric. Once all of them are done we will generate an Excel file of the results for further evaluation that is how we are going to interpret the results. After that we will move on to finding the structural similarity of the process models. For that we will generate a business process graph of each process model and use it as an input source. We will evaluate all the three operations described earl ier (Node deletion or insertion, Node substitution and Edge deletion or insertion ) and use their values to compute the similarity among the business process model by using the concept of edit graph distance. content: It is a petri net that models the definition of a workflow process. A workflow net typically satisfies two requirements.
