heading: 3.1 Structural Variations
content: The concept of Business process management is to deal with the changes effectively, this would only be possible if business proce sses are flexible , w hich provides the quick mapping and managing the radical changes in business. Change are made according to the policies that exists or addressing the new characteristics. Flexibility requires a response to changes that should be quick. Quick reaction is the competitive advantage to the companies that surely helps them to grow their business demands and their business by following the trends that are latest. We can achieve flexibility by producing structural change in the process model. Different people have studied structural change [8 -11,13-2,31]. Michael Becker [ 15] was also the one who studies structural changes in a process model. He introduced different variants of process models but they are not applied on any of the datasets. Furth er, there is no process repository available where they  can apply their studies of structural variation. Barbara Weber et al [2] introduced new ways in order to make process model with change flexibility. Change in flexibility of a process model is describ ed by introducing fourteen adaption patterns [16]. These adaption patterns provided us the basic guidelines for making structural changes. We produced five types of structural variations rooted from Michael Becker and Barbara [ 15] [16]. In our study, we ha ve produced repository of process models depends on the structural variations. Following are the variations: 1) Redesigned a process by putting the activities in parallel that are in sequence between the XOR gateways. 2) Added/Deleted the activities anywhere in a process model. 3) Insertion of control edge. 4) Swapping the activities. 5) Changing the labels of the activities. These variations are designed in such a way that their semantics should remain the same. Adaption patterns like [AP2, AP4, AP6, AP7, AP8, AP10, AP13, AP1] [2] and variants C and F [ 15] changes the semantics of the process models when applied, so that’s why they are not deployed in the dataset. Our study is based on those patterns and variants in which semantics should remain same. For this purpose, we used adaption patterns AP1,  AP3, AP5, AP9 [16] and mapped with variants B, D, E, G and H [15].

heading: 3.1.1 Type 1
content: The first structural variation which we denote as “Type -1” mainly deals with process models having the same number of traces, (here the word tr ace means a Path) but the structure will be different (compare Type -1 with Original model for changes). In other words, a Trace defines number of distinct execution patterns in a process model. P a g e  | 29 The Type-1 Variation is achieved by Adding of Gateways. The g ateways will be used to change the structure of the model while semantics remain the same. What a gateway does, is that it simply helps in executing activities in parallel  which changes the flow of activities that are in sequence into Parallel so that they can be executed simultaneously. Executing activities simultaneously requires (AND -Split) and on the other hand for synchronizing parallel flow involves (AND -Join) gateways. We use (XOR -Split) for mutually exclusive flows in which selection of activity is based on any data or external event and to merge these alternative flows (XOR -Join) is involved. Gateways basically give variations to the structure of any process model. Process models have control flow which is used to describe the order of the activities. Control flow can converge and diverge using available gateways. Strict sequencing describes combined fragment/activities where sequence of the event needs to occur in the order in which they’re defined. Strict sequence is not being followed here, due to which we see activities being executed in Parallel. Structure variation proposed by [15] [ 16]. In study [15], process model can be changed structurally via adaption patterns. These adaption patterns, allow users to change a process schema at the process type or instance level with help of high -level change operations (e.g. addition of activity in parallel to another one). From structural Adaption Patterns, in Adaption Pattern [AP9], the activities which are not restricted to execute in sequence can be executed in parallel by using parallel gateway. After parallel execution of activities, traces of the process model will remain same. Traceability of process models can be identified through cross examination of the connections between the pre -and post-conditions of specific process models. Process mode l will be ready for execution when some specific pre-and post-condition is satisfied. (i.e. a customer registers a claim) if this condition is true then (the customer claim can be processed). Pre -and post - conditions of a process model can be associated to the pre -and post -constraints for specific organizational goals. Michael Becker et al [15] also suggested structural variations according to which an original process can be redrawn into different process model variants with respect to structural variations. Among all variants, however in (variant B) at first traces of the original model are drawn then model is re-drawn by adding connector in the existing gateway. Barbara Weber at el [16] and Michael Becker at el [15] emphasized on the addition of gateways but it has some variations. The Type -1 variation is rooted from these tw o structural variations referenced under [15] [16]. In Type -1 variation, we do the re -designing of a model by parallel execution of the activities within a gateway that were in a sequence in the Original model. P a g e  | 30 Parallel activities will only be executed when strict bounding doesn’t exist between the activities. Structure Variation Type-1 Change: Addition of Gateways Explanation: Process fragments/activities which have been confined to be executed in sequence so far are parallelized in a process schema. Illustration: In the ACME INC process model, when employee sends overtime registration to manager he then evaluates for approval or rejection of request by executing activities which are in a sequence within gateway, in parallel. Rooted from: AP9 [16], variant B[15]. Rules for implementation: 1) First step is to draw all execution traces of the original model. 2) Common Activities to be drawn both before and after the gateway among traces while not considering any of the gateway. 3) Join activities with the gateway. 4) Execute activities that are in sequence within the gateway in parallel by deploying AND Gateway. 5) Amongst the number of traces, draw the longest trace till the end of a process model by carefully following steps (2) & (3). 6) Attach remaining traces using step (4), while drawing traces by following steps (2) & (3). For connection XOR gateway is used. 7) Every single trace performs independent operation. 8) Parallel activities can only be executed if strict bounding doesn’t exist in between the activities. The utmost reason is because traces drawn do not take into account the AND gateway.

heading: 3.1.2 Type 2
content: The second structural variation which we denote as “Type-2” mainly deals with when an activity or activities can both be Inserted and Deleted in the process model that will eventually bring changes to the structure of a model. The Activity can be added as well as removed by evaluating the description of the original model such that the semantics of original model stay the same. This very change can possibly be achieved by inserting or deleting of activity. The activity X or whatever activity that we intend to insert can be added anywhere in the model. It can be deployed at any place in our process model without any restriction.  There is no particular rule as to which activity needs to be deleted  or inserted . It can be removed or P a g e  | 33 inserted at  any place in our process model without any restriction as the main concern is changing the structure of a model. Structural difference proposed by [15] [ 16]. Barbara Weber at el. [16], structural differences can be observed through adaption patterns. In adaption pattern [AP1] and [AP2] activity or activities can be added to a process model and can be deleted too. In other study Michael Becker at el [15]  suggested that a process model can be redrawn into different structural variants. One of these structural variations includes addition of activities into a process model. The proposed Type-2 Variation is rooted from adaption patterns [AP1], [AP2] and (variation D) [15] [16] and has its own set of rules for addition & deletion of activity from a model. The Type -2 variation re -designs a model in order to generate its structural variants based on proposed set of rules. In the Type -2 variation activities can be inserted and as well as removed but by entirely understanding the description of original model in order for the semantics to stay the same even if the structure is different w.r.t. original process model. Structure Variation Type-2 Change: Addition or Deletion of Activity/Activities Explanation: Activity is added to or deleted from a variant of an original model. Illustration: Before creating Overtime Registration, the Employee now needs to Fill the Overtime Registration form first and then send it to Manager. Rooted from: AP1, AP2 [16] variant D[15]. Rules for implementation: 1) Activity can be added or deleted anywhere in the process model. 2) One or more activities can be added or deleted. 3) Addition or Deletion of an activity doesn’t change the semantics of a model. 4) Addition or Deletion of activities will only be performed if strict bounding doesn’t exist between process models.

heading: 3.1.3 Type 3
content: Type 3 change tells us about inserting a control edge/control flow anywhere in the process model. In process models, edges are present between the  activities and are present at the gateways. In this type 3 we have added an edge between the gateways which make process model structurally different. In process models, control flow is used in explaining the sequence of activities. Vertices are defined by {V} and edges are defined by {E}. Process models consist of multiple types of Control flows. Study [ 15] shows that there are four types of control flows which are helpful in defining the behavioral semantics differently. These are Parallel structure (AND ), loop structure, choice (XOR) and sequential structure. First, we consider the sequential structure activity which is only be completed if its previous activity has finished its execution. In choice structure, after the execution of the activity person h as a choice to exclusively execute any one from the two succeeding activities, not allowing both two activities to execute. Parallel structure allows you to execute the succeeding activities in parallel. All these types of control flows help to produce a difference in structure of a process model. Change primitives becomes the basis for the structural differences recognition. Change primitives includes inserting edge, removing edge and shifting the edges in a process model. Process model correctness can be verified by the suitable change primitive. Studies [ 15] [16 ] P a g e  | 35 introduced the variation in structure which helps in modifying the flow of the model so that it deals with the changes at runtime against the user requirement. In Barbara at el [ 16], AP11 AND AP1 2 Adaption patterns allows to insert or delete the control edge in the process model. In adaption pattern 11 when the edge is inserted, confirm that the extra control dependencies do not affect the accuracy and semantics of the process model should not be changed. According to the adaption pattern 12, control dependency may be deleted from a model without effecting the semantics of process model. Michael Becker at el. [ 15] explained in his variant E and variant F that the control flow can be changed in process models. According to the variant E, edge is inserted between the gateways block. According to the variant F of Michael Becker we change the flow of the activities by transforming activities in a sequential flow. Moreover, inserting and deleting of a co ntrol edge should not change the semantics of the original model. Change Type 3: Model with modified control flow Explanation: Control edge is inserted between the gateway of process model and can also be deleted from anywhere AP12[16]. Illustration: In the ACME INC process model, when manager evaluate overtime registration to approve or decline request, then we add control edge between gateway. Rooted from: AP11,AP12 [16], variant C, E,F [15]. Rules for implementation: 1) Conditions are satisfied in a process model if single primitive change is applied. 2) Activities Pre -and post -conditions are verified in a pro cess model. 3) Control edge can be inserted within gateway control block in order to add further condition. (Variant E, AP11). 4) Control dependency can be deleted in process models (F, AP12). 5) We must assure that conditions must be fulfilled after implementing this change of type 3. 6) We only insert an edge if the bounding between the process models is not strict.

heading: 4.2.1 Tool Introduction
content: As a part of our project we must develop a program which will calculate the metrics that we have discussed in the previous topic and also have described a way and their respective formula to evaluate them. We have been given 900 process models in the form an XML files that were generated by CAMUNDA modeler. Camunda Modeler is a desktop application for modeling BPMN workflows, CMMN cases and DMN decisions. It is very easy to use, which means that business analysts can use it as well as developers, working on the same diagrams.  Besides the visual modeling, Camunda Modeler also allows you to edit all properties that are necessary for the technical execution. Since Camunda Modeler works directly on the BPMN, CMMN and DMN XML files, developers can easily combine it with their prefer red IDE. Camunda Modeler leverages bpmn.io, which is probably the most awesome modeling framework in the known universe. P a g e  | 48

heading: 4.2.2 Understanding of the XML code
content: XML language uses different tags to store different type of data. In our case, there are also special tags that are used to represent the data from the process model in the XML file. The process name is given under the hierarchy of tags -> definitions/collaboration/participant and found under the variable called name. The lanes are given under the hierarchy of tags  -> definitions/process/laneSet/lane and found under the variable called name. it is stored with a unique ID as well that is used for mapping. The ID is available under the sane hierarchy but available under the variable id. To map the lanes and nodes ther e are special tags used -> definitions/process/laneSet/lane/ flowNodeRef. This tag maps the lane ids to the node ids that are present in the code. Start Event is given under the tag of -> definitions/process/startEvent and is accessed with its id which we will use it to differentiate it from other events. End Event is given under the tag of -> definitions/process/endEvent and is accessed with its id which we will use it to differentiate it from other events. Tasks are available under this tag -> definitions/process/task with a unique id and the value that its named for stored in a variable name. Exclusive Gateways are available under the tag -> definitions/process/exclusiveGateway with a unique id only. Parallel Gateways are available under the tag -> definitions/process/parallelGateway with a unique id only. The edges are available under the tag -> definitions/process/sequenceFlow/@targetRef , which represents the target node and under a tag -> definitions/process/sequenceFlow/@sourceRef , which represents the source node. P a g e  | 49

heading: 4.2.3 Data Extraction from XML Code
content: For storing the metrics, the protected variables will be used as they are easily accessible in the same package. For Data Storage HashMaps are used which are efficient and easy to use in our case where we have to deal with the keys of events, tasks and gateways. They will also be used for lanes, and mapping among the lanes and nodes. To Save the sequences that joins the nodes or that marks the flow of information we will use an array because it contains 4 variables. The data of each sequence will be stored twice marked as incoming and outgoing in reference to the two nodes it is connecting. The first variable is used to store Source/target depending on the incoming or outgoing node, the second for  marking it as Incoming or Outgoing, the third for sequence id and the fourth one for Source/Target node. This information is stored in the same sequence in the array. An extra variable will also be used to store the size of the array along with the array. P a g e  | 50 To render the XML Files, we will import special classes from the JAVA library that will help us extract the data from the xml files. Javax.xml.xpath and javax.xml.parsers will be used along with some of their inner classes. Given a file path from th e procedure mentioned earlier the object of these classes will be constructed. The path variable has the location the files that was passed onto this class. DocumentBuilderFactory and DocumentBuilder are used to create the Xpath variable that is used to render the xml files. Then the newly created variable of doc and Xpath are passed onto the Extractdata method. The Extractdata method uses the tags mentioned earlier and the variables it is being passed on to extract the data from the xml files and store them in the respective variables that are assigned for the type of data it is extracting.

heading: 4.3.1 Structural Similarity
content: The business process models we are using are in BPMN, which includes these properties (Lanes, Labels and Node Type ). In order to calculate the structural similarity, we will use all these 3 properties. Structural similarity is calculated on the values of  Node Insertion/Deletion (SN) , Node Substitution (SB)  and Edge Insertion/Deletion (SE) . Using these values, we can calculate the Graph-Edit distance similarity of the process model. Node Insertion/Deletion will be decided upon the name of the lanes and the node types, which will be when the nodes are mapped between two process models, i.e. Ta sk will be mapped on Task and Gateway will be mapped on the Gateway without considering their respected labels. Node Substitution will be calculated using the Syntactic Similarity (String Edit Distance). String Edit Distance is the number of atomic string operations necessary to get from one string to another. Includes removing, adding and substituting the character.  Node Substitution will only be calculated between the mapped nodes, which have the same lane and node type. In our case it will be applied onl y to the tasks as they have the labels.  Edge deletion/Insertion will be calculated only when two nodes are mapped between two process models and they are connected to each other with an edge and there is a same edge available in the other process model connecting the same nodes.  For each node deleted/inserted and edge deleted/inserted P a g e  | 65 a value of 1 is incremented in SN and SE respectively.  If all these three properties are a perfect match between two process models then no operation will be done as all these  will produce a value of zero which doesn’t affect the final result.  If no lanes are mapped between the two process models then all the nodes and edges are inserted/deleted. Using the SN, SE and SB we can calculate the snv, sev and sbv as shown in the for mulas below. Then using snv, sev and sbv we can calculate the similarity between any two process models by calculating the average of these values and subtracting it from 1. This value will be between 0 and 1, 0 being dissimilar and 1 being the exact similar to each other. If SNV and SEV is equal to one then we will automatically set the SBV to one to make the value go to zero as no nodes or edges are mapped between the two process models to avoid the division by zero.

Using the data about lan es we will map the lanes based on their names. The lanes with same names will be mapped. Once lanes are mapped we will check for nodes in the mapped lanes and map those nodes between the two process models. Based on the mapped nodes we will calculate the similarity. Unmapped nodes will represent the SN. Unmapped edges will represent the SE. Mapped nodes with different labels with their String Edit distance value will represent the SB. heading: Abstract
content: Used mobile phone market has a big share in the telecom industry. People with a moderate budget, basically everyone prefers to look for some used phone in the nearest market as the brand new ones doesn’t differ convincingly from them in terms of condition and use. We analysed that this is very difficult and teasing job for the buyer to visit different shops in search of a good mobile within his budget. There is a huge chance of forgery in mobile phones and it is very hard to spot a difference between the new and frogged versions if you are technology impaired. So there is an immense need to coupe with this problem of the buyers. Hence our idea is to provide a trustworthy platform to the buyers which will help them get the best product against their money without leaving their couch. This website is very user friendly and efficient for every kind of buyer (men, women, teens, old and handicapped). They can easily look for a good conditioned use phone on this website and then can directly call or can get directions to visit the buyer using (map view). On the other hand there are large number of shopkeepers who have the best products and deals but are unable to convert it in profit due to lack of accessibility and marketing. Vendors find it difficult to promote their deals online as social media platforms are not good enough to gain customer’s trust. Buyers do not trust the authentication of such  social media groups and  pages. In order to tackle this issue we put forward an idea of an interactive platform for the vendors where they will meet new buyers everyday resulting in convincing increase in sales. Vendors can put amazing deals online to attract large number of buyers.

heading: 1.1 Introduction:
content: Online shopping is an emerging business in the world. People have adopted the new system of finding good deals straight from their home. The traditional system had many drawbacks in it. M any of those problems are efficiently tackled by modern day websites and apps. Finding a used mobile/accessories/tablet online is very convenient for the customers. Some platforms have provided users with the facility to make deals online but they have many drawbacks and limitations. People do not trust their principals of dealing online as the probability of fraud is very high. Similarly the vendors find it difficult to promote their new deals through social media pages as people these days do not trust the authentication of such pages. In order to bring back customer’s tru st we have devised a new way of authentication to avoid possible scams and frauds. We will provide users (sellers) with the facility for B2C to open their online shop on our platform. The purpose of this is to take the pain of promotion from the vendor. So  now we will promote their latest deals online and bring them potential buyers through our website. This websites and App basically unites the buyers and the sellers from the nearest local markets. A vendor from a nearby plaza opens a virtual shop online a nd posts all of the available phone with eye catchy deals. The buyer using the website can now look for all options in used mobile category straight from its couch. Now the buyer don’t have the need to physically visit shop by shop, which is an arduous tas k. When the phone is selected then the buyer can get locations from map view and can quickly get to the vendor and can purchase the phone. This one to one interaction of the buyer and the vendor at the end will increase security and trust. No chance of forgery or scam. Simply pick the right phone and then visit the vendor and collect it. There is no shipment and payment system initially in Lahore but as per our future plans we will launch a trustworthy payment system (In this system when the deal will be finalized we (admin) will keep the money from the buyer for 7 days as check warranty then we will release it to the vendor. Just like fiver!!). The registration system on the website is very simple but authentic. Every Seller / Buyer ( vendor or individual) will provide its credentials. Similarly the customers (buyer) will also have their registration mechanism which will also be properly verified and authenticated via sms verification. In start the registration would be free of cost but we have a plan to charge later. The registered user will be facilitated with the news feed of latest trends and upcoming gadgets. We are in search of business so when user comes to our site user are looking for something, and if we put ads related to user’s search we’re going to get a very high click-through rate. On the internet, search business models can work if you have intent, and when user comes to catchmob user have intent in the right product. The combination of having intent plus being in value-laden deals leads to high CPM”

content: The iterative model  (waterfall) is the most feasible one for both developers and Supervisor. User requirements are recorded as stories that can be revised at any time  later in the development process. Prototypes of software are released and then more requirements gathered to enhance the  next release. This model highlights the successive procedure of the diverse periods of advancement while likewise attempting to amplif y the advantages of permitting changes, upgrades, and augmentations to be made between every addition. After gathering all the requirements and interviewing the stakeholder we had finalized the requirements but do not have a right image of this platform in our mind. Appling the iterative waterfall model is the best choice for us. We gathered the requirements and ranked the importance of functionalities to be added and what are the most important ones. So the release are designed such that to bring the impo rtant ones first so that stakeholders can give the feedback.

heading: Abstract
content: Overweight and obesity are significant public health problems worldwide with serious health consequences. With increasing urbanization and modernization there has been an increase in prevalence of obesity  that is attributed to reduced levels of physical activity.  Globally, around 23% of adults aged 18 and over were not active enough in 2015 (men 20% and women 27%). In high -income countries, 26% of men and 35% of women were insufficiently physically active, as compared to 12% of men and 24% of women in low-income countries. Insufficient physical activity is a key risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as cardiovascular diseases, cancer and diabetes. Globally, 1 in 4 adults is not active enough . Doing gym on routine basis enforces you to eat clean and avoid fast food, smoking etc. You feel much more fit, become much more enthusiast about your daily activities and starts to live life more.  Our Gym Management System  incorporates as an intermediary between gym member, trainer and gym Management. Therefore, it becomes easier for everyone to interact with each other. Even when there is a slight change in the records, we  need to updat e each and every excel file. Our s mart Gym Management System eradicates most o f the restrictions of the existing system. These Apps are  designed to assist the user i n pursuing a healthy lifestyle by encouraging them to perform  positive activities, and improve lifestyle choices. Factors that are typically targeted by such  applications include exercise, workout , and diet. Applications like this have the potential to motivate its users into maintaining a cycle of positive lifestyle decisions and breaking a cycle of negative lifestyle decisions. Our proposed gym Management System  is for gym owner s that can handle members, employees,  gym staff, products, expense, income of  gym & all transactions that occur in Gym. Secondly, our system benefits gym members by providing an app that help them to record their workout, add their body measurements and view nutrition & workout routines . content: This chapter introduces and summarizes the related works a nd similar systems to the project by describing and explaining the problems of these systems, also comparing between systems functionalities and its advantages and disadvantages and the choice of technology for our project.

heading: 2.1.1. Effect of Exercise on Mood
content: Studies have shown the positive effects that increased exercise can have on a person’s overall mood, and it has been widely recommended that people suffering from a history of mental disorders such as depression and anxiety incorporate more exercise into their daily routines. There are several theorized reasons for  this correlation between an increase in daily exercise and an improved state of mind. The first is the idea of distraction. A person placing his or her focus on exercise rather than the stressful or anxiety-inducing aspects of life, are more likely to temporarily forget  about these depressants and have an improved state of mind. Another possible side  effect of continuous daily exercise is a general improvement of a person’s self -image due to becoming more physically fit, and healthier overall. Exercise can lead to an  increase in self -esteem, and physical acceptance. In general, there is a direct correlation between a person’s self -esteem and their overall happiness. Finally, when a person exercises, they are constantly  overcoming obstacles and improving themselves. heading: 2.9.1 Prototyping Model
content: The Prototyping Model is a software development cycle model  in which a prototype is built, tested, and then reworked as necessary until an acceptable prototype is finally achieved from which the complete system or product can now be developed. This model wo rks best in scenarios  where project requirements are not well defined. An iterative, trial-and-error process takes place between the developers and the users. The first reason for a model is to enable clients of the product to assess engineer's proposition for the outline of the possible item by really giving them a shot, as opposed to interpreting and assess the plan in view of depictions. Prototyping can likewise be utilized by end clients to portray and demonstrate prerequisites that engineers have not considered, and that can be a key factor in the business connection amongst designers and their customers. This case of model is helpful within the case once necessities don't seem to be represented at first. T his model is developed supporting  the presently far - famed necessities. Development of the model clearly undergoes style, coding, and testing, however every of those phases is n't done terribly forma lly or totally. By applyling this model, the client will get an actual feel of the system, as a result of the interactions with the model will modify the client to higher perceive the wants of the required system.

heading: 2.9.1.1 Advantages of Prototype
content: 1- Provides a working model to the user early in the process, enabling early assessment and increasing user's confidence. 2- The developer gains experience and insight by developing a prototype there by resulting in better implementation of requirements. 3- The prototyping model serves to clarify requirements, which are not clear, hence reducing ambiguity and improving communication between the developers and users.

heading: PAGE 45
content: 4- There is a great involvement of users in software development. Hence, the requirements of the users are met to the greatest extent. 5- Helps in reducing risks associated with the software.

heading: 1. Requirements Gathering phase
content: A prototyping  model starts with necessities examination and the prerequisites of the framework are characterized in detail. The client is met keeping in mind the end goal to know the necessities of the framework.  The user is interviewed in order to know the requirements of the system.

heading: 2. Quick Design phase
content: At the point when prerequisites are known, a preparatory outline or fast plan for the framework is made. It's anything but a point by point plan and incorporates just the imperative parts of the framework, which giv es a thought of the framework to the client. A snappy outline helps in building up the model. Assemble model stage Information accumulated from fast plan is changed to shape the main model, which speaks to the working model of the required framework.

heading: 3. User evaluation phase
content: Next, the proposed framework is displayed to the client for exhaustive assessment of the model to perceive its qualities and shortcomings, for example, what is to be included or expelled. Remarks and proposals are gathered from the clients and gave to the designer.

heading: 4. Refining prototype phase
content: Once the client assesses the model and in the event that he isn't fulfilled, the present model is refined by the necessities. That is, another model is created with the extra data gave by the client. The new model is assessed simply like the past model. This procedure proceeds until the point that every one of the prerequisites indicated by the client are met. Once the client is happy with the created model, a last framework is produced based on the last model.

heading: 5. Design
content: In the design phase , the interface architect formally characterizes the application and re checks to guarantee all bases are secured, we consider every one of the parameters fundamental for building a fruitful application including plan ideas, usefulness and course of events.

heading: 6. Implementation
content: Application development phase begins with designing the user Interface (UI) and then coding it in minimum time. The prototypes of the application are subject to client approval on a regular basis. Server component must be involved, in parallel engage resources to improve development efficiency. As quality assurance is a critical factor, we deploy several techniques from code level to usability.

heading: 7. Testing
content: Throughout the whole development ph ase, the project team follows testing process to check AMAHF application's functionality. They keep in touch with the client during development phase to ease the monitoring of the project. They have to healthy competition amongst the other terms which stri ves to achieve quality beyond client requirements.

heading: 8. Maintenance
content: After the customers and end clients endorse the final product, it is completely put into task. The most important factor of this stage is the upkeep procedure to guarantee the product keeps running without blunders. What's more, we will consider having overhauls and extra component onto programming. While there are such a significant number of variable along the product advancement life cycle, it is, the support stage that guarantees the product keeps running on new working frameworks. Much the same as in other life cycles, software programs get to their last stage where they are redesignd in for more up to date items.

heading: Abstract
content: The current generation of search has been around since the early days of google and prior. The current generation of a product tend to lend itself to incremental improvement where we lack on features and move the needle by small amount. Existing search engines are open ended and provide historical usefulness. Conversational search is next generation of search. The user interaction of searching on internet will going to be more conversational. This conversation starts with questioning answering related to search. The user interacts by entering a keyword. This generates the list of response questions determining what the user actually wants. When people search for something, the conversational search finds 10 relevant results and also find summary of these results on each question until their satisfaction. To do so requires a new method of building the database. This new generation search attempts to remove the uncertainty of meaning from ambiguous terms used during search questions. Table of Contents

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: In today’s word, the vast source of information for everybody is internet. Important information is being added frequently in the internet in the form of websites. In the present age, Search Engines (SE) are the most important tools for the retrieval of in formation. There is huge volume of documents which are available on web servers and publicly accessible through Search Engines (SE). Internet users largely rely upon the results that are offered by Search Engines (SE). With the exponential increase of use of Search Engines, the number of information and documents are being put thrice on the web servers. Due to this the users have to write long sentences or phrases in the search bar to get closer to their answers. Now a days, there is great boom of Search En gine Optimization (SEO). Search Engines (SE) like, Google, used the algorithm of page ranking. The website developers try to design their website in the way that their websites appear on the first page of google. The fact is no one visit the second page of google. It may also because of shortage of time or might be the trust on the search engines (SE). Very often users do not get their answers right. For this reason they have to rephrase their sentences again and again. These Search Engines are not the contextual based. The current generation of search has been around us for a long period. It is obvious that a word can have many different meanings. People searching keyword might have different meanings and might not fi nd the top 10 items useful the Search Engine (SE) provides. Search Engines are like top 10 lists, not databases. For example, type cat into google.com, the first page is Wikipedia page for cat, the second page is reference to caterpillar the heavy equipment manufacturer company. The next is also a reference to Caterpillar Company. We are also served with photos. It becomes obvious that cat can means different things and that people searching cat might not find the first 10 items the search engines returns as useful. Searching for something on go ogle provides nothing useful. It provides average usefulness. Existing search engines are open ended and provides historical usefulness. Millions of people have found these pages useful, mix together a musical, with photos, with a Wikipe dia article and we get SEO gone bad. This promotes convergence to useful posts and limits users to only what millions of people

heading: 10 of 46  14 May 2018
content: have already found.  The preferences of users are changing now. They want their Search Engines (SE) should behave like Personal Digital Assistants (PDA) like Amazon’s Alexa, Microsoft’s Cortana and Apple’s Siri. Our approach is Conversational Search Engine which is also a keyword based search.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The goal is to build an engine that works more like a layman’s database where you whittle down millions of pages to just a handful that relates to what someone is looking for. With this, we can also disambiguate the meaning of words that are ambiguous, by utilizing other words on the page. With this, we can build a list of appropriate questions to whittle down in a conversational form until we just get the 5-10 results that a search user wants to know. This will allow people to find any of the pages (or in general, files) available in the index.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: People searching keyword might have different meanings and might not find the top 10 items useful the search engine provides. They have to write very long statements or sentences. No one goes to the second page of google. The solution is conversational search based on a keyword. The conversational search finds 10 relevant results and also find summary of these results on each question until their satisfaction.

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: The existing work to our project is google conversational search. But that search is search by voice and questions initiate by user. For example, a person asked question what is circle. Google reply him back and save in its memory the word circle. Now again if person asked what is its radius. Google reply back to him. Now the word ‘its’ used here which refers to the word ‘radius’ and conversation about radius continues until user close the browser. Our conversational search is search by text. The specialty of our conversational search is that it is keyword based search and one can continue the conversation by answering to questions which are generated by our application until the satisfaction of user and that has not been done by any search engine. heading: 4.3 Generation of Questions
content: We have created a knowledgebase for this purpose. The knowledgebase contains the words and against that words, we have populated phrases in it. Our knowledgebase contains 540 million results. These phrases are results on the basis of summary we have generated. On every search, the keyword and the related phrases on the basis of summary passed to knowledgebase. We took these phrases from the suggestions page of Google.  We have populated 450 thousand keywords in the knowled gebase. Upon every search, 10 phrases are generated. Against every single keyword, 1120 phrases generated. We combined all the alphabets, numbers and helping verbs as a prefix and suffix one by one as shown in figure 6. User will search a keyword through search bar. Let name this keyword k1. The phrases which we have stored in knowledgebase, let we named them k2. When user will search a keyword, which we named as k1, it will pass to web service and at the same time it will pass to knowledgebase. The web service will crawl the URLs from the google and will be displayed to user interface.

heading: 7.2 Project Summary
content: Our Project is Conversational Search Engine. This is the solution to current search engines. Today’s search engines are only top 10 results, not databases. Our search engine will be more like a layman’s database where you whittle down millions of pages to just a handful that relates to what someone is looking for. With this, we can also disambiguate the meaning of words that are ambiguous, by utilizing other words on the page. With this, we can build a list of appropriate questions to whittle down in a conversational form until we just get the 5 -10 results that a search user wants to know. This will allow people to find any of the pages (or in general, files) available in the index. It take the user interaction of searching something on internet and make it much more conve rsational. When people search for something, the conversational search finds 10 relevant results and also find summary of these results on each question until their satisfaction. The innovation is a conversational refinement tool. For example, you ask CAT, it will return 10 results with 5 follow up questions like do you want biological information, ownership information, products, images, videos or something else. Word based searching throws 5 different things into a single bucket.

heading: Abstract
content: The continuous process of Learning ends with life. The traditional way of learning is book reading. Books are the major source of learning. But book reading become-time consuming and hundreds of pages are require to explain a piece of concept in a conceptual course like computer programing. Therefore it’s a very difficult to understand a course consist of multiple other courses like Web development. Beside this lectures are good source to understand conceptual course in less time than book reading. This project aim to give platform to learn course online. There are many website that are providing the same services like Udemy, Coursera and edx but most of these websites do not provide live session and chatting. Some of them provide live session also like udacity. This project is marketplace for tutors where they can create their gig about particular topic they can teach or projects they can do. This feature distinguish this product from other related websites like udacity. It also produce a strong sense of community among students within online courses is essential to supporting their learning experience (Carrie Demmans Epp, 2017).

heading: 1.1 Introduction

The first and the most is the gap between the tutor and student. They do not have live course session, which creates the gap. Student can ask question on chat but there is high chanc e that they do not get their answer instantly. Here comes ELEARN to remove this gap through live courses and live question answer session. ELEARN is the great place for tutors to share their knowledge and expertise with others and get offers from the seeke rs. This is also great place for learners as it provides experts and best tutors around the world in their field and ready to answer and any questions and give lecture on any topic. Users can enroll in the full live course sessions. Live question answer se ssion with tutors. All these features makes our web application unique from others. Tutors have many options to make their revenue. They can get offers form the learner to get lecture for particular topic. They can create full course and schedule the dat e and time of the live course. Time and date will be notified to the followers. Learners can search for the courses, tutors and the gigs. They can also like the tutor to get notified when new gig is created by the tutor. They can enrolled in the courses. There will be live question answer session in the every course so learner can ask questions and get satisfied answers.

heading: 2.6 Software Development Life Cycle
content: The software development life cycle which we used in our project is the RAD (rapid application development) is a concept that was born out of frustration with the waterfall software design approach which too often resulted in products that were out of date  or inefficient by the time they were actually released) and  Waterfall Model (Waterfall Model is a sequential model that divides software development into different phases). Following are the reasons why we used this model:  We used Rapid Application Devel opment RAD model for clear requirement gathering from users.  We used waterfall model because as this model is very simple and easy to understand and use. As it is suitable for small projects where requirements are clear and well understood. So, it’s the best option for our application to develop under waterfall model, because the requirements of our application are clear and fixed, so there are no risk of changing requirements.  The amount of resources required to implement under waterfall model is minimal.  Moreover, it is easy to manage due to the rigidity of the model – each phase has specific deliverables and a review process.  It is helpful where quality is more preferred than cost and schedule.

heading: Abstract
content: As technology is improving and is being adapted in almost every field. Maintaining account records manually is time taking so everyone is moving towards web applications that allows access to maintain records effortlessly. Our project also involves the dev elopment of a Web based software application that will allow Jinnah Polytechnic College to maintain their account records in an easy yet manageable way. This application will inherit all the properties of computerizing an accounting system which includes l ess processing time, reliability and fast recovery. Time is the most important factor that should be saved to improve the lifestyle. Website is a basic need of business. Website can be used to accomplish different marketing strategies to help a business grow and specifying significant information about business for user ease . The project we are developing is a real time project which refers to the development of  comprehensive website of Jinnah Polytechnic College that will provide a solution to market their  business and will provide the user an ease to access all necessary information about the college. Furthermore website will include a portal where student can get access to examination results and fee status. v | P a g e Table of Contents

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: There is a need of every educational institute to have a website where necessary information about the institute can be specified. Besides website allows a business to grow more quickly as it helps in marketing. Because of refinements in technology manual maintenance of account records is depreciating. Our project will provide solution to these problems. We are developing a real time project for an educational institute named Jinnah Polytechnic Institute, Lahore. Project includes the development of an accou nts management application and an informative website of Jinnah Poly Technic Institute, Lahore. Our project is divided into two modules. • In the first module we will develop a website which is further sub divided into three sub modules, first sub module includes designing of basic web pages that comprise of related information about college  i.e. Admission Details, Fees Structures, Contact Details, Offered Diplomas, Faculty Information etc. Secondly, we will make a portal for Administrator where admin can u pload Internal Examination Marks and Fee status of students, and ultimately we will make a Student portal from where students can check their examination result and fee status by providing a valid registration number. • Our second module  is developing a Web  Application for managing accounts which is further sub divided into two sub modules. First module is Income and second is Expense. Income has following attributes: Monthly Tuition Fees of Students, Prospectus Fees, Promotion Fees Annually, Test Session Fe es, Returns in form of checks/cash and any other income that is not listed. Expense has following attributes: Utility Bills, Miscellaneous Expenses, Repair and Maintenance Expenses, Printing and Stationary Expenses, staff salaries and any other expense tha t is not listed. At the end of month a balance sheet will be prepared which will include every detail including income and expenses for that month. Accounts manager will also be able to view details of any category individually. If expenses of some month  will be more than the income, then the remaining expenses of that month will be added to next month’s balance sheet as an expense and if income will be more than expense then that amount will be added as cash in hand in the next month balance sheet. Accoun t records will be saved in a secure database and can be recovered anytime.

heading: 2.1.1 SAP (System, Application & Product)
content: SAP [1] accounting software is designed to streamline the collection and consolidation of accounting data, accelerate the financial close process, assist in regulatory reporting and create high-quality financial statements in accordance with necessary financial reporting standards. It has special functions to handle areas with more complicated accountin g needs, like real estate management, and to simplify expense reimbursement work. It also assists the accounting and finance department with everyday tasks, such as managing invoices and accounts receivable and performing financial analysis and planning.

heading: SAP [2]:
content: • Records all your financial processes into a general ledger • Get complete financial accounting by integrating assets, payables and receivables • Use powerful management accounting tools for orders, projects and profit centres

heading: 2.1.2 YENDO
content: Yendo [3] is a very new type of online CRM and Accounting software for small businesses. One can create his own management accounts with ease, giving you a perfect picture of your company's monthly performance. Yendo [4] is most suitable for the financial and CRM needs of small businesses. The software offers a variety of features specifically tailored for the needs of small business ventures. The software has been deployed in education, finance, media, and technology industries.

heading: 4 | P a g e
content: The software [5]offers sufficient accounting, CRM and payment features to meet the needs of any small business, regardless of the industry. The accounting module offers the management of invoicing, purchasing, expenses and payments. You a lways have the facility of creating profit and loss reports as well as balance sheets.  The CRM module of the software takes care of sales pipeline and customer management. This module also offers accounting and social media integration. For payments manage ment, the software offers you the facility of taking the customer payments without any need of merchant account. Credit card integration and processing is also provided. Some other important accounting and management features of the software that you can benefit from include accounts payable and receivable, bank reconciliation, cash and collections management, expense tracking, financial analysis, and general ledger.

heading: 2.1.3 KASHOO
content: Kashoo [6] transforms how small businesses manage their  finances. Kashoo is a powerful and affordable online accounting solution designed specifically for small business. With no accounting experience, the business owner can quickly and efficiently manage accounts and move on to running the business. Financial goals are met and disasters are avoided via Kashoo.

heading: 2.1.4 Less Accounting
content: Less everything was a successful web firm for several years. In the beginning, they struggled with accounting, because accounting was boring and difficult to handle. In short nobody lik es accounting. So, they created Less Accounting  [7]. Over time they expanded the app to include online invoicing, client proposals, mileage tracking, everything about Less Accounting is very simple and easy to use. You can track all of your business expenses with Less Accounting [8], quickly. You can put your expenses into categories, income into categories and make a balance sheet faster.

heading: 2.6 Software Development life cycle model
content: We are using an evolutionary model that is Incremental Model for our project because we need increments at every stage if changes are required then we will make the desired changes and g o to the next step. The advantage of this model is if we need to make any change it can be done at any stage and resume our work from the stage where we left for the increments and it can be repeated many times to improve and enhance our system. Incrementa l model works for our project greatly. We as a team worked by focussing on one functionality and test it before moving to another functionality. In this project development we were supposed to present the work done to the customer and review his feedback o r any changes that were needed to complete this functionality. It includes four steps:

heading: Abstract
content: Pakistan is a beautiful country. Anyone can fall in love with the beautiful natural sites in northern areas of Pakistan. Due to this reason tourism is a growing industry in Pakistan as there are many heavenly places. In 2017 there were over 1,750,000[1] to urist visitors, which shows a huge rate of interest of tourists to visit beautiful places present in Pakistan. However, tourists arrange most of the trips by themselves. There is lack of platforms that can help tourists to find suitable tourism companies t hat can turn tourists experience more enjoyable. Some tourism companies are operating by using just Facebook. The aim of our project is to provide a platform for both tourists and tourism companies so that they can interact with each other in arranging trips. More specifically, the purpose of this shared and collaborative platform with synchronized web interfaces is to help tour guiding companies to offer packages and services to tourists. Moreover, the application will also provide people to easily interac t with guiding companies and make deals about their own tours or join with already available tours. We hope that with the usage of this application, tourism of our country will flourish further.

heading: 1.1 INTRODUCTION
content: With the stability in law and order in Pakistan, we have witnessed an increase in tourism in Northern areas of Pakistan. Even foreigners from other countries are coming in good numbers to visit beautiful places present in Pakistan. Our country  is enriched with natural beauty. It includes places like Swat, Narran, Kagan and many more. Even Kashmir is said to be a part of Heaven on Earth which is also present in our country. Right now tourist from other countries and even the residents of our cou ntry faces the problem of finding a good guide for their tourism desires. Moreover, people nowadays face lack of trusts on guides for their bad behavior in past and they do not know beautiful places hidden on the sacred map of Pakistan. They only know and mostly visit that two or three places, again and again, every year. To overcome this complexity, people need an online forum that will work as a bridge between clients and companies. Our goal is to provide a platform for people to find new places present in our beautiful country and to provide a trusted platform for guides to promote tourism for both foreigners and the people of our country. The uniqueness of our project is that it will act as a bridge between clients (tourist) and companies which are willing to take people on trips to different places of Pakistan. In Pakistan right now companies are only working on social platforms like Facebook, Instagram etc. Our goal is to provide them with a platform which will be much easier for both the company and t he client to be easier access at a single platform. The companies will register and upgrade details of their trips with their cost. The client will get information about the trips by visiting our online platform. They will contact that company through our platform. By this, our platform will act as a middleman between client and companies. This will surely promote tourism by making it easier for tourists to easily access companies to guide them to the hidden places in Pakistan. On social media platforms, it is really difficult for people to find trips of their interest. To do so they have to visit different sites. This is a total wastage of time. Our goal is to minimize people effort by gathering companies on a single platform. This will surely save people e ffort. They only have to visit our online platform to get any information about tours of their interest. The client will contact the company through our platform and will hire a guide and will pay in return for their guiding services. By this, the company will generate profit and will pay us for our services for acting as a bridge and for promoting there company and tourism on our platform. Moreover the clients can generate their own events. The companies will contact the user and can bid on that event. The  user will respond to that bidding and will select the company of his/her own choice.

heading: 1.2 OBJECTIVES
content: The goals and objectives of our project are listed below:-  Our goal is to provide a platform to companies providing them with an online application which will act as a bridge between clients and companies.  To build a time-saving web application for people so they do not have to waste searching for a trusted company.  To make it easier for tourists to develop and search for their particular trip.  To provide a good and user -friendly interface which will be easy to use as compared to the standard websites available on the internet.  To provide a good and user -friendly website with standard interface in comparison with other websites.

heading: 1.3 PROBLEM STATEMENT
content: Tourism is one of the growing industry in Pakistan. For this growing business there are many companies which are providing guiding services to tourist and earning money but all these companies are working on their own without any collaboration. People lack trust on these companies and question their credibility as many companie s are unauthorized . So the goal of this project is to provide a trust worthy platform on which people can select the company of their choice to assist them on their tours according to the best bid and accommodations being offered.

heading: 1.4 ASSUMPTIONS AND CONSTRAINTS
content: The assumptions and constraints of the project are following:  As we need to provide a user friendly platform, so we need to provide an interface which has least training time for layman which could be a user or a company.  The user had to b e provided  a suitable layout  with choices of the tours  in the form of bids provided by different companies from which he could choose the most suitable bid.  To design such an elaborate system with a big  subset of actors in limited time and deadline along with the research to pinpoint the required functionalities would be a difficult task to carry out.  To attract companies and tourists to this platform, this platform should use minimum resources on the user’s device i.e. least CPU usage, least memory resources, etc.

heading: 1.5 PROJECT SCOPE
content: Our project will provide a trust worthy platform for both, tourist and tourism companies. Tourism companies will provide there service on our  platform. We will not provide  any tourism services to the clients but rather a platform where companies and tourists can collaborate to arrange trips and tours. Thus this system will provide  all of his actors to keep track of the tours which are either posted, booked, available for bidding or the tours in finalized state.

heading: 2.1.1 Literature
content: Different countries around the world are earning billions of dollars just because of tourism industry. Millions of travelers all around the world travel annually within or across their own regions. To facilitate such a big number of travelers, tourism has always remained an interesting area for researcher s. For example, the author in [1 ] surveyed with tourists to identify diffe rent patterns that can help industry in making their products to enhance tourists’ travel experience.  The GUIDE system reported in [2 ] was developed to facilitate tour of Lancaster city on the basis of tourist’s individual cont ext and needs. The authors in [3] developed and evaluated a system that can help museum’s visitors to collaborate with each other to explore about diffe rent objects. The authors in [4 ] used linked data resources to help decision makers in promoting tourism in their regions. The authors in [5] developed a tourism application that used geofencing in order to guide visitors about their surrounding by using audio guide. Even the authors in [6] used drones to support virtual tourism in real time rather than pre-recorded videos. In addition to the research work in literature a lot of websites have also been developed to support tourism. An overview of such websites has been discussed in the following section.

heading: 2.1.2 Tourism Related Websites
content: The site trip.me [7] is a tour based website which was foun ded in January 2013 in Berlin, Germany. This site is for all the tourists present around the world except Pakistan (as this site is not present in Pakistan right now). Its concept is that it allows travelers contact agents. The travelers can then personali ze and book trips directly with the local agents of that area. Another website working right now is tripadvisor [8]. This site tells the best Restaurants, lodgings attraction places and prices of flights around the world. You can also book a Vacation Renta l through this site. In the context of Pakistan, Pakistantours  [9] is a website working right now in Pakistan which was established in 2010. All of their offices are located in Lahore. There are providing diverse services. These services include tour guida nce, visa consultancy, conferences and mice, catering, meet and assist and many others. Tourhq [10] is also a tourism website in Pakistan. This tourism site is run by only one person who is the acting as both the owner and the guide. You can easily contact him through the phone number provided on his website and can plan a tour. Pakistantourguides [11] which is another tourism website in Pakistan. On this website, you can register as a guide and add an event with details. People who visit this site and are w illing to go on a trip with you will contact you through your detail. However, it does not allow tourists to create their own trips which can be a more flexible and tourist cantered approach.

heading: 2.6 SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE
content: Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) is the continuity of tasks which are performed to produce the desired results. Mostly SDLC consist of six steps which are Analysis and gathering of Requirements, Designing, Implementation, Deployment and Maintenance.

heading: 2.6.1 Waterfall Process Model
content: Waterfall process model when all of the requirements are defined and no further changing are required. In waterfall process model when a phase is completed we rarely revisit that phase. In waterfall process model at requirement phase all the requirements of the application are analyzed and are gathered in the form of document. Than this gathered requirements are carefully analyzed to generate design of the application which includes programming language, data layers etc. Than in the next step the actual code is written. After coding testing phase is applied on the generated code. After the success of testing phase the code is deployed. After the deployment phase waterfall process model includes maintenance phase  which is the last phase. In this phase patches are released to overcome the issues faced by the clients.

heading: 2.6.2 REASONS
content:  System requirements of our project are clearly defined.  As it is difficult for all of us to make changing in the design later as the process exceed. The waterfall process is well suited as it lends the designer well to change the design in the early stage of the application.  After deployment patches can be released to update the application.

heading: 3.4 SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
content: System architecture is the process in which all the functional and non-functional requirements are gathered and a structured solution for them is generated so that the desired system can be constructed. This process is used for complex structures as we can develop simple structure without system architecture. There are ma ny system architectures to build a system. Multiple architecture can also be used to develop a system. These multiple architectures are named as “Software Architecture Styles”. The Software architecture styles used to develop our system are given below:

heading: 3.4.1 CLIENT SERVER
content: Client server architecture includes two groups, Client and Server. In this system each process occurs between a client and the server. In this architecture style a client request the host server and receive services in return. Mostly servers do  not have any information about the identity of the client but the client must know the identity of the server i.e. IP address in order to access and get services from the server.

heading: 3.4.2 MODEL VIEW ARCHITECTURE
content: Model View Architecture is the kind of architecture which separates an application in to three parts which are presentation, information and interaction. The user is allowed to interact with views and is also allowed to input any data. When a user input any data the input is send to the concerned controller and the controller updates the concerned model if needed.

heading: Abstract
content: Travel Smart aims to allow smart management of road network and plan efficient traffic routes to avoid traffic jams. It will also provide maximum utilization of bus. Users can obtain bus services through our Smart Route app. They can check routes and pay charges of the selected bus through the app. The app will also act as a guidance system for the driver as it will alert the driver about traffic jams ahead and will advise an alternate route. Smart Route will be a huge advancement in the transportation technology. It will be a huge leap towards the automation as paying bus charges, selecting routes and avoiding traffic will be mere taps away.

heading: 1 Introduction
content: Travel Smart app is divided into three modules each module with different functionality but are linked with each in some way. First module is for the bus drivers, every driver's data will be recorded in our database which will include their names and id given by  the companies and a GPS tracker device will be placed in every bus which will help us monitor their location. This device will keep us alert on the location of the bus. If in route of bus driver face traffic or any other road difficulties it will alert driver and the app will suggest driver a complete new route with destination remain same. Second module of the bus is for passengers. Passengers belonging to an institute who wish to avail their institute’s bus service have to pay their fees. A fee challan can be print from the website of our app. After he fee is payed the data will be directly updated in database. After paying fee passengers will have to install and launch the application, from there they will sign up for the service. The passengers will share their information which will include their home address. After all passengers who wish to avail the service have signed up for the service, the application will calculate how many passengers live in which areas of the city and based on that data the ap plication will make routes for the bus company . Routes marked out by the application will be based on maximum number of passengers not having to travel far to reach a bus stop, and efficiency in terms of traffic and speed.  After mapping out all different routes for the bus company, it will alert passengers about which bus stop they would need to reach and at what time to get on their respected bus. Since because of traffic and or other situations the bus can be late to arrive at a stop, so the passengers can use the application to check the current location of the bus. And in a situation when a user feels they are running late, they can use the application to figure out how much extra time they potentially have to reach the bus stop and still catch the bus.  Or if they should move towards the next bus stop instead.

heading: 1.1 Objectives
content:  Passengers are able to sign up for their institute’s bus service and share their home address.  Based on home address of all passengers who have signed up, the application will map out the most effective and efficient route for the bus company.  Help the bus company to figure how many buses would be required to run on a route if there are a lot of passengers for a single bus to handle.  The application will help passengers track location of the bus, how long will it take for their bus to reach their stop, and if a user is running late, help them make a decision which stop they should move towards in order to catch the bus.

heading: 1.2 Problem Statement
content: Nowadays due to traffic jams most people are not able to reach their destination in time. Most of the time people have to wait for their bus or public transport for travelling from one place to another. It is diff icult for the public to keep track of their bus routes or the changes in traffic and the number of passengers in a bus which makes it difficult for the people to travel using a bus service and manage time. With our application, we are making it easy for the passengers to keep track of their bus location, routes and bus stops by easily signing up for their specific institute’s bus service.

heading: 1.3 Assumptions and Constraints
content: The assumptions and constraints of this project are described in section 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 respectively.

heading: 1.3.1 Assumptions
content:  High Speed internet at least 3G is available to the users.  The User has an Android or IOS operating system installed on his/her phone.  The Users phone has GPS tracking.

heading: 1.3.2 Constraints
content:  The user needs to pay a fee before (to complete the registration process) so he can start using the application.  There is a chance that the driver might change the route because of traffic jam and take alternate route so you have to move for that alternate stop.

heading: 1.4 Project Scope
content: The scope of this  project aims to allow smart management of road network and plan efficient traffic routes to avoid traffic and maximum utilization of bus resources by enabling maximum number of passengers to travel through buses.

heading: 2.1.1 Uber
content: This a network designed for enterprises and small businesses who wish to deliver customers. The drivers are ordinary people who are registered with Uber also known as Uber partners. Uber partners either use cars or bicycles for their business, they provide live tracking so you know all the time where your location is. The pricing of transportation is based on zones, if the passenger’s destination is in the same zone then the expense will be lower as compared to use of any other source of transportation which includes local buses.

heading: 2.2.1 Passenger
