heading: Abstract
content: The aim of the proposed project is to develop a marker based augmented reality android application named “AREd” (Augmented Reality Education). The traditional way of teachin g doesn’t seem to engage the students fully into studying. Students need visuals to get them motivated to study. This application’s basic purpose is to make the learning experience more interesting, lasting and interactive. Motivation behind AREd app is that students can get fuller understanding of a concept relating to what they are studying if they get to view 3D model of that abstract idea. For example, if a student is studying biology and wants to see the structure of human organs like brain, and for better understanding, the student can use AREd application to view the 3D model of brain and interact with it. AREd application will be used to generate 3D models of human anatomy for anatomy students. The 3D models can be seen by scanning the desired target  image through a smartphone’s camera. Once the target image (digital or printed fro m website) gets scanned, the application will generate interactive 3D model (a model which you can rotate and scaled around on screen.).The interactive 3D models will provide better understanding of concepts related to human anatomy. This application will make the learning through augmented reality quite engaging. Sometimes what the student has understood can be incorrect, so proper visualization of their study material will clear away any misconceptions. It would be very helpful in educational sector for students to interact with 3D models and make learning interesting like never before. It would be beneficial for teachers to teach in an innovative way as well. Table of Contents Evaluation ................................ ................................ ......... Error! content: Augmented reality is a new technology which can be used in educational environment to engross and motivate students.  AREd application is a marker based augmented reality application that allows students and instructors to visualize 3D models in the real environment, real scale and real time. Students can understand concepts by viewing and interacting with 3D models that are generated by application upon scanning the target image through smart phone’s camera.  Target images can be scanned from the AREd website directly or printed images. Upon correct scanning of target images, interactive 3D models are generated. heading: 1.1  Objectives
content: Objectives of AREd are as follows: • To help teachers teach in an innovative and interactive way so that students can understand anatomy concepts easily. • To help anatomy students to achieve better grades at school by scoring above average marks after using it for studying.

heading: 1.2 Problem Statement
content: The traditional way in which students are taught has little to no engagement of students, the teacher comes and tea ches what is to be covered in the syllabus. To make the classroom sessions more interacting, interesting and innovative, it all depends on the teacher if he/she wishes to do so. Traditional way of teaching gives no guarantee that things taught by the teacher will retain in minds of the students. The traditional teaching ways include communication between the teachers and the students and involve static paper representations and exchanges and have limited visuals. Visual aids are of great significance in the  learning process but many teachers don’t utilise them during their lectures. The teachers can use the new and emerging tec hnology to aid in the learning process. Especially subjects like biology, astronomy and chemistry need more visuals and pictures to grasp the concepts firmly. Teachers can collaborate their teaching methods with new technologies like augmented reality based applications (like AREd) to help them in conveying their lectures in an interactive and engaging way.

heading: 12 of 85  20 December 2018
content: AREd will not only help the teachers in their lectures but the students can also benefit from it. Many students who do self -study can use AREd applicati on to help them get the full picture of what they are actually studying. When the students use AREd, they will remember things bette r than memorising a bunch of text written in the books, they can recall the 3D models and their interactions and remember what they have studied. They get to practically see what they have just learned as it is more interesting. Use of this application will improve the learning curve and result in better grades.

Everyone knows that visuals are important especially for a hard concept to make it more comprehensible. heading: Related Work
content: Aug That  [4] is an augment reality application that makes learning fun and interesting for students, this application aids teachers and parent s by making it easier for students and children to learn through the app. The application utilized the mobile phone’s camera. W ith the help of the camera, the scanned target images provided by the applications triggers 3D shapes. The student is immersed in  a virtual environment, allowing the student to have a 360 -degree view plus a chance to play with the interactive model be ing displayed. AugThat utilises augmented reality, and interact with the models that popped up. AugThat is different from AREd (augmented reality education) as AREd will allow interactive models of human anatomy for students and teachers, while AugThat has no specific domain. Inspired from AugThat , AREd will include an audio option that will read out the function of the interactive model  that is being displayed. 4D Anatomy [5] has impressive graphics which makes use of augmented reality, where the user of 4D anatomy gets to interact with human body organs. The student using the app gets time to study the application’s study content at his/her own pace. This application is best suited for teaching in a classroom. 4D Anatomy application includes quizzes that will assess the student’s capabilities. It lets the student manipulate the images. Also  other intuitive f eatures help to navigate around the model. 4D anatomy allows the teacher to define the syllabus for their students. The application grants access to the teacher to change the syllabus at any time. One major difference between AREd and 4D Anatomy is that both the users (i.e. both students and teachers) can use the application but none can make changes to them. AREd  doesn’t grant access to the users to make changes in the app unlike in 4D Anatomy app where teachers can change the syllabus. AREd will also prov ide students with compreh ensive quiz to test student’s comprehensibility and grasp on the concept they learned through AREd application. heading: Existing System Study
content: This section is concerned with the study of the work which already exists related to the proposed project. This work is the basis for setting  up the requirements of the proposed project and helped in deciding the features of the application. Jorge, Peña, Wanda, María, and Carlos [25] in their research paper aimed for interactive study using augmented reality in the field of electrical engineering. Using AR, it was made sure that students can do their laboratory practice without any assistance from teachers. As well as, a connection to be established between a theoretical concept and laboratory practices. The applicat ion used virtual animati ons along with audio files by teachers to view abstract concepts in the real world e.g., role magnetic field plays in power generation and operation of electrical engines through electromagnetic forces. Students considered this appl ication easy to use and quite helpful for their studies. The application also facilitated teachers by improving their teaching methodologies as well as increasing their interaction with students through a direct explanation of complex concepts. So, it is concluded that if AR appl ications are planned properly they can help students a lot to successfully perform any learning process. Such AR application should also be extended to other domains of subjects for facilitating students. Sergey, Fedor, Chebotarev, and Rabinovich  [26] in their article proposed the use of augmented reality in secondary level education for implementation of Interactive Educational Content (IEC). The motivation was to replace traditional old -school teaching methodologies with 3D visualizations of educatio nal content. To achieve this goal, software architecture modules of IEC along with toolset for IEC creation were developed which involved all the AR and 3D visualization techniques. For the presentation of virtual lessons to students in the physics laboratory scenarios and content was developed. Lastly, methodologies were finalized to actually implement IEC in the secondary level of education. Developed approaches helped the creation and implementation of IEC  in different educational domains like chemistry, physics, biology, mathematics etc. which can work on different hardware platforms both online and offline. Altogether 55 studies published in between 2011 to 2016 in Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI) were examined. Paper discussed the future trends in the usage of augmented reality for the field of education. Experts find ou t that usage of augmented reality in education has been increased since 2013. Through this study, it was discovered that quantitative research methodology was most commonly used for augmented reality in the domain of education. The highest usage of AR application was in higher education and very few AR applications were for childhood education. It was revealed that 40% of AR studies were from the field of science. The main benefit of using AR is increasing the learning capabilities of students and providing motivation by making education interesting for them.

The AR book will be developed after the low -tech prototyping and the participants will write their suggestions on sticky notes after experimenting with the AR. The candidates of the survey were all students’ fifty-eight females and fifty- eight males and age ranging from fifteen to twenty-two. From the results, it was clear the majority of the students were willing to be taught from new and innovative teaching methodologies that involves latest technology but not all institutes can afford such technologies, but majority of the students nowadays own a smart phone so using AR will not be costly. Another one of their aim was to know the opinions of pa rents about an app that monitors their child usage of the smart phone while using the AR app as smart phone’s radiations are quite harmful if the exposure is prolonged. The marker-less AR app developed was for android operating system and was developed usi ng Unity3D. Marker- less app refers no requirement of a target image such as QR code so trigger the AR. Only the device camera point to any surface and the mini -games and interactive sc ene having explorable objects will appear on the screen. Making learning , more interesting. The app will also allow parents to monitor their kid’s activities and usage remotely. heading: 24 of 85  20 December 2018
content: Luis and Jose  [49] in their article  work proposed using augmented reality to make up a smart class (SaCl).  The article was an extension o f their previous successful work that proposed the architecture of the smart class. Their main aim was strengthen their theory to use AR in smart class will incredibly improve the quality of education. The rese arch was conducted between two groups of 50 st udents per group. One group was taught using traditional teaching methods on the other hand the other was taught by simulations using AR and augmented reality based apps. Hypothesis recorded and was proved corr ect. To finalise the results a survey was cond ucted whose result reflect that students are willing and motivated to learning using AR in education.  There was an improvement too in the learning curve of the students taught by AR. The contents learned from AR lasted longer compared to the one from traditional methods.  Not all schools find this idea welcoming as the implementing such as change can be costly. Many schools strongly believe that their traditional teaching methods cannot be replaced by technology. Joonhyu, Boram, Choongho and Woontack [50] in proposed AR-Class-Notes. AR-Class- Note, are the handwritten notes that can be shared among the class, the instructor and across multiple head -mounted devices. The main aim of re search to develop an app that incorporates AR and networking together onto AR headsets so notes can be shared from any location in a virtual classroom. The main constituents of AR -Class-Notes are: note creation, interaction of user, network among users. The components that make up the notes each have 3 functions Server, personal, and server. Algorithm for optical character recognition and a head -mounted device for client was required. For the client head - mounted device use was Microsoft’s HoloLens and a Win dows 10 professional OS was used for serving a s a server. At the server side, Unity3D 5.6 Vuforia’s extension  was installed. It was installed and used to design the interface of the app for HoloLens at the client side using Visual Studio 2017 editor.  Using the AR-Class-Note makes it easier for distant learners and teachers to share their notes especially of the notes are not stored electronically.  The equipment used in the proposed system is quite expensive and it is less likely that people are willing to make such investment. A study was conducted with fourth-year architecture students that studied how temperature estimation was impacted by visualizations. The students liked the idea of virtual human based visualizations more than particle-based visualization. Participants rated the level of motivation to learn about how temperature in the house was influenced by its design. It was not clear how children will be affected by visualizations. To make this study a part of curriculum, more effort needs to be put in this project.

heading: 5.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: During the documentation of project  and development of the AREd application we faced several problems due to requirement creep even though the scope of the project was clear but gold platting caused delay in the initial phases of the project. As the requirements became clear the development of the project was smooth and steady. We learned several new skills during the project such as we got to learn new and basic level concepts of Unity game engine and got to learn C# and how to code in C# to perform several actions. We got to a grip on the modelling tool 3Ds max to model 3D model at beginner level and how to label the 3D models in 3DS max. Also we got hands on experience of conducting research and how to write up a research paper.

heading: 5.2 Project summary
content: New trends in technology are emerging every other day which is also one of the reasons for change in interests of people, especially the young generation. To blend in the changing trend we have to change our traditional methods to advanced ones. One of the change in traditional methodology is in teaching. AREd is an application that uses the concept of augmented reality  to help anatomy students study anatomy using our app. With the help of the application the student using it can view and interact with labelled 3D model of human systems such as the digestive system and organs such as the brain. In order to view or generate the 3D model the user needs to install the application into their smart phone and need a targe t image which will be scanned just like QR code once scanned, on the smart phone screen the user can view and interact with the 3D model. Along with the model the user can also hear the audio which will provide general information on the model which is bei ng displayed. Each human system has its own target image that will generate its respective 3d model once scanned. To test their own concepts that the user also as the option to take a multiple choice quiz that will during and at the end will display their overall scores upon every correct answer. The users also have the option to view video  related to the system that they are interacting with. The video can be viewed through a virtual button that is present on the target image. The video will be played duri ng the moment the button is pressed or covered and stop as soon as the button is relea sed. In this way the user can get additional information related to the model they wish to study.

heading: Abstract
content: COMSATS Programs and Courses Outcomes System (CPACOS) is being developed in order to compete with other educational institutes in developed countries to do this  there are some parameters defined by their institutes that our educational institutes have to fulfil  first. Their institutes have built their educational principles upon Bloom’s taxonomy  and is one o f the frequently used procedure for distinguishing and organizing levels of expertise  in a particular domain. There are currently many assessment models serving as single online platform both for students and faculty which allows them to perform their corresponding roles causing problems like not knowing how the learner performed in a specific content rather following a traditional system. CPACOS got enough potential to match up with them even it is better as platforms like  that are not into working mode, by providing Outcome Based Learning and Course Based Learning where the Faculty will be able to define their objectives and how they will demonstrate significant and important lea rning that learners will learn  to initiate a new assessment criteria break ing the traditional one. CPACOS is one such web application that is built on the principles and standards of Bloom’s Taxonomy.

heading: 1 INTRODUCTION
content: In this chapter we will discuss about our projects its goals and objectives, the problems in the existing system and how we have encountered them.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: CPACOS will use the  concept of Bloom’s Taxonomy which will tell the level of knowledge to achieve the required results.  Differentiating and establishing quantifiable student results in this manner will help us to choose the desirable evaluation methods such as assignments, quizzes or by conducting vivas for a particular course. There are information-oriented areas, ability-oriented areas, and affecting areas. Remembering, Understanding, Applying, Analyzing, Evaluating, and Creating are the application used for the concept of Bloom’s Taxonomy. So, it is about time that the educational world will see a platform that is going to address all assessment and learning issues. This one will be going to be revolutionize the universities assessment system. CPACOS has also used the idea of OBL (Outcome Based Learning) [4] as well as CBL (Course Based Learning) that will be a check to define how good or bad a student is in a given topic and course. These measurable student outcomes will eventually allow  us to easily differentiate the students with higher level of expertise  in a certain areas  and those who have lower level of expertise lacking in certain areas . By applying the idea of Bloom's Taxonomy  much described branch OBE, CPACOS will provide a much convenient and flexible way to dictate the degree to which the students are comprehending and using concepts in order to demonstrate particular skills. This will also show their interest ratio towards particular content of the course. In addition to that this will also help in planning and designing the assessments techniques.  This will also help to assess the instructors by mapping the objectives which they have decided to achieve through the course. By giving the complete report about the assessments and the objectives met to deliver an outcome. However, when it will deploy it will have a more generalized look. Although, that CPACOS is built for COMSATS, still if other educational institutes will feel the need to use this. It can be customized as well for them.

heading: 1.2 Goals and Objectives
content: In this section we have discussed our main goals and the objectives we need to meet.

heading: 1.2.1 Main Goals
content:  Our primary goal is to develop and deliver such a platform that aid the university in the assessment of students with respect to different goals such as knowledge goals, course objectives by Bloom’s Taxonomy and to describe the major learning outcome that has been achieved and what the student has learned and will he be able to deliver something in that particular area. As well as how to create a better student assessment system.

heading: 18 | P a g e
content:  The Faculty will be able to have a visual representation of all the assessments they took in a particular course by mapping them with the objectives, by generating reports and the assessment is carried out on t he principles of Bloom’s Taxonomy, OBL (Outcome  Based Learning) as well as CBL (Course Based Learning).

heading: 1.2.2 Objectives
content: This will provide a platform where it will show Students interest ratio towards particular course. In addition to that this will also help in planning and designing the assessments techniques.  Evaluating the course content deliverables as well as Students expertise.  Improve the overall assessment system in Pakistan.  We want to address the issues in the current assessment system which isn’t providing any healthy competition need to make well-skilled individuals.  Manage the Assessment criteria of evaluation.  Relationship between Course Learning Outcomes and Program Learning Outcomes.  Provide Assessment Plan for the Course and identify key aspects of learning.  Deliver direct Assessment.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: Although many online systems are currently giving a platform where Faculty are given the ease to perform their tasks online like Add Attendance, Add Marks etc. Giving each student a specific login so that he/she can view his/her progress. Only allowing the faculty to upload marks of the whole assessment making it unclear about how the student performed in the specific content of the course or whether the objectives of the course are met or not.  But we thought that there is a need of a system where Faculty can add assessment marks on the basis of specific contents of the course being taught by the instructor and delivering an outcome which is suitable enough to contribute to their skills as Pakistan is a developing country and the current education system isn’t competitive enough to cope u p with the developed countries so  we want to develop  a system where faculty and student both will know their progress not only in a specific course but also in the co ntents of that specific course.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions and Constraints
content: The assumptions and constraint are as follows:  This application can run only on web platform.  CPACOS (COMSATS Programs and Courses Outcomes System) can possibly have many users. It is idealistic to deliver teaching to everyone. Therefore, the system should be intended for easy to use, providing help commands, and suitable error messages for invalid user inputs.  System will only be available to COMSATS faculty.

heading: 19 | P a g e
content:  Faculty will decide course contents and they are changeable according to the market needs.  System will be completed upon agreed quality metrics or conformance with internal quality standards of COMSATS.  The project must be completed within the due date. heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: IT sector is progressing so rapidly and we have the capability to automate such systems and contribute in the educational sector. We are completely optimistic about the scope of this one as it has introduced a simpler and more efficient way for coping with the troubles and give us a new direction in educational world. It will help faculty for the better understanding of concerns, traits and trends to make better decision making regarding course content. Eventually, universities will realize the significance of such platforms sooner or later they will feel the need to adopt it in order to s urvive in this competitive age.  We believe educational institutes will use CPACOS to implement the concept of direct evaluation.

heading: 2 REQUIREMENT ANALYSIS
content: In this chapter we have gathered our requirements, the applications made on our concept and the constraints on our functional requirements.

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: Considerable amount of work has already been done by using the concept of bloom’s taxonomy. Whether it is visible to us or not, Bloom’s Taxonomy is being used in a number of fields for serving different purposes. For an in stance, by using the idea of it, procedures have been developed for teaching adult effectively. Not only that its idea is being used in the development of learning technologies. Churches’ Digital Taxonomy [6] is a fine example of it. In the app store, you will come across a couple of apps that are built upon this idea of bloom’s taxonomy. Applications for mobile that can increase student commitment and association, and that can be us ed for learning methodologies.

heading: 2.1.1  “Remembering” applications
content: Diigo Inc. [7] – A tool that is used for bookmarking. You can use this app on an iPad to add lists and sub-lists of bookmarks. Evernote [8] – This app users can take notes, photos and can make voice reminders.

heading: 2.1.2  “Understanding” applications
content: It should help users understand facts and generate information: ShowMe [9] - The users of this app can record tutorials and then can upload them. You can also create ShowMe group for your assistance. Skitch [10] – This app allows users to add symbolic notations and can add text to images.

heading: 2.1.3  “Applying” applications
content: It helps students demonstrate methods or procedures, can do experimentation with concepts and let them discover a new path to be discovered: Audioboo [11] – App intended to be used for the purpose of voice recordings. The audio should be more than 3 minutes and posting is also enabled. MindMash – Critical thinking application lets users think out of the box by allowing them to think in virtual manner.

heading: 2.1.4  “Analyzing” applications
content: It helps users to differentiate the facts from th e hypothesis, check the details and then again construct the content: Wufoo [12] – A quite handy app for teachers as they can create surveys for students on safari on iPad. Users are allowed to create 1-3 surveys and get 5-100 responses per month. Inspiration Maps [13] – Students use symbols to create maps, update, and delete content.

heading: 2.1.5  “Evaluating” applications
content: Help users to detect data inconsistencies, tell efficiency, and provide critical solutions to problems and to evaluate procedures: Easy Chart [14] – Users create charts of various sizes. Side by Side – It offers offline functionality for book -readers. Allows them to see 1 -4 sites in a split screen.

heading: 2.1.6  “Creating” applications
content: It helps users deduce design decisions, give possible pathwa ys for the ideas, and deduce hypotheses: ScreenChomp [15] – Allows a user to generate an idea with screenshot and recording facility. Splice [16] – A platform where you can edit your videos  by GoPro which agree to the linking of HD photographs and videotapes. It allows them to create their own music playlist.

heading: 2.3.2  Non-Functional Requirements
content: The non-functional requirements are as follows: NFR01: Performance NFR01-01 Average load time of the starting page of the system must be less than 2 second. NFR01-02 Average processing time taken by the system to complete a request should be less than 10 seconds. NFR01-03 The System must be able to perform a simple search within 5-8 seconds and an advanced search (multiple search criteria) within 10-15 seconds regardless of the storage capacity or number of cases in the system. NFR01-04 System Mean Time to Failure should not be more than 10 minutes within 24 hours of use. NFR01-05 Average system response time should not be greater than 5 seconds. NFR01-06 System must successfully run on a client machine with 256 MB RAM or above. NFR01-07 100 users should be able to simultaneously access the system and update the database.

heading: 2.6 Software Development Life Cycle
content: SDLC model is used to a software that meets the user potentials. The best suitable SDLC for this project is Waterfall Model which is also called linear sequential life cycle model.

heading: Waterfall Model
content: According to project “ COMSATS Program and Course Outcome System (CPACOS) ” the most appropriate model is Waterfall Model. The reasons to choose Waterfall are:  All requirements are well known  Each phase of SDLC is well known  When current requirement is fulfilled then move to next phase.  At the end of each phase review is being taken by our Supervisor to ensure that the project  is on right track.  In this model one phase is completed at one time. No overlapping of phases take place.

heading: Figure 90 System Architecture
content: COMSATS Program and Course Outcome System (CPACOS) is a complex system which is based on web-application. This system uses the concept of Objective Based Learning (OBL) and Course Based Learning. Model View Controller (MVC) architecture is the most used architecture in web -applications, most importantly when you are working in a framework. MVC is used to implement interfaces, its logic lies in three parts i.e. Model, view, controller. Model is used to inform  the view to update itself according to data as it contains the project database, it knows what data is needed for the particular interface. View shows the interface the data which needs to be displayed, it will display the data whenever updated. Controller stores all the logic on which model and view will work whenever an input is received. Our project model contains our database, view contains all the displaying interfaces and controller will contain all the controlling logic. This separation will make our work easy, flexible and more secure.

heading: Abstract
content: In this project, we have created an online shopping website that allows Pakistani customers to find out deals on American websites which they don’t found in Pakistan’s online shopping stores. This system shall allow users to search deals from our website t hat they need  and can compare them as well . Customer will see all the deals alongside with products that are available on different shopping websites there especially American website. Customer can also keep their credit with us in dollars. They can see ho w much Dollar they have or withdraw credit from system and, they can check how much amount is remaining in system. The customers will be able to place an order by selecting a desired product using the proposed web portal. The system shall accurately mainta in a list of all the deals and current amount of dollars according to Pakistan rupees for user to view. The website will be MVC based and shall be using ASP .NET language for development and using SQL SEVER as a Database service.

We are also grateful to our friends for their support and all those who motivated us or helped us in any way during the completion of this project. Table of Contents

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Time has been changed and now people are tended to shop online rather than to go out to the stores and look for their desired items in different stores wasting too much time. With online shopping stores people now not only save a great amount of time and get their desired products easily. Now deals are very hot topic when you talk about online shopping . Another reason why people are moving towards online shopping is that they are looking for exciting deals in which they get their desired products with discounted price. If we talk about online shopping in Pakistan, then we can say that now people here as well started moving towards online shopping. Although people still go out for shopping, but the trend is now changing.  Customers here in Pakistan also looks for deals and unfortunately, they hardly get good deals because of several reasons. Shopit aims at providing shopping products from American websites for Pakistani customers. Shopit provides exciting deals directly from American online shops to Pakistani customers. All the deals  from different online shops are first fetched and stored at Shopit database. Then all those deals are regularly  posted on Shopit website where Pakistani customers can see them. Customers here in Pakistan can post orders and Shopit system will generate bill in dollars w.r.t to order including shipping price. The orders are then forwarded to American online shopping store. The American website that we  have used initially are Deals2Buy.com, NewEgg Marketplace, NewEgg.com. Shipment is very important process in whole system and Shopit guarantees fast, steady and reliable shipping service for orders delivery.  The system also allows customers to communicate real time with Shopit representative for their queries. For the owners  of system , it allows to carefully analyze and generate different type of reports and graphs i.e. sales, revenue, order graphs and reports  for analysis purpose. Payment of order is necessary part of online shopping. It is really a problem for customer who don’t carry dollars with them to pay their order bill in dollars. For this purpose, Shopit will allow our Customers to keep their money within system. So that they don’t have to worried about currency because customers can deposit money in rupees and Shopit system  keep it in system w.r.t latest dollar rate. Similarly, customers can withdraw their credit anytime. If the value of dollar raises anytime and customer wants to withdraw money, then the profit is divided between customer and our system with respect to set percentage i.e. 10%.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Our main objective is to allow our Pakistani customers to get more and more exciting deals that they can’t found on Pakistani online stores. Not only our Pakistani people will get latest deals but also, they can keep their money that is dollar converted in to our accounts so that they can directly pay from it when they shop in future. The main objectives are listed below. • A complete web-based shopping website. • Provide a Friendly User Interface. • Shopping service for our customers. • A soft currency system for Pakistani customers. • Develop the system with latest technology and trends.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: In current era, people are moving towards online shopping. Although in foreign countries all the shopping system is now online, and the trend is also changing in Pakistan. People in Pakistan usually attracted towards online shopping because of deals and di scount offers. But unfortunately, Pakistani online shops don’t offer exciting deals regularly. They often offer deals when the stock is old or when it is festival or important day coming  like Christmas, Black Friday . Not only this  after when customer orders products from foreign shops or local online shops they get their products with opened packing and sometime original accessories are also replaced by replica ones. Shipment is also a problem sometimes orders get delivered too late and customer keeps waiting for their orders.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions & Constraints
content: • The application is web based and will run on every browser. • Project must be completed within budget tolerance. • Project schedule will not be violated and will be finished within schedule  and in case of any delay no more than 10 days will be added to project schedule. • The Shopit System can potentially have hundreds of users. It is unrealistic to provide training for everyone. Therefore, the system should be designed for easy to use, providing help instructions, and appropriate error messages for invalid user inputs. • The Shopit p roject has full support from senior management across all departments. • Developers team can produce quality and professional manuals and guide. • The final product must be developed according to customer’s need and stakeholder’s requirements.

heading: 1.5 Project scope
content: From the previous recent years, the technological advancement is increasing steadily, and all the shopping is now being shifted online. No need to go out to stores for shopping. Especially the tech market is very hot place for shopping in online stores now a days.  The motivation behind the idea of Shopit is to plan, design, build, and implement an online Shopping store for Pakistani customers with a soft currency system which will help Pakistani customers in getting great, exciting deals from American stores and a system to pay bills from stored credit . The focus on this website is on tech gadgets.  System will let admin managing Customer’s accounts and let them see customer’s all orders list. System will also let admin to take actions and manage customer reports. The system will let customers see products, its details, order it and can give reviews & ratings for it. System will also let customer to use and save dollars in their accounts and ability to manage their accounts. All the transaction will be done after logging into Shopit customer account. What is not included in Shopit system for now is types of products. That is, we will be initially targeting some specific products from American online shops. Shopit will be developed on localhost and later it will be shifted onto the domain.

heading: 2.1  Literature Review
content: Currently we have different website that provides shopping and shipping services. On the other hand, various currency exchange websites that are currently dealing with customers for money exchange.

heading: 2.1.1  PkShip.com
content: PkShip is a Pakistani website that provide ser vices like ours. They purchase product from American stores and ship it to you. The only drawback in this website is, customers first must visit original website from which they want to purchase product and then they give that web link to PkShip and they p urchase it and deliver it. Whereas in our system we will be providing all the products, deals at our own web page so customer don’t have to search products at different websites.

heading: 2.1.2 Alibaba:
content: Alibaba provides different products from different websites for its customer. It also let customer select supplier by region. But only flaw in Alibaba is that their shipping service is not good enough and good deals are not often provided to customers. We in our system will be providing different deals from various American website so that customer can take advantage of those deals. And shipping service will be made efficient so that customer will not have to wait much.

heading: 2.1.3  Nazdeeq.com:
content: Nazdeeq.com is a Pakistani eco mmerce website. Their mission is to  enable simple cross-border ecommerce with technology and unique payment solutions. But still in this website you must go for a product in a query then it will return you results. Whereas in our system we will be providing all latest deals, so customers don’t have to search through product. They will get product category. So, the basic difference here will be of user friendliness.

heading: 2.3 Software development life cycle model
content: For the development of Shopit system, we  are going to use Waterfall Model & RAD.  The 2 models have been selected because of our requirement’s and stakeholder’s nature.  We have chosen waterfall model because i t is used when the requirements are well known,  product definition is stable, and technology is understood. RAD is chosen because it is used where customers are non-technical and usually don’t know what they want and what they can have. Due to unclear requirements of what will be easy for the users, an d moderate chances of requirement changes, we will use prototyping model to provide users with prototypes and they will update our prototypes which will help us in clearing our requirements according to those feedbacks provided by the users, till all requirements are captured and are cleared. Then we will use waterfall model to implement those requirements. Because waterfall model needs clear requirements, the clear requirements will be taken to start the waterfall phases. In waterfall model, we get a comp lete document at the end of a phase to verify that all the requirements are implemented according to requirement plan. Because of these documents, maintenance of app becomes easy. Figure 32 Software development life cycle model

heading: 3.1 Work Break Down Structure (WBS)

WBS is a foundation document that provides the basis for planning and managing project schedules, costs, resources, and changes. heading: 3.7 Architecture
content: The architecture that will be used for Shopit  website is 3 -tier architecture i.e. Model View Controller (MVC).  All the user interface section will be kept in Views, whereas Database related section will be kept within Model and all the business login will be contained within controllers. We will crea te different controllers i.e. Home

heading: Controller, Admin Controller, Deals Controller, Shipment Controller, Currency
content: controllers for different modules of Shopit website. All the database tables will be created in Models. Different user interface that will be d eveloped in HTML, CSS, Bootstrap, JavaScript, jQuery that will be contained within Views. Through MVC architecture we can reuse a lot of code throughout development period.

heading: 5.1.1 Lessons Learned
content: As we were unaware of tools and technology and how ecommerce shopping website are being run, we face difficulties for this reason . This document contains requirements and detailed diagrams  that demonstrate our project. The system design phase was challenging because many diagrams like Database diagrams were created iteratively because it wasn’t matching our requirements.  The documentation stage of project was challenging but it also clears our concepts. Website working prototypes were created on designing tool  i.e. Justin Mind Prototyper . It was a bit different and new task for us as it was our first experience of using this type of tool.  The work breakdown structure created many details of the processes it took time to  analyse. But in the end, it gave us values we required and learned Microsoft Project implementation and other project management tools . Creating diagram s was a difficult task as it  took a lot of time and revisions . The implementation of currency module was also challenging. As most of payment gateways requires company’s legal documents or not operate in Pakistan i.e. PayPal, Stripe. For this reason, we only implemented this module on 2Checkout sandbox. The main question that was a big barrier for us was to decide which tool and technology we should choose for the development of this project. After analysis and talking to some senior market developers it was decided to use ASP .NET programming language with MVC framework and SQL Server as database service. IT was big challenge to understand and learn all concepts of chosen language in a professional way. The learning phase of language took a huge amount of time as we learn everything from scratch and in th e end, we managed to develop good looking website with good programming logics. As we are software developers and not testers but, in this project,  we have to be testers for our project as well that was a challenging task itself. The unit testing and then system testing also took great amount of time to find out our website’s bugs.

heading: 5.1.2 Lessons Learned
content: • We learn ed how most of today’s website gather data that is Scrapping  or Crawling. • We learned how to develop professional software for market level. • We learned how software requirements are gathered and finalized, which ones to be ignored and which ones to accept. • We learned how to develop database for a software and how to integrate it with software. • We learned a lot of concepts in chosen language and also some other publicly available libraries that we used in our project. • We learned how software is developed in organizations i.e. we understand and followed software development life cycle. • We learned how to work in team and how to cooperate with each other.

heading: 5.2  Project summary
content: The basic purpose of this project was to introduce an online shopping store that allows Pakistani customers to get deals  from American we bsite that are very cheap as compared to their original price . We also added seller module so that if any seller wants to sell items on deal then they can sell on our website.  This document consists of all the requirements i.e. SRS, Software Design, Scope, Goals of the project. The first step of our project was gathering requirements and started working on the documents, after it we started creating web design on tool.  Despite of the fact that there are already many similar websites for providing deals from other countries , our system will provide comfort zone to the customers of Pakistan as they hardly get good deals from the online stores here in Pakistan. heading: Introduction
content: Virtual reality (VR) is a  computer-generated scenario that simulates a realistic experience. The immersive environment can be similar to  the real world in order to create a  lifelike experience grounded in reality or sci-fi. Augmented reality systems may also be considered a form of VR that layers virtual information over a live camera feed into a headset, or through a smartphone or tablet device. Moreover, Unity supports the low -level APIs Metal on iOS and Mac OS and Vulkan on Android, Linux, and Windows, and additionally Direct3D 12 on Windows and Xbox One. [3] Ever since the gaming industry has evolved, in the world many  game developers have stepped up and developed the games belonging to different categories. This game will provide training to the driver who have not driven cars in mountainous areas. Our project aim is to provide the facility of training drivers using smart phones and Virtual Reality (VR) gear. Our game idea can be elaborate as follows: From the Beginning of gaming development games are mostly used for entertainment purpose. People use games for passing spare time and for entertainment purpose. Our idea f or this game is to provide them a game which will train them for driving in mountainous areas along with entertainment. It will also help the particular government to decrease the accident ratio in hilly areas. For example, if a driver is driving from a long time but have not driven in mountainous area, the game will train them to prepare such a journey through elaboration of driving rules and different accidental situation which may occur during journey. It will help driver to understand the condition, situation and traffic rules for driving on hilly roads. For example how to drive on sharp curves, how to overtake and how to pass vehicle through stream of water. The target audience of this game will be everyone who wants to drive in precipitous roads.

heading: Objectives
content: Following are the Goals and Objectives of our project: • To avoid accidents in Pakistan. • Teach people traffic rules. • Teach people what problem they can possibly face when driving on hilly area. • To utilize our smart phones in such an effective way that we can get maximum benefits out of it. By using it in such a smart way so journey is safer. • The basic objective of this project is to overcome accident ratio all over world especially in Pakistan.

content: Literature review / Existing system study    Jonathan steuer et al  [4] explained the concept of virtual reality. He described that the presence and telepresence are two very similar but different concepts. When we talk about virtual reality it means that we are talking about the telepresence. Telepresence is about feeling the environment completely but not being physically present in it there is a medium i.e. a hardware (head mounted display) by which we are able to sense the environment and by the use of an input device i.e. remote we can interact with it.  Abel Angel Rendon et al [5] describes physical therapy interventions that increase functional strength and balance have been shown to reduce falls in older adults. Wii Fit, a balance board which helps patients to keep their body stable while performing specific movements.  In the virtual reality group VRG group, each participant used three different balance games from the Wii Fit software package. Participants were instructed to follow the onscreen visual displays while maintainin g their limit of stability during dynamic stance activities this study compared a virtual reality group (VRG) and a control group (CG) and Participants in the VRG showed positive changes towards clinical assessment outcome measures versus the CG that showed minimal to no change.  Gustavo Saposnik et al [6] portrays the strokes which cause hemiparesis to patients and most survivors suffer from  motor deficiencies. Controllers have speed sensors which empowers member to collaborate with the amusement through the deve lopment of hand or wrist. Virtual reality gives straightforwardness and stimulation as recovery treatments and there are odds of speedier treatment.  T. Roma Jasinevicius et al [7] portrays dental simulation system created to enhance dental understudies' change from the preclinical lab to the facility utilizing virtual reality. VR utilizes one of the four virtual reality recreation units —the Exemplary DentSim. It additionally portrays how utilizing virtual reality enhances the execution and exactness of dental understudies. heading: 1.12 System Architecture
content: The software architecture we used is Layered Architecture as our project could be decomposed into a number of higher and lower layers in a hierarchy. For instance, our project is decomposed into tasks like Building User Interface, Creating Environment, Creating levels, AI car Movements, and connecting controller etc.; each task demanding separate work. The layers contain related classes that either we encapsulated in some package or as a group of subroutines in the format of method library or header file. Each layer in our project has its own sole responsibility as AI car movements intends to move cars while the other layer modelling just tends to build an objects. The upper layers calls lower layers in order to complete its tasks, e.g. layer Create car’s Movements calls the lower layer Character Building as a character can’t be moved until and unless it’s not been created. Furthermore, layered architecture provides opportunity for group members to divide tasks and work in modules in parallel. Hence, we used Layered Architecture.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Cloud based IT Resource Provisioning is a web-based application which provides a virtual machine to the users (FYP Students) with installed windows or Linux operating system. The user can use virtual machine for testing of these projects for those higher hardware is required. These virtual machine s also provide the user installed software in the operating system according to his requirements. Every time when a new user requests for the virtual machine, he gets the newly installed operating system in the virtual machine to avoid the viruses which may affect the user’s system or affect the performance of the virtual machine. In these machines, the user can choose the RAM and Hard -drive according to his requirements so he can perform his task in these machines which he was unable to perform on his own. Although there are many cloud-based applications, used successfully and are being utilized in many applications as a fleet. Most of them use the Software as a service (SaaS) or Platform as a service (PaaS) but our application will work on Infrastructure a s a Service (IaaS). The application will provide the web page where user can choose the software which he wants in the virtual machine and specification of the machine and also select the operating system. Web page interacts with the hypervisor through controller then hypervisor provides virtual machine to the user according to his requirements. Live Migration between the servers is also used in this application when one server is over loaded. It provides more than one virtual machine at a time. Application will also have billing and monitoring module, Bill is decided on specification of the virtual machine and time interval in which the user uses our services. The billing module has been created in such a way that when the user tries to delete the VM that he has created. The bill is calculated according to the date at which the VM was created and the date at which the user deletes the VM.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Application for creating a VM on a cloud.  Set an environment for private cloud.  Design and develop a web application for the purpose of creating a virtual machine on the cloud.  Creating a database for the user that sign up for using the application and also use his account for later use.  Live Migration of virtual machine from one server to another for the purposes of load balancing.  Creating a Billing module according to the services chosen by the user.

heading: 1.3 Goals
content: In such a remarkably short time, the evolution of cloud -based platform has reached at a new level and many related applications are made which provi des a virtual machine and also provides installed software in these virtual machines. So, the main goals of our application are follows:  Developing a virtual machine on a private cloud.  Creating a module that automates the creation and deletion of the VM created by the user  Select the type of OS.  Select the amount of Ram.  Select the amount of Hard Drive Required.  Select the needed softwares.  GUI based application for creating and deleting the VM created by the user.

heading: 1.4 Problem statement
content: Now a day’s, technology is grooming very fast and every manual work is shifting to automation. For that purposes sometime, a developer required a higher hardware for testing purposes which his computer does not support and he does not afford to buy a system which fulfill his requirements to test the application. Sometime, a developer is currently using a window but he required Linux environment for his project but he does not want to destroy all his personal data from windows only for the purposes of Linux operating sys tem. Developer needs a set of software for development but he does not have time to install all the software on his system. So, we will develop a web application through which a developer or any other person can choose the hardware according to his require ment and select the operating system which he need for his virtual machine and he can also select the software which will be installed in his operating system.

heading: 1.5 Assumptions & constraints
content:  We assume that our user has an internet access to use our services.  We assume that user has information related to the virtual machines launch, so that he did not get panic in case of little delay.  We also assume that user has knowledge about the online payment method, so he can easily pay for our services.  Our system only allows 10 VM at a time due to lack of resources.

content: OpenStack glance has client -server architecture that provides us with the REST API through which we use to send requests to the server and actions can be performed. heading: 1.1 ABSTRACT
content: Drive N Deliver is an on-demand delivery network application designed to enable people to send/receive packages from one place to another. It also enables people to earn money while commuting on their destination. Furthermore, people who are transporters by profession or courier/freight delivery companies can use the application to further increase their customers.

heading: 1.2 INTRODUCTION
content: Drive N Deliver is a delivery network application designed to meet the needs of modern fast paced and comfort able lifestyle. The application allows anyone to send a package which can be small as an envelope and as large as furniture, from one location to another without having the need to move from the comfort of one’s home or where ever he may be at.  Transporters can view the package and offer to transport it to the desired destination. The sender/receiver must register with the application before being able to create a package for delivery, the transporter must also register with the application but for safety purposes they must provide scan of their driving license and registration information of their vehicle along with their other personal information. After the sender has gone through all the steps of creating a package in the application he can then view the estimate cost of the delivery. The package can then be viewed by all the transporter. The transporters will offer to transport the package, this offer will be sent to the sender who can then view the transporters profile, as there can be multiple offers the sender can choose one amongst them. Upon selection of the transporter by the sender, the transporter will arrive at the pickup point to get the package and will deliver the package at the set destination. The sender can also track their package while it  is in transit. If the sender wishes to cancel the package he must do it before the transporter arrives to pick up the package.

heading: 1.3 OBJECTIVES
content:  Allows people to make money while going on their daily commute as they may take up the role of the transporters.  This will help people save time and fuel. Instead of going to their nearest courier service outlet or for finding a transporter for large items such as furniture.  People who are transporters by profession can find work using this application  People will be able to send packages from anywhere without having the need to go to their nearest courier service shop.

heading: 1.4 PROBLEM STATEMENT
content: Nowadays people are becoming busier day by day, people cannot afford to waste time in small chores hence our application aims to provide on demand delivery service to people anywhere they may be. Also the cost of commuting is rising these days hence we aim to provide an opportunity to general populace to help them r educe their commuting expenses.

heading: 1.5.1 CONSTRAINTS
content: Few constraints of the system are listed below:  The Transporter needs to visit the company’s premises (to complete the registration process) one time before he can start using the application.  There is a chance that the transporter might run off with the package, for that we have safeguards which include getting official documents of the transporter before allowing him to use the application and doing a background check.

heading: 1.5.2 ASSUMPTIONS
content:  High Speed internet at least 3G is available to the users.  The User has an Android or IOS operating s ystem installed on his/her mobile device.   The Users phone has decent camera and has GPS tracking.

heading: 1.6 PROJECT SCOPE
content: The scope of this application is to provide a service where people who, want to send a package, can easily find people who are willing to pick up their package from desired location and deliver it to their respective destination. On the other side people who are commuting are provided an opportunity to cover their travel expenses.

heading: 2.1.1 Uber RUSH
content: This a delivery network designed for enterprises and small businesses who wish to deliver items to their customers. The drivers are ordinary people who are registered with Uber also known as Uber partners. Uber Rush partners either use cars or bicycles to deliver the packages; they provide live tracking so you know all the time where your package is. The model of Uber requires you to have a delivery partner who will confirm the delivery once the item is delivered to him. The pricing of delivery is based on zones, if the items are to be delivered in the same zone the delivery will have lower cost as compared to getting items delivered in other zones. Uber Rush does not support delivery of large packages as their partners struggle to deliver them.

heading: 2.1.2 Roadie
content: This a delivery network in which people create gigs to send items from one place to another, drivers are ordinary people who may deliver items to make extra cash while going on a trip or daily commute. This application is only meant for people to help cover so me of the cost of their transit not meant for peoples whose profession is courier services. The user starts by creating a package and drivers quote their fee for delivering the product, the drivers can have any type of vehicle hence packages of all size ca n be delivered. Roadie provides insurance coverage of any package sent using their application according to the packages value up to maximum of $500. Roadie also provides live tracking of delivery so that you always know where your package is.

heading: 4.1.3 User Creates Package

heading: 7.1 Problems faced & Lessons learned
content: 7.1.1 Problems Faced.  Limitations when using Google Maps API free version.  Online support for Ionic 3 is limited other than the documentation.  Pymongo the extension that is used for communication between the server and database lacks proper documentation.  Geolocation plugin of Cordova malfunctions subscribing for locations cannot be unsubscribed.  Frequently changing versions and documentation of tools used.

heading: 7.1.2 Lessons Learned
content:  Better to build a large scale app on a native platform rather than a hybrid one, as support for functionalities can be easily found on native platforms.  Use of tools and technologies that are mature and have a large online community.  Use of JSON based database only when handling data in bulk.  Rather than testing on a testing on local server, better to test on an online server from early on.

heading: Chapter 1: Introduction
content: There is a growing interest to develop cognitive virtual agents. In virtual environment, these agents are not only resembled to humans but also exhibit human -like behavior. Learning of these agents are quite different than the ways through wh ich humans acquire knowledge [1]. Most agents collect data from users and the environment and then implements efficient algorithms on collected data to infer knowledge [2]. In this methodology, a model  is trained and the trainer provides on-demand information to model through learning process. Trained model is used as a perceptual semantic capability of an agent. Machine learning differs from human learning because it requires an active social partner in learning environment. In virtual environment, an agent is able to interact with environmental objects and gather knowledge to differ between various objects. A trained model is able to simulate previously learned knowledge with current perspective [1]. For this purpose, a model is trained and used with middleware. Graph database is used to store semantics data with a set of training examples to infer cognition for knowledge representation. Whenever a robot will face an object,  it will perform detection by perceiving it and recognition by semantic knowledge. Perceptual semantics capabilities are essential to employ this kind of architecture in cognitive robots and it is a first step towards symbol grounding problem. It addresse s the problem that robots do not have to understand the language symbols objectively but they have to understand it subjectively and have to understand the meaning of symbol through semantics [3]. An agent will be able to recog nize the objects by identifying the meaning of symbols through perception and its features through semantic memory.

heading: Perceptual Memory:
content: Perceptual memory enables the robots to be kept simultaneity with the environment to obtain and sense new data and an ability to ground t he knowledge of given information through perception [4]. To perform these kind pf tasks, it is not feasible to establish predefined knowledge to anticipate all possible actions. Crangle and Suppes[5] introduced a model of language calibration to robot perception and steer to a symbolic model to conform grammar with semantics. The symbolic model links the actions and perception to meaning of discrete words. Afterwards, researchers have introduced comprehensive models to formalizing the meaning of terms [6], [7], verbs [8], and color names [9]. To allow the robot to interact with humans, it is necessary that they behave appropriately in different environments, to cope with changing tasks and environments and able to exhibit their intentions and motivations. A coupling of action and perception is needed to perform goal - oriented tasks [10]. It demands interpretation capabilities, reasoning capabilities, and planning capabilities. For storing and manipulating the environment, robot needs perceptual capability. The information that is gathered through is a key path for semantics learning in robotics.

heading: Semantic Memory:
content: Semantic memory contains data about articles, its highlights and connections. Semantic memory is sure to perceive and connect with objects. It has a place with the class of definitive recollections, wh ere the perceived objects are put away and can be proclaimed and recovered [11]. Semantic memory can tie the characterization of prepared information so information could be communicated through associations which helps in perc eiving different objects. Real part of this memory is to connect objects that show up in a similar environment [12]. Quillian proposed a model of semantic network which led to further researches in this domain. These networks are represented in graphs. Nodes of the graph specifies a concept and an association between them. Knowledge in a semantic network may be represented in a hierarchical form. In a hierarchical design, nodes at the bottom level inherit all the properties of the nodes at the upper level. The knowledge is important to accomplish tasks and retrieving facts [13]. Semantic memory is based on facts, word meanings, concepts and general world knowledge [14]. For example, a pen. A type of semantic information called conceptual knowledge [14]. A concept is a mental representation of something, e.g. a pen. Semantic memory can generalize knowledge gained based on presented training dat a. Thus the knowledge stored in semantic memory is used to perform and simulate different tasks in a given environment.

heading: Cognitive Robots:
content: The plan and improvement of psychological design is a dynamic region of subjective science, manmade brainpower, a nd cognitive robots [15]. Cognitive robots are clever and cerebrum motivated robots are equipped for recognition, derivation, and taking in the subjective systems of the mind[16]. Verifiably, subjective structures have been intended for three principle reasons: 1) to catch the human comprehension instruments, including the basic elements of control, picking up, thinking, discernment, memory and activity [17], 2) to shape t he premise to create psychological abilities over broadened timeframe, 3) to achieve human -level insight additionally called general manmade brainpower[18]. An abstract architecture of cognitive robot contains: a perception com ponent gathers all information through sensors to obtain the actions of user, a reasoning component updates the environment model and establishes methods to attain goals, an action component supervise the execution of actions, according to  current plans a nd goals, and learning component works in the background that records foreground activities and conceptualizes the experiences [10]. The outcomes of conceptualizations are stored in memory. There are many different cognitive ar chitectures such as ACT -R [19], SOAR [20], CLARION [21], the iCUB [22] etc. These agents have been tested on several cognitive tasks involving learning, reasoning, perception, recognition, and action execution [23], [24]. Cognitive architectures aimed to build and im plement the model of cognition and focuses on aspects concerning completeness, generality and to identify a standard model of mind [25]. Cognitive information provide models of information processing involved in perception and cognition. Cognitive robots tend to achieve their goals on the basis of learned knowledge through the process of perception and learning.

heading: Socially Interactive Robots:
content: Social interaction of human-robot is an important aspect in utilizing the use of robots. Interaction can be made in physical environment and virtual environment. In physical environment, human interacts with physical robot and a robot interacts with real world objects. In virtual environment, a virtual robot is modeled and human interacts wit h the robot in simulator and robot simulates the tasks and interacts with objects through interaction. These robots can be used as object avoidance, object picking and placing in industry. A robot avatar is a representation or a representative of human. Fo r example, a robot is intended to remote communication, it must act socially in order to efficiently convey message. These robot should have the capability to recognize conventions and contexts in order to be acknowledged as interaction associates [26]. If a robot is designed to learn about different objects, an agent must improve its knowledge to perform that task efficiently. Walter built the robotic tortoises in late 1940s [27]. These robots have headlamps attached at the positive and front phototaxis, the robots collaborated in a social manner even though there was no collective recognition and direct communication. Researchers explored the field of artificial life as stigmergy to enable incidental communication between robots through enhancements made to shared and common environment. It is used to achieve swarm or collective robot behavior. In early 1990s, Deneubourg and his co -workers launched the project on stigmergy in physical and simulated ant -like robots [28], [29]. Afterwards, researcher used these models for studying social behavior of insect robots [30]. Socially interactive and cognitive robots are import ant because they exhibit perceptual and recognition skills. heading: ROS:
content: Robot Operating System (ROS) act as middleware. ROS is freely available and open -source tool that provides strong features to develop robot applications. ROS framework belong from main framework that use for research and development purposes in robotics and running across worldwide in hundreds of thousands of robots. ROS major focus is on mobile robots. Physical location of mobil e robots is not fixed and these robots are capable to move around in their environment [38]. Mobile Robots also contains autonomous robots which means they are capable of moving in an environment without the need of electro -mechanical guidance devices or without any physical. ROS handle many use cases of robotic software development. ROS supports C, C++, C#, Python, JAVA. Graphs architecture is used to represent processes where all the processing has been done which held in nodes which can post, receive and control actuator, multiplex sensor, messages and planning. A message is published to topic s and subscriber to receive a message. It provides the capability of platform independence for developing ROS applications. ROS currently run on unix based platforms like Ubuntu. It also provides robot models, planning, simulation tools and various algorit hms. It provides tool to run and develop and make changes in its code even in multiple computers. ROS resembles to some extent with other robot frameworks such as MOOS, YARP, CARMEN, OCRA. ROS is divided into three levels of concept first is file system le vel, the computation graph level is second and third one is community level [38]. The ROS community level allow ROS user to exchange resources and software among community of ROS users. These includes Distribution, Repositories. The ROS wiki, bug ticket system and Mailing Lists.
