Industrial technology c onverging towards automation and an era of industry 4.0 has forced technological improvement and expansion, industries are moving towards complete automation  through Artificial Intelligence and Robotic . Automated palletization in the manufacturing industries is widely demanded. Pallets are used in industries for transport and shipping of goods. They are disposable and are thrown away when damaged or broken. Pallets may be of different sizes. A lot of loads can be transferred from one place to another on pallets quickly and efficiently [1]. Palletization is used for transport of goods or products on pallets from one place to another. As every robot is providing ease to humans, palletizing robots will also help humans in picking and placing of heavy and hard objects. The manual process of loading and unloading takes a large time and delays the production of a company, whereas, automated palletizing will be faster. Palletizing robots require certain essential tools such as dedicated offline - programming for effective use [2]. The offline -programming system requires a graphical simulation environment. The system should have kinematics model of the robot [3]. Object detection based palletizing application will allow robots to pick up the objects of interest from a conveyor using object detection algorithm. The robots will place the objects on pallets in sequence and proper position. Grippers of different dimension can be used on the robots for picking up the objects of varying dimensions. This document is divided in a number of sections. First section is about the collaborative robots, second chapter includes details of the project and the last discussion elaborates the work done in services syndicate.

In fact, collaborative robots are far different from industrial robots. Cobots are solid, lightweight an d nimble-fingered. Smart cobots can operate three times faster than today’s robots.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: In this project we will mainly focus on the working of collaborative robots. The objective of this project is to develop Object detection based palletizing application for collaborative robots that will help the Pakistani manufacturing companies to increase rate of work and productivity in less ti me, make progress in the world market and compete with the developing countries. It will also help to decrease human effort. It will save time and cost. Placing of product from one place to another will be more protected, easier and faster through collaborative robots. The Goal of our project is to make object detection based palletizing app which will be more accurate and fast in picking and placing objects on pallets, which will handle box sizes (length, width, and height), pallets size as we ll as boxes alignment on the pallet and the speed of conveyor. We want it to work faster and more accurate to compete with the world market. Accurate Object detection power of robot is also required.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: Palletizing and depalletizing are the one of main tasks performed in warehouses. The packing of every product may be different in an industry. The manual process of palletizing consumes a lot of time, human energy and cost. It also decreases the production rate of an industry to great extent. The industry requires an automation system which should perform the palletizing tasks for warehouses. The system should be able to palletize different objects according to their dimensions on respective pallets.

A graphic pattern system was introduced to store pattern, but it was so simple for complex pattern. A new plan is recommended for user-defined pattern for palletizing robot. In this method after producing user-defined pattern generatio n pattern reads user-defined files first, checks its overlapped part get the position for upper layer and generate pallet pattern. content: 3.2.1UR-Script In this module we learn about the UR-Script. UR-Script is a High-levelscript language developed by UR. It can be used instead of building program structure in the PolyScope GUI. It has similarities to Python script language. Script manual contains all available script codes. PolyScope programs are converted to UR-Script before execution. A number of potential approaches to using URScript. There are several ways to use UR-

heading: Script,
content: • Assignment: Assignment can return value to a variable. It Allows values returned to be viewed in variables window. • Script Code – Line: We can execute a single line of UR-Script. Variables define in script do not appear in variable window. Waypoints in script do not appears in graphic window. • Script Code – File: We can load and run an existing script file. We can execute multiple lines of script. We can insert three new script lines and save the file. • Calling functions: A function in script is declared as def. name (). A function can take argument and return processed argument. A function can be called multiple times within a program. We can make a simple function which adds two values and returns result. • Client Interfaces: In client interfaces script codes can be sent directly to the controller over Ethernet from an external machine. In this module we write a short UR-Script file that defines a function. Receives an argument and Processes the received value and Processes the received value. We load this file in a program and call function from assignment.

heading: 6 Chapter 6: Conclusion
content: In the previous we performed test cases of the application. The object of this chapter is to find the result after doing the project. The mainly focus will be on how project has been done, which problems comes during the project. We will provide an overview in the form of a summary and will also discuss on future work.

heading: 6.1 Problems faced and lessons learned:
content: As our project is related to the robotics, we required several collaborative robots for our project, but somehow, we manage resources. We could only access one UR5 robot provided by Services Syndicate Org. This was the only robot we had, so we have to use it carefully. Our team though did enough in the first phase of the project to complete the initials of the project. We have come to know by this project that how collaborative robots are useful in the industries of Pakistan. Pakistani industries are still lacking the technology and are bounded to industrial robots. The industrial robots are time consuming and hav e risk for hu man lives. Industry 4.0 offers great opportunities for innovative manufacturers, system suppliers.

heading: 6.2 Project summary
content: The Object detection based palletizing app is actually an effort for improving industries in Pakistan especially for those who are using industrial robots. The project is divided into two phases i.e. learning and implementation. In the learning phase, the Universal Robots training was completed. The Universals Robots training include two training sets i.e. Core training and Advan ce training. In the implementation phase, a desktop application is developed for managing the inventory warehouse through collaborative robots. The application can also be used for communication between the user and the robot. Each transaction is recorded in the database.

heading: 6.3 Future work
content: ODBPACR is just a beginning so industry 4.0 can be introduced in Pakistan. The project will be extended in the future. The future plan includes following components: • In the future, the project will include several collaborativ e robots that can communicate through sockets. • The pistons will be used for the motion of the robot. • The robots with respective payloads will be tested for huge warehouses. • Demos will be provided among industries for awareness purposes.

heading: Abstract
content: The aim of this project is to develop an automated programming assignment assessment system that can check Java Programming assignments. We have developed an assignment submission portal, on which Instructor and students registered themselves. An instructor creates a class and Students joins that class. Further, Instructor uploa ds an assignment which is solved by each student and submit it before the deadline. The assignment is then assessed by the Instructor. The assessment criteria in based on syntax checking, coding standards, plagiarism checker, execution time and testing by running it on different test cases. An instructor can also evaluate the assignment manually. After a successful evaluation, a report is generated. Furthermore, a separate question repository for each Instructor is also developed where a question along with their answer is stored for future use and it is updated each time teacher uploads a new question.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: With the emergence of technology, rapid progress taking place in every field including computer sciences. For the ease of mankind, this computerized innovation has brought a significant change in many areas including education. For saving time and effort, manual checking procedures and documentation have to replace by automation tools and systems. In the educational system, these tools and system serve in many ways like online documentation, filling forms, mathematical problems, and examine ass ignments etc (Ala -Mutka, 2005) [1] . Computer field like programming mostly contains coding assignments that must be evaluat ed on different criteria, which require a lot of time and effort. A practicable solution is the automation of the assessment system which includes assignment checking, plagiarism checking, code analysis, coding mistake analysis etc. [2].  In this project, our main purpose is to develop an online assessment system which helps students and teachers equally in educational life. In this project, we have developed a web application in which teacher creates a class and students join that class. For assignment te acher upload the assignment with its possible solution(s) and assignment deadline must be mentioned by the teacher before submitting the question. A student then tries to solve the assignment and uploaded their solution. After the deadline has been ended. The teacher has an authority to check the assignment by just clicking one button and all the assignment of whole class has been checked. Checking has been made on several bases,  First part is code analyzer that analyzes the code for the coding standards.  The Second part is the Syntactic Analyzer that checks the syntax mistakes.  The Third part is the Plagiarism checker  that checks all the plagiarism between assignments.  The Forth part is  the Compile and Run  that runs the assignment on different user defined test cases and give grades according to it.  The Fifth part is Execution Time Checking, it checks the total execution time of the assignments and gives grades according to the results.  Sixth and the last is Additional Marking Criteria’s, criteria like Number of for Loop, Number of Methods, Number of Objects etc.

heading: JASSY :: 15 |
content: After the completion of checking, a report has been generated in which each student assignment correction percentage along with each assignment plagiarism percentage has noted. And the grades\marks has been given according to it.

heading: 1.2 Objective
content: Followings are the Objective of our proposed project:  The main objective of this project is to develop an automated assessment system.  To saves a lot of teacher or instructor time, and there are fewer chances of mistake.  Through this Student learn good programming practices.  Different standard style guidelines are also guided to the student.  Style guidelines to check function length or naming conventions are part of this.  Syntax mistake are also analyzed and marks are given according to their importance.  Plagiarism is also being checked between assignments of students.  Report is generated with all the grades and mistake mentioned on it. We achieve all these objectives by designing these five main modules.

heading: 1.2.1 Coding Standards Checker
content: This module is used t o evaluate whether the assignment submitted by students are properly following java programming practices or not. It’s also helps students to learn good programming practices. Programming practices such as Code Indentation, Line Length should not be more than 80 Characters.

heading: 1.2.2 Syntactic Analyzer
content: This module is used to check whether the assignment submitted  by stu dent has no syntax error.

heading: 1.2.3 Plagiarism Checker
content: This module is used to check plagiarism, between the submitted assignments by the students. Though this module, Instructor will be able to check and visualize the similarity of the assignments.

heading: 1.2.4 Compile and Run
content: Checking of logic of program is almost impossible. So to assess and accurate distribution of marks we developed a Compile and Run or semantic checking module. In this module, we execute the student assignment by running it on 10 different test cases to make sure that assignment is 100% accurate.

heading: 1.2.5 Execution Time Checking
content: This module is designed to check execution time of an assignment semantically. It is also helpful to check whether there will be some infinite loop in program and stop s it’s accordingly. Its value should be near to that of Instructor program to ensure proper grading.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: Today’s era technological devices are used more than other devices. A Technical person uses technology to improve their life task. In a programming world, there are many problems that can be solved by programming. It’s all about the game of logic where a programmer faces a problem and solve his problem by progra mming. As learning perspective, the programmer must have to build their skills according to solve their problem. In this project, our problem is to provide a tools that help students to learn programming by their own mind’s logic, rather than plagiarize other programmer logic. This tool provides students to analyze their own sk ills, differentiate them from their past programming skill for solving their problem. As a teacher perspective, this tool helps a teacher to check assignments by one click as they can concentrate on preparing their lecture that deliver s to their student rather that concentrate how much assignment left for checking and take stress for checking assignments before deadlines. This system also saves the efforts and time for the teacher.

heading: 1.4.1 Assumptions
content:  Every user must have their electronic device like laptop, mobile.  Every device must have an active internet connection through which they can access the website.

heading: 1.4.2 Constraints
content:  User must belong to an institute where he learns java language and have a teacher and student relationship.  Users should have prior knowledge about usage of software.  Users should have a laptop or smart phone with active internet connection.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: The project scope statements discuss about the deliverables and tasks necessary  for functionality of the project. It  provides the outline of the project and define where project is not covering their scope. Its scope was defined by extensive requirement gathering. All collected requirements are then analyzed carefully. After prudently analyzing we made Project scope. The project statement contains components which is describe below:

heading: 1.5.1 Coding Standards Checker
content: To correctly evaluating the assignments, we developed Coding Standards Checker. This is a syntactic analyzer that tokenized the assignment code and with the help of an open source tool we examine the code for different programming practices and guidelines violations. For this we used many books and research paper especially the Book “Java: How to Program”. Guidelines are th en finalized by proper meeting held with our supervisor. Then we

heading: JASSY :: 17 |
content: implemented these guidelines and practices as conditions or checks in an open source tool “CheckStyle”.

heading: Include Exclude
content: Only for Java Language. Not for any other programming language except java.

heading: Technique Used:
content:  Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).  Regex Patterns.  Tokenization. Other techniques like String matching or other advanced techniques were not used.

heading: 1.5.2 Syntactic Analyzer
content: For uniform checking and proper grading, we developed Syntactic Analyzer. This is a syntactic analyzer that checks the code for some syntax mistake. For that we compile the code. If the code is compiled successful, then it is ready for our next module i.e. Compile and Run. On the other hand, if it is not successfully compiled then the marks are deducted accordingly.

heading: Technique Used:
content:  Compilation through ‘javac’ command in shell_exec method  in php. No other way to compile it.

heading: 1.5.3 Plagiarism Checker
content: Plagiarism is not allowed. For its prevention and equal grading, we developed a module, in this we first tokenized the source code. Then we used a string searching algorithm known as Rabin–Karp String Search algorithm. This algorithm is used to find the similarity between all the source codes. Report is generated after evaluating the results.

heading: Include Exclude
content: Rabin Karp Search String Algorithm is used to detect plagiarism No other algorithm except for Rabin Karp string search algorithm.

heading: Technique Used:
content:  Only String Search algorithm is used. No other type of algorithm is used like copy paste detection algorithm.

heading: 1.5.4 Compile and Run
content: Compile and Run on test cases is our main module because it executes the program by executing on different test cases. Test cases should be provided by the Instructor. Total of 10 Test Cases should be uploaded by the Instructor. Test Cases should cover all scenario. It is the main module that ensure quality in code.

heading: Include Exclude
content: Input can only be given through file. Other way to give input to program except from file. Checking the output of the program. Checking of the program internal structure. For Java Language only. Designed for other programming language. Output is only through file. Other way to receive output from program other than file. Grades are assigned after evaluating the program on its output. Grades are assigned after comparing it with Instructor Solution.

heading: 1.5.5 Execution Time
content: We developed this module to check the execution time of the assignments. It is helpful in identifying unconditional infinite loop which is only eating up  server’s memory and  the clock time while execution the code. After identifying , corrective actions were taken to save the server from crashing. This module also includes comparing the student’s assignment execution time with the Instructor Solution.

heading: Include Exclude
content: Total program execution time is calculated. Individual parts or method execution time is calculated.

heading: 1.6 Tools
content: We used following technologies and tools for our project.  REST (Representational State Transfer):  It describe how system inter communicate with other systems. It can be any like XML, JSON or plain text. But it should be same in the whole application. It is not some service; it is a design concept.  MongoDB Database:  MongoDB stores data in very flexible, JSON or XML type documents, and its data structure can be changed any time. It is document oriented database.  HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language):  it is a set of mark -up tags that is inserted in .html file for display in World Wide Web. We used HTML to build basic structure of our application.

heading: JASSY :: 19 |
content:  CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): CSS is a mechanism to add style like font size, font style to HTML tags to alter the appearance of web sites. heading: 2.1 Existing System Study
content: 1. A successful effort made by authors of Dept. of Computer Science University of Liverpool in modeling and construction A Semi -Automated Approach to Online Assess ment of programming assignment [3] . Which include submission of assignments, Testing, Style Analysis, and Report Generator. It doesn’t have any interface for assignment submission, they use simply by emailing the assignment. And there is no  syntax checker component and class diagram comparison. [3] 2. A noticeable effort made by computer scientists from University Teknologi Malaysia in which they develop a semi -automated grading system for assignment assessment. It compiles the code and give the output whether it is correct or incorrect but it doesn’t have any syntax checker, coding standards checks. It only compiles the code and run it on the test cases provided by the teacher. [5] Basic Architecture is show in Figure 2.1.1. Figure 2.1.1 - JAssess and Moodle Framework [5] 3. A successful effort made by computer scientist of, Wee-Chong Oonc Dept. of Computer Science, National University of Singapore. They develop the system that check plagiarism between assignments. They also added query hogging e.g. First Come First Serve. Drawbacks are that the For assignment checking the question should be straight forward and simple, and solution must be same as that of teacher solution. It also can not handle Extreme Cases well. [6] 4. Another attempt to use E-Assessment for assignment checking is developed by Fatima Al Shamsi and Ashraf Elnagar from Computer Science Department, University of Sharjah. They developed a graph -based grading system for java assignment named, eGrader. It Check the syntax, compiles the code, run it on test cases and generate the report. It doesn’t have any coding standards checker. [4] Phases is shown is Figure 2.1.2

It only checks the syntax mistake. And instant feedback is provided to student. [7] 6. BOSS is another open source system created by master minds of University of Warwickto the Mike Joy, Nathan Griffiths and Russell Boyatt which checks java programming assignments. Its many versions are available online. BOSS includes two paradigms of testing. First is available to student at submis sion time which helps them by providing immediate feedback. Second mode is post submission report. It consists of three users, one is student, second is Instructor and third is course manager. heading: 3.3 Software Development Lifecycle Model (SDLC)
content: Software Development Life Cycle are methodologies used to develop the high-quality software that fulfill the user expectations, or become a successful system. SDLC can choose based of system context. There are many types of SDLC process models that define the life cycle of the system, names are given below: 1. Water Fall Model: Water Fall Model is used when requirements are clearly defined and does not need any further changing

heading: 2. Rapid Prototyping Model: Rapid Prototyping Model is used when requirements are
content: unstable or not clearly defined.

heading: 3. Incremental Model: Incremental Model is used when basic functionalities of the
content: system are known but requirements can change over time. 4. Spiral Model: Spiral Model is used when cost and risk evaluation is important. 5. Agile Model: Agile Model is used when the customer’s requirements are not clearly defining enough information and require some functional requirement ready in less than three weeks. The best suitable SDLC for this project is Rapid Prototyping Model.

heading: 3.3.1 Rapid Prototyping Model
content: According to project “JASSY” the most appropriate model is Rapid Prototyping Model. The reasons behind choosing this model is given below:  The prototype demonstrates the problem and suggest solution and improvement.  Supervisor give corrective feedback.  When the Supervisor is satisfied, the prototype is used built for the final product.  Provide a more accurate end product  Interaction with the prototype stimulates awareness of additional needed functionality

heading: Chapter 4 – System Design
content: System Design is the phenomena of defining components of a system like architecture, its interfaces, modules which is based upon on the specific requirements.  It is the process of outlining, developing, planning systems which satisfies the specific needs and requirements. It consists of multiple components like class diagram, data flow diagram, activity diagram, sequence diagram etc.

heading: 4.1 Software Architecture
content: System architecture translates the logical design of a system into a physical structure that includes hardware, software, network support, and processing methods. We have used Client Server Architecture shown in Fig. 4.1.1 for centralized backup, remote access, better and enhanced reliability. Higher level Software Architecture of your application is shown in Fig. 4.1.2 Figure 4.1. 1 – Client Server Architecture of JASSY Figure 4.1. 2 – High Level Software Architecture of JASSY

heading: 6.1   Problem faced and lessons learned
content: We have faced some problems during requirement gathering, designing, implementation, and testing. Some problems are also occurred due to lack of coordination and management. Some are listed below. 1. A lot of work is already done on this project, which is quite difficult for us to differentiate our project with others. To counter that problem we have done an extensive literatur e review. More than 100 research papers were reviewed by us in order to find out their functionality and how to make our project is different from others. 2. Finalizing the requirements, is one of the major problems we faced because this field is very vast and covering all the paths and possibilities is not possible so we first covers the most important features and leave others to future work. 3. Selecting right back end and front end technologies was a major problem we faced. Decide whether to use SQL or No-SQL is one of them. And same for backend technology whether to use java, dotnet or PHP as server side language. And if PHP, then which framework is more suitable for development. After analysing all possibilities, we find Laravel(PHP Framework) and mongodb is the best combination to work with. 4. During the designing the interface, the right choice of content and colour scheme matters a lot. We considered many design and colour scheme and then choose the best one out of them. 5. Division of work is another problem, all of the group members wanted to learn new technologies. To cater that problem we consult our supervisor, he decided to assigned work to each project member according to their expertise and skill level in that particular field. In the end we easily integ rated all the developed components to become whole system. 6. While developing Standards Checking module, selecting the right one source library is the most important decision, we have 3 open source tools to check standards in code. But only one of them is ex tendable so we choose that because we have to add some additional standards or checks. 7. While responding to the student request of joining in class, our ajax is not working properly. We have checked the code multiple times everything is perfect but record f rom database is not updated. We have posted in stackoverflow but none of the answer has solved that problem so we had to changed the technique. 8. Properly integrating project is also a problem because all we are working one different module at a same time, so we used proper versioning control so that if some error occur by any member code, we can switch back to previous version.

heading: 6.2   Project Summary
content: The aim of this project is to develop an automated programming assignment assessment system that can check Java Programming assignments. We have developed an assignment submission portal, on which Instructor and students registered themselves. An instructo r creates a class and Students joins that class. Further, Instructor uploads an assignment which is solved by each student and submit it before the deadline. The assignment is then assessed by the Instructor. The assessment criteria in based on syntax chec king, coding standards,

After a successful evaluation, a report is generated. Furthermore, a separate question re pository for each Instructor is also developed where a question along with their answer is stored for future use and it is updated each time teacher uploads a new question.

heading: Abstract
content: In this age of internet and technology, e -commerce has flourished with leaps an d bounds. Currently in Pakistan it’s on the rise but still not yet earning the trust of the online users. Our idea stems around using e -commerce to further empower the young entrepreneur and to showcase their designing talents  but also providing an electronic commerce website that is safe and trustworthy. The theme of the project is to create an online print -on-demand marketplace where different will make use of an online creative canvas to design customized Cotton tee-shirts , mugs and leather shoes and sell these products on the website via a mini -store that will be connected to the users account. The idea will allow the users to create customized shirts, mugs , leather sanda ls (traditional footwear) via our site. The options for customization would include colors, design, type of leather (simple, suede, skin) etc.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: With the advancement in the internet technology, the methods to make internet for useful for human life have also increased with the field of e-commerce being one of the major working fields in the past few years. A lot of work has been done to improve the online shopping facilities and to earn the trust of the customers. In Pakistan, E-commerce is still taking its baby steps. The general trust of the users has increased but this field is still devoid of innovation as we see similar web-stores like Daraz, Homeshopping [1] and Shophive [2] which don’t allow much customization and innovation. The Pakistan Government has also taken encouraging steps to help the e-commerce business as the foreign investors are allowed to invest up to 100% in the online businesses and the e-commerce sector is heavily backed as it brings a lot revenue in the country. In Pakistan, the field of e-commerce has been constantly improving and the general know-how has also improved as e-commerce has also been added as part of the curriculum. In 2016 according to strong estimates and research the e-commerce revenues in Pakistan stood around $120 Million dollars [3] with major stores and small scale facebook stores have all played a part in this figure. Large e-commerce companies like Yayvo and others have shown an estimated 300% growth annually [4] So, just like the rest of the world with good innovation and great ideas the e-commerce field in Pakistan is a very fruitful area of investment. Graphics designing is a field that is one of the major earning fields in the freelancing industry. But due to highly saturated market, many talented and creative designers are not making enough use of their skills. Our idea is to make a platform that uses e -commerce to help these designers be entrepreneurs on their own and sell thei r designs. Designers would be able to use our website to design Tee -shirts, mugs and chappals on this platform, sell these products and earn valuable re venues and make a mark on the industry. This project uses this platform of e -commerce and incorporates it with the ever-growing fashion industry by developing a  website that has allowed our users to design teeshirts by uploading their designs/images. heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: The main idea for this project is to allow talented and creative graphics designers to design merchandise such as t-shirts, mugs and other products on the website via on-site design platforms with the goal to empower these designers and allow them to earn by selling their creative art-works in the shape of the above mentioned products. The freelancing market is highly saturated and this project should allow the designers another way of making an earning and a name for themselves and their creative art-work. Each seller/Designer should have their own storefront on the website with a name of their store and the products will be added through the design platforms for tee-shirts, mugs, chappals. A seller can also edit and change the outlook of their store however they want. The mission and motivation behind our work is to make a fraud-proof platform where sellers can design and sell their artwork in the form of these products by using our on-site design platforms that will be easy to use and design on, and buyers can search quality products, designers and sell these products. The production of these designs will be handled by the staff and not the designers as they only have to design. At the end of a month, the designers will be able to withdraw their profits via a secure payment gateway. The focus would be to provide the entrepreneurs and designers a chance to showcase their creativity and make profitable use of the talents. Our website will serve not only as a customizable merchandise panel but would also have the functionalities of a complete e-commerce site.

heading: 2.1.1 Websites:
content: GearBubble [5]: This is a website that allows you to upload your t-shirt designs(.png) on the website and then open a mini- web store to further sell these shirts/designs. It allows users to sell high quality products such as necklaces, shirts, bracelets, hats, beanies, hoodies, cups, smart phone cases etc. GearBubble is a print-on- demand company with major focus on tee-shirts and western clothes. In contrast the focus of this project is on traditional footwear and local designers as websites such as GearBubble are mainly saturated with the US community, as according to official stats, GearBubble attracts 43.7% of its visitors from the United States of America, followed by Australia with 10.6%. [6] So there is a void in the market in regards to the demographics and this projects aims to bridge that gap by providing print-on-demand and footwear customization options to the local community. If we look into further statistics of gearbubble, we will also realize that there is a lot of scope for such websites and apps in the market as according to website outlook the overall worth of gearbubble.com is $67,000. According to gearbubble itself, the service has so attracted over 1,000,000 customers, and more than 100,000 users have sold their designs while the company claims they have paid about 15M+ to these sellers.

heading: Teespring [7]:
content: Teespring is another print-on-demand website where users can search, buy and sell customized t-shirt designs and earn profits at the ease of the arm chair. They like Gearbubble also focus on western products and aim to empower the users to design and sell the products they want to and love. Very similarly to Gearbubble, the major share of users of Teespring comes from United States of America with 51.7% [8] of the website traffic comes from the states followed by United Kingdom. The amount of traffic coming from Pakistan on these websites is very small and almost ignorable. Hence, a void that can be filled with a locally based platform. NIKEid [9]: Nike is one of the world’s biggest manufacturer of sportswear and sports shoes.This platform by nike was developed to boost the company’s sales and profits by allowing the customers to design customized Nike shoes. There products involve different materials, designs, colors and innovations (newer technologies). Nike id is an online platform that allows the users to make customized Nike shoes while paying a premium fees to acquire the service at the first place.

heading: 5.1 Problems faced and lessons learned:
content: This project has served as our first experience of developing a professional product. So many of the issues, delays and problems we faced were down to lack of experience and professionalism. Once the research and analysis phase was done, the amount of time required to get the developing phase done was undermined by us and due to own underestimation, the time constraints affected our progress. Some of the customization features of chappals discussed in the proposal was later omitted as the real-life production turned out to be unrealistic. A lot of professional development learning has been done by all of us as individuals and this project has honed our web development and design skills. We have learnt a lot more about the software engineering processes and the ways and standards implied while analyzing and planning a professional software product. Time management is one of the biggest lessons that we have learned from this project and the lessons from this project will continue to guide us in our future and always be a shining light as to how to manage projects in the professional world.

heading: 5.2  Project Summary:
content: This project has been carefully thought upon for the purpose of empowering the many talented graphics designers to allow them an online platform on which they can earn by selling their designs in the form of merchandise. The website project will allow designers to use an on-site designing platform to design tee- shirts, mugs and leather footwear; set their price and sell to customers on the website. Throughout our requirement analysis phase we have carefully defined our goals and objectives to make sure a fraud-proof production-on-demand website can be created which an empowering tool for the entrepreneurs and an easy to use platform for the novice user.

heading: Abstract
content: With the speedy invention in the computerized technology there was a need of having all such innovations to be gathered at a single place. For this purpose, a new technology was introduced named as Internet of Things (IoT). This emerging technology (IoT), can be someone having a small gadget implanted in the body, a farm animal with a biochip in it, or a car with implanted sensors to aware the driver when tire pressure is below the level, or any other object that may be assigned by an IP address and a power  is provided to transfer information over a network. (IoT) can play a vital role in the health. Health is one of the most important factors for every person and in order to maintain the good health exercise is the key. Therefore, every person requires doing specific amount of exercise  on daily basis which may vary  on the basis of age and health conditions of individuals. This exercise also includes daily life activities. Only if we can get the amount of the exercise from or daily activities we can assure that we have achieved our daily goal. With the help of IoT we can monitor our daily activities by implanting wearable’s and sensors where needed. We are developing an activity based smart health management system using (IoT) which will use the data from wearable’s and extract the amount of exercise from it. Then using it this data will be transmitted to android apps which is connecting the user and doctor. Doctor can prescribe him medicines after checking his performance. We also have an additional service of hiring a physician who can check his diets plans and all other routine body changes. The user will also get notification on his smart phone of his goals and his daily achievements either they are fulfilled or not. Whereas the doctor and physician are also  notified about their patient’s progress.  Every new order by the doctor  and nutritionist will also be notified. heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Good health is the real jewel of the world which can lead us to every luxury of life; it’s the real possession of a man. The famous Dalai Lama explained the importance of health as he was asked about the most surprising thing of the humanity his reply was “A man sacrifices his health to make money and then he spends all this to recuperate his health. Man is always worried about his future instead he forgets the joy of present, and at the end he does live nor in present neither in future. And he lives thinking that he is never going of die but all in vain he dies having really never lived.” That all concluded was that first wealth is always health. A healthy life can be obtained by exercise which reduces the risk factors of many chronic diseases like heart failure, diabetes, stress and obesity. Exercise would also reduce economic burden of one’s family by reducing risks of lifestyl e disorders. People have a misconception that exercise is done by only going to fitness centres but that is wrong. Our body performs exercise by our daily routine too. As the modern era is affecting our lives too much, so in order to track those actions an d routines we are developing an application that would be calculating the amount of exercise done by user’s body. Our major focus on exercise was due to its benefits not in terms of that it gains or pumps up your muscles but it also improves one’s mental h ealth. Following are the benefits that exercise can give are: o These days the routines are getting tough and tough day by day so the people are mostly facing from stress and they cannot focus on their health so for such people exercise is the key to get relief from their stress. It increases norepinephrine a chemical that moderates the brain against stress.  o Exercise releases endorphins which create happiness and euphoria.  o More and more exercise increases cells in hippocampus which is responsible for memory and learning.  Page 10 of 86 o Brain releases dopamine in return to any form of pleasure like sex, drug addiction. Exercise can help us to recover quickly and can distract drug addicts.  o No need of sleeping pills now even for the people suffering with insomnia, a moderate workout can do it for you.  o The more intense you do a physical activity the more you burn your calories and can easily control your weight. Consistency is the key.  Regular exercise helps you to fight against health conditions and diseases. And you ca n be an inspiration for many others. Some facts and figures provided by the World Health Organization about different age factors are: People aging 5–17 needs to do exercise for at least an hour with full intensity physical activity daily. Such activities or exercises should be taken in a free oxygen environment. High intensity exercises should be given a higher priority, in addition to all those that increases muscle and bone strength at least thrice a week [1]. People aging between 18 and 64 should do a m inimum of a 2.30 hours of medium power free oxygen exercise in a complete week or have to perform 1.15 hours of a high vigour exercise in a week or should be doing both activities simultaneously for much better results. Such exercises that are done for lun gs and hearts should be done in sets of 10 minutes. For gaining plus points/advantages, adults should increase their normal level exercise to 5 hours a week, or don a forceful exercise for 2.30 hours a week. Muscle should be strengthened by involving special exercises daily [2]. People aging greater than 65 should do at least 2.30 hours’ low intensity exercise in a week, or at least 1.15 hours of a vigour exercise or if stamina is in a good condition then must do both of them. Oxygen free activities must be performed in sets [3]. Considering these factors, we felt that we people are not up to the mark. IOT connects real physical devices or objects to the internet. Devices can be accessed anywhere in the world when they are digitally connected with an internet server. The basic idea of IOT is to collect data and transferring it to the server from the devices having IP addresses. This technology of accessing the real objects helps them to interact with the external environment.  IOT is the evolutional force whi ch allows any company to obtain Page 11 of 86 high performance with the help of analytical analysis and security with improved results. Growth and data association has made things and connections important by creating business and industrial opportunity to the world. That’s why we are aimed that our user should complete its exercise and for this we are using (IoT) as it became mature by the junction of electromagnetic wave technologies, (MEMS), micro servers and cyberspace networks. So we are developing an activity based smart health management system using (IoT) which is to monitor the exercise routine of the patient. It consists of such ware outs which would be examining the patient on the basis of its regimen (a course of medical treatment prescribed by his m edical practitioner). It has three  major modules, First module is based on (IoT) which consists patient module that will record the person’s routine who with the help of the sensors attached on our wearable gadget . These sensors will be departed at his body parts,  or some of the utensils he would be using daily and at the end module will calculate some values from the body. Then will transfer those values to our android app. We will create an algorithm which will be computing those values and then converting them into some points. These point are now the target that is achieved by the individual. These routines would be transferred to  the respective doctor(optional) and physician. They can communicate to their patients and as well as guide him in their medicines or diet plans. Second module is the doctor’s module. Now the patient is always connected to his doctor who is maintaining a complete check on him. Doctor can also monitor his daily routine and can directly make contact to his patient. The doctor will be prescribing medicines or edibles to the patient. He would also be responsible of verifying and approving the diets suggested by the physician . Our android application is simply creating a window between a health oriented personnel and a doctor. Our app is crea ting users interest through a type of  co channel communication encouraging to fulfil the target prescribed by his medical practitioner. Initially we are concerning about the daily routine of our user and specially the exercise he did while its body did during his hectic routine. Now if he is not moving enough to complete his target our app will be providing his serious alerts on the notification. Same on the other hand if he is moving sufficiently our app will generate such interesting alerts on the notification bar that he will keep keen interest to complete the target assigned by his doctor. Page 12 of 86 Third module is the physician’s module. Now this is the main person who is always connected to the patient. We can say a physician is compulsory for the person willing to use our application. Physician will be viewing patient’s daily goals achieved and his  total calories burnt for the day and how many steps he took. The most interesting thing we got is that physician can also view either patient has hired a doctor or n ot. If yes, then every diet prescribed by him will be forwarded to the doctor for approval. If no, the diet recommended will be sent directly to the patient and he/she will be notified about the change in plan. Physician is also responsible of updating the goals of his respective patients and no approval is required for this update/process. Now all we are talking about the target is that it will be settled into as 100 points on the patient module and the sensors or the ware outs having an eye on his body m ovement will help us to extract some values from them as to calculate either the mark is achieved or not. The user can also enter his daily edibles which would help the doctor to understand his current condition. Another facility provided by us will be a c heck up on medication. User has to check on the medicine checkbox and if he fails to do this our app will provide a notification to the user. This information is also transferred to the doctor who will also help the doctor in reviewing his recovery status.  At the end of the day user will be enjoying a happy and a healthy life.

heading: 5.1 Sensing Unit
content: In this section we are discussing about all the sensors used in our activity monitoring device which will help us to collect data about the total steps taken by the user and their heartbeat at every moment they are wearing the device.

heading: 5.1.1 Pulse Sensor
content: This sensor as visualized in (figure 5.1)  has a simple phenomenon transmitting signal at Tx and receiving them at Rx node. This sensor is attached to the A0 node of the Arduino pro mini.

heading: 5.1.2 Accelerometer
content: Figure 5.2 is a small and the first world motion tracking device that can work on low power, low cost and high performance. This device works with the combination of 3 -axis we can say it gyroscope as well. We are taking data from it on the basis of x-axis.

heading: 5.2 Local Processing Unit
content: In this section all those things are explained which will receive and computer the values transferred from the sensor.

heading: 5.2.1 Arduino Mini Pro
content: Figure 5.3 is a board which was developed for the products that required less space and more efficiency. This board has 6 PWM pins. From which we use A4 to connect with SCL pin of the MPU 6050 and A5 was used to connect with the SDA pin of the MPU 6050. Both sensors were giving data to this board and then this board was responsible of sending this data through Bluetooth module. Its 3 pin was receiving commands from Bluetooth and 2 was to transmit through module. A0 pin was used to connect Heart Rate Sensor to connect to the board. This bo ard is designed to work on two voltages 3.3V and 5V. We are using 5V model.

heading: 5.3 Wireless Data Transmitting Unit
content: In this section we have explained the module which would transmit data from the monitoring device to the mobile application.

heading: 5.3.1 Bluetooth Module
content: Figure 5.4 is our data transferring module, now discussing the two edges of the module which are not being used in our project are one at the lower corner is of an LED pointing towards pin 32 claiming it is on or not. And the other one is for returning the module to its default module or state, in short it is about resetting to default.  Now coming towards the top most ping used is for receiving function of Bluetooth module the second one to this is the sender point of the signals emitting from module. Third one is the ground pin of the module and last one is the live terminal of the Bluetooth module which requires (3.6v - 6v). This module charter to act like after every second and does not wait for any AT command. So in this manual configuration is quite impossible.  The receiver pin of the module connects to the 3rd pin of the Arduino mini pro and the transmitter pin is connected to the 2nd pin of Arduino.

heading: Notation
content: BPMN was a project by Business Process Management Initiative (BPMI) group and was maintained under Object Management Group, both groups introduced BPMN first back in 2005. Its other version 2.0 was introduced back in 2011 which was more refined and was capable  of defining the semantics and logics more precisely. Diagramming elements were also introduced. The logic behind is same as of flowcharts and activity diagrams  [8]. A Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) can give businesses with the potential of understanding their internal business procedures during a graphical notation and can offer organizations the flexibility to speak these procedures during a standard manner. So BPMN helps in understanding the collaborations of transactions and other processes that are initiated or being run in the system. This also helps technical, business and lay users to understand the system visually and to all those who can’t understand coding can understand any flaw in the system using diagrams and visuals.  This is to  make sure that businesses will perceive themselves and participants in their business and can modify organizations to regulate to new internal and B2B business circumstances quickly [9]. So we have focused on the latest version of BPMN launched which is named as BPMN 2.0. Here are some visuals of our very own project. Page 79 of 86

heading: 8.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: Main problem faced during the project was connectivity of Android application to smart gadgets. System wants the users to have access to their doctors wherever and whenever they wish. In earlier times the only solution was connecting the devices to the server and then communication will be performed. There were multiple solutions to this problem i.e. using servers, API’s or internet. Finalized solution was that we will use some API’s to perform communication of the gadget with the android system and then will the help of internet two or more android platforms will communicate. We learned many new things which we never experienced e.g. working on new API’s, gadget connection with android, android studio for creating android application, android to android communication.

heading: 8.2 Project summary
content: A prolonged way in a remarkably short time has been completed in the history o f android utility development. Where a  cellular device has become a help ing hand for human being in terms of smart applications. Health monitoring is one of the killer programs available on the cell devices. Consequently, this report proposes for an application which lets in specifying your daily progress about the amount of exercise done by its users that they did in their hectic routine. The application is cost effective and needs to require an additional gadget. The application runs on a single cellular accompanying with the gadget to monitors the daily activities and goals achieved by its patients and the alert messages or reports are sent to their respective physicians. We also have an interesting feature that with compulsory physician our patient also has an option of hiring a doctor.  Here the doctor can review recommend m edicine approve diets to the patients . But the goals recommendations and diet plans are only told by the physician.  As a result, this proposed system permits patients and their doctors to communicate on the android system by staying at their own places. The general evaluation result is that the device proved to be dependable as to monitors someone’s health conditions and directly send them to his doctors and physician. Page 84 of 86

heading: Abstract:
content: This project is basically based on a game where we are focusing on developing a 3D racing car game. This game would cover implementation of real-time graphics and physics engine. This game would provide a free and outclass entertainment to the people of all age group. The Project also aims to inspire game developers to develop real time games. This game would be totally developed using latest technologies and tools for excellent support and results.

heading: 1.1  Introduction:
content: Since the time that the gaming industry evolved in the world, large portions of game developers stepped up and developed enormous amount of games belonging to different categories . Categories incorporate action, racing, shooting. Gaming platforms such as Windows, Android, iOS and so on really urged individuals to amuse themselves using their cell phones and personal computers. Features that user prefer in a well-built game would be implemented in this game. This project is basically based on a game where we are focusing on developing a 3D racing car game. This game would cover implementation of real -time graphics and physics engine. This game w ould provide a free and outclass entertainment to the people of all age group. The Project also aims to inspire game developers to develop real time games. This game would be totally developed using latest technologies and tools for excellent support and r esults. The target audience of this game will be children; however, anyone can play it as it will be free of cost for the people. We plan to keep those features that users (or gamers) would generally like in a well-built game. The game features are discussed below:

heading: 1.2 Game Features
content: Game features are discussed below:  You can select Car of you own choice.  Multiple racing tracks would be available.  Score and time would be recorded.  Real time Street design would be provided for racing.  Tournament would be available to play.  You can use Nitro to boost your car during race and would collect that too.  A free mode would also be available to roam your car around.  Upgradation of your car.  Collection of points to unlock newer events.

heading: 1.3 Steps of development:
content: Primary of all, we need will visit a few roads Also detract pictures for them. After that we plan to implement the design of roads in our game track. Design of our game include:  Modelling of Objects and Environment  UV Mapping

heading:  Creating Textures
content:  After outlining the game, we’ll script the game design and will make it playable. This methodology will incorporate coding. This will permit us to characterise different controls for the user gameplay.  After proper testing the game will be available on the Android play store for free.

heading: 1.4  Objectives:
content:  Most games that are currently available provide side camera view. We tend to give game players a front view of the game which would enhance the gameplay.  We tend to provide less or no advertisement as that would annoy the user.  Gameplay and graphics  of the game must be  really good i.e. graphics like scorecard, time should not take too much space on the screen.  Push gaming industry over Pakistan.  Provide a real-life time domain/environment of gaming.  Make this game free. It should be a source of free and good entertainment for the people.  This car racing game would help the automobile industry of Pakistan to flourish.

heading: 1.5  Problem Statement:
content: To make a car racing  game that actually depicts the real time street environment and provides a good gameplay experience.

heading: 1.4.1    Assumptions:
content:  The game will be able to charm more users due to its astounding graphics and user friendly interface.  The game will provide a good gameplay experience.

 The  game would not be only for particular age group as it would target all groups of audience i.e. adults, children etc.  The game should be bug free and shouldn’t crash.  The game is good enough to compete with other related games on the Play store.

heading: 1.4.2. Constraints:
content:  As there are various vendors of related games so advertising our game would be one of the constraint.  Developing good 3D models of cars will be challenging.  Providing a good and real-time  gameplay experience would be difficult.  As the development team is small, so this might delay the completion of the game.

heading: 1.7  Project Scope:
content: In the world of game development, this project focuses to design and implement a car racing game that would be based on real time street environment .This project of us would help to promote the game development in Pakistan. Today, developing game and then launching it on play store is very necessary as it implements everything from designing an environment to coding it and have a hands-on experience of game development.

heading: 1.8  Tools and Technologies:
content:  Unity 3D will be used for developing the game  Blender or 3ds Max for designing cars and environments.  For UML diagrams we will use MS Visio  C# will be used for coding.

heading: 2.1  Literature Review:
content: The purpose of this game is to motivate and inspire other game developers in Pakistan. A detailed analysis was done on the existing games relevant to the racing category. These games are available on Google Play Store. The purpose of this analysis was to have appropriate ideas of how should a game’s design must be and what sort of gameplay attracts the users. These games are mentioned below: CSR Racing [1] provides a very good experience but user can only control the throttle and gear shift. User doesn’t have steering control of the car as that game only supports drag racing. Dr. Driving [2] also have a fine gameplay in which you have to follow the directions and avoid Collison. Driving School 2016 [3] is the game where you can learn to drive different kind of vehicles i.e. cars, trucks and buses. This allow you to play with manual transmission with clutch and shift stick. CarX Drift Racing [4] gives you a unique simple experience in handling sports car, in this you use separate handbrake button to start drifting and burn tires doing donuts. Our game will focus on the front view and a better gameplay. STAKEHOLDER’S

heading: 2.2  REQUIREMENTS ELICITATION:
content: Vertex Racing is a game that is designed to provide a real life time environment of gaming. The requirement specification of this project is classified into functional and non-functional requirements. As the game is played by a player or a user, so the player or user will be our actor here. A list of the functional and non-functional requirements is discussed below:

heading: 2.2.1  FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
content: FR01: Choose Between different menus
Player selects between Play, Options and Quit.
Play menu will take the user to the next menu i.e. Select Car.
In Options menu. The user will be able to adjust the display and volume settings.
The user will quit the game by clicking Quit. FR02: Select car
The player selects a car of his/her own choice to play.
Car’s attributes such as speed, handling, brakes etc. will be displayed FR03: Select Racing Track
Our game also provides an opportunity to the player select the race track of his/her choice. FR04: Select Mode
Game provides two modes i.e. Racing Mode and Roam Around Mode. He/she can select mode of his/her own choice.
The Racing Mode will allow the user to race against some opponents. The opponents will be BOTS not other users.
The Roam Around Mode will allow the user to freely ride his car on the streets. FR05: Manoeuvring of the Car
The player can manoeuvre the car using certain controls depending on the platform he’s using to play the game.
On Windows platform, the Up Arrow Key will be used to accelerate the car.
On Windows platform, the Left Arrow Key will be used to turn the car to the left.
On Windows platform, the Right Arrow Key will be used to turn the car to the right.
On Windows platform, the Space Bar will be used to apply brakes. FR05- On Android smartphone, the buttons will be available to manoeuvre
06 the car. FR06: Unlocking new tracks
The user will be allowed to unlock new tracks by winning races on default tracks. FR07: Upgrading Car

heading: 2.2.2  NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
content: NFR 1: Availability of devices and internet
The player needs to have a PC or an Android smartphone in order to play the game.
Moreover, he should have an internet connection to download it. NFR 2: User-friendly interface
The game will provide a user-friendly interface. Menus and settings will be easy to understand.
The controls of the game will also be common i.e. like other racing games have. NFR 3: Front View
A front view of the game will be provided because most of the car games don’t provide a front view to the player to ride his/her car in the game. NFR 4: Game Errors
The game shouldn’t crash in any situation. NFR 5: Android OS 2.3 Required
The Android device must support Android OS 2.3 or above in order to run the game.

Categories incorporate action, racing, shooting. Gaming platforms such as Windows, Android, iOS and so on really urged individuals to amuse themselves using their cell phones and personal computers. heading: Abstract
content: In the world of rapidly innovating technologies which revolutionizes our ordinary daily tasks in a smart manner, we opt to bring the concept of smart cities to our rapidly developing country. For this purpose, we will be bringing the idea of “RIDE” to reality. Ride is an application that tracks a bus and gathers the distance to each station along its route. Ride involves the installation of an electronic device in a vehicle, with an installed driver side Android App on any SMART phone to enable th e user to track the vehicle's location. There are two applications one for server and the other for the client. Buses carry GPS devices· to track their positions. By this positions to server are periodically updated. Client application displays map showing  the position of bus. It shows where buses are on a map and provide users the updated information at different time interval. The users can get flexibility of planning travel using the app, to decide on which bus to take or when to catch the bus. The waiti ng time of the user can be reduced. Simple mode of communication is the key feature of the Bus Tracking system. This application can be easily extended for central tracking system to keep track of all the public vehicles. The different queries and efficien t route management can be easily done through central server system. Hopefully with our GPS observance system which will be supported with an application we will be able to provide the city with a better, smarter way of travel. Our GPS observance system will hold these key features: 1. Driver and client side applications. 2. GPS based real time location tracking. 3. Searching of buses on their route number. 4. Calculating shortest distance from client’s location to the nearest bus stop.

heading: Abstract
content: The task of developing intelligent machines that can understand visual scenes and then relay back their understanding in natural language has been a challenge for the fields of Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing. Recently, thanks to advancements in computer hardware, data - gathering techniques and most importantly, Artificial Intelligence, quiet a lot has been achieved in this domain in a short span of time. Through this project, we present the fundamentals of two such models that accomplish the task of image captioning using Neural Networks. We elaborate on their respected methodologies, argue on the quality of the captions they produce and suggest improvements for even better -quality captions. We then prove that these models can be used in countless applications with immediate and practical benefits. Our contribution lies in performing an in -depth analysis of machine generated captions using automatic evaluation metrics and our proposed ‘consensus -based’ Human Evaluation plan, rather than designing and staging complex algorithms for the Image Captioning task. We show that t he automatic metrics give better scores when the captions are being compared against more than one reference sentence. Moreover, our study suggests that the evaluation of Image Captioning systems may be fully automated. We propose strategies for collecting human judgments cheaply and on a large scale, which allows even better analysis of the captions produced by machines. We also suggest improvements in the models discussed and then implement both the models accordingly.

heading: 1.1  Brief Introduction
content: Differentiating between a tiger and a cheetah, identifying a pen on your desk, or recognising a person on a bus all seem so easy. The ease by which a human is able to perform all these visual tasks is amazing, even when there are thousands of object categories to choose from and no more than a second to process all the data. A clear understanding and  appreciation of the complexity of this feat is required from the reader, to showcase the challenge of replicating it on a machine. How can the human visual system process each retinal image, and report the identities or properties of the objects that are present in that scene, all at run time? Since artificial vision and Neural Networks practically imitate the human brain in building models, they best answer this question in a more ‘human’ way. We define Artificial Cognition as the task of automatic image captioning in which a machine describes an image with a meaningful statement. The statement has to be descriptive but concise, and has to be grammatically correct. The quality of a caption describing an image is defined as the overall quality of the sentence, in terms of its fluency, adequacy and punctuations. The caption has to be precise in identifying all the entities present in the image and their relationship. The complexity of designing such a system is obvious and remains a challenge for Computer Vis ion scientists. Computer Vision is basically all about artificially intelligent systems that can obtain data from images or visual scenes. Previous work in this field has focused on face detection, matching, feature detection, motion tracking, and most imp ortantly, image classification. As image classification involves classification of the objects, this is where most of the recent work has been building on. For a machine, the process of classification is to categorise the pixels of an image into different labels or classes. Same pixel values are grouped together in the same class. These categories are also then used to identify the different labels in another image. The task of automatic image captioning involves taking an image as an input, analysing its v isual content, and generating a textual description (normally a single sentence) that aptly describes the salient features of the image. The description generated can be very diverse in nature, since it can talk about any visual aspect of the image: it can  mention the different objects and their attributes, the physical features of the scene, or how the objects in the scene interact with each other. In short, a good image caption requires full image understanding, and therefore provides with an excellent opportunity to evaluate the accuracy and precision of object detection systems and image classification models. Better evaluation scores mean that these models can then be applied to real life problems where the chance of error is as minimal as possible. For instance, the feature of auto- drive in some cars need to be very accurate and robust, so that people can trust it completely. The more accurate the auto-drive feature is, lessen the chances of collision or an accident. In our work we use the state of the art automatic evaluation methods that offer the highest correlations with human judgments and expect that additional progress can be made in further improving these methods in the future. In this project, a thorough examination of the whole image captioning task is presented, focusing mainly on Neural Networks. Two Image captioning models are highlighted in this report, based on the works of Karpathy  et al [1] and Johnson et al [ 2]. Both the models are very similar in architecture, except for their outputs. The model proposed by Karpathy et al produces one caption describing an image, while the other model outputs multiple descriptions per image.

heading: 1.2 Image Captioning Challenges
content: This is easier said than done. The complexity of the fact that a computer must transform an image into pixel patterns and then translate the patterns into vector representation, must be fully appreciated. A dog from a different breed, under different lighting conditions or a different camera angle, in a different pose is still a dog, but the patterns representing the visual image would obviously be different. On the other hand, pixel patterns which represents similar labels at a low - level might instead be part of many different objects (carpets, coats, etc.) or animals (dogs, bears, monkeys, etc.). The same kind of challenges are present on the language side. The natural task performed by a human of identifying and describing the salient features of an imag e is in fact, for a machine to actually identify some pixel values against a grid of a few million brightness values and annotate them with sequences of integers, which are representing words (Figure 2). In addition, it is often required from an image capt ion that it should describe some high -level concepts that require inferences based on previous knowledge, unrelated to the image, as well. The evaluation of machine generated captions is yet another challenge. In the case of image classification, each image is labelled under a category or a class, making it a straightforward task to analyse and evaluate the performance and accuracy. However, in the case of image captioning, the output is a sentence in natural language which can be difficult to evaluate. On e way is to compare the machine generated captions against human captions, but that is not ideal solution. Every person has a different perception of what they see, meaning that a caption given by one person for an image, may not be even mentioning the same object or objects as identified by some person. Whatever the reasons, but the baseline that has been established is this: human captions vary from person to person. This makes the captions biased, non -serious, inconsistent and even speculative. heading: 1.3 Report Organisation
content: Section 2 presents a brief introduction of Neural Networks, the mechanism they use and most importantly the role they are playing in automatic image captioning.  From perceptron and single layered networks, basic structures of a Neural Network, to the more advance and abstract concepts (Recurrent Neural Networks, LSTMs) are described. Section 3 identifies the types of models available for the image captioning task, the evaluation methods to analyse the generated captions and the different datasets available for the job. Section 4 describes our selected base-line model that generates a single sentence against one image. Section 5 describes the second model selected, which generates multi ple descriptions per image. Even though this model cannot be utilised for image captioning tasks, other interesting prospects are discussed. Section 6  presents our methodology of evaluating the machine generated captions using both human judgments and automatic metrics. We conduct a number of experiments to analyse and enhance the quality of the generated captions. Section 7 displays the evaluation results and explains the conclusions that we have drawn from the experiments. Based on these results, we give suggestions for improvement in the next section. Section 8 points out the drawbacks and limitations in the models and in the evaluation techniques that we encountered through our project, and presents our improvements and suggestions against them. heading: 2 Neural Networks
content: Neural Netw orks has recently received a lot of attention, specifically for the task of image captioning. The concept of NN is not a recent one, but dates back to the late 1940s when terms like neurons, perceptron’s and machine learning were already being used. This c omplete section is dedicated to NN, with the intention of building a clear and definite understanding of the topic, starting from basic concept of an artificial network, and leading on to more abstract concepts based on, for the sake of image captioning, Convolutional networks and Recurrent networks.

heading: 2.1 Artificial Neural Networks
content: NN are basically inspired by the human central nervous system, where an artificial neuron behaves the same way as biological neurons do. The biological neuron has to receives signals  through dendrites, then a structure to process those signals. The output signals leave through the axon and are transmitted to other neurons. Similarly, artificial neuron has a number of inputs to receive signals, a processing mechanism, and only a single output that is connected to other neurons.

heading: Figure 3: Biological Neuron
content: NN learn human-similar tasks through a number examples or training Data, which is a completely different approach from the traditional way of explicitly programming the required f unction or functions according to the specified requirement. In image captioning tasks, which is the primary point of focus in this project, a NN may be trained to identify images that contain, let’s say, dogs by evaluating example images that have been ma nually labelled by humans. Then, using these resulting images, dogs in other images can be identified. This is done without any kind of prior knowledge about dogs. Instead, a NN builds its own set of rules to identify and categorize objects, along with their attributes. These rules are then used at the time of evaluation to correctly identify the objects in an image. The applicability of neural networks is not only limited to image captioning. Tasks involving face identification, speech recognition, texts translations, controlling vehicles and robots automatically, detecting anomalies and so on, are using NN for better and better results.
