heading: 4.2 Unit Testing
content: The objective of unit testing is to check each and every code segment or code bits of a web application  separately and check its working before running the whole web application and testing it . Unit testing is performed to resolve the minor issue s of a web application. For example, code for login and code for register account in a web application is tested separately. Components may be required to be disconnected from each other while unit testing.

heading: 4.3 Integration testing:
content: The goal of integration tes ting is to test the modules in a web application that are connected with each other and their functionality gives a mutual unique result. Integration testing is always done after the web application is along with unit testing. In integration testing all functional requirements are tested. For examples: cart module and payment module are connected and they give a mutual output in result. Their connection is checked by integration testing and their result is analysed. After unit testing, we continued incorporating units to give appropriate shape to item. After every unit coordinated, we performed incorporation testing o n our framework. It was a time taking procedure and we did it deliberately in light of the fact that it is critical piece of any venture. We had a few issues while performing it and incorporating it however we worked out on our issues effectively.

heading: Abstract
content: The online leave management system is something which is needed in every field of Pakistan. We are living in the 21 st century but we still follow the old leave system. We are coming with such an idea that employees of organization will be able to apply for the leave online sitting anywhere. The main idea is to eradicate the oral leave system i.e. handwritten leaves, calling the higher authorities, manual record keeping etc . The application will prove useful for all professional fields as every other organization requires to upgrade their system of attendance of the employees.

heading: 1.1 Objectives
content: To keep up with the enhanced society views and aspects regarding modern technology and innovations, the application shall prove a rising star in ev ery professional field possible. Mostly organizations in Pakistan has their own way of leave management system, mostly organizations use manual system for their leave management and  record keeping, which is a very time-consuming process and it is very hard to manage the whole record manually. We are making android-based application and a website that shall allow the employee to apply for an automated leave by selecting the dates for leave. A notification shall popup to the employer that employee has applied for a leave and if the employer approves/disapproves it, a notification of approval/disapproval will be sent to employee. The following actions will be considered in developing the application o If leaves are available, the admin will approve his/her leave and t he system will generate a notification to the employee. o Then leave section will be updated. o This all work will be done through website and android application.

heading: 1.2 Problem statement
content: COMSATS University also follows the old leave system(manual), the leaves are applied manually, and the administration have to keep the records manually. This is a very time- consuming process which needs a lot of effort. Manual teacher works as th e teacher applies for the leave, if he is applying for casual leaves for less than 5 days then HOD of the department who send this case to senior manager of HR who approves or disapproves the casual leaves, if he is applying for more than 5 days than this case goes to HR and from HR it goes to director to approve or disapprove.  On the other hand, if he is applying for earned leaves this case goes straight t o HR department and they handle  it. This is a very long and complex process o In COMSATS University:

heading: Page | 9
content: o Every teacher has 10 manual leaves o Every teacher earns 2 leaves monthly o Earned leaves has a limit of 90 and cannot exceed that limit, after that leaves can only be reduced but not added to the account of employees account.

heading: 1.3 Solution
content: The online  leave management system will help to apply leaves online and the record keeping will be automated. This will be more efficient and less time consuming and it will make the process of applying leave easy for both the user and administration. The user will be added in the system by the admin. Then  he/she will sign in into his account. He will go on apply leave option to a pply the leave specifying dates . His leave request will go to HOD of department through mail then it will depend on the HOD of department to approve his/her leave or not. If his/her leave is approved/disapproved by HOD a notification will be sent, and the leave section will be updated automatically. The user will also have the option to see his/her leave history, he will also have the option to reset his password.

heading: 1.4 Motivation and scope
content: We are living in the age of technology and internet; every other individual wants access of information at their fingertips. As we are computer science students we observe every innovation introduced around the world. Online leave management system is functional in many countries but in Pakistan we still follow the manual system in almost every field. Through observation we came up with an idea that we should also introduce this concept in our country. This will be very useful app for every domain. When people will realize its importance, they would make this concept a part of their system.  We are introducing this system in COMSATS University because they also follow the old manual system. By applying this system in COMSATS University the leave system of the university will b e fully automated and will impro ve the attendance system of the organization and will make it more efficient.

heading: 10 of 84  06 January 2018
content: 1 Introduction World wide web has provided us with various ways to interacts with each other. They perform certain activities like shopping, search information and interact with others through online sites. These websites allow customers to share their feelings, attitude and personal experience regarding to the products and services. Costumer’s opinion on social websites considered as valuable information for merchants and customers as well. The main purpose of conducting reviews is to enhance the product quality and reshape them according to the consumers need. If the reviews are positive, one is likely to buy the product and if the reviews are negative, one will certainly not buy it. Positive reviews about product give significant benefits and fame to the organization and manufactures. Unfortunately, it also provides the opportunity for writing fake reviews to promote specific products or demote their competitors’ product. Such activities known as Spam reviewing and those who write deceptive content about products known as spammers. Spam reviewing refers to “illegal” activities that try to mislead potential customers to buy the targeted product or by giving false negative reviews to damage their competitor’s reputation [1] Study of spam detection in different fields has gain significant attention from the research community. Web spam and email spam are two major types of spamming studied extensively for last few years [2]. Review spam is somehow like the Web spam. In the context of Web spamming, the spammers try to mislead search engine by giving high rank to specific pages to gain more traffic to their pages. Whereas, In Review spamming, fraudsters try to mislead potential customers by writing spam opinions for their organizations. As there is no quality control on user-generated content, anyone can write anything on websites, which leads to the fake opinions, and effect the potential users in their decision.  Our study specifically consists of product spam reviews only. For the trustworthiness of authentic user’s opinion, we need to identify those deceptive reviews to make reviews authentic and trustworthy. The main challenging problem in Spam review detection, which make it differ from other types, it is very hard to identify the fake opinion from the real ones, as no one can judge the sentiments of other human only by reading the reviews. Because Supervised learning requires labelled data, so you must label these reviews as spam or not before applying supervised algorithms. Different researchers have devised different ways for this. In this project, we have used a different yet more reliable way for this. We have used Amazon.com reviews dataset for this project and labelled those reviews using behavioural features. That labelled dataset was then further used in training and testing of both linguistic and behavioural models.  Our main purpose is to detect spam reviews more accurately that is why, we applied both approaches on our dataset to get maximum accuracy [3]. A new review will be passed to the both models to evaluate. Both models will return a normalized value between [0-1]. Value close to “1” will be considered as spamming and value closed to ”0” indicates non-spam. The output of these two models will then passed to novel statistical spam algorithm to combine and predict whether the newly received review is spam or not.

content: 1.1 Objectives The main objective of this project is to create the best and efficient algorithm that will detect the malicious content and deceptive reviews. Moreover, to propose an approach that will identify illegal content like fake messages, spam opinion about products or brands. Furthermore, to propose an efficient system that will filter out spam and malicious reviews/content to maintain true costumer’s opinions. The main objective can be further divided into the following objectives. • Highlight the Fake Reviews – To highlight the untruthful reviews is a very challenging problem as no one can manually judge whether that review is spam or not simply by reading the review are fake or original. However, spammers always consider two main factors while writing fake reviews, the review should look like original reviews and secondly the fake reviews should be generated as quickly as possible because they need to write uncountable reviews within less time so they never prefer to write lengthy reviews.  • Making E-commerce websites reliable and trustworthy –   Genuine reviews make e-commerce websites strong as they gain some extra trust from their customers, which also lead them towards more profit. Authenticated reviews are also helpful for companies as they understand the real need of customers and reshape their products according to them. Through genuine reviews, good products will be promoted while the bad products reshaped according to consumers need.  • Detecting spammers trends – Detecting and labeling reviews as spam or not can also provide us with the reviewers who are spammers. We can analyze these spammers behaviors to find out their trends which can help us detecting spam and spammers more efficiently. This can also help other researchers in their work.   • Contributing in Research sector– Number of people have done some great research in detecting and finding spam reviews which has helped us getting here. Similarly, the research that has been conducted during this project can help others who will work in this field.

content: 2 Requirements Analysis 2.1 Literature Review / Existing System Study Study on online reviews have become the most trending research topic from last few years. Most research trends concentrate on opinion mining and opinion extraction. The existing methods for opinion detection in the context of machine learning (supervised and unsupervised approaches) which further split out into three categories by their features: Behavioural, linguistic and combination of both.  Ø First work in Spam review detection was done by Jindal and Liu [5] in the context of product reviews. The analyzed million reviews from Amazon.com, and showed how widespread the problem was. They ran a logistic regression classifier on a model trained on duplicate or near-duplicate reviews labeled as Spam, and the rest as not spam. They combined behavioral and textual features aiming to detect non-duplicate review spam.  Ø Lim, Nguyen, Jindal, Liu, and Lauw [6] used spammer features for this in 2010. They used pre-processed Amazon reviews, based on highly active users that had written at least 3 reviews. They used features like general rating deviation, early deviation. The training data was labeled manually using group of evaluators, however this was proven to lead to low accuracy in real-life.  Ø First, Ott, Choi, Cardie, and Hancock in 2011 [7] demonstrated that it is impossible detect fake reviews just by reading the text.  Ø Second, Mukherjee, Liu, and Glance [8] proved that not even the dataset generated from crowdsourcing is valid because model doesn’t generalize in real life data. 2.1.1 Reviewmeta.com ReviewMeta is the only complete independent website, which we can relate to this project It works at its best when there are lots of reviews and reviewers. Classification of unauthentic reviews based used different machine learning algorithms and Artificial Intelligence. ReviewMeta only look at the text of the review in three of our twelve tests: Phrase Repetition, Word Count Comparison, and Incentivized Reviews.  The other nine tests are looking at data beyond the language. They currently support reviews from Amazon and bodybuilding only. 2.1.2 Amazon Review Filters Amazon is a vast e-store that with millions of users from all over the world. The most common mode for consumers to express their level of satisfaction with their purchases is through online ratings. Although it plays an important part in affecting buyer actions and decision making, and therefore attracting many spam reviewers to insert fake feedback or reviews to handle review content and ratings. Amazon is always aware of such companies and keeps on suing them from time to time. They have been continuously improving their technology for review classification and shaping human behaviour by some review posting recommendations.

content: 4.5 Linguistic Feature Analysis In this phase, we try to identify the spam review by analyzing its text content.  This approach is widely used when it comes to detecting spam review. Especially spam reviews are like other spam reviews by their content. Linguistic approach takes advantage of this to detect spam reviews out of others. A Machine learning model that has already been trained and tested with appropriate training and test data is responsible for this task. A new review is passed to the trained model which then decides whether it is spam or not. The linguistic analysis mainly consists of two main steps • Data Pre-Processing • Classification Algorithm  4.5.1 Data Pre-Processing As we know that machine learning model only works on numerical data both continuous and discrete and cannot be applied on text data. Because of this we need a way to convert our text data into numeric. To do so we need to pre-process our data and create a Document term matrix.  Similarly, we also have pre-processed our data to use it in our model. The Pre-processing of our data in this project can be divide in following steps: 4.5.1.1 Stemming Sometimes, we want to count various forms of a word together. This procedure is referred to as stemming. Stemming an English text treats the words (works, working, worked) as instances of the word work. Stemming must be applied on the document before tokenizing it. 4.5.1.2 Removing Stop Words or Punctuation Before tokenizing we need to delete un necessary words, words which appears most throughout the documents like punctuation (is, are, am etc.). These words do not help us in detecting spam reviews so it is better to remove them before tokenizing to avoid un necessary token. For example, the document/review “This is a very good car"  after removing stop words and punctuation will look like “good car”

For example The review “I have bought this book since a year now; this book is one of the best one I have ever read. content: 4.5.1.4 Tokenizing Tokenizing is an important preprocessing step. This is the process of splitting a text into individual words or sequences of words (n-grams). Decisions regarding tokenization is very complex and depends on various aspects. For example, previously processed review “good car” Unigram: ["good", "car"] Bi-gram: ["good car"]   Uni + Bi-gram: [“car”, “good”, “good car”] Similarly, we can create several combinations of N-grams. We have tried different tokenizing techniques and compare their results to choose the best technique suitable for us.   4.5.1.5 Document Term-Matrix As we have discussed before that the machine learning models does not work well with textual data, we need to convert our data into numeric form before passing to the model. After tokenizing the next step is to create a document term matrix based on the previously created tokens. Document term matrix is usually defined as: Document-term matrix or DTM is a sparse matrix (containing mostly zero values) use to define the frequency of terms or tokens that occur in a collection of documents. In a document-term matrix, rows represent the documents in the collection and columns represents the terms.  There are various schemes for defining the value of each token in matrix, here we have used two of them: • Simple Count: In simple count technique, the value of term in matrix is determined by the no of times it occurs in a document e.g. if a token occurs 2 times its value will be 2 or 0 If it does not exist in document. • Term Frequency and Inverse document frequency (TF-IDF): TF-IDF technique is intended to reflect how important a word or token is to a document in a collection of corpus. The TF-IDF value increases proportionally to the number of times a token appears in the document, but is often decreases by the frequency of the word in the corpus, which helps to adjust for the fact that some

content: Step 1: The Amazon.com dataset consisted of 1,99,500 reviews, containing 30% spam and 70% not spam, was taken into consideration. Step 2: Text reviews always consist on absurd data, needed to be removed before using them for classification, most commonly which of them are following • Stop words • Numeric and Special characters Step 3: After cleaning of the text reviews. They are needed to be converted into numeric form to be used in the classification model this can be done by converting them Document term matrix of numeric vectors. Following two are 2 methods to do this, • Count Vectorizer It converts the text reviews into the matrix of tokens based on their number of occurrences in the document, it is a sparse matrix   • TF-IDF In this approach, the obtained sparse matrix or Document term matrix will have fractional values of tokens which will be between 0-1. TF tells us about how important a specific token or word is to a review high TF will lead to high value in matrix and IDF tells about how important this specific token is to all reviews high IDF will lead to less value in matrix because tokens which are widely used in all reviews will not be of much help when it will come to classification. High value of token in matrix means that those tokens are highly important. Step 4: After the converting to document term matrix, these matrices are used as an input for the following classifiers or models and evaluated for prediction • Multinomial NB • Bernoulli NB • Logistic Regression • Support Vector Machine • Random Forest Step 5: The prediction from the classifier model will be then used and compared for evaluation.

It helps us to analyse what our model has predicted the most or less, and can also be used to define customer threshold values for the probabilistic model.

content: 5.2.1 Individual Spammer Behaviour 5.2.1.1 Content Similarity The CDF of content similarity (Figure 37) shows that almost 50% of spammers have similarity index between 0.1 to 1. However, rest 50% have exactly 1 similarity index of their reviews, it means almost half of the spammers copy their previous reviews instead of writing new one. On the other hand, the non-spammers also write similar reviews. Almost 60-70 percent of non-spammers have little similarity index (0.5 approximately). 5.2.1.2 Maximum Number of Reviews As we know writing too many reviews in a day is not a normal behaviour. According to this CDF (Figure 38) 5-8% of spammers have lesser ratio of reviews in a single day. However, rest of the spammers show that they tend to write more and more reviews in a day. For non-spammers, they have a very moderate reviewing rate. Approximately 60% do not even write more than single review every day. The ratio of their reviews posted gradually increases. content: 6.2 Project Summary Fake reviews on user opinion websites making doubtful to trust on e-commerce industry. Our research and prototype will provide a solution for customers to trust on e-commerce websites. The project will perform Spam review analysis on real life dataset with authentic fake reviews labels. It divides the reviews into two categories, i.e. spam and not-spam. Firstly, once we received a review, linguistic approach will be applied on it and get the results after that all the selected features both author and review content features will be applied on the review and pass it to the naïve Bayesian model and get their results. Both results will be combine for final output and compared it when defined threshold to judge whether it is spam or not. 6.3 Future Work Currently, this project is limited by project’s scope. However, our study can be used by other researchers to further enhance the outcome and build a well-organized prototype. If we had a proper dataset with sufficient number of attributes then a lot more behavioural features can be added in our proposed model to get more accurate results. When the system comes online and in proper running form we can log user’s data like their location of review, IP address, MAC address, time of login/logout from system. These are some of the key features that can help us in detecting spammers more easily. Currently in our project we only work on individual spammers. However, this project can be extended to work on group spammers as well. Opinion spam detection is a very vast field and there is a lot of work which can be done in this.

heading: Abstract
content: In the world today there is a lot of research work performed in every field of study. The issue of finding research papers for researchers still remains  difficult. It has been so for a very long time and a researcher's life is all about consuming time prop erly. This issue can be addressed by creating a software system that is integrated with the biggest of the  researcher paper repositories and helps research worker by going through th is repository by itself. The researchers look for the research papers by checking out the references of research papers which is a difficult and time consuming job. However this an integral part of research activity and it is known as systematic literat ure review. We intend to aid such a tool that facilitates the researcher in s earching and identifying  relevant studies automatically. This tool will make the job much easier for them as it would automatically go through the reference section, thus automating the effort of researcher and providing ease for them to sort o ut which research papers to read. The system serves a great deal in helping them in their research work. Table of Contents

heading: 1.1  Introduction
content: Referencer is research papers' references search tool. Each research paper contains references. These references are basically names of research papers given by the researcher to indicate the whereabouts of the information he used to gather the information in his paper. The references of a research paper might point towards sources which are not directly related to it, but the domain of both is more or less the same. Research work involves reading, going through the context and reading between the lines. Moreover the researcher has to analyze the information he is gaining from his research. This part of research work is to be done by him and a software might not be abl e to help him in this part. But, after reading a research paper, the researcher has to check its references for more material to help him accomplish his goal  in order to find work related to his field of interest and this is systematic literature review [1]. Checking the reference section and then opening another  research paper related to previous one gets a little difficult and inconvenient for the researcher. It involves opening new research papers and the main problem occurs when they have to find rela ted research papers on the online repositories. Mostly the research paper and its content is not what they are looking for and they end up wasting their time. This problem needs to be solved so that the researchers can perform efficiently and without any hassle.

heading: • Time Saving System:
content: This system shall save time for all the researchers by providing them with the relevant context they are willing to research on. This way they can go through double amount of research papers in the same time. This tool can save their time and will allow them to perform their tasks quickly.

heading: • Performance:
content: The system shall be performing swiftly and shall not cause lag. The response time of the system shall not be greater than 2 to 3 seconds and the system shall occupy the least amount of resources possible. • Precision and Accuracy: The system shall have a high level of precision and accuracy. All operations shall be done correctly and there shall be a surety that the information being displayed to the user shall be correct.

heading: • Reliability:
content: The reliability of the proposed system shall be high as the system shall not have any bugs. The system shall not crash due to proper handling of exceptions and removal of all possible errors.

heading: • Non-Redundancy:
content: The system shall have zero redundancy by ensuring that there would be no chance of repetition of records over and over again. • Easy to Operate: The system shall be easy to operate by each individual. It shall consist of user friendly interfaces and shall not take more than 15 minutes of usage for its user to learn how to use it.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: The researcher has to waste a lot of time on the repositories in order to find work which is completely or remotely related to his domain of research. Thus, the research work gets more complicated and difficult. Moreover, there is no platform that provides searching repositor y and downloading the results of the search . This means that each time researcher needs to search a different repository, the researcher would have to open the interface of th at repository and then search it. Even after doing so, he might not be certain about finding scholarly documents he intends to find.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions and Constraints
content: The constraints that exist in this project are as following: 1. As this project is based on an in novative idea, no work to this project has yet been done. So, it might be difficult to find online help at some points in future. 2. The constant load of semester studies work and this project is an issue as unequal or improper division of time could cause less focus on either one of these two. 3. Using APIs of repositories is an issue. E.g., Google Scholar does not share an API in order to share their data. Moreover, they also block all bot requests by giving a form for human-user confirmation. So, writing a whole API in such short time might be an issue.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: A lot of researchers nowadays are facing the same issue identified in the introduction section. This project is intended to make things easier for all the researchers and those who want to writ e their own research papers. This project will search any keyword entered by the user in the Google Scholar repository , download research papers from it  and then process them using a processing library provided by Apache known as PDFBox [3].  Thus, through processing the software will extract the reference section of the research papers by using simple String manipulation techniques i.e. processing the String formatted paper [4]. This project will ask the user to put a limit up to which he wants to download research papers. Universities and different research organizations have been trying to find a way to speed up their research work, make it easier and hassle free. Thus, they are looking for a way to speed up any part of their research work so that the wh ole process can be shortened . The proposed software system provides a solution as researchers waste a great chunk of their time in just finding the research papers which are related to their area of research. This tool will provide a platform to all the people associated with research work if made according to proper market standards. It would also help the researchers have to save a big chunk of their time so that they can properly theorize their wo rk to provide a qualitied research work. Thus, the Referenc er basically provides an automation of the process of Systematic Literature Review by using simple methods and libraries [9].

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: You can find many repositories which provide electronic research papers data. Some features that the Referencer is going to provide are already offered by these repositories. But, there is one core feature that the Referencer provides and simple repositories of research papers do not provide. For building a proper differentiation between  Referencer and other ordinary electronic research data repositories, we will discuss some of these repositories. Following is the discussion about some major repositories:

heading: Google Scholar:
content: Google Scholar is one of the most used and updated repositories of academic data. It offers research papers regarding all the fields of present era. The bulk of data present on this site makes a plus point for it. Moreover, small repositories provide their data to Scholar by becoming Google Partners and this makes Scho lar a bulky repository. Google does not offer any API for Scholar which is a big drawback for developers trying to embed Scholar into different web applications and software systems [5].

heading: Microsoft Academic:
content: Out of all the academic repositories, MS Acade mic is the one most intelligent as it uses better search algorithms. Other repositories provide mostly keyword matching data but MS Academic provides us data intelligently. This data is most related to the user's intent and is extracted by semantic search engine algorithms which can process the most complex of the user's queries [6]. ArXiv: ArXiv is another bulky repository for research papers with publish approval. These papers are related to all aspects of modern science including the ones like Astrophy sics, Computer Sciences, Finance, etc. ArXiv is also free for use and provides a free API for the users to use the data available on this repository. DVN (Dataverse Network): Dataverse Network is a Harvard owned library for electronic papers which are approved for publication. DVN provides free data for its user, even the ones trying to use it as an integration in their software or web applications without limitations. This project contains recent publications and journals, and is installed in most leading universities at 30 sites across the globe [7]. IEEE Xplore: IEEE Xplore is another database of electronic publications and is used across the globe. Around 20,000 publications of researchers from around the world are added to this repositories every month. For regulation of data being used, IEEE had to restrict their results to 200 per query. Otherwise there are no limitations for the users or developers associated with this database [8].

heading: 2.2 Critical Analysis
content: All of repositories mentioned in the Liter ature Review section above , except Microsoft Academic, works on the basis of keyword search algorithms. For instance, Google Scholar works on keyword search algorithm for the sole purpose of SEO and indexing of the pages. Thus, these search engines are not  intelligent at all. This makes it difficult for users to find publications and journals they require because the intent of their search might not be delivered through the search query. Moreover, none of these systems have implemented techniques or provide d any tools to help users in systematic literature review, which is the most time consuming part of the research work. Instead, the users have to go through all the papers they get from running searches of these repositories and then getting the journals related to their topic, just to find the most relevant data. Thus, this prolongs the research process and that is why Referencer will be a much helping tool for the researchers trying to save their time.

heading: 2.8 Software Development Life Cycle
content: Since we are developing a java based tool with high level of coding, our software development cycle will be an Agile based development cycle. It contains multiple functionalities which are quite simple for the front end users but involve complicated programming techniques. This level of complicati on in our software indicates that it requires a lot of discussions and meeting. Thus, we choose Scrum framework to carry out our software’s life cycle. Following are the key reasons of choosing Scrum framework: 1. Level of complication of our software. 2. High level of collaborative efforts required. 3. Regular meetings for coping with confusions. 4. Regular audits for team work evaluations. 5. Sprints based development. 6. Development of software in a test-first manner.

heading: 2.8.1 Scrum framework
content: A scrum based software life cycle consists of the following phases:

heading: 5. Sprint retrospective (Process inspection and adaptation)
content: The most initi al phase of the Scrum cycle is the initial product backlog. This process basically consists of gathering the features required by the product owner. In other words, it is the process of gathering functional requirements. After product backlog comes the st age sprint planning. This stage involves the planning of the sprints in presence of the development team and the product owners. Thus each targeted feature is then broken down into small chunks of tasks. These tasks are macroscopically called a sprint backlog. The phase next to sprint planning is the sprint execution phase. Sprints from the sprint backlog are chosen one by one, starting from the top priority. Each selected sprint represents a feature. Thus, the selected feature is then developed. The sprint execution includes meetings on daily basis, known as daily scrums. At the end of each sprint execution, the developed feature is delivered to the product owners as a product. The sprint review phase, initiated after each sprint execution, includes the i nspection and adaptation of the product developed in sprint execution. This meeting is to discuss the developed feature, keeping the whole product in view. Another inspection and adaptation activity at the end of sprint execution is the sprint retrospective. This includes the discussion of the Scrum methodologies being used in order to convey the sprints. Thus, this phase helps the team to realize what caused convenience or issue in the last sprint and should or should not be done in the next sprint.

heading: 29 of 65  16 May 2018
content: After these steps, the whole cycle is repeated, starting from sprint planning and picking up the next prioritized sprint from the sprint backlog.

heading: 6.1 Project Summary
content: This tool is being developed by using a simple client server based architecture in which the server is the repository. It allows the researchers to find work relevant to their field of research, in the form of references of research papers, without wasting their time and without extra effort. All the researcher needs to do is as simple as following:

heading: 2. Enter a search query
content: As, the research papers are already provided with the largest repository i.e. Google  Scholar, so, we do not need to develop a server or a repository for any purpose. The connection between the tool and the repository is created by using APIs which are provided by open source libraries providers like Apache, etc. Thus, the development of this tool is based just on complicated, high level coding only.

heading: 6.2 Future Work
content: The short span of time provided to complete this project has limited the number of features being provided to the researcher. In future, this tool might have greater number of repositories to search research articles from. There might be a functionality for the user to share the collected references by email with other research colleagues. At present, this tool has an incomplete channel for licensing. A proper way of licensing this product might be added in order to make commercial use of this tool in both field based and study based research processes. This would also make it easy for the d eveloping team to keep record of the user pool of this software.

heading: 6.3 Problems faced and Lessons learnt
content: The problems faced in developing this project were following: 1. Downloading research papers was difficult as the download link might be dead, the server might be down or the user connection speed might be too low 2. The research papers available on any of the repositories d o not follow any certain format which made the extraction of references an issue. 3. Google Scholar rejects any BOT.txt script. 4. When converting t he papers into String, the header and footer part of the paper was very tricky to omit. 5. Some of the papers were a scanned image in the form of a PDF. So, reading text from them was not efficiently possible.

heading: 64 of 65  16 May 2018
content: The lessons learnt on the basis of the development of this project are stated as following: 1. It is a tough job  to write a generic reference extraction code without using Machine Learning. 2. Downloading re search papers from the repository is not a time specific job and depends on many factors like user connection, latency, repository response time, etc. 3. The research papers on the repository do not have a certain format. This justified the need of IEEE and other formats of writing research papers. 4. Selenium Webdriver is dealt as a proper browser by Go ogle Scholar , whereas, the Python or other scripts are blocked by it.  So, the only efficient way of downloading research papers in by using a headless browser.

content: 1.6 SHORTCOMINGS IN THE EXISTING STRUCTURES DUE TO WHICH THE NEED FOR A BETTER

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: In Pakistan it is difficult for every student to afford academies to prepare themselves for entrance tests as well as mostly due to large number of students the academies have to select some of them to prepare them. So other students do not have right direction to prepare and they do not have enough knowledge about universities and universities programs being offered as well as last dates to apply. Student preparing in academies will not be informed in proper manner through an account of his own. Preparation is the key to success for every student who wants to get admission in good university and for this they need a lot of practice. This project comprises of a website and mobile based application that contains all types of material for students which include books, notes, tutorial and past papers as well from all well-known universities/ colleges in the country. This material is grouped into subjects covering all mandatory subjects which are required for entry test preparation for major universities. This project aims to provide a platform for all students who want to get arranged for a university entry test, where a student can register with website/mobile application and get most of the helping material related to his/her field which will be free of cost. Students can attempt online tests and their results will be maintained in record which will appear in their portal and upon these results our application will suggest them about their field which they may opt. Students these days strive hard to prepare themselves for entry test and for that they go to various expensive & time extensive academies and entry test sessions. Not everyone can afford these expensive sessions. On the other hand, helping material likes past papers and notes are also available in market but for that you need to pay heavy amount which obviously everyone can’t afford. This application (Web & Mobile) will provide all students with a platform where they will get relevant data on their fingertips and they don’t need to spend large sum of money on academies and material which are available in market. Our website and android application will past papers, notes and universities details for everyone, thus they have guidance. Registered students can view account and attempt tests. Through mobile application student will be notified about dates. Through all this a student can prepare in a comfortable environment without spending a huge amount of money.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The main objective of our project is as follows 1. Our main goal is to help students to prepare themselves for entry test in various universities.
2. To provide a common platform to these students where they can find out what they need regarding their studies and which field they may choose. 3. The user can register with us.

heading: 4. Profile of student is maintained individually according to their performance.’
content: 5. An opportunity for students to know their strong and weak areas of various subjects 6. Considering Pakistan, due to less number of good universities most of the students, they don’t know about different fie lds, hence this project will help them to take different test and prepare themselves for entrance test. 7. To provide students with a platform where they can get all study material for entry tests specially those students who cannot afford these notes and fee of entry test sessions. 8. Preparation for test is very easy no need for students to wait for academies to start their session. They can start their preparation right after giving exams

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: Students these days are much uncertain about which field they must choose and what really their key areas of interest are. They join different academies and entry test sessions after they are done with their A levels and F.sc. This is the most critical time for them as they now have to choose their field and then make preparations for entry test accordingly. This is high time for these students to get some useful guidance and for this they need a platform where they can test their skills and then evaluate themselves according through their performance. Students can register to this application. After registering with us they have to choose from different levels. There are the two levels available. First is the basic level, then there is intermediate level and then there is Complex level, the application maintains profile of every user of how many papers attempted of how many subjects and their grades accordingly .and profile is showing their individual performance in every subject. If a user is attempting more papers of physics and his/her grades are low in mathematics, then a message is given that you need to focus on mathematics. They can attempt proper tests of various fields which they wish to. After every test which they will attempt, their records will be maintained in their portal and they can view their current and previous performance at any instance. Every test which user attempts is saved with its respective date, time, score, field and subject wise profile, marks wise profile. Based on these individual evaluations, our application will compare their scores in all attempted fields and make an aggregate of that. This will be final evaluation of student and based on this evaluation our application will suggest student about which field he/she may choose.  All fields which he/she had already attempted will appear in a list which will be designed priority

wise, with highest priority at number one and so on. Student can know which field he/she can excel in and what their strong and weak areas are. All tests will be designed according to entry test patterns followed by maximum universities. This project will also contain list of all major universities in Lahore. Their basic information along with address and contact details. We will be providing all entry test details for these universities which will include starting date of form submission, test date and result date. Android application will be providing reminders through notification when student will on notification in settings. This application and website will be a platform for students where they can get a chance to practice maximum and enhance their skills which will further help them in attempting actual entry tests of different universities and it will also help them to choose wisely among various fields.

heading: 1.4.1 Assumptions
content: The system will provide students to understand the pattern of entrance test and prepare well for different universities test. Student will learn by attempting tests and will be able to identify his interest in subjects.

heading: 1.4.2 Constraints
content: 1. Financial problems while purchasing papers from different institutes.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: The application will offer user with an overall system to prep are for entry test of various universities which will be free of cost. This system will cover different subjects which may include MATH, English and Physics, under their respective field such as math and physics under engineering field. Students will get all material under one roof which will be factor for them to use this application. This project will provide with a platform for students to cope up with problems and students will get solutions to some serious issues which include deciding which academy to go for entry test preparation. The students would not have to face unsuitable timings, uncomfortable environment of academies because the students which came from out of city would have to stay in hostel and they have to pay accommodation fees, pick and d rop charges and difficulty in understanding teachers and which field they should select. Not every student can afford fee of expensive academies, and most of the intelligent students belonging to an rural area have no knowledge about academies so they are unable to prepare for test on the other hand students which are not so smart but with right preparation they are able to get admission ,this is unfair for those intelligent students who are unable to prepare for entry test .This is our primary

motivation to give students with a platform where they can prepare for entry test and choose wisely among various available fields. This system will have capability to generate test simulation papers for students to practice. Students will also be provided with details of universities in Lahore along with their entry test schedule, address and contact details. Students don’t need to waste their energies and money on various academies they can get everything which they require for entry test preparation on their fingert ips. heading: 2.9.1 Methodology& software lifecycle for this project
content: The software development life cycle which we used in our project is iterative model. Iterative model is a model in which process starts with simple implementation of small set of software requirements which are gathered previously. Further iterations are performed to the evolving version until complete system is formed which is ready for deployment.

heading: Software Development Life Cycle
content: Following are the reasons why we used this model: • In this model we can produce high level design of the application before we actually built the product and define the design solution for entire prod uct. Later on we can design and built a dummy version of that, and then produce the design based on what had been built earlier. • In this model we always build our product step by step along with its improvement so we can easily locate faults at early stage which later helps to avoid any downward flow of the faults. • In this model we can get reasonable user feedback because when we are presenting sketches and blueprints of the product to users for their feedback, we are efficiently asking them to imagine and tell us about how the product will work. • In this model we spend much of the time in designing the project and less time is spent on documenting it
Figure 4:  Hybrid Model: Incremental model with (mini Water falls)

Following are the steps which we followed in iterative model. • The first step is to analyze the requirements of the customer what they want from you. These requirements include both functional and nonfunctional requirements. • The second step is to design the collected requirements which includes designing interface of your application • The third step is to code • The fourth step is to test your product • The fifth step is to review this product • If there is any issue the system is deployed for 1st increment and this process is repeated until all issues are resolved. heading: Figure 13: Class Diagram
content: There are Eight classes in the class diagram (Admin, signup, Login, past paper, Notes, Student, tests, and result). Signup and Login have composition relation (Formation of one class as a result of one class being aggregated but the key purpose is emphasizing the dependence of contained class). Login and Student have relation of inheritance and 1 to many relations because multiple students can login after registration. Admin have one to many relationships with other classes as admin can add multiples notes, past papers, test and results. Similarly, student have one to many relationships with other classes because student can attempt multiple test. view multiple notes and past paper and view result accordingly multiple times

There are 16 tables in the database: (Student, Admin, Notes, Result, testroom, academic, unis, tests, Past Paper, verbal, quantitative, analytic, physics, chemistry, math and English) All have primary key of id. Student ID is primary key for Student Table which is being used as a foreign key in Academic Table because records there would be of a Student, In Testroom Table because only student is able to give test. Admin ID is primary key for Admin Table which is being used as a foreign key in Notes and Past Papers Table because only admin can insert past papers and notes. Test ID is primary key in Test Table which is used as a foreign key in Chemistry, Physics, Math, English, Verbal, Quantitative, Analytical and Testroom table because all these will have test question against a test and this will be make sure by foreign key that data is valid. Along with that in Testroom Table it is foreign key because we want to keep the record of which test is attempted by the student and that test does exist in the database.

heading: 4.2 Unit Testing
content: We have applied unit testing because in unit testing individual components of the software are testing and this gives the detailed outcome that exact module is working properly. The purpose is that each unit of the system performs as it is designed for. For unit testing we perform: • Module Testing: To test correct data flow of the software. • Output: valid outputs are generated. • Data structure: data structures with proper convention are used. • Data Integrity: While interacting with database, data is correctly stored in correct database. • Boundary Value Evaluation: Boundary values are tested for modules. We divide our Software system into sub modules considering each as one module and performed unit testing to ensure proper functionality of these modules.

heading: 5.2   Project Summary
content: Preparation is the key to success for every student who wants to get admission in good university and for this they need a lot of practice. This project comprises of a website and mobile based application that contains all types of material for students which include books, notes, tutorial and past papers as well from all well -known universities/ colleges in the country. This material is grouped into subjects covering all mandatory subjects which are required for entry test preparation for major universities. This project aims to provide a platform for all students who want to get arranged for a university entry test, whe re a student can register with website/mobile application and get most of the helping material related to his/her field which will be free of cost .Students can attempt online tests and their results will be maintained in record which will appear in their portal and upon these results our application will suggest them about their field which they may opt. Students these days strive hard to prepare themselves for entry test and for that they go to various expensive & time extensive academies and entry test sessions. Not everyone can afford these expensive sessions. On the other hand, helping material likes past papers and notes are also available in market but for that you need to pay heavy amount which obviously everyone can’t afford. This application (Web & Mobile) will provide all students with a platform where they will get relevant data on their fingertips and they don’t need to spend large sum of money on academies and material which are available in market.

heading: Abstract
content: From almost a decade, it has been the basic requirement of every reader to have strong vocabulary, make comprehension strong and understand the context of text easily. The purpose of our project, Reading Assistant for Transcript with Enhanced Searching (RATES), is to enhance learning aptitudes, knowledge, understanding and literal level of user while reading  a document. It will be realized in a desktop and mobile application. Using this app, a user may capture a text or pictorial image of document. For pictorial image, relevant thumbnail of image on internet with labels, will be provided. On the other hand, textual image passes through optical character recognition (OCR). User selects a content (word, technical terms, sentences, paragraphs) and application will provide vocabulary contents (dictionary, synonyms, antonyms etc.), text-to-speech, short summary, translation, web search results and keyword based searching features based on selection of text contents. App submits the request of user after each selection of content to external application program interface (API). Based on response from API, user gets t he required result within the application. It is believed that RATES will assist people in getting relevant and specific information in smart, systematic and efficient way.

heading: 1 Chapter 1: Introduction
content: Intellectual development, Interactive and exclusively intensive learning are considered to be the most important components in order to process information related to any particular problem. People are considered to be poor learner  due to their learning disabilities, basic literal level and auditory discrimination problems. Manually searching on internet is a time consuming process which includes great effort too. These problems are faced by the users when they start read ing a docum ent. They often quit  learning. Moreover, they are more enthusiastic to get the main idea from a large text instead of reading it whole. Therefore, it's a major concern of people to seek for an assistant to enlarge their problem solving and learning skills by capitalizing less  effort and time. Their basic motivation is to provide such assistant through smart and systematic way. A lot of work has been done in this field but failed to overcome all the needs of users. We have analysed these difficulties at first stage and come up with an idea to develop a reading assistant application to serve and ease them. The main idea to develop RATES, Reading Assistant for Transcripts with Enhanced Searching, is to provide an assistant (mobile and desktop application) to solve all kind of problems that might face by a poor learner with less literal level. This work is expected to enhance learning abilities and literal level that become the key hurdle in reading process. We aim to provide a complete package which will help the user to build the knowledge and understanding of text and pictorial image of a document. By using this application, there is no need to suffer from headache of manually search on internet. It will serve the user as language translator by translating the source language text  into desired target language. This work will reduce time and effort on reading a large and lengthy paragraph by putting the main idea of large text into short summary. Project will serve visually impaired people by converting the text into speech. RATES will take textual or pictorial image of a document as input from user. User takes the image by using camera. The input image can also select from gallery or any other storage area. The course of action taken by this app highly depends on type of image input by the user. If a text ual image has input, the app will apply optical character recognition (OCR) to convert into editable format. After having editable format of text, user is free to select text area of interest. According to the selection, further opti ons will be provided by this app. If user select a word, app will generate a request. App will submit this request to an external API to get the response of dictionary contents (i.e., meaning, synonym, antonym, pronunciation, class, and usage) against the word. After getting the response, the results against the word will be shown to user. In case of sentence selection, a drop down menu is active. It will show list of value i.e., translation, text -to-speech and search of sentence. If user choses translation  of sentence option, it will show the source language text into desired target language text by generating and getting the response of user’s request to external application program interface. The selection of text-to-speech will ease

heading: 2.1  Literature review / Existing system study
content: There have been a lot of findings and research in  digital image processing and applications like RATES’ main features, but as whole package it is never been discussed.

heading: 2.1.1 Novel
content: A software system, designed for people with speaking disabilities [1]. The tendency of this work is to benefit the society by producing the speech of entered text data. The system reduces the noise and convert text into speech. The functionality of system is based on three algorithms Longest Common Subsequence, Levenshtein distance and Soundex algorithms. To reduce the noise, these algorithms picks superlative variant of word from pre-defined list of words and replaced the word with superlative likely replacement. After reducing noise, text -to-speech converter takes this as input and produces an analogous sound file. This sound file then played and audio-able to user.

heading: 2.1.2 Gurmukhi Script
content: The OCR system, designed to perform equitable well not only on new document but old as well [2]. Working methodology is based on four classifiers. These classifiers work in serial and parallel mode. The combination of classifiers working in parallel mode results into a method called carpus based weighted voting. By preserving the strength and compensating their weakn ess of these classifiers, better results are achieved. A structural feature algorithm is used to compensate with broken text that is widely appear in old document.

heading: 2.1.3 SynSem
content: An approach introduced to implement and summarization of single document inste ad of multiple document in this study [3]. This approach fuses syntactic, semantic and statistical methodologies. By using these methodologies, SynSem reflects the significance of text heading. Thematic keywords in sentence are al so reflected by this approach. The results reflected by this approach were evaluated by Document Understanding Conference. Moreover, the results generated by SynSem were compared with baseline.

heading: 21 Chapter 2: Requirements Analysis |
content: A prototype system, used to browse picture  on mobile devices  [4]. By employing the novel technologies, MobiPicture automates multiple picture browsing tasks on small screen. Features are deployed. Based on picture attention model, generated from contents, features are dep loyed. Thumbnails, generated by this approach, are difficult to view or recognize because sometimes the size of the thumbnail is too small. This approach presents the information in better way inside any image.

heading: 2.1.5 Vocabulary builder
content: This paper discusses how various mobile apps can be used to enhance vocabulary acquisition with four research-based vocabulary learning strategies: [5] dictionary use, phonological analysis (i.e., learning words by analysing the sound parts), morphological analysis (i.e., learning word meanings by analysing the componential word parts), and contextual analysis learning word meanings by referring to learning context

heading: 2.1.6 Detection, recognition and classification
content: On Detection, recognition and classification, [6] this paper aims to focus on elaborating the dynamic and diversified nature of techniques available and how these techniques have evolved over the past years. This paper discuss the five major branches include document representation, feature selection, constructing a Vector Space Model (VSM), application of a data mining method and finally an evaluation of the text classifier for text classification.

heading: Description:
content: The above shown SDLC model is the hybrid of Waterfall and Agile methodologies. We use this model to capture the whole requirements of our project. Model is divided into two portions, Waterfall in blue and Agile in green. Agile is a combination of iterative and incremental process models. It is also best suited for our project because it will be relatively quick and as we have time constraints to finish this project, we would like to have working modules available. This would largely decrease the complexity of the project. We do not deliver these working versions, we work on next increment until all the modules, and features are captured. Then we deliver the project as a whole like traditional way of Waterfall.  Since our project has rigid and static requirements and captured in the phase (requirement specification) and documented in a software requirement specification (SRS) document.  Once all t he requirements are gathered in the first phase of SDLC, we divide them into different modules and then use agile model for design, coding, testing and integration of each module.  Each module is integrated with the system separately, start next iteration for the coming module.  Once all the modules are developed, we use waterfall for the final integration and the whole application will be deployed.

heading: 4.1 Tessaract Optical Character Recognition (OCR) API:
content: The Tesseract OCR engine, as was the HP Research Prototype [8]. Since 2006 it is developed by Google .It is an offline Application Programming Interface (API) library for Optical Character Recognition (OCR). Due to different fonts OCR detection is a difficult process and requires lot of effort to train the system because different transcripts use different  font style. Broadly speaking there are two ways to recognize a text. First is pattern recognition (based on entirety of text) and second is feature recognition (detecting individual lines and characters). heading: 94 Chapter 4 Application Programming Interfaces (API): |
content: When we need to convert a textual image into editable format we can use this API. For that first of all we need add the specific language trained data set in our application that will activate the specific Tessaract classes we need to use in the process, e.g. we have used eng.traineddata file in our application, so that it can convert English textual image into editable format. Then we need to import TessBaseAPI in order to use built -in methods like ‘checkFiles ()’, copyFiles (), etc. of the API. Then we pass a textual image using mTess.setImage (image) to these methods and get editable text using mTess.getUTF8Text (). After that we can display the text anywhere we want. heading: 5.1 Overview
content: While reading when people encounter a problem then they can open RATES application, which has two modules, desktop and android. Working of each module is same along with some constraints. However, each module is described below with screen shots of working criteria. When user open the application it asks user to take image from gallery or any other storage area or user can take ima ge via camera. When selects image from storage or take image via camera, application shows a window to adjust the width and height of the image. User can select the knobs and adjust the size of the image and press OK. When user press Apply Optical Character Recognition (OCR) button, RATES scans the image through Tessaract OCR Application Programming Interface ( API) which allows the recognition of printed characters. It also allows photo scanning of the text character -by-character, analysis of the scanned -in image, and then translation of the character image into editable format. Therefore user gets an editable text format of the textual image. When user selects text  then all the RATES operation like Find Dictionary, Translate  text, Search on Internet, Text to Speech, Get Summary, and other  operations like copy, cut, select and even delete operation  become active for  the selected text . When use press on ‘find dictionary’ option the application requests Oxford dictionary API and gets short definition, word history, usage example, word class, synonyms, antonyms and pronunciation for the select word. When user taps on ‘translate text’ then the application display list of multiple languages and user has to select one target language. When  user selects one target language, RATES requests Google translator API and gets translated text of selected language for the selected text. When user selects ‘search on internet’ option for the specific text or image, app provides more specific options for searching such as ‘search related content’ and ‘search via keyword’. When user selects ‘search related contents’, i t provides online results based on selected contents . While when ‘search via keyword ’ is clicked, a list of keywords appear and user selects a keyword and gets google search result based on the select keyword for the selected content. When user selects ‘text to speech’ option for the selected text, RATES starts to read out the selected text. While when user select ‘get  summary’ for the select ed paragraph or paragraphs, the application display menu for summary length (standard, medium and extended). User selects summary length. The application analyses paragraph. It extracts the main idea and provide summary  of respective length. When user select an image, RATES display two options ‘search on internet’ and ‘label image contents’. Search on internet works like ‘search related contents’ which is described above. When user selects ‘label image contents’, RATES sends request to Google Vision API  and gets labelled image, which detects individual objects and faces in image and also provides description of all set of objects. heading: 5.3.2 Apply OCR
content: In this phase, OCR (Tesseract OCR) is apply to input file (if text image is input by the user). It converts the text image into editable and researchable text. Input image is limited to 64 fonts in total. Handwriting image is not appreciated while applying the OCR on current image. Moreover, pre-processing on input image can improve the accuracy of the result. A well colour contrast and horizontally aligned text can make the results more optimal. Sometimes, phase does not read the header of the input image.  There are numerous tools available in toolbar to achieve the desire accuracy of the input text image. heading: 6.2 Unit Testing
content: Unit testing is a parameter of test -driven-development and it is a part of software development process. It is often perform to identify the problems at early stage of the development, so fever compound errors occur. In this process, the smallest testable part of an application, called units, are inspected individually and independently for proper functioning. All the modules of RATES are divided in a way that they can perform the expected operations separately. We have taken every single operation as a single unit. We have written a test case for every single function. We have tested and executed all the test cases individually and independently and got the required results. The basic purpose of the unit testing was to ensure and compare th e expected results with actual results. Moreover, unit testing is done so if the expected results would have not found then failed test cases revised again to get the required results.

heading: 6.3 Integration Testing
content: Integration testing is a phase where individually and independently units are combined together and tested. Units are tested as a group. We have integrated correlated units as a group and tested them to achieve the desired functionality. Navigating to file system unit is integrated to OCR (for text image) and image thumbnail and image vision. Were OCR unit is integrated with translation, summary, related search, text-to-speech, keyword based searching and dictionary units. During the integration of these units we have exposed some faults and later revised those faults to get the expected outcomes. In order to assist the integration testing test, test driven and stubs were used.

heading: 6.4 Acceptance Testing
content: For the acceptability of RATES, we have conducted acceptance testing. The greater benefit we have achieved after this phase was to evaluate the application’s compliance with the requirements (proposed idea). Moreover, this phase has given the idea whether the application meets the requirements of delivery or not. We have conducted this testing after the improvement phase but at deployment phase. We also came to know that our proposed project is going to target a great range of people.

heading: 1. Introduction
content: Every year some people are missing, and the major issue is that the representatives of these people are wasting too much time to search them in different places. Anyon e whose whereabouts cannot be established will be considered as missing until located, and their well -being or otherwise  confirmed. Finding lost person can be a difficult task. The currently available Manual System for  finding missing person have very long  procedure and takes more time. More time is required for  launching a FIR (First Information Report) in police station. Also, time required for finding lost  person is more. It is possible that they faced some accident and went to hospitals. On the other ha nd, some people lost homes due to some family matters and went to orphan’s house as well as some other  different NGOs. The finding of these John Doe/Jane Doe is quite a challenging task. So, with the help  of the public, we will develop an Android application which will be installed in their smart  phones which will be connected to every NGO and hospitals in the city. When any person brings to these  hospitals or NGOs their data will be uploaded to this application, and their representatives can easily  track t hem by searching.  Moreover, the representative of these missing persons will also be notified.  This is an android application for free, dedicated to missing persons. It keeps  track of all information pertaining to a missing person such as the name, age, CNIC and more, all on your mobile device. The purpose of this application is to  assist in finding the relatives of the people who have gone missing or been admitted to the hospital for  treatment, and whose personal details and families are not known. This application provides a cross -platform solution for finding missing persons from any device, any operating system, and any screen  size. Using these programs, you can: • Search for a person using text or photo. • Apply sorting and filtering to search results. • Add/Delete/Edit missing persons. • Notify the representatives of the missing persons.

heading: 2.7 Software Development life Cycle Model
content: We are using the incremental model for our project. The  incremental build model is a method of software development where the model is  designed, implemented and  tested incrementally (a little more is added each time) until the product is finished. It involves both development and maintenance. The product is defined as finished when i t satisfies all its requirements. This model combines the elements of the waterfall model with the iterative philosophy of prototyping. The product is decomposed into several components, each of which is designed and built separately (termed as builds). Ea ch component is delivered to the client when it is complete. This allows partial utilization of the product and avoids a long development time. It also avoids a large initial capital outlay and subsequent long waiting period. This model of development also  helps ease the traumatic effect of introducing a completely new system all at once. There are, however, several problems with this model.

Our main purpose of using this model is that it is easy to test, and functionalities can easily provide. Until now we worked on databases and web development. In future we will merge android with web. In first phase we will implement data bases and in second phase we will implement web technologies (web -site development).

content: The software development life cycle which we used in our project is iterative model.

Iterative model is a model in which process starts with simple implementation of small set of software Requirements which are gathered previously. Further iterations are performed to the evolving Version until complete system is formed which is ready for deployment.

heading: Software Development Life Cycle
content: Software development life cycle defines a strategy for enhancing the qu ality of software and general development process.  We used waterfall approach for our project. In waterfall appr oach entire procedure is divided  into discrete stages, and result of one stage acts as input for next stage , that’s why it is sequential model. The following table list out the advantages and disadvantages of waterfall model.

heading: Pros                                   Cons
content: • Waterfall approach is Simple and easy to utilize. • Only one phase at a time is processed. • If require ments are fully understood then this approach works admirably for little project. • No ambiguity, all stages are characterized clearly. • Simple to organize tasks. • This methodology doesn't function admirably for large projects. • This methodology can’ t accommodate change in requirements • Amount of risk and uncertainty is relatively large. • Hard to measure progress with in stages.

Problems Faced and Lessons Learned: This project was very challenging for us. The challenges we faced were:

heading: The
content: development of an android application was a new task for us as there was no single course existed in our degree relevant to android application development.

heading: We
content: studied detection and recognition using haar-cascades, so we tried to do camera detection using haar-cascades.

heading: For
content: this purpose we collected positive images (images of number plates in

heading: Punjab)
content: and negative images(Any random images) and trained

heading: But
content: unfortunately their integration with the android application was not much efficient.

heading: Our
content: algorithm was not fast enough. So we had to use Open ALPR for detection and recognition purpose.

heading: The
content: data storage was also a difficult task.

heading: We
content: collected the data from several processes.

heading: First
content: of all the owner and vehicle details were extracted from

heading: QR
content: code was generated and stored.

heading: Saving
content: all this data in the database and then generating tables and graphs from this data was a huge task.

heading: This
content: project was developed to facilitate traffic police of

heading: Pakistan
content: by detecting stolen vehicles in real time in an automated way.

heading: We
content: developed an android application as well as a website for this purpose.

heading: In
content: the application we detect the number of vehicle and obtain its relevant information.

heading: We
content: also store extra information like

heading: Code
content: which is then printed and can be used for scanning next time so that when we want to inspect the same car we will just scan the

heading: Code
content: and all information will be displayed.

heading: All
content: this information will be represented in the form of tables and graphs on the website for better understanding of data.

heading: Some
content: applications are available already which are somehow related to our project but our application is more automated, can be used in real time and have larger number of functionalities comparatively.
