heading: Abstract
content: In the digital world of computers, several software applications have been developed to ensure spellings of various words. English language is found to have gone far  ahead in development for spell checking applications whilst other languages specifically naming Urdu, lack behind to cherish such technologies. Our project “The Urdu Spell Checker” handles detecting incorrect spellings of a word and providing a list of op tions containing correct spellings with other possible words of similar text formation alongside; latter is chosen on priority basis [Tahira and Sarmad 2007]. The application carries correct spellings of words residing inside a predefined lexicon or corpus . It is to ensure whether entered word is correct or not. In case the input matches corpus, word is considered correct. Furthermore, the application provides an interface to enter words which are to be checked. Although not worldwide, but Urdu spell checker application is a big necessity for people of Pakistan reason being Urdu to be the national language of the country. Now developed, the application can help Urdu writers, poets, journalists and other workers in similar fields save their time checking spellings manually and rely on this application software to correct the spellings for them. Table of Contents

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Issue of programmed spell checking is not new in the ranges of Information Retrieval and Language processing. The exploration began as early as 1960s. A wide range of procedures for discovery and amendment of spelling errors are proposed since past 40 years. Some o f these procedures exploit general spelling mistake patterns while others utilize the phonetics of incorrectly spelled word to discover likely correct words. Lately, statistic based procedures, which are not exclusively based on error trends but through tr aining, adjust to error patterns, have gained greater prevalence. Many of these techniques are being utilized with text editors and other context handling and are demonstrating great execution. All things considering the issue of spell checking is as yet thought to be open for additionally research and upgrades. There are two reasons behind considering this issue still unsolved; one has to do with the execution of existing methods and other with their scope. For the first reason in Natural Language Proces s it is advanced over the year. The text that is computed is sufficient and errorless. But as far as we are concerned about the human implies spellchecker it is so much reliable. Automated spellcheckers have few choices which the replace the word with. But with human implemented spellchecker we have a plenty of choice and we choose the word accordingly which is actually 100% correct. This level of accuracy has not been achieved. The second reason for considering the spell checker application is that the ar ea of this language is not so vast. As we consider English or Latin languages much work have been done in it. Every language spellchecker has a boundary in checking other language. In English spellchecker you want to check the spelling of French you will f ail on the first step because it is outside the boundary of the system. Therefore, even English which is very vast language is limited in its scope. From the above discussion it is concluded that for making a new spell checker software one has to clearly i dentify the language specific issues and deeply investigate general spelling error trends of the language, only then a reasonably effective spell checking approach can be proposed. Urdu is also a language which is written differently  from English. It has its own patterns and technique of writing. Therefore, existing techniques will not be applicable on this language without modification. This document presents the details of a study performed on Urdu language to identify the problem areas of Urdu spell che cking and to test the effectiveness of existing spell checking techniques on Urdu. So we have given a  hybrid approach for Urdu spelling error correction which uses a combination of more than one existing techniques. These techniques are modified to cater U rdu specific problems and make the software or technique reliable.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The project revolves around the concept of following statement: “For an incorrect word to be spell checked against a given list of valid Urdu words, it should be replaced with the closest possible valid word.”

heading: 9 of 32  31 May 2018
content: Objectives the spell checker app has covered are: • Detection of spelling errors from text by following a defined algorithm. • Provision of a number of options for correct possible words. • Enhancement of readability of text that is input by user. • Prevention of mistakes being committed by  user in important and sensitive documents. • Prevention of adding any incorrect word to corpus/database by user. User is given freedom to have last call on replacement of the word.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: Following are the problems from the perspective of user: • Lack of grip on Urdu vocabulary results in incorrect context. • Less interaction with Urdu language leads to spelling mistakes. • Difficulty in typing a certain word. These factors result in fr ustration and disappointment for the user along with undesired time delay causing user dissatisfaction and unease regardless of the various benefits provided by an Urdu text editor.

heading: 2.1.1 According to the History
content: Spelling mistake is a common phenomenon that occurs while writing text. It needs to be detected and corrected. Hence, spell checking was taken under research consideration with advent of text processing becoming common to users in computer world. Fred J. Damerau provided some basic techniques for the purpose of spell checking. According to him, spell checking is process of any input being compared to acceptable terms in a master list. If t here is no match found then input is rejected. Errors that were brought into light by Damerau were: ❖ Substitution- where a letter substitutes another letter by mistake ❖ Insertion- where a letter is added somewhere in the word by mistake ❖ Deletion- where a letter is deleted from anywhere in the word by mistake ❖ Transposition- where two letters in a word are swapped by mistake Table 2. 1 Types of errors in Urdu Error type Correct word Misspelled word

heading: 2.1.2 Classification of Spelling Error
content: Urdu language does not only contain words that have similar sound but also those which have similar structure for example [د ,ذ]. This increases the chance of typing errors. These errors are classified into two main categories that are, cognitive error and typographical error. Typographical error occurs when user enters incorrect word by mistake even though he knows the correct spellings.

heading: 11 of 32  31 May 2018
content: Cognitive error is occurred when user is not aware of correct spellings and gets confused due to homophonic sound. These types themselves hold errors mentioned by Demarau. According to a study, some data was taken from a newspaper which depicted how Urdu language has chances of error among visibly similar and phonetically similar words. They include: • Minimum Edit Distance- measures distance of difference between two strings • Similarity Key Technique- based on sound similarity • Jaro Distance- measures distance of similarity between two strings There has been a lot of research on spelling correction in different  languages including Urdu ever since computer revolution. Different researchers have provided multiple studies and techniques to solve issues of spelling errors including above mentioned literature review. heading: 5.1 Problems Faced and Lessons Learned
content: Time management is a crucial factor while work ing on a project besides catching up with regular studies. The biggest challenge for us was to manage time for our project with scope alongside. It was because hectic schedule of university and abundant workload of courses left us with little time to work on the project. This challenge certainly taught us to have a grip on managing time. Also, it helped us plan our time constraints for the project. Furthermore, as our project is researched based and we started from scratch, exploring everything related to U rdu spell checker was extremely tough for us . We observed the vast scope of this domain and research work in the  field. There were some changes in the requirements in the initial phases which could jeopardize our scope, but thankfully guidance from our supervisor helped us to tackle those issues. It was a problem to cope up with the scope upon introducing even minor changes in code. However, it was all resolved with team effort which helped us to coordinate with each other.

heading: 5.2 Project Summary
content: The project is based on a software application which helps a user with writing error free Urdu text. It provides user the facilities to correct any spelling mistakes committed. Developing this kind of application through research was undoubtedly a difficult task. However, writing the documentation played vital role in clarifying the concept of our project to a better level. It cleared out l atent ambiguities that could have highly affected development of our project otherwise. Moreover, most of the concepts we learned throughout the years of undergraduate degree got revised during different phases of development as well as documentation. Cour ses of Object Oriented Programming and Software Requirement Engineering were very beneficial from one end to another.

heading: 5.3 Future Work
content: Internet is one of the best ways to introduce and provide improved approach of technology to the world. The software we have developed is limited in terms of platforms. It is just a desktop application. However, in future we plan to come up with its web based version to augment its use. Also, we intend to merge it as a tool/add on for Microsoft Word to check the spellings. It already has the feature for incorrect English input word where it displays the list of related correct words; likewise, the add-on will provide same feature for Urdu language. Moreover, we plan to update the software to attach with other software systems as a build -in function that if we download software it will automatically downloaded along.

heading: .............................................................. 26 1 Introduction 1
content: 1.1 Introduction Issue of programmed spell checking is not new in the ranges of Information Retrieval and Language processing. The exploration began as early as 1960s. A wide range of procedures for discovery and amendment 1of spelling errors are proposed since past 40 years. Some of these procedures exploit general spelling mistake patterns while others utilize the phonetics of incorrectly spelled word to discover likely correct words. Lately, statistic based procedures, 1which are not exclusively based on error trends but through training, adjust to error patterns, have gained greater prevalence. Many 1of these techniques are being utilized with text editors and other context handling and are demonstrating great execution. All things considering the issue of spell checking is as yet thought to be 1open for additionally research and upgrades. There are two reasons behind considering this issue still unsolved; one has to do with the execution of existing methods and other with their scope. For the first reason in Natural Language Process it is advanced over the year. The text that is computed is sufficient and errorless. But as far as we are concerned about the human implies spellchecker it is so much reliable. Automated spellcheckers have few choices which the replace the word with. But with human implemented spellchecker we have a plenty of choice and we choose the word accordingly which is actually 100% correct. 1This level of accuracy has not been achieved. The second reason for considering the spell checker application is that the area of this language is not so vast. As we consider English or Latin languages much work have been done in it. Every language spellchecker has a boundary in checking other language. In English spellchecker you want to check the spelling of French you will fail on the first step because it is outside the boundary of the system. Therefore, even English which is very vast language is limited in its scope. From the above discussion it is concluded that for making a new spell checker software 1one has to clearly identify the language specific issues and deeply investigate general spelling error trends of the language, only then a reasonably effective spell checking approach can be proposed. Urdu is also a language which is written differently from English. It has its own patterns and technique of writing. Therefore, existing techniques will not be applicable on this language without modification. 1This document presents the details of a study performed on Urdu language to identify the problem areas of Urdu spell checking and to test the effectiveness of existing spell checking techniques on Urdu. So we have given a 1hybrid approach for Urdu spelling error correction which uses a combination of more than one existing techniques. These techniques are modified to cater Urdu specific problems and make the software or technique reliable. 1.2 Objectives The project revolves around the concept of following statement: “For an incorrect word to be spell checked against a given list of valid Urdu words, it should be replaced with the closest possible valid word.” Objectives the spell checker app has covered are: ? ? ? ? Detection of spelling errors from text by following a defined algorithm. Provision of a number of options for correct possible words. Enhancement of readability of text that is input by user. Prevention of mistakes being committed by user in important and sensitive documents. ? Prevention of adding any incorrect word to corpus/database by user. User is given freedom to have last call on replacement of the word. 1.3 Problem Statement Following are the problems from the perspective of user: ? Lack of grip on Urdu vocabulary results in incorrect context. ? Less interaction with Urdu language leads to spelling mistakes. ? Difficulty in typing a certain word. These factors result in frustration and disappointment for the user along with undesired time delay causing user dissatisfaction and unease regardless of the various benefits provided by an Urdu text editor. 1.4 Assumptions and Constraints Assumptions of our project include the following: 1. Take input from user. 2. Find input word in corpus. 3. Return error to user if no match is found. 4. Replace incorrect word with correct one on user’s command. 5. Store file in the memory. Constraints of developing Urdu Spell Checker are as follows: 1.4.1 Scope Constraint: ? The application has functions which detect the error. ? The application has functions for calculating error rate. ? The application has functions for replacing incorrect words. ? The database has most words from Urdu language. 1.4.2 Time Constraint ? Processing time of database is long which is balanced out by reducing execution time of error correction functions. ? Extra features such as smart text and auto text are excluded to increase accuracy of main functionality of software. 1.5 Project Scope Scope of our project revolves around how the application is going to facilitate the user. It is as follows: ? Major focus is on facilitating the user in writing an error free document. ? User is provided with a user friendly interface to interact with the application. ? User has to work on the platform and easily catch up any typing mistakes. ? Project team has worked along project supervisor in order to control scope. ? Team members have made sure that tasks executed are not different than those mentioned in the WBS dictionary. 2 Requirements 6Analysis 2.1 Literature Review 2.1.1 According to the History Spelling mistake is a common phenomenon that occurs while writing text. It needs to be detected and corrected. Hence, spell checking was taken under research consideration with advent of text processing becoming common to users in computer world. Fred J. Damerau provided some basic techniques for the purpose of spell checking. 2According to him, spell checking is process of any input being compared to acceptable terms in a master list. If there is no match found then input is rejected. Errors that were brought into light by Damerau were: ? Substitution- where a letter substitutes another letter by mistake ? Insertion- where a letter is added somewhere in the word by mistake ? Deletion- where a letter is deleted from anywhere in the word by mistake ? Transposition- where two letters in a word are swapped by mistake Table 2. 1 Types of errors in Urdu 2Error type Correct word Misspelled word Substitution ﻧﺎﺗﺳﮑﺎپ ﻧﺎﺗﺻﮑﺎپ Insertion

content: 2.1.2طوﺑظم طوظﺑمClassification of Spelling Error Urdu language does not only contain words that have similar sound but also those which have similar structure for example [ د, ذ]. This increases the chance of typing errors. These errors are classified into two main categories that are, 13cognitive error and typographical error. Typographical error occurs when user enters incorrect word by mistake even though he knows the correct spellings. Cognitive error is occurred when user is not aware of correct spellings and gets confused due to homophonic sound. These types themselves hold errors mentioned by Demarau. According to a study, some data was taken from a newspaper which depicted how Urdu language has chances of error among visibly similar and phonetically similar words. Table 2. 2 Single edit distance errors in Urdu 2Total errors Visually Similar Phonetically similar Substitution 75 40 12 Deletion 42 4 5 Insertion 21 2 1 Transposition 12 3 0 Total 150 49 18 2.1.3 Techniques for Spelling Error Correction The correction of errors is comprised of three phases: 1. Detection of incorrect word 2. Searching possible matches for the incorrect word 3. Replacing incorrect word with correct word depending upon match strength There are a number of techniques that are applied to perform above mentioned phases. They include: ? 2Minimum Edit Distance- measures distance of difference between two strings ? Similarity Key Technique- based on sound similarity ? Jaro Distance- measures distance of similarity between two strings There has been a lot of research on spelling correction in different languages including Urdu ever since computer revolution. Different researchers have provided multiple studies and techniques to solve issues of spelling errors including above mentioned literature review. This sums up the state of art on Urdu spell checking. 2.2 Stakeholders List The stakeholders of this project include the following: ? Developers ? Supervisor ? heading: Project Abstract
content: Game Cosmos is a integrating solution for software developers who have to who have to write lines of code again and again for integrating different social networking services into their games and software with cloud based services. These s ervices include Leader Board, Achievements, Localization, Social Authentication and Cloud Storage. Game Cosmos will be used by different developers to include in their own game code via a plug and play module to allow them to use the services being provide d by us. Developers will be able to use the same portal for both ANDRIOD and IOS platform games. Its main purpose will be to ease the developers by helping then in stopping them having to rewrite the same code again and again so that it helps in such a way  that they won’t have to reinvent the wheel every time they have a game development project. Instead they can integrate our Game Cosmos module into their code and spend the time where they were originally supposed to invest in different areas of software development for instance making gameplay better and integrating more functionalities in their game. By helping software developers reduce the code they have to write they will have much more time to make their software much better, their time investment in a project will be lessened and their software could be much better and their work flow will be progressing at optimal levels. This shift software development will be beneficial for the software developer in ways which reduce the amount of time which is req uired to make a software or game and by reducing their time on development of a single project they will have time to invest in many other projects which in term will help them develop more software in a shorter time span. This will not only prove improvement for the average software developer but very much so for the market as well with more products coming out in shorter and shorter time span.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: In the current market software developers do not have enough time. In our case the time to integrate different social authentication modules via code. If they do however do it, it costs them much more time than should be required to do so. For instance if they have to integrate Facebook in their games login they would have to write a hectic amount of code which will allow them to do so and will evidently result in extreme time loss. The market is saturated with solutions like brain cloud app42 which do the job for the most part but don’t provide a custom package which makes it difficult and the tiring and constricted use of multiple service providers (like the above mentioned) is required. That is why software developers have to use multiple so lutions like Braincloud, app42 and other solutions which in term uses much more of their time. Our goal is to save the developers’ time by removing the factor of rewriting code each time whenever they need to integrate. This will be done by providing the game developer a set of plug and play modules so that he may allocate and focus most of his time implementing the gameplay of the modules. Which will provide social login to commute with friends, localization so that people all over the world may enjoy the game in native language, Achievements and Leader board giving the player a reason to continue playing the game as well as making the game more competitive. With all this another feature will be cloud services which will ensure that the user’s game progress is always secure and accessible and retrievable from any mobile device at any place any time via login. By using modules developers won’t have the need to re -invent the wheel again.

heading: 1.1.1 Leader Board
content: Leader Board will allow different players to see who can get the higher score this will especially be good for friends to compete with one another. It will bring a competitive environment to the game’s social nature and add another aspect of good fun. Also  this will make user tune in more to play the game in order to see where his/her friends are in terms of their scores. The leader board will be divided into categories of Daily, Weekly, Monthly and even all around top rank.

heading: 1.1.2 Achievements
content: As users progress in the game and complete certain tasks new achievements will be unlocked and experience points will be awarding upon completion of a particular achievements. These can be from, the total hours put in playing the game to even most kills, depending  in the game format. Every game that uses the achievement API will have its own achievement hierarchy. Achievements are a panicle of a games progression. Once a player progresses in the game he/she will unlock newer and more precious achievements. In the s ocial aspect of the game achievements play a vital role. The achievements will define how good the client is at a particular game the reason being they become harder to achieve as the game progresses.

heading: 1.1.3 Localization
content: The localization API will a llow users/players from different locations in the world to choose the run the game in the language they prefer. This will allow people to comfortably interact with and understand the Unity Game U.I (User Interface). This in term will provide the users to have a more localized experience per say because of the nature of their language being in the game. Also this will make the user experience much better than before as the language that is selected comes naturally to the client at hand. This will probably and in some cases certainly give us more satisfied clients who would navigate around the game much more easily.

heading: 1.1.4 Cloud
content: Firebase will be used to create a cloud platform such as the Google Play, Brain Cloud and App42.It cloud will be used to upload a particu lar players game high scores achievements and other game progression milestones and will be present in the database where the results will be compared. These comparisons will help update the Leader Board and Achievements will be unlocked according to what task one has completed in the game. Cloud will also save the players progress status indefinitely so that even if he/she loses the phone, logging in the cloud from a new device will result in restoration of game process.

heading: 1.1.5 Social Authentication
content: Social Authentication will allow user to use their current Gmail, Facebook accounts to get access to the cloud services. Instead of making new accounts the users data will be automatically taken from the previous account he/she created in the past with other forms of  social media such as Facebook, Gmail and other accounts like mentioned above. Social authentication will automatically allow social friends to compare game statistics such as their leaderboards, achievements and other various forms of progression via the cloud storage provided by the server and keep players game data or game progression more secure ensuring only he or she plays from a particular account and no one else also saving their achievements with the help of their previous social media accounts. The entire above -mentioned API will run on both ANDRIOD and IOS. This will be done through testing the API in 2 games, one made for each operating system.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Our goal this to provide all the above-mentioned features in on single customized package so that an ease will be created for the developers by saving them time and making the process of integrating different modules much more simpler and easier for them .  Developers will be able to implement the package into their games without having to change the code for every single game that they create and all of the above features will be integrated by themselves into their games. They will only need to focus on how  to use these modules in their game play. Also, it won’t be necessary to implement the entire package, developers may integrate a single or multiple module of their choosing. This in term will allow the game developers to focus their precious time on making their games much better and helping them produce more games in a shorter amount of time.

heading: 1.5 Project scope
content: Unity has captured 1/3rd of the mobile gaming market, it is the most widely used game engine by developers of both ANDRIOD and IOS games and is also used for various other platforms as well. Users from both platforms will be able to compete with one another with will enhance the competitive experience in games. The usage of cloud storage wi ll allow the users to play care free of their progression. This would mean that their data will be very secure and will remain safe because it is being stored on a different system. The users will benefit from this in various ways because this will not onl y allow them to save their game achievements, high scores and other various forms of game progression according to their games respective developers but also they would know where they stand in the current market. This could possibly attract new gamers and also enthusiast gamers which will compete with one another to and will form a community which will be gaming together to see who is on top. In the current tenure cloud base services are a must for all gamers as it reduces memory usage. Bringing cloud stor age to the game development and gaming community mix will enhance the gaming experience. Localization will allow users to play the game in their own and understand it in their own language which would help them enjoy different users to enjoy the game play from all over the world. Social login will allow the users to interact with one another and ease their coming in to the gaming community as they won’t have to enter a new account which they may lose the password for instead they will enjoy the experience without the need for doing so as they would use the account they did before hand in other social media. The project being made will not only be for mobile gaming but with future enhancements can be used for AAA tiles such a Battlefield, Call of duty. Multip layer games such as Counter Strike can also use the API to further improve cloud based actions. Current cloud solutions miss out on some of the APIs and developers have to integrate 2 or more cloud solutions to their game. Our solution will reduce this fac tor by including solutions from different platforms and some self-build ones to one custom build package.

heading: 2.1.1 Google Play Services
content: Google is one of the largest play service providers. [1] It provides all the functionalities required in for mobile gaming. These include cloud storage for game saves. Leader boards for local games as well as achievement unlocks at different levels of a ga me. Alongside this it keeps track of the total number of games played according their genre and keeps track of the games that were played associated with a particular Google Account. Example: xxxx@gmail.com. The problem in this is that this cloud platform is limited to ANDRIOD

heading: 2.1.2 BrainCloud
content: BrainCloud is a readymade, cloud -based backend which is used for the development of games and different social applications. [2] It provides monetization, so developers may use this feature to put in app purchases to improve game experience and make money off what they have offered to the game enthusiasts of the world. Multiplayer games can be developed with the help of social network fram ework, also a BrainCloud API, along -side multiplatform support for games. BrainClouds multiplayer support includes random match making with player active around the globe and even with friends if using the social network framework. A great example to descr ibe the multiplayer API is the Clash of Clans game. Also included are push notifications so you don’t miss out on any of the updates as well as customisable promotion campaigns.

heading: 2.1.3 App42
content: App42 is an online API call service which provides data storage solution, leader boards and other essentials online services [3]. This service is widely known and trusted by many reputed and recognized companies such as Reliance entertainment, Kodak, Hungama.com, 99games and other highly recognized companies. This provides a  very effective cloud solution for Banking, Insurance, Gaming, Media and other problems that commonly occur. Currently App42 has 800+ APIs, 25+ modules and 16 SDKs. This service is providing over 90 Billion API calls with 100,000 calls per minute at this date to its users.

heading: 2.1.4 GAMESPARKS
content: Gamesparks is also an online API service which has all the services mentioned above related to games [4]. It provides a single environment/platform which is compatible with various operating systems such as IOS, Android, Windows, Mac, Unreal Engine, XBOX, Playstation and many more. The platform provides Social and Multiplayer services such as real -time chats, tournaments, matchmaking, et c. Live game operations are also available in this cloud service such as player management; this facility is used to provide a summary of real time game play of a particular player. Other services include segmentation Analytics, Ca mpaigns and Marketing Automation, Notification and Messaging, Authentication, Test harness (Testing your APIs through device simulation) etc. It provides integration services as well.

heading: 2.6 Software development life cycle model
content: Iterative uses the basic idea to develop a system through repeated cycles. We are implementing this model on our module and package as it helps us to do iteration time to time. This process minimizes the expected errors as different iterations lead us to d evelop a better product. It allows us to learn from the experience from the development that took place earlier parts or versions of the product. The major requirement of our project is known but minor details are yet to be figured out, so this will help t o make changes as we move along thus making our final product efficient and affective attracting the eyes of many developers. This will help us in stepping to the game market as our product make the lives of developers an ease as well as make the game user experience more immersive. This model is explained by the following figure

heading: Iterative Design (Figure 7)
content: Advantages of Iterative model: In iterative model we can only create a high -level design of the application before we actually begin to build the product and define the design solution for the entire product. Later on, we can design and built a skeleton version of that, and then evolved the design based on what had been built. In iterative model we are building and improving the produc t step by step. Hence, we can track the defects at early stages. This avoids the downward flow of the defects. In iterative model we can get the reliable user feedback. When presenting sketches and blueprints of the product to users for their feedback, we are effectively asking them to imagine how the product will work. In iterative model less, time is spent on documenting and more time is given for designing. Disadvantages of Iterative model: Each phase of an iteration is rigid with no overlaps Costly system architecture or design issues may arise because not all requirements are gathered up front for the entire lifecycle

heading: 3.6 Database Diagram
content: Data in MongoDB has a flexible schema. Unlike SQL databases, where you must think, determine and declare a table’s schema/outline before inserting data, MongoDB’s collections do not enforce or need a document structure prior to insertion of da ta. This flexibility facilitates the mapping of documents to an entity or an object. Each document can match the data fields of the represented entity, even if the data has of considerable important variation. In practice, however, the documents in a colle ction share a similar structure or are of the same type. The key challenge in data modeling is balancing the needs of the application, the performance characteristics of the database engine, and the data retrieval patterns. When designing data models, always consider the application usage of the data (i.e. queries, updates, and processing of the data) as well as the inherent structure of the data itself.

heading: Document Structure
content: The key decision in designing data models for MongoDB applications revolves around  the structure of documents and how the application represents relationships between data. There are two tools that allow applications to represent these relationships: References and Embedded Data.

heading: References
content: References store the relationships between d ata by including links or references from one document to another. Applications can resolve these references to access the related data. Broadly, these are normalized data models.

heading: Embedded Data
content: Embedded documents capture relationships between data by storing related data in a single document structure. MongoDB documents make it possible to embed document structures in a field or array within a document. These denormalized data  models allow applications to retrieve and manipulate related data in a single database operation. Due to the flexibility that MogoDB allows to the user and no generic schema it is difficult to plan the database structure as the database adapts itself acc ording to the json objects or the values needed to be entered.

heading: 1. NO SQL:
content: Working with a noSQL backend database system was a major challenge. It was not as simple as it seemed on the outside. The problems raised when we integrating the module with our test game. The best thing we could do was google it all out and start completely fresh. The conver ting of classes into Json objects which were then received by the server finally at the end really helped us to cover major new grounds on the base of this project. Once that task was finally completed the rest became much simpler and defined for us.

heading: 2. Generic/Modularity:
content: Another problem we faced but couldn’t predict was making our system package modular and generic. The simplistic opinion we kept was that we would make a package which would automatically adapt to any games backend environment but we were proven wrong because our knowledge on the subject was not up to the mark. Every game has a different backend environment and adapting to such environments is a task that is really hard to do properly.

heading: 3. Centralization of Code
content: Centralization of code was difficult because we weren’t using project management systems which caused problems catastrophically regarding the stitching of our code together. We were trying stitching our code properly for hours and hours on end because of our lack of experience in this end o f our system. Overcoming this was a major hurdle in our progression. It was difficult but as it was done very easily by using a project management system called trello.

heading: 5.2 Project summary
content: Game Cosmos will help us provide different game developers different features and modules so that they will be aided by saving their time. They won’t have to do the hectic task of reinventing the wheel again and again but instead they just have to download  a package provided by us and integrate it into their software/game which will save them an etiquette amount of time. This will allow our game developers to focus the majority of their time in making a much more professional and customer/client oriented game which will in term make their project much better and fruitful by giving the software/game developers more satisfied clients. We are using BaaS (Backend as a service) using firebase to provide our mobile app developers a way to link their applications t o backend cloud storage and APIs. Although a new industry, trends indicate these services are gaining more and more popularity with enterprise customers.

heading: 5.3 Future work
content: After the implementation of this system more modules can be added to the pa ckage, such as push notifications, monetization etc. These modules can be moved from the gaming sector to Retail, Media, Insurance, Banking and Travel. The Data Base used for the package can be refined to be used in these sectors. Support can also be added  to the system to help developers when they come face to face with problems integrating the modules. This is a project where expansion is limitless. All that stands in between is how broadly you can think and how much innovative your mind can be. Furthermo re this will allow us to add advertisement to our games. Our attention was caught by AdMob. It is a monetization technique launched recently by Google which allows us to run adds on our software via our leader boards and other facilities that we provide. It is supported by Firebase which will allow us to gain profit from our project and hopefully help us financially also this will help us know where our project lies in the current market. If this doesn’t work we will upload our code to GitHub and allow different developers to enhance our code and help them help us to make a better product for all of us.

heading: Project Abstract
content: Keeping in view the problems of existing higher educational system, facilities do not ensure the availability of teachers of all subjects to the greatest extent in the exact and assigned time frame. In case of absence of teachers, there is no proper system to ensure the commencement of lectures to minimize the ratio of missing lectures. Also it disturbs the students and institute’s schedule in case of makeup lectures and it wastes a lot of time to arrange time slot with space acquisition. We are just puttin g in our efforts to maximize the utilization of teacher’s knowledge in universities having the similar contents. In this project we will be providing HEC a centralized system having registered subject based teachers as data entities. HEC registered teacher  of any institute will apply for leave using this system, our system will search for teachers as visiting faculty nearby having similar domain after approval of leave, system will forward requests to nearby teachers, first within same institute if any avai lable otherwise it forwards request to externals within in specified distance. All the progress of teachers will be monitored by central body HEC. It will also be able to approve and terminate the teacher’s membership from the system.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: In Pakistan there are many flaws in educational system, one of the major issue is that there is no such a system for educational institutes which ensures the time scheduling issue and teachers availability in absence of any teacher or in case of shortage of any subject based teacher in any institute under HEC. However there are some universities based systems in western countries which tackles some similar problems but there is no such a centralized system in Pakistan. So we are proposing ADHOC Centralized Teachers Availability And Monitoring System Using Ontology For HEC. This is the system which ensures the lecture delivery in institutes to minimize the missing lectures ratio to improve our educational system and to best utilize the availability of internal and external teachers in their free timings so we may be able to avoid rescheduling of missing lectures, which may cause disturbance of routine and wastage of time. Every teacher of universities will register in this HEC centralized system by secure and accurate mechanism. Also that teacher will be the permanent or visiting faculty member of any university under HEC regulations. The purpose is to use HEC owned resources when required to any other university within the distance concerns. Any permanent faculty member when wants to avail a leave, he/she will apply through this system. After authorization from university, similar subject- based teacher will be searched by the system. System will check their availability, their presence in specified distance and forward request. Then system will ask their accessibility under visiting faculty rules and regulations with sharing lecture contents that needs to be delivered. However lecture material will be provided after accepting the lecture request from the system. There are three steps involved in our project where we apply different data techniques; we are using no SQL technique so all data related to system will be arranged semantically by using editor protégé tool  to make Ontology. The structurally arranged d ata would be in form of RDF/OWL format. Retrieval of data is done on basis of Semantics. Ontology describes the domain in terms of properties and classes which include description of different objects. SPARQL is an RDF query language that is used to generate queries to perform different operations and functions on the semantically arranged data , the data would be accessed and retrieved  by using SPARQL instead of SQL because our data is stored semantically. Our system will be web and android based. SPARQLlib is a PHP library to communicate with RDF files. EASYRDF will provide a way of interaction with RDF files using SPARQL.

heading: 2.3.2 Non-functional requirements
content: 2.3.2.1NFR01: Performance NFR01-01 Average load time of  the starting page of the application must be less than 2 second. NFR01-02 Average processing time taken by the system to complete a transaction/request should be less than 5 seconds. NFR01-03 System Mean Time to Failure should not be more than 60seconds within 24 hours of use. NFR01-04 Average system response time should not be greater than 4 seconds. NFR01-05 Web Application must successfully run on a client machine with 256 MB RAM or above. NFR01-06 Android Application must successfully run on Jelly Bean 4.1 or above. NFR01-07 500 Teachers should be able to simultaneously access the system and update the database. 2.3.2.2NFR02: Security NFR02-01 System must provide access to authorized users only that enter through the login module. NFR02-02 System must not provide access to ANY user EXCEPT the designated user to update the data. NFR02-03 No user can view data of any other user through any report or views provided by the applications. NFR02-04 After the end of a user Session, no information must be saved any where on the client machine. 2.3.2.3NFR03: Defects-Maintenance NFR03-01 Post Release defects of the system must not exceed 1 critical bug per month. NFR03-02 Post Release bug fixing should not take more than 5 hours. 2.3.2.4NFR04: Documentation NFR04-01 Help documentation must be complete in providing information about each and every module and functionality provided by the system. NFR04-02 Help option must be easily accessible on all system web pages. NFR04-03 Help must be written using minimal technical terms; any technical terms used must be additionally defined at the end of the document 2.3.2.5NFR05: Disaster Recovery NFR05-01 In case of client /server crash all information/data should be recoverable within 30 minutes of the incidence.

heading: 3.6 Entity Relationship Diagram

heading: 5.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: 1. Completing this document has not been without its challenges. We had decided to develop our application using RDF ontology instead of using SQL for storing data. In RDF ontology based system you need to learn SPARQL language and ontology design techniques. We didn’t learned ontology design and SPARQL language before in any course so it was a big problem for us first to learn ontology design and then SPARQL query language but our supervisor and co- supervisor were very supportive throughout this document she helped us a lot to learn SPARQL and to understand ontological engineering she taught us how to research and provided us with related articles so that we can learn easily. 2. For requirements gathering and finding out the existing similar systems it was also a challenge for us because we didn’t even find a single system with close similarities. As our system is totally different from existing systems so making literature review and adopting good features of existing systems was not easy for us. 3. Due to lack of similar systems, designing an interactive user design was a challenge for us. We spent enough time on thinking about interaction design of our application but we were not able to design it magically but luckily we were studying Human Computer Interaction course at university that helped us a lot in designing the interfaces of our applications with first designing the low fidelity prototypes and then high fidelity using automated tools. In this way we learned different designing techniques. 4.   Our project is both web and android based but we are using same data files for both applications. Designing different classes to interact with data files was difficult for us so our supervisor told us to develop REST API where both applications will interact with data files from one access point. It solved our problem for both applications now both applications will easily interact with data files. 5. We also faced problems in managing time at start of the project as we were studying other semester subjects also, managing time was not easy at start  but after sometime we get grip on work  and management because we followed the guidelines and planning of our supervisor and co-supervisor.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: The application we have produced, Albatross, is an android application that brings people even closer together by providing them a cheap and reliable source to find the people they care about. Albatross helps friends and family members look for their loved ones know by knowing their location in hour of need. Since typical tracking applications require GPS and internet connection simultaneously (referred to literature review) to track the mobile phones, our application will track them using GPS or connected cell towers location only, via SMS. The acknowledgement (hand-shake) between users will make them track each other, at any time, via the SMS service. Our application will be available on Android app store only. Major Albatross provides following functionalities:  Hand Shake.  GPS based tracking.  Cellular network based tracking.  Camera takes picture in case of 3 wrong unlocking attempts.  Wipe entire target’s mobile phones data.  Lock target’s mobile phone with target known custom password.  Ring and vibrate target mobile phone.  Location on SIM change.  Location on battery power less than set threshold.  Save tracked location history From above few, handshake, GPS based tracking and cellular based tracking work as follows: The users will download Albatross from the play store of their respective mobile phones. The user will then sign in to Albatross to become a member. Once a user has become a member, the members will then form hand-shakes with each other via SMS. Member 1 will send encrypted SMS (containing his / her IMEI number) to Member 2 for handshake access. A notification will be generated as the SMS reaches the Member 2 mobile phone. Member 2 will tap the notification to accept or decline the request. Member 1 can mean-while himself / herself, also, delete the sent handshake request. Member 2 will acknowledge (accept) member 1’s request. As member 2 accepts the request, Albatross will send an encrypted SMS to member 1 containing Member 2’s IMEI number. Albatross will save IMEI numbers of member 2 in member 1’s mobile phone and of member 1 in member 2’s mobile phone. This will be one time only and will allow the members, who have shaken hands, to access each other’s GPS

To track member 2, member 1 will select member 2 from white list. Member 1 then send encrypted SMS to member 2. Albatross at member 2’s mobile phone will get member 2’s GPS coordinates without letting the member 2 know. Albatross will send these GPS coordinates to member 1. Albatross at member 1 will plot those coordinates on the map and will pinpoint the location. If by any reason, Albatross at member 2’s mobile phone cannot get its GPS coordinates, Albatross shall identify the connected cell towers. Albatross will send the cell tower identities to member 1 via encrypted SMS. Albatross at member 1’s mobile phone will process the received cell tower data using internet. The processed data will get us precise location of member 2. Albatross will plot the location on map and will pinpoint precise location.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Our objective is to commercialize the use of affordable tracking; to make tracking less dependent on internet. Albatross’s services can be availed by other users who want affordable tracking system at their hand.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: Following problems provided a strong base for Albatross:  Current tracking gadgets have big prices.  Not every concerned person can purchase a tracking gadget for their loved ones like a tracker fitted transportation source or backpacks.  Current tracking gadgets are costly and cause fatigue to carry.  Current tracking applications offer services at costly membership plans ( some of them rounding to $50 per month).  Current applications use both internet and GPS to get location. o If GPS is off, last known location is of the trackee is sent.

o If the internet is unavailable, accuracy of the application decreases, and the GPS does not work alone in congested indoor areas.  Current applications do not offer solution to the problem that what if GPS is toggled off.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions
content: While defining requirements for the Albatross’s functionality, following assumptions were made focused on;  An application is made that may track by minimizing the dependency on internet.  Albatross is installed in the mobile phones of both of the tracker and person being tracked  The mobile phone of the tracker and the person being tracked are not in air plane mode.  The mobile phone of the tracker and the person being tracked are not out of network grid (signals should always be there).  There is credit for SMS in both of the mobile phones SIMs, tracker’s and the person’s being tracked.  Albatross should run on Android operating system.

heading: 1.5 Constraints
content: While managing requirements for the project functionality, following constraints were identified;  Tracker and the person being tracked should support android versions above or equal to lollipop 5.0  Tracker and the person being tracked mobile phones should be out of reach of signal jammers for effective tracking (unable to locate because of jammer even if the location service is enabled).  In case of factory reset, the mobile would be unable to be tracked as the application would have got deleted from the mobile.  Mobile phone would be unable to get located in case it is destroyed.  Mobile numbers that are still in use but have been discarded by network providers or have not yet been registered.

 No cellular network (no signals) on the mobile phone.  No SIM in mobile phone.  No balance for SMS.  Cellular tower data process through internet.  Cellular location tracking accurate up to few hundred meters.  Requires internet for the map.  GPS module will not work in tightly bound and constrained spaces.

heading: 1.6 Project Scope
content: Albatross is an android application that helps people to keep track of their concerned ones using IMEI number via SMS. Following are the features offered by Albatross:  GPS based location tracking.  Cellular tower based location incase GPS is not available (internet based processing on the tracker side).  Acknowledgment between users for privacy.  Mode of communication between tracker and trackee is SMS.  Use IMEI number to uniquely identify the mobile phones.  History of tracked location will be saved respective to every contact.  SIM change alert.  Battery thresh-hold alert.  Added users can ring; lock; wipe; and can track on both bases, GPS and cellular.  Non added users can ring; lock; and track based on GPS only, if allowed by the target user.  If camera switch is enabled, mobile’s front camera takes photo upon 3 wrong mobile unlocking attempts.  Lock and wipe depends upon if the respective switches are enabled from target’s device admin.

 Tracker requires internet to process data received from trackee in case of cell towers, and for Google maps.  Trackee doesn't require internet for anything.  If location service is enabled the application will prefer getting location from GPS rather than cell towers.  Cell tower location will be real time. The only delay will be getting cell towers in 2 min duration, and sending of SMS.  Cell tower accuracy depends upon the density of the towers captured by the mobile phone. Following are the features not offered by Albatross:  Exact mobile tracking (for this we will need more accuracy. As accuracy depends upon the tilt of transmitter, angle of transmitter, area covered by transmitter, and DCR or drop call rate. These attributes are only known to network provider and security agencies).

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: Albatross distinguish feature is the tracking of the user via the cell towers. Cell towers are used for the tracking of suspects by the police investigation. To track a user via a cell towers requires parameters:

heading: 1. Environment
content: a. Urban area b. Rural area c. Weather d. Interference of signal from cell tower to the MS (Mobile Set) 2.  Transmitting power of a cell tower. 3. Direction of cell tower transmitter. 4. Angle of opening of a transmitter. 5. Height of a transmitter.

heading: 7. DCR (drop call rate)
content: 8. Gain of a transmitter. Environment matters in the transmission of a electromagnetic waves because of path loss though objects they lose their power density with distance. Path loss depends upon the environment if the environment consists of buildings, path loss can be of 30 dBm per wall depending upon the number of walls and their thickness. Weather also effects the transmission, i.e. in thunder storm the EC/IO (signal strength indication with the interference in the energy) is very low. Power of the transmitter is set up by the company depending upon the area of the where they are deploying a cell tower. If the area is urban and lots of users, the power will be around 40dBm to 50dBm but the DCR will be low and the tilt of a transmitter will be more and if the area is rural the transmitter power will be higher 50dBm to 60dBm depends upon the company than the DCR will be high and the tilt will be 0 degrees. Gain of the transmitter depends upon shape of an antenna which combines the antenna direction and efficiency. If the antenna is omni-directional than the gain is 0, otherwise it can be 1, 2 or 3 depending upon the shape. Means it will cover 30-degree, 60 degrees or 120 degree. 120-degree antenna is more common. All this information leads us to the Friss transmission equation.

heading: Where

There is Link-budged analysis which considers the interference.

heading: 9. CellID (cell tower identification)
content: The issues we faced were that even with the data that we can get, we were still unable to pin- point the exact position of the MS because of the interference calculation and the data of the transmitter on the cell towers that are unavailable to us. We method we applied to get the approximate location of the user is to get cell tower the phone connects in 2 minutes, processing the cell tower data from the API and using the location of cell towers to get the mean position from it. The mean position is only reliable if the MS connects to more than 1 tower in that duration otherwise it will show only the position of the cell tower to the user.

Literature of different Albatross’s related applications were studied from play store and their respective web sited to finalize requirements of Albatross. Following are some related works of Albatross and their summarized literature:  PreyAntiTheft[1]. Prey AntiTheft is a free android application that helps its users to locate and retrieve the lost or stolen mobile phone through GPS and Wi -Fi. But it does not answer questions that are, what if there is no Wi-Fi connectivity or What if the GPS is turned off? Albatross answers these two questions which may be considered as Albatross’s competitive advantage against Prey Anti Theft. Figure 1: Prey Antitheft screenshot  GPS Phone Tracker [2]. GPS Phone Tracker is another free android application that helps its users by finding lost mobile phones, plots directions to the lost mobile phone and uses GPS to get the lost mobile phone’s whereabouts. GPS phone Tracker works on Wi-Fi and GPS, which can be considered competitive advantage for Albatross.  mSpy[3]. mSpy is another mobile tracking application available on play store. mSpy provides numerous functionalities, in fact mSpy is one of the best tracking applications you can find on android play store. Further, mSpy comes with huge monthly membership cost that is about, $70 per month which can be considered competitive advantage for Albatross.  MobileSpy[4]. MobileSpy is another application that provides tracking services using Wi-Fi. Recently Google has suspended their application from the play store due to their

hidden camera functionality but MobileSpy is available on web. MobileSpy not available on android play store any more will act as Albatross’s competitive advantage. Furth er Mobile Spy comes with a monthly membership cost of $50.  FlexiSpy[5]. FlexiSpy is another application available on android play store that provides tracking services along with many other functionalities. Albatross’s only competitive advantage with FlexiSpy will be, FlexiSpy comes with constant support and update costs.  Bonrix SMS based GPS tracking [6] is an android application available on android play store that provides SMS based tracking services but the application only has 5000 downloads on the play store and 3.0 star rating. Further it only provides SMS based tracking, it still doesn’t answer the question what if GPS is turned off? So, this may become competitive advantage for Albatross against “Bonrix SMS based GPS tracking”  Where’s My Droid [7] is an android application available on google play store that provides SMS based tracking to users while also providing other features. The main drawback is what if the GPS location based service is turned off by the user. The application was unable to answer that question. Albatross works on GPS as well on the location from cell towers that does not require internet or GPS to be turned on at the trackee side.

Figure 2: Where’s my Droid screenshot  Google Find my Phone is an excellent tool that works on the users google account, but the issue arises what if the location and internet service is off. Find my phone doesn’t provides a real-time location to the user. Albatross is providing real time approximate location to trackers via cell towers.

heading: 2.6 Software Development Life Cycle Model
content: The software development lifecycle model we are using is iterative and incremental development. Iterative and incremental design is a combination of iterative modeling and incremental modeling styles. Here we continuously plan through every iteration and incrementally added features concluding to a complete application. This helps us focus on more than one module at the same time. The major reason behind choosing this combination of models was we had to perform gradual increase in features with every release of the module. We started with initial, simplified implementation of the modules like sign up and login and went on to tracking module incrementally, adding additional functionality like battery and SIM alerts iteratively. For example, Albatross offers functionalities like location tracking, battery alerts, SIM change alerts, add new contacts, handshakes, etc. Location tracking was a basic module at the start into which we added functionalities like battery alerts to members and SIM change alerts to members. Similarly we made every main class / functionality independently as an application. All these independent applications will be combined at the end to form Albatross. Iterative and incremental modeling helped in adding additional functionalities to each separate application.

heading: 3.4 Software Architecture
content: The following figure shows an abstract level architecture of Albatross, based on peer -to-peer architectural style. Here the peer -to-peer architecture is composed of components/peers and connectors. The members in a ha nd-shake represent components while the data streams, passing network messages between components work as connectors. Every component is connected with a connector that connects the component with every other component in the family. For example, there are four members A, B, C, and D. A, B, and C are members of the same family i.e. A is connected to B, B is connected to C and C is connected to A. While a member of a family can also be a member in another family i.e. C is connected to D with a hand-shake. The main purpose of implementing peer -to-peer architectural style was to avoid data centralization. Further purposes of using this architectural style are:  Every peer acts as a server to entertain another peer that will be acting as client.  Every peer actin g as a server will help us maintain database of the application for the member, his / her hand-shakes, and family members in that member’s mobile phone.  Peer-to-peer architectural style supports a two way communication between the components.  If a mobile phone gets lost and finder of the phone factory resets the mobile phone to delete the application, peer -to-peer architecture will help us keep the data (like mobile’s IMEI number) in the mobile phones of other members of a family.

heading: 6.1 Problems Faced and Lessons Learned
content: There were a few problems we have faces so far among which following are of significant importance.  At first we planned to make Albatross for every platform i.e. android, windows and IOS. Later we just kept our focus to android as IOS and windows had high security problems and we had less time to cope with those problems.  We started our development phase in Xamarin but due to its limitations we had to shift to android. The limitations that we faced were, 1. It had security problems. Cross platform application was to be built for IOS, android and windows so security had to be ensured for all three of these operating systems. 2. More functionality could be implemented in android. 3. More research work was available in android. 4. Xamarin used C# as programming language. It converted C# into java libraries to use it for android version, so performance issues occurred. While android studio uses java for development which made the application perform better.

heading: 6.2 Project Summary
content: Albatross is an android application which provides an efficient and less costly mean of tracking a mobile phone or loved ones yet providing the application owners monetary value against the services. Other similar applications use Wi-Fi and GPS to track while Albatross uses GPS or cellular towers to track. Albatross uniquely identifies its different members using their IMEI numbers and all the communication between members takes place via SMS. Users signup to Albatross to become Albatross members. They then form handshake by one member acknowledging the other member’s request. This helps the member to share their location only to their concerned ones. Albatross saves members’ contacts to their phone memory. Apart from this Albatross provides many exciting features like wipe; lock; ring; take photo on 3 unsuccessful phone unlocking attempts; tracking history; edit profile; and delete a member from White List.

The overall work of Albatross, from requirement gathering and charter signing to final delivery of the application and user manual, has been spread over the span of almost 1 year time, starting from January 1, 2017 to December 20, 2017. The overall budget estimate is expected to be Rs. 2.7 million only.

heading: 6.3 Future Work
content: We will revise our project while improving some details and removing some of the limitation (that we are unable to do currently due to limitation of technology). Three of the improvements that we are expecting in the near future are:  Avoiding Albatross from getting deleted at factory reset.  Tracking even without installed applicat ion for law and order institutions of the government.  Password protection facility will be provided for deleting Albatross i.e. only the owner of the mobile phone would be able to delete Albatross by putting in the password.  Toggle GPS on implicitly if it is off on the target mobile phone.  Enhance location accuracy while tracking through cell towers.

heading: Abstract
content: Our proposed systems aim to develop a system/application for the job seekers that facilitates job searching in an efficient manner. There is a need to develop social media content based expert system that finds the best suitable organizations for a given applicant. As dealing with a vast amount of data present on the internet today the user has to utilize his thousands of hours going through a large amount of information to find a job in a suitable company. So, we aim to develop a system for the job seekers that recommends jobs and shows market trends based on the information of the previous and current employees working in a specific organization or a company. Different machine learning models have been applied on our dataset comprising of current employees in the company to achieve a organizational predication rate  of above 74% in classifying employees in companies and using these models we try to help the employee to find the best-fit job/organization that matches their area of expertise and help them save their time.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: We are living in the age of Information Technology. Today, the most common and efficient way to communicate with the public is through the internet and the social media. Day by Day, with the rapid growth and development of the internet technology; the web is getting overloaded with a great amount of information. With such a vast range of information available on the web today, the big data information is not being utilized the way it should have been. Nowadays, recommender systems are an important tool tha t is used in all domains that assess the user's taste, his preferences and provide him/her with a list of things that would be according to his or her taste. As going through this vast amount of information regarding recruiting and jobs, a job seeker has to spend hours trying to find a suitable job for himself; for a solution to this problem job recommenders are gaining a great importance. The job recommender recommends the user with a job that is totally according to his taste. Social Media and Networking websites are used in the HR department of the companies. Based on research by Lucie Bohmova and Antonin Pavlicek, It is believed that social media and networks are an important HR tool that helps in hiring new employees. [6]. Finding Job candidates that best fit your organization is a great deal and a great and challenging responsibility for the HR department. So, the HR managers use social media as a source to find job candidates with the skills and expertise your company requires; The use of social media for job recruitment is making a big difference in the recruitment process and is gaining great success. In fact, Researchers have proved that half of the companies and the organizations throughout the world are using social me dia as a tool for hiring employees [7]. Job seekers lack guidance related to jobs and to help them find jobs in an easy and efficient manner we have proposed this system. The job seekers want to search for the most appropriate jobs for themselves that best fits their area of expertise (skills, education , and previous experience). The job seekers are always curious about the hiring criteria of the companies and whether their education, skills and previous experiences match the jobs in the market. They are always in search of the best suited and satisfactory jobs for themselves by trying to improve their skills, education, and experiences. So we have explored some of the main companies of Pakistan i.e. PTCL, JAZZ, Telen or, TERADATA and NETSOLE and by exploring the features of the employees of these companies we designed an effective and personalized job recommender and statistical system that helps the users to match their expertise to the best suitable jobs for themselves. Our system intends to classify the users in different companies by giving a probability of job by evaluating the trends and the features of the previous and the current employees of the company. We are considering professional and social networking website LinkedIn as our main data collection source and by using different data mining techniques we are trying

The procedure we are following works a s follows: 1) Collect employee profiles from an authentic source and extract features of the employee; 2) Train different classification models on the data 3) Eliminate the data features that have low correlation; 4) Find trends on the data; 5) choose the most optimal model for the data out of the models tested; 6) Predict jobs for the job seekers based on his/her features (skills, education and experiences). heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: Today, recommender systems are used in every possible domain of use. However, the types of recommendation systems differ from one another based on the use of the domain i.e. Music Recommendation systems, Clothing Recommendation systems and many more. A lot of work has been done on this nature. This section analyses the previously built systems and research work done on the doma in that is similar to the systems we are constructing. Job recommendation systems have emerged and gained a vast importance in the last few decades and are playing a great role in the market. Many job recommendations exist today that try to explore differe nt methodology of recommendations. The existing online recruitment systems have been summarized with their advantages as well as disadvantages by AlObtaibi et al [1]. Many Job recommender systems have been constructed in the past but there is no such system or research work that caters the Pakistan industry at a wider scope and if there is they are not that efficient. Some of the features and technology of the previously made systems match our system. But the previous systems comprise of some problems. So, we are trying to produce a system that overcomes the problems faced by the previous systems. Many online recruiting systems and websites have emerged such as Rozee.pk, Monster, LinkedIn, and Indeed.com. These websites are being used as the main resource and channel to find jobs and have been used for more than ten years now. All these systems use the mechanism of keyword matching which is not an efficient manner of job recommendation as it has a very less accuracy rate and has  made job searching a tedious task. These applications let the user search for jobs by using a keyword i.e. JAVA; that gives you all the jobs related to Java and the user has to send his curriculum vitae to all the companies available. Whereas our proposed  system uses different data mining techniques and methodologies for job recommendations. The algorithm used for extracting data from LinkedIn is using a web crawler. Below some algorithms and applications are listed that helped us in gathering the requirements and to build a system with more demanding features.

heading: 2.1.1 Web Crawler: Extracting the Web Data
content: With the increase in the usage of the internet hypertext, links are used to find out the related resources and pages. The web crawler iterates the given pages and extracts the related data from the website pages it is basically used to download data from the pages.  The mechanism used behind the web crawler is keyword driven crawling that uses the Ontology Concepts ensuring improvement in crawler’s performance. This includes extraction of URLs based on the keywords and furtherly, extracts data containing those keywords. It considers only the data containing the ke yword as important and doesn’t download other pages.

heading: 2.1.1.1  The architecture of Web Crawler
content: Web Crawlers are the most used component behind a search engine. A list of URLs (called a seed) is available with the web. The web crawler visits every URL one by one and identifies the hyperlinks in the page and create a list (crawl frontier) of all the links/URLs to visit. Using the rules, the URLs are visited one by one individually. Pages from the internet are downloaded and stored in the database system. The URLs are then placed in the queue and can be accessed one by one whenever required. Web crawlers use different algorithms to find the relevant links/data and use them further on. [5]

heading: 2.1.1.2 The process of Web Crawling
content: The web crawler follows a process, which is as following 1. It keeps a track of the pages to download. 2. Checks if the page could be downloaded otherwise moves to the next page which is downloadable. 3. Download the page. 4. Extract all the links of the page. 5. Filter out data required from the page. 6. Save the summary and move to the next page.

heading: 2.1.2.1 Introduction

heading: 2.1.3.2.1 LinkedIn architecture
content: LinkedIn started as many another social website . It is one of the most used social and professional networking website available today. When this application started it was called “ Leo” which hosted web servlets. In a social networking website, member to member connections needs to be handled so a system was needed that used graph traversals for querying connection data so a system “cloud” was born for member graphs. As the application increased the member profile database started to overload. The read and write traffic both were handled by the profile database and in order to scale more a “replica slave DB” was introduced which was the duplicate of the member database. But as the traffic increased Leo failed. Now the LinkedIn application uses t he “Service Oriented Architecture”. While transforming from Leo architecture to the service-oriented architecture the APIs were inconsistent. So a new API model “rest.li” was introduced [3]. Rest.li is a REST + JSON framework.

heading: 2.1.3.3 Features
content: The main features of LinkedIn include:  It allows the users (employees and employer) to create profiles describing their work training, education, experience and skills and allows them to create a connection with each other. Figure 5: LinkedIn Architecture
