heading: 1.1 INTRODUCTION
content: Student admissions play a very important role for running any university because students are what keep a University alive. Student admission system is the most important activity for a university to survive. If there will be a better admission system then it can be easy for students to apply and the ratio of applying students of will be increase. A poor admissions system can mean less students being admitted into a university because of mistakes or an overly slow response time. After the intermediate students are worried about admissions and they want to know which college or university is suitable for them. Our website will provide complete information about admissions. Our website will be a free platform where students get connected with colleges, universities. . This is a user-friendly website. The student will create his/her account with all information like personal data, marks, subjects, and level of education which are required. .  Students can apply online through our website. There will be a common application form, which contain all information that a university required.  The student can also update their information time to time. Our website will update the information regarding admissions of all universities. Our website will send them a notification when admissions will open. In merit calculator Student just enter the marks of entry test and previous degree , our System will show the universities and discipline in which he/she is eligible. They can also search for specific colleges or universities. We attached GSM (Global System For Mobile Application) with our system to send notifications on mobile. Subscribe users can only receive messages on their mobiles. No need of internet to get notifications. It’s become easy for students to get information about admissions on mobiles through SMS.

heading: 1.2 GOALS AND OBJECTIVES
content: Our goals and objectives are as below.  We want to help the student for making decision for choosing a right college.  Students do not have to go personally to universities office for their admission.  This application enables the students to be updated with universities admissions..  This site is user friendly.  Our aim to save the time of the students.  It is fast, reliable and efficient.  Avoid data redundancy and inconsistency.

heading: 1.3 PROBLEM STATEMENT
content: In Pakistan, there is no such a platform which helps students regarding to their admissions. After intermediate  mostly  students  are  confused  about  admissions.  They  don’t  know  how  many universities offering their relative degree. They even don’t know how many universities are available in Pakistan. This is the major problem in Pakistan that student can’t get right guidance from anywhere. After intermediate students visited different universities for admissions. They wasted a lot of time to visit that places. If there will be any platform in Pakistan that helps students regarding their admissions and in selection of right path, then it will be most beneficial for bright future of students. Through our website they can save their times, they can apply online and can pay the fees online.

heading: 1.4.1 ASSUMPTIONS
content: • Every user must have internet facility through which they can get guidance. .            • Every user must clear intermediate.

heading: 1.4.2 CONSTRAINTS
content: • Users should have prior knowledge about usage of Web Application. • Users should have laptop or pc on which web application will going to run.

heading: 1.5 MOTIVATION AND SCOPE
content: Currently, there is no such a website in Pakistan that provides a complete platform to students regarding to their future studies. The major issue in Pakistan is that 60% people are living in rural areas and they do not know about the universities and colleges. Even they don’t know the eligibility criteria of universities. Due to lack of information they can’t select the most appropriate field and they select that field which is not suitable for them. In this way mostly student can’t give 100% to their studies. As a result we waste thousands of students every year. From our website they will be able to apply according to the desire field. They can get any type of information from our website. In this way we can save the future of many students.

heading: 2.1 EXISTING SYSTEM STUDY
content: This idea is unique in Pakistan. No one create such a website in Pakistan which helps students to find out the universities according to their marks. Some websites are available

such as UniRank [1] is a website that provides ranking of universities world wise and you can search universities country wise. Which? University.com [2] is another website which helps the students to select best university in the world. Our website is quite similar to this site but it’s just for Pakistan universities.  CollegeDekho [3] is a website that is currently working  in  INDIA  which  provides  the  facility  of  online  admission  only  for  Indian universities.

heading: 2.3.1 FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
content: FR – 01 Register 01 The user must click on the signup button to sign up. The signup button will lead the user to user registration page. 02 For login user have to fill the basic username, email and password field of the signup form. 03 After the signup the user dashboard will be displayed successfully. FR – 02 Login 01 The user must click on login button to login. The login page will be opened after the user click on the button. 02 The system shall allow the user to login through username and password.

03 The system must verify the username and password, notify on incorrect username or password and allow to re-enter. 04 The system shall allow the user to reset password using the provided email address, in case he/she forgets. 04 The system shall allow the user to login with Facebook or Google account. FR – 03 Student 01 The system shall allow the student to register as a student through name, email, phone number etc. 02 The system shall allow the student to search university. 03 The system shall allow the student to select university. 04 The system shall allow the student to select degree. 05 The system shall allow the student to apply for admission. 06 The system shall allow the student to fill the admission form. 07 The system shall allow the student to pay the Admission fee. FR – 04 Degree/program 01 The system shall allow the student to view the list of degrees which are provided by the university. 02 The system shall allow the student to search a specific degree. 03 The system shall allow the student to select a degree. 04 The system shall allow the student to confirm a degree or program. FR – 05 Admission Fees

01 The system shall allow the admin to create challan form of the admission fees. 02 The system shall allow the student to download this challan form of the admission fees. 03 The system shall allow the student to pay this challan form of the admission fees in bank. 04 The system shall allow the student to send back this paid challan to admin. FR – 06 University Admin 01 The system shall allow the university admin to get the student data. 02 The system shall allow the university admin to provide the university related information. 03 The system shall allow the university admin to send notification to student about the conformity or rejection of the admission. FR – 07 Admin Control 01 The system shall allow the admin to check the detail of students who apply for the admission. 02 The system shall allow the admin to get the student data and send to the university. 03 The system shall allow the admin to provide the list of university. 04 The system shall allow the admin to create the form of the admission. 05 The system shall allow the admin to create the challan form of the fee. FR – 08 Logout 01 Admin/user can logout from website at any time. 02 Session will expire after logout.
03 Admin/user have to login again to use the website after logout.

heading: 2.6 SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT LIFECYCLE
content: There are many software development processes such as:  Water fall Water  Fall  Model  is  used  when  requirements  are  clearly  defined  and  does  not  require  any  further changing.

heading:  Rapid Prototyping Model:
content: Rapid prototyping Model is used when requirements are not clearly defined.

heading:  Spiral Model:
content: Spiral Model is used when cost and risk evaluation is important.

heading:  Incremental Model:
content: Incremental Model is used when basic functionalities of the system are known but requirements can change over time. Software Development Process that will be used here is incremental model. There are five phases of  incremental  model.  Requirement  phase  is  the  first  phase  in  which  all  requirements  are specified and before finalizing that phase all the requirements are verified before going to next phase. Second phase is design phase in which all the diagrams are made for each requirement and also made class diagram and system architecture and all the phase activities are tested before going to next phase. In third phase implementation is done before finishing unit testing. Fourth phase is testing in which all the code is tested and after that it is deployed to the user which gives its feedback and software goes in maintenance phase for as long as it exists. The fifth phase is maintenance phase, whenever there is any requirement creep it goes back to design phase to make the changes and after that on Implementation phase required changes are performed and then these changes are tested and deployed to the user. User got free hand to request to change requirements.

heading: Reasons:
content: • We just know the basic requirements of the system. • Requirements can be changed within the time. • We know the actual problem which our system is going to resolve and  also the requirements which are needed to complete functionality of the system. • Because of incremental model changes can be done easily.

heading: 3.4.1   Most commonly used Architectural Style
content: There are multiple architectural styles.

heading: Object-Oriented Style
content: In this architectural style objects encapsulate state and accessing functions and close mapping between external entities and internal objects is sensible. There are many complex and interrelated data structures.

heading: Connectors:
content: Whereas connectors are the messages and method invocations.

heading: Client-Server Style
content: This  architectural  style  separates  the  system  into  two  parts.  Client  makes  request  to  the server and server is a database represented. Clients communicate with other clients through a server-based. Clients read and send data to a server.

heading: Components:
content: Components are client and server.

heading: Connectors:
content: Connectors are the RPC-based network interaction protocols.

heading: Black-Board Style:
content: In this style the whole system is divided into two major parts, one is black-board and the second one is knowledge source.  Black-board is used to store data while in  knowledge source domain specific knowledge is stored.

heading: Components:
content: There are two components, one is central data structure and the other component is operating on black-board.

heading: Data-Flow Style:
content: In this architecture style, separate programs are executed sequentially with a batched input. Problem can be easily formulated as a set of sequential, severable steps.

heading: Connectors:
content: Connectors are the human hands carrying tapes between the programs. Types of execution sequences:  Batch and filter  Process control  Pipe and filter

heading: Layered Style:
content: In this style hierarchical organization of system is exist. Each layer exposes an interface to be used by the above layers for system interaction. Each layer acts as a server for the above layers and as a client for the below layer.

heading: Connectors:
content: In this style connectors are the protocols which are used for layer interaction.

Rule-based Style: In this architectural style, interface engine determine whether the input is a fact or query. If the input is a fact then it will be added to knowledge base, and if it is a query then the rule will be found from knowledge base to resolve that query.

heading: Components:
content:  Interface engine,  Knowledge base  User interface.

heading: Connectors:
content:  Procedure calls  Shared memory through which all interfaces are tightly interrelated.

heading: Interpreter Style:
content: In this style interpreter passes and executes inputs, and also update all states maintained by the interpreter. Commands are dynamically improved and the new competences are made based on present primitives while the system remains constant.

heading: Components:
content:  Command interpreter.  Its state  User interface

heading: Connectors:
content:  Procedure calls through which interfaces are tightly interrelated.

heading: Mobile Code Style:
content: In this architectural style data element is data element is dynamically converted into a processing component.

heading: Components:
content:  Execution dock which handles receipt of code and state.  Code compiler.

heading: Connectors:
content:  Network protocols Peer to Peer Style: This Style commonly used computer networking architecture in which every workstation/node has the same responsibilities.

heading: Component:
content:  Every component acts as a client and server.

heading: Implicit Invocation Style:
content: In this architectural style event announcement will be done instead of method calling. All listening components register themselves and when the event is declared the system invokes all the registered methods implicitly.

heading: Connector:
content:  Invocation is either explicit or implicit in response to events.

heading: Abstract
content: Time is the most influential factor in this world. All the scholars, teachers and students need to read files and research papers for their study or research purposes. That’s why they go to internet to find as many files as possible related to their work q uickly. The system will search the keyword from search engines and get the top most relevant files from first 04 pages. Also, the user can upload the related pdf file and the search engine finds other pdf’s from its references of the uploaded file and the results which are most relevant to the uploaded pdf file are shown to the user.  This will reduce time and effort the user need to put to get the document /files that are relevant to what he searches for. The system will also read those files, check the references that are given in it and get the files from these references too. heading: 1.1 INTRODUCTION
content: There was a time when people are unaware of science and technology but people knew that they cannot do all the research alone they have to rely on the work done by the other people. So, whenever someone do any research they used to write it down as a document on the paper so the other people can learn from it for their own research. But there was a problem that if a person is doing research he has to get information by reading the research work of many authors and it was difficult to find them. So, libraries w ere built that contain different books and research papers of different author from different countries. It made people easier to learn things to do research and gain information but still it was not enough because one cannot find all the work of people in the world in one library. Then mankind evolves, era of science and technology started and internet introduced. It made the life of the people much easier because it connected the whole world. Now people can get any information, book, data, research work of any author from all over the world at any time. The existing solutions provide so much help to people because you have search engines that can give you all the files, document and research papers again st the keywords. But most of the time those results are not relevant to what you are looking for. As now internet itself a gigantic library that contain almost everything but the problem is to really find something that you are actually looking for. It is just like you walk into the library and you have to find a one file from billions of files. A person now has access to all the files but he does not know all the names of books, authors file and research works. So, he has to search by a keyword to get all the research work that is relevant to that keyword. But the search engines do not provide all the documents and that makes a person equal to the person of the ancient times who did not have access to all the books, files and research works for his research. If a person wants to get all the relevant data, the only option he has, is to search by a key word, find the files that are most relevant to his topic, check the references given in those files and search them too to get actual data he wants. Or user has to upload a pdf file and search engine will search its references and show the relevant results searched from the references.  All that things are very time consuming, and that makes almost impossible for most of the people to adopt this method and hence they have to rely on less data given by the search engines. The project is to made this Page 8 of 36 method automated, so people can get quality data from all over the internet without wasting so much time.

heading: 2.6 Software development Lifecycle (SDLC)
content: Software development lifecycle (SDLC) is referred to as the application development life cycle. It is the sequence of different tasks like planning, creating, testing and deploying the information application. It can also be described as, it is the sequence of steps through which a software product/application progresses to produce the expected results. It is the way to organized the activities to develop a software product. Normally software development life cycle is divided into six phases. The first phase is requirement gathering and analysis, the second one is design, implementation in terms of coding, testing, deployment and last one is maintenance. A better way to use SDLC in the form of a framework that describes the activities at each stage of the software development pr ocess is the use of “process models”. There are different types of software development lifecycles as Waterfall Process Model (uses when requirements are very well known and technology is well understood), Rapid Prototyping (used when requirements are not known or unstable), Incremental Process Model (when the basic functionalities of the product are well known and it could be changed over the time) and Spiral Process Model (uses when risk evaluation is important, users are  not known of their needs and when the requirements are complex). The Software Development Process Models which we will use in our project are the Incremental Process Model and the other one Rapid Prototyping Process Model. Firstly, Incremental Process Model will be used in our project th rough which the whole project will be divided into builds and in each build partial functionalities will be implemented in the system. Later on, the increased functionalities will be added gradually. Incremental Process Model consists of five different phases. The first one is Requirement phase, in this phase all the possible requirements are gathered and then requirements are analysed and verified in a specific documented format. And using these known requirements and known functionalities the whole system is built in an increasing order of their functionalities based. The second Process Model we will used in our project is Rapid Prototyping Process Model. This process model will be used because the gathered requirements are not complete and they are not st able, using this process model the initial versions of the product will be generated and the whole dummy product will be critically analysed against their functionalities and the gathered requirements and on user needs certain functionalities will be added accordingly and gradually the final product will be developed and deployed. All modelling artefacts and system diagrams are tested before its development. System Implementation takes a time to implement the whole system and then time for unit testing of each single module and then the system testing. Once it is tested accurately, it goes into

heading: Abstract: -
content: The Online Systems help us in purchasing of products and services. Nowadays people are leaning towards online shopping because it saves time, but existing systems of buying products have numerous drawbacks. For online exploration, trust is the main issue and our challenge is to build such a system which recommends the customers the desired/ideal product with inadequate resources and consequently building customer’s trust on our system/product. Now the trouble with existing online system is Bootstrapping problem, that is, if a new Company emerges in the market then the existing system cannot generate rating for it; same goes for new product. This issue causes an uncertain situation for the customer to, whether go for the existing product with less specs or the new product of a new company with much higher specs in same price. There is a need for a system which can remove this problem of bootstrapping at granularity level. If granularity level is high, the level of details of the product will be deeper and it will help in making a system in which customer’s trust can be restore. This system shall strengthen the decision-making power of customer.

heading: 1.1 Introduction: -
content: Nowadays if a customer needs to buy some product it is hard for him to go out and get the product by himself because it takes time. New products with different variations are launching excessively. Customers are confused and have hard time in the selection of the product because there are so many choices. In online exploration customers cannot determine or examine the quality of the product only through textual and graphical description. The customer deserves to know more, so there is need for an application which can critically rate the products and customers can easily choose/select the product according to their needs. For online exploration, trust is the main issue and our challenge is to build such a system which recommends the customers the desired/ideal product with inadequate resources and consequently building customer’s trust on our system/product. Now the trouble with existing online system is Bootstrapping problem, if a new Company emerges in the market then the existing system cannot generate rating for it; same goes for new product. This issue causes an uncertain situation for the customer to, whether go for the existing product with less specs or the new product of a new company with much higher specs in same price. When a new company is launched, it has to compete with the products of existing companies. When the existing companies launches a new product, the rating of the product can be driven from the historical data of that company. Now the challenge is to give ratings to the products of new companies. So, there should be a service that can build the trust of the customer and analyze the respective products to determine its price, reliability, comfort and quality to compare it with existing products of different companies according to the standards that are set and give critical ratings and grading. Critical rating on products includes consumer feedback, expert analysis, company reviews and comparison with the competitor's product. On the basis of a scale customer can easily trust the product. The rating scale is from 1 to 5, 1 meaning worst and 5 meaning excellent. Formula is built by assigning different weightage at grain level of product (mobile parts), quality of services, seal, and warranty.

content: The scope of our system is to eliminate Bootstrapping problem only. The bootstrapping issue causes an uncertain situation for the customer to, whether go for the existing product with less specs or the new product of a new company with much higher specs in same price. As a result, there must be a system which can remove this problem of bootstrapping by comparing multiple products or companies at grain level. If the granularity level is high, the level of details of the product will be deeper and it will help in making a system in which any product, new or old or any company, new or existing can rated by our system which consequently will leads towards customer’s trust towards the product/company and also on our system’s rating.

heading: 2.1 Literature review / Existing system study: -
content: 2.1.1 [1] Trust bases service oriented Architecture by Zainab M. Aljazzaf, Miriam A.M.

heading: Capretz, Mark Perry
content: Web Application development that based on services uses Service Oriented Architecture but it has trust issues so they integrate trust Framework (metrics) to it. They add a component with the registry that describes the trust level of service provider. They add service provider trust, service trust, and feedback of service requestor in metrics. They also remove biasness (cultures adjustment). For service trust, they monitor latency (delay), execution time and response time. If existing service provider introduce new services they give same trust level to those new services. If new service provider introduces new services they give trust level according to their monitoring services. They develop formulae according to their metrics. In the end, they concluded that their Framework (Total trust evaluator framework) is responsible for trust process.

heading: 2.1.2 [2] Bootstrapping Quality of web services Zainab M. Aljazzaf
content: Quality of services (QoS) used as distinctive factor b/w similar services. When new service arrives, we need to justify its QoS. They build framework for it known as QoS bootstrapping Framework. In their Framework, they introduce some QoS factors that is throughput, availability, reliability and accessibility. They develop formula of each factors and calculate respective value. They generate graph of these factors. In the end they concluded that their proposed solution used to develop high performance application and shows the importance of bootstrapping techniques.

content: IMDb Owner is Amazon and created by Col Needham (CEO). The Internet Movie Database is an online database of information related to films, television programs and video games, including cast, production crew, fictional characters, biographies, plot summaries, trivia and reviews. The site enables registered users to rate any film on a scale of 1 to 10, and the totals are converted into a weighted mean-rating that is displayed beside each title. IMDb allow users to rate the movies and related stuff. [9]

heading: 2.1.4 [4] Yelp:
content: Yelp was founded in 2004 by former PayPal employees Russel Simmons and Jeremy Stoppelman. Yelp is a website and mobile application that connects people with local businesses in which individuals or organizations use contributions from users to obtain needed services or ideas like reviews, anything from restaurants to smartphone reviews, through more than 90 million consumer reviews in 30 countries. Yelp only publish crowd-sourced reviews about local businesses, but our project can give critical ratings to the products (such as smart phone) of new companies as well as existing companies.[1]

heading: 5.2 Project summary
content: The trouble with existing online systems is Bootstrapping problem, this paper proposed a solution to this recurring bootstrapping problem by providing a model that focuses on the granularity level of the product/service. Granularity level include the detail description of the product/ service. This model is a comprehensive solution, because it comprises of all the parts that are used in a product/service. This model will generate ratings that is composition of the granularity level, environment, authentication and quality. This trust building model of rating will increase the decision-making power of the customer. As this project is R&D so we develop a research paper with our project. Future work  The grain attributes can be divided at hardware level to achieve more accurate results.  Bootstrapping itself is a very diverse field, Bootstrapping security module can be integrated to our proposed model. In our project we are restricted to mobile phones but our model can be used in any business environment like  Fashion industry  Shoes industry

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: In this modern era, time is very precious and people are very busy in their lives. They need to relax their mind by spending their time in those places which are worth watching. Tourism is expanding in Pakistan in every year. According to the Travel and To urism Competitiveness Report 2017, released by the World Economic Forum, the direct contribution of travel and tourism to Pakistan's Gross Domestic Product in 2015 was US$ 328.3 million, constituting 2.8% of the total GDP (gross domestic product) and it is estimated to grow at high rate. Our main aim to promote tourism in Pakistan and to contribute in countries in GDP (gross domestic product).With improvement in countries security tourism is expanding in Pakistan and many foreign tourists are comi ng to Pakistan. Our aim is to provide a complete platform where they can get information without any difficulties. Many tourism companies are working and promotin g the tourism in Pakistan. Thesetourismcompanies use social media platforms for their advertis ement and promotions.We will provide a platform by which these companies can make their own site. A subdomain will be assigned to the tourism company at which they can create their own website. Predefined theme will be provided to the tourism companies by which they can create their own websites.The companies will provide full description of their tour regarding total amount per person, places they will visit, stay in hotels, meals, etc. along with their own introduction. People will be able to search for best places to visit during their holidays. For example i f someone has 3 holidays h e/she can search for 3 days trip organized by companies. User will also search for a tour according to his budget and compare the whole trip with other tourism companies. Users will be able to post the images and give description of places which they would like to recommend others to visit.Users will first signup and then provide the information of the places that are newly explored by them.Map will provide the direction and distance of the recommended places from user.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content:  Provide a reliable system, through which people can find all the available tours within Pakistan, and select a tour that suits best to their needs.  Provide a direct relationship between users and the tour companies via our provided platform.  Provide thorough comparison between different tour packages.  Allow users to view hidden attractive places and view their images as well.  Provide a range of tour packages suitable for all Socio-economic classes.  Allow user to select tours according to their budget and preferences.  Promote tourism all over Pakistan, especially within northern areas to diminish the fear of terrorism.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: In Pakistan this type of project has not yet been developed  and implemented. Many tourist companies have not given a platform to tourists where they can search for different trips  and do comparison of facilities  provided in the tour plan. The main motive of our project is to facilitate tourism companies to provide  the information to the tourists. It will also let the tourists explore new locations based on the guidance provided by different people. People who have already visited the locations will share pictures of the locations and distance and road guide etc.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions & constraints
content:  All payment gateway APIs were not easily accessible. Proof of income was required to get the API.  Google Maps API is not free of cost any more for web based applications.  The system will be accessible and responsive on all devices.  Stakeholders of this project are available for all project meetings.  Experts and Consultants of this domain are required for Requirements analysis purposes.

heading: 1.5 Project scope
content: Many tourism companies are working and promoting th e tourism in Pakist an. These tourismcompanies use social media platforms for their advertisement and promotions.We will provide a platform by which these companies can make their own site. The project will have three front ends one for administrator, one for sub-domain administrators and one for users or site viewers. A sub-domain will be assigned to the tourism company at which they can create their own website. Pre -defined themes will be provided to the tourism companies by which they can create their own websites. The comp anies will provide full description of their tour regarding total amount per person, places they will visit, stay in hotels, meals, etc. along with their own introduction. As far as project’s scope is concerned, we tend to develop a system that will enable  the tourists to search for best places to visit within their available time and budget. The project is being designed for indigenous tourism companies.

heading: Administrator Side
content: This system will not be completed without the presence of admin. The admin will monitor the activity of each user. The admin account will be created by providing the required credentials. The information will be updated by the admin. Admin will also be able to change the password for security reasons. Admin will log into the website via email along with his verified password.

heading: User Side
content:  User will create account for uploading images and description related to different places.  User will login into account by providing password and other relevant information.  User will add information for posting the images and description of new places.  User will view the trip plan along with its complete description.  User will select trip plans for comparison.  User will be able to cancel the trip plan. Fine will be deducted on cancelation of the trip according to company terms and conditions.  User can pay the payment online.User can also pay through Pre Paid Card, Visa Card, Master Card etc.

heading: 2.1Literature Review
content: There are some existing systems related to tourism platforms in other countries but none exists in Pakistan and offers the features that our system does. Some examples are as following:

heading: 2.1.1 Tourradar.com:
content: Tourradar is an international tourism based website. On this platform users can search for international tours for specific destinations. These tours are posted by the tourism companies. The tourism companies can login as a tour agency and post tour packages. These trips can also be selected on the bases of the type, such as, Cultural Trip, Marine Trip, Adventure Trip, etc.

heading: Pros:
content:  Tourradar provide worldwide tours.  It provides insurance to its customers in case of unexpected expenses.  It provides local support to tourists.

heading: Cons:
content:  Any payment done to tour  company is via Tourradar, who hold the payment for some time. This can delay the payment for the tourism companies.  Tour companies have to pay a lot to make an account on this platform.  No tour comparison is available with other companies.

heading: 2.1.2 Tourplanner.com:
content: Tourplanner is a Pakistan based tourism website which offers national tour packages along with accommodation facilities. On  this website user can select trip packages by selecting destinations and dates.

heading: Pros:
content:  Provide flight information.  User can select tour destination with date.  Provide local guidance to tourists with private transportation

heading: Cons:
content:  All packages are provided by  the website owner only. No tourism company can post tours.  The tour packages are very expensive, and are defined only for the luxury class people.  No tour comparison is available.  User cannot book or pay online for the tour.  No google map is provided for understanding of customers.

heading: 2.1.3 Makemytrip.com
content: MakemyTrip is an Indian online leading travel company. Company provides online travel services including flight tickets, domestic and international holiday packages, hotel reservations, rail and bus tickets.

heading: Pros
content:  Offers flights, cabs, and international tours in USA, India, and Australia.  Offers users to create their own trips.  Provide local guidance to tourists with private transportation  Also operate through 51 branches in 47 Indian cities along a branch in New York.

heading: Cons
content:  No tour comparison is available.  This website deals with international tours.  No service is available in Pakistan

heading: 2.1.4 FalconClub.pk
content: FalconClub.pk used t o make people free of worldly tensions, with a motto to provide mental and physical health fitness established in 2011. At first they targeted university students by creating their own adventure clubs. COMSATS adventure club was also their initiative.

heading: Pros
content:  Offers local tours  Offers local guide  Provide transportation, Hotel services.  Offers hiking, paragliding, Cycling, Camping, Rock climbing, Rafting etc.  Users can select their own tour.

heading: Cons
content:  No tour comparison is available.  No Google map is provided for understanding of customers.

heading: Some Common Issues:
content:  No tour comparison is available.  No Google map is provided for understanding of customers.  No platform available for tourism companies

heading: Abstract
content: “Fun with Stickman” is a stickman game engine application. This application is developed using the .Net Framework. This application will provide a platform for creating stickman games. Players will be able to create and play a wide variety of stickman games. Players can create games using the built-in features present in the application. This application consists of a toolbox with a wide variety of features and built-in animations and arcades for creating games. Players can create and customize their stickman character for the game using the features and options available in the toolbox. Players can create games using the built-in animations and drag and drop features present in the toolbox. . Players will simply select an animation and drag and drop features from the toolbox into the animations to create games. As compared to conventional game engines, this application is easy to use, people of any background can use it to create games without involving any sort of coding or programming.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: “Fun with stickman” is a stickman game engine. The major mot ive behind doing this project was building a unique product that is different from ordinary gaming applications. “Fun with stickman” will change the way how gaming is done, unlike ordinary conventi onal games this application is unique in its own way .The major interests behind doing this project was my interests in animation and gaming. This application is a perfect blend of high quality animations and provides a unique gaming experience. By introducing this application in the market players will be able to create as many games as they want with ease and will be a constant source of entertainment for them. “Fun with stickman” is a windows form application that will basically revolve around the stickman character. A stickman character is generally used to represent a human figure. This application is a game engine for the stickman. Stickman is  the main character in this game. This application will allow players to create game for the stickman. This goal will be achieved through the help of built in features and animations in the application ’s toolbox. Players will  be able to create their own games according to their imagination and level of perception. After cr eating and designing their games players will be able to play their created games easily. This application allows players to build their games through a step by step process. First, the players will select a basic stickman using the options available in the toolbox. After selecting the stickman players will be able to customize the stickman. This goal will be achieved through built-in features in the toolbox. This toolbox will provide players with a wide variety of options to customize their stickman. After designing the main character for their game players will  be able to create games for the stickman with the help o f built-in animations. Players will simply select an animation and will start building their game with the hel p of drag and drop features in the toolbox . Players will select any feature from the toolbox and drag it onto the animation. Players would be able to create their games according to their level of perception, imagination and how they want their game to be. After creating their game, players will be able to play their created game.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Following are the goals and objectives to be achieved during this project. i. To build an application with an interface that is easily understandable by the players and provides ease of use to them. ii. To develop a high quality animated game engine application. iii. To develop an application that provides a wid e variety of features and options to create games. iv. The major objective is to change the concept of conventional game engines, and providing players with a platform where they are able to create and play their own games easily. v. To build a high quality animated application that will give a boost to the gaming industry in Pakistan. vi. To promote the gaming and animation industry in Pakistan. vii. To develop a high quality recreational application.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: In the present time there are numerous game engine applications available like Unity, GameMaker and GODOT etc. One thing all of these applications have in common is that they involve some type of coding to create games and all of these applications have very complex features and functioning which can’t be understood without proper knowledge and practice. As game engines are becoming very popular there is a need to have applications that make game development convenient and simple. So that people interested in game development can easily experience the pheno mena of game designing and development. Computer Science has evolved a lot in the past few decades, but not everyone is familiar with coding or programming. So, the purpose of this project was to build a game engine with such features and functionality tha t allows people from diverse background s with having no  proper knowledge of coding or programming to easily create and play games.This idea has been brought to life using the .Net Framework and windows form application, having built in tools, animations and arcades that will allow players from any background to easily develop games.

heading: 1.5 Project scope
content: With the passage of time game engines have become ex tremely popular in the gaming industry. Developing games from scratch is not a trend anymore and majority of the game developers use game engines to create and develop all sorts of video games. Pakistan’s IT industry is growing very fast with game developm ent being the fastest growing area.  With the rapid  development in the gaming and animation industry in Pakistan developing animated gaming applications like “Fun with Stickman” can prove to be very helpful and can actually create an impact.  As developers I think we need to work to promote and help our industry grow as much as possible. So creating a game engine that can be accessed and used by any sort of user to develop games will prove to be extremely helpful for the growing gaming industry in Pakistan.

heading: 2.1 Literature review / Existing system study
content: There are thousands of stickman games available online. Some of the most popular stickman games are Stickman Impossible Run, Stickman Games: Summer, Stickman Ski Racer, Gun Fu: Stickman, Stickman Basketball, Stickman Soccer, Stickman Tennis, One Finger Death Punch, Stickman Battlefields and League of Stickman etc. “Fun with Stickman” will not be a simple game like these gaming applications, but it will  be a game engine. A game engine is a software that allows developers to build 2D and 3D games. There are many famous open sour ce game engines available like U nity, game maker studio, Panda3D, CRYENGINE, Blender game engine, GODOT, AppGame Kit and Marmalade SDK etc (ElHady, 2017) . Majority of the game engines available are used to develop games using programming languages like python, C++ and C#. The Game Maker Studio is a game engine that allows players to build video g ames using a drag and drop format and uses a scripting language known as Game Maker Language that is used to write scripts and events in the game. The GML is used to enhance the control and functions in the game (YoYoGames, 2018). This system will also have a toolset consisting of features that will be used by simple drag and drop method. The main difference of our system from the Game Maker Studio is that it will not involve any type of coding to enhance the controls and featur es in the game. The application will have already built -in animations and controls to be used in making the games. The players will not have to use any coding to build the game. The application will provide ease of use to the players. Similarly the GODOT game engine also provides drag and drop function to build the visual parts of the game but that is not simple enough to use and involves a lot of complex procedures. GODOT has its own scripting language known as GDScript that is closely related to pyth on in syntax so people with strong background knowledge of python can use this game engine easily. GODOT also uses open source C++ modules to improve the controls in the game  (GodotEngine, 2017). Our system unlike GODOT will be simple and easy to use, players of any background will be able to build games without having to use any additional scripting or adding any modules. The system will be user friendly and will be easy to use. Players will not have to write any type of coding to create games. Unity is one of the most popular game engine these days. It is easy to use but it also has features that require you to use C# and Java script. Using unity also requires a lot of experience as building arcades and scenes for the game can become difficult for the players (Unity, 2017). In “Fun with Stickman” there will be a variety of ready to use animations and arcades, players will not have to create any new animation, they will simply select an animation and will start creating games by dragging and dropping features from the toolbox. All these game engines are used to create games for multiple platforms such as android, iOS etc. But “Fun with Stickman” will only create games to be run on windows platform. “Fun with Stickman” is also character specific, this application will only create stickman games any other type of games cannot be created.

heading: Abstract
content: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a task to identify Named Entities (NEs) in a text. NER is a very important step for Natural Language Processing (NLP) which is a subdomain of Information Extraction (IE). The focus of this project is NER for Urdu Language which is a low resource language in terms of availability of benchmark corpus and related research. Significant amount of NER research has been done for English and other western languages, but NER for Urdu Language is a very challenging task. It becomes difficult to recognize NEs due to presence of words from other langu ages, no capitalization of Named Entities, ambiguous names that can also be used as common nouns or have multiple associated meanings with them. The goal of this project is to create a Dictionary and an NER for Urdu Language.

heading: Introduction
content: Named entity recognition is an NLP task that can detect entities in text and then classiﬁes them into their respective entity types such as persons, organizations, locations, events, etc. It is a field that has seen a considerable amount of work done in re cent years. Most of the credit goes to the Message Understanding Conferences (MUC-6) which is the sixth MUC Conference. NER grew to be more accurate in MUC-6 and MUC-7 by using statistical machine learning models trained with human -annotated data over rule -based model.

heading: 1.0.1 Importance of NER
content: With the rise of data mining and exploding amounts of data becoming accessible, it has become very important for us to extract as much useful information as we can. NER enables us to structure text and make it meaningful for machine searching. NER can be termed as the most important sub-task of IE, it not plays a vital role in IE but also helps in reference resolution,  solving disambiguates, and representation of meanings in other NLP applications. The goals of NER as defined in MUC-6 and MUC-7 were to extract entities like person, location, organization, time, date, currency and percentage  [1]. A strong NER system has the capability to generalize and recognize unseen data (data which was not used before) based on its lexical and contextual features.

heading: 1.0.2 Applications of NER
content: At the beginning MUC focused on tasks for IE such as  information extraction from unstructured text like defence information, company routine information and newspaper article, which essentially in spired the first NER system. For the past couple of decades many applications of NER emerged in the real world as a by-product of intense and continued research and development in this field. Few of the most fundamental roles of NER can be found in speech recognition, Chat-bots and machine translation. NER provide users with quick information about the text. Other applications include Q&A systems, textual entailment, automatic forwarding and searching document and news. Even at the basic level, if an understanding of the Named Entities is involved in a document it can provide much richer analysis with cross-referencing.

heading: 1.0.3 Information Extraction
content: It is the process of extracting useful data from existing data by using different statistical techniques of Natural Language Processing (NLP) [2]. It is defined as the act of identifying, collecting and regularizing

heading: 7 | P a g e
content: relevant information from the given text and producing the same in a suitable output structure [3]. Although the process for extraction has been aut omated over the years, the need to train your system to work according to the rapid changes within specified time range is very important. Using a modular approach, the process of extraction can be decomposed to make its functionality simpler for each of its task of selection, reordering and composition. The major modules identified under IE are: segmentation, classification, association, normalization and co -occurrence resolution. For the text given as the input, segmentation focuses on dividing the text based on the semantics and syntax of the data format. Lexical analyzers are commonly used to define the semantic rules to enable an effective data segmentation process. The most commonly used segmentation technique is by the Viterbi  Algorithm [4] which works on the concept of state machines. Machine learning approaches [5] are employed based on the probabilistic rules followed by the Context Free Grammars.

heading: 1.0.4 NER Classification
content: Classification methods follow segmentation which categorize similar data units into a common group such that meaningful relationships can be constructed between the grouped entities. The normalization module is used to confirm that the  extractions are according to the specified formats to enable  synchronization between the forms of data obtained at each  module. In case of repetition, co -occurrence [6] is used such that identity of each data entity is maintained. Classification in  extraction enables us to classify the major domains into which the segmented data is finally stored by using machine learning approaches. If the process of Extraction is automated, using Machine Learning techniques like Hidden Markov Model or Rule Based Approach, patterns covering different areas can be extracted in a very minimal time duration. Commonly used Machine Learning based Extraction methods can be classified as unsupervised learning and supervised learning. Supervised learning is used when there is user interaction in defining the rules for the extraction process, or in defining the sample training example based on which the supervision task can be carried out. The categories of supervised learning are propositional learning and relational learning. The need for human interaction to provide the training example is one of the major drawback of the supervised learning technique which has paved way for the unsupervised learning mechanisms which are developed by employing  corpus bootstrapping method [ 7] to obtain the seed rules from annotated systems.

heading: 1.1 Problem Statement
content: As there is a lot of information present in today’s world, there’s always a need for a system which can help us in gathering relevant information from all the data that we interact with. NER is just another tool which can help us in extracting information which can later be used for different purposes. This project aims to develop a NER System for Urdu Language which works on the same or more efficient principles of NER Systems developed for other major languages like English so that people can use this tool to extract information for the text available in Urdu.

heading: 1.2 Scope of the Study
content: A lot of work has been down and is still going on in the field of NLP and NER but, major focus has been facilitating the English Language. We are hoping to create a NER system for Urdu Language so that it can be useful for us. Taking the first step to create such a system can trigger a lot of research and development in this domain which will leave a positive impact on our work. NER can help us in many ways, we can extract information such as name of a person, organization or location from newspapers and articles. It can help us not only by extracting information but also finding relationships between the extracted information. This information can further be used for surveys, or by analyst of different organizations to find trends. NER can be used for machine translation or speech recognition. Further, we can create search engines in Urdu Language just like Google so that we can find relevant information available on the internet or on the servers.

heading: 1.3 Objectives of the Study
content: Following are the major objectives of this research work: • Generate a large-scale dictionary of Named Entities for Urdu Language • Implement Dictionary Look-up Approach for solving NER problem • Design a prototype system for NER Urdu

heading: 2.1 Introduction
content: In this chapter we will discuss the existing work on the NER System for English and other major languages.

heading: 2.2 Stanford NER for English Language
content: Stanford developed an NER which label entities in a text. It is implemented on java and it is flexible as you can define feature extractors. This system works best on the 3 classes (PERSON, LOCATION, ORGRANIZATION) but you can train it for your own data sets [8]. There are several models avai lable for Stanford NER. 4 class (PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MISC) 7 class (PERSON, LOCATION, ORGANIZATION, MONEY, PERCENT, DATE, TIME) models which are trained on MUC 6 and MUC 7 training data sets. Stanford NER uses machine learning to train itself on the data sets either built-in for the system or the data sets which you have created on your own. It tries to recognize entities present in a sentence on the basis of rules. These rules define where the system most likely will find entities in a sentence.

heading: 2.3 Stanford NER for Other Languages
content: Stanford developed NER for German  [9], Spanish, and Chinese Language. German NER uses IOB1 Classifier and the tags that are given to words are LOCATION, PERSON, ORGANIZATION, MISC, B - LOCATION, B-PERSON, B-ORGANIZATION, B-MISC, O. It is trained through CoNLL 2003 data sets using the distributional classes built from German Corpus. There are two Chinese models, distributional similarity and one without it. They work on word - segmented Chinese. Spanish model is also available.

heading: 2.4 NER for Urdu Language
content: IJCNLP-08 Workshop made huge contribution in the development of NER systems for sub -continent languages. Their focus was on five languages i.e. Urdu, Hindi, Bengali, Oriya and Telugu. They used Statistical and Hybrid Approach. Hybrid approached was used by Sujan Kumar [10] for developing hybrid NER for these languages. Rules were only defined for Hindi and Bengali Languages. Using the MaxEnt Model the accuracy for Urdu language was 27.79, 28.59, and 35.47 for Maximal, Nested and Lexical respectively.

heading: 10 | P a g e
content: Another System for these five languages was developed by Karhik Gali [11]. It uses CRF based machine learning as well as heuristic rules. It was specifically designed for Hindi and Telugu. Its accuracy for Urdu was 39.86, 39.01 and 43.46 for Maximal, Nested and Lexical respectively.

heading: 2.5 NER for Urdu Language Using Hidden Markov Model
content: An Urdu NER System was developed by researchers at Punjab University, Lahore. First, two different tagging schemes, i.e. Inside -Outside-Begin (IOB2) and Inside-Outside-End (IOE2) were used to conduct experiments [12]. The reason to use two different tagging schemes is that IOB2 is more suitable for prepositional languages and IOE2 is suitable for postpositional languages like Urdu that’s is why two tagging schemes were compared to show IOE2 produces better results than IOB2. Different techniques were used to improve accuracies, i.e. Character Level, Word Level Normalization, Part of Speech and Regular Expressions. First, the Urdu NE data from the SSF format was converted to the IOB2 and IOE2 formats. HMM was used for training and testing of Urdu NER. The precision, recall, and f-measure values using IOB2 are 38.38%, 54.04%, and 44.89%, respectively. Using IOB2 no entry for NEB, NETE, NETO, and NET P is found, whereas the highest f-measure value of NEM is found. Similarly, the precision, recall, and f-measure using IOE2 are 39.00%, 54.65%, and 45.52%, respectively.  No word is correctly classified against NEA, NEB, NETE, NETO, and NETP. After performing character level and word level normalizations, the results improved significantly with precision, recall, and f -measure as 43.91%, 57.94%, and 49.96%, respectively. However, the model was unable to recognize  NEA, NEB, NETE, NETO and NETP. using the rules, names list, and the POS information, the improved precision, recall, and f-measure were achieved as 66.71%, 71.70%, and 69.12%, respectively.

heading: 2.6 Rule-Based Named Entity Recognition in Urdu
content: Researchers at University of Minnesota used Rule -based approach instead of machine learning for NER. They used Becker-Riaz corpus [13] for their system out of which they selected 2,262 documents. In their system, lexical cues are used to form FSA. Cues are found at found randomly; at the start, middle or end of the finite state machine. These rules are corpus , heuristic and grammar based. Rules are represented as a regular expression. The algorithm finds entities in the string instead of searching the whole document . It takes a UTF-8 or UTF-16 Urdu text string as an input. Each document contains the title of the document and the paragraph in the form of two strings. In order to limit the length of input text, an n-gram technique was used. After several experiments, a 6-gram model was selected. As the bigram and  trigram were either too small or they had no room for multi world entities. Also, four and five-gram models were incapable for holding space for cues and anchor texts.

heading: 11 | P a g e
content: If an entity is found, it is sent to all 6-grams and checked. If it is found in other 6-grams as well, it is then tagged as an entity . Each processed 6 -gram is processed only once . Some famous  cities like Islamabad, Multan, and countries like Canada, India, Pakistan occur frequently with no cues. A small authority file is created so there is no need to write complicated regular expressions for these names. Lookup is used to identify and mark these entities first and then rules can be applied. The results generated by the algorithm were in 171 true entities out of total 187. The results show the recall, precision and f1 measure of 90.7% 91.5% and 91.1% respectively. Suffixes cues and anchor were though very useful but at the same time cause of most false positives and noun phrases were mostly false positive. Rules were then applied on set of 36,000 token Urdu data provided for IJCNLP. Without tuning any of the rules and with few rules the 𝑓1 – 𝑚𝑒𝑎𝑠𝑢𝑟𝑒 was 72.4% and 81.6% respectively on the test set.

heading: 3.1 Introduction
content: In this section we will discuss the approach used to generate dictionary and the algorithm by which we tag, and extract entities in a text.

heading: 3.2 Dictionary Lookup Technique
content: Dictionary lookup technique (DLT) uses a dictionary of tokens, which are Named Entities such as person, location and organizations along with their classification, and match these to kens when they occur in the lookup. Lookup is the input text given to the system.  This technique works in a linear form as each token from dictionary is matched with the text in the lookup, if there’s a match then the word is tagged with its specific classification i.e. PERSON, LOCATION or ORGANIZATION. Algorithm for DLT can be found in the Appendix A. This technique is easier to implement and it is less complicated than Rule Based Approach, which is more commonly used for South Asian Languages. In Rule Based Approach, you need to define set of rules, or create list of words and each word from the lookup must be according to those rules so it can be tagged by the NER System. The efficiency of DLT can be increased by increasing the size of the Dictionary, but this comes at the price of slow performance. As the list of words increase, the number of comparisons also increase which can slow down the performance.

heading: 3.3 Dictionary Generation Process
content: The first step towards implementing a DLT is to generate a Dictionary of words. For this, we used several methods to collect Named Entities along with their classification. The dictionary Generation Process can be broken down into the following steps:

heading: • Raw Data Collection
content: • Running Stanford NER on Data • Using Google Translate to Generate the Output • Removal of False Entities

heading: 3.3.1 Raw Data Collection
content: To collect raw data, we used the following methods: • BigQuery BigQuery is a Google’s cloud storage database. This cloud storage contains huge amount of data including list of names. We used SQL Queries (see Appendix B) to extract list of names. Two queries were used, one for each gender Male or Female. As the BigQuery doesn’t allow to download a large csv file, we divided the records in chunks of ten years each from 1910 to 2013. T his list only contained First Names and frequency against each name occurring i n the list. B y using this information, we can filter out most common names which are more likely to be found in any given text. After filtering repeated named, we got about 420 unique and correct First Names. • WebCrawler A WebCrawler can be used to extract links or plain text found on the website. We designed a WebCrawler for Geo News  website (Appendix C), which would return a file containing all the sub - links found under the Latest Section. Another WebCrawler (Appendix D) will then use this file to  go through each sub-link and extract paragraphs of plain text found on it. We focused on the Latest section because it contains more names of persons, locations or organization than any other sub-category. All the extracted text is in English Language. We used Stanford NER, which is a NER System designed for English Language, to tag the Named Entities found in the extracted text. An Algorithm is used to extract the tagged entities from the text into a separate file. Using this technique, we were able to extract about 1500 Named Entities.

heading: • Wikipedia Data Dump
content: Wikipedia provides free data dumps which contains millions of words. These dumps are in a form of text files. We ran a single file of about 170 MB through Stanford NER by dividing it into smaller parts, because of limitations from the software. Each smaller file contained te xt, which then returned a file with tagged Named Entities. These entities were then separated through an algori thm, which resulted in about 1030 correct and unique Named Entities after combing files and filtering repeated names. Following table summarizes the total entities which were found from each method and how many corrected entities were left after filtering repeated and wrong entities along with the division of entities according to their NE class.

heading: Wikipedia 5680 1030 448 485 97
content: Table 3.1: Number of Entities Found Through Different Methods

heading: 3.3.2 Google Translate the Output
content: Throughout the process of Raw Data Collection, all the Named Entities that are extracted are in English Language. To convert the data in Urdu, we chose Google Translate instead of manually translating each entity. As it is not always accurate, the efficiency was 81.33% over 1500 words.

heading: 3.3.3 Removal of False Entities
content: After Google Translation, there were some untranslated or wrongly translated words. All the wrong or untranslated words were either removed or corrected so to have a perfec t Dictionary of Named Entities. At the end of Dictionary Generation Process, we had 2950 Named Entities from the NE class of Person, Location and Organization.

heading: 3.4 Dictionary Lookup Approach
content: Dictionary lookup Approach requires a Dictionary and a Lookup. Lookup is a plain text given as an input to the NER System. A Sample of Dictionary is shown below:

heading: 15 | P a g e
content: Dictionary follows the format of one Entity per line. Each Entity is followed by its NE class and a > symbol for example, “Organization>  فوج .” Dictionary Lookup Approach works by taking a single word from the D ictionary is selected an d compared to each word in the Lookup. If there’s a match then the word is tagged from the Lookup with the NE class of the word matched from the dictionary. This process is repeated until the whole dic tionary is compared with the lookup text. In this approach if there a possibility of NE being found in the sub-string of a word from Lookup, it will not tag it as NE. For example, in the word “انٹرچینج ”there exist “چین ” as a sub -string which is a Location but it will not be tagged by the algorithm. Also, if there is no space between a NE in Lookup but there is in the Dictionary, it will not tag it as a NE. For Example, if “محمدقاسم ”is found in Lookup but there is “محمد قاسم ”in Dictionary, it will not recognize it as a same string and will not tag it. heading: 3.5 NER System for Urdu Language
content: We have a user-interface system for NER in which you can copy the text from  which you want to extract the Named Entities into the text field. Also, if the size of input file is large for it, the system has an option to directly open it and run NER to generate a t ext file with tagged Named Entities. Generally, input text size that can be easily executed by our system is more than 34,000 words. The system tags all the entities and display them through highlighting each NE class entity with a different colour. Following is the screenshot of our NER system:

heading: 17 | P a g e
content: Figure 3.2: Screenshot of GUI for NER System In the text field there is text which is a lookup for our dictionary, and on the right panel all the NE class, with their respective colours, are listed. That means for example, all the words highlighted with Red are Locations. Same applies for rest of the NE classes. There is an option to Save the output. The output follows the format of IJCNLP where each sentence is separated and each word is on the new line. The tags are written next to the word which is a Named Entity. Another silent feature of this System is, if an NE is missed by it there’s an option to add the NE to the Dictionary by simply highlighting it  and using the buttons on the right panel. Each button can assign the highlighted text with their respective NE class. For example, if “لاہور ”from Lookup text is not tagged by our System after running it, we can highlight it using the cursor and add it to the Dictionary by clicking the Location button on the right panel. Once the NE is added to the Dictionary, it will get tagged if it appears in the Lookup text. This feature makes the Dictionary more flexible and gives the user a choice to add more to already existing dictionary of words.

heading: 3.6 Evaluation Methods
content: In NLP we use Precision, Recall and F -measure to evaluate the system. We calculate these values for Nested, Maximal and Lexicon matches. Nested can be both nested and largest possible Named Entity ,

heading: 18 | P a g e
content: Maximal is the largest possible Named Entity whereas Lexicon are the items inside the Named Entity found in the text. Precision and Recall: In IE, fraction of relevant instances retrieved is called Precision. Recall is the name of fraction of relevant instances retrieved over total number of instances. We use Recall to determine Quantity and Precision to determine Quality.

heading: F1:
content: Precision and recall scores are often combined into a single measure. Example of it is the F -measure. Basically, F1 is the average of p and r, where p and r are precision and recall respectively. With 1 being the best value and 0 the worst.

heading: Formulas:
content: Following are the formulas for calculating precision, recall and f-measure for nested, maximal and lexicon matches found: • Maximal Precision: Pm = cm/rm • Maximal Recall: Rm = cm/tm • Maximal F-Measure: Fm = 2 × Pm × Rm / (Pm + Rm) • Nested Precision: Pn = cn/rn • Nested Recall: Rn = cn/tn • Nested F-Measure: Fn = 2 × Pn × Rn / (Pn + Rn) • Lexical Precision: Pl = cl/rl • Lexical Recall: Rl = cl/tl • Lexical F-Measure: Fl = 2 × Pl × Rl / (Pl + Rl) where c is the number of correctly retrieved (identified) Named Entities, r is the total number of Named Entities retrieved by your system (correct plus incorrect) and t is the total number of Named Entities in the test data.

heading: 4.1 Introduction
content: In this section, we will discuss how we will evaluate our system and what are the results produced by our system.

heading: 4.2 System Testing
content: To evaluate our NER System, we used the script given in the Appendix E which is provided by IJCNLP. This script requires two files as arguments, one is our output file generated after running NER and second is the reference output file, which is a test file provided by IJCNLP on its website. The script compares both files and the precision, recall and F-Measure are calculated for all Maximal, Nested and Lexical  matches found.

heading: 4.3 Results and Analysis
content: We compare the results with the performance of IJCNLP on the same test data. This helps us to know how close we are in terms of efficiency with other models. We are benchmarking IJCNLP because it provides best scores in terms of NER for South Asian Languages, especially Urdu. Figure 4.1: Comparison of Results Generated by our NER System against IJCNLP

heading: 20 | P a g e
content: We tried different techniques to improve the results. There is improvement as the results are close to the one of IJCNLP but there is still room for it. The different techniques applied are discussed below:

heading: • Adding Training Data
content: As the IJCNLP’s Training Data also contains Named Entities  like Person, Location or Organization, so we used their training data to extract all the entities. Adding more to the Dictionary can improve its performance. • Removal of Other Entities The evaluation script provided by IJCNLP evaluates the system for more than 3 NE classes i.e. Time, Currency, Measurement, etc. As our dictionary only contains words from 3 NE classes i.e. Person, Location and Organization the results are automatica lly reduced because it is evaluating for entities that are not present in the Dictionary. So, to improve results we manually removed tags from the annotated test data file which is passed as an argument for evaluation to the script. It can be concluded th at performance of the Dictionary can be improved by addin g more words to it, for current and other NE classes as well.

heading: 5.1 Introduction
content: In this section we will discuss what are our future plans regarding the development of this project. Future work includes the tasks yet to accomplish and goals which we want to achieve after the system is fully developed.

heading: 5.2 Future Work
content: Following are the major goals for the future of this project: • Further refinement of the Dictionary Lookup Technique • Expanding the Dictionary • Expanding the features of the System Our major focus would be trying to make the DLT more efficient. For this, we can use different approaches of Supervised Machine Learning like Hidden Markov Model or Rule Based Approach. These approaches can be implemented using the Dictionary as a training set or using these approaches along DLT to improve efficiency of the System. Also, refinement can be made in the Dictionary Generation Process in order to make it less time consuming and more efficient. Expanding the Dictionary can improve the results of our System as it would be able to detect even more Named Entities found in text. This can be achieved by adding more NE for all NE classes into it. Currently our system works for NE class Person, Location and Organization. In the future, we want the system to detect entities like Time, Currency, Measurement Units, et c so it can serve as the most versatile NER System for Urdu Language.

heading: Abstract
content: In this project, we have created an Online Medicine Delivery Marketplace (OMDM). This system reduces the gap between the consumer and the pharmacists and allow them to communicate with each other. The system allow s the users to search medicines from our database on the basis of diseases i.e. by typing ‘ headache’ in the search bar lists all the medicines which can be used for the treatment of ‘headache’. The system will allow the users with a messaging board functionality, to share ideas and experience with other users. Users can view all  pharmacies near them. The customers is able to place orders by selecting a specific pharmacy using the proposed android application or web portal. This system allows the pharmacist to create promotions and discounts of their products which is visible to c ustomers. The system also provide s comparative discount rates of pharmacies in nearby places. In addition, the proposed system will show the updated deals placed by the pharmacists. The system accurately maintains a list of medicines for user to view. The Website is MVC based and using ASP NET technologies for development and using SQL SERVER as a Database service. While the Android is created in Java language and is using the Web APIs to communicate with the Server. Page 4 of 132  May 15, 2018 Table of Contents
