heading: 1.1 Brief Introduction
content: The Pharmacy Council of Pakistan (PCP) is a professional and statutory federal institution for accreditation and regulation of pharmacists and promotion of pharmacy education in the country. The PCP regulates the pharmacists, their pharmacy’s support perso nnel and infrastructure in Pakistan. The Pharmaceutical Industry of Pakistan meets around 70% of the country’s demand of Finished Manufactured Medicine. The domestic pharma market, in term of share market is almost evenly divided between the Nationals and the Multinationals [1]. Although Pakistan’s pharmaceutical sector is expanding and becoming more sophisticated at a high pace, but about more than 50% of the population has no access to modern medicines and find it difficult to locate these medications nearby [2]. Pakistan still being a developing country still lacks a way to distribute its modern medicine to the whole population. Developed Countries such as USA, UK and Australia have online market place which allows the customer to buy the medicine on the internet and get delivered to their homes via their own local delivery service. The main motivation behind this system is to connect the consumer to their local pharmacist in the area or the specified area defined by the user through the Internet. Our system not only provides user with all the medicine info, including the dosage, the ailment it cures, and much more. It also allows the user to buy medicine online and keep track of their orders using the web or the android portal provided to user. The system will also allow the users to interact with each other using online message board functionality , also known as forum, via posted messages. They can also discuss various topics with each other using the message board. The system shall be apt for viewing and ordering medicine and allowing communication with different users and with the pharmacists themselves. This system will not only improve the business of the pharmacies but also advertise the deals the pharmacist shall be offering. Page 13 of 132  May 15, 2018 Our system will have all the medicines stored in the database which shall be easily accessible by the user of the web portal and the app.

heading: 1.2 Goals and Objectives
content: All the medicine’s information is at the consumers fingertips all the time. No need to search online for it on different sites.

heading: 1.2.1 Main Goals
content: The Main goals of our project is/are:  Develop an online medical market place which provides medium for a customer to order medicine from a pharmacy near him  Provide a Friendly User Interface  Provide a Web and Android Portal  Develop the system with latest technology and trends

heading: 1.2.2 Objectives
content: The Objectives of our project is/are:  Improve the overall Medical E-Commerce in Pakistan  Provide a bridge for the consumer and pharmacists to communicate with each other  Provide the details of all medicines at the fingertips of the consumer  Improve the distribution of medicine in Pakistan  Create a forum which will allow different users to communicate with each other  Educate the users with all kinds of details of Medicines

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: Although Pakistan’s pharmaceutical sector is expanding and becoming more sophisticated at a high pace, but about more than 50% of the population has no access to modern medicines and find it difficult to locate these medications nearby. Pakistan still being a developing country still lacks a way to distribute its modern medicine to the whole population. Developed Countries such as USA, UK and Australia have online market place which allows the customer to buy the medicine on the internet and get delivered to their Page 14 of 132  May 15, 2018 homes via their own local delivery service. There are some online medical delivery systems present in Pakistan, but the common problem is they are bound to their own medical stores. They have their own stocks of medicines in their store and medicine is delivered to whole city from that particular store which results in high charges of medicines and delivery. Well known pharmacies from where people usually buy their regular medicines, none of them is providing online facility and there is no online system in Pakistan which targeted such pharmacies. OMDM is targeting all pharmacies present in different areas of Lahore, which provides an opportunity to customers as they can order medicines from same source rather than switching to any other online store.

heading: 1.4.1 Assumptions
content: 1. A mobile and web application will be developed to provide medicine data anywhere to the user. 2. The system will provide variety of analysis on the data acquired from multiple orders.

heading: 1.4.2 Constraints
content: 1. The project budget must not exceed from final recommended budget. In case the project is not completed within the budget  project team will be responsible and will accommodate within the required budget. 2. The project must be completed within the due date. In case project is delayed, the delay period must not exceed more than 10 days. 3. The final product must fulfil all the customer requirements.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope
content: Technological change has been the significant main push for an increase in pharmaceutical productivity and improvement in the commerce of medicine field. In developing country like Pakistan individuals know about the innovations of the IT sector and use of it in day to day life but are not utilizing it to increase profitability of their business and making ease for themselves. The main reason behind this scenario is, there is currently not any system available that would be  intelligent enough to help consumers and pharmacist, so that’s the main motivation for us to develop Online Medicine Delivery Marketplace (OMDM). We believe pharmacies will use the OMDM if they expect to get boost in their business and promote the medicines which they have. Page 15 of 132  May 15, 2018

heading: 2.1.1 Dawaai.pk
content: Dawaai.pk is an online store still in use in Pakistan. Basically, here medicines with their rates are displayed on the wall straight away, you can buy which medicine you want to buy. There are different sections also, you can select your particular section and it will take you to tips and medicines relating to that part icular problem. The issue with this site is that the medicines are too expensive and not matching the rates of market, hence people who require less expensive medicines can’t use this site [4].

heading: 2.1.2 Servaid
content: Servaid Pharmacy. Servaid is a medicine delivery stor e, which is present in different cities having more than one branch in every city of Pakistan. This company delivers medicine at door step. This show all the big medical stores in Pakistan on the map, but it doesn’t show local stores near your location [5].

heading: 2.1.3 Health Online
content: Health Online is another online medical store that is still in working. They have different categories to display at the very first click made to go to this site. There is a special deals option, in which they have displayed some good products relating to medical field and most importantly that sections carry the products that are on promotion, that are available at a discount price. They have their own prices at which medicines are bought. They are not connecting the customer with the pharmacists [6]. Page 16 of 132  May 15, 2018

heading: 2.1.4 Punjab Medical Store
content: Punjab Medical Store is also an online medical store. This one is unique from others and its uniqueness is that it allows us an option of "Choose File" to order our medicine. That means all we need to do is to upload a picture of our desired medicine and the rest is done. We can share picture of medicines or we can share any piece of paper con which that medicine is mentioned or in other way we can say that, simple upload picture of prescription given by your doctor and you are done. The site is too slow and doesn’t offer the location feature [7].

heading: 2.1.5 Chemists World
content: Chemists World is another website. This one includes some really good feature in which you can register at this site and also there is an app available for this store, you can just sit and can get medicine at your doorstep with just a cell phone in your hand. Another amazing feature of this website is live chat. You can chat with them regarding your problem and regarding your medicine and what can be better than h aving a complete discussion about what you want [8].

heading: 2.1.6 Easy Medico
content: Easy medico is a website in which they sell medicines at a discount, most of the time medicines are available at a discounted price. Also, they have online doctors and pharmacist to act afte r your order. You need to upload your prescription, pharmacist will prepare the cart, just select the medicine then, select the quantity and you are done with it. Consumers can privately and conveniently order medicines from online chemist store as well as  get to avail free home delivery, indeed, the access to written product information is a lot easier to obtain than in traditional drug store [9].

heading: 2.1.7 MedPlus
content: MedPlus is an online medicine ordering app, the common problem with this app is their poor customer service. They don’t deliver their medicine on time or they are willing to provide medicine at door step if it is of some good cost otherwise they prefer to deny the request. Page 17 of 132  May 15, 2018 1 mg is another app that is very well known for ordering medicines online. One of common problem that was found in this system was a group was unprofessional people was handling the app who did not have any idea about medical field, many doctors who were linked with this app, they complaint about this issue [10].

heading: 2.1.8 Inayo
content: Inayo is another  app for this purpose and issue with this system that there are registration problems. Web registering is not available, usually many people complaint about this problem that they are interested in registering but they are unable to register [11].

heading: 2.1.9 Netmeds
content: Netmeds is also an app for online medicine system and issue with that app money transaction method is not reliable at all. Sometime people pay money but didn’t get any notification back and also the team of Netmeds find it difficult to figure out sometime  who paid for his/her order [12].

heading: 2.6 Software Development Life Cycle
content: Waterfall Model with Rapid Prototyping: We are going to use a mix of Waterfall Model with Rapid Prototyping. Why use Waterfall Model? It is used when the requirements are well known, product definition is stable and technology is understood. Why use Rapid Prototyping Model? It is used where customers are non-technical and usually don’t know what they want and what they can have. Due to unclear requirements of what will be easy for the users, and moderate chances of requirement changes, we will use prototyping model to provide users with prototypes and they will update our prototypes which will help us in clearing our requirements according to those feedbacks provided by the users, till all requirements are captured and are cleared. Then we will use waterfall model to implement those requirements. Because waterfall model needs clear requirements, the clear requirements will be taken to start the waterfall phases. In waterfall model, we get a complete document at the end of a phase to verify that all the requirements are implemented according to requirement plan. Because of these documents, maintenance of app becomes easy. Figure 2 Rapid Prototyping and Waterfall Page 71 of 132  May 15, 2018

heading: 3.4.1  K-Mean
content: In our project we have implemented a machine learning algorithm known as K-Mean Clustering, which is a type of unsupervised learning algorithm meaning it performs calculations on a the given input without any specific target output in mind. Hence without telling what this algorithm should be looking for in the inputs provided, it itself does the work and finds structure within the data. K-Mean clustering as the name indicates, finds N fixed numbers of clusters based on the input data provided. A cluster is a group a data that are grouped together due to similar properties. In this algorithm, a cluster is known as centroid which is point at the centre of a cluster. Every point in the data set is a part of the cluster is the most nearest to it.

heading: 3.4.1.1 The Algorithm
content: First we provide two things to this algorithm firstly is the number of centroids (k) to make and from which data set it is to make from. This algorithm starts by randomly defining N number of centroids. From there, it works in iterative steps to perform two tasks: 1. Assign each data point to the closest corresponding centroid, using the standard Distance formula. 2. For each centroid, calculate the mean of the values of all the points belonging to it. The mean value becomes the new value of the centroid. Once step 2 is complete, all of the centroids have new values that correspond to the means of all of their corresponding points. These new points are put through steps one and two producing yet another set of centroid values. This process is repeated over and over until there is no change in the centroid values, meaning that they have been accurately grouped. Or, the process can be stopped when a previously determined maximum number of steps has been met. [3]

heading: 3.5.1 MVC Architecture
content: The software architecture which will be used in this project is MVC (Model View Controller).

heading: Figure 28 System Architecture
content: Online Delivery Market Place is a complex and huge system which is based on web-application and android created for Pharmacist and Customer. This app records all the brands, company, medicines, customer’s info, etc. Our project is based on MVC architecture with ability to take large number of data. The model view controller (MVC) architecture is used to implement interfaces. MVC is a famous choice for web apps.it separates the logic in three parts i.e. model, view and controller. The model will inform the view to update its display according to data as it contains the data that app should use. In our project the model will specify what data the interfaces should contain that doctors interface, nurse’s interface and patient’s interface and it will inform the view to update display according to the changes that has occurred. The controller will handle all the logic that updates view and model in reply to input from the users. Our project could have input buttons and forms to add delete and edit information from their  profiles, in prescriptions etc. Our project data model will be contained in database ( SQL Server) our applications controlling code will be written in java script and interfaces will be written using CSS/HTML. This is similar to MVC. This separation of re sponsibilities in MVC architecture will help to make our project more flexible, secure and will increase performance. Page 92 of 132  May 15, 2018

heading: Abstract
content: The current marketplaces are more oriented towards customer empowerment rather than brand empowerment. The goals of customers such as shipment tracking, payment methods etc. are well served, whereas, the goals of brands are not properly realized. The brands find it difficult to manage their storefront, sales and marketing, to do so they use a separate solution or service providers for each occurring problem; which requires more time, labor and cost. So, the idea is to develop an all-in-one platform that will allow the brands to manage their problem under the same hood. The marketplace will include product selling solution such as analytics to monitor ad performance, sales, impressions etc, and product promotion methods that will allow brands to run ads on Fa cebook, Instagram and Twitter to grow their sales and revenues. The brands will also have the leverage to benefit themselves with our analytics module. This module will include the implementation of analytical reports such as sales growth, ads performance, product success, increase or decrease in revenue etc. The seller can use the collected information about views, sales, impressions etc. to offer products to the consumer in a most effective way. The platform is made intelligent and unique using Machine Learning and Predictive techniques. The platform identifies the patterns of sales and user behavior to recommend trending products to its user.

heading: 1.1. Introduction
content: With the advancement of web and mobile technologies, various innovative solutions are proposed in the market which are made to improve e -commerce experiences of both the buyer and the brands/vendors. The rise of e-commerce in Pakistan has resulted the interest and investments of various venture capitals and companies including some major players such as Rocket Internet [1]. Various marketplace models and solutions are introduced recently which tend to solve the problems of consumers and businesses e.g. Daraz [2] and Kaymu [3]. From shipments to payment securities, product comparisons to discount offers etc. The ability of an e-marketplace to fulfill the needs of both consumer and businesses determines the success of the marketplaces. Since the needs, require ments and expectations of buyers and sellers from the marketplace keep on changing with the passage of time, the existing system does not remain adaptive so there is always a need to improve that system or even sometimes there is a demand to introduce a new system. The basic model of the existing marketplace remains the same; such as listing, buying and selling of products etc. There are some strengths that make these marketplaces successful.  However, there remains some loopholes in current solutions due to which th ese marketplaces cannot fulfill the needs of customers and/or sellers. One of the major weakness in the existing marketplace is the digital product marketing which is quite an expensive and time-consuming task. Brands and businesses often hire a team of digital marketing professionals which makes it a little more expensive. If not, freelance digital marketers run advertisement campaigns for the brands which requires their constant attention and monitoring. Another weakness in the existing model is that they are commission oriented. Brands must pay an enormous amount of commission on a sale of an expensive item. Our proposed system is not commission oriented rather it encourages the seller to grow their businesses. The problem of digital advertisements can be solved with an automated online marketplace solution where brands and businesses can continue their sales as well as digital marketing campaigns on various rich-user social platforms such as Facebook, twitter, Instagram etc. This marketplace will contai n all the modules that are involved in sales, analytics and ad campaigns. The analytics section will allow the seller to critically analyze the customer’s behaviors, sale’s growth and ad performance, so that the seller can recommend trending products to its customers and grow their business. The ad campaigns section will allow the seller to advertise its products on the rich -user platforms like Facebook, Twitter and Instagram, so that the seller can acquire more potential customers. It will be a lot time saving and cost effective for businesses to manage these three task s from single platform. On the other hand, the machine learning and predictive techniques are used to identifier the patterns of sale and purchase of products based on customers and market trend behaviors.

heading: 1.2. Objectives
content: 1. To develop an All-in-One solution for the brands allowing them to list and market their products on the same platform. 2. Allowing brands to do more online business without paying commission on sales. 3. To develop business analytics for individual brands allowing them to monitor their sales.

heading: 1.3. Problem Statement
content: The e-commerce sector has grown to a great potential in Pakistan. More and more people are attracted towards e-commerce rather than traditional markets. With this increasing growth of customers, brands find it difficult to find the correct audiences for their products. The need of an automated marketplace arises here where brands can create their storefronts, list their products and market them to the right audience.

heading: 1.5. Project Scope
content: Many websites, applications and different online platforms are developed for brands where they can sell products online and increase their sales. In the recent decades, a lot of work is done on e-commerce and many platforms are available for sellers but on  this platform which we are going to create is very effective for emerging brands. 1. Commission free sale of products. Brands will pay for only the features they use. 2. More focus towards brand empowerment. 3. Complete analytics of product sale on mobile applic ation and website so that brands can analyze the growth, profits and impressions etc. 4. Automated marketing solutions for brands so that they can run their marketing campaigns on rich-user platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and Twitter. 5. Brands consider th eir brand identity as a prime factor when entering a marketplace. This includes their fonts, logo, designs, layouts etc.

heading: 2.1. Existing System Study
content: Several applications and web products have been made over the time to meet brands’ need for customer acquisition, e -commerce store building and product marketing. A few products that are providing solution for individual modules are listed below. Woo-commerce [4] is an ecommerce store building plugin available for WordPress CMS. It supports both physical and digital goods. Several small e-commerce businesses such as Over Clothing [5], The Untold Wish [6] etc. are using woo -commerce at the time. A vast community of theme designer’s familiar with WordPress and woo -commerce is design ing several themes and designs so that ecommerce stores can choose among them. These themes and designs are available on many marketplaces of digital goods such as ThemeForest [7]. Another existing e -commerce platform Ecwid [8] is providing a shopping cart  solution that can be integrated in any website. It gives the ability to seller to create an e -commerce store in the existing website instead of creating a new storefront. Ecwid is also transforming the concept of e-commerce to f-commerce i.e. Facebook-commerce by allowing sellers and vendors to create their stores and selling the products via Facebook pages. Once the seller attaches their Facebook page with Ecwid store a new tab is created on the Facebook page where buyers can place order for any product o r add the products into cart. Fishry [9]  is a Pakistani ecommerce storefront builder and inventory management platform. Few of Pakistan’s major brands such as Nishat Linen [10], Hush Puppies [11] and ECS [12] are using Fishry’s inventory management solution. Interactive reports are provided to the brands so that they can analyze sales and user behavior. Shipment services are not offered as a subscription. eBay [13] is a globally working marketplace that has made it successful to automate online person to person auction. It also allows retailers to sell goods to the consumers. Browsing and bidding on auctions is free of cost but sellers are charged for listing of their goods on eBay. There are two types of transaction fees. 1) A non -refundable fee for listi ng the items and      2) 1 -5% fee of final sale price when the auction is completed. Kaymu [3] and Daraz  [2] are C2C and B2C aggregator marketplaces working in Europe, Asia and Africa. The platform allows buyers and sellers to perform deals in the domain o f fashion, home appliances, electronics, beauty products etc. Sellers can list as much products as they want. Logistic service providers relate to stores for carrying out goods to the consumers. Another example of online marketplaces and store builders is Shopify [14]. Besides just store building, Shopify also allows drop -shipping i.e. instead of instead of linking directly to the supplier’s website, the seller takes the responsibility of selling the goods and delivering them. In social media marketing an d advertising domain, Hootsuite [15] is a social media management platform enabling its users to manage all their social media account from one place. It also allows to publish content on multiple channels, run advertisement campaigns on different social p latforms and provides analytics about the ad performance i.e. impressions, clicks, reach etc.

heading: 3.1. Entity Relationship Diagram
content: Fig 13 – Entity relationship diagram (Final Version)

The application is developed using the MVC architecture model in PHP Laravel framework. Models are the representation of entities in this architecture and responsible for providing the attributes either directly from database or customized on runtime and for maintaining the relationships with other models existing in the application. Laravel Eloquent provides the functionality for model implementation  and makes it easy for models to retrieve data from database using Eloquent query builder. An important component of this architecture are  controllers which are responsible for request processing each time a route is invoked by the user. This includes the validation of headers received in the request, saving data into database via models and passing it to the views. The validator instance of user’s request is passed to the controller’s method to validate the request on server side. Views are the render-able front-end that are server to the user for interaction and experience with the application. Views receive data from the controller and render them using the directives available in Blade templating engine provided in Laravel. The basic architecture and request flow is showed in Fig. 14.

heading: 3.2.2. Recommendation engines
content: The platform is made intelligent and unique using Machine Learning and Predictive techniques. The platform identifies the patterns of sales and user behavior to recommend trend ing products to its user (which includes not only buyer but also the seller). For the very reason Prediction-IO is used; which is product of Apache.  It’s an open source Machine Learning standalone server which is bundled with

Apache Spark, MLlib, HBase Spray and Elasticsearch which enables you to create predictive engines for any machine learning task. It lets you: • Quickly build and deploy an engine as a Web-service with customizable templates. • Responds to dynamic queries in real-time • Deploy multiple engines variants at a time. • Support machine learning and data processing libraries such as MLlib and OpenNLP. • Implement your own machine learning model and incorporate them into your engines. The application makes a request to Event Server to store data. E vent Server is used for continuously storing data from our ecommerce platform. The basic workflow of request in Prediction-IO engine are showed in Fig. 15. Fig. 15 – PredictionIO Architecture

heading: 4.1. E-commerce
content: E-commerce marketplace is developed using Twitter’s Bootstrap framework for front -end and PHP Laravel along with MySQL database for backend.

heading: 4.1.1. Login/Signup
content: The application uses Laravel’s Socialite package to for the implementation of login and signup via Facebook and Google. Data from these social platforms is saved into database.

heading: 4.1.2. Entity Records
content: The headers in the request are validated in the controller using form request validators. After validation a model for the entity is created in order to save the form data in database.  A sample code for storing storefront records upon registration is given below. public function store(Requests\StorefrontRequest $request){ $store = new Storefront($request->all()); $store->creator_id = \Auth::id(); $store->save(); $role = StoreRole::where('name', 'Admin')->first(); $user = \Auth::user(); $store->users()->attach($user, ['store_role_id' => $role->id]); flash()->overlay('Store Created!','Your store has been created successfully. Complete your information and upload products.'); return redirect()->action('StorefrontsController@edit', $store); }

heading: 4.1.3. Authorizations
content: Authorization logics provide a security measure on each request by disabling unauthorized users to send request. Application uses policies and request authorizations for implementing this behavior. A sample code for update storefront policy is given below. class StorefrontPolicy { use HandlesAuthorization; public function update(User $user, Storefront $storefront) { return $storefront->creator_id === $user->id; } }

heading: 4.1.4. Categories using Nested Set Model
content: It is not predictable that how many levels of subcategories will a category belong to. For example,

Men’s clothing has Western clothing as subcategory and Western clothing have Formal wears as subcategory and each subcategory might have further subcategories. Because of this, nested set model is implemented to maintain parent and child categories  keeping in consideration the parent -child relation and the left-right positions of each category. For populating categories for the first time, a seeder is written based on this nested set model. For implementing nested sets following columns are added in categories table. • parent_id • _left • _right

heading: 4.1.5. Search
content: Search is implemented using Algolia[16] ES for which Laravel provides a driver to interact with . The Laravel Scout driver post the JSON containing all data for the product model. Algolia’s server indexes the entity. When a search query is fired to Algolia server it returns the index by searching the complete JSON using NLP instead of searching only one column.

heading: 4.1.6. Analytics
content: The application provides analytics for orders, revenues and views. Each time one of these three event occurs, the IP address of user is stored in the database. The location and other geographic attributes are retrieved based on the IP address of the user u sing GeoIP. Interests of user are retrieved based on his frequent pattern of actions in different categories.

heading: 4.1.7. Marketing
content: Facebook provides a marketing API  for running social media campaign from the platform.  Facebook OG API provides permission for pages management required for marketing API. A token is generated and renewed on hourly basis via Facebook authentication and authorization for the user intending to publish an ad on user platform.

heading: 4.1.8. Payments gateway
content: Stripe and 2Checkout payment methods are used as payment gateway. In stripe and 2 checkout unique hashed key is generated against every order payment for user  and we also record these payments because if user want any refunds than we can assist him easily. A sample code for payment gateway is given below: public function store(Request $request, Order $order) { $amount = 0; foreach ($order->orderedProducts as $ordered_product) { $amount += $ordered_product->product->latest_price->amount * $ordered_product->quantity; } \Stripe\Stripe::setApiKey(env("STRIPE_SECRET")); $token = $_POST['stripeToken']; $user = Auth::user(); $customer = \Stripe\Customer::create( array( "email" =>  $user->email, "source" => $token, ) ); $charge = \Stripe\Charge::create([ "amount" => $amount*100, "currency" => "usd", "customer" => $customer->id ]); $input = $request->all(); $payment = new Payment($input); $payment->user_id = \Auth::id(); $payment->stripe_id = $customer->id; $payment->amount = $amount; $payment->order_id = $order->id; $payment->save(); return redirect()->action('OrdersController@continue', $order); }

heading: 5.1. Project summary
content: The developed web application not just run as a business but help s other businesses run through it’s different modules like marketing automation, audience selection and analytics. Sellers can easily setup their products on their storefronts and set the pricing and discount offers. They can keep record of orders and sales for each product. Once the product is listed, the system allows the seller to run marketing campaign to engage more customers to the listed product. The campaign runs on rich -user platforms Facebook and Instagram which are proven to be best converting platforms for ecommerce. The analytics and insights section help the seller to know to targeted audience which will be most likely to buy the product. The customers, on the other hand , will get a wide pool of brands and their products to choose from according to their need, budget and preferences. Our machine learning engines help the customer find the best product taking into consideration his own actions, the actions of the other users having same interests and the products.

heading: Introduction
content: Our aim to make delivery system more and more efficient reliable easy to deliver and low cost for our customers. There are many problems which people face in delivery process, like they have to pay extra charges for extra weighted and also for urgent delivery. We are solving these issues through our idea of direction base delivery system. We are providing urgent  delivery system city to city and within city too. We deliver things through registered persons with our system. For example, a person is travelling from one city to another and a person wants to deliver something to that city where the registered person is going, he will take his material and deliver it to the specific point. Our system will also charge less than the other delivery system. This project is basically a direction based delivery service. There will be number of registered persons especially tr avellers which are travel on daily basis with our system. The registered persons have to be clearance for security issues and their data will be testified through our system. His / Her criminal record will also be checked. After their registration with our system they will be allowed to deliver through our system. The one who wants to deliver something will post his request to our website with required detail. Now one of our registered person will response to the request to that requested (sender) person. A fter contacting each other delivery person will deliver the product to the require destination. After the package arrives at the destination the sender will be notified about it through our services. The receiver should have valid code and CNIC to get the package from our delivery person. We also providing facility that if someone wants to get something from other city and location he / she can post request of that thing and our register person who is coming from this direction and get this thing for this p erson. Sender will have to pay the charges to the System. The payment will be divided into the ration of 70:30 for delivery person: system. Motivation and Scope This project is basically designed to improve the delivery system by decreasing time consumption and shipment cost. Our system will provide the live tracking (Streaming live geo location) method for both sender and receiver. There is a lack of such service in all courier company currently operating in our country. Time saving: Our system will be time saving .As most of the deliveries will be delivered within hours or in less time. The customer will be able to select his desired route and the delivery person will then deliver the package to its required destination. Our system will be a very quick system as compared to the other delivery services because the delivery will be done by the person who will be already going to the place where the sender wants to deliver his package.

heading: Less Costly:
content: Our system will be less costly as compared to the others.  The price will not be completely dependent on the weight of the package. This means that our system is not weight conscious. Price will not get higher with the increase of few kg’s like every courier company does. It will get higher but not with the incre ase of every kg. So, that is why our System will be less costly as compared to the other courier companies that are currently operating in the country.

heading: Live Tracking:
content: Our system will provide the live tracking facility for the delivery. The sender and rec eiver both will be able to track the current location of their package through our tracking facility. No such facility is currently being provided by any other courier service in Pakistan. This will surely help the customers to track their deliveries in a much better way. Easy to access: Our system will be very easy to access. The customer will just need to enter his desired destination and select the person from the proposed list and it is done. The customer will then contact the selected delivery person and provide him the package to be delivered.

heading: A Proper Rated System:
content: Our system will use the proper rated system for the delivery person. The ranking will depend on the number of the deliveries done by the person and the time in which that person has made his deliveries. Through our rated system the customer will be able to get the better idea about the delivery person and easily select anyone with better ranking from the proposed list.

heading: Luggage Delivery:
content: Our proposed system will also include the lugg age delivery. One can also send his luggage through our delivery system.

heading: Project Abstract
content: The basic aim of this project is to create a system that is capable of providing solutions of daily life problems to the effected people at their doorstep. Thus, saving their time and energy as most of the people are tired of their daily tasks and tough routine. People cannot spend time in going out, finding a suitable worker/ professional and that’s not all. After they find a suitable and experienced worker that may have skills good enough to provide them a perfect solution to their problem, there comes the bargaining time. Here start the quarrel and the consumer might end up settling up with a mediocre professional as he is promising to charge a reasonable amount in return of the mediocre service. So, to eliminate this, we designed HAZIR, a system that has the capability of providing the best for the best with the best. This system comprises of 4 layers. One for the admin, one for the company representative where he’ll respond to the customer complaints. From remaining 2, one is for the professional and the other is for the user. Both layers (the professional and the user) are actually the iOS applications that are going to interact not only with one another but with the admin and representative layer as well. Here the admin and representative layer are the web applications. The flow of this system has been designed very carefully and professionally in order to remove any hurdle in getting the best. The Professional will register himself by entering credentials through iOS application to ensure the security measures being taken by our team.

heading: 1.1 Introduction:
content: In these busy days it is very hard for common people to take out time out of their schedules to go to a plumber, electric operator or a mason. It’s hard for them to search skill full worker which they require in their daily house hold activities. This phenomenon created a need in market for platform which facilities the blue collar personal as well as the skillful personal in other fields as well. This project would be a platform where end users would get all major home services sitting at home. We shall make an IOS application which will contain a portal that hires skilled personal from common people through a short registration process. These personal shall provide services according to their expertise. Nowadays people are extensively busy in their work so it is difficult for them to arrange these people in time for their homes and even if they find a professional or a mason, quality of work can’t be guaranteed however, Hazir will facilitate them with experienced and approved people that have years and years of expertise. These professionals will register themselves by filling the form according to their profession. They will be registered by their area so that they can entertain their clients in that specific area. Each personal will intimate his/her per hour charges and they shall be quality rated by the customers .Professionals with high and positive ratings shall be put on a high priority mark whilst the user is looking for a worker, whereas the professionals with low or negative ratings shall be blocked from the scene for a while unless or until they raise their ratings positively. Customers will have their account and they can choose the required personal according to their area. Customer will search according to the area so they can avail services from a nearby professional in no time. There shall be fixed charges of visit which would be mandatory to pay and later. When the service provider arrives he/she will on timer would start when the work begins and at the end this session would be completed by service provider, this will allow application to calculate the total time and bill which shall be generated according to the time spent on the field and at the end of the session customer will quality rate the service provider.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: If we closely observe the technological trends there is immense shift in people shifting to smartphone these days. People like to buy online and avail any online services if available at reasonable rates. Our objective is to promote this trend and encourage people to be a part of this trend following. This will bring vast change and ease in daily life of every individual who avails these services. People don’t need to Vander here and there and waste their precious time in finding such services. They shall be facilitated at their door step with quality services. Quality shall be maintained with help section available in which consumers can complain about any query they want to put in and they shall be answered in sue time. This application will give people a sense of security as all personals who will provide services will come through proper channel after proper verifications. Authentic people will be available to provide services which will ensure quality services.

content: From the above data, we analysed that most of such companies are actually either hiring their own professionals (workers) or they are contracting or collaborating with 3rd parties to provide services to the customers who contact them through their platform. heading:  User Interface
content: It is obviously very important we are much focused on that. The application we are trying to build is rather simple, with most of its concepts relaying on already established start- ups, but our application comes with a some more top notch facilities that we hope would leave the user/customer coming back for more. Our application is totally for free at App Store, as the team would first like to see the progress being made before any further investments are considered.  Area Control and Category Check To make sure, that only the relevant professional receives the request and the request is sent to the professionals who are closest to the user we designed this feature.

heading:  Complaints System
content: The system will judge the Professional on the basis of the complaints made by the user in regarding the services he provided. The Professional will be notified of the complaints and will be encouraged to improve his quality of performance thus, creating benefits for both the professional and the user as well. The user just has to tap complaints button, and type the issues he faced regarding the professional. So, gone are days when people had to make calls and get things done. The user shall be responded immediately by our representative.  Smart Phone Application for iOS: Our rivals, such as sukoon.com.pk are providing such services but only through a web application. They are currently not having the smart phone application. But on the other hand, we have designed an iOS application, Android version of which is planned to be made in the near future.

heading: Abstract
content: The project aims towards the development of cognitive robots which possess certain level of Artificial Intelligence.  Scientists have been putting their efforts to build robots that can perform different tasks and solve daily life problems efficiently; but still they lack human intelligence and cogni tion. This project includes cognitive frameworks for designing and implementation of simultaneous localization and navigation approach, and utilize computer vision as a primary technique for the development of robot. Here cognitive system is referred as a system which has a tendency to acquire knowledge about environment and perform rational actions according to the collected information. Cognitive framework will provide artificial general intelligence (AGI) developers to program and implement cognitive constructs in robotics (for example ASIMO and iCub ). It will regulate mental activities of the robot in order to ensure the smooth execution and synchronization of cognitive cycles. Robot will localize itself in the environment and navigate towards its destination by recognizing and avoiding obstacles throughout the path. heading: Chapter 1: Introduction
content: Artificial intelligence  in robots is the ability to recognizes its environment (localization) and maximize its chance of success by taking decisive actions to achieve some goals (Russell, 1995). The main purpose of artificial intelligence is to build such cognitive agents that think like humans and act like humans  (Dafoe & Russell, Nov 2, 2016.) . Cognitive agent is such an agent which performs mental functionalities based on general perception and response under the guideline of cognitive cycles (Franklin & Ferkin, 2006). Robotic industry is getting flourished rapidly in a way that it has maneuvered major modules of intelligent robots such as navigation, obstacle avoidance, problem solving, object recognition etc. As far as industry is concerned, there are f abulous examples such as autonomous explorer, turtlebot etc. These robots have features of localization and making a path by avoiding hurdles for proper navigation. As these robots assist in our daily housekeeping jobs, they are capable of cleaning and mov ing objects to different places. For simplification and making these jobs accessible, there are innumerable middle ways such as ROS, MIRA and YARP. Indeed, so much work has been done but still limitations occur in a way that whenever the features of navigation and obstacle avoidance are needed, either they are implemented every time or they have to be integrated according to the application in building process. There are so many places where domestic and assistive robots not only socially interact but also perform multitasking; another extensive issue is the design and engineering. Considering a robot has to perform multiple tasks such as communication, navigation and exploration of its environment and avoiding obstacles, there is a need of an architectural solution in that case, so that navigation and architectural level can be integrated instead of having algorithmic solutions. A large number of algorithmic solutions exist, although the need of hour is to have a solution that is implemented on architectural level. In this regard, the best way is to use cognitive architectures as they provide memory systems along with other cognitive modules like procedural memory, perceptional memory and so forth. This modular approach at architectural level on which all th e cognition is mapped provides us a lot of advantages which are not available otherwise, for example to maintain the map of environment localization is needed we can construct all this in its memory which is not only for navigation rather with the help of codelets, it can use this content for different purposes. Codelets are small chunks of code, each of them is responsible for executing a well - defined and simple task (Andre´ L.O. Paraensea, 2016). Intelligent Machines and Robotics group at COMSATS Institu te of Information and Technology Lahore is developing a general purpose self -aware artificial general intelligent socially assistive robot. That include properties such as Embodiment, Emotion, Dialog, Personality, Human - oriented perception, User modelling,  Socially situated learning and Intentionality. Cognitive modeling is one of the approaches to achieve artificial intelligence. Various groups are working on each of the above-mentioned modules. The sole purpose of this project is to build an artificially intelligent socio-cognitive robot having human oriented perception to avoid obstacles in its path and navigate in the indoor environment. Implementation of another i.e. Cognitive Conversational/Dialog Agent is in development process and its proposal has be en submitted in COMSATS to FYP committee (Arshad, Shafqat, & Arif, 2017). Indoor navigation and Obstacle Avoidance in Domestic Robots Cognition can be described as “process of acquiring knowledge” with respect to environment (Long, February, 2010). Cognition lies in various fields of life, including Philosophy, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Neuroscience, Computer Science, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). The word “Cognition” is a complete world in itself. Considering how immense the scope of cognition is, it looks like an impenetrable job to indulge that in robots , as a whole (Long, February, 2010). However, it can be accomplished to some extent, such as observing environment by robot and capturing the important details, observing obstacles and navigating through them feasibly. The phenomenon of genetically-equipped abilities in a biological system has occupied biologists' and artificial intelligence researchers' interest a lot. The learning mechanism in humans is an ever- lasting cognitive ability which enables them to acquire knowledge and summarize facts. Therefore, to understand human learning mechanism and indulge those aspects in computer system is a worthy scientific objective. Having that achieved, the computer can provide a significant assistance to human society and can also be used to test the consistency o f learning theories. The idea of cognition in an intelligent robotic system incorporates functionalities of memorizing and learning, solving problems and communication. Therefore cognitive architecture has been designed to meet our needs. (Catherina Burghart, 2005) What would be the reason of relating consciousness with robot machines? There are two main answers to this question. First and foremost would be to improve our technological understanding of the idea of consciousness. At this period of time, c omputer models of the certain aspects of cognition may result in being useful in improvising our approach of processing conscious - information, just as computer models have been useful in many other fields. Computational modeling has become a fruitful and a ccepted methodology for studying consciousness. Mainly there have been two provocations for cognitive work: to create a better and rational understanding of the essence of biological system's consciousness and to develop machines that actually showcase awareness. (Reggia, (2013)) Vision is an engineering aspect for the cognitive architectures that proceed in a real environment, it creates a chain of certain computer vision techniques for a particular situation. Like obstacle avoidance in navigation tasks is solved in the same manner as in robot control architectures: robot restructures the scene from stored images and relates machine learning to collected data and color histograms to find passable ground. Similarly, the ATLANTIS robot architecture constructs  a height map from binaural pictures and utilizes them to recognize obstacles. The CARACaS architecture also calculates a map for hazard avoidance from stereo images and range sensors. In addition, identification of moving objects in the scene needs optica l flow and model -based segmentation (Iuliia Kotseruba, 2016) Detecting people and their gestures is a distinctive task in social robotics. Combination of input from camera and sensors, and common vision techniques are frequently used here as well. For instance, DIARC architecture practices a neural network for face recognition, laser readings for leg detection (M. Scheutz, 2004) and least-cubes deterioration over SIFT(Scale Invariant Feature Indoor navigation and Obstacle Avoidance in Domestic Robots Transform) features for object recognition  (P. Schermerhorn J.  K., 2006) . The cognitive architecture indulged in child -like robot iCub utilizes SURF features, AdaBoost (Adaptive Boosting) learning and a mixture of Gaussians for hand detection and following. RoboCog and CORTEX find people in a robotic salesman set -up using camera and a branded software from Kinect. Then, local binary patterns and a SVM (support vector machines) classifier are trained to identify specific people and deduce their gender and age. Kismet, a social robot, uses simple motion detection, skin tone feature map and neural networks to find the faces and eyes of its caregivers. (Scassellati, 2002) A very rare percentage of systems integrate biologically reasonable vision. One of the most decorative examples is the Leabra vision system called LVis  (R. C. O. O’Reilly, 2013), which is based on the structure of the ventral passageway of the brain: the primary visual cortex (V1), inferior temporal (IT) cortex and the extra striate areas (V2, V4). Just like in human visual system, the responsive grounds of neurons become less location specific and more characteristically intricate in the advanced heights of the hierarchy. All layers are communally interlinked, enabling the higher-level information to engage the bottom-side-up processing during both the preliminary learning and successive recognition of objects, and contain local, persistent inhibitory dynamics that bounds motion levels across layers. Amongst its several solicitations, Leabra is intelligent to discriminate loads of object classifications fr om artificial images with noise and constriction  (D. Wyatte, 2012). The visual system of Darwin VIII is also demonstrated on the biological ventral visual passageway. Similarly to LV, neurons in succeeding areas contain increasingly larger receptive areas. With this system on board Darwin VIII is able to fragment a scene and classify visual substances (simple shapes and colors) (A. K. Seth, 2004). The SASE structural design practices a Staggered Hierarchical Mapping (SHM) for low -level visual characteristi c processing. Although the structure of the human visual pathways is not replicated, SHM is a categorized neural network having localized associations, where each neuron receives input from a constrained section in the preceding layer. The receptive fields’ sizes are the same within the same layer and bigger in upper levels. SHM was tested on a turtlebot robot in an indoor navigation scenario. ART and HTM are further biologically inspired neural networks which are used for several visual identification and organization tasks. Considering how deep learning methods are becoming progressively widespread in computer vision, it seems unforeseen to see that not a lot of cognitive architectures engage them. One of the examples is deep learning architecture DeSTIN, that proceeds visual input in the OpenCogPrime architecture (B. Goertzel T. S., 2013). Generally, the dedicated channels are used for each scenario by the architectures that work with genuine visual input, which is becoming easier with the broadly accessib le software toolkits such as OpenCV or Kinect API. On the other hand, the systems that try to model more commonly used and biologically conceivable visual systems such as, Leabra or BBD, are not as resourceful and their services are limited to meticulous situations. Despite unpredictable visual complication and saneness, simulations generally provide the same data: objects, their belongings (label, shape, color etc.), positions and properties of the agent itself, occasionally environmental factors too (e.g. weather). Some simulations provide pixel-level data, for example, the simulation used the experiments with Leabra  (R. C. O’Reilly, 2013) . This simulation is epitomized by 100 grou pings of objects extracted in 3D with multiple enlightenment levels and fractional constrictions. Else, the visual saneness of the simulation generally functions in purely appealing commitments (R. Evertsz, 2009). The world of robotics is developing and n ourishing majestically. With improvements in the development of intelligent agents, the reuse of specific cognitively inspired strategies and designs has brought about the development of the field of Cognitive Architectures (Langley, Laird, & Rogers, 2009; Samsonovich, 2012), a special kind of control systems using inspiration on how cognitive functions from the human (or animal) mind might be computationally implemented and used to provide intelligence to an artificial agent (Paraense, Raizer, & Gudwin, Oc t 2015). The latest emerging technology and its development is named as fourth industrial revolution 4.0 (Moavenzadeh, 2015). This era is the time of the accessible and proficient sensors, artificial intelligence, smart and learning cognitive machines and robots. Japan is a practical example of fourth industrial revolution, according to Japanese Prime Minister, robot market would reach $21 billion by 2020 (Saiidi, 2017). And expect revenue for robotics to be near $70 billion by 2025 (Thomas, 2009). However, world is adopting robot workers in entire industry such as Japan has 315 robots per 10,000 workers. On the other hand, South Korea is at 478; Germany has 292; United States is at 164 and in China the number is at 36  (Knight, April 2016). Within such an im mense market, robotic firms all over the world are now unanimously shifting their attention towards cognitive architectures to build robots equipped with humanoid intelligence. A cognitive architecture for an intelligent robotic system is required to sup port fast perception, recognition and understanding complex contexts and learning of anonymous behaviors (Burghart & Mikut). Every cognitive robotic architecture consists of Simultaneous Localization and navigation approach as a basic building component wh ich enables a robot to localize itself in an alien environment and navigate accordingly and avoid obstacles to reach its selected landmark.

heading: 1.1 Objectives
content: The aim of this project is directed towards the development of domestic service robot whose basic functionalities are navigation, localization and obstacle avoidance. And to achieve that very purpose the robot requires to interact with the environment, that is where computer vision comes in as a driving force.  More specifically the final objective of th e project is to develop an application that can operate a robot which performs the task to localize itself in that particular environment , detect the obstacles and reach to its destination by avoiding the Indoor navigation and Obstacle Avoidance in Domestic Robots obstacles in its path. The project develops a syste m for a robot that performs following functionalities:  Implementation of localization and navigation techniques  Implementation of image processing technique for visualization and recognition of surroundings and its own position using Kinect sensor.  Recognizing obstacles, landmarks and objects.

heading: 1.2 Problem statement
content: To build a cognitive robot that can simultaneously perform localization and navigation through an indoor environment by avoiding obstacles.

heading: 1.3.1 Assumptions:
content:  It detects the obstacles in its path towards the destination.  It recognizes the obstacle at a predefined threshold.  It navigates through the path avoiding all the hurdles.

heading: 1.3.2 Constraints:
content:  We have to limit the navigation and obstacle avoidance abilities of the robot for an indoor environment.  It is a very hard job for a small capacity robot to process the huge amount of data collected from the outside world using a simple Kinect sensor.  The robot will operate in a scenario created by the user in a small indoor area.

heading: 1.4 Motivation and Scope
content: Robots are procuring intelligence with time and they are becoming an  integral part of the society and human society is evolving into man nourishing society, so the role of robotics, particularly the socio-assistive robots, is very essential. As they work like a human colleague, the interaction and relationship between humans and machines is very crucial and to strengthen that relationship there is a need of cognitive abilities. Although the project is about navigation and obstacle avoidance which can be accomplished without cognition, however cognition provides architectures/ frameworks to the robots which allow them to learn about the environment and it transforms the manual and repetitive robots into learning and interacting robots. Localizing a robot in an environment is a phenomenon that gives a precise and accu rate information of its position to the robot with the help of different kinds of sensors that visually sense the environment. Just like when a human wants to confirm his location, he visualizes the surroundings to get familiarized with the environment. Th e autonomous robot can do the same with the help of various localization and mapping techniques. (Negenborn, 2003).  Monte Carlo localization (MCL) Also known as particle filter localization, refers to a phenomenon that enables robots to localize themselves in an entirely unacquainted environment. Giving a map of the territory, it provides an algorithm that helps in approximation of the current position of robots, as it changes its position and senses the environment.  The representation of current state/position is done by using particle filter, that means a hypothesis of locations. Particle is basically a guess about the environment randomly generated by robot. Robot releases a number of particles and then senses the environment. And when it finds about the wrong guesses, it discards them and make new particles closer to the accurate ones. It is done parallel to its movements

heading:  Occupancy Grid Mapping
content: Is a set of algorithms helping mobile robots to construct maps of the environment around it by using multiple on-board sensors. Moving robot emits rays and estimates the distance of objects around it with the help of reflection of emitted rays. With that information robot creates a map of the surroundings and localizes itself in that map.  3D Sound localization An algorithm that applies aural technology on robots enabling them to decipher the sound waves, locate the source and calculate distance between the origin of sound and robot in a three-dimensional space. The sensors on the robot helps in determin ing the directions of incoming (horizontal and vertical) soundwaves and calculate the distance between them. It needs a specific design of sensors to occupy wider range on all sides.  Sound localization Indoor navigation and Obstacle Avoidance in Domestic Robots technique is commonly used in many real–time applications such as hearing aid and sonar technology etc.

content: Abstract  Our most of the population is using bikes due to the convenience of riding and parking. However, the theft rate of bikes from parking is very high. The proposed system consists of two modules: 1) face detection and recognition, 2) license number plate recognition and conversion of number into text format. This project is aimed to implement an automated theft prevention security system for bikes by combining the recognition of rider’s face and license plate number using digital image processing. In recent time, many parking management systems are in practice like token system, toll system, keeping information about vehicle features, etc. But the problem with these systems is that they are unreliable and old-fashioned and can be easily cheated. Many measures have been taken by different organizations to prevent theft in the parking areas. One of these was the use of token system. The parking meters which rely on coins or tokens are inefficient and insecure due to lots of dependency on humans for the management of parking and possibility of the use of fake tickets. These systems need to be modernized in an efficient way so that they require less human effort and processing time. On top of that, they should be able to provide required security features. Our system stores face image of rider and the back license plate number of same rider’s bike. Every rider entering the parking lot goes through an appropriate channel of security measures so that theft cases can be reduced. Digital image processing provides us some of the best solutions to tackle with these problems. Face recognition and license plate recognition are two major components of our project. Human face is the key feature of human body on the basis of which we can differentiate one human from other. We employed this key property of human face in our system for identification and verification. Variation in human face can be used for identification of an individual and license plate is used to identify the registered vehicles, which has made it essential component of many monitoring and vehicle identification systems. Besides the security of bikes in our system, its further benefits include the control on the entrance of suspicious rider or any person who is expelled from the institute or organization. Further, the log file of daily entrance/exit records of riders would be helpful in investigation after the mishap.

This software have the ability to verify image of a person taken with digital camera by matching it with hundreds of images stored in database. It provides very efficient searches up to 1,000 registered face references [8]. This software is very useful for face recognition purposes having very high percentage of accurate result. Our project is also very similar kind of general purpose software but their functionalities are very different. Our software not only uses face recognition technique but also employs it to provide one of the best security solutions. 2.1.2 Literature Review of Face Recognition Techniques Face Recognition is an important field of study traversing various disciplines. The progress in this domain has advanced to a level that Face Recognition systems are being manifested in real world i.e. security monitoring, surveillance and identification systems, defence systems etc. This fundamental concept is of utmost importance for constructive interactions among people and effectual communications.  The rapid growth and development in this discipline is due to a variety of factors which includes the development of efficient algorithms, the accessibility of databases consisting of facial images and the methods for evaluating the efficiency and performance of different Face recognition algorithms. Various Face Recognition problems may include: Identifying and verifying one or more faces from an image or video by comparing the detected faces with faces stored in the database. This section gives an overview on the major human face recognition techniques that apply mostly to frontal faces, advantages and disadvantages of each method are also given. The methods considered are Eigen faces (eigenfeatures), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and neural networks. The techniques are analysed in terms of the facial representations they used.   2.1.2.1 EigenFaces: EigenFace is one of the most deeply investigated technique of Face Recognition. They proposed that face images could be reconstructed by a collection of weights and a face picture known as Eigen picture. For this purpose, different face images of the same person are collected so that variation can be obtained. Each image from this collection corresponds to an eigenvector using a covariance matrix. The representation of these eigenvectors are known as eigenfaces. Weights are calculated by projecting the image of face onto the

The match face image is determined by evaluating the face class image that gives the minimum Euclidean distance. Figure 4: Samples of Five classes along with their mean As shown in figure 4, sample images of five different faces was added one by one in the database. Mean of all these classes is then kept by eigenface algorithm which continuously updates it as the database is updated i.e. upon the addition of a new image in the database. Therefore, Eigenface appears as a simple, practical and fast method. However, it does not provide invariance over changes in lighting conditions and scale. 2.1.2.2 Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA): Linear Discriminant Analysis is a very widely known technique for dimension reduction and feature extraction. In this technique, the projection of data is done onto a vector space (lower-dimensional). This is done so that the ratio of the distances (between-class) to the distances (with-in class) is maximized. This helps in attaining maximum discrimination [9]. LDA and the related Fisher’s discriminant are the methods used in machine learning and pattern recognition to find linear features which characterize two or more classes of objects. The Fisherface approach solves the problem of illumination as it maximizes the ratio of the distances (between-class) to the distances (with-in class). However, its drawback is the small sample size. This problem is often faced in practice as the total number of training samples fall less than the feature space. In this case the traditional LDA algorithm fails.  2.1.2.3 Neural Network: The feature extraction of neural network is more efficient than other face recognition techniques. WISARD was the first neural network technique used for face recognition. It maintains a separate network for each stored person [17]. Successful recognition is based on the way you construct a neural network structure which is almost dependent on the application you want to develop. Convolution Neural Network [19] and Multilayer perceptron [18] are used for face detection whereas Multi-resolution pyramid structure is used for face verification [20]. Support Vector Machines (SVM) are also used for Face recognition [14]. The training time is as long as 4 hours whereas the classification time is less than 0.5 second. The Back Propagation Network (BPN) is the most widely known and best algorithm in Multilayer Perceptron’s training.

content: The BPN provides an efficient computational method where it changes the weights in feed forward network with differential units of activation function through which learning of training set of input and output data can be obtained. However, its drawback is that it is a slow technique. 2.1.3 Literature Review of Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Techniques Character Recognition is the process of detecting, identifying and segmenting characters from an image. But to say in more precise terms, it is an art of recognizing and detecting characters from an image and converts it into machine editable form or American Standard Code for Information Technology (ASCII) [13], [14], [15]. Character Recognition is also one of the most fascinating and interesting areas of artificial intelligence and pattern recognition. It is getting more attention since the past few years due to its vast applications. Advancement is also going on in Optical Character Recognition (OCR) that is the processing of handwritten, computer generated or printed document and documents which are created manually.  Optical Character Recognition recognizes characters which are optically processed. The difficulty with character recognition can be explained on the basis of two criteria. One complication is the type of text which is handwritten or printed. The other depends on the acquisition process. This process can be on-line or off-line. The on-line method gives better results than off-line method. In on-line recognition of characters, real time character recognition is performed. In this method, the searching of character’s location is not performed. However, in off-line method the character is given in the form of grey scale or binary image to the character recognition algorithm. The methodologies of pattern and character recognition are used extensively in Character Recognition systems. Over the past few years many techniques have been given for character recognition. Some of these techniques i.e. Matrix matching, Feature Extraction, Fuzzy Logic, Structural Analysis, Statistical Techniques and Neural Networks are discussed below: 2.1.3.1 Matrix Matching: Matrix matching technique uses matrix to convert each character into a pattern within that matrix. Then the comparison of known characters with pattern is done with the help of indexes of those known characters [16]. It works best on uniform and monotype single column pages. The drawback of this method is that its recognition rate is sensitive to image deformation and noise. 2.1.3.2 Feature Extraction: Feature Extraction technique defines each and every character by the absence or presence of some key features. These key features include width, height, lines, loops, stems, density and other characteristics of characters. This technique is a best approach for Optical Character Recognition of high quality images, laser print and magazines.

heading: 19 of 73  16 May 2018
content: 2.1.3.3 Fuzzy Logic: Fuzzy Logic has a key concept of multi-valued logic which differentiates it from other OCR techniques. It allows the definition of some intermediate values between conventional evaluations like black or white, true or false, yes or no etc. This is a way to infuse a more human-like approach to the logical thinking of computer programming. Its application is majorly done where answers have uncertainty and distinct values like yes or no are not involved. 2.1.3.4 Structural Analysis: Structural Analysis is an OCR technique which identifies characters by determining the shapes of sub features of the image. It also examines the sub-horizontal or vertical histograms. Its major advantage is that it works best for newsprints and low-quality text. 2.1.3.5 Statistical Techniques: Statistical Techniques undergoes statistical decision theory and uses some sets of optimality criteria and decision functions. This helps in determining the probability of patterns observed in the type of a certain class [12]. These techniques make assumptions that are based on the statistics that are available for each class, set of features extracted from images. Major types of statistical methods include Clustering Analysis, Quadratic Classifier, Hidden Markov Modelling, Bayes Classifier etc. 2.1.3.6 Neural Networks: A neural network is an architecture that consists of neural processors which are adaptive. Its adaptive nature makes it very efficient as it can adapt to certain changes in data and learns from the input. It takes an image and samples its pixels and matches those pixels to an index of character pixel patterns which are known. This kind of behaviour is good for damaged text and fixed documents. It can perform computations more efficiently and at a faster rate than other classical techniques. 2.2 Stakeholders List Stake Holders of this software are those who have an interest or concern in this system.
