heading: Abstract
content: Software requirements are considered as the main building blocks of a software system. But it is very difficult way to build a software system just from the requirements. Usually requirements are in natural language(s) and are considered as non-technical. Here we need a software architecture that provides ease to the technical persons to understand the model of a software system. Software models are the true reflection of requirements. A small amount of change in requirements can vary the behaviour of a model. The feasibility to implement the stated requirements can be verified by analysing the models. Nowadays Software industry is adapting Model Driven Software Development (MDSD) that involves less human interaction and more automation. The base of MDSD is a software model which depends upon requirements. Virtuous requirements produce a perfect model that leads to an efficient, flexible and reliable software product ultimately. Project is suggested as an application of Model Driven Engineering (MDE) and its aim is to provide a shared and collaborative platform with synchronized web and mobile (android) interfaces to remote team members in purpose to create/edit a syntactically and semantically verified software model on the base of structured requirements.

heading: 1.1 INTRODUCTION
content: Suggested project is the core application of Software Engineering domain. Day by day the domain is going mature and demands maturity throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). After Requirements Engineering, designing itself is a challenging phase so the need of hour is to give more concentration on designing to gain better development results. Complexity of a software model grows as the complexity of requirements increase. To overcome this complexity, Software Designers needed a tool (A Software) that will work like a bridge. In fact, a syntactically and semantically verified model is the need indeed. Project is recommended as a designer assistant to the software designers. Its uniqueness is that it produces the software models on the basis of software requirements; like a traditional designer and it is not just like drag and drop or drawing tool. The Project is focused to provide synchronized web and android interfaces to the software designers to generate UML diagrams. Initially project is bounded to the Class diagrams with synchronization. Currently the scope to reuse the modelling artefacts is limited as compare to code reusability, so the designers redesign the similar models from scratch that demands the high investment of resources. With the availability of collaborative and shared space, verified models can be used to design analogous model or to gain an insight to a domain. As each software system has some inputs to operate on outputs, inputs and outputs for the proposed system are the structured software requirements and a software model respectively. Structured requirements mean that requirements are captured under some rules and regulations and is bounded to write the requirements in a pre-define format. Major and the most important component is to capture and analyse the requirements and provide a suggested model on an editable canvas that is derived from the provided requirements. On the canvas, explicitly end users can modify the model and as a result requirement will be changed implicitly and changes will be applied to the remote repositories. Both requirements and models will be controlled with a joint traceability mechanism. To join the system, each user will have credentials to login to the system and the user that will initiate the project will have the administrative privileges. Other team members will join the project. At the end, final outcome is a requirement based verified model that was collaboratively designed by team members.

heading: 2.1 RELATED WORK
content: As Software Engineering (SE) field is near to automate every possible work and now it had been turned toward Model Driven Engineering (MDE) to automate software designing. To achieve this goal world had started work on it. There are both new research and old development work available in the market. In the start developers developed just drawing tools to draw software models. After the passage of time mature tools were also developed like MS Power Point, MS Visio, Visual paradigm, Concept Draw etc. All of them are desktop base applications and support manually drag and drop. Now the market demands have changed from manual desktop base drawing or drag and drop applications to the automated mobile and synchronized software designing tools. There are also android base applications like “Draw Express”, “UML Creator” and “Flowdia Diagrams Lite” etc. The coolest feature of “Draw Express” [1] is that it provides freely drawing facility over a canvas where you can draw roughly images and it will convert it automatically to the similar well-formed images. You can easily handle each activity by your fingers. “UML Creator” [2] is also an android base application that provides colourful icons for entities that is its beauty which makes it more attractive and it also provides extension to the network diagrams. Another android application “Flowdia Diagrams Lite” [3] provides an interface to create UML diagrams but it is specialized to business process and process flow diagrams. Again, the issue is that these applications are not generating requirement base verified models. Besides these desktop and android base tools, there is another touch-base application named as “Calico” [4]that provides sketch-base designing environment. [5] It provides a freely drawing canvas where users can draw roughly and approximated sketches of models which they have in their minds during discussion. And they can refine these sketches to a precise model in future. Calico uses slates, tablet PCs, electric white boards and iPads to operate it. [5] In the above examples developers are paying their best to work out in this field, researchers are also paying their part. Like code versioning, [6]Mr. Rocco and his peers described a concept of shared and collaborative repositories for model versioning. As the size and complexity of a project exceeds the number of team members also increase, and they required shared resources to work on the project. The idea of collaborative repositories provides ease to a community of users. The verified and validated models can be shared with beginners for learning purpose. In the publication, Mr. Rocco supports the idea of creating models at collaborative repositories with an example. Some nontechnical challenges are associated with the shared repositories, one of them is to control the quality of artefacts and manage their sharing. uploaded models should be analysed to satisfy the quality of required requirements before sharing them to other users. [6]

heading: 3.3 SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE
content: Software Development Life cycle (SDLC) is the sequence of steps through which a software product progresses to produce expected results. It is the way to organized the activities to develop a software product. Normally SDLC is divided into six phases, Requirement gathering and analysis, Design, Implementation or coding, Testing, Deployment and Maintenance. A better way to use SDLC in the form of a framework that describes the activities performed at each stage of software development process is the use of “Process Models”. There are many types of process models such as Water Fall Model (it is used when requirements are clearly defined and there is no need to changing), Rapid Prototyping Model (It is used when requirements are not clearly defined) and Incremental Model (which is used when the basic functionalities of the software are well known but requirements can change over time). Software process models which we are going to use for our project are the Rapid Prototyping and the Incremental model.

heading: 3.3.1 RAPID PROTOTYPING PROCESS MODEL
content: Rapid Prototyping is used to capture the unambiguous requirement by making an interactive prototype of the system. At the start we were confused about the system, then we made an interactive prototype of the system to gain the clear understanding of the system.

heading: 3.3.2 INCREMENTAL PROCESS MODEL
content: Incremental process model is used throughout SDLC. Incremental model divides the whole project into builds and each build construct the partial implementation of the system. Later on, increased functionality is being added gradually. Incremental model consists of different five phases. Requirement phase is the first phase in which all the requirements are gathered and then analysed and verified before going to the next phase of specification in which previously verified requirement are specified in a documented form. The next phase of Architectural designing is totally based on specified requirements. Architectural model is the true reflection of requirements. All modelling artefacts and system diagrams are tested before its development. System Implementation takes a time to implement the whole system and then time for unit testing of each single module and then the system testing. Once it is tested accurately, it goes into the maintenance phase as long as it exists. If there any change request occurs in the maintenance phase, complete process model is initiated again from requirement phase to the maintenance to accommodate that change.

heading: 3.3.3 REASONS
content:  System requirements were not clear so that we used the prototyping process model.  After that we are well known about the will be developed.  These requirements can be changed over time or further new requirements can be added to increase the system functionality so that Incremental model will help to make these changes.  Even after development, change request will be accommodated due to Incremental model.

heading: 6.2.1 UNIT TESTING
content: Unit testing is a software development process in which the smallest testable parts of an application, called units, are individually and independently examined for proper operation. Unit testing is often automated but it can also be done manually.

heading: 6.2.2 INTEGRATION TESTING
content: Integration Testing is the interaction between the modules and interaction with other systems. It starts when two of the product components are available. It ends when all component interfaces have been tested. The final round of integration involving all components is called Final Integration Testing.

heading: 6.2.3 SYSTEM TESTING
content: System testing is performed to precise the functionality of a system as a whole. For this purpose, perform black box. Black box testing is based on taking inputs from users and confirms that output is correct or not. By using heuristic evaluation, the usability of the system is also evaluated that provides the ease of use to the users.

heading: 6.2.4 ACCEPTANCE TESTING
content: In acceptance testing, a system is tested with the intention of acceptability. The main purpose of acceptance testing is to evaluate the system’s compliance with business requirements and also evaluate either it is acceptable for launch or not.

heading: Abstract
content: Technological advancements these days always d emand ease and comfort to common user’s life in all possible means. People want to grasp what they acquire with few clicks on their smart devices. Everyone wants quick and easy solutions As the name suggests, the name "Host el-Pedia" is a software developed for the management of various hostel activities and the search for a better and adequate shelter for the applicant. This particular project deals with problems in finding and managing a shelter and avoiding problems that occur when manually performed. The idea will allow the user to locate the hostel at the desired place and can book the room in seconds by using this application. The focus will be to provide the ease and comfort for the students in order to fi nd the hostels  and in searching  their dream place.

heading: 1. BRIEF INTRODUCTION
content: This project has been developed so it also becomes very easy for a person with a small computer knowledge to function. This Application is very easy to use and does not require any technical person to operate. Therefore, the project is also operationally feasible. From the point of view of business people who make use of this application does not need to visit hostel manually and fill out the form. You can do all these tasks sitting at home with the touch of your fingers. So, you do not have to spend the whole day or a couple of days to find the hostel and get fit. So, you can pay more attention to your other job more efficiently. Hostel is the place that is like a second home for people living outside their home. They feel safe and cheap, living in a shelter. "Hostel -Pedia" is an innovative idea that reduces the burden of the burden manager and the applicant (student or anyone  who wants to enter a hostel). Hostel -Pedia is an Android -based application to provide hostel accommodation more efficiently. This project will help the applicant find your ideal h eaven and provide you with ease of checking nearby hostel structures and places and also provide you with the ability to control the state of your home away from home. This project will also help in managing the various activities at the hostel and to avoid problems that occur when done manually.

heading: 1.1. Problem Statement
content: Everyone thes e days is too much busy to waste their time in useless and unhelpful application. These applications keep on sending unnecessary notifications which users are annoyed of. People are too much busy in their daily life engagements such as job, business and ot her household work. They rarely find a time to investigate and search the hostels physically. There is no such work done in which user is kept in his/her comfort zone showing him/her all items of their own interest and demand. If they want to search for HOSTEL they have to go through hostel applications beside this if they want to locate hostel they need to visit application  to can come up with different hostels with pictures. A survey was conducted in this regard in which One hundred people were questio ned that weather they find it relevant or irrelevant to go to the hostel manually or physically or it will be better to use this application. The results are shown below in pie chart.

heading: 12 of 60
content: Figure 1 Pie chart From the result above it is evident that most of the people find this irrelevant and they feel annoyed because in their busy schedule they have to visit hostels frequently and most of the times they are irrelevant to their own individual context. When peop le were asked about their option they stated that their perception about these applications is always high that it will be according to their own individual interest and they will be provided with easy, fast and relevant solutions but the actual world is different. Girls are always busy and it’s difficult for them in our society to move freely and locate for hostels especially for the girls from out stations. So  this application is a gate way for them to get the desired one. This can save their time and much of their energies and they can give time to their family. Living in a Muslim society some women are not allowed to visit markets most often or they them self -avoid going out excessively. For th ese women it is very important to provide them a relevant platform where they can avail the rooms on their own interests and needs.

heading: 1.2. Objectives
content: Our main objective is to facilitate user to maximum extend in which user is provided with information of his/her own interest. In their busy routines of everyday commitments users must be provided with a platform where they are ensured about safe guarding their own individual interest. The objective of "Hostel Pedia" is to help people daily lives. We want to give everyone the "Hostel Pedia" platform, so it's possible: • Reducing traffic congestion. • Reduce road use. • Make hostel search simple and efficient. • Provide a user-friendly interface. • Display the most suitable search according to user preferences • Let the applicant confirm the hostel as the cheapest price. Figure 2 Trends in online services

heading: 14 of 60
content: According to Information and communication technology (ICT) From the above graph the trend is evident that people are shifting to modern day means of services which are online services. With every single year number of users who are using or viewing online services is increase. The core objective of this project is to target this audience and encourage them to use online services. This can only happen when users will get  interesting, easy, and relevant information which they wish to get. This project does not aim to be a mediator who will be providing online services and act as a middle man in between the franchisers and users. This project will only provide relevant information to users. This application will provide a relevant platform to both users and franchisers where interests of both the stake holders will be protected. There will be a help section in which people can give their review and put queries which shall be answered in due time.

heading: 1.3 Project scope
content: Scope of this project is not limited; this project is not limited for present use and can be used in future for further works. The system will deploy on a wide destination range. This means that the system can be used in multiple Cities.

heading: 1.4. Methodology & software lifecycle for this project
content: The software development life cycle which we used in our project is iterative model. Iterative model It is a model in which process starts with simple implementation of small set of software requirements which are gathered previously. Further iterations are performed to the evolving version until complete system is formed which is ready for deployment.

heading: 1.4.1. Software Development Life Cycle
content: Following are the reasons why we used this model: • In this model we can produce high level design of the application before we actually built the product and define the design solution for entire product. Later on, we can design and built a dummy version of that, and then produce the design based on what had been built earlier. • In this model we always build our product step by step along with its improvement so we can easily locate faults at early stage which later  helps to avoid any downward flow of the faults. • In this model we can get reasonable user feedback because when we are presenting sketches and blueprints of the product to users for their feedback, we are efficiently asking them to imagine and tell us about how the product will work. • In this model we spend much of the time in designing the project and less t ime is spent on documenting it.

heading: 16 of 60
content: Following are the steps which we followed in iterative model. • The first step is to analyse the requirements of the customer what they want from you. These requirements include both functional and non-functional requirements. • The second step is to design the collected requirements which includes designing interface of your application • The third step is to code • The fourth step is to test your product • The fifth step is to review this product • If there is any issue the system is deployed for 1 st increment and this process is repeated until all issues are resolved. heading: 5.1.Conclusion
content: Problems faced and lessons learned There were few problems which we faced during our work which include our meetings with franchisers. It was very difficult to locate the right concerned person who may talk and act on the behalf of that franchise. For instance we visited ALHAMAD hostel and they had no idea how to deal with us and their warden also had no prior knowledge and he said that all decisions are made by owner and you must fix an appointment in order to meet some responsible person. A survey was conducted on more than 100 people asking them different questions whose results are illustrated above in problem statement section. It was difficult to find people of all age groups and then convincing them to fill our questionnaire. The lessons which we learned from  this are that it is very hard to convince someone to agree on what you demand from them. People are not ready to invest shortest time in your things. You need strong communication skills and convincing power to convince someone to take some time out for y ou and perform some task for you or even give minimum input. Project summary This project is designed for common users who want to search of hostels according to their interest . They don’t need to search the hostels manually or by visiting them they can  do this with the help of this application by sitting at their home or work place . This application will provide users with relevant data and with notifications for only those hostels which they have selected. They can also find contact details and directi ons from maps to reach to their desired hostel. This application will be a cheapest platform for hostels to advertise and reach to their customers in efficient manner. They can generate notifications for discounts and add, update or delete any hostel branch. Rating system will enable other users to know about the hostel quality which will ensure quality services. Future work At first target audience for this project is ANDROID users. Later on this project intends to increase its scope in future by develop ing it on IOS which will give quality services to IOS users as well. The reason why we opted for ANDROID application at first includes it has faster real -world speed, better hardware and software integration.  For all these mentioned advantages we decided to go for ANROID application at first. This project aims to bring ease to consumer’s life by maintaining his/her interest in our services by giving them only that material what they wish to get. New features s hall be introduced for efficient advertising for franchisers which shall maintain their interest in this application. Since the software will be a great success, we are planning to add some additional features to the software, such as: • An online chat system for communication between the host and the director. • A system for providing online payments so that hosteller (if you want) can pay their allowances at the hostel online. • If the software is successful then we are planning to introduce the softwa re internationally. It will be introduced globally and will not be linked to Pakistan.

heading: Abstract
content: Blockchain is an advance technology which is used as a mean to transfer digital currency from one node to another using a peer to peer network where secure transactions can be made. Bitcoin is a digital currency based on Blockchain technology that is extensively ado pted by different organizations and people . Many hackers are trying to steal the Bitcoins by accessing your system. For every transaction we need a combination of public and private keys to sign any transaction. Wallet is the main part where public and private keys are stored. So to avoid hacking and stealing of the coins a secure wallet is required. If we save our key properly then chances of hacking can be minimized. Storing the whole private key on the wallet increases the chances of threats of hacking. We seek to fill the gap between a transaction and a secure wallet. This report figures out issues of already existing wallets identified through literature review and proposes a new method for a secure wallet. Steganography along with hacker deceiving technique aims to protect the private key for the wallet. Therefore, this combination decreases the chance of stealing Bitcoins. Our wallet serves to achieve high availability, security and effectiveness as a product. It is feasible to use by customers withou t any professional knowledge.

heading: Keywords
content: Blockchain, Bitcoin, Virtual Currency, Cryptography, Steganography, Wallet, ECDSA.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Bitcoin is a modern mean to money transfer services. It does not disclose the identity of a person . If we look at traditional way to send money, there will be a third party which is bank. Bank will store all the data of sender and receiver. In Bitcoin system, no third party is included in  money transferring so that people are more attracted towards this technology. Blockchain is also very secure, decentralized technology and it creates trust among the people by verifying the transaction. The transactional information is stored on each node. Everyone contains the log on their transaction on their own so, no one can make fake transactions otherwise the chain will breakso the Bitcoins uses Blockchain technology to transfer money. To keep the coins, people need to have a wallet. The Bitcoin wallet consists of the Bitcoin address and each wallet contains a key pair the public and private keys. Public key is used to encrypt the message and private key is used to decrypt that message. As the name shows public key is publically available to everyone so anyone can send coins to your public address. The private key is just like a password hence, so it is kept private so that no one else can decrypt your script. These keys are used as the locking and unlocking script for the transaction  so, if someone knows your private key it would be very easy for him to decrypt your script. Whenever any wallet is installed, it generates a key pair for you to make the transactions. That key pair is neither encrypted nor store d on a  secure place. Sometimes, the keys are stored on local storage and sometimes in wallet. It is very easy to get the keys from wallet and from the local storage.  An attacker can attack to the wallet and can get the private key to steal coins without any hurdle. Though the Blockchain provides a secure medium for a digital currency but insecurities lie in the Bitcoin wallet. If a wallet is lost this means that the public and private keys information is lost and eventually the Bitcoin is lost. Moreover, the information provided to the wallet providers will also be lost and the attacker can use these leaked information leads to the marketing purpose. Spam messages are sent to the account so it is important to secure these wallets. There are different means to store keys like online storage and offline storage. Everything that is kept online is not safe. User has to face difficulties while using online means of storage. Although it is very convenient to get the key from cloud but it is a ccessible to everyone. Offline storage has its own disadvantages  like availability issues it is not available all the time and if you store the key in an offline hardware, it may get lost and it will never come back. The security of wallet is really needed  because if it is not secured then the owner will face difficulties in terms of money. His all the coins will be transferred to other account and due to anonymity of the technology he can never track the attacker. Sometimes an attacker will become the owner of your wallet when he gets the key; he can easily control your wallet.

heading: Page 5
content: In short, the types of problems e ncounter in Bitcoin wallet are secure storage and availability of keys all the time. We need to store the keys at that secure storage from where it is available all the time but not accessible to everyone.  We need to propose a solution in which the keys are properly encrypted.  The vulnerabilities of attacks will lessen in our wallet. It will be very difficult for hacker to get the private key and if we keep it online, it will be secure and available to the user only in any time.

heading: Chapter 1: Introduction
content: Blockchain was originally formed as a digitalized, open record of all the cryptographic money exchange. Blockchain is a latest trend which is flourishing day by day in advancement to a secure and a reliable transaction among the peer such that no outside body is responsible for the any type of transactions. Every node of peers gets updated for every single transaction  automatically without the consent of third party. The structure of a Blockchain is a combination of a header (hash value of current, previous and nonce) and a body (transactional data). The hash function and public key -based verification is utilized to ch eck the block data and transaction data for a Bitcoin transaction. heading: Chapter 4: Methodology
content: Blockchain is one of the secure medium to transfer money from one node to another but many threats were made to the private keys to steal money, which leads to the issues of securing  the storage of theses public and private keys. In our methodology we have proposed an algorithm for a wallet, which works in such a way that it deceives the hacker by dividing the original private key into a combination of fake key and user’s input values. This wallet will falsifies the meaning of wallet to Blockchain system for a hacker but works best for the owner of the wallet . We are using a modern technology of cryptography called steganography which hides the data inside the image.  So, any transaction will happen by entering  user’s input values and then identifying the fake key which will construct the private key. Our method contains following steps:

heading: 4.1.1. Public and private key:
content: After installing the wallet the user will sign up where he will enter his name and some information. The private keys will be generated automatically through SHA-1 PRNG algorithm. To generate public key we use private key, SHA 256 algorithm (used to generate the hash value of each new block against the transactions). The public key and hash function cr eates the public address of wallet which will be known by others to send and receive the coins.

heading: 4.2.1. Fake key Method:
content: After the sign up and getting the private keys,  the system will work in such a way that it will pick only 4 characters of the user’s name mentioned at the time of sign up. For the names greater than 4 characters, the system will pick only the last four characters and for names less than 4 characters will add 0 to make  4 characters. The system will now take the ASCII values  of these characters and the increment of four will be added to these ASCII values to form up new characters these new characters are replaced with the last four characters of the original private key to generate a fake private key. This newly generated fake key is then encrypted. We are using Caesar cipher algorithm to encrypt the replaced private key. Caesar cipher is a type of substitution cipher where the characters changes according to the key. This is one of the simplest algorithms which contain the encryption text and key for encryption. For this implementation we consider the following.

heading: Page 29
content:  Let p is our original private key.  N is the number of characters of the user’s name while installing the wallet.  F is the Fake bits added in original private key.  The combination of (p,N) is required to reconstruct the key again.  N should be exact, If N is not placed on its original place the key will not be reconstructed and signature will not be generated. The novelty of this method is; for each transaction the key will be reconstructed again  by knowing combination (p,N). It will be very difficult for anyone else to reconstruct the key. As user is familiar with the N so, he can easily reconstruct the key.

heading: 4.2.2.  Probability of reconstruction of key:
content: As our private key is 256 characters long then it would be very difficult for hacker to know it. He cannot apply brute force attack because he needs to make 2256   combination to find out the key.  If the system takes only 1 bit (N=1) then probability to reconstruct the key is ½256.  If the system takes 4 bits (N=4) then probability to reconstruct the key is 4/2256 So if N is greater, then the probability to reconstruct the key is low. So, brute force attack will not be worked in this case to crack the fake key. We are taking N=4 because if N is too long then it would be very difficult for user to remember it. This tactic will overcome many issues that are produced in paper wallet, offline and hardware wallets such as in these wallets there is a great chance of loss of hardware wallet where the whole private key is stored but our method is bases on human memory i.e.  user’s input values and fake key . heading: 4.3.1. ECDSA
content: Blockchain implementation such as Bitcoin or Ethereum makes use of Elliptical curve digital signature algorithm. ECDSA was invented by Neal Koblitz and Victor Miller. For a secure signature, we use ECDSA the elliptical curve digital signature algorithm. ECDSA is the most efficient method as it uses smaller size of key (ranges from 163 to 571 bits) for the security of the signature which is beneficial for situations where storage space are limited. Additionally reduces the power consumption, bandwidth and processing power. ECDSA itself comprises of the key genera tion, signing and verification.  It refers to the elliptic curve equation for signature i.e. y 2= x 3 + ax + b. This equation is a generalized form to the solution of cryptography at a certain point D. The ECDSA comprises of 3 major steps.

heading: 3. Signature verification
content: Initially it figures out the private and its corresponding public key necessarily used for the next two steps i.e. signing and verification. Private Key is used to sign the tra nsaction. The signing process is carried out for the actual digital signatures and at last the resultant signature is verified to demonstrate the authenticity the signature. If someone else gets your private key he can authenticate any incorrect transaction.

The script is not easy to chang e.  In multi signature, when a business presents its script to spend a transaction, its internal access control policy is exposed to the world. It also has some anonymity, confidentiality and scalability issues. We are not facing some issues in our method. Except the mentioned above, user can get some other advantages by using our wallet like: No Parallel Control: In multi signature sch eme, it is very hard for an individual to  perform transaction alone. He needs 3 of 5 people to make a transaction. So, parallel control is maintained there. In threshold scheme, shares are divided in employees. To reconstruct the key all the employees are required to meet the threshold and reconstruct the key so parallel control is maintained there too. In above two scenar ios a person cannot spend money by his own. They need to rely on each other for transaction. But in our method a person alone can make transaction. He does not need any other person to authorize or approve his transaction. He can spend his coins according to his will safely. Secure Script: The script contains the transactional information. The participants who are involving in the transaction, time of transaction and the amount sent or receive. The script will be secured if it cryptographically stores the transactional information. In shared wallet, to secure the information is very difficult. A number of participants are involving in reconstruction of the private key so it is very hard to recognize which user signed the transaction. In shared wallet, PKI is mapped on employee’s public key which proves their identity in script. In our wallet, the wallet is controlled by a single person. The Blockchain itself manage the individual’s identity and logged all the transaction by maintain the chain.

heading: 7.1 Discussion
content: We began this research with a consideration that Blockchain is the most secure mean of peer to peer transaction as this technology has no reversible algorithm that could be tracked. This new technology motivated a majority of people to adopt it as a reliab le medium. But the Blockchain got a turning point when it had to deal with the keys at the owner’s side because not only securing the transaction was a meaning to security of Blockchain but also securing the private key required to transaction was the majo r issue. . Our research is based upon not only handling the flaws of Blockchain wallet so that people could feel free to use this technology. We proposed a tricky method for a wallet that provides an authorized transaction and verified signatures to transfer Bitcoins using a steganography.

heading: 7.1.1.  Significance of Wallet:
content: If we look at chapter 3 we will come to know about several existing wallets. Every wallet was proposed with a unique set of characteristics that could handle the issues with the blochchain wallets but every wallet exists with some issues. Hardware wallet faces issues of theft. Threshold wallet contains flexibility, parallel control issues. Multi-signature has confidentiality issues, scalability issues. In the light of these issues our wallet handles all the issues mentioned above. The chances of hacking ar e minimized in this wallet as compare to other wallets. There is no physical and financial loss in our wallet.

heading: 7.1.2.  Worst case scenario to Wallet:
content: In general if someone talks about a Blockchain wallet it means that it contains the public and private key. If a wallet contains these keys then this is the alarming situation that any attack made to the wallet means that you will eventually lose your keys which means you will lose your Bitcoins. So we have proposed a method where wallet act as medium to reach the private key. As steganography is used in our wallet this means that some data is hidden behind anything so even for a hacker it will be difficult to identify where the private key is as it is not stored the wallet but it could be either between thousands o f images inside a folder or on the cloud where its access is nearly impossible. For worst case scenario the private key is still secure because identifying the image does not mean that you gained access to the wallet, because the image contains a fake enc rypted private key. The reverse of it is only possible if the user’s is authenticated. This authentication is done if the user enters values he entered at the time of signing up the wallet. This scenario proves the best in case where wallet is lost but sti ll the owner feel satisfies as his keys are stills safe.

heading: 7.1.3.  Role of wallet’s owner:
content: Every object has an owner. In case of wallet he is usually an individual. The owner has a major role towards the wallet security as he has to choose the image to map his pri vate key onto it and owner has to enter the input value used for the decryption process. The question arises is that if the owner forgets the value he has to enter?  For that purpose a relationship between the owner and wallet providers is maintained by me ans of a backup system readily available to the systems access.

heading: 7.1.4.  Evaluating the Wallet:
content: The wallet is evaluated in terms of the following characteristics.  Storage: Our method secures not only the private key but also secures the storage problem of private keys as evaluate using steganography.  Reliability: our wallet guarantees the privacy of users and maintains the anonymity of the owner.  Performance: our wallet is fast to use and it is depended on the speed of internet if the image is stored on cloud.  Availability: cloud makes the availability of the private key possible at any place and at any time. The wallet has the high availability of the system.  Usability: The wallet is simple can be used easily by the people without any professional knowledge of computer science.  Economy: For a user, it is the cheapest medium to transfer money without any taxes.  Security: Security was the major purpose of this research which is highly achieved. However 100% of the security can never be achieved.

heading: 7.2 Conclusion:
content: Although the Blockchain is going through continuous process of security enhancement but still problems have been reported and active research has been made to tackle to these problems. Our research is mainly based on the fact that private keys are stolen t o get the Bitcoins. Keeping in view the characteristics of Blockchain and its security, our key management scheme is efficient to authorize and sign the transaction. The emergence of Steganography fake private key with the Blockchain has the high availability architecture of the wallet. Steganography makes it harder for the attacker to know about the image where the key is stored. Even if the hacker identifies the image still he won’t be able to make any transaction as he has to answer to system defined question which only owner knows. Abstract  Currently there are many marketplaces like Uber, Careem, Amazon, Ebay, Airbnb etc but no one is focused for just printing services and print media designs so we decided to create a printing industry focused marketplace. The printing brands find it difficult to manage their websites and marketing, to do so they prefer physical shops to find the buyers which requires more time, labor and cost. In all this they also lose hundreds and thousands of online buyers. The main focus of our website is to connect printing shops and print media designers with the buyers. We’re creating an online portal for the printing shops and designers where they can create their profiles, that can be viewed by the buyers and can order the services from all over the world.

heading: Abstract
content: Hand paralysis is a common consequence of stroke which significantly impacts patients’ daily activities. Hand rehabilitation is important to allow the patients to regain lost functions. The present project concerns the Smart Wearable Hand Rehabilitation system which combines both Mirror Therapy and Task-Oriented therapy. The system consists of two gloves: a sensory glove to be worn on the unaffected hand, which measures gripping force and finger joint movement with force and flex sensors, the other one is a motor glove for the affected hand with micro motors for performing rehabilitation exercise. Th is Project involves employing Machine learning algorithms (ML) like Support Vector Machine ( SVM), Random Forest Regression (RF, Gradient Boost Regression (GBR), and Decision Tree (DT) with accuracy of 96%, 60%, 50%, and 50% respectively that will complement the existing system to increase the recognizer to distinguish the small finger gesture required for mirror movement therapy for individual fingers along with the coordination. Besides mirror therapy, the proposed system contributes to task-oriented rehabilitation which provides different training tasks. The material used in gloves is Rexine which is tender and elastic compared to stiff and rigid appliances that are associated with conventional devices; therefore, the system is more appropriate for long-term use during the rehabilitation in homes. Further, it also consists of an application through which hand rehabilitation may be done by feeding different gestures to be performed and all the data contained on the application. A combination of advanced machine learning approaches, soft robotics and therapy makes the system a useful tool in to improve hand dexterity and functionality in the stroke patients. heading: 1. Introduction
content: Stroke is a life-threatening condition caused by the death of brain cells, with around 55% to 75% of survivors experiencing impairments such as paralysis. The loss of ipsilateral motor function, or hemiplegia, is one of the most frequent consequences of a stroke [1]. This ailment frequently has a serious impact on one's quality of life and imposes a major strain on family and society. Rehabilitative treatments with assistive devices have been successful for paralysis caused by limb problems, particularly for big motions and extremities function. To solve this, this study presents a cutting-edge smart rehabilitation tool that helps patients regain finger mobility, especially those who have lost the ability to move their fingers voluntarily. These wearables, which make use of state -of-the-art mobile and Internet of Things  (IoT) technology, enable patients to perform repetitive hand exercises, such bending and stretching their fingers, without requiring continuous hands -on therapy. A properly calibrated servomotor enables these movements, and real -time motion data is transmitted to a mobile application or secure web platform [2]. Patients recuperating from neurological injuries like strokes, spinal cord injuries, or traumatic brain lesions require hand rehabilitation because these conditions have a significant negative influence on motor function and quality of life. Repetitive, strenuous exercises that need careful therapist supervision are a common feature of traditional rehabilitation therapies. But the development of sensor -based technologies has created new opportunities for more individualized and successful rehabilitation plans. One such innovation is the creation of wearable gloves with sensors that play an important part in rehabilitation by leveraging machine learning  (ML) and IoT. Wearable sensor technology and ML algorithms have revolutionized the area of medical rehabilitation. Wearable gloves as shown in figure 1-1 are cost-effective and allow patients to exercise at home, reducing their reliance on doctors and physicians [3].

heading: Figure 1-1: Sensory Glove [4]
content: Information about various physical parameters, such as bending of hands, and grip strength are obtained by sensors installed into the gloves.  Since they are a hardware device, they are able to conduct interactions of data [3]. Machine Learning is a method to simulate the human learning process on computers whereby machines learn independently without having to be programmed or study the most apt utilization of data in order to mine in instructions and information that is either latent or helpful in large behemoths of information. These algorithms then provide the data with a personalized rehabilitation program, which changes and develops along with the increased needs and improvement of the patient.  Even in non -clinical environments, health professionals can monitor the progress of a patient.  Some of the traditional ML techniques are gradient boost (GBR), random forest regression (RF), decision tree algorithm (DT), support vector machine (SVM), etc. The support vector machine (SVM) algorithm is one of the more popular algorithms of supervised learning to be used in statistical classifications and regression analyses [5]. The DT predictive analytic model of a tree is typically used to describe the decision tree algorithm, also a vital technique of data mining technology conducted in case of classification and regression [6]. The reason is that the size, depth, and the number of the leaves of the decision tree model influence its comprehensibility. The decision tree is very precise and possesses a low number of calculating levels [7]. Thanks to the IoT, due to the convenience of data collection, storage and monitoring it would be possible to make a remote observation of rehabilitation . In the meantime, ML algorithms analyze this data to forecast rehabilitation results, offer practical insights and automatically modify treatment regimens, guaranteeing that every patient gets the best care possible given in their recovery path. The design, features and benef its of sensor -based wearable gloves will be explored in the following sections, highlighting their revolutionary potential in the field of hand rehabilitation. This innovative approach represents a significant shift from traditional rehabilitation techniques and has the potential to improve patient outcomes, reduce recovery times, and increase accessibility to therapy. Figure 1-2 shows the hand gestures that will help in the rehabilitation of patients.

heading: 1.1.1. Hand Rehabilitation
content: The main goal of the project is to make rehabilitation easy for the patients, especially after injuries such as strokes, accidents or surgeries. It helps in physical recovery of the patient. The project includes the development of hardware to make rehabilitation cost and time efficient. It reduces the need for frequent in -person therapy sessions. The ability to continuously monitor patients’ progress leads to more efficient recovery [9].

heading: 1.1.2. Machine learning for personalized therapy
content: Rehabilitation plans can be adjusted according to the patient’s progress. For example, if a patient’s progress is quicker, more complex exercises may be introduced. Conversely, if the patient is struggling, the system can adapt to provide simpler and manageable tasks. Based on past data, machine learning models can forecast a patient's course of recovery, assisting medical professionals in evaluating their  patients' progress and making well -informed treatment recommendations. The use of advanced techniques such as ML was integrated in the determination of the level of rehabilitation required. Some scholarly work is done with SVM network which improved the ability to do rehabilitation by fetching data and moving it towards the motor glove. The number of the machine learning algorithms illustrates the shifts of the landscape in computational methods, with each possessing their strength.

heading: 1.1.3. IoT integration for remote monitoring
content: IoT ensures provision of real time data. The integration of the sensors within the glove helps in increasing the understanding concerning hand issues. This focus on IoT solutions means that this project could focus on gathering, evaluating, and judging the flow of information when it comes to the signs of slumbering tendencies. IoT enables the gloves to connect to a network or cloud, allowing healthcare professionals to remotely monitor the patient's progress. This is especially beneficial for patients who live in remote areas or have mobility issues, reducing the need for frequent hospital visits. The data from the gloves can be shared with healthcare providers in real time, allowing them to offer advice or modify treatment plans promptly based on the patient's progress.

heading: 1.2. Project Scope
content: The Hand Rehabilitation Program aims to assist patients recovering from hand injuries or surgeries by improving their hand function, strength, and dexterity. The project is designed for individuals who have experienced hand trauma, surgeries (such as tendon repair), or neurological conditions like stroke. The goal is to provide a tailored rehabilitation program using wearable gloves for therapy using ML and IOT.

heading: 2. Literature Review
content: This project discusses the most recent information found in the peer reviewed literature.

heading: 2.1. Overview
content: Integrating sensors into wearable gloves along with ML and IoT increases the efficiency of rehabilitation. Flex sensors measure the bend of a finger or joint and convert it into electrical resistance. These sensors are worn on the affected hand. Force sensors measure force applied by the patients during rehab ilitation exercises and give feedback as well. These sensors are worn on the non-affected hand. Data from the affected hand goes to the machine learning algorithms such as RF, SVM, GBR and DT. These algorithms analyze how much rehabilitation is required an d improve patient's efficiency of recovery process.  As this is a classification problem, these algorithms provide accuracy, precision, recall and f1 score as evaluation parameters. Additionally, IoT will display various exercises a patient requires and will show the rehabilitation percentage. Through the integration of IoT technologies and ML algorithms, these gloves facilitate data-driven insights, real-time monitoring, and individualized therapy [10].

heading: 2.2. Significance for Rehabilitation
content: Conventional rehabilitation training is ineffective, and stroke survivors who are released from the hospital do not receive adequate rehabilitation training. Additionally, a thorough evaluation system for rehabilitation training is lacking, making it chall enging for doctors to maximize training to provide stroke survivors with the best possible care [11]. Many patients have barriers that keep them from enrolling in rehabilitation programs, such as limited funds or trouble traveling to therapy facilities because of distance. Additionally, people are unable to receive the necessary rehabilitation for their physical enhancement due to a shortage of medical personnel. Rehabilitation techniques that rely on medical personnel become more important, especially duri ng pandemics. To get over these obstacles, remote rehabilitation techniques have been created for a variety of Internet of Things (IoT) applications. These techniques use sensors to gather and interpret data in real time. This increases the accessibility, affordability, and effectiveness of remotely supervised training, which in turn affects patients' motivation during therapy sessions [12]. Furthermore, there is a dearth of thorough rehabilitation guidelines for stroke survivors and a high burden for doctors due to the vast number of stroke survivors and the little number of doctors. The stroke therapy technology now in use is costly and uns uitable for at -home use. There are many stroke survivors, there are few medical resources, and it is challenging to ensure the effectiveness and intensity of typical rehabilitation training. Objective data to assess the training parameters and rehabilitative results is lacking. After leaving the hospital, stroke patients still require ongoing rehabilitation therapy. Only a small percentage of stroke survivors may finish the rehabilitation plan because of the absence of subjective enthusiasm, and the rehabilitation doctors are unable to monitor the health status of those stroke survivors who have been discharged because the rehabilitation data cannot be sent back to them in a timely manner.

heading: 2.3. Research Studies
content: This literature review is mainly divided into three parts. i. Wearable Gloves ii. Machine Learning iii. IoT

heading: 2.3.1. Wearable Gloves
content: The physically challenged community's physical abilities can be restored and improved with the use of contemporary rehabilitation therapy techniques and procedures . To assess the effectiveness of the community -based rehabilitation appropriate technique (CRAT) program across five sites, the stroke survivors were assessed using a quasi -experimental methodology. In contrast to the control communities, the intervention group received rehabilitation instruction and a three-month course of CRAT treatment. Except for social activity among patients under 50, the end measure sho wed a significant increase in the number of patients participating in rehabilitation as well as improvements in motor function, daily living, and social activity scores in the intervention group. The findings confirm that CRAT encourages stroke survivors t o participate in therapy and achieve functional recovery  [13]. A bilateral upper limb training therapy has been proposed by Muddied et al . Unlike unilateral and linked -hand bilateral practice, the current study involved an evaluation of bilateral isokineti c training (BIT), which is a newer approach to improving upper limb functioning after the occurrence of a stroke. BIT produced significantly greater increases in motor performance on most tasks with many participants returning to normal ranges of performance and maintaining these gains at follow- up six months later  [14]. To help stroke survivors who have upper limb paralysis regain neurological control and coordination of their motions, Giovanni et al. have tried to utilize the characteristics of mirror neurons [15], electromyographic (EMG) biofeedback would enhance upper limb function for stroke patients with hemiplegia. Sixty -four patients were assigned by chance to either the control group or the experimental group and the additional group benefited from EMG biofeed back training. After three months, both groups got better, but the experimental group saw much bigger improvements in EMG amplitude, range of wrist dorsiflexion and Fugl-Meyer scores. It was shown that EMG biofeedback helps improve motor function in people with hemiplegia  [16] and therapeutic electrical stimulation . Nawi et al. developed a smart hand glove  for post stroke rehabilitation.  The most frequent motor impairments after a stroke are hemiparesis or hemiplegia in the upper and lower limbs. If movements are performed and intensified often enough, motor therapy can help enhance motor recovery, even though it varies greatly. By telling the patient and therapist how many hand movements (such as wrist and finger extensions) are performed during therapy, smart gloves are meant to offer a tool that may be able to enhance motor recovery. To create novel arm rehabilitation monitoring systems that can enhance patients' lives, more research is required to ascertain whether this type of feedback aids in the quicker restoration of hand function in individuals with neurological disability  [17]. A VR -based rehabilitation system using Cyberglove and Rutgers Maste r II-ND was tested on four chronic post -stroke patients over three weeks. Significant improvements were observed in finger fractionation, thumb range, and speed, with some functional gains retained after one month. Performance in hand function and prehension tasks also improved, demonstrating real -world applicability. [18]. Based on the brain-computer interface, Floriana et al. have investigated the application of motor imagining exercises during stroke survivors' recuperation . The purpose of the article un der review is to examine whether the use of motor imaging (MI) with brain -computer interface (BCI) technology can help improve motor recovery in subacute stroke patients in a more effective way than MI alone. To examine the ways BCI can enhance stroke recovery, it measures functional outcomes and brain activity changes. [19]. Guo et al. used pneumatic actuators with varying stiffness to develop a soft robotic glove for hand rehabilitation. The stiffness of each actuator at different positions, which permitted the actuator to bend at specific places, was the main feature of this design. The introduction of fabric sleeves, which allowed the actuators to apply greater bending force to the hand under pressure, was another essential component. Modeling was used to verify the actuator's feasibility, and experiments were conducted to evaluate the soft actuator's and the device's overall performance. It was shown that this device could do some hand rehabilitation tasks [20]. Sheing Meio presented an IoT and ML based system for upper limb rehabilitation using mobile sensors, dynamic time warping (DTW) and k-nearest neighbor (KNN). Accuracy and efficiency can be improved by further using enhanced algorithms such as neural networks or introducing spatial coordinate conversion method [10]. Research interest in wearable technology for hand rehabilitation is growing. The main objective of many robotics and bioengineering -related labs' studies over the last ten years has been to create automatic or semi-automatic hand rehabilitation devices. A rehabilitation robot that was simple to use and adaptable to different finger sizes was developed by Child et al. [ 21]. Each finger on this robot has its own actuator, which is pulled by a wire. Data format composed of each finger joint is shown in figure 2-1. Figure 2-1:position of each finger joint [22] The control was not in real time, though. Additionally, wearing comfort needs to be enhanced and the thumb design further modified. A rehabilitation robot that can sense and control applied force was created by Leonardis et al. [23] using a straightforward design. Worn on the injured hand, the robot was controlled by the surface electromyography (sEMG) signal from the healthy hand. However, the thumb design required more work, and the device was stiff, which could have caused greater pain to the victim. The robot could only move its four fingers in unison. A 15-motor-powered hand exoskeleton hand functional rehabilitation robot was created by Ueki et al. [24]. The thumb was internally rotated, and each of the five fingers was separately flexed and stretched. There was a training interface for virtual reality (VR). The data glove worn on the healthy hand can control the exoskeleton worn on the injured hand. But the structure is complicated. An electric motor-powered exoskeleton robot was created by Rahman et al. [25]. The exoskeleton robot of the wounded hand is controlled by the placement of each finger, which is determined by the resistance in the glove of the healthy hand. However, secondary hand injuries may arise due to the exoskeleton's rigidity. In summary, robot structure is the primary focus of research on robots for hand rehabilitation. Wearable gloves and exoskeletons are examples of current scientific trends. Most exoskeleton robots use stiff links, which can be difficult to wear and cause major hand injuries. The majority of designs do not allow for the independent movement of every finger. Human thumb movements are not the same as those of robots. One practical way to help individuals with hand dysfunction perform rehabilitation training exercises on their own is to use the movements of the healthy hand to control a robot that assists with the damaged hand's movements. Min Li proposed a 3D-printed pneumatic-driven soft robotic glove. A data glove is utilized to assist the damaged hand to record the finger movements of the user's healthy side. The system's average delay was 0.8 seconds. Future research on reducing system delays will be carried out adding shielding and haptic feedback devices to improve the actuator's performance [26]. Research has thus far concentrated on two categories of rehabilitation devices: stiff hand exoskeletons. With this study, robots that can fix themselves by heat healing from cuts or punctures were developed. Soft pneumatic actuators such as a gripper, hand and artificial muscles were built, and it was shown that they quickly recover and are more durable for situations where damage could occur [27] and soft assistive gloves, The suggested method is to use a vector equation to model how a multi-cavity soft actuator can move in a flexible way. The study was confirmed in the lab on a three -cavity actuator by creating a nonlinear model that connects air pressure, position, and def ormation. This model made accurate predictions about the actuator's movement and gave researchers a useful tool. [28]. Because of their flexible nature and advanced soft actuators, soft robots are suited for medical, deep-sea and tough use, but they still grapple with problems caused by the inflexible nature and weight limits of their actuators [29]. Gloves with flexion and extension capabilities that are relatively light and soft could be produced using 3D printing techniques. The glove will suit various contact and healthcare professions since it is fully 3D-printable, does not need joint alignment, and can generate up to 40 N of fingertip force. [30]. Soft glove control and position estimate could be done with deep learning. The glove allows easy donning and allows complete finger movement, gives transparent feedback between free and constrained areas, and can apply a fingertip force of up to 4.09 N  [31]. Additionally, force feedback gloves were suggested for producing haptic signals, which could improve the specificity and controllability of distant or virtual working tasks [ 22]. The most recent advances in 4D printing soft robotics, including grippers, actuators, and smart materials that contract in response to external stimuli  are discussed by Yasir Khalid in this paper. To achieve realistic implementation, it focuses on the contemporary problems and possible solution s whilst demonstrating new material, modeling methods and applications . The main elements of soft robot actuation include cable/tendon drives [33], pneumatic/hydraulic drives [32], and other intelligent material drives [34]. Polygerinos et al. [35] employed soft actuators consisting of elastomeric chambers reinforced with fibe rs to build a soft wearable glove that generates bending, twisting, and stretching trajectories under fluid pressure. Yap of the National University of Singapore [30] demonstrated a soft robotic glove made of fabric for rehabilitation training and assistance with daily duties for individuals with hand disabilities. The glove provides bidirectional motion modes, including active finger flexion and extension, and has a folding chamber wrapped within to increase the bending angle. Shanghai Jiao Tong University's Gu group [36] created a high-force fabric-based pneumatic actuator with asymmetric chambers made of two layers of textiles. To increase the output force and stiffness of the pneumatic actuators, interference pads were placed on adjacent pleat surfaces. Cappello [3 7] used two layers of different fabric materials to create a fabric - based rehabilitation glove. The glove c ould help with hand opening and closing by using different fabrics and layering them according to the air packs within. Korean D. H. Kim et al. created a circular finger stretching mechanism for hand rehabilitation in a biomimetic study that replicated the  extensor tendon's origin, structure, and tendon orientation . Most wearable tendon-driven devices for hand rehab have lightweight, compact designs, but usually do not provide a natural finger extension movement which can cause the finger joints to move too far back. The research lays out a ring-type mechanism that imitates how tendons work and move. It could move the fingers as if performing the action, more accurately and in better posture than existing assistive devices [3 8]. The University of Hong Kong's Ning Guo [3 9] created a rehabilitation glove with a flexible soft actuator component as an independent component and a non-deformable rod as the bone. Because of its convenient regulated electrical performance, PDMS may be suggested for adoption on the so ft hand's skin to further increase the sensing property [ 33]. To improve finger rehabilitation and gripping, this study presents soft rehabilitation gloves (SRGs) with flexion/extension and abduction/adduction capabilities. With the help of hybrid PID-controlled hardware, design, fabrication, and testing showed improved hand movement freedom and gripping range. heading: 2.3.2. Machine Learning
content: The usage of computationally demanding techniques for biomedical signal analysis has skyrocketed in recent years. In the general method, a computer program "learns" significant elements of a dataset such that the user can make predictions about new data that were not part of the initial training set. This falls under the purview of artificial intelligence or machine learning. Making classifiers that can divide subjects into (typically) two or (infrequently) more classes based on the attributes measured in each subject is only one of the many uses for this methodology. Analyzing biomedical data to identify or diagnose disease is a clear potential application for such a classifier. Although comparable remarks would apply to other machine learning approaches as well, this paper focuses on the usage of support vector machine (SVM), a computationally demanding statistical technique that became a study issue in the late 1990s [41]. heading: 3.1. Conceptual Framework
content: The underlying idea behind this project is to help patients who have had a stroke or are paralyzed focus on restoring hand dexterity. This is done with the help of Sensors based wearable technology, Machine Learning for giving dynamic feedback and IoT for connecting the device with a mobile application. The design concerns itself with manufacturability, functionality and fluidity to mimic natural hand movements to improve neuroplasticity and recovery outcomes. The conceptual framework integrates the following principles: • Mirror Therapy: There exists evidence regarding mirror therapy as an effective approach in rehabilitation which involves perceptual changes imitating the movement in the paralyzed limb by mirroring activities of the healthy limb. This approach promotes the neural pathways  and can help with recovery afterwards. Figure 3 -1 illustrates the pictorial presentation of mirror therapy. Figure 3-1:Visual representation of mirror therapy [51] • Task-Oriented Therapy: Analysis of various sources of information show that skills practice improves motor coordination. Using predefined hand gestures, as described in figure 3 -2, to assist patients in participation of goal - directed and repetitive activities important to rehabilitation. Figure 3-2:Various hand gestures used in task-oriented therapy for hand rehabilitation [52] • Real-Time Feedback: It gives timely feedback mainly in force and movement data that guarantees dynamic application of therapies depending on the patient’s progress.

heading: 3.1.1. Basic Techniques Used
content: • Sensor Integration: Flex sensors are included in the sensory glove to quantify the angles of bending the fingers and gripping strength. This data is important for correct emulation of movements on the motor glove. • Servo Motors for Movement Replication: The motor glove consists of servo motors keyed by the data from the sensory glove or a set of predefined gestures. These motors control the angle and force of the operated hand of the human body. • Machine Learning: It is used to assess rehabilitation and to control changes in motor speed through ML algorithms based on force sensor data. • IoT Connectivity: A mobile application serves as a control center for the identified therapy modes as well as a gesture mode selection panel and progress tracking platform. Here IoT helps the gloves to have proper communication with the app.

heading: 3.1.2. Viability of Design
content: The design is inspired by existing research and technologies: • Mirror Therapy Research: According to numerous investigations, the imitation of the movements of an unaffected limb can help stroke patients regain the function of the affected limb. Other mirror therapy devices are available in the market, but these generally do not include mirror-specific task-oriented activities. • Robotic Rehabilitation Systems: For movement therapy, equipment such as exoskeletons deploys motors, and as we have seen, the devices are large and costly. Our glove-based approach is more compact and thus cheaper. • Hand Gesture Recognition: Similar prior studies have shown the application of flex sensors for sign recognition, thus justifying the selection of the sensors in this project. By combining these elements, the proposed system provides a comprehensive and viable solution for hand rehabilitation tailored to individual patient needs.

Cost-Effectiveness In the proposed system, the cost of the sensors and the servo motors are also relatively low thus increasing the reach of the detection system. Indeed, this mobility would make it very useful in several rehabilitation contexts, something that cannot be said of many current systems that have been developed for use by certain classes of patients. f. Motor Control The system employs servo motors for controlling speed; it can be manual, automatic depending on the physical improvement of the patient. Proportions of the contemporary systems are less flexible or have some fixed or lesser motor speeds in most cases. g.
