heading: 4. Implementation
content: The proposed system will be a complex integration of the cloud -based communication, wearable devices and machine learning to help in real-time tracking and replication of hand gestures. It has two hardware components, the Sensory Glove and Motor Glove. The flex and force sensors of the Sensory Glove are introduced to detect the pressure value and movements of the fingers in a secure way that enables the user to capture the movements of his hand. Wireless transmission of this information with the help of Firebase Realtime Database has guaranteed low-latency, constant communication. To permit the interactive gesture imitation, data analysis with the Motor Glove will be performed, and that will utilize actuators or motors to sketch the prompts on the receiving end accordingly. The Sensor input is then interpreted, binary types of gestures are modeled, and the precision and reactiveness of the system are enhanced with a bespoke Machine Learning (ML) algorithm.  Also, a mobile application created on the Unity platform serves as a user interface and enables the system performance visualization, control, and monitoring in real time.  Such applications as teleoperation, remote rehabilitation, or human -computer interaction may use the proposed intelligent, responsive solution based on the easy integration of hardware and software items.

heading: 4.1. Development Stages
content: The following are the development stages of the project.

heading: 4.1.1. Sensory Glove
content: The sensory glove has the capacity to capture the hand movements and the pressure of hand of a user. It forms the transmitting part of the system that identifies real-time data and sends it to be processed and replicated.

heading: • 5 Flex Sensors:
content: The sensors placed by the Sensory Glove are located in such a way as to cover all length of a finger. They are mostly used to measure the degree of flexion or the bending of the fingers. The structure can register exact data concerning finger positions since the flex sensors resistances can change depending on how it is bent as the fingers itself moves its position.  This data is required to determine the shape of the hand gesture being made. The possibility of full-handed gesture detection is achieved due t o the individualization of each sensor, which is a separate finger: the thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. • ESP32 Microcontroller: ESP32 is the core processing and communication hardware, of the system. Having acquired the analog data of the flex sensor and force sensor, it uploads the readings into the Firebase Realtime Database wirelessly in the cloud.  It is ideal when it comes to the real -time communication application since it has Wi -Fi and Bluetooth. Moreover, ESP32 manages the process of sensor data intake and processes any code onboard the device and ensures that the data is appropriately delivered to other components, such as the Motor Glove or the mobile app.

heading: • Power Supply:
content: To enable Sensory Glove to stay in business without being affected, a reliable power source is a necessity. The voltage and current needed by the sensors and the ESP32 microprocessor are supplied by the power supply unit. Depending on design it could be a portable power bank or a charged battery. Since it is applicable to wearable or mobile apps where fluctuations in power may cause either loss of data or failure of the system, it ensures optimal performance stability during usage. Gesture cognizance, reproduction, and investigation depend on a powerful sensor system comprising of these components that are able to capture carefree hand development and interaction information a more realistic time.

heading: 4.1.2. Motor Glove
content: The motor glove acts as the response and output part of the system. It also emulates the motions identified by the sensory glove and records force information of the feedback force to be examined and monitored.

heading: • 5 Servo Motors:
content: The five fingers which are connected to each servo motor are the thumb, index, middle, ring and little finger. These motors control reproduction of the hand motions by carefully controlling the movement of the glove fingers.  The servo motors analyze the data and adjust their angles to recreate the same fingertips when the Sensory Glove transmits gesture data via the Firebase real-time Database. More complex movements of the hand can be simulated more correctly and more naturally since separate movements of fingers were possible due to the use of different servos. Thanks to that, the Motor Glove can be used in such applications as robotic teleoperation, physical therapy, and distant control of a hand.

heading: • 5 Force Sensors:
content: Such sensors are placed on the fingertips of the Motor Glove to measure the amount of pressure being exerted on the actuation.  The force sensors provide real -time measurements of contact pressure or resistance that is felt as the servo motors cause the fingers to perform specific gestures. This feedback loop ensures that the glove is capable of working safely, effectively and with ease since an adjustment of the grip strength ensures that there is no discomfort or harm. It is best useful in cases such as assistive robotics or a situation in which the user needs to deal with objects that are fragile, or their safety is of the first priority. • ESP32 Microcontroller: The motor glove ESP32 microcontroller acts as a principal controller of the glove, handling the data of the input of the force sensors and the control signal data that is to be sent to the servo motors. As it wirelessly receives gesture data (from Firebase Realtime Database) on which fingrie movements it should take and it therefore sees that it should be in a particular position, pulse-width modulation (PWM) signals will be transmitted to the servo motor s to move them into the appropriate positions. It also reads the data of the force sensors of the glove to monitor performance and make necessary adjustments to movement.  The Unity -based mobile application and Sensory Glove can also remain in real-time contact with the ESP32 due to the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities built-in it and ensuring flawless system functionality.

heading: • Power Supply:
content: The Motor Glove requires a constant and sufficient power supply to run its servo motors, as well as the ESP32 microprocessor. Servo motors especially need more current when operating especially when it is lifting or pressing against something.  The energy supply should be in a position to supply the correct voltage and current that will support clean and continuous movement. It may be any mobile source of power suitable in a wearable, e.g. a rechargeable lithium-polymer (Li-Po) battery pack. With a power system that is well designed, the glove will run efficiently without any unforeseen performance lapses or connection interruptions caused by power issues.

heading: 4.1.3. Machine Learning Algorithm (SVC Header File)
content: As part of the proposed system, the key and new addition is a lightweight embedded Support Vector Classification (SVC) algorithm that is a prerequisite  of gesture detection and classification. The given machine learning system will receive data of force sensors in Sensory Glove and will predict what type of hand gesture is performed by the user. The SVC methodology inherently developed was optimized to embedded environments, where most conventional machine learning algorithms have been known to run in comparatively high- end machines and require a significant amount of processing power.  Since it is well implemented in C + +, it is highly fast in processing speed and memory consumption. In order to ensure that hardware was being integrated well, all the algorithms were coded as a whole presented as a C++ header file, enabling the ESP32 microcontrollers to be installed on the Sensory and Motor Gloves, could be inserted and effective as of the present moment.  This embedded approach eliminates the need to constantly connect to cloud-based services or other servers to make any predictions by allowing on-device categorization. This, therefore, enhances responsiveness at real time, elevates data confidentiality and reduces latency significantly. The system is also more standalone, mobile and suitable in real -life, real -time systems such as assistive technologies, gesture-based interfaces, and tele-rehabilitation as the ESP32 can do this calculation locally. Additionally, the system is made easily portable and reusable by compiling the SVC model into a header file. It simplifies development and deployment because it can be updated or moved between devices without complicated dependencies. All things considered, the incorporation of this embedded SVC algorithm is a prime example of how machine learning and embedded systems may be combined to produce a wearable solution that is intelligent, responsive, and effective.

heading: Support Vector Machine
content: SVM is one of the most famous supervised machine learning methods used in regression and classification applications.  It performs specifically well when the feature dimension is compared with the number of samples, especially in high dimensions. The SVM works by the aid of the ideal hyperplane to separate the various classes of data points. The aim is to perform a maximization of the margin, which is the space between the hyperplane and the support vectors, or nearest data points of each category. The problem with this in practice is that under many conditions there will not exist a hyperplane that can perfectly separate all the data without any exception except that the points required to be separated are noisy or overlapping. It is due to this fact that SVM introduces slack variables that render the model more lenient so that some of the data points may not lie within the margin or may even be erroneous. This optimization process requires the C parameter of SVM.  The tradeoffs of having a large margin and a low training error are regulated by this regularization parameter. More specifically: • The classification errors in the training data is given more priority when C is greater. Although in this case the margin is smaller, the model will still attempt to fit the training data as accurate as possible.  However, this may lead to overfitting of the model which means that the model performs well with the data that is used to train it yet the model performs badly with previously unseen data. • Instead of training misclassification, the given model is able to tolerate more misclassifications in exchange of a larger margin in case C is lower.  This has potential to increase test data performance and to facilitate stronger generalization, especially when noise or LS is present in data. • In this way, C parameter tuning is important to obtain the proper balance between the model complexity and performance. For sensor based hand gesture recognition, the choice of C value would mean the Support V ector Machine is able to perform gesture classification well and at the same time be insensitive to sensor noise and to variation in input of users. In total, the C parameter serves as a penalty term over the slack variables of SVM optimization problem and this directly affects error stability and its ability to generalize unseen data in the model. Adequate tuning of this parameter also has a substantial possibility of increasing the accuracy and reliability of the gesture classification systems developed on the embedded platforms. heading: Random Forest
content: Random Forest is a powerful ensemble machine learning algorithm that is widely used for both classification and regression tasks due to its high accuracy, robustness, and ability to handle complex data patterns. It operates by constructing many individual decision tree during training, each of which is trained on a randomly selected subset of data. When a prediction is required, the model aggregates the outputs from all the decision trees —either by taking the majority vote (for classification) or the average prediction (for regression). Such ensemble leads to a decreased probability of overfitting and a higher generalization ability of the model. Thus, in terms of the offered system of hand gesture recognition, a Random Forest is used to hand gesture recognition based on the features input data provided by the glove including bending angles, force reading, and more. Among the main benefits of applying Random Forest to this study, there are the qualities of dealing with non -linear relationships and interactions between features; hence, it is optimal in describing the multi -dimensional data set created by wearable sensors.  Various statistical measures are normally used to assess the performance of the Random Forest model; and they include the Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 score. Accuracy shows the percentage of correct predictions of gestures to the total samples.  Choices of parameters in designing the Random Forest models including number of trees, maximum depth of the trees, and finally the number of features take into consideration at each split point are important in defining the performance of the model.  Within the training process, these parameters are tuned with extreme care to maximize the compromise between accuracy and computational performance. heading: Gradient Boost
content: Gradient Boosting is a powerful ensemble machine learning technique used for both classification and regression tasks. It works by combining the outputs of multiple weak learners, usually shallow decision trees, in a sequential manner to create a strong predictive model. Unlike methods that build trees independently, Gradient Boosting builds each new tree to correct the errors made by the previous ones. This way, each tree focuses on the residuals—the differences between the predicted and actual values— of the model trained before it. The algorithm optimizes a loss function using a process similar to gradient descent, where each new tree is added in such a way that it minimizes the overall prediction error of the ensemble. As more trees are added, the model becomes increasingly accurate . Gradient Boosting is known for its high performance, especially on complex and unstructured data, and is widely used in applications like gesture recognition, fraud detection, and recommendation systems. However, it must be carefully tuned to avoid overfitting, especially when working with small or noisy datasets. heading: 4.2.1. Firebase Realtime Database
content: Firebase Realtime Database serves as the central communication middleware in the proposed system, enabling seamless connectivity between the Sensory Glove, Motor Glove, and the mobile application. It acts as a cloud -based data bridge that supports real -time, bidirectional data exchange, ensuring that gesture information is transmitted instantly across all components of the system. When the Sensory Glove detects finger movements and pressure levels through its sensors, it sends this data to Firebase via the ESP32 microcontroller. Firebase then immediately makes this data available to the Motor Glove and the mobile application. The Mo tor Glove receives this information and interprets it to replicate the same gestures using its servo motors, allowing for synchronized and dynamic gesture imitation. This information is also visually presented in the monitoring, visualizing, or interacting with a mobile application developed on Unity. Low latency is one of the strongest points of Firebase; it is significant especially in the case of real- time systems, such as gesture replication.  The slightest of pauses can lead to synchronization issues or even eliminate organicity of interaction.  Additionally, Firebase is scalable, data synchronizes automatically and has great availability making it suitable in terms of wearable devices, which require high performance of the device at various network conditions and international sites. Moreover, Firebase simplifies system design that involves the elimination of the need to build complex server-side frameworks. It has a reliable scalable secure processing data that starts with sensor data collection, actuation, and the update of UI to make the system seamless throughout. Thanks to this fact, Firebase can be regarded as the most appropriate means of organizing cloud -based communications in wearable and interactive Internet of Things implementation.

This gives real-time response of the user hand movement as it allows the user to view the gesture category detected through the force sensors signals. It is especially useful where immediate feedback increases usability and effectiveness, e.g. with remote control of gestures, or in the rehabilitation of a hand.

content: The program contains graphical feedback, which demonstrates how the fingers move and by which finger they press so that the user can cope with program usage easily and intuitively. This visual interface allows users or doctors to get insight into how each finger reacts to any kind of gestures by presenting either real-time angles of finger bending and force amounts in a precedent form similar to that of a bar graph or a moving repres entation of the fingers.  This visual representation helps in system debugging, the assessment of patient care and overall user participation.

heading: • Predefined Controls:
content: Also, the app comes with pre -set control buttons to make standard gestures such as a closed fist, an open hand, or single finger motion.  In absence of wearing or using the Sensory Glove these buttons represent shortcuts to imitate specific hand positions. o When a button that has already been set is activated, the application sends, to the Firebase Realtime Database, a configured set of instructions of gesture, which are encoded as values of servo angles or control signals. o The Motor Glove, which constantly listens to Firebase updates, reads this data and performs the corresponding movement using its servo motors. The mobile application enhances system usability by allowing users to interact with the motor glove remotely and view live updates of gesture and force data, making it suitable for rehabilitation and teleoperation scenarios [64].

heading: 4.2.3. Data Flowchart
content: This flowchart illustrates the data flow and interaction between components of a smart hand rehabilitation system using sensory and motor gloves. The sensory glove captures finger bending through flex sensors and pressure through force sensors. Bending data is sent to the Firebase Realtime Database, while force data is processed by a Machine Learning algorithm to classify the type of force applied (force class). This classification is also stored in a Firebase. The motor glove receives bending data to repli cate hand movements using servo motors. A mobile application serves as a user interface, displaying real-time glove status, receiving force class data, a nd sending predefined function commands to the system. Firebase acts as the central hub, ensuring real -time data synchronization across all modules.

heading: 6. Conclusion
content: The project reveals how to use different smart technologies such as sensors, microcontrollers, wireless links and machine learning, to construct a smart rehabilitation system for hand patients. The project focused on providing a glove -based system that is affordable, real -time and easy to use for patients in rehabilitation after stroke, accident or surgery. The result was a flexible glove sensor system that measured both finger motion and the pressure generated by the user. A sensor’s data was collected and sent using an ESP32 microcontroller which acted as the data collection point and a connection to Wi -Fi. The movements of the patient’s active hand are recorded by the glove and used to guide the motors on the other glove. To relearn motor skills, as well as practice bilateral training, therapists often use this reflective strategy in physical therapy. A Machine Learning model was applied to review the sensor data, detect anything unusual and sort out several types of finger movements. As a result, the system can help with movement and also measure the improvement made during rehabilitation. Using IoT platforms, therapists or caregivers could see a patient’s activities in real time and review previous activity logs using the cloud dashboard. It’s particularly helpful for remote rehabilitation. Old-fashioned ways to build hand strength are usually the same, require close supervision all along and are boring for the individual doing them. Due to automatic steering, immediate response and flexible modifications, this technology handles these difficulties. The use of IoT and ML in the glove allows physiotherapists to closely supervise their patients’ exercises, record key outcomes and improve their patients’ rehabilitation overall. This glove system reproduces the newest concepts in helpful healthcar e and wearable devices, giving an adjustable, budget-friendly choice for use at home or in hospitals. It supports rehabilitation since it makes the needed movements simpler, leads patients to use their hands frequently and requires fewer visits to a therapist. For the most part, the prototype did as the specifications said, but there were a few issues. Repeated calibration of sensors improves the accuracy of the collected data. Their construction prevents servo motors from moving in the same flexible manner as a hand. The model currently works, but it does not have much variety because it was trained on a limited number of examples. When data is expanded, the model can be modified to cover more cases. Future improvements may involve: • Vibrations as feedback to encourage users. • Involve adaptive ML to observe and employ a user’s unique actions. • Developing a mobile application for easier interaction, controlling different actions and seeing the outcomes. This project proves that interdisciplinary engineering can greatly help solve problems in healthcare. By using both electronic, embedded and mechanical tools along with machine learning and IoT, the sensors in this rehabilitation glove help bridge the difference between common physiotherapy and recent technological advancements. Using the glove system provides a range of useful benefits. This glove can be afforded by most people worldwide, in contrast to commercial rehabilitation robots or exoskeletons that  are often costly. Users can benefit from therapy at any convenient place by taking the portable and wireless device home. Because of ML, the system may learn from a person’s progress, making rehabilitation programs more effective and appropriate over time. With IoT, the glove collects and exchanges real -time rehabilitation information which helps therapists follow patients’ progress, determine the best course of treatment and change strategies as necessary. Being an academic and engineering project, it allowed us to put our classroom lessons into practice. Students could apply sensor hardware, handle control system design, lea rn algorithms and experience network communication. It also focused on the difficulties of creating real-time systems, controlling noise in signals, using what’s available in hardware and keeping healthcare solutions focused on users. Besides, this effort may serve as an early effort for future, more involved rehabilitation systems. It forms a path for new roles of augmented reality ( AR) for virtual therapy sessions, AI to improve movement diagnosis and cloud -based access to collaboration and health record archives for therapists and clients.

heading: Abstract
content: Skin diseases are most common diseases all over the world and they spread more in populated countries. Skin diseases also affect the patient’s confidence. So, the early detection and prevention of skin diseases are very important. Skin diseases detection needs a high level of expertise. An android based system is proposed in this project for efficient skin detection. Derma diagnose is an android based application which takes an image from the user and detects  the image if it is one of the five diseases which are Psoriasis, Scabies, Fungal Infection, urticarial and Eczema. On the click of a button, the user can diagnose his skin disease using the system. An interface will be provided to the user by which he can capture the image of the infected skin and fill the provided questionnaire related to the skin diseases. The application will send the image to the server where all the pre -processing, segmentation, feature extraction and classification will be done and t he result will be sent to the user. The user can also get information about the diseases, get home remedies for the five diseases or search for a doctor (dermatologist). The system will only work for android based devices.

content: Human skin being the largest organ of the human body protects the body against many viruses, bacteria, allergies, fungal infections and controls human body temperature. Around the world, skin diseases skin is among the most extensively known medical issue [2]. Due to its complexity, dermatology is the tough territory and hard to identify. heading: 1.2 Objectives
content:  To support and assist users that suffer from skin diseases and do not have fast access to a relevant skin specialist.  To provide users with knowledge regarding their skin disease.  To find a doctor (skin specialist) near the user.  To search for home remedies for the five diseases.  To help people feel more confident in their lives.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: Skin diseases are an issue in populated countries and places with poor hygienic conditions. People with skin diseases feel depressed and embarrassed which results in a lack of confidence in them. In Pakistan, over 3% of the total population is affected by psoriasis. To make people aware of skin diseases and how to prevent them is very important. There are many remote areas in Pakistan where people do n’t have access to skin specialists. The proposed system will help the patients in diagnosing their skin disease according to five diseases: Psoriasis, Scabies, Fungal Infection, Urticarial, and Eczema. The system will also help them getting information about these diseases and how to treat them with home remedies.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions & constraints
content: The main limitation in the system is that it will be an android based application and it will diagnose the images better which will be taken from a particular distance from the skin and in enough light. The system interface will only be in the English language and no other language will be used. The system will diagnose the five listed skin diseases which are most common in Pakistan. The system will only deal with Psoria sis, Scabies, Fungal Infection, Urticaria and Eczema. The main functi onality is to provide the patient with a correct diagnosis from among these five diseases.

heading: 1.5 Project scope
content: The proposed android based system will be able to deal with five types of diseases  i-e: Psoriasis, Scabies, Fungal Infection, Urticarial, and Eczema. The user can capture an image from the application where the skin is infected, and then the system will diagnose the image if it is any of the above five mentioned diseases and will show the result to the user. The system will also inquire a list of questions from the user to get more information about the type of disease. Gender of the user will not be considered by the application; it will detect diseases on general skin of the patient. T he system will work for android based devices. It will also provide an option of checking information about the five diseases to the user. Training in using the system or providing ongoing user support is unlikely to be covered by the project. Showing noti fication of the application to the user is also not covered by the project.

heading: 2.1 Literature review
content: The topic under consideration for the literature review is the applications/systems research performed under this category. The application being made is an expert system that assists users in diagnosing Skin Diseases. This expert system is basically designed for the detection of five skin diseases which are Psoriasis, Scabies, Fungal Infection (Tinea corporis, Tinea pedis), Urticaria, and Eczema. The android application interacts directly with the users that have know-how of Smartphones. These are the list of similar systems that are related to this project:

heading: 2.1.1 A.I. Diagnose skin
content: It is an android application which asks the user to select the body part to diagnose (Scalp, lip, eye, tonsil, neck, mole, nail or skin). After selecting the body part, it asks to take a picture of the area you want to diagnose. After the picture is taken it diagnosis the picture and shows its opinion if the skin is norma l or infected. It shows some names of skin diseases each one has an option to look up online for them. According to the reviews of this application, its accuracy level is low.

heading: 2.1.2 DermoMap
content: It is an iOS-based application which has the ability to photograph a lesion to compare with pre-existing photos in the app database. Each disease entry contains one or multiple photographs along with a brief explanation, encompassing an overall description, common symptoms, the diagnosis, and treatment of the disease. This application only works on the iPhone and iPad 2. It is difficult to navigate the diagnosis section. A few low memory issues cause the application to occasionally crash.

heading: 2.1.3 All Skin Diseases and Treatment – A to Z
content: It is an android based application in which many types of skin diseases details are discussed. The causes of skin diseases, what the disease is, their pictures, if they are hereditary or not, what it looks like, how to diagnose it, can it be cured and its treatments (by medical prescriptions and gels, creams and lotions) and their side effects are also discussed. This application doesn’t provide any assistance to detect skin diseases by analyzing the image.

heading: 2.1.4 Skin MD Now – Expert Skin Help
content: It is an android based application which functions in three steps. At first, it asks the user to share a photo and describe his/her skin problem by asking some basic skin related questions. Then it asks the user to select a provider (doctor). In the end, it asks the user to submit his request and payment to receive a diagnosis, treatment plan , and prescription. This application doesn’t provide any assistance to detect skin diseases by analyzing the image.

heading: 2.1.5 SkinApp
content: It is an android based application which functions in three steps. The first step is locations in which the application asks the user to select the location of the infected area and if it is localized or generalized, asymmetrical or symmetrical. The second step is signs and symptoms in which it asks the user to select from the mentioned signs and symptoms of skin diseases. After selecting signs and symptoms, the last step is diagnosed in which many skin diseases are mentioned? The application asks the user to select from the mentioned skin diseases. After selecting any disease, the application shows details of the particular disease, its treatment, its images and how to diagnose it. This application needs many manual inputs.

heading: 2.1.6 Expert System for Diagnosis of Skin Diseases
content: This paper presents an approach combining all of the previous methodologies used previously to perform skin disease detection. This paper suggests combining the approach of image processing, data mining and Q/A to detect diseases like Eczema Impetigo and Melanoma. The paper presents three approaches to perform skin disease detection and their accuracy in terms of results and then leads on to compare them to the fourth one presented by this paper. The results presented seem to have a ratio of 85% to 65% of accurate results. The approach is very optimizing and efficient but requires a lot of complex working as well.

heading: 2.1.7 A survey of skin-color modelling and detection methods
content: The paper [16] claims that using skin color as the main feature to perform detection has both its pros and cons. The whole research paper is divided into three parts. It starts by explaining the different color spaces used when doing skin detection using color. After this, it moves on to the techniques that can be used for classification. Later on, it concludes by discussing the techniques that specifically use the color constancy and perfo rm well regardless of the constantly changing lighting, temperature , and other environmental factors. The paper also indicates the conditions in which this approach works best.

heading: 2.1.8 Design and Rules Development of Online Children Skin Disease Diagnosis System
content: This paper [17] indicates that skin diseases are mostly unrecognizable because of the similarity of symptoms. To solve this particular issue, the paper presented the Rule-Based Approach to solve this issue where every disease will have its own unique characteristics and questions to identify the correct disease. The paper aims at creating an expert system for children which will assist parents or people with medical know how to detect skin disease and also suggest a suitable treatment for their disease.

heading: 2.1.9 Mobile-based Medical Assistance for Diagnosing Different Types of Skin Diseases Using
content: Case-based Reasoning with Image Processing This paper  [18] indicates the cons of using a rule-based approach when doing skin detec tion and suggests using Cased Based Reasoning (CBR). The paper indicates using CBR and image processing to avoid the problem of contradiction and redundancy that was faced in Rule Base.

heading: 2.1.10 Remote Skin Disease Diagnosis System Using Machine Learning Techniques
content: This paper [19] aims to develop a skin dise ase diagnosing application working on a mobile interface using SVM Classifier and Bag of Features Model for diagnosis. The system was initially designed for one user only which means multiple people cannot access it time and cause the system to slow down.

heading: 3.2 Activity diagram
content: The system activity diagram shows the main activities of your application defining the interaction between them. The application starts by opening the main page with option of take photo, select image, search home remedies and find a doctor. The user starts by taking a photo or selecting from gallery. The affected area will be cropped; the cropped image is then uploaded to a server side via PHP Bridge. An interface will appear with multiple questions to be answered in a yes/no format, then using image processing techniques the image is sharpened after which feature extraction techniques GLCM and LBP are calculated. The classifier is trained with the features and a result is generated in the end based on the Q/A answered and classification.

content: This chapter contains experimental setup (Dataset used for experiments, evaluation met hodology and features that are applied on dataset), evaluation measure used to evaluate the performance of methodology. Results and analysis of applied approaches are also discussed in this chapter.

heading: 5.1 Experimental Setup
content: This section discusses about the dataset and the evaluation criteria used to analyze the accuracy behind the code.

heading: 5.1.1.1 Purpose of Dataset
content: The most important aspect for the analysis of our system is the availability of Dataset. It is the main component used for developing the Derma Diagnoser application. There is no benchmark dataset available which can be used to detect diseases with high accuracy. Thus, the main focus of our FYP work is to develop Dataset for detecting diseases with high accuracy.

heading: 5.1.1.2 Data Collection Methodology
content: We have collected data from hospitals and internet sites which are as follows:  https://www.dermnetnz.org/image-library/  https://medicine.uiowa.edu/dermatology/education/clinical-skin-disease-images.

heading: 5.1.1.3 Data Collection Challenges
content: The following are some of the challenges we have faced during data collection.  The dataset that was present on internet was mostly edited. We need such type of data that is not edited.  Collection process quite time consuming.  The Dataset that was shared with us was of very bad quality for example focus of image was not good.  Some research labs were not willing to share their dataset with us.

heading: 6   Conclusion
content: In this application, the user can diagnose skin diseases at an early stage before it gets more critical. The techniques used for diagnosing were a combination of image processing and rule -based methodology. For checking the accuracy level of our system, we used classifiers. The application also deals with the newly discovered skin diseases which will be stored in the system’s database. This information can be further used for testing and research purposes by dermatologists and researchers. The reason why users choose this application is that it uses both image processing and questionnaire results combine them into a more reliable result of a certain disease. In the end, the application generates the diagnostic report and provides the user with the option of searching home remedies. It also provides the option to finding a doctor for consultation.

heading: 6.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: Among the various problems we faced, the major ones were deciding the techniques and methodologies to use for image pre -processing, image feature extraction and image classification. Another problem faced was meeting deadlines and finalizing the design and data flow of our information. The lessons learned from these issues were to start making a design from the beginning as the requirements are 80% finalized and divide the project in equal chunks and make deadlines so that it’s easier to integrate the work towards the end.

heading: 6.2 Project summary
content: The largest organ of a human body is Skin. Skin diseases are infections of skin that people from all age groups, regions and ethnicity suffer from. Skin diseases vary from a simple Skin Rash to Skin Cancer. Skin is the largest boundary against external infections and germs hence, Skin Care is very important. Skin diseases are one of those problems that  are very common yet are not treated with the same determination as other types of diseases. The aim behind this project is to develop an expert system that assists users in diagnosing Skin Diseases. This expert system is basically designed for the detection of five skin diseases which are Psoriasis, Scabies, Fungal Infection (Tinea corporis, Tinea Pedi’s), Urticarial, and Eczema. The android application interacts directly with the users that have know-how of Smartphones.

heading: 6.3 Future work
content: Data mining, digit al image processing , and rule-based methodology together can be used for the detection of skin diseases. The system can be integrated as a web -based application in which more modules can be added for the users. This system can be further transformed into an iOS application as well.

heading: Abstract
content: In Natural Language Processing  (NLP), the Semantic similarity is one of the core fields that are  used to measure the level of similarity between two linguistic items (words). Semantic similarity between words has important usage in natural language processing, Information retrieval and Artificial intelligence. There are two commonly used approaches in measuring similarity one is by using thesaurus i.e. WordNet and secondly is by using corpus-based approaches. The project purposes a corpus-based approach using knowledge- based techniques. For this purpose, a corpus is created and the knowledge represent ation technique is to be applied to find the similarity score on the scale of 0 -4. There are many systems for semantic similarity in the English language you just enter the two words and their similarity score is shown. Similarly, we have developed a system for an under resourced language i.e. Urdu. Our system uses various text similarity techniques to find the similarity between two given words. For test purpose we have used a dataset containing thousand words annotated by the linguistic experts.

heading: 1.1  Semantic Word Similarity
content: Semantic similarity is the relatedness between two linguistic words on the basis of their meanings. It is used for measuring the level to which linguistic words are similar i.e. there is a fair amount of similarity between the words 'Apple' and 'Peach' as they belong to the same category of food i.e. 'fruits' however these words are not s imilar but the similarity between their meanings makes them fairly similar while the similarity between the words 'Apple' and 'Potato' is very less because they didn't belong to the same direct hypernym though there is a small similarity between these two words which is they belong to the similarity network of the word food. Words representation is increasingly popular in the field of Natural Language Processing for example  dependency parsing (Bansal et al., 2014), named entity recognition (Miller et al., 2004) and parsing (Socher et al., 2013).

heading: 1.2 Types of Semantic Evaluation Techniques
content: A lot of text similarity tools and techniques are used to find the relatedness between two words in a numerical form. Computationally, semantic similarity can be estimated by:  A [directed acyclic graph] (e.g., a taxonomy) in which the concepts are mapped in the form of a tree like structure or in a graphical form showing the relation between each node in the graph.  Statistically to correlate words vector space model are used  A lot of available tools are used to measure semantic word similarity such as [WNetSS API], which is a Java based API having a wide range of semantic similarity measurements based on the [WordNet] semantic resources.

heading: 1.4 Applications of Semantic Word Similarity
content: Semantic Similarity is the basic concept which is very important in many fields such as natural language processing, artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and psychology, from the perspective of both academic as well as industrial point of  view. An accurate measure of word similarity is important for many useful tasks such as information retrieval, document clustering, and synonym extraction, etc. The similarity between two words/objects is the most common way for the humans to compare two words/objects. Obtaining semantic relation/ similarity between  two or more words/concepts is required in many applications of psycho-linguistics and natural language processing.

heading: 2.2 Techniques for measuring semantic word similarity
content: Previously there were many approaches that were suggested to find similarity between words. E.g.  Distance-oriented measures computed on semantic networks.  Metrics based on models of distributional similarity learned from large text collections. To find semantic word similarity three main techniques are used i.e.  Dictionary or thesaurus-based approach  Corpus-based approach  And Machine learning approach.

heading: 2.2.1 Corpus-Based Approach
content: In the corpus based approach we use the knowledge provided by a large corpora to find similarity. The two main corpus -based approach used are pointwise mutual information (Turney 2001), and (2) latent semantic analysis (Landauer, Foltz, & Laham 1998). Pointwise Mutual Information: It was given by (Turney 2001) in the form of unsupervised learning method for evaluating semantic word similarity. It is based on the word which co- occurs using numbers/counts collected over a very large corpora. Latent Semantic Analysis(LSA): It was introduced by Landauer (1998). In LSA, term co- occurrences in a corpus are captured by means of a dimensionality reduction operated by a singular value decomposition (SVD) on the term-by-document matrix T representing the corpus. For the experiments reported here, we run the  SVD operation on the  British National Corpus.

heading: 2.2.2 Dictionary-Based Approach
content: Semantically related words of a specific word are listed in a manually created lexical ontology with an IS-A relationship. The most common example of this kind of network is WordNet. A synset consists of the synonyms of a specific word. Though the similarity of the words changes across the different domains. In Lin’s similarity measures modifications consists of the information content of the concept that is to be compared while assuming their independence. heading: Abstract
content: Human beings have been gifted with five recognized senses including sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch. Each sense plays its vital role in human’s life. The deficiency of human sense (sight) to see around is known as visual-impaired, and the people who are not able to see around because of their vision deficiencies are generally visually impaired. Blind people face several problems in their life. One of these problems that is the most important is to identify the things in their daily life. Technology i s playing major role in every field of the world and it can be helpful to such problems. This project is designed for visually impaired  people. The purpose of this project is to facilitate these people so that they can get information about things around t hem. In this project, we want to explore the possibility of using the hearing sense to understand visual objects. We will design an android a pplication that will recognize the objects or things in smartphone’s camera and against each recognized object, a s ound is spoken. Voice will be in simple English language so that more and more people can be facilitated. Now this is the age of technology so, this project will assist people with some innovations. Some researches have been done i n this field, however, very few systems have been develope d. This application will provide more convenience and less effort in identifying objects, colour, text, currency, and distance at which object is placed from camera.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Sight or vision is the capability of eyes to see the objects around. Human beings have been gifted with five senses including sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch. Each sense plays its vital role. People who are not able to accurately see things placed around are generally kno wn as visually impaired. Visual impaired-ness is the deficiency to see the objects around. People who are blind from degradation or damage to the visual cortex, but still have functional eyes, are capable of some level of vision known as blind sight. Eyes play a vital role in daily life. We all have seen visually impaired people and know about some of the problems that they may face in their life. Identifying the things placed around is most important problem for visually impaired people. In order to identi fy the thing that can block (or create difficulty into) their way when they walk, they use stick but stick can help them to hint them about objects on the ground. Technology is playing major role in every field of this universe and it can be helpful to suc h problems. The advancement of technology has not given much benefit to this field as it should be given. Smartphones are the essential part of our lives regardless of the field we are working. It has huge impact on all fields. The conversion curve from fe ature phones to smart phones is very high as some brands are providing smartphones under low budget, so that most of the people can get benefit of it. This is the age of technology, so mobile applications can be solution to such problems. Some applications  who facilitate these disabled people to recognize things around them are not much efficient. In this project, visual world has been  transformed into audio wor ld with the potential to inform visually impaired people about the information of objects. In this project, we are planning to provide the visually impaired not only with the facility to identify the things around them but also to identify the colo urs, distance between object and smartphone’s camera, currency value and to read the handout or document.  In this way, these people will not feel much inferiority complex and they will be more confident to go anywhere unfamiliar to them. To transform the visual sense into speaking sense, a mobile application is designed in such a way that it uses Smartphone’s camera to recognizes object in camera , and against each recognized object a voice is

content: produced which contains the information about  that object in simple English language s o that more and more people can be facilitated. The proposed mobile application has been developed for android operating system because most of the smartphone manufacturing brands support this operating system, so most of the smartphones users can be facilitated. Back -end development has been  done in Java programming languages wh ereas Front-end development has been done in XML. The techniques that has been  applied in this project are based on Machine Learning, and Computer Vision technologies. Some features of the proposed project are similar to another project named “Visionary Vision f or Blinds” but not all. Similar features include object recognition, colo ur recognition and text reader whereas the proposed project “EyeSight” includes some more features that make this application unique are • Identify the distance between smartphone’s camera and object • Identify the value of currency (amount) The proposed project named “Visionary Vision for Blinds” integrates hardware including camera, headphone, microphone and Raspberry Pi. Camera captures the image then image is sent to Google Cloud Vision API through raspberry pi for image processing. This proposed project can only be used when user has access to the internet. The integration of the hardware can be difficult for blinds so the difference that makes the proposed project named “EyeSight”  unique is using smartphone’s integrated camera to focus objects, colours, currency and text using autofocus feature for efficient output. Mobile application named “EyeSight” can be easily accessible to the user by using smartphone’s voiceover. Focused ob ject, colour, currency or text in camera is sent to Google Cloud Vision API and some Third -party APIs for processing and recognizing online. The recognized object, colo ur, and currency is stored in database for offline usage. This mobile application facili tates the Blinds or visually impaired people to use offline. This mobile application also facilitates them to identify the distance between smartphone’s camera and object. Usually everyone use smartphone in his/her hand so it can inform the user about the distance between object and him/her. In this way, these people will not feel much inferiority complex and they will be more confident to go anywhere unfamiliar to them.

heading: 2.1 Literature Review
content: Much work has been done in this field as many renowned organizations have already been working extensively in the field of machine learning and computer vision. Much work has already been posted on the internet and published to provide us with all the necessary information required in this field.  A prototype system was proposed to find objects for blind assistance by the camera -based network and matching -based recognition. A dataset of daily needs is collected and feature descriptors SURF (Speeded -Up Robust Features) and SIFT (Scale Invariant Feature Transform) are applied to recognize objects in this prototype. [1]  An organization named “CloudSight” implemented a mobile application called “TapTapSee”. This application uses mobi le camera to capture objects and mobile voiceover to speak the information of objects loudly. This application allows the user to double tap the photograph then it analyse, recognize objects, and speak it aloud in required time. [2]  A company named “BlindSight” offered a mobile application called “Text Detective”. This application uses mobile camera to capture the document or handout and recognizes the text in it using Optical Character Recognition technology then uses mobi le voiceover to speak recognized text aloud. [3]  Statistical methods were developed by  [4], which allow effective visual identification and tracking of objects. These methods learn hierarchical models of objects, understands the parts that compose them and scenes that surround them.  A well-known social network “Facebook” introduced tool called “Automatic Alternative Text” for the blinds. It automatically generates the captions for p hotos in News Feed of blinds and fit together tightly with text to speech engines. [5]  Chinese company “Baidu” introduced a device called “DuLight”. It contains a tiny camera that captures the object and sends its photographs to an app installed on smartphone. App analyses the

heading: 16 of 64  05 January 2018
content: photograph and recognizes what object photographs depicts and a voice is produced which contains object information that can be heard by connected wired-headphones. [6]  An electronic device called “Eyeborg” was developed by  [7]. This device turns the visual colour information into sound frequencies. Sound frequencies can be heard as musical notes.  The vOICe vision technology attempted to provide blind -assistance to blinds via visual to sound sense conversion. The system scans snapshots from left to right while associating height with pitch and brightness with loudness. [8]  A system was introduced by [9], which facilitates the discovery of point of interests in unfamiliar indoor environments using spatial audio.  Aipoly Inc. developed a mobile application called “Aipoly”. This application uses mobile camera to capture objects around and recognizes objects through deep learning. Mobile voiceover is used to produce a sound against each object. [10]  A system was suggested to detect obstacles, in which two cameras placed on blind person’s glasses that take images from diffe rent sides. Obstacles could be found by comparing these images. In this method, the probability of existence of an object is investigated by use of special points then binary method, standardize and normalized cross-correlation are utilized to verify that probability. [11]  KONGU Engineering College, India implemented a project called “RFID Based Object Identification for Blind People” by using radio frequency identification technology to identify objects. In this project, RFID reader module tracks an object and microcontroller processes signals received from RFID reader module to provide assistance to the blind.

heading: Abstract
content: The aim of this project is to help people manage their stress with the help of a smartphone which is owned by almost everyone. Stress, anger and anxiety can be managed. Distance, distraction, delay, and distort. In a stressful situation, our application will encourage the user to distance themselves from what is causing the stress. This could mean going to a different room or leaving the building. Followed by distraction. We have countless things to distract us with, but most of them waste significant amount of our time. The application will make sure not to waste precious time. Then comes delay. And distort, changing the thought, and will be achieved with the help of mini game, some physical activity monitor, and other features. The application will also work proactively, to make sure the user doesn’t encounter more stressful situation in the future by enabling them to organize their tasks.

heading: 1 Introduction
content: Stress is a feeling of pressure on the human mind. A type of psychological pain. Stress can be divided into two types. Good and bad stress. Good stress is beneficial for yo u, encouraging you push forward and get things done. However, bad stress caused by excessive amounts of stress is harmful for your body. It can cause headaches, anger, fatigue, lack of interest, and change in appetite. And can increases the risk of heart a ttacks, and mental illnesses such as depression and panic attacks. Stress is related to anxiety, and is the dripping of adrenalin into our body. Adrenalin is a chemical released by the brain into a person’s body when that person faces a fight or flight si tuation, Adrenalin is released into our body in order to survive. In the past this helped our ancestors protect themselves from predators. But today, this causes stress. Stress is something which everyone faces. And unfortunately, most people do not know how to manage it in a healthy way. Some common, but unhealthy ways people cope with stress are nail biting, pulling their own hair. Turning towards alcohol as a coping mechanism. Developing a habit to smoke cigarettes and or other drugs. “Eating the stress  away” meaning excessive eating, another habit people develop to cope with stress which can lead to being overweight and even diabetes. And excessive sleeping. Stress, anger and anxiety can be managed in a healthy way. A quick way to reduce stress is by first distancing yourself, this can mean moving to a different location such as going to another room. Distracting yourself, changing your thoughts to something else. Distorting the thoughts, so that the previous stressful thoughts do not come back, and if they do, they are not that stressful on your mind. And delaying, trying to delay the stressful thoughts. These techniques help people reduce their stress. Another great and popular way to reduce stress is by catharsis. Sharing your problem. This gives peopl e the ability to vent out their frustrations and anger. And possibly get great solutions to their problems. And lastly, the most effective way to avoid extensive and unhealthy stress is by being proactive. Having a ‘to do’ list. Completing different tasks on time.

heading: 1.1.1 Video Games
content: Videogames have been shown to reduce stress and anxiety , and increase our problem solving skills along with awareness levels , however one major drawback of video games is that it has become an activity which people use to escape reality. Which causes people to waste their precious time which they could have used to be more productive. If we play videogames in a controlled way, not wasting a lot of time on them, we can effectively use them to reduce our stress.

heading: 1.1.2 Physical Activity Monitor
content: Being physically active has also been shown to reduce stress. Joining the gym is recommended for everyone who suffer from stress, anxiety and even depression. Exercise & other physical activities produce endorphins, chemicals in the brain that act as  natural painkillers and also improve the ability to sleep, which in turn reduces stress. [1] A simple exercise such as walking every day is considered to be one of the best exercise a person can do.

heading: 1.1.3 Relaxing Audio and Visual Cues
content: Music, movies and TV shows are also a great way to distract oneself from stress. And help people relax. However, movies and TV shows requires an individual to invest time in them. What people should do instead is watch a funny clip or two and spend less than 5 minutes on them. Or listen to some relaxing sounds that are widely available on the internet, which include things like birds singing, water walls etc. This will help distract the person under stress.

heading: 1.1.4 Being Proactive
content: Having a disorganized life, falling behind on schedule ar e some of the reasons people deal with stress. Especially in modern age when our smartphones have become a major distraction for us, as we waste our time on it browsing social media and watching countless videos. And not completing any tasks that need to be completed on time. All of this has become of stress too. If a person is proactive, and completes their tasks in a given time, then they face less stress over all. As they don’t have to worry about approaching deadlines. For this a person needs to carry and maintain a to-do notebook. Where they will note down all the tasks they need to complete over a given time. And check off the tasks that a person has completed . This helps the user to stay focused and stress free.

heading: 1.1.5 Catharsis Forum
content: Sharing problems with others, problems that one doesn’t know a solution to, can be a great way to reduce stress. It allows people to open up. And get feedback on how they can improve their situation. We have implemented a forum inside our application. The user must first signup , using some allies as their name. Then the user will be able to use the forum and share their problem anonymously with others. And other users would be able to help the user by giving su ggestion to possible solutions. The user can also go through the foru m, read other people’s problems and offer solutions to them.

heading: 1.1.6 Find Help
content: “Women seek help – men die” (Angst & Ernst, 1990). It is possible someone is experiencing extreme levels of stress, anxiety and depression. And in that case, self -help material isn’t enough for someone to reduce their stress. In that case a person should seek for professional help. They should look for therapist or psychologists.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The objectives of our project are to help users in reducing their stress with the help of some activities built into the application. These activities will distract the user, but will also make sure not to waste user’s precious time. Give them a platform to vent out their frustrations. So that users may share their problems with others, anonymously. And get solutions to their problems. Provide a feature that will make the users more proactive in their lives, so that they may avoid stressful situations in the future. And the ability to predict when the user will be under stress again in the future by  monitoring their past usage of the application.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: Stress is something that everyone faces. It is the cause of a lot of diseases and illnesses. Most people do not know how to cope with stress in a healthy way. A lot of the coping mechanism that people may find online or in some psychology book are difficul t to adapt to for most people in their lives, as they require time and effort. We have designed an application that will help people manage their stress easily. That people can integrate into their lives without wasting a lot of time and putting in a lot of effort.

heading: 2.5 Use case descriptions
content: Under stress, the user launches the application and presses on “I’m Stressed” button. He/she is then taken a page where he/she can choose from  either a mini game or  be asked to perform a physical activity. In case of the mini game, the user has to fly across the sky, avoiding obstacles that include a flying skull and a spaceship, and reach a set destination . If the user is taken to a physical activity, the software asks the user to take to walk for some time. When the time limit is reached, the application notifies the user and ends the activity . This encourages the user to walk and exercise. The user can press on Proactive notebook. Here the user can add new tasks they need to complete. Such as buy groceries, paying bills, washing the dishes etc. They can a lso assign a deadline to each task and be reminded of them when the deadline is near. And when the task has been completed, they can press the check mark, giving them a sense of relief and encouraging them to continue to complete the remaining tasks. For example, a user needs to change the car oil. They can set the deadline for Saturday. On Saturday, the application will notify the user to change their car oil. After completing the task, the user can open the app and press on the check mark, signalling the task has been completed. Catharsis forums has been implemented. Here a user can share their problems with the rest of the community. Weather they are going through some difficult times such as loss of a loved one, or some financial loss, or study/work rela ted stress. They can share their problems here. They identity will be completely anonymized. So that they may feel safe and secure while sharing their problem. And get feedback from the community. Some users can be going to extreme amounts of stress, where  our software isn’t enough to help them. In that case, users can press the button “ Find a Therapist ”, which will pull up all the available therapist nearby.

heading: 6.1.1 Game Development in Android Studio
content: Android studio is fairly limited when it comes to designing games, as compared to tools like Unity and Unreal Engine. And integrating a unity game inside an android application is a hit or a miss. With countless tries to get the game to integrate.

heading: 6.1.2 Step Counter Inaccuracy
content: While testing physical activity tracker, it was observed that the step counter wasn’t accurate. It would count steps even when the user just placed their phone into their pocket. And would sometimes ‘miss’ steps, or count more than one step at a time. So, if the target assigned to the user was 100 steps, the user would have reached that goal early even th ough they would have taken around 70-80 steps. To combat this issue, a timer was implemented. ‘Walk for 30 minutes’, and at the same time the step counter was running just to know if the user was walking or not. In other words a hybrid solution was taken t o overcome the short comings of step counter inaccuracy.

heading: 6.1.3 Mini Game Too Easy
content: The mini game originally implemented in the project was too easy. All they had to do with either move the block left or right to avoid the obstacles. And the gap between two obstac les was around the same area, allowing the user to not move as much. The original target of the game was to make it accessible to majority, but while trying to make it so gave us a game that was too easy to play and not distracting and rewarding enough to  the user once they had completed the game’s assigned target. To fix the problem, a new game was designed. One which was more attractive and challenging, but with an easy learning curve so that anyone can pick up and understand how to play the game.

A catharsis forum, where the user can share their stressful thoughts with the community and get feedback on how to deal with their problems. Find a therapist, if a user feels extreme amount  of stress and need to seek professional help. These combination of models would work collectively and help the user to manage their stress

heading: 5.1 Problem Faced and Lessons Learned
content: Our Project was about Research and Development on Hadoop Big Data Framework.  One of the major challenge we faced during the learning of Hadoop was, cluster setup for the first time and verification of its configuration .We have learnt the architecture paradigm of Hadoop and its cluster setup from scratch. Another problem for us was, to purchase the nodes from the Linode to test and develop the our cluster creation code on it. Mr. Asif Shahzad shared his Linode account for the purchasing and testing our code on the Linode machines.

heading: 5.2 Project Summary
content: Hynod is aimed to provide Hadoop based cluster in low cost compared to the existing solution in the market. Hynod will be a cloud base application whose services and offers will be available on user demand just one click away on the internet. Hynod will purchase the nodes from third party cloud based Linux server providers  i.e. Linode  and setup the nodes according to Hadoop requirements using Apache Ambari. Hynod will allow the users to create instances of Single core, multi core, SSD, simple hard disk instances according to their needs. Furthermore, Hynod shall provide fully managed Apache Hadoop [1] cluster on a very affordable pricing range. Hynod clusters on the cloud will be highly scalable, secure, and provides service monitor on one page, Hadoop Job execution and its monitoring on the next page.

heading: 5.3 Future Work
content: This is E ra of Big data where we will work on our system to provide support other big data frameworks like Spark, Flink, Storm, and Samzawith one click cluster creation. Future work will also include following:  System will provide support for  other  big data frameworks as well like Spark, Flink, Samza and Strom.  Make Login more secure through mobile verification code.  Migration of system resources on fly.  Email notification after the completion of submitted job. In future Hynod will help the users work on multiple core clusters without buying the hardware, Job Manager only would need to create instance and all the services will be provided on their system via Hynod web app. If some users want to use Hynod services on their local infrastructure Hynod will facilitate such users as well in future.

content: There has been a growing need of homebased services in Pakistan and other regions as well which  is attributed to several contributing factors which include, local demand, market influence, having second homes, income/rental units and commercial property maintenance and people’s lives becoming busier and more wild with additional people now seeing fo r help with odd -jobs around their home, like exchanging Electronics things, or setting up shelves. But, instant contact of such services has confirmed to be a difficult task specially when one is travelling or settling in a new area. We know that the service providers are found across diverse areas and vary in costs, quality and variety of service that they deliver. Due to that diversity in work so we trying to resolve this problem to make people life easy and satisfying. The aim of this project is to provide any kind of repairing services in just one platform. If user need any kind of indoor or outdoor services they can avail it by using this application. Indoor services like calling Electrician, plumber, carpenter etc. and outdoor services includes any veh icle mechanics. This a pplication basically provide easiness for those who wants to avail indoor or outdoor services by just one click. The whole system will have a user friendly Graphical user interface which can be operated even by users who are interacting with it for the first time. In web application we will make admin and user panel in admin panel admin can view, update, delete, save all information from database and in user panel people can see services and this web application also helps us to promote our android application. This application will also promote application development in Pakistan.

heading: 1.1  Introduction:
content: In Pakistan for local job, the selection of manual workers has always been a thought-provoking task. For instance, the search for an electrician or plumber means first visit a market or hardware store then after negotiation , take labour with you and after the completion of the work drop him to the st ore. Searching for a person is a major problem, we overcome this problem by making an Android Application that fulfil the user queries in an efficient manner, because people enjoy to use smart phones and smart apps that resolve their issues. As scope of the android application is concerned, statistics indicate that the trend of surfing internet on smart devices has seen a steep increase during the past few years. This trend is likely to continue due to drop in cost and availability of smart devices. Pakista n, being a developing country has huge potential in the field of mobile software industry and rise in smartphone usage is most likely to be a perpetual entity. These types of applications can increase empl oyment opportunities for handyman sector, which is far left behind from the society, where technological advancements are progressing day by day, and people tend to depend more on technology to meet their requirement than ever. The purpose of this project is to provide indoor or outdoor services in Pakistan to the next level of ease. In this project, we are developing web as well as android application. Graphical User Interface (GUI) of both applications is user friendly. Customer can use these services by using our “Repair It” android application. We are developing Customer and Repairman applications separately. When someone is register as a customer, he  will select what kind of service he want, after that he can view the estimate bill and then send a request to repairman. If repairman accepts the request then customer can see the repairman’s profile and repairman’s current location. Customer can also contact  with repairman  by sending messages or make a call through this application. After job completion, customer can rate him. If customer send request by mistake, then customer can cancel that request and same scenario for repairman that if repairman accepts the request and he is not willing to go there then he can also cancel that request. Now you do not have to waste the time in searching a worker for indo or or outdoor services they can simply approach them thr ough this application. We are developing admin panel for this application on website. User can send a message or any kind of query regarding our services through this website without signup. In addition, user can subscribe us or can see all the information regarding our services through this website.

heading: 1.2 Goals and Objectives:
content: Following are the Goals and Objectives of our project:  Our application helps users to select a verified repairman.  To provide better quality of work.  To provide easiness.  To provide a user friendly GUI which can easily be operated.  To promote application development in Pakistan.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement:
content: Finding “Handyman Service Providers” is a challenging task particularly when one trave ls and move to a new residence because service suppliers are situated across different areas and change in costs, quality and type of facility that they offer. The inspiration behind this was the difficulties that one would face of finding a skilled person to solve the household issue. Currently people have no any application to get in contact with these repairmen. In addition, there is no standard way to ensure that the repairman have performed well on past jobs. Moreover, the availability of repairman is also of concern along with no standardized charging. To summarize above paragraphs, it is evident that such application shall not only be of benefit to end user but as well as increase the employment chances of skilled labour.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions and Constraints:
content: Following are the Assumptions and Constraints of our project:  Our application is free of cost.  Our application requires registration to avail or deliver services.  The developers will deliver the milestones and deliverables as per time mentioned in the plan.  At the end of December, our application will be ready for deployment.

heading: 1.5 Project Scope:
content: Our goal is to provide easiness to those who do not want to go outside and search repairman for indoor or outdoor services. With so many internet and smartphone users, it is important to use such modern technologies that have a future demand and scope in the market. It is aimed for such areas where people are so busy in the hustle and bustle of their daily life that they are unable to fix their household queries or tired of the behaviours of local repairman.

These methods are used from frameworks going from simple to quickly created frameworks. Se lect to pick software design approach is very essential. From above all software development life cycle, we have found that Iterative Software Development Life Cycle is the finest for us. We choose this Due to, we can have achieved results early and from time to time in it. We can measure the development of our project in it very easily and the most main thing is that it is less expensive if requirement Creep occur. Other purpose is it we can provide the product with every creep of requirements, it provides the capability to take the advice from customer early in the development phase and this model is finest for large projects and give us a mechanism how to handle the risk factor.
