heading: Project Abstract
content: The number of deaths due to accidents are increasing day by day. Most of these lives can be saved if the concerned authorities are informed in time, as most accident victims die as they don’t receive medical attention in time . The main reason of so much deat h toll is that victims do not get basic facilities of first aid on time. The rescue authorities or nearby hospital staff are not able to get to the victims proper location because they don’t use a proper digital location tracing system to get to the victims location. So we have developed an automated system that will reduce the time to inform the concerned authorities , and they can react quickly.  Our system will increase  the probability of saving lives by reducing the time for the au thorities to respond, by reducing the responding time of the concerned authorities the victims would be able to receive at least basic facilities of first aid on time. Another reason of so much causalities that after the accident the patient is unconscious and he is not able to contact and inform any one about the accident . Our system will automatically detect the accident using the mobile phone sensor, so despite of the unconsciousness of the victim the concerning authorities will be automatically informed about the victim ’s location and his health condition. The sensor will be triggered when the pressure experi enced exceeds a certain level, j ust like an airbag sensor. The emergency responders and the emergency contacts of the user would be informed with the location of the user.

heading: 1.1 INTRODUCTION
content: With the growing population, traffic accidents are on e of the emerging problems our society is going through. Road crashes are the 9th leading cause of death globally. Nearly 1.3 million people across the globe die in road crashes each year with an average of 3,287 casualties per day. Unless an action is taken to encounter this problem, traffic accidents are predicted to be 5th leading cause of death by 2030. Recently on 25 June an oil tanker lost control and crashed on the highway near the city of Bahawalpur. A local mosque in a town nearby announced it on its speaker. When the locals heard about the oil tanker’s crash, they rushed to the site, not to help but to collect the oil for their personal vehicles. While the locals where busy collecting the oil, a disaster struck. The fumes of the oil from the tanker ignited by a spark, the source of the spark hasn’t been yet confirmed. The spark caused the tanker to explode and killed at least 200 people. Most people died as the responding teams didn’t had the facilities and weren’t prepared for so many victims. This  was a tremendous tragedy and the people suffered a great loss. We should do our best to prevent from this kind of event to take place again in the coming future and to provide best possible efficient emergency services in such situations. Conventional vehicular sensor systems for accident detection, such as OnStar, notify emergency responders immediately by utilizing in -vehicle sensors, such as accelerometers and airbag deployment monitors, to detect car accidents. Unlike OnStar our system will use onboard sensors of a smartphone such as accelerometer to detect car accidents. The sole purpose of this project was  to design and implement such an automated system that counters these emerging problems and reduce the casualties as much as possible. The detectio n system would help reducing fatalities stemming from car accidents by reducing the response time of emergency responders. The system would counter the other emerging problems by notifying the respected concerned authorities about the incident . For example letting the ambulance know the location of an accident that toke  place, and its exact location. This would let the respected authorized personal to take action accordingly, and reduce the damages and fatalities. The end product would be such an intelligent system that would utilize internal sensors of a smartphone to detect any automobile crash and then interact with the nearest rescue station to communicate the exact location of the incident. The system would guide the authorities with the shortest possible route to save both time and energy. The patient’s report will be sent to the doctor before he reaches the hospital.

heading: 1.2 OBJECTIVES
content: Our projects goal is to decrease the level of casualties and losses which occur from traffic accidents by decreasing the response time of emergency responders. Smartphones and their onboard sensors are promising platforms for constructing such intelligent systems.

heading: 1.3 PROBLEM STATEMENT
content: Nearly 1.3 million people die in road crashes each year, on average 3,287 deaths a day.  An additional 20-50 million are injured or disabled. Road traffic crashes rank as the 9th leading cause of death and account for 2.2% of all deaths globally.  Each year nearly 400,000 people under 25 die on the world's roads, on average over 1,000 a day. Over 90% of all road fatalities occur in low and middle-income countries, which includes Pakistan. Most people don’t die directly on the impact, but they die as they don’t get medical attention quick enough. The main reason of not getting the proper medical response i s that the responding authorities are not aware of the accident. Our system will automatically inform the authorities about the accident. Another reason of not getting medical treatment on time, is that the responding authorities don’t have the exact locat ion of the incident. Sometimes there is a confusion that on which side of the road the accident happened. This is due to the fact that responding authorities don’t use a proper loc ation tracing system. Our app  will provide a proper system to guide  the responder to the  exact location. Our project will decrease the response time of the Emergency response teams. This would increase the probability of saving lives.

heading: 1.4.2.1 Detecting Accident without Onboard Vehicle Circuitry
content: A key challenge of developing such systems to detect collisions is the lack of integration between the smartphone and the vehicle. In contrast, conventional in-vehicle car accident detection systems rely on internal sensors integrated with the vehicle itself and can assume that any instance of high acceleration/deceleration is caused by a collision. Similarly, Smartphones onboard sensors without being integrated with the vehicles must be able to compute similar set of data.

heading: 1.4.2.2 Avoiding False Positives
content: Due to smartphone mobili ty, it’s hard to differentiate between an actual cars accidents versus a phone dropped. This inability to precisely identify and ignore false positives could eventually lead to waste valuable time of the emergency responders.

content: This project has a scope to save many lives and could benefit our society in the upcoming future, as it saves time and energy of the responding authorities. It can be used in any hospitals and people all around the world hospital. This system minimizes the delay to inform the respected authorities of the situation in hand. To do something just for the betterment of the people in the world is a fulfilling feeling all by itself. And implementing this project gives us an opportunity to do it.

heading: 5.1 PROBLEM FACED AND LESSIONS LEARNED
content: The detection of accident using a mobile app was a difficult task, as compared to the just installing a sensor on the body of the vehicle. The detection of accident was the main problem faced by us , as differentiating between a phone drop and accident is hard , as the phone experienc e the same kind of changes. The detection of real collision using a mobile phone sensor requires implementing a java sensor code. If your vehicle is on a track that consists of too much obstacles and road is damaged then it’s not an accident. The sensor do es not activate the service, so differentiating between the real collision and small shakes through coding is quite difficult task. If the detection is wrong it would sent false data and waste the time and energy of the emergency responders.

heading: 5.2 PROJECT SUMMARY
content: Our project is an android based accident detection system. It’s a mobile app that automatically detects accident. The user has to install app in the phone and activate the sensor that would automatically detect the accident. After detecting the accident the application sends the user ’s location to responding authorities. O ne app is for the responder that would receive the victim ’s location. The responder will respond accordingly. The responder will then immediately get to the victims location to provide q uick assistance. The responder will generate a report of the victim. The report will consists of victim’s credentials e.g. the victim’s name, address, blood group, age. This report will be send to the doctor, in this way the form of the patient will be aut omatically filled so that arrangements for his treatment can be made before the arrival of the patient.

heading: 5.3 FUTURE WORK
content: To make the system much smarter and accurate in the future, work can be done to get the data of accidents occurred and apply data mining algorithms to help us find what are the main reasons that cause accidents are. The areas where the most accidents occur, can be highlighted, and the user s can be made aware of those areas or turns beforehand, so we drives with caution. The system can also be made more efficient by providing signal free routes to the responder that would make our system more efficient. Voice activation system can also be introduced to make activate the sensor  in case of robbery or other emergency situation other than the accid ent. In this case the sensor will be activated by a speaking a specific keyword by the user. So the nearby police stations will be informed about the robbery and they can respond accordingly.

heading: Abstract:
content: Today our agriculture industry is facing a great challenge with respect to both quantity and quality that’s why there is a need of new tools for the Agriculture industry to improve its performance, efficie ncy and cope up with environmental conditions. We have developed a decision support system which is performing comparative analysis and data - mining. The proposed system is providing the guidelines to the user through web portal and by using it’s inference engine which  takes a decision based on the past experiences and current calculations of data -mining and machine learning algorithms. Our system monitors the conditions of the crop which might not be able to do manually by human. It provides such an ease f or agricultural industry that they are able to manage these tasks remotely. It is considering the factors like soil water content, pressure, temperature, humidity, weather and manages different managerial tasks in the farm. It also follows the concept of precision agriculture to remain up-to-date with current situation every time. heading: 1.1 Brief introduction
content: Pakistan’s economy relies upon the agricultural industry and is highly known as an agricultural country. Precision agriculture is the concept which can change the concept of farming for the farmers [1]. In the past it was difficult to implement because the technology was not available lik e smartphones, mobile apps, cloud computing and sensors. In that time precision agriculture was only available for large operation which could support the IT infrastructure and other technology resources required to fully implement and benefit from the ben efits of precision agriculture. Now it is possible to make it available for the agriculture co-operatives and even small family farms. Agriculture industry contributes around 24% of GDP (Gross domestic product) and records for half of employed labour force and is the greatest source of outside trade income [2]. Unfortunately, Pakistan is not utilizing the resources properly and improvising the methods whereas many developed countries are improving agricultural techniques and have introduced precision -farming. content: The proposed system gives the real -time data to the farmers by using different sensors. The different modules which are included in the proposed system are as follows. • Water observing module:  In water observing section, the rainfall in the fields will be measured and the intelligent algorithm will calculate that how much quantity of water is required of water and will give results accordingly, by using one of the weather station sensor “pluviometer” the rainfall will be measured.   Page 14 of 71 • Soil observing module:  Soil observing sensor will measure the moisture in the soil. • Weather observing module:  In weather observing module, detect the direction of wind using wind vane instrument. So, farmer can make counter measures in case of unacceptable conditions.   • Crop Water Stress Index module The crop water stress index (CWSI) is based on crop evapotranspiration and reference evapotranspiration to detect crop water stress. heading: 1.7 Methodology
content: The research methodology used in the proposed system is Qualitative. Qualitative research introduces non-qualitative sort of dissection. Qualitative examination is gathering, dissecting and deciphering information by watching what individuals do and say. Qualitative exploration is considerably more subjective and uses altogether different strategies for gathering information, mainly individual, in-depth meetings and focus groups. The first step in this project is to gather the requirements and reduce the deficiencies of the current methods, which are being used to analyze the crops. In agriculture sector  the crop monitoring currently is not being analyzed by an automated system in Pakistan. While the proposed system is based on sensors and is able to monitor crop more accurately. In recent years, the agricultural part of the country has been confronting genuine issues, for example,      decrease in harvest yield, increment in input costs, water issues, Soil issues and decreased acknowledgment of agricultural items in global markets. In phase of implementation, sensor values are captured through the sensors attached to the  Waspmote sense respective values i.e. temperature, soil moisture create frames for these values and send to Waspmote, upon receiving frames, Waspmote send all the frames to the Meshlium. Sensor parser run upon the receiving of the frames p arse them to structured data and save it to the local database. The synchronizer on Meshlium runs after every 5 seconds and synchronize the data on the connected cloud database. So that we have a synchronized data on all the devices connected to the cloud database. After computation, data-mining algorithm is applied on dataset and efficiently determines the crop water stress level. The provided instructions are based on the stress level of the crop which is determined by using Data Mining algorithm. The data-mining algorithm that has been implemented is J48 algorithm which generates the results efficiently, accurately and with less error rate. This algorithm uses the Supervised Machine Learning to predict the outcome. Supervised Learning is when you have input and output variables and you use Page 17 of 71 algorithm to determine the approximate mapping function. According to the mapping function it predicts the output for the new input data. This algorithm follows the Classification for Prediction Architecture. Figure 1 Classification for Prediction Architecture [4] The values stored in the database is the agriculture data. The agriculture data is further used as training set and test set for data -mining algorithm implementation. Pre -processing phase is implemented when there is need of removing unwanted or adding required information. According to our dataset the agriculture database is the pre-processing data. The pre-processed data is further converted to ARFF file for algorithm implementa tion using WEKA. The training data -set is used to determine the mapping function. The new input data is the test set in which the mapping function is applied and predicts the output. The input variables are crop name and crop water stress index. The output or class attribute is the stress level. First training phase is implemented and generates a knowledge base according to the Page 18 of 71 dataset. After the system does training, it implements the classification algorithm i.e J48 on the test dataset. It retrieves the predicted outcome on the basis of previous training. In testing all modules are tested individually involving data extraction, data Pre -processing and classification. All these modules are tested successfully. After integration of all these modules the wh ole integrated system is tested again.

heading: 6.8 Stress Testing
content: Stress testing is the way toward deciding the capacity of a program to keep up a specific level of viability under ominous co nditions. heading: 1. INTRODUCTION
content: In this era, people are so much busy in their routines that they don’t get enough time to shop for the things they love. For this purpose, E-Commerce is preferred, which let them get their things at home at ease. There are many applications which let the o ne to shop for online footwear’s. The user must have to know their exact foot size for the purpose of buying the footwear that they want from the application. In addition to that the user must also have the knowledge for different scale size of different f ootwear brands and companies. This project aims to develop a software framework, which can be utilized by users to help them measure the size of their foot. This framework will provide a set of interface for measuring the size of the foot. This project will be mainly used for online shopping purposes so that the user gets the right size of footwear that best suits the user. This framework is the implementation of image processing in MATLAB, and Android as an interface. This application requires the user to  take the picture of his foot or select a previously captured image with a reference object, which will be used for the purpose of measuring the depth of the image. The image from the Android interface shall then be forwarded to MATLAB in the result of the successful integration between Android and MATLAB. Image processing techniques are then applied on the image to analyze the image and measure the foot size after measuring the depth of the image with the help of the reference object, and applying the regression function on the image. The foot measured results are then sent back to the Android interface where the user shall be shown the size of his foot. According to the measured size of the user, the application shall then display the footwear products tha t are relatable to the user, and allow the user to shop for the footwear products that matches his foot size.

content:  To get command over image processing  To facilitate the user in measuring the foot size  To provide footwear that are relevant to user needs  To provide a user-friendly interface to the user  To explore the capability of Image Processing  To save user’s time by providing only relevant products

heading: 1.2. Problem statement
content: With the rapid development in the field of mobile application, user expects less effort and more output. And most of the users are focused on saving their time in performing their task. There are no applications that can allow the user to measure his foot size from the app and displays the relevant results to the user. When it comes to buying footwear of right size that one expected is fairly a difficult task. Different companies and different brands got their customized scale of sizes and one cannot adjust accordingly even if one knew ones exact foot size. There is no mechanism for the user to facilitate the problem of measuring the foot size and getting only relevant products in the results by saving the user’s time, no matter he is a novice or expert user.

content: Everyone expects from an application to save time for performing the specific task. The user expects to save as much time as possible in buying footwear online. In the most cases the user got confused in the size of his foot and the size written on the product. The user might be unaware of his foot size or in the other case might not have the knowledge about the size scaling of that product company. This application save the user to measure the size of the foot and display the results that are relevant to the user. The application shall measure and analyze the results of the image and then provide the user with his required expected products. This shall be a pretty better source of shopping the footwear online according to user needs and expectations.

heading: 2.1.2. Object size measurement
content: The size of an object in the image as well as measuring the maximum approximate distance from the camera to the object are involved in the field of image processing [6]. For this purpose there shall be any criteria to define the number of pixels and measure those pixels over a given defined matrix.  The “pixels per metric” ratio The reference object that shall be used in measuring the size of an object in the image must be first analyzed properly. For the purpose of deciding that what reference object shall be used that reference object must follow the following two important properties.  The size of the object in the image should be known i.e. the size along vertical axis (height) and the size along horizontal axis (width).  The reference object should be quite distinguishable in the image so that it can found easily. In order to so either the placement of the object should be known e.g. we fix the location of the reference object in all the images say left-top corner or via appearances i.e. the color of the reference object as well as its shape must be unique from every other object in the image, so that it can be identified and distinguished properly. Consider the following example, in which there is a quarter which will be used as a reference object in this case throughout the example to measure the size of tablets also present in the image but it will be also ensured that the reference object will always be the left-most object in the following image: Figure 1: Pixel per metric Ratio: The quarter present in the image placed as the most left object making it easier to extract through sorting We will check that the reference object will be on the left hand side, when the metric ratio of pixels is obtained, this shall provide the sorting that will start from left side will get the left most object first. The formula for this is given as follows; pixelMertic = Width_of_object *1/ Object_of_known_width The quarter has a  Object_of_known_width of 0.955 inches which was calculated or was known before. The computed Width_of_object is 150.00 pixels. Hence the result; pixelMertic = 150*1/ 0.955 = 157 pixels The ratio has been calculated to be about 157 pixels for each 0.955 inches in the above image. The size of objects in an image can be computed by the help of the above ratio. After that the output image will be as shown below: Figure 2: Measuring the size of objects in an image through image processing techniques. The size of the object in the image has been successfully computed. Similarly, the sizes of each of the objects have been calculated as shown in the above image. On the contrary, not all the  results are  perfect, e ven with the same size / Both quarters have a height difference of 0.1 inches. There mainly two reasons for this: 1. The angle is not 90o. The angle should be, “looking down” at the objects like a bird’s eye view. This is not true in this case so the dimensions of the objects present in the image can appear slightly distorted. 2. Both the intrinsic and extrinsic parameters of the camera should be checked for calibration. The better size approximation of the image can be done by firstly undistorting the image.

heading: 2.1.3 Image Analysis
content: Image analysis is the process of analyzing the image for the purpose of extracting some information that shall be meaningful.  [8] Image analysis mainly deals with  the digital images by using image processing techniques. Image analysis contains some simple tasks that are responsible for analyzing the image. Moreover, there are more image anal ysis tasks which are responsible for the much more complex analyzation of the image. The image analysis on complex data is very difficult with computer technology. This implies that the computer visual cannot provide meaningful information easily and the analysis of image through computer technology is a complex task. On the other hand, the computer visual is far much better in analyzing any kind of image. The computer image analysis cannot be replaced with that of human image analysis but for this purpose the techniques of neural networks and detectors acts as an important tool for computerized image analysis.

heading: 2.1.4 Laser Measurement
content: This was developed for the mainly purpose of estimating the length of different animals and was developed for the Wild Life [1]. This system uses two laser points i.e. starting and ending points and then mark it on animals. And after that with the help of an image and different algorithms an estimated length of that specific animal was calculated. This system attracts everyon e globally but unfortunately did not make count. As the results was not too satisfactory, but for research purpose it was surely gold by introducing an entirely different concept. After this research work is in continue for making it accurate enough. Our proposed system shall just take an image to calculate algorithms and then to produce the results. And this system shall help in identifying the Human Body objects and calculate results for its measurement. Figure 3: Measurement through laser projection

heading: 2.1.5 Object Distance Measurement
content: The Object Distance Measurement [2] was developed to measure the distance of a piece of paper from the random distances. In this, a piece of paper was attached with the room door and the camera detect that paper first, and after detecting it correctly the camera roughly gives an estimated length from its current position to that paper position. The algorithms behind the project was accurate enough to give a pretty good estimation. This surely helps in studying the Image Processing domain from different angles. The project we proposed not only help in detecting objects but also help in measuring the size of that detected object. Figure 4: Distance measurement through digital camera

heading: 2.1.6 Object to Object Distance Measurement
content: This project involves a set of objects in an image and one reference object. The system works in a way that all the objects dimension was to be saved already and among the objects, one object is  said to be the reference object. Mostly this system is limited to set the left most object as the reference object. After that the algorithms and calculations includes to identify the edges of other objects and then the system estimates the distance from the reference object to the other object [3]. Our proposed system shall identify the object from the image and instead of measuring the distance among the other, it helps in measuring the size of objects and then to produce the results.

heading: 2.1.7 Object Measurement
content: The system is developed to measure the size of objects in inches from a captured image. The system must know one reference object among the objects in the image i.e. limited to the left most in this system. The system then uses Image Processing techniques to compute the size of each object by giving an estimation, but for this the image to be taken must be from a good angle i.e. 90 degrees. The system estimates the size of objects with mostly accurate enough results. The system we proposed measure s the size of Human body objects by first identifying it and then using Image processing techniques to estimate its size [4]. heading: 2.1.8. Web Image Processing using new Edge Detection Algorithm
content: For understanding complex image manipulation and more feasibility in images, Image Processing plays a vital role. This understanding can later on be used in specific domains of science and technology like medical science, satellite etc. But here a question comes in mind how to deal with images that are not connected. For this purpose, edge detection algorithm can be used for image processing for web based services. Thus providing an online connection for image processing. This edge detection algorithm as the name suggest is used for detecting edges/lines in an image. By applying this research work with the satellite image to find out the edge detection method this algorithm is very accurate. [9]

content: on Error-Tolerance Due to different and various insensitivities of images with different frequencies that reacted by human beings, we have to used appropriate and accurate thresholds so that we can detect and determine these different frequencies found in test images. In this way we check the acceptability of thresholds of images in term of error rates.

content: A set of all possible values that each parameter can take are better expressed with a 3D image. A robust methodology is used in the image processing so that Primary Ignition Map or PIM can be optimized which in turn is used as a base value by Engine Control Unit or ECU that then used in the ignition of air- fueled mixture so that the end result is the maximization of torque and power output of the engine. These techniques are used in the reconstruction of various maps along with the manipulation of maps their comparison, combination etc. [11] 2.1.11. An algorithm will be used for step by step extraction of object of interest and then measuring the size of the image like a diameter, length, height etc. [12]

heading: Techniques
content: There are two techniques for measuring human height. One is a contact techniques, the other is a non- contact technique. For non-contact measurement a fixed laser point and a triangular distance measurement method is used. A laser beam was used for signal emission while a digital camera is used for signal detection as a hardware. In software, however, the distance between both of the laser beam projection image and the center of the image was used to get the measured length. While, to calibrate the error and increase measurement precision an offset compensation data is used. Similarly, for better measurement precision the space between the laser and digital camera is adjusted. For simulation all kinds of different and various conditions were used.

heading: 5.2. MATLAB Image Processing
content: The work related to Image processing is done on Matlab, and different image processing techniques were combined and applied to find and measure the foot region and the reference object.

heading: 5.2.1. Finding and Measuring Foot
content: The first step applied in the image processing is the extraction of our region of interest i.e. the foot. Extracting the foot from the image and then measuring the pixels calculated is the first input in the regression function that is applied to predict the foot size according to the data of the regression function. Figure 24: Methodology of foot extraction and measurement Figure 25: Proposed Methodology for foot extraction and measurement Figure 26: Proposed Methodology for Coin Extraction and Measurement This is the original image, in which the foot and the reference object i.e. the coin is present in the image. The picture also contains some noise in the background, which will be removed by applying the skin mask on the image by using Image processing on the Matlab. Figure 27: Finding and Measuring Foot Skin mask is prepared by giving the algorithm 25 skin images, and then taking the mean of the three color space. The skin mask is applied on the YIQ color space. The color space I and the color space Q is used to create the skin mask. Applying the mask on the mask extracts the foot from the image.

heading: Figure 29: Greyscale Image
content: The image is then converted into grayscale with the help of Image Processing on Matlab by using the rgb2gray function.

heading: Figure 30: Binary Image
content: The gray image is then first converted to binary image and then passed to find the binding box of the image in order to get the pixels size of the foot. After the binding box is applied on the image the image is then cropped by its boundary with the help of the extreme pixels and binding box. The pixel size of the foot is then calculated by taking the one-axis of the foot i.e. the longest one (x-axis). Finding and measuring the coin diameter (reference object) For calculating the distance and the depth of the image we need a reference object. We have used 5 type of coins i.e. 10-rupee coin, 5-rupee coin (silver), 5-rupee coin (gold), 2-rupee coin (silver), 1- rupee coin (silver) as reference objects, from which any one can be chosen at once. The coin is first extracted from the image and after the successful results its diameter is calculated using the morphological image processing function i.e. EquivDiameter. This is the second input in the regression function with the foot pixels. Figure 31: Original Image with coin This is the original image from which the coin is to extracted, the picture also contains the foot i.e. our region of interest and some noise in the background. The coin is extracted by using the threshold color mask and by combing the different image processing techniques together. Figure 32: Threshold color mask Threshold color mask is applied on the coin according to its coin type, in order to extract the coin from the background. Figure 33: Edge detection Edge detection is then applied on the result of the threshold color mask to get the edges in the resulted picture.

heading: Figure 34: Dilation Function
content: Dilate function is applied on the resulted picture of the edge detection to make the coin more obvious in the picture and in order to make it prominent for the next techniques to get the coin extracted. Figure 35: Fill Holes function Fill holes function is then applied next in order to fill holes in the image and make the coin shape complete for that it can be extracted and its diameter can be measured.

heading: Figure 36: Erode Function
content: Erode function is then applied on the fill holes resulted image for the purpose of eliminating some part background noise or for separating the noise from the coin if its connected. So the round solidity can be applied.

heading: Figure 37:  Round Solidity
content: In the next step the round solidity is applied on the image with the help of morphological image processing, for the purpose of removing the noise from the background and get only the coin as a result. The solidity value is set to extract the coin i.e. round object, from the resulted image

heading: Figure 38: Extracted Coin
content: The coin is then extracted from the image after extracting the biggest blob from the image. The biggest blob will be the solidity result of the image i.e. the coin. The coin is then extracted after being applied the threshold color mask on the I and Q color space of the YIQ color space and then applying the image processing techniques together.

heading: 5.2.2. Regression Function
content: The results of the coin diameter and the foot pixels are passed on to the regression function which predicts the results according to the data. The predicted results are then passed on to the Android for the further processing

heading: 6.1. Problems faced and lessons learned
content: While working and during the process of developing the application many problems were faced by the entire team such as time management, team member’s collaboration and to identify and understand the actual problem faced during the project. We have applied different Image Processing techniques for the purpose of segmenting the image. We have tried to segment the image on different image color spaces. We consumed a lot of time in solving the complex background problem in the image, for extracting our reference object i.e. coin and the region of interest i.e. foot. Moreover, different reference objects were tried to calculate the image depth. We chose the best possible solution for the purpose of making the project work better after applying different techniques on the image. We have also faced the issue of MATLAB and Android Studio integration as MATLAB server is not available and no related material on research papers can be found. The detail is attached with Appendix A.

heading: 6.2. Project summary
content: Measurement through Image Processing is based on the techniques of Digital Image Processing. We take an image as an input that contains our region of interest i.e. foot and reference object i.e. coin. The image is uploaded to the server. The server is connected with MATLAB and MATLAB reads the image by the path stored in the database. MATLAB extracts the foot with the help of Threshold color mask on the YIQ color space. The pixel of the foot is measured with the help of bounding technique in the image processing. The reference object is extracted from the image with the help of Threshold color mask on the same YIQ color space and then extracted with the help of combining the different image processing techniques. The extracted coin is then measured and passed on to the regression function as with the foot pixel value. The regression function then predicts the foot size with the help of provided data. The results are then passed on to the database. The size value is then displayed by the Android Studio in a dialogue box and then a list of related footwear products will be shown. The product category on the basis of gender and the Android will rescale the size results to show the different gender product results.

heading: 6.3 Future work
content: This application will be used in online footwear shopping to solve the issues in different sizes while buying a product. As different countries have different foot size scales. So, this issue of different foot size scales will be solved by the use of this application. In the future, companies will also be able to use this application for manufacturing customized footwear products. Moreover, Machine Learning will be applied in the future to automatically detect which gender does the foot belong to and which type of the reference object is used.

heading: 8. Techniques applied and lesson learned
content: We have used and tried different Image processing approaches to deal with the segmentation problem and for the removal of background noise and the region of interest extraction. This section summarizes the techniques we have applied and their results. These techniques were giving good results for simple and plain background but when it comes to complex background the results were not satisfactory.

heading: 8.1. The Masking RGB
content: This technique is the most simple for extracting the specific points from the image. The Masking RGB (Red Green Blue) is based on the combination of Red color pixels, Green color pixels and Blue color pixels. Masking was applied on the RGB color model and the results were tested over a large number of samples of images for the verification of results. This technique was proposed for extracting the foot from the given set of image and later on which can be processed.

heading: 8.2. Implementation of the Masking RGB
content: Implementation of the Masking RGB is based on the proposed technique above. Large numbe r of sample of images were collected for the purpose of applying the technique and in result getting the best throughput from it. This technique was quite helpful in areas where the object (region of interest) was situated with different colored background . Following is one the image taken for the implementation of the Masking RGB: Figure 39: Image with Simple Background The first sample of images is composed with the simple background. The first task to be initiated was to remove the shadow of the object from the image. The masking RGB was quite successful in identifying the object from the image and districting it from its shadow. But do not provide us the best throughput that can be further processed. The Masking RGB can b e applied with two further combinations i.e. one with the AND operation and the other with the OR operation. The results of applied Masking RGB with the both operations are given below: Figure 40: Masking RGB with AND operation Figure 41: Masking RGB with OR operation The Masking RGB resolved of issue of not considering the shadow part from the image by first applying the different colored mask points on the image and then displaying the results in the binary format. The above results are quite visible in order for identifying the best operation with the Masking RGB. AND operation makes the best possible combination with the Masking RGB technique for removing the shadow and extracting the object (region of interest).

heading: 8.3. The Masking RGB on Separate Channels
content: The Masking RGB can also be applied on the different channels of RGB image i.e. Red, Green and blue. The different channels then can be used to combine a new solution for the specific expected output. Following is the result of applying the mask on different channels of RGB separately: Figure 42: Masking RGB on Red Channel Figure 43: Masking RGB on Green Channel Figure 44: Masking RGB in Blue Channel Following is the code for applying the Masking RGB technique on Matlab for the throughput of combine channel and separate channels:

heading: //Reading Image
content: >> rgb = imread ('rgbimage.jpg');

heading: //Separating Channels
content: >> redChannel = rgb (:,:,1); >> greenChannel = rgb (:,:,2); >> blueChannel = rgb (:,:,3); >> maskSimple = impixel(rgb); //Applying mask on combination of channels >> hthreshold = redChannel>89 & redChannel<193 & greenChannel>73 & greenChannel<175 & blueChannel >58 & blueChannel<151; >> imshow(hthreshold); //Applying mask on separate channels with AND operation >> rthreshold =redChannel>89 & redChannel<193; >> gthreshold =  greenChannel>73 & greenChannel<175; >> >> bthreshold =  blueChannel >58 & blueChannel<151; >> imshow (rthreshold); >> imshow (gthreshold); >> imshow (bthreshold); //Applying mask on separate channels with OR operation >> final = rthreshold | bthreshold | gthreshold; >> imshow (final);

heading: 8.4. The Lightning Technique
content: The lightning technique was based on the Lab color space also known as CIELAB or CIE L*a*b. Where the L channel in Lab color space consist of the brightness layer, a channel is consist of indications where the color falls along with the red and green axis,  and the b channel consist of indications where the color falls along with the blue and yellow axis. The lightning technique allows in differentiating the object from the image by using this Lab color space. The lightning technique is another technique for  the shadow removal of object and the extraction of the region of interest.

heading: 8.5. Implementation of Lightning Technique
content: This technique was applied over a large number of samples of images to get some specific results for the purpose of evaluation. Same like the Masking RGB technique this technique can also be applied with the combination of the both operations i.e. AND operation and OR operation. This technique was basically used for the shadow removal of the object from the image and in the result we can get the only foot from the image. As Lightning technique is applied on the Lab color space, we shall be able to see the brightness level of our given input image and can also be able to see that which color falls at which level on the image. With the help of this we shall be able to see that our object what brightness level and what are the colors imposed on it and to what extent. This technique still not is able to resolve the issue of giving best results for the image to be further processed. Morphologica l operations play a quite prominent role in the Lightning technique to be fully applied. Following is the result of converting a simple image to Lab color space: Figure 45: Lab Color space image conversions

heading: 8.6. Analysis on Operations
content: The conversion of Lab color space allows in differentiating the color indication of the object from the image and also allows seeing the brightness level at different pixels of the image. Getting the idea of the object from these specifications we can able to distinguish the shadow of the image which is having less brightness level. Based on the analysis we applied the Lightning technique on this Lab color space image. Applying lightning technique with the AND operation provides a general backbone of the object that is our region of interest. The Lightning technique with OR operation differentiates the image with different given brightness level and color falls indication. Whereas, applying the Lightning technique with the OR operation provides the result with all the channel combinations. Lightning technique with OR operation however clarifies our region of interest more visible that will be later on used for the measurement. Following is the result of applying the Lightning technique with both the AND operation and the OR operation: Figure 46: Lightning Technique with AND operation Figure 47: Lightning Technique with OR operation Following is the code of applying the Lightning technique with the AND operation and OR operation, implemented in the Matlab: pic = imread ('labImage.jpg'); //Conversion of image to Lab color space >> colorTransform = makecform('srgb2lab'); >> lab = applycform(pic, colorTransform); >> imshow(lab); >> mask = impixel (lab); >> L = lab (:,:,1); >> a = lab (:,:,2); >> b = lab (:,:,3);

heading: //AND
content: >> hthreshold = L>93 & L<162 & a>133 & a<137 & b >137 & b<148; >> imshow (hthreshold);

heading: //OR
content: >> hthreshold = L>93 & L<162 | a>133 & a<137 | b >137 & b<148; >> imshow (hthreshold);

heading: 8.7. Mature Saturation Technique
content: The Mature Saturation technique is based on the HSV color model. The technique is mostly relying on the saturation channel of the HSV color model. The saturation channel provides the best throughput regarding the background removal and distinguishing the object and region of interest. This technique is provided the best results of background removal among all the other applied. The points from Hue channel and Saturation channel is collected togethe r to make a mask to then threshold the image to get the specified result. The mask is applied to individual channel of HSV color space and then combines together to form a result.

heading: 8.8. Mature Saturation Implementation
content: The Mature Saturation technique is again applied on various numbers of pictures with simple plain background and also with less complex background. This technique is as by its name is the most mature among all the other implemented techniques. The results are tested over a large number of s amples with different angles and different less complex backgrounds. The following are the images of the image after dividing it to the Hue channel, saturation channel and value channel (also known as brightness channel): Figure 48: Dividing the image to Hue channel The Hue channel of HSV color space only provides us the general boundary of our interested object. This segmentation makes it quite prominent by giving it a darker color, as the Hue factor counts in this Hue channel. The background noise is somewhat visible in the Hue channel. Figure 49: Dividing the image to Saturation Channel The Saturation channel is the key channel in the Mature Saturation technique, as all of the technique mostly depends on this channel of the color space. The details of the image are quite visible in the output result of the sample image. The saturation channel provides the mature results by differentiating the background noise with our interested object. The saturat ion channel also removed the shadow factor from the sample image, and making the boundary of the sample image mature enough to be distinguished from its background. Figure 50: Dividing the image to value/brightness channel The saturation channel just provides the brightness level information of the sample image, by distinguishing the brightness level at different pixels of the image.

heading: 8.9. Analyzing the Mature Saturation
content: The pixels points of the image are collected and stored in a variable to be used later. Those samples points are consist of the pixels values of our interested object. The points are combined to form a Mature Saturation mask which is mostly affected on the Hue channel and the Saturation channel. Following are the images of collecting a sample mask from the Hue and Saturation channel: Figure 51: Points collection from the Hue channel Figure 52: Points collection from the Saturation channel

heading: 8.10. Shaping the Result
content: The above mask is applied over the channels of Hue, Saturation and Value separately. And together to combine with the AND operation and OR operation to get the desired output. Following are the results of applying the Mature Saturation technique: Figure 53: Mature saturation technique on Hue channel After applying the mature saturation technique on the Hue channel, the noise which is quite visible on the Hue channel is pretty much removed from the background an d the shape of the object is visible to much extent. Different morphological operations are used later on to make it much visible and to fill the holes. Figure 54: Mature saturation technique on Saturation channel The saturation channel is the mature among the all and provides the best result and the details of the image. The boundary and edges of the object are very much clear and the result is satisfying when compared to other techniques. Figure 55: Mature saturation technique on Value channel The Value channel provides a general idea of the object, and displays the brightness level of the image and the object present in it. Following is the comparison the original sample image and the Mature Saturation technique with AND operation between the collected Hue, Saturation and Value channel: Figure 56: Original image Figure 57: Final output of mature saturation technique The background noise which is a little much disturbing in the saturation channel also is removed, only our interested object i.e. foot is visible in the image with its boundary and edges. The morphological techniques like erode dilate and filling holes plays a vital role in making the  image clearer and more visible to be processed further. The following is the code of applied mature saturation technique on matlab: pic = imread ('Image.jpg'); //Conversion of image to HSV color space >> hsv = rgb2hsv(pic); >> imshow(hsv); //Segmentation of HSV channels >> h = hsv (:,:,1); >> s = hsv (:,:,2); >> v = hsv (:,:,3); >> imshow (h); >>imshow(s); >> imshow(v); >> huepixel = impixel (h); >> saturationpixel = impixel (s); >> valuepixel = impixel (v);

heading: 8.11. Ellipse MS
content: Ellipse MS (mature saturation) is an extension to the Mature Saturation technique. This technique is basically responsible for identifying the eclipse in the image. But for that purpose the image must be clear from the background noise as good as it can. The image is then processed over its region props to identify the ellipse based objects from the image.

heading: 8.12. EMS Implementation
content: As the EMS (ellipse mature saturation) is an extension to MS (mature saturation) technique, so the above technique must be applied in order to apply this technique. The results of the EMS (ellipse mature saturation) shall be helpful in the identification of objects later on. Following is the result of applying the Ellipse MS technique: Figure 58: Final output after applying Ellipse MS technique The image shows the entire ellipse shaped object from the output of the Maturation saturation technique. The bigger ellipse is our main object of interest. The other small ellipse will be automatically removed when morphological operations are applied on the result of the Mature Saturation technique. Following is the code for the applied Ellipse MS technique: //calculating region props s = regionprops(thres, 'Orientation', 'MajorAxisLength', ... 'MinorAxisLength', 'Eccentricity', 'Centroid') bw = thres; imshow(bw) hold on //analyzing the region props technique phi = linspace(0,2*pi,50); cosphi = cos(phi); sinphi = sin(phi); for k = 1:length(s) xbar = s(k).Centroid(1); ybar = s(k).Centroid(2); a = s(k).MajorAxisLength/2; b = s(k).MinorAxisLength/2; theta = pi*s(k).Orientation/180; R = [ cos(theta)   sin(theta) -sin(theta)   cos(theta)]; xy = [a*cosphi; b*sinphi]; xy = R*xy; x = xy(1,:) + xbar; y = xy(2,:) + ybar; plot(x,y,'r','LineWidth',2); end hold off

heading: 8.13. The Magnetic Watershed
content: All the above techniques are quite helpful in dealing with the images that have simple background or less complex background. For that purpose, another introduced and applied technique is Magnetic watershed technique. In which firstly the watershed algorithm is applied and then the gradient magnitude is extracted. Opening and closing is done to more clarify the image.

content: The result of Magnetic watershed does not provide the best possible output for the complex background as the complex background noise was still visible on the results. heading: 1. Chapter 1: Introduction
content: Final Year Project is a quite crucial for the final year students. The main aim of this project is to broaden the student’s knowledge and give them a chance to enhance their skills according to the market trend. Final Year Project consists of ma ny phases from submission to till end. Final year project is very crucial for the undergraduate students. The aim of this project is to broaden the student’s knowledge and give them a chance to enhance their skills according to the market trend. FYP’s have to go through many phases from submission to till end. In the earlier stages students picks up the idea and after discussion with their supervisor they choose to implement this innovative idea. They write proposals for the selected project and submit thei r proposals. FYP committee accept or reject these proposals. Then after the approval of proposals by the committee, FYP report 1 have to be submitted and then at the end of the final year the FYP report2 has to submit. Our objective is to develop an online portal for the FYP procedure. In this portal, students register their projects and send requests to other students to become group members. Then they send request to supervisors to supervise them in their projects. Student can easily upload their proposals which their supervisors can view and evaluate them. After the evaluation of the supervisors, proposals are available for the Batch -advisors to evaluate. Committee Members send these evaluated proposals to faculty members that have similar skills as  project have. Faculty members evaluate assigned proposals and send their response against these proposals to Committee Members. Committee Member send these responses to supervisors and students. On the submission of Report1 and Report2 from the students, supervisors first evaluate these reports. Supervisor can accept reports or can ask student for resubmission with improvements. FYP committee member can schedule the Final year presentations, all list of projects will be shown to them and they will assign internals, externals and room numbers to them. This list will be saved and sent to supervisors and students. During the assessment of projects, internals and externals will have a form, they will just click the radio buttons and give comments. At the end ma rks will be calculated automatically for the students. Portal also have an admin panel for the exceptional cases if any group needs to change its project and further issues. Admin can add new students and faculty members by filling form one by one or admin  has option to upload excel sheet having student’s details. Students and faculty members can manage their profiles and can send messages to each other. The Design of the web portal will be user-friendly providing all the users to easily understand and operate the portal. The Development of the portal will be done by using the latest and the powerful technologies such as the Laravel Framework for the best production of the portal. Therefore, this portal will eliminate most of the headache of the FYP process by automating the process and will help the students, supervisors and the FYP committee in completing the process in a smarter way so that the time and the resources of each of the person involved, which gets wasted during the traditional process can be reduced as much as possible. heading: 1.1 Objectives
content: The objectives of our project are as follows: 1. One of main objective of the FYP management portal is to make the process efficient as well as effective by reducing the workload of the FYP Committee. 2. The proposed system will increase the productivity by reducing the time required to complete the various phases of the process into a few numbers of clicks. 3. The portal will also provide the Students to access the previously completed projects to avoid the clash between the two projects. 4. To provide the data to the Students, Supervisor and the FYP Committee in the most organized way by using the database. 5. The portal will also provide the reports to the FYP Committee based on several parameters in just a few clicks. For example, the Committee can view the list of the Students who have cleared the phase 1(Report-I) of their project. Similarly, they can also view the number of A’s given by any supervisor. 6. The Supervisor can easily uploa d the grades by just logging into the portal instead of the traditional method in which the Supervisor had to fill and calculate form. 7. The Reports that is accepted can be uploaded on the portal and are properly archived in the database so that can be retrieved later on when required. 8. Project will provide ease to the students from submission to end. 9. Reducing the paper work and workload of the students and faculty. 10. Will make the workflows smooth. 11. It will provide archives that will help new students in choosing their FYP. Page 11 of 89

heading: 1.2 Problem Statement
content: One of the issues of the FYP process is that the FYP Committee needs to physically execute them. In other word, the procedures are neither successful nor  effective, as time has been wasted in carrying out the compilation. The way that the FYP process being supervised is extremely badly arranged. An example is the  situation when student first manually visits supervisor to evaluate its proposals, then visit batch-advisor and then committee member. This all procedure is quite difficult due to time clash between members and students. Another example is grading the  projects, supervisor manually calculates each assessment report of internals and externals and then calculate marks. Secondly, searching for the students who are taking the Project 1 will also be not as easy as by using this portal. In addition, when a student selects an FYP idea he/she does not know that whether this idea is already implemented or chosen by another group or not until he/she discuss it with the supervisor, so to avoid this confusion this project is the best solution. By using this portal student can easily sort out this type of confusion.

heading: 1.3 Assumptions and Constraints
content: There are certain assumptions  and constraints that were made for our project . New accounts for students and faculty members will be created by admin.  User has a knowledge about the FYP process. Exceptional cases like a student want to change his/her project after the submission of proposal would be h andled by admin . Only last year students will be accommodated.  It is mandatory for the user to have good internet connection to interact with the portal.

heading: 1.4 Project Scope
content: Today world is advancing towards the paperless work, so this project is a step ahead toward this goal. The project will provide easiness to university’s students and faculty members. As the Educational, institutes are increasing day by day in Pakistan, so this project can provide facilities to all the people that are involved in the FYP’s process comprising a huge scope. Project will consist of the following modules:

heading: 1. Register ideas:
content: Supervisor will float their ideas by first logging into the system by using their username and password. After log in, they will have to fill a form which will include the details of the idea such as title, group members allowed, innovation in the idea, skills that will be required etc. which can be viewed later by the Students.

heading: 2. Supervisor Assignment:
content: When an idea floated by a supervisor inspires a Student, he/she can send request to that Supervisor depending upon the status of the project that whether it is available to be taken or is already taken by another group. When the Supervisor will get the request from a Student who is representing his/her group, the Supervisor has the authority to accept or reject it. Page 12 of 89

heading: 3. Grade Entry:
content: Grading system will be automated, marks will be automatically calculated by assessment reports filled by internals and externals.

heading: 4. Report Generation:
content: By using the portal, the FYP Committee can view different reports that are related to the project. For example, the Committee can view the list of the Students who have cleared the phase 1(Report -I) of their project. Similarly, they can also view the number of A’s given by any supervisor.

heading: 5. Search Record:
content: Supervisor and the FYP Committee is able to view the details of the Projects and students.

heading: 6. Reports Submissions and evaluations:
content: Reports will be submitted and evaluated online that will reduce the workload of students as well as members. Page 13 of 89

heading: 2.1.1 MMU FYP Portal:
content: MMU (University Multimedia Malaysia)  [1] provides an FYP management portal that is maintained by FET Web Applications Development Committee (FET-WADC). It contains the section where announcements and updates are made so that the students taking the final year project can view and can get guideline. Students can also get all the forms and sample that needs to be submitted. Portal also allows the students to view the information of the academic and supporting staff. Students can also provide feedback to the technical team of the website through email.  MMU portal also allow the student to check for the lecturer’s details before taking him/her as supervisor.

heading: 2.1.2 UTAR’S FYP Portal
content: UTAR (Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman) [2] have their own uniqueness in their user interface design and the arrangements of the elements in their Final year project management portal. It also contains an announcement section where all the announcements are made. Portal also allows the students to submit their Project Report. This portal also contains the FYP Equipment page using which; Final year students can view the images of equipment that the students can borrow for research purposes. One of the important features of the portal is the guideline, which will guide the students throughout the process.

heading: 2.1.3 FYP Online System
content: Final Year Project (FYP) Online System  [3] project is a step ahead to help the usage of Outcome Based Education (OBE). OBE has turned into a model for learning condition and educational modules outline for the educational structure. This project is supporting the OBE keeping in mind the end goal to make a straightforward and target assessment of every student, which is serious to present constant quality change (CQI) as ordered by Engineering Accreditation Council (EAC) in Malaysia. By using such a system, the FYP Administration will become more efficient and powerful. Technologies that were used for the development of this system was Apache Web Server, MySQL for the database handling, PHP for server-side scripting and JavaScript framework.

heading: 2.1.4 Project Management System
content: Project Management System (PMS) [4] is a system to come out of the traditional ways of dealing with the FYP’s and has converted these activities into an automated process, which is automatically managing, controlling and monitoring the projects of students. Individuals include in this system are students, project coordinator and project guide. Students and project guide can login to the system. After login, Students can form their group on their own and can choose their domain based on which system will assign them the project guide. Project guide and Coordinator can also communicate with each other. Project Coordinator Page 14 of 89 assign different tasks to the students and the progress chart of the group is created based on their performance, which decides the marks of the particular group.

heading: 2.1.5 Final Year Project Management System
content: Final Year Project Management System [5] is a facility and a platform where students can display the knowledge and technical skills, which they have learned. It is a web-based portal along with the Student, Supervisor and Head of Department (HOD) authentication -using login and password. HOD can make groups of students, assign supervisor to them. Students on the other hand can add the project information on the portal, which can then be submitted to the HOD for evaluation. Students can also check the tasks that are assigned to them by the HOD. Supervisor can check the status and progress of the tasks assigned to the students. Supervisor can also make comments and can ask for the resubmission if required by using this portal.

heading: 2.1.6 Final Year Supervision Management System
content: Final Year Supervision Management System  [6] is playing an important role in planning, design and development of the FYP of students. The traditional method in scheduling the project takes up a lot of time especially when a supervisor is supervising more than 10 students at the same time. Generally,  this process includes 3 parties’ students, supervisor and the HOD. System is consisting of 3 modules. Appointment module arranges the time for meeting between the supervisor and the student, which are to be decided by the supervisor. Student and supervisor Profile module contain the personal, academic and other information of both the Student and supervisor. Third module is the Schedule monitoring module, which is responsible for monitoring the project, and for detecting whether a project is delayed or not.

heading: 2.1.7 Final Year Project Management System
content: Final Year Project Management System  [7] tries to build up an online stage, which make promote the last year projects (FYP) implemented. The entire FYP is a yearlong process including gatherings of groups and their supervisor to complete specific tasks that will lead them to the project completion. It is extremely important to use the most recent innovations keeping in mind the end goal to enable diverse gatherings to contribute and convey to become more productive. In addition, they can share assets about the project including source code and in formation documents. This platform is built up to better help the three sorts of clients; they are the FYP program coordinator (PO), project supervisor and the group members. Students can set their preferences, group, and Project Co -Ordinator can make evaluate and mark the submissions of the student through the submission and grading module. Project Supervisor on the other hand can view the progress of the project. Group members can also communicate with each other using this portal. Page 15 of 89

heading: 2.1.8 Student Project Performance Management System
content: Student Project Performance Management System  [8] is an e -supervision structure constitutes an effort to join the communication and the procedure between every single included group in a last year and thesis venture. Student is responsible for carrying out the project and the supervisor is responsible for guiding motivating, monitoring and advising the student according to the supervisor instructions. The examiner is the person who assess the student’s work that he/she will submit on the portal. The administrators are a team of persons who will be responsible to give instructions to the student about what to do. System also includes Project Database contains all projects proposed, Supervisory Database which contain the list of all the supervisors. System also contain a Performance Management Plan in which milestones, tasks, goals, and their expected deliverables are defined.

heading: 6 Chapter 6: Conclusion
content: The aim of this project is to broaden the student’s knowledge and give them a chance to enhance their skills according to the market trend. FYP’s have to go through many phases from submission to till end. In the earlier stages students picks up the idea and after discussion with their supervisor they choose to implement this idea. They write proposals for the selected project and submit their proposals. It will be a web-based portal on which students can communicate with their supervisors. Students can update their project details on the portal that can be evaluated by the supervisor and the FYP Committee. In the beginning of the project we try to rush towards the development instead of defining requirement clea rly. We learned from our experience that we should give a plenty of time to requirement gathering and analysis phase. With proper Requirement specifications, implementation becomes easy. The first problem that we have to face is the scope of the project because each faculty member has its own assumptions so defining the scope of the project was difficult and we try to accommodate all members and stakeholders. In our web course, we were only taught very basics of the Laravel framework and the features that we have planned for the portal requires an advance knowledge of the framework for which we will have to work day and night in order to learn that advance knowledge to make our project successful. We have to work day and night to complete this report and we try to make it better because our project has many features. In our diagrams we have included the main features of our project neglecting features that were common. We did not have sufficient skills so that some times during our development when an error occurs it took plenty of time to understand and removing it. So, these were some problems that were faced but for us these problems were challenges from which we have learnt so much skills and experience. As we know that, the scope of such a project can be expanded as much as we want. Since we have a very limited time, so for the time being we are only able to implement few of its functionalities but in the near future we have planned to apply the following advancements in our project: • Suggestion of ideas according to the interest of students. • Student can sale their projects. • Applying Portal to other universities. • Assignment of tasks from supervisor to students and keeping their track. heading: Abstract
content: Toddlers nowadays know how to use tablets and Smartphone, sometime even better than their parents. This gives us an opportunity to use the same medium for learning and move with the modern times, the old methods of learning through blocks and shapes for counting are already obsolete. And the teachers in school cannot give their absolute attention to each student. So, we intend to develop an android based Teacher for Numbers and Counting. This application will facilitate learning of numbers and basic count ing in terms of speaking, writing and listening. More specifically, it will teach children how to write numbers using tracing on the screen, we will research on the activities used for learning and create a digital form similar to those for teaching purpos es. And games similar to push the button on the book to speak the number will start the learning process for the youngest. Activities will be divided in levels and arranged in a format such that each level of activity will teach something new. The app will  have an interactive colourful screen that looks appealing to children. This way toddler can be kept busy in a productive way.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Toddlers nowadays know how to use tablets and smart phones to play games and for other entertainment. The blocks and toys for learning are not very ef fective because they don’t give any kind of feedback and the numbers and objects printed on them are not very helpful. They don’t get much attention in school as well because of the sheer number of students in a class and it’s not possible for a teacher to  give hundred percent attentions to every student. They have a very short attention span and they don’t have fine motoring skills to write correctly. So, we decided to create a learning application that can provide some basic learning in a fun way using th e same medium (i.e. tablets and smart phones). It will help toddlers learn numbers, develop motoring skills that will help them to read and write correctly. They will learn numbers and counting through our app. The Title of the project is “Numbers for Todd lers”. It will be an android based application. It will have a user interface that is easy to use for the kids and has basic menu. There will be 3 main functions that are listening, speaking and tracing for numbers. And some basic activities like number puzzle etc. Our application will provide listening and speaking functionality that will help in learning numbers by repeating what the voice from the system said. The tracing feature will first provide an outline so that kids can learn the proper shapes of these numbers and then help learn numbers by writing what the voice in the system said. We will provide a course to learn numbers in the best way possible. The course will start with learning numbers through listening then it will continue with teaching sp eaking numbers and writing them. It will also teach c hildren the sequence of numbers . All of these activities will be created by researching on the methods and activities used to teach children at home and in schools. Then the activities that are most effe ctive will be used and made into digital forms to teach children through our application. The main activities explained in detail:

heading: 1.1.1 Listening
content: Listening will start the learning process. It will teach numbers through visual and auditory feedback. The user will be able to interact with some buttons, that when pressed will show the user a simulation by writing the number on the screen. And  it will pronounce the numbers which is pressed.

heading: 1.1.2 Speaking
content: Speaking will be the second step in teaching, it will unlock after the user has completed the listening levels. Here the user will be asked to repeat the numbers as pronounced by the computer. This audio feedback by the user will be listened by the system through a microphone. This will be analysed and the user will be gi ven feedback on whether the pronunciation is correct or not.

heading: 1.1.3 Writing
content: Writing will be the next step in teaching, it will unlock after the user has completed from speaking. Here the user will be asked to trace the number that is shown on the screen. The system will show a simulation of tracing the number to show the user how to do it. Then the user will repeat the action by tracing and get feedback on whether the number is written correctly or not.

heading: 1.2 Goals and Objectives
content: Main objective of this application is te aching numbers and counting. Help kids learn by using voice recognition of numbers, tracing numbers to learn how to write correctly and counting numbers using some activities like matching pictures and counting apples etc. Another major objective is to keep this application kid friendly and fun so that kids find it fun to learn. The goals and objectives of our project are following: ● Teach Numbers and Counting. ● Voice recognition of Numbers. ● Tracing Numbers. ● Activities to help kids learn numbers. ● Poem and puzzle

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: Kids in this era know how to use tablets and Smartphone, sometime even better than their parents. This gives us an opportunity to use the same medium for learning and move with the modern times, the old methods of learning through blocks and shapes for counting are already obsolete. And the teachers in school cannot give their absolute attention to each student. So, we intend to develop an android based Teacher for Numbers and Counting. This application will facilitate learning of numb ers and basic counting in terms of speaking, writing and listening.

heading: 1.4 Assumption and constraint
content:  Assume that our user has an internet access to use our services.  It runs only on android smart phones.  Application can only run on lollipop version or greater than lollipop.  Microphone should be working to take user input.

heading: 1.5 Motivation and scope
content: Children use tablets and mobile phones to do unproductive thing for an unhealthy amount of time. And parents allow them because they are busy doing something and don’t bo ther them after parents come home from their jobs. We decided to use this unproductive use into something productive where kids can learn and be productive. This way they can be playing on these smart devices and learning at the same time. So, we wanted to  seize this opportunity and create an app  that can teach children while they are playing. The application is able to teach reading and speaking through voice recognition and feedback. Also teach writing and develop motoring through tracing. It will be deve loped for toddler age group. The scope of the application will be to teach children reading, speaking and writing numbers and then learns sequence of number. All of this is done after doing research on activities used for teach toddler basic numbers and c ounting and creating similar activities in digital form to teach the same thing.

Software testing is a process that establishes correctness, comprehensiveness, quality and verification of developed computer software. It consists of a set of activities performed with the purpose of making it “defect free”, so that a defect free product is released for the end user. heading: Integration Testing:

heading: System Testing:
content: It is a stage of testing which is carried out by a p rofessional testing agent before the product is released to the market.

heading: Acceptance Testing:
content: Testing done by the actual end users of the product developed.

heading: 4.4 Acceptance Testing:

The user will check the quality of the application and how much it is completed to their desires and expectation. A user friendly application satisfies user and their needs too.
