heading: Abstract
content: Human brain has a very complex structure and understanding this complexity demands high level of skills. Different imaging modalities are being used to identify irregularities in the b rain and MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) is one of them. Radiologists view the MR Images and generate the reports accordingly. But due to the large amount of generated MRI’s, it has been incommodious for radiologists to write the reports promptly. And eff ect of this delay can be catastrophic to the patient’s health. To avoid this, we proposed to develop a semi -automated tool that will take the MR i mages and segment out the tumor d part upon the identification of ROI (Region of Interest). The actual purpose of developing such a tool is to assist radiologists in the analysis of MRI’s and serve for humanity. During the field research we had visited dif ferent MRI centres in Lahore and inquired about their procedure. Private and public centres has their differenc es in giving dates and the rates. S ome of the MRI centres provide reports after 2 to 3 days or some even after a week. Analysing the MR Images were time taking and this is what we have focussed i.e. to provide with a helping tool that will ultimately speedup this process and patients can get their reports earlier. Table of Contents

heading: 1.1 Tumor detection in Brain
content: Tumor is an abnormal growth of tissue t hat form lumps and cause swelling. It is a generic term for group of diseases. Tumors can be non -cancerous also known as benign tumors; they don’t affect their surrounding tissues and stay at the place of their origin. Cancer causing tumors are also known as malignant tumors; they affect the surrounding tissues. Due to its invasive nature, every cancer is not curable which makes it the second leading cause of death worldwide. Hence it’s the need of hour to diagnose and cure such harmful disease. So far doct ors have identified more than 100 types of cancer  [1]. Each tumor vary in its nature, symptoms and cure depending upon its area of origin which leads to multiple type of cancer like blood cancer, lung cancer, skin cancer, brain cancer and many more.

heading: 1.2 Brain (the command centre)
content: Human brain is the most important part of the body. Its complex anatomical structure controls everything that goes on in the human body. From a single mood swing to nervous break, everything is controlled f rom this command centre. Millions of neurons communicate with each other and make it possible for us to perform our daily tasks  [2]. Understanding the working of human brain is not a child’s play. It requires experience and tremendous amount of knowledge to understand its working. Different Imaging Modalities are being used to identify any irregular behaviour. MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) is one of those modalities.

heading: 1.3 Why MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging)
content: CT (Computer Tomogr aphy) and MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) are the most commonly used modalities for brain imaging. CT scan uses x -rays to get internal details of human brain while MRI uses magnetic field and radio waves. MRI being comparatively the latest technology is s afer and has no effects on human body while in CT scans, exposure to x -rays has adverse effects on human body. MRI uses body’s natural magnetic properties to produce detailed images from any part of the body [3].  When a strong varying magnetic field is passed through the human body, the hydrogen nuclei in the body create a nuclear magnetic resonance which is detected by the MRI scanner. Nuclei of different tissues resonate with different frequencies and these frequencies are used to image different parts of the body.

heading: 1.4 Objectives
content:  To assist the radiologists in the analysis of MR images.  Help the patients in getting MRI reports earlier.  Allow the novice users to use this tool without putting extra effort.  Help in controlling the brain tumors.

heading: 1.5 Problem Statement
content: Cancer has been the leading cause of death and in 2015, 8.8 million people died worldwide which is nearly 1 in 6 of all global deaths [4]. Most of deaths are due to the procrastinating behaviour of the patients because of the complications of the check-up. The hour of the need is to simplify this process and help the patients in getting the required treatment with as little effort as possible. The development of this tool will surely help the radiologists but it will strong the bond between them and the patients. We will upload the demos on the platforms just to show them how quickly we can detect the tumor and the MRI report can be generated. They will not be required to wait for days and weeks to ge t their reports. If the radio logist is available at the cent re, they can get it within hours or a day.

heading: 1.6 Assumptions & constraints
content: Being semi-automated tool, the tool is required to be handled by someone who has some know how about the shape of tumor and di fference between various MRI sequences in order to select the ROI correctly. The data sets obtained from multiple sources are being used to test and improve the efficiency of this tools.

heading: 1.7 Project scope
content: While working on this project, we had a chance to visi t different radiology centres and see their working. No radiology centre generates the MRI report the same day because after taking the MRI, scans are sent to the radiologists who already have a lot to deal with and the scans just get pile up. Analysis of the scan is the most critical and time consuming part. The development of this tool will help the radiologist to speed -up that process. Multiple images can be fed to our tool and it will highlight the tumord part from all of the fed scans.

heading: 2.1 Introduction
content: Many segmentation techniques are available at this time. Technology is swiftly shifting towards automation. We have presented a semi-automated tool but will pursue it in future and develop the fully automated version. Following is a descript ion of segmentation techniques that were explored.

heading: 2.1.1 Thresholding
content: The technique is based on getting a binary image from a grey scale image. It is the simplest and frequently used technique for discriminating foreground from background. After segmentation, the object can be extracted using edge detection techniques.  [5]

heading: 2.1.2 Fuzzy c means clustering
content: According to a study [6], this technique is quite useful in boating regions more homogeneous than those of other methods. Moreover, it reduces spurious blobs and noisy spots. It works for both single and multiple feature data with spatial information.

heading: 2.1.3 Watershed segmentation
content: The study [7] showed that watershed is one of the best methods to group pixels of an image on the basis of their intensities.

heading: 2.1.4 K means clustering
content: K means clustering is one of the simplest un-supervised learning algorithm which is used to solve the clustering problems. Number of clusters are fixed initial ly. The block diagram is shown  in figure-1. [5] Figure 1.  Block Diagram of K-means clustering

heading: 2.1.5 Histogram Based Methods
content: Histogram is computed and the peaks and valleys in histogram are used to locate the clusters.  It is an efficient method of image segmentation as it requires only one pass through the pixels. [8]

heading: 2.1.6 K means clustering and improved Watershed technique
content: According to another study  [9] , simple watershed has the drawback of over segmentation and noise. This approach uses automated thresholding on the gradient magnitude map and post - segmentation merging on the initial partitions to reduce the number of false edges and over - segmentation.

heading: 2.1.7 Seeded Region Growing Method
content: Automated and semi-automated tools usually make use of this technique. A seed point is selected according to some criteria and region growing starts from that point. In our study, we have used combinations of various texture features and proceeded with the work. Following are some of the texture features that we have explored.

heading: 2.1.7.1 Co-occurrence
content: The Variance is a measure of the histogram width that measures the deviation of gray levels from the Mean. Skewness is a measure of the degree of histogram asymmetry around the Mean and Kurtosis is a measure of the histogram sharpness.  These features generated from first order statistics does not provide any information about the relative positions of gray levels within an image. Rather, they just provide information about the distribution of gray levels in the image. This is where Co-occurrence matrix comes with its properties. It can tell if all the gray levels are positioned together or inter -changed with high -value gray levels The co-occurrence matrix is a function of two parameters: relative distance measured in pixel numbers (d) and their relative orientation θ. The orientation θ is quantized in four directions that represent horizontal, diagonal, vertical and anti-diagonal by 0˚, 45˚, 90˚ and 135˚ respectively.

heading: 2.1.7.2 GLCM
content: Gray Level co -occurrence matrix considers the spatial relationship of pixels, i.e. how o ften different combinations of gray levels co -occur in an image . This co-occurrence can be measured in different directions (                      ) with different displacements (d=1 by default i.e. the neighboring pixel) . The number of gray levels det ermine the size of GLCM.  The calculation technique is shown in figure-2. Figure 2. GLCM calculation  [10]

heading: 2.1.7.3 Properties of glcm
content:  It is square: reference pixel has same range of values as the neighbor pixel.  Has the same number of rows and columns as the quantization level of the image.  Symmetrical about diagonal.

heading: 2.1.7.4 Spatial relationship between two pixels
content: GLCM texture considers the relation between two pixels at a time, called the reference and the neighbour pixel.  Window size

heading:  Displacement
content: Tuning these three parameters according to the given scenario affects the results.  Window size possibly influence the resultant texture features due to the amount of variance included. Large window size migh t not get all the textures due to the over - smoothing.  The orientation parallel to the look direction of the sensor will give more accurate results.  Displacement determines the distribution of factor in GLCM. If it is >1, this leads to reflect the degree of correlation between distant pixels.

heading: 2.1.7.5 Features calculated from glcm
content: Following are some of the features that were used in this research.

heading: 2.1.7.5.1 Homogeneity
content: Lack of variability or amount of local similarity. High homogeneity values suggest small gray tones differences in pair elements

heading: 2.1.7.5.2 Contrast
content: It is measure of the amount of local variation in pixel values among neighboring pixels. It is high for regions exhibiting large local variations

heading: 2.1.7.5.3 Entropy
content: Entropy is large when image is heterogeneous.

heading: 2.1.7.5.4 Variance
content: Variance is high when there is large standard deviation of gray levels in local regions

heading: 2.1.7.5.5 ASM and Uniformity
content: Are measure of texture uniformity and pixel pair repetition respectively. They are high when GLCM is locally homogeneous

heading: 2.1.7.5.6 Correlation
content: It is a measure of gray level linear dependencies in the image. High COR means a linear relationship between gray levels of pixels.

heading: 2.1.7.6 Local Binary Pattern
content: Local Binary Pattern is a neighborhood based texture operator which labels the pixels of an image by thresholding the neighborhood of each pixel and considers the result as a binary number. [11]

content: 1. Dividing the image into a 3x3 window. 2. Using a 3x3 window skimming through the whole image finding a binary pattern for each center pixel of the window. 3. Every time compare the centre pixel of the window with its 8 neighborhood pixel and assign 1 and 0 to 8 neighborhood pixels accordingly i.e if  center pixel value > neighborhood pixel value a. assign 1 else  0 4. heading: 2.1.7.6.2 Advantages
content:  High discriminative power  Computational simplicity  Invariance to greyscale changes  Good performance [12]

heading: 2.1.7.6.3 Disadvantages
content:  Not invariant to rotations.  Size of features increases exponentially with the number of neighbors which lead s to an increase of computational complexity in terms of space and time.  Structural information is limited as only pixel difference is used, magnitude is ignored. [12]

heading: 3.3.2 Data pre-processing (Binning)
content: Binning is applied to remove minor errors in observations. There are three binning strategies  [15] linear, non-linear and clipped. We have adopted  clipped binning in which lower gray levels are assigned one bin and higher gray levels are also assigned a single bin. All other gray levels are accumulated in bins of ‘n’ numbers (30 in our case). Low intensity gray levels are mostly background pixels. The low intensity gray level I 1 is set to be the value of first valley, as pixels with gray levels from 0 to it are mostly background pixels. The high intensity gray level I 2 is chosen as the first one with very few pixels, as these pixels are trivial.

heading: 3.3.3 Data Processing
content: After pre-processing of data, it is send to for the actual processing where different texture features were calculated for the segmentation of the tumor.

heading: 3.3.4 GLCM
content: GLCM for every pixel in ROI was formed and then following features were calculated for every pixel.

heading: 3.3.5 Haralick Feature
content: 14 haralick features were calculated from the Gray level co-occurrence matrix calculated for each pixel in the ROI.

heading: 3.3.6 Semi-variogram
content: Semi-variogram is used to extra ct textural features using spatial auto -correlation function. Measures of spatial autocor relation describe the degree to  which observations (values) at spatial locations (whether they are points, areas, or raster cells), are similar to each other. So we ne ed two things: observations and locations. Semi-variogram in all directions were calculated for every pixel of ROI then mean, standard deviation and sum of perpendicular ratios were calculated and added in the feature matrix.

heading: 3.3.7 Distance Measure
content: Distance measured:  Distance of each pixel of ROI from center in spatial domain.  Distance of each pixel from centroid of ROI in feature space.  Sum of distances of each pixel from its neighbours in feature space. Following distance calculations techniques were explored in our research:

heading: 3.3.7.1 Mahalanobis Based Distance Metrics
content: These distance metrics are applied after transforming the vectors (among whom the distance is to be measured) from image space to Mahalanobis space. Mahalanobis space is a space where the sample variance along each dimension is unity. The transformation from image space to Mahalanobis space is achieved by dividing each Co-efficient in the vector by its corresponding standard deviation. This yields a dimensionless feature space with unit variance in each dimension. The Mahalanobis distance measures distance relative to the centroid — a base or central point which can be thought of as an overall mean for multivariate data. The centroid is a point in multivariate space where all means from all variables inter sect. The larger the MD, the further away from the centroid the data point is. [16]

heading: 3.3.7.1.4 Uses
content: The most common use for the Mahalanobis distance is to find multivariate  outliers, which indicates unusual combinations of two or more variables. For example, it’s fairly common to f ind a 6′ tall woman weighing 185 lbs, but it’s rare to find a 4′ tall woman who weighs that much. However, suppose that the contour lines of a probability distribution function (p.d.f.), which is not normal, is given as in Figure-13 It is natural to evaluate the distance not along a straight line but along a curve. In order to realize such a distance, the Mahalanobis metric was proposed. [17]

A major issue with the MD is that the inverse of the correlation matrix is needed for the calculations. This can’t be calculated if the variables are highly correlated (Varmuza & Filzmoser, 2016).

Different imaging modalities are being used to identify irregularities in the brain  and MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) is one of them. Radiologists view the MR Images and generate the reports accordingly. But due to the large amount of generated MRI’s, it has been incommodious for radiologists to write the reports promptly. And effect of this delay can be catastrophic to the patient’s health. To avoid this, we proposed to develop a semi -automated tool that will take the MR images and segment out the tumord part upon the identification of ROI (Region of Interest). The actual purpose of developing such a tool is to assist radiologists in the analysis of MRI’s and serve for humanity. During the field research we had visited different MRI centres in Lahore and inquired about their procedure. Private and public centres has their differences in giving dates and the rates. Some of the MRI centres provide reports after 2 to 3 days or some even after a week. Analysing the MR Images were time taking and this is what we have focussed i.e. to provide with a helping tool that will ultimately speedup this process and patients can get their reports earlier. Chapter 1 I ntroduction 1.1 Tumor detection in Brain Tumor is an abnormal  growth of tissue  that form lumps and cause swelling. It is a generic term for group of diseases. Tumors can be non -cancerous also known as benign tumors; they don’t affect their surrounding tissues and stay at the place of their origin. Cancer causing tumors are also known  as malignant tumors; they affect the surrounding tissues. Due to its invasive nature, every cancer is not curable which makes it the second leading cause of death worldwide. Hence it’s the need of hour to diagnose and cure such harmful disease. So far doc tors have identified more than 100 types of cancer [1]. Each tumor vary in its nature, symptoms and cure depending upon its area of origin which leads to multiple type of cancer like blood cancer, lung cancer, skin cancer, brain cancer and many more. 1.2 B rain (the command centre) Human brain is the most  important part of the body. Its complex anatomical structure controls everything that goes on in the human body. From a single mood swing to nervous break, everything is controlled from this command centre. Millions of neurons communicate with each other and make it possible for us to perform ou r daily tasks [2]. Understanding the working of human brain is not a child’s play. It requires experience and tremendous amount of knowledge to understand its working. Different Imaging Modalities are being used to identify any irregular behaviour. MRI (Ma gnetic Resonance Imaging) is one of those modalities 1.3 Why MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) CT (Computer Tomography) and MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) are  the most commonly used modalities for brain imaging. CT scan uses x-rays to get internal details of human brain while MRI uses magnetic field and radio waves. MRI being comparatively the latest technology is safer and has no effects on human body while in CT scans, exposure to x-rays has adverse effects on huma n body. MRI uses body’s natural magnetic properties to produce detailed images from any part of the body  [3]. When a strong varying magnetic field is passed through the human body, the hydrogen nuclei in the body create a nuclear magnetic resonance which is detected by the MRI scanner. Nuclei of different tissues resonate with d ifferent frequencies and these frequencies are used to image different parts of the body. 1.4 Objectives ? To assist the radiologists in the analysis of MR images. ? Help the patients in getting MRI reports earlier. ? Allow the novice users to use this too l without putting extra effort. ? Help in controlling the brain tumors. 1.5 Problem Statement Cancer has been the leading cause of death and in 2015, 8.8 million people died worldwide which is nearly 1 in 6 of all global deaths [4]. Most of deaths are due to the procrastinating behaviour of the patients because of the complications of the check -up. The hour of the need is to simplify this process and help the patients in getting the required treatment with as little effort as possible. The development of th is tool will surely help the radiologists but it will strong the bond between them and the patients. We will upload the demos on the platforms just to show them how quickly we can detect the tumor and the MRI report can be generated. They will not be requi red to wait for days and weeks to get their reports. If the radiologist is available at the centre, they can get it within hours or a day. 1.6 Assumptions & constraints Being semi -automated tool, the tool is required to be handled by someone who has some k now how about the shape of tumor and difference between various MRI sequences in order to select the ROI correctly. The data sets obtained from multiple sources are being used to test and improve the efficiency of this tools. 1.7 Project scope While workin g on this project, we had a chance to visit different radiology centres and see their working. No radiology centre generates the MRI report the same day because after taking the MRI, scans are sent to the radiologists who already have a lot to deal with an d the scans just get pile up. Analysis of the scan is the most critical and time consuming part. The development of this tool will help the radiologist to speed -up that process. Multiple images can be fed to our tool and it will highlight the tumord part f rom all of the fed scans. 1.8 Thesis Outline Our dissertation contain following chapters: Chapter 2 (Literature Review) Various techniques are available for the effective segmentation of the tumor. This chapter focusses on some of the frequently used techniques as well as detailed description of the adopted technique which is seeded region growing. Chapter 3 (Extant works) This chapter encompasses the workflow and the detailed description of every step of the followed methodology. From the collection of data  set to its pre-processing and then the processing of the data, every step has been highlighted and explained for the sake of understanding. Chapter 4 (System Design) This chapter is wr itten to show the system design. How the structure was break down and how the data flows. It includes the sequence of operations that can be performed. Data flow diagrams for specific operations as well as the complete work breakdown structure has been shown. Chapter 5 (System Testing) Testing can be done in many ways; this chapter presents some of them through which we have checked our system. Results are only being validated when goal is achieved along with having the same accuracy as of human’s judgement result. Chapter 6 (Conclusion) A project is not the effort of days or weeks. It is the effort of months. From the selection of the project to the successful completion, we had many obstacles in the way and not having a research experience was the biggest problem. Some of our hardships has been discussed in this chapter. Chapter 7 (Program Code) This chapter includes the source code of the Main function. The workflow of the code can be seen in this chapter. From taking an input image to region growing. Chap ter 8 (Results) Results have been shown in this chapter and are briefly described. 2 Chapter Literature Review 2.1 Introduction Many segmentation techniques are available at this time. Technology is swiftly shifting towards automation. We have presented a semi-automated tool but will pursue it in future and develop the fully automated version. Following is a description of segmentation techniques that were explored. 2.1.1 Thresholding The technique is based on getting a binary image from a  grey scale image. It is the  simplest and frequently used technique for discriminating foreground from background. After segmentation, the object can be extracted using edge detection techniques. [5] 2. 1.2 Fuzzy c means clustering According to a study [6], this technique is quite useful in boating regions more homogeneous than those of other methods.  Moreover, it reduces spurious blobs  and noisy spots. It works for both single and multiple feature data with spa tial information  2.1.3 Watershed segmentation The study [7] showed that watershed is one of the best methods to group pixels of an image on the basis of their intensities.  2.1.4 K means clustering K means  clustering is one of the  simplest un -supervised learning algorithm  which is used to solve the clustering problems. Number of clusters are fixed initially. The block diagram is shown in figure-1. [5] Figure 1. Block Diagram of  K-means c lustering 2.1.5 Histogram Based Methods Histogram is computed and the peaks and valleys in histogram are used to locate the clusters.  It is an efficient method of image segmentation as it requires only one pass through the pixels. [8] 2.1.6 K means clustering and improved Watershed  technique According to another study [9] , simple watershed has the drawback of over segmen tation and noise. This approach uses automated thresholding on the gradient magnitude map and post - segmentation merging on the initial partitions to reduce the number of false edges and over- segmentation. 2.1.7 Seeded Region Growing Method Automated and semi -automated tools usually make use of this technique. A seed point is selected according to some criteria and region growing starts from that point. In our study, we have used combinations of various texture features and proceeded with the work. Fol lowing are some of the texture features that we have explored. 2.1.7.1 Co -occurrence The Variance is a measure of the histogram width that measures the deviation of gray levels from the Mean. Skewness is a measure of the degree of  histogram asymmetry around the Mean and Kurtosis is a measure of the histogram sharpness.  These features generated from first order statistics  does not provide any information about the relative positions of gray levels within  an image. Rather, they just provide information about the distribution of gray levels in the image.  This is where Co-occurrence matrix  comes with its properties. It can tell if all the gray levels are positioned together or  inter-changed with high-value gray levels  The co-occurrence matrix is a function of two parameters: relative distance measured in pixel numbers (d) and their relative orientation θ. The orientation θ is quantized in four directions that represent horizontal, diagonal, vertical and anti -diagonal by 0˚, 45˚, 90˚ and 135˚ respectively.  2.1.7.2 GLCM Gray Level co -occurrence matrix considers the spatial relationship of pixels,  i.e. how often different combinations of gray levels co-occur in an image. This co-occurrence can be measured in different directions (   = 0°, 45°, 90°     135° ) with different displacements (d=1 by default i.e. the neighboring pixel). The number of gray levels determine the size of GLCM. The calculation technique is shown in figure-2. Figure 2. GLCM calculation [10] 2 .1.7. 3 Properties of glcm ? It is square: reference  pixel has same range of values as the neighbor  pixel. ? Has thesame number of rows and columns as the quantization level of the image. ? Symmetrical  about diagonal. 2.1.7.4 Spatial relationship between two pixels GLCM texture considers the relation between two pixels  at a time, called the reference and the neighbour pixel.  ? Window size ? Orientation ? Displacement Tuning these three parameters according to the given scena rio affects the results. ? Window size possibly influence the resultant texture features due to the amount of variance included.  Large window size might not get all the textures due to the over -smoothing. ? The orientation parallel to the look d irection of the sensor  will give more accurate results. ? Displacement determines the distribution of factor in GLCM. If it is >1, this leads to reflect the degree of correlation between distant pixels. 2.1.7.5 Features calculated from glcm Following are some of the features that were used in this research. 2.1.7.5.1 Homogeneity Lack of variability or amount of local similarity. High  homogeneity values suggest small gray  tones differences in pair elements  2.1.7.5.2 Contrast It is measure of the amount of local variation in  pixel values among neighboring pixels. It is high for regions exhibiting large local variations 2.1.7.5.3 Entropy Entropy is large when image is heterogeneous.

heading: 2.1.7.5.4 Variance Variance is high when there is large standard
content: deviation of  gray levels in local  regions 2.1.7.5.5 ASM and Uniformity Are measure of texture uniformity and pixel pair repetition respectively. They are high when GLCM is locally  homogeneous 2.1.7.5.6 Correlation It is a measure of gray level linear dependencies in the im age. High COR means a linear relationship between gray levels of  pixels 2.1.7.6 Local Binary Pattern Local Binary Pattern is a  neighborhood based texture operator which labels the pixels of an image by thresholding the neighborhood of each pixel and considers the result as a binary number. [11] 2.1.7.6.1 Algorithm 1. Dividing the image into a  3x3 window. 2. Using a 3x3 window skimming through the whole image finding a binary pattern for each center pixel of the window. 3. Every time compare the centre pixel of the window with its 8 neighborhood pixel and assign 1 and 0 to 8 neighborhood pixels accordingly i.e if center pixel va lue > neighborhood pixel value a. assign 1 else 0 4. When all neighborhood pixel of the window are assigned binary value then we will create a binary number by following respective preference of LSB and MSB as shown in figure - 3 Figure 3. Binary Number Gen eration 5. Where A is center pixel 6. This 8 bit binary number is then the new value of the center pixel of the window. 7. Repeating the above steps for each pixel of the grey scale image as shown in below (figure -4) ... ..... Figure 4. Getting binary code  for every pixel 2.1.7.6.2 Advantages ? High discriminative power ? Computational simplicity ? Invaria nce to greyscale changes ? Good performance  [12] 2.1.7.6.3 Disadvantages ? Not invariant to rotations. ? Size of features increases exponentially with the number of neighbors which leads to an increase of computational complexity in terms of  space and time. ? Structural information is limited as onlypixel difference is used, magnitude is ignored.  [12]

From the collection of data set to its pre-processing and then the processing of the data, every step h as been highlighted and explained for the sake of understanding. 3.1 Introduction We have discussed the methodology and workflow of our research. How the data set was obtained and what were the difficulties faced. The working start with loading an input image. Pre -processing will be applied and output will be s end to next phase which is calculation of feature matrix. Costs will be calculated and a seed point will be selected for region growing. All the similar pixels will become seed and will be segmented out. And we will get the tumor as segmented region. The workflow is shown in below.Figure -11 Figure. 11 Workflow 3.3.1 Data collection Different data sets were used throughout the research work. Some of them are freely available. We have a data set obtained from Bahawalpur Victoria Hospital (BVH) which was mainl y used in our work. In the beginning, we didn’t have any idea about which data set to use and what is annotated data. After getting guidance from our project supervisor, we followed his instructions and avoid any other inconvenience that might have given u s hard time. 3.3.2 Data pre - processing (Binning) Binning is applied to remove minor errors in observations. There are three binning strategies [15] linear, non -linear and clipped. We have adopted clipped binning in which lower gray levels are assigned one bin and higher gray levels are also assigned a single bin. All other gray levels are accumulated in bins of ‘n’ numbers (30 in our case). Low intensity gray levels are mostly background pixels. The low intensity gray level I1 is set to be the value of first valley, as pixels with gray levels from 0 to it are mostly background pixels. The high intensity gray level I2 is chosen as the first one with very few pixels, as these pixels are tr ivial. 3.3.3 Data Processing After pre -processing of data, it is send to for the actual processing  where different texture features were calculated for the segmentation of the tumor. 3.3.4 GLCM GLCM for every pixel in ROI was formed and then following features were calculated for every pixel. 3.3.5 Haralick Feature 14 haralick features were calculated from the Gray level co-occurrence matrix calculated for each pixel in the ROI. Figure 12. Haralick Features 3.3.6 Semi - variogram Semi -variogram is used to extract textural features using spatial auto -correlation function. Measures of spatial autocorrelation describe the degree  to which observations (values) at spatial locations (whether they are points, areas, or raster cells) , are similar to each other. So we need two things: observations and locations. Distance of each pixel  of ROI from center in spatial domain. ? Distance of each pixel from centroid of ROI in feature space. ? Sum of distances of each pixel from its neighbours in feature space. Following distance calculations techniques were explored in our research: 3.3.7.1 Mahalanobis Based Distance Metrics These distance metrics are applied after transforming the  vectors (among whom the distance is to be measured) from image space to Mahalanobis space. Mahalanobis space is  a space where the sample variance along each dimension is unity. The  transformation from image space to  Mahalanobis space is  achieved by dividing each  Co-efficient in the vector by its corresponding standard deviation. This yields a dimensionless featu re space with unit variance in each dimension. The Mahalanobis distance measures distance relative to the centroid — a base or central point which can be thought of as an overall mean for m ultivariate data. The centroid is a point in multivariate space where all means from all variables intersect. The larger the MD, the further away from the centroid the data point is. For example, it’s fairly common to find a 6′ tall woman weighing 185 lbs, but i t’s rare to find a 4′ tall woman who weighs that much. However, suppose that thecontour lines of a probability distribution function (p.d.f.), which is not normal, is given as in  Figure- 13 It is natural to evaluate the distance not along a straight line but along a curve. heading: Abstract
content: “Student Career Finder” is an android application developed for today’s stude nt in order to guide the student which career option are available for them and in which group of studies matches the student in which he/she can perform better than other. It provide a platform to help them choose their most favorable and successful field s of interests.  Assessment procedures are applied, which will provide better outcome of their fields of interests and will be used in this useful android application. It plays an important role in eradication of the gap between instructor, student and par ents. The student can perform quiz subject wise in end it buildup a scorecard which will be given to the assessment part to analyze and generate pie -chart from it. From pie -chart the student can understand his/her performance in that field. The quiz materi al is picked by research for which we also conduct interviews, study different books related to level of understudies which are being utilized here. The result of this application is that an approved instructor will advise the student by conversation through this android application. The parent will be part of this application by overviewing the result of their children’s. Student career finder

heading: Abstract
content: Our project marks extensions in research works of Software Define Networking. Software Define N etworking is a field of research and development where we work on separating the control plane from the data plane in a network and instill dynamic routing in the network. Through SDN we can achieve remote programmability of a network and achieve much more  robustness in our network. We tried to simulate SDN environment in a virtualized space in a SDN virtualization software called Mininet. We benchmarked different possibilities in the network and devised algorithms to achieve efficiency in network itself. W e are trying to calculate the most efficient ways to implement SDN in networks.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Our developments in this project would result in following objectives being achieved  We would be able to replicate complex dynamic networks with the aid of SDN architecture. That would help us cement the benefits of turning to SDN based networking ideology.  We would be able demonstrate the viability of a state -of-the-art remotely controlled network that would sufficiently fulfill the growing needs of achieving flexibility in the fast pace variable networking environment.  It would allow us to show traffic at different nodes and then show how to direct the flow of traffic to meet user needs.  It would suggest the shortest and the most eff icient path in the network to reach optimum performance in the network and meet consumer needs.  We would be able to extract statistics to make decisions upon.  We would be able to achieve a balanced network, which can adapt to   variable needs in the network.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Our objective is to demonstrate the possibilities of implementing SDN base networks in the mainstream market. We want to show that, how easily can we set up an SDN environment and reap its benefits. We want to show its virtualization capabilities in the simulated environment. With the increasing user expectations, the service providers are facing day by day increasing pressure to keep up with the steep demand of the consumers, with this in mind SDN pr ovide dynamic allocation of resources in the network to provide seamless experience for the users. Our project performs at large bandwidth environments to recreate the scenarios of real life situation, so by replicating those experiences we can correctly measure the scalability of traffic state in the network. We intend to use our project for load balancing and also for providing statistics for the administrator for efficient utilization of resources available in the network. Our project will involve near s elf-awareness of the current traffic situation in the network and we strive to achieve perfect load balancing capabilities in our project.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: User demands have been increasing steeply in these days and service providers are striving to achieve competence in every department to meet their user expectations. Although, the current infrastructure of networks does the job, it lacks robustness and var iety. For example to achieve some dynamic possibilities, one must have to be there at the networking facility to program the situation to control network flows. But With the arrival of SDN architecture, network programmability is not an issue now, it abstr acts the complex infrastructure of the network and gives accessibility as well as business value at the same time. Just by achieving dynamic routing and packet forwarding by this architecture provide a significant amount of financial benefits as compared t o legacy networking infrastructures. Service providers can allocate bandwidths or change the routes of individual packets by using SDN architectures. This solves the ever present problem of complexity and cost posed by the legacy systems.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions & constraints
content:  We must assume that there is a proposed topology present at the moment of the implementation.  We must assume that the switches and controllers being used support Openflow as their underlying standard for communication between the said devices.  A virtualization software is installed on system to check the viability of the proposed topology.  Proper and extensive training of the operator is required, as the technology is new and there isn’t a lot of help available for the operator to cope with the technology as it is intended to be.  We must test these setups on a capable hardware because the simulators used in the projects take lot of resources from the control devices.

heading: 1.5 Project scope (what and what not to consider)
content: As the technology progresses, the need for better means of communication arises. SDN comes to the aid of service providers for providing them with means to cope with the dynamic nature of data transfer. Our project aims to demonstrate the success and viabi lity of implementing SDN architectures on network topologies. It provides statistics to measure the viability and algorithms to find most efficient routes in the network and transfer the traffic on them acting as a dynamic load balancer. What our project d oes not do is that it does not increase or enhances bandwidth of the network. It just balances the load in a way that it is most efficient and financially viable for the user.

heading: 2.1 Literature review / Existing system study
content: The purpose of the project is to implement the shortest path algorithm in a Software -defined Network. It is achieved by setting up our system on virtual machines. Two separate virtual machines are used. One is used to install Mininet while other is used to install OpenDaylight.

heading:  MININET
content: Mininet is our virtual environm ent which is installed on virtual . We use it to create our custom topology. Custom topologies are created in a python script. Python language is used to create the custom topology, in which we can add hosts, switches and controll er. Connections between the elements  can be made as desired. In our topology we have used hosts which are connected with switches and a topology is created.

heading:  OPENDAYLIGHT
content: Opendaylight is our controller which is used to control the Software -Defined Network which we create. Opendaylight is installed in a separate virtual machine. The two virtual are connected over Secure -Shell Protocol (SSH). The network created on Miniedit is then connected with Opendaylight co ntroller by adding a controller in the topology. The controller in the topology is connected with every switch of the network. The IP is configured over both the virtual machines.

heading:  OPENDAYLIGHT UI
content: The Opendaylight User Interface allows a graphical image of  the network. It also views other sorts of information about the network, such as number of hosts in the network and bandwidth of the network. The user interface providing the bird -eye view of the network, one can easily get the idea of the network, the current topology and the flow of traffic between one node to the other. Traffic is generated through the tool Iperf which is also used in this project. Iperf allows us to generate random traffic along the network. This traffic can be used for experimentation  of the network such as bandwidth  utilization and traffic routing.

heading: 5.1  Problems faced, and lessons learned
content: The field of SDN is a bit new at the moment, so there is not much help available for the new developer at the moment. We had difficulties installing features required to operate the controller at its maximum. A lot of the features in the controller are still yet to be explored, but their documentation is so limited that we could not experiment completely on the controller. Learning the complete architecture is a bit difficult at the moment ,but future work might ease up the process of further development in the field.

heading: 5.2 Project summary
content: Advancements in the field of technology has sparked a great question for the service providers and data center owning companies to provide state -of-the-art customer support to their loyal customer-base. As every company is in the race of providing quality services to their consumers, the big question arises at their doorsteps about how to achieve these goal most efficiently. As the legacy infrastructure fails to abstract and simplify the process of networking, it cost companies serious resources to keep the  maintenance of their infrastructures up at all the time. SDN comes to the rescue of these service providers as it provides them with network programmability at lower costs by making the system more robust and remotely controlled. It basically separates th e data plane from the control plane to provide manual manipulation of the traffic at the individual packet level. It keeps the traffic balanced at the most busy times. Our Project demonstrates the viability of SDN on current network topologies and gives st atistics to decide upon the routes that are most efficient for the network flow of traffic. It tries to answer the question of implementing SDN network in the current state of affairs of networking business.

heading: Abstract
content: City Plat is an Android based application with an admin portal that provides the information about locations of hostels and their nearby places like restaurants, ATM’s, and hospitals, especially to the students. It has 2 basic functionalities. One is to help students specifically those are strangers to the city to find out their best suitable hostels near their universities and second is to help Hostel Owners so that they can easily upload their information of hostels and advertise their Hostels in a best way. heading: 1.1 Brief introduction
content: Students from different rural areas are moving to the cities to complete their education but after their migration they could not find the desired place to stay. City Plat, our android application, will help them to find the best suitable hostels for both boys and girls near their educational institutions. Hostel Owners have not any platform to display hostels and their facilities. City Plat, our android application, will help them to make their profiles as Hostel Owners and uploads hostels with in competition of others. By using this application, anyone can give his/her house or property as Hostel for students on rent by uploading required information.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: In this project we exp ect to make a system that enables the students from rural areas to access, search and inquire about the best suitable place for them to stay in the city they are moving  and hostel owners to add their hostels information for advertisement . As of today, we are not aware of a single application that is dealing this problem specifically for students  and hostel owners . Basic objectives to build our application are as follows  To provide an application where Students and Hostel owners have their profiles.  To provide an application where students can search best hostels.  To provide an application where students can Like and reserve their beds or rooms.  To create a contact between Students and Owners through application.  To provide a list of hostels along with their information and locations on map.  To provide hostel owners a platform to display their hostels with facilities.  To provide hostel owners to take part in competition.  To provide hostel owners ability to add or delete or update hostel information at any time.  To provide an application where students can give feedback on hostels.  To provide an application where privacy will not be ignored.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement
content: The hunger of education in the peoples of rural areas is bringing them to cities which can be seen using the merit lists of different educational institutions. They are moving to cities to fulfil the desire to get education. But when they move to the city, due to totally unaware of the local areas, they could not find a proper place, a hostel, to stay which is not far away from their institution and have basic necessities like hospitals, markets, parks near them. Our application will not only provide a list of hostels to students but also the information about its surrounding environment. On the other hand, some students are scared that they will not find place to stay if they move to the city and hence they do not migrate or move to the city. This application will also help them to move to the city and complete their education in a friendly environment. Our project’s aim is to concentrate specifically to those hostels which are not on Google maps. There are many hostels or houses on rent for students but there is no any platform or source to reach these hostels unless anyone near to us belongs to that. And hostel owners also have not any method of advertisement other then banners and pamphlets. On these pamphlets not all information can be provided that our application does so it is a very perfect platform for hostel owners.

heading: Project Description:
content: Our project’s idea reflects the aim to help students which are seeking to move to some other city for the first time and are totally unaware of the place. Besides this, hostel owners can also become a part of this. City Plat is a useful application with an admin portal for students (male/female) and hostel owners. Those students which have travelled from others cities for the first time to get education, it will provide a facility for them to map out all hostels which will suit them best according their educational institution. This application will also show users many other things in the surrounding of their hostels and like hospitals, restaurants, banks and ATM’s in the map so that student can easily decide about their location to stay. Hostel Owners which have hostels but not any platform to display their hostel can easily use this application to upload their information. Hostel owners can also advertise their hotels through this application. If anyone wants to give his/her property on rent to students, he/she make a profile and upload information and become a hostel owner. Admin panel will be used for handling all data on hostels and users.

heading: Boundaries:
content:  Initially limited to one city (Lahore).  The application is only for android operating system users.  This project will only show locations and all information of the hostel that is selected by the us

heading: 2.1 Literature review
content: Around the globe various applications are working and providing hotel related information to the people but none is focusing specifically on students which are new to the city. Some other related applications working around the globe are as follows Youth Hostels in Germany: Itis an android application available on playstore working in Germany.It can find hostels near Germany’s touristic hotspots. User can get information about all accommodations. It also specifies the availability of rooms and dorms. It also provides online booking functionality. User can also get local tips for his/her travel. [1]

heading: Hostel World:
content: Itis another application available on the app store that lets backpackers book a bed, or private room, in any one of over 33,000 hostels around the globe. It allows search by city and date, or use your location to find hostels nearby. View results on an interactive map, or scroll through the pictures. Hostels can be filtered by price and property type, sort by customer rating, name or price. It also allows user to create his/her own travel wish list. [2]

heading: Booking Hotels, Vacation Deals:
content: It is yet another android application available on the app store that helps user search hotels by city, landmark, hotel name or properties close by, in one tap. It shows location on map to make sure your hotel, motel or vacation rental is where you want to be. User can save his/her favorite properties to a list and share with friends and family. User can also make changes to his/her bookings online with the app. [3]

heading: Agoda – Hotel Booking Deals:
content: An android application with useful search filters, hi-res photos, map views, local experience information, and verified traveler reviews help user find the perfect accommodation for specific journey and budget. The app also provides booking facility. It save your booking vouchers to your device and also help you find properties near you. [4] All these applications do not work in Pakistan but are only available within some other countries.

heading: 2.7 Software Development Lifecycle
content: Prototyping model is the most suitable development lifecycle for our project “City Plat” as it does not require much preplanning and also less documentation is needed in this model before development. This model includes step by step development using several prototypes which involves some basic functionality of the system and then the system is shown to the user. Why this particular model is chosen Prototyping has several benefits which are serving us to a great extent, convincing us to use this development cycle. A few of them have been stated below:  Early feedback from users  - The software developers can get feedback (from the users) early in the development lifecycle.  Regular client & contractor meetings  – Using software prototyping, the client and the contractor have regular meetings to compare and recheck whether the soft ware meets the specifications required. In our case, this will allows us to have regular meetings with our evaluator. It will also make it easy for the evaluator to determine the feasibly of our research work.  Stay on track  – When a software prototype is developed iteratively, a software developer gets better insight on what the research would yield and if he is on the right track or not.

heading: Abstract
content: In public dealing places and departments, the people face a lot of hassles for their turn. Some of the people benefit from this situation and some face severe issues. The one who comes late, sometimes, doesn‟t require to wait and he gets his work done earl ier than those who was already there. This situation creates serious conflicts and it becomes difficult for the staff to handle the situation. We faced similar problems in COMSATS student service centre. To resolve this issue in COMSATS student service centre, we introduced an efficient a queue management system. A person entering in student service centre will get a token number by selecting his concern from the token machine placed at the entrance or reserve the token from his android device. He will not require to stand in queue or rush towards the operational windows. He can see the current serving number and wait for his turn. During waiting time, he can do any other task and utilize his time. The serving persons sitting on operational windows will call  the next person after serving the current client. Operators can transfer token from their counter to another if there are another query. The system will make the announcement for the next client by showing token number and window number on counters and LED screen.

heading: 1.1    Introduction
content: The rapid increase in the use of technology from the past few years shows the interest of the people in technological development. Now-a-days everyone doesn‟t afford to waste his time and prefers to use technology where it is possible or available. The people shows their interest in automated systems. Most of the automated systems have been developed to map the daily life tasks on systems. These systems solve the routine problems of the people without any hassle and save their time. Many offices and departments are switching towards automation to resolve their issues. In COMSATS, many students visit student center daily fo r their issues related to registration, accounts, admissions and other operations. Due to rush of the students, it becomes impossible for the management of the student service center to maintain discipline. COMSATS student service center queue management s ystem will help the students to save their time by issuing them a token & help the staff of the student service center to serve a student according to his turn. The student will get token of his concerned window only and the staff for that particular task will serve the student. The token will tell about the waiting time to the students so that they can wait for their turn. When the member of staff, sitting at window, call the next student, the system will announce the token number and window number. They c an also transfer token to the other counters from their counters. In this way, the student will not need to ask anyone about his concerned window.

heading: 1.2    Objectives
content: COMSATS student service centre queue management system will help the students to save their  time by reserving a token from their personal android devices or by issuing them a token with mentioned estimated waiting time on it , showing ongoing serving token number & help the staff of the student service centre to serve a student according to his turn. The student will get token of his concerned window only and the staff for that particular task will serve the student. The token will tell about the waiting time to the students so that they can wait for their turn. When the member of staff, sitting at  window, call the next student, the system will announce the token number and window number. In this way, the student will not need to ask anyone about his concerned window. Here are some COMSATS strategic goals and objectives: A guide for the new people a) The people who come for new admission, they will not need to ask anyone for guidance about operational windows. The token machine, available at door, will provide interface to the visitors. The app in Google Playstore will also provide interface to reserve  token from personal android devices. Using this interface, the visitor will select his purpose of coming and the token machine will give him a printed token that will guide the visitor to wait and visit the concerned section or window. In this way, this queue management system will guide the new people. b) The LED (TV) will guide the people about their turn by showing overall progress of the queues. LED TV will display the current serving token and the coming up next token with window number.

c) On each window, there will be a PC screen hanging outside. EachPC will display ongoing token number. Utilize technology dynamically & enhance adaptability d) The system will be web based and android applications . Frameworks and conventions will be followed. Hence, it will be more maintainable, adaptable and extendable. e) Android, Bootstrap and Laravel are open source, hence, maintainability will be easier. Serve the students faster f) The system will provide token numbers to the visitors and they will be served faster due to queuing process. Avoid conflicts in student service center g) In rush hours, many conflicts occur. The people go to wrong window which results in wastage of their time as well as the time of the operator serving at the window. The queue management system will guide the people about the right window in which they should stand with the help of hanging tablets on each window that show current serving token number. h) Operator can transfer token from their counters if there is another query of the visitor. So that there is no conflict between the present visitors. Avoid rush in student service center i) The visitors will be able to reserve token from their personal android devices. j) The visitor can see ongoing serving token number from his android device. k) Estimated waiting time will be mentioned on tokens. l) According to given token number and current ongoing number, the people will be able to know about their waiting time, hence, it will help the student service center to avoid the rush in student service center and the people will be able to save their time as well.

Helping managing staff m) Queue management system will help the managing staff to manage the overall environment of the student service center. The rush will be controlled by token reservation. Signaling about turn n) Queue management system will inform the visitors about their turn. o) It will also inform about the next token that will be served. p) It will guide about the concerned window.

heading: 1.3   Problem Statement
content: During the peak hours, due to the rush of the  students, it becomes impossible for the management of the student service center to maintain discipline. The students, who came first, sometimes keep waiting for their turn and those, who came later, get their work done earlier. When this happens, the stu dents start blaming the management and it results in wastage of time of staff as well as students. Those people, who comes to enquire about new admission, face difficulties and feel uncomfortable in such situations. To resolve this issue, we propose COMSATS student service center queue management system. It will help the students to get their issues resolved as soon as possible. It this way, they will visit only concerned window on their turn and they will have information about waiting time.

heading: 2.1     Literature Review
content: Databyte‟s[1] Advanced Token Management System is one of the leading token system in India. This system specified in decreasing the waiting time of a user, and somehow technologically advanced with less confusion and easy to operate.  It tend s to eliminate long lines, boost staff productivity and gain insights. It is featured as to support 30 services and 50+ counters, TV based displays, token number display for counters, voice announcement, installed central monitoring systems, get customer r emarks as feedback. Databyte‟s specially designed there systems for banks to avoid long queues. It collect inputs before issuing a token from the

customer, it supports group calling, it support multiple counter services, facilitate customers to add remarks, prioritize customer, delay alerts, generate reports for breaks taken. Databyte‟s also designed there systems for hospitals to avoid rushes and inconvenience. It provides multiple queue types for patients, operator consoles for doctors, chat option betwee n doctors and receptionist, token forwarding with comments, supports multilingual display, master displays, nested services, get patient feedback. Qmatic[2] is one of the leading companies in today‟s world providing queue management system. It is widely sp read across the world and well known regarding it services. content: We will consider waterfall model as our model for software development life cycle. For the following reasons, we considered waterfall model more suitable for our project.  The requirements of our project were very clear and fixed.  COMSATS had confidence on us.  There was no ambiguity in our project. heading: Approach
content: For the testing of the CQMS Black box and white box testing should be done, as the code of the software is available on different locations. For the Black Box testing Test case software should be used. All of the software is tested manually and automation. Test case is available free for the student usage. For the manual testing each use cases, test cases should be built for the better understanding.

heading: Item Pass/Fail Criteria
content: There should be three steps for items pass/fail criteria. 1. Functionality completed should be mentioned in test cases and passes the test case criteria. 2. An item will be considered as pass if it means the „Expected outcome‟ defined in corresponding test cases. 3. Item is passed by the testing manager. Suspension Criteria and Resumption Requirement Suspended criteria for CQMS is that it suspends the testing of the software when: 1. Unavailability of resources. 2. Project time is over. 3. Unexpected holidays. 4. Budget is less.

heading: Remaining Test Task
content: CQMS is a waterfall process model, so all the tasks done here are in flow.

heading: 7    Conclusion
content: Problems faced, and lessons learned During this project report, we gained much experience in making documentation. We learnt that before starting any project, we should focus the target market and stakeholders. We learnt that spending more time on getting requirements is better than to face requirements creep. We faced issues while collecting requirements because we visited our client‟s office many times with appointment but most of the times, he was not available due to some is sues. Each and every phase of the software development lifecycle is important. If we do not make mistakes in initial phase, our next phase will be easier for us. Project summary In today‟s world, management is the only key for any organization to achieve i ts goals respectively. Our project is queue management system in COMSATS Student Service Centre which would help the administration to run the organization with best possible chances of avoiding mismanagement. In our designed project , we intend to develop a system accordingly where a person entering in student service centre will get a token number with necessary details and estimated time by selecting his concerns from the token machine placed at the entrance. An android tablet will be installed on entranc e with print generator for issuance of the token. A person will not require to stand in queue or face rush towards the operational windows. He can see the current serving number and wait for his turn. An a ndroid tablet will be installed on each operational window to guide the respective person. The serving operators sitting on operational windows will call the next person by incrementing the token number after serving the current client. The system will make the announcement for the next client by showing t oken number and window number on counters and LED screen which are programmed with android box. After making his query done a remote visitor will provide feedback by submitting his experience, leaving a secret review, rating the system and administration. The users will also save their time also by reserving token online from their android devices without visiting the Student Service Center. All the system will be supervised by the manager with high managerial skills in an organization. At the backend an ad ministrator will handle the system with full command. Administrator can add various companies to the system too which desired to install this system and also authorized to remove them. Our motive is to develop a system which would be able to provide all th e services which are not offered  by the present related systems and this part is briefly discussed in related work. We intend to implement the system with fully functional qualities which would handle all the exceptions and counter the possible occurring problems in the system. Future work At this time, CQMS will support only FREE tokens. It does not support any paid appointment or token. But in future, we will add paid appointments option that will help the users to get paid tokens. For example, if anyone wants to get a token for a cli nical laboratory or appointment for a doctor, in those cases, he will be able to pay appointment fee.

At this time, there will be no cost on any company for using our system and we will generate revenue by showing ads of 3 rd parties. But in future, we wil l allow premium accounts and limit the number of free counters for each organization. The companies with premium accounts will pay per month. At this time, remote reservation app is only for android devices. In future, we will add iOS & windows support. We will also provide an online web based portal for PC users to reserve tickets from their computers.

heading: Abstract
content: Speech to Text is an android based application for the recognition of human voice and conversion of this human voice into text form after performing certain operations. The key exercise to be performed can be mentioned as detection and removal of stationary and non- stationary sounds. After this progression, the voice will be converted into text and will be displayed on the screen. This manipulation will lead us to a list of activities mentioned as sig nal processing, Noise removal. Practical implementation of these will be performed using android programming and respective APIs and SoundTouch Library for the enhancement of the resultant application.

heading: 1 Introduction
content: As far as the introduction of Speech to text app is concerned the name explains itself. Speech to Text application is developed with an anticipation to facilitate users with the transcription of audio into text with maximum achievable accuracy. Talking abo ut accuracy lets discuss this first; a speech to text recognition process is hypersensitive depending upon the quality of input sound. So, first step forward in achieving this good quality sound will be detection of stationary and non- stationary sounds. Th e second step we take will be the removal of these stationary and non - stationary voices. Stationary voices can be described as sound of non-living things as car, airplane etc. Furthermore, non-stationary voices can be described as irrelevant conversations in the respective sound. Furthermore, the accent of the speaker is a factor that matters a lot in the transcription process. There is always a difference between a novice and mature speaker. So, our application will be developed by keeping in mind the l ocal speaker so they will not face any difficulty in transcription. Here the point to ponder is why to develop an android application for speech recognition when numerous speech to text kits are available in the market. So, the reason is all these tools  are serviceable after charging stakeholder a bulky amount of money. So, if someone bother to use free services of speech to text apps they are just useless because their noise detection and removal system will be useless. So, this application is developed  with intent of providing free services to the users that are comparable with the paid ones. Including more another notable reason to develop this android base application is that most of the speech to text kits are developed by keeping in mind the mature language speakers and not the novice ones. So, this application will target the novice language speakers. Below is the description of all main four modules of this android application and the process we will follow to achieve them.

heading: 1.1 Noise Removal
content: Unwanted sound is judged to be unpleasant as well as loud or disruptive to hear. Android platform provides us with a noise suppressor class in Android API level 16. Noise suppression is an audio pre-processor which removes the background. As mention in Introduction noise is either stationary or non-stationary. Noise Suppressor mostly used in voice chat applications. The implementation of the Noise Suppressor in AndroidNoise Suppressor in a particular AudioRecord, define the audio session ID of AudioRecord when buil ding the Noise Suppressor. The audio session is recovered by calling getAudioSessionId () on the AudioRecord instance. On few advanced devices, NS can be injected by default in the capture path by the policies according to the MediaRecorder, AudioSource used. The application should call NoiseSuppressor.getEnable () after generating the NS to check for the default NS activation event on a special AudioRecord session. AudioRecoder and MediaRecoder class describe below. [1]

heading: 1.1.1 AudioRecoder class in Android:
content: The AudioRecord Class delivers a tested form of the Audio files that are recorded and deals with the audio assets for Java applications to record audio from the audio input equipment of the platform. After the recording is done, the samples need to be pulled b ack in the data form from the AudioRecord object. The advantage that the AudioRecord Class offers is that while running the App the Samples are spared in a temporary variable and can be accessed to and controlled through the App running time. This implies that MediaRecorder Class there is no reason to save the samples to the external memory of the smart  phone. This can spare Memory space. Audio Class is a Class in Java and for having the capacity to utilize it, a constructor must be produced containing the desired specification. The Desired parameters are: [2]

heading: 1.1.2 MediaRecodeer class in Android
content: The MediaRecorder Class catches Audio and Video files and saves them to the mobile phone memory external or internal. The configuration in which the audio and video are captured is .3gp and by utilization of the MediaPlayer Class, this file can specifically be played on the mobile phone. However, the MediaRecorder Class isn't suited for signa l processing. heading: Abstract
content: Printing and Press business is flying at the moment. People have to go through unnecessary delays in their orders because of the high demand. Even th ough, they do not get their desired product. Furthermore, the prices in this market are very high as compared to the work required. Hence, we introduced DPP (Doorway Printing & Publication). DP P is a smart online printing press platform that receives online orders in two major printing domains, i.e. Digital Printing and Offset printing from all over the Pakistan. The customers can sign- up and choose their desired templates from 1000’s of templates available or can order a custom template on special request. As all the details related to printing industry cannot be shared using  template only, so DPP has provided a chatting module for communication between buyer and seller. The seller completes the order of a customer and send it to the address provided by the customer . DPP provides escrow system to support the successful and secure payments to complete deals am ong the buyers and sellers. DPP provides a Support & Resolution Centre for resolving issues and disputes among sellers and buyers.
