heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: This system will be much more than an ordinary hotel booking website offers. It will have extraordinary features in it which will finally lead to the customer satisfaction and generate the business for hotel owners. How will the job be done technically and managerially?  From advertisement to easy navigation of the desired place, it will attract both the customer and the businessmen to come to this online hotel booking website. In addition to this, the website will offer both the customer and the manager an online chat facility to solve the queries on the spot. The website will make the page for the one who will register their hotel just like Facebook does for its users and a man ager can further customize and enter the information according to the user requirements. We will provide ease for people of different regions by including their national languages and currencies into our website. Integration with different conveyance services like Uber and Careem will be provided[9]. The front face of BOOK IT ONLINE (ONLINE HOTEL BOOKING SITE) will be quite simple in which registration and location filters will be provided to the clients. Once the right location is entered; the client will be directed to the relevant page. There he will be provided with a bundle of interactive features such as filters, the type of hotel the client is looking for.

heading: 1.2 Problem Statement
content: How can we cater the needs of tourists for providing safe passage and hu nt for accommodation through their journey?

heading: 1.3 Scope:
content: Why is the system being developed?  There are a couple of factors which compelled us to choose this system. Lack of the good and user friendly online hotel booking website is one of them. Secondly, the loop holes in the present website on this specific idea. Thirdly, there can be much more in an online hotel booking website than just the aligned pictures of different hotels .Finally this system will enable us to give Pakistan such a website that will ha ve an impact worldwide and help this country known by this brand name.

heading: 1.4 Goals and Objectives
content:  The best door to knock at where deals will prove cost effective and time saving.  Full-fledged customization profile to users which means that hotels will have their own distinct profiles.  Adding pleasure to travelling, chat services will be provided to the users for their respective hotels.  Advertising prospects will be provided to the registered hotels.  Present market demands a perfect framework to work on  , so we are using Laravel in order to meet the market demand.  Providing offers and deals on the basis of festivals arriving.  Chatbot Services will help users to find their passage and guidance through the destination.

heading: 1.5.1 Flow in Cost will affect the demand:
content: At this moment the value of the money has an impact our lifestyles. But we don’t know when it will fluctuate it would certainly effect the life of those doing businesses. There is always an uncertain situation going on which would affect our customers. The number of 3G and 4G internet users on mobile is 42.08 million. They cannot reach our site if the prices of internet packages arise to a high level and it would effect their demand.

heading: 1.5.2 Network barrier may cause trouble:
content: The technological barrier is one of the major risks that has to be discussed. The networks must be important in order to reach our website if no suitable or proper connection of internet will be provided to the users it can make us unreacha ble. For example, the recent attack on internet cable was affected in the Indian Ocean. This caused more than 90% of internet users to reach any sort of facility online.

heading: 1.5.3 Personal preferences of the Users:
content: Some users of the internet has no good ex perience as they might have a bad experience or they find it really difficult to fill out the forms and other sort of data. For example aged people never like to use a complex looking website front -end, they choose services which are a click away.

heading: 1.5.4 Environmental Hazards:
content: Floods, earthquakes, civil unrest, political situations etc. can change the mind -set of the customers who will use our website. The situations can generate a wave of unrest within themselves.

heading: 1.5.5 Face value of others stakeholders:
content: The companies which will provide their services through are website can gain a lot of profit but there is always a risk in discussing other companies in you websites. UBER has cases in which they are sued in the court. Some people find this company a real threat to them. This might create a loss of confidence of our customers on our website.

heading: 1.5.6 Planning Overlap:
content: Our time interval for the completion of this project is approximately one year and we hope to launch a site that has no competitor at this m oment. But we cannot say that with 100% surety. There are thousands of software houses working on web technologies and web engineering. Within the time period of our FYP completion there is a risk that another website equal or most probably more revolutionized then ours can arrive at market. This can make our schedule unusable as we have to create and plan a new web services to reach the level of these competitors.

heading: 1.5.7 Code management:

heading: Abstract
content: ‘The Social Hub’ is a social media application that allows the user to use other social media applications on one platform and all these social applications can   be used and  manipulated from that platform. Users can connect social apps by signing -in from their account of respective social apps. Main interface of The Social Hub provide a swipe -able tab like structure for the ease of switching between different social applications that the user has connected with The Social Hub. The Social Hub  also enables  the user to search other people  that have Social Hub accounts. There are two main methods of searching in T he Social Hub. One is Location -based search and the other is Type-based search. There are different types of filters to apply on search as well, that dynamically filter the search result on the basis of user preference. The Social Hub  also maintains  its own chat feature independent of other social media applications. This chat is maintained by backend Social Hub Server.  User can talk to people that he/she has searched. There is also an inbox module that allows the user to keep track of their messages. The Social Hub also provides a highly dynamic and smooth interface that is simple and easy to use. Table of Contents

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: The Social Hub is a social media application for Android devices that will allow the user to use multiple social applications on a single light weight platform. It is basically creating a hub for other social applications [1 ], or, in other words, to use al l other social applications from a single application that provide a smooth and easy to use  multi-tasking feature [2]. Furthermore, it also features ‘location-based search’ provided with different filters that users can select from. There is also a facility for type-based search. In-order to fully understand The Social Hub, it’s aspects are divided into three parts as following.

heading: 1.1.1 Visual Structure
content: The visual structure of social has been made as simple as possible af ter multiple iterations of heuristic evaluation. In order to make the interface smooth and easily accessible, the project team held different test cases and user evaluations to develop an interface that would best suit the usage of The Social Hub [3]. The main interface is simple but uses the concept of multitasking intelligently  with less task consumption and more performance [2] . On the very top is the Hub bar which contains all the social applications icons to identify which app is active on the main sc reen that the user will use to The Social Hub. Under the bar there is the main window for the current selected social application to be displayed. The application, which the user will select from the app bar, will be displayed in this window below. One imp ortant thing to keep i n mind is that this window work  as a multitasking window for all the apps that are added in our Hub. In other words, while using a social app in this window, if the user  decides to switch  to another app then goes back to the previous app, it will start from the exact point where it was left previously [2]. Inside the main window, there is a floating  shortcut button  that is connected to application’s other features. Interacting with the icon expands options for the user. One option lea ds to a window that is used for location-based searching purpose , one for type -based search  and the other option leads the user to his/her personal inbox [3]. The Search list of The Social Hub is uniquely designed to show searched user along with their actual address of current location and the social accounts that they have connected with Social Hub. There is also a floating button  on this search list screen that enables the user to manipulat e search with different filters such as gender based filter or vicinity radius filter [3]. User can chat with other people, either by selecting them form the search list or from the inbox.

heading: 1.1.2 Features
content: To fully use Social Hub, a person is first directed to L og-in or Sign-up to a Social Hub account as it is a necessary step to access The Social Hub. The Social Hub’s chat can also be accessed once the account is created. This chat feature is Social Hub’s own chat independent of other social accounts. The Social Hub features a smooth and multi-tasking environmen t for other social media application. All social applications that are added by the user can be used simultaneously through multitasking [2]. The search engine is the main feature of the Social Hub. This app lication keeps track  of location data of the user. If the user wants to search a person, they can either search by typing the name or simply by using l ocation-based search feature . Location-based search feature will give you all the list of people who were or are nearby your location along with the address of location. The location-based search is only possible if the other user , who is being searched, is using T he Social-Hub as well  [4]. The result of search engine returns the name of Social Hub account of people, their location  address, along with the pointer to all social app accounts of those people that they are using on The Social Hub . One thing is important to mention here that Social Hub respects the privacy of other people hence the social app accounts of other people can  only be displayed if they have allowed it through Social Hub [5]. The Social Hub also has its own chat function with its own database server on the backend.  User can conveniently send and receive messages to other people.

heading: 1.1.3 Working
content: The working of T he Social Hub is very simple. In -order to use it, the user must first create an account of Social Hub or sign in if they have a pre -existing account. After creating an account, the user must link his/her social apps. The link process is done by signing into the Social Hub via other social apps. The user can also define which social accounts to be shown when they are being searched by other people. Social Hub only points to the social account of the searched person. It doesn’t show any important or personal information [5]. The Social Hub allows the user to use multiple social apps in a single window or multitasking for social apps [2]. The search-engine feature of Social Hub is simple as well. A user can simply search by typing names which will result in t he search engine showing the Social Hub profil e of the people you searched. Location -based search is also available in this search engine. It will list out all the Social Hub accounts which were nearby your location. The search can further be filt ered using user selected options such as gender based search or different vicinity radius search [4].

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The objectives of Social Hub are following. • A platform which allows the control and use of social applications without l aunching each app independe ntly and without harming any privacy policy of other social application. • Saving the precious time of people and reducing the amount of eff ort put to access social apps. • Less consumption of smartphone processing power and use of social application efficiently. • Providing an interface that as smooth as possible and easily understandable. • More battery life for smartphones. • Meeting new people and socializing. • Finding long lost friends. • Making new connection with people. • Being aware of friends or people who are or were nearby you.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: These days, almost every individual has a smart phone. We can find people of any age clinging to their mobile phones throughou t the day and spending more and more time on social media. People nowadays are spending hours on different social media applications and all they do is switch between different social apps so that they can stay updated with what is going on in their social life and to stay in touch with their friends or to make new ones. Social apps are the widely used mobile apps in the world and each day new apps are created. It is becoming difficult for the user to manage all social apps individually because using too much apps all day with each app l aunching independently not onl y consumes a lot of battery life  but also wastes a lot of precious time of the user in the process of switching between these apps [3]. The other problem we are dealing with is the process of searching. Right now there is only  one way to search people using social apps, which is by typing their name in the search bar. No other viable method is convenient enough for us to use besides typing their name and if we don’t know the name of people we are searching, it’s nearly impossib le to reach them on social media if they are not already in our ‘friends list’ [4].

heading: 1.4.1. Constraints:
content:  Project team: We have complete trust in the project team but we also have to realize that individuals on the team have other tasks on their hand that might, at times, takes priority.  Upgrades: Our project is an android application and applications these days are regularly updated with the change in technology or according to customer needs. Upgrades come with a high cost a ttached to them. Every time an upgrade is needed the team will have to integrate that change with previous features intact.  Tight time frame: Our project has a tight time frame an d should be completed  at least a month before the final delivery.  User testing: Getting users to participate in user testing can be difficult as they have trust issues with third party applications.  Privacy: In social media applications the users have concerns that their private information must not be misused. The user’s data sh ould be kept private. Hence, steps should be taken to ensure user’s vital information’s security.  New Technology: The technologies used in this project are relatively new and difficult to understand for a new developer  but they are powerful enough for our  goal to be accomplished in the way we envisioned.

heading: 1.4.1. Assumptions:
content: Data Integrity: The data integrity is the major risk that we can face in this project. Our application concerns about integration of data. Social apps are integrated with each other on a single platform. Hence, to maintain the data integrity and accuracy is one of the major concerns [5]. Requirement Problem: As we are developing a social application, basically a hub of the social applications like Facebook, Instagram, twitter. So in the development of the social application the requirements gathered at the initial stages of the project are not clear and not goal oriented [1]. Schedule Problem: The problem of re-scheduling may occur when the milestones are not achieved and work is not  done according to the schedule. To achieve the accurate results we have to complete the working modules according to the time line given. If it is not possible then reschedule the plan. Personnel Risk: This one is an unpredictable risk. The developers/te am members working on the project may get ill or may face some issue that forces individual to lose focus or to quit as well. Mental health is an important part of studies. A group member may face some mental issues as well than can critically affect the project.

heading: 1.5 Project scope
content: There are many social apps available and their number will only increase in the future. So, the motivation behind this application is to help and facilitate people by providing them a platform through which they can control and use all their social applications  [1]. It not only saves the precious time of people but also reduces the amount interac tion with the smartphone’s OS [3 ]. Furthermore, it also helps people to search social accounts of distant friends who are nearby your location, or people whom they might know but don’t remember their names. Hence this app is developed for purpose of searching nearby people’s social accounts without entering their names.

heading: 2.1.1 Facebook
content: Facebook started using the user location data a few years ago, it basically takes the location of a user and determine their area such as a specific place, city or country and use it  in the process of posting a status on Facebook. A feature such as location -based events was  also created on Facebook to let people know any special events nearby their location. Furthermore, there was also a feature of check -in in which a user shares a Fa cebook status of a place (restaurant, city, et cetera) based off on location created on map.  ‘Find friends near you’ is also a new feature that they have recently started , which lets you know about location of nearby friends.

heading: 2.1.2 Snapchat
content: Snapchat becam e the new trend in the market recently . I t is comparatively a new app as compared to some old social apps. It basically enables the user to make stories of their day in form of pictures and/or videos. It also uses the location of a user and suggests certain filt ers for the user to use them in their photos and/or videos.

heading: 2.1.3 Android apps
content: There are many other android apps on android Play Store that have few features somewhat near to The Social Hub. There are many applications that create a sort of folder for all social apps, but these apps are neither efficient nor are they able to provide a light weight platform for social apps multitasking feature in a single window. There is no such app that lets you search all the social accounts of people in a single search w ithout even entering their name. Furthermore, there are also many applications that utilize the location feature in apps but none of the apps have the Location-based search as Social Hub will introduce.

heading: 4.1 Unit Testing
content: Unit testing refers to testing of each function that has been built against functional requirement that was collected during software requirement specification. Each unit is to be built and tested by the assigned person agains t the document .Since our platform  is an android application so we have divided our whole Social hub application  into functions taking each perspective as one function. Whenever a unit is com plete, the unit test is performed to verify the functionalities of the system. We divide our application in different modules and check their functionality based on their expected result. To ensure the quality of the application each divided module passes different tests.

heading: 4.3 Integration Testing
content: Integration testing is done to assure the interactivity of the modules with each other . In integration testing we integrate our main modules to check whether they are performing expected functionality and also check their sequence that they are integrated correctly. So the main modules of our applications are following.  Login and Create Account is the main module and it is tested by integrating both.  Different search filters like location range filter and gender based search filter modules are integrated and tested  User interface is smooth with storing and retrieving  Chat feature is integrated with location based search and typed based search and tested respectively.  All other modules are tested separately. After developing the functionalities of the system, their integration is one of the major tasks. While integrating, many errors which are not known at the time of integration are occurred but are available only when the system is tested thoroughly by integration testing. So we performed integration testing when all the perspectives (units) were developed and tested properly.

heading: 4.4 Acceptance Testing
content: An acceptance test is a final test performed by the end users. This test verifies that our software is in working conditi on, adaptable, understandable, and we conducted through the software itself after initial use. The questionnaire we made to answer the following  How long did it take to get familiar with the software?  Was the language used for specific actions were clear and generic?  Had the software reduced the working time and effort?  Was operating social apps easier?

heading: 5.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: Until now, for the completion of this document, decisions  had to be made whether to pursue an original idea that is new and had the potential to bring a change in the social app genre, or to adapt to the regular projects that most of the students opt for, to clear their studies without any challenge. The former was the decision that we came up with after careful discussions. Complex researches and requirement analysis iterations were main challenge to bring this project into inception. At the moment of disc ussing the scope of this application, we decided to properly launch it in the market after completing it as a final year project.  As being a relatively new application in the market, the Social Hub also has the potential risk of being copied or stolen and  being re-released on larger scale. This  is a kind of risk that every entrepreneur has to take, while entering the marker. The original idea of The Social Hub  is on a much l arger scale with various ground -breaking and innovative features but we had to limi t them to only two major features due the time limit and lack of resources. The full potential of this application is currently out of our reach to be developed, thus we are only able include only those features that are necessary for the scope of a final year project. One of the major problem s that we faced was to decide which tools were to be used to develop this application. As there are many tools available for android applications but it’s a tricky thing to decide which tool will be best for the Social Hub. Hence, after consulting with a professional software engineer we came up with a solution to develop The Social Hub on React Native, a framework for Java Script. These were  some of  the problems that we came across , while making the documentation of t his projec t that resulted in continuous change in designs and diagrams of The Social Hub.  The main issue was the continuous API policy change of different social media applications. There were no clear indications that to what extent third party app access  was granted to developers. Furthermore many applications changed their policies within the development life cycle of this project hence creating issues for the project at many occasions.

heading: 5.2 Summary
content: Developing a proper application and to release it in the market is not an easy task to perform. Complete knowledge of requirement gathering, designing and testing is required to be able develop an Application that people can use in a daily life. Putting all your knowledge into creation and proper utilization of the available resources are the main thing that we have learned while doing computer science and that is  exactly what we are trying to do to develop The Social Hub. But it just doesn’t end here. Maintaining and making this application successful, after its release, is also our obligation. The only reason we were confident enough to be able to work on The Social Hub was because of the life lessons we learned in our various courses throughout our degree, Such as coming up with your own and unique ideas and ma king them a reality through hard work and professional commitment. Applying various software engineering techniques to develop complete and accurate documentation of our project, using analysis techniques to understand the user and design the user interfac e accordingly. Understanding how the front end, back work and how they are mapped to each other. How the database of system works. The software development lifecycle is one of the major concerns that shape up the final face of any software project. It is o ne of the vital techniques from which projects are completed effectively and timely. These are some of the major aspects that were used and kept in mind while developing the documentation for The Social Hub. heading: Project Abstract:
content: Natural Language Tool Kit (NLTK) is a leading platform for construction Python programs to work with human language data. Natural language resources and tools are routinely available for several European languages for instance English, Spanish, Italian, etc. However, several South Asian languages are still under -resourced, i.e. Urdu language. Urdu has aro und 450 million native and non-native speakers worldwide. However, in terms of Natural Language Processing (NLP) resources, it is still in its infancy. Even basic linguistic tools, corpora, and techniques are hard to find. Therefore, the primary objective of our final year project will be to address this gap by contributing basic pre -processing linguistics tools, corpora, and techniques for Urdu NLP. Resulting into Extended Urdu Natural Language Toolkit (ExUNLT) will have three primary pre - processing tools that are required for an Urdu NLP pipeline; spell checker, text classifiers, and hybrid part-of-speech tagger. All three developed tools will be tailored on statistical, rule -based and hybrid approaches. Furthermore, we will evaluate and compare developed  resources of ExUNLT, these tools and developed resources will be freely available for academic use to stimulate computational research in a wider range of text analysis tools in Urdu and application.

heading: 1.1 Introduction:
content: Natural Language Processing (NLP) toolkits are widely available, to analyse text of different natural languages such as English, Arabic and Chinese etc. For instance, Apache Open NLP [5] , Stanford Core NLP [1] , Machine Learning for Language Toolkit (MALLET) [2], General Architecture for Text Engineering (GATE) [3] , Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) [4] etc. These toolkits have been used in a range of NLP and Human Language Technology (HLT) applications as well as domains. For instance, Computer Sciences [8], Bio-informatics [6] [7], Corpus linguistics [9] etc. Text processing pipeli nes are built on three basic linguistic tools: (I) spell checker, (II) text identifier, and (III) Part -Of-Speech (POS) tagger. Spell Check is a syntax  checker that finds public spelling errors and structural mistakes in language text. This tool has been widely applied in spelling boost, text classification, and corpus linguistics domains. Text Classification is a NLP relevant task whose aim is to choose the correct class label for a given data. Some examples where classification tasks may be applied are, detect whether an email is spam or not, detect the topic of an article, word sense disambiguation, etc. Whereas, Part -Of-Speech (POS) tagger is a linguistics software that reads text in language and allocates its grammatical class to every word. POS tagger is worth for semantic field disambiguation, word sense disambiguation, text classification etc. Currently, the above-mentioned text pre-processing tools (spell checker, text classifier, and POS tagger) are primarily available for English and European langua ge, and there is a lack of such linguistics NLP tools for South Asian languages, particularly Urdu a topic of interest, which is widely spoken and used around the world. The Urdu language is an Indo -Aryan language. It is derived from Persian, Arabic, and Turkish scripts [10.]. Urdu script is written from right to left and follows the Nastalik calligraphy style. It is a free -word order language and sometime follows the Subject -Object-Verb structure [12]. Therefore, the developed tools for English and other sibling languages is not a promising basis of Urdu NLP [11]. Urdu NLP is important for several reasons. Therefore, this Final Year Project (FYP) will present the design, development and evaluation of an Extended Urdu Natural Language toolkit (hereafter called ExUNLT). Our novel research contribution in this project will be focus on Urdu text pre- processing as follows: (I) ExUNLT initially, contains three Urdu text pre-processing tools including a spell checker, text classifiers and a POS tagger. (II) In add ition, we will create supporting resources to develop and evaluate the ExUNLT text pre-processing tools, (III) proposed algorithms for all these three tools, and (IV) toolkit, supporting resources will be freely available. The need for the Urdu NLP toolkit (ExUNLT) is clear from above discussion, and for us, it presents the first step in a larger project. First, we intended to use ExUNLT to design and development of sentiment analysis system in Urdu. Second, it will serve as a benchmark and baseline to Urdu, Spell Checker, Text Classifiers, and POS tagging tasks. Thirdly, for intelligent processing of text in Urdu and to develop large-scale Urdu resources. Fourth, it has an extensible pipeline that provides core linguistics annotation for Urdu language text quickly and painlessly. Finally, to stimulate the NLP beyond our project there is a desperate need to develop a toolkit.

heading: 1.5 Motivation and Scope:
content: Over the last several years of research on corpus annotation, now it becomes a fundamental part of NLP and corpus-based language study. Because lot of research efforts have been carried out for the development of a wide range of linguistic annotatio ns tools, such as, POS tagger, text classifiers and named entity identification etc. The scorching areas of research interest for the NLP research community are primarily focused towards European and East Asian languages; in consequence last twenty-years different state-of-the-art NLP tools are becoming available for these languages such as in [13, 14]. However, less attention has been paid towards South Asian languages for instance, Urdu. Urdu is widely spoken not only in Pakistan, but India, Europe and in  the West. It is first language in Pakistan and used as a medium of instruction in most government organizations. It has community more than a million that is spread around the globe including Europe, Middle East, United States of America and Canada [15]. Urdu NLP is new and emerging area of research where very small effort towards research and development is paid, having its footsteps back in 2000 when a project was initiated by Lancaster University with the name EMILLE [16]. Therefore, the primary motivation of our FYP is to develop off-the-shelf NLP tools. The scope of this FYP will be to develop following NLP tools: spell checker, text identifier, and POS tagger for Urdu language. All these tools will be tailored around statistical and rule -based techni ques. Furthermore, supporting resources (corpora, dictionaries, and wordlists) will be generated where required.

heading: 2.1.1 Spell Checker
content: To develop a large scale and freely available resources to explore the problem of spell checking is a non-trivial task. However, there have been a number of research efforts in past to develop spell checkers, but most of them are for English language. One of the outcome of these efforts is a novel binary spell checker [20]. There are similar efforts in developing data sets in other languages such as Chinese. The outcome of these efforts is a hybrid Chinese spelling correction [17]. Furthermore, there are attempts in developing a spell checker for Arabic as well. The results of these attempts are: (I) towards automatic spell checking for Arabic [18] (II) hybrid Arabic spelling and punctuation corrector [19]. There are also some spell checkers in Urdu languag e. One of them is Urdu spell checking [21]. The novel binary spell checker [20] is a simple and eﬃcient approach, which is based upon phonetic matching, supervised learning and associative matching. This approach is a combination of: (I) n- gram approach (I I) hamming distance approach. This spell checker aims to high recall accuracy possibly at the expense of precision. However, the scoring allows us to rank the retrieved matches, so we can limit the number of possibilities suggested to the user to the top 10 matches, giving both high recall and precision The most competitive work in the past year, for the development of monolingual spell checker for Chinese language is hybrid Chinese spelling correction [17]. This approach is combination of: (I) language model-based method to generate correction candidates (II) Statistical machine translation, which is to correct candidates. In addition, support vector machine classifier to re -rank the candidates provided by the previous two approaches. To overcome the low resource problem, they generated around 2 million artificial sentences with an easy rule, which replaces each alphabet in the given 700 sentences with the character in the confusion set to generate a new training corpus and used unlabelled data corpus to evaluate actual Chinese texts. One of the spell checkers in Arabic language is towards automatic spell checking for Arabic [19]. The technique used in this spell checker is heuristic. It also involves developing a morphological analyser, techniques of spelling checking and spelling correction and efficient methods of lexicon operations in Arabic. This spell checker can identify spelling errors for standard Arabic and Egyptian dialects. This spell checker is also very helpful for automating the proofreading of human typed Arabic text. The other spell checker in Arabic language is hybrid Arabic spelling and punctuation corrector [21]. This paper deals with each error independently and uses different techniques that proves to be most accurate for the problem un der discussion. This technique is the combination of: (I) Heuristic rules to normalize the text. (II) Conditional random fields classifier for correcting punctuation errors. (III) Dictionary -language model correction and alignment based correction, which deals with misspelled words error. This is the first system to handle punctuation errors. The technique used for Urdu spell checker [21] is the variation of edit distance that is reverse edit distance approach. In this work, focus is on spelling error detec tion and correction feature. However, this work is concentrated on gathering various spell checking and correction techniques that are suitable for correcting Urdu spelling errors.

heading: 2.1.3 Text Identifier:
content: There has been a growing  range of research efforts on topic identification task in English Language. These efforts are primarily based on knowledge-based and machine learning algorithms approach. As an example , in [25]  where essential words are matched with Yahoo directory titles for topic identification task.  In [26], where finding WordNet based concepts in a textual document based on their importance. There are some others, which match the language model of documents with those of Google or Yahoo directories [27]. A study in [28]  allotted ontology nodes to the document clusters [29] to classify its topics. There is another group exists of topic recognizable task, that predicts topic(s) of a document applying numerous machine learning approaches. These Machine Learning (ML) approaches can be classified either into single-label or multi-label subject distinguishing tasks. In the previous ML group approach, a document is labeled with a single -label (coarse-grained) subject. Though, the next ML approach allotted one or many subjects to a document with pre -defined labels, in this manner, give all the finer grained examination. For instance, the writer in [30] utilized Naïve Bayes ML classifier to assign single-label Wikipedia articles into one of the pre -defined topic classifications utilizing stemming, tiff, with semantic classifications as a feature set. This type of topic-identification can give just a coarse-grained study, which is outside some real -world NLP and HLT appli cations [31], e.g. web contact topical association, email routing or news topic recognizable for such sort of grouping tasks, there exists another kind of multi-name ML approaches in which each document can have a place with one or more subjects. For several topic identification tasks, there exists various kinds of multi-label ML algorithms. These can be characterized into two: (I) Problem transformation algorithm (ii) Algorithm adoption. The next group of multi-label approach stretches out the current ML classifiers to deal with the multi- label information directly. Nonetheless, these kinds of methodologies are more suitable for domain problems [24]. Though, the methodologies of first group transform the multi -label issue into a single-label issue, in thi s way, any state -of-the-art single-name ML classifiers (e.g. Naïve Bayes, K-NN, SVM) can be applied to suit the requisite, in this way more flexible and scalable [32]. Directly associated with us to our work, authors in [31] used problem transformation al gorithmic rule to spot the three topics of newspaper documents, using Naïve Bayes ML classifier. Additionally, this study used topic likelihood threshold value, word form and lemma as feature extraction approaches. The score of the F1 report is 0.64. Where, writers trained multiple Naïve Bayes classifier on each separate label and only one finest label is given to each news article, the reported feature extraction technique is word weighting. heading: 3.1 Introduction:
content: A spell checker determines the correctness of spelling in a given string based on the language set being used. Spell-checking is a major technology of sizable monolingual corpora. Some spell - checking application demands to find an error in a word and also to correct that erroneous word. In a spell checker application a d ictionary is required. The dictionary can be used as a database to store only valid words. As we know that a dictionary does not include proper nouns and mostly person names. So, we can say that it is essential to add a morphological analyser and a table o f proper nouns in our database. Else, we will not get the desired output. The key to this issue is to have a sizable monolingual. This process is categorized into three stages: Firstly, It detects erroneous or mistaken words. In this stage, lexical analyzer finds an error in the given string. In the second stage it suggest us words against the identified mistaken word.  In this stage, it generates likely candidates to replace the mistaken word. The third stage is automatic correction of errors. In this this stage, each candidate is assigned an error weight. Based on these weights the candidates are arranged from the most possible replacements to the least possible replacements.

heading: 3.2 Error detection:
content: The initial stage in spell checker system is to detect an erroneous or a mistaken string. This system finds the entered string in its dictionary. And then check that the entered string is correct or not. We discussed two possibilities below: (a) The misspelled word which is detected, is  correct. Spec ifically, detected string as a mistaken or a misspelled word is matching with any word in the dictionary or a database. These words are gener ally known as real errors . Look at this example, ‘device’  can be written as ‘devise’ or ‘طاقتور ’instead of ‘طاتقور .’ b) Identified mistaken word is not a valid string. Specifically, string identified as a mistake is not available in the dictionary of the program. Such as, substituting ‘betore’ as ‘before’ or ‘احتتام ’as ‘اختام.’ In this process we are not dealing with real word errors. It needs a full -bodied smart parser or a consistent stemmer. Though, many people attempted  to find the first type of errors  by using statistical methods. To define in simple way, a spell checker program finds a mistake in the given word. Then find that word in the database. And if that entered string does not exist in its database, it is a mistaken string. And  same rule goes for proper nouns, inflections a nd out-of-vocabulary words. These are known as mistaken words, until same situation arrived in this system. This is the phase to identify a mistaken word.

heading: 3.3 Generation of candidates:
content: Efficient systems have the ability to detect errors in a word. They also deliver the users with many suggestions for an identified mistake, as our users assume spell checker systems to propose word for erroneous words.

heading: 3.4 Correction of errors:
content: The detection of errors and giving more than one candidates, the next step is to arrange them. Replacing the most possible to the least possible. With the help of  many approaches, a weight is assigned with every candidate. Next, the suggested order is arranged. Such programs in which the computer interacts with the user, it is the computers task to rank the system  and selection task is performed by the user itself. This spell checker system does not have the ability for automatic correction of errors. The possible suggestions are showed according to their degree of edit distance. From the minimum edit distance to the maximum edit distance. The fact is, it is a kind of automatic ranking, from the most possible occurring suggestions to the least possible ones. The selection of a suitable substitute will be left to the user.

heading: 3.5 Types of errors:
content: Study of many previous people , shows us that there are four types of mistakes or errors which is the reason there are so many misspelled words. The errors can be categorized as below: a) Insertion: Having an extra alphabet in a correct word can lead to a wrong word. It does not matter where the alphabet is inserted. togerther in the place of together سیکیورٹیin the place of  سیکیوررٹی b) Deletion: removing any alphabet from a correct word, such as: winow in place of  window استعمالin place of استمال c) Substitution: altering and alphabet with another alphabet leading to a wrong word., such as: husitate in place of hesitate حکومتin place of حلومت d) Transposition: swap two alphabets in a single word can lead to a mistake or a wrong word, such as: Nutrition in place of nutrition منتخبin place of متنخب Above we have seen many error types. If these four types of error are found in a single character. It is known as single -error misspellings. If the above discussed errors are found in multiple characters, they are referred as multiple -error misspellings. The example for the second situation can be seen as, possibility that user will write ‘seituatoin’ in place of ‘situation’. As we can see that there are two types of errors being use d. It can also happen that a valid word is formed while a mistyping. For instance, the word ‘next’ may be written when the purpose is to write is ‘nest’ or the Urdu word ‘کاروائی ’ may be written as ‘کارروائی ,’ as both these Urdu words are correct.

heading: 3.6 Sources of errors:
content: There are numerous ways that an erroneous word can be created by a user or writer. Main aim is to tackle such type of errors which lead us to non -words. There are many sources for these type of errors. Such as: a) Typographic errors: These errors can be created when a writer types and does a mistake. Even though, the writer knows the original word but still makes a mistake. The word ‘silence’ in place of ‘silance’ or ‘احتچاج ’in place of ‘احتجاج ’are decent samples for this. b) Phonetic errors: These errors can be categorized as: (1) this kind of error can be produced due to less know-how to type an accurate string. For example, writing ‘goverment’ instead of ‘government’ and writing ‘اکستان ’instead of ‘پاکستان .’Urdu language have  numerous alphabets which have an unlike appearance, that might cause multiple issues. By looking at some example, letter ‘z’ has 4 different sounds in Urdu, these are: ‘ذ ,ز ,ض ,ظ ’and three different forms of a character that is‘s’  as ‘ث ,س ,ص’ .Each word having these letters, written in differently because of the writer’s lack of knowledge. The later error is created due to the sound of that word. For example, ‘caushion’ is a wrong word or it does not exist ‘caution’ is the true word. The string for Urdu i s, ‘خاہش ’ is written instead of ‘خواہش ,’ you can see that phonetic error is produced.

heading: The Algorithm:
content: Step 1: The entered string (ES) which  fails to show up in the database is to be taken as an erroneous word. Step 2: If the final string is searched in the database or a dictionary were found to be valid , yield the suggestion string for the mistaken word. Step 3: Initially combine ES to a string and after to the next string and then perform the above mentioned task and repeat this. Step 4: Replace every alphabet in ES with alphabets of Urdu step by step, after that perform the previous step again. Step 5: Remove every alphabet in ES step by step, and after doing this perform step 3 again. Step 6: One by one, insert letters of the Urdu alphabet in between two head-to-head alphabets and the 2 ends of ES, after doing this do step three again. Step 7:  Interchange each pair juxtaposed alphabets of ES, after finishing this repeat step number three.

heading: 4.1 Introduction:
content: The Part Of Speech (POS) Tagger is a tool in which an input text is entered in it allocates different parts of speech to every word in the given input. POS tagging is a major requirement for systems like Summarization. It is also a requirement in many advanced level natural language jobs. The major benefit is that we can get annotated corpora. Furtherly, these dataset can be useful for language study. To produce improved taggers, for several other language-processing tasks. There are many systems created for POS tagging.  Some knowledge-based taggers are implemented by using statistical approaches. There are also many developed  programs that merge several implementations with a voting process. This effort shows a learning to find a  suitable method to train a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) POS tagger. When dealing with languages with a small number of training dataset. We match many smoothing approaches and many orders of this model. After training the tagger we perform different tests to choose the best configuration. We then repeat these steps for the training corpus in Urdu language to cement our results. For every Hidden Markov model, we configure out tests in a different way. We use three types of Hidden Markov model, and two smoothing techniques. We use all of this to determine the parameters of our model.

heading: 4.2 Existing Urdu POS Tag sets:
content: With respect to Urdu language, different POS tagsets have been designed. The very first POS tagset was designed by Hardie in 2003. He uses the EAGLES guidelines (Hardie, 2003). It is purely based on morpho-syntactic classes of Urdu language. It has 350 tags. We know that the greater the tag numbers the more complexity is created. There has been constrained follow up work dependent on this tagset, outside the initial POS tagger through the EMILLE project (Lüdeling & Kytö, 2008). Later on, Sajjad (2007) & Sajjad & Schmid (2009) designed a tagset. This tagset consist of 42 tags. It also contains finer distinctive categories for pronouns. But, it did not do enough integrity to the Urdu verbal and tense program. In 2008, another tagset2 was designed by the Center for Research on Urdu Language Processing (CRULP). This tagset follows the guidelines of the Penn Treebank. This tagset contains 46 tags. In this tagset, a verb category has many tags based on the morphology of the verbs. Also, common nouns were also categorized with fine  distinctions.  Muaz, A li & Hussain (2009) compared  two tagsets and proposed a different tagset. This tagset has 32 tags. 17 tags are identical as in the earlier two tagsets, but changes among kinds of nouns,  were removed as their syntactic distribution is same.

heading: 4.3 Tag set Design:
content: We studied the design and tags of previously available tagsets. And provided a tagset which includes many functionalities. This Urdu POS tagset is legitimately various leveled in nature i.e. it

conveys 12 essential POS types and afterward 35 sub-types. We have likewise included, erased and blended diverse labels based on: (an) examination with different taggers, (b) syntactic appropriation and other phonetic issues. Basically, this tagset is proposing labels that are intrigued by a promptly recognizable transform syntactic example and conveyance. Coming up next is a point by point depiction of the labels.

heading: 4.3.1  Noun:
content: It is partitioned in 2 categories, (I) Common noun (NN) (II) Proper noun (NNP). We calculated that one POS tag will be allocated to multiword and name objects. heading: 4.5.2  Smoothing:

All of these approaches include, minimising the probability allocated to all the seen events and thus distributing the lasting mass between  the hidden events. For this effort, we considered two smoothing approaches: Laplace law and Linear Interpolation.

heading: 5.1 Introduction:
content: Text classiﬁcation is a system which categorizes the documents into predeﬁned set of topic classes. In text classiﬁcation we are  only considering the multiclass classiﬁcation whereas in the binary classiﬁcation there are more than two possible classes. The goal is to assign a related topic to a document after reading it. The algorithm used in text classification is a part of a complex s ystem and is used for keeping large volumes of text data. Since it has been shown that not only the size of the training data is important, but also the right scope of the language models in training texts is needed. The  topic identiﬁcation algorithm is us ed for large scale language modelling  and data ﬁltering. The  discriminative techniques like support vector machines (SVMs), decision trees, gradient boosting and neural networks  are some of the main approaches to text classification. It describes a method based on general topic model normalization for ﬁnding a threshold which defines a boundary between the “correct” and the “incorrect” topi cs of a newspaper article in generative classiﬁcation techniques. The generative classiﬁer outputs a distribution of probabilities and a method for processing this d istribution into the sets of “correct” and  “incorrect” topics is needed. The proposed method is used to get the better results of decision trees and gradient boosting in the topic identiﬁcation module.

heading: 5.3 Multi-Target Text Classification:
content: Classification: The current known mechanisms for multi label classification can be split into 2 main categories. First, there is the data transformation (DT) method category via which problems are modified to single label classification problems. The secon d category focuses on algorithm adaption methods which enable the existing algorithms to work with multi label data without deviation. We may subdivide the existing data transformation methods; DT1 and DT2 being the first 2 techniques simply alter the multi-label data set into single-label. Technique DT1 chooses one out of the many labels given for each data occurrence while DT2 discards all multi -label data occurrences in the set. The two techniques cannot really be used in a multi-label classiﬁcation since they remove all the stored multi-label information. DT3, the third technique, recognises each set of labels as a single label. Therefore, the single label classiﬁer could potentially be used, choosing one of the pre-determined sets of labels for each set. There are, however, disadvantages of this method. First and foremost, one may end up with a great number of label sets while there would be limited examples of training data for each set. Furthermore, we would not be allowed to assign distinct label compounds to the classiﬁed data instead of those seen in the training data. The most trivial data transformation technique, DT4, and also used as a baseline for other methods testing. This method trains a binary one -vs.-rest classiﬁer for each class. The binary classifier returns a positive output for the labels and this output is accredited to the tested data instance. Like any other, this method too has its disadvantages. Firstly, you would have to alter the dataset into |X| datasets, containing only positive and negative examples. Secondly, you would have to ﬁnd the threshold for each and every binary classiﬁer. The DT5 method, disintegrates each training data with ‘p’ labels into ‘p’ data items, each with only one label. One classiﬁer with the distribution of likeliness for all labels is then derived from the transformed data set. The distribution is then processed to ﬁnd the correct labels of the data item.

Using DT6, each training data item is disintegrated into |X| data items each with only one label x and a value Y (x), where Y (x)=1 for the labels corresponding to the data item  and Y (x)=  −1 contrarily. The algorithm adaptation methods are techniques administering the multi -label data directly or techniques merge one of the DT methods with an existing assignment method.

heading: 5.4.1  Feature selection:
content: Feature selection is one of the better ways to extract a feature set. Useless features such as noise are removed, this results in reducing the size of the feature set and hence the chances of over fitting are reduced. The smaller the feature set is; the less time it will take to p rocess it. Using this dimensionality reduction, the training time of the algorithm can be reduced quite significantly without any actual performance loss. For instance, we can remove the words that have the highest frequency as they are just increasing our  computation time but not actually contributing towards improving the overall performance of our algorithm.

heading: 5.4.2 Train/Test:
content: We divide our dataset into two parts. Namely, the training part and the test part. The training data contains ground truths and labels using which we will classify our test data or the actual data for which we are preparing for. The test part of the dataset is used to test that whether or not the training we have done on similar data is accurate enough to classify this data. If the model is ideally trained (there is neither under fitting nor overfitting) then it will accurately classify the test data based on the training performed on the train data.

heading: 5.4.3 Cross Validation:
content: Cross validation is the process to check the accuracy of our model as compared to other models or to check which model would suit best to our needs by training our data on several different models and deciding which one best satisfies our needs. We define a variable k that divides our dataset into several different subsets which is equal to the number of models we are going to train it on. This is known as k-fold cross validation. Fig. 9 k-fold cross validation

The value of k can be chosen by any of the following methods:  Representative method: We chose the value of k keeping in mind that the test data should be sufficient to accurately statistically depict our dataset.  k=10 method: The more commonly used cross validation method. Also known as 10-fold cross validation. It has tested to yield the best results in most scenarios.  k=n method: Also known as leave-one-out cross-validation. Where k is equal to the size of the dataset.

heading: 5.5 Text Classification Module:
content: The aim of the text classification module is to ﬁlter the large amount of data according to their topics. Text classification  module used a Gradient boosting  and Decision tree classiﬁcation algorithms. It also assigned topics selected from a hierarchical system - a “topic tree” to each article.

heading: 5.5.1 Classification Algorithm:
content: Currently, the version of the text classifier module uses a Gradient boosting and Decision tree classiﬁer. It is selected  because of the experiments result . It is known to be th e fastest learning classiﬁer. But, it has better accuracy than Random Forest classifier. For our goal Gradient boosting and Decision tree classiﬁer is the best approach. As stated earlier, our text classifier runs in a real application. The articles are stored in a database, so the “training” of the classifier is done simply by counting the statistics. These containing the number of occurrences of each word in the whole collection, number of occurrences of each word in each document and the number of occurrences of each word in the documents belonging to a topic. Gradient boosting is  robust technique for developing predictive models. It is a machine learning technique for regression and classification problems. It generates a prediction model by combining weak prediction models, usually decision trees. The purpose of any supervised learning algorithm is to define a loss function to be optimized, a weak learner to make predictions and additive model to add weak learners to minimize the loss function. Mathematically, gradient boosting can be represented as: Suppose, we have mean squared error (MSE) as loss defined as: We want our predictions, such that our loss function (MSE) is minimum. With the help of gradient, descent and modifying our predictions based on a learning rate, we can find the values where MSE is minimum.

The predictions are being updated such that the sum of our residuals is adjacent to 0 (or minimum) and predicted values are adequately adjacent to actual values.  Gradient boosting is a greedy algorithm. It  is suitable for  a training d ataset. It can benefit from regularization methods that penalize various parts of the algorithm . It usually  boosts the performance of the algorithm by reducing overfitting. A decision tree is a directional graph. It contains many nodes. A directional graph starts from the base with a single node and spreads to the many leaf nodes. This shows the tree’s classification of the categories. It acts like a  decision-support tool. It  uses a tree -like representation to show the predictions. Fig. 10 Decision tree structure The components of a decision tree can be described as:  Root Node: The starting note, depicts the whole population.  Leaf Nodes: The ending nodes (that do not have any children).  Splitting: Splitting a node into sub-nodes.

 Decision Node: If we split a sub-node further, it is called as decision node.  Pruning: Removing some of the sub-nodes is known as pruning.  Branch: Any sub-portion of the tree is called as a branch  Parent Node and Child Node: A node following another node is called a child node and its predecessor is known as its parent node.

content: Text classiﬁcation assigns one or more classes to a document according to their topic. The goal of goal of our system is to read a documents and then assign a topic related to it. We will be developing our system in Python language. Python language has extensive support libraries, which reduces the length of code. Most importantly, python has a natural language toolkit. . The toolkit we are using is very reliable and has many text pre-processing libraries.  Python language is a viable option for our system. We have used Pycharm for implementing Python language. Pycharm is the most widely used IDE for Python Language. In our system, the dataset we need is in an annotated form. We will input this dataset in our system. After that we will encode the dataset. After encoding we will split up or divide the dataset. The major portion of our dataset will be used for training purpose. The remaining portion will be used for testing. For validating the dataset, we will be using 10-fold cross validation. After that we will apply classifiers. We have used two classifiers for our system: (I) Decision tree, (II) Gradient boosting. On the last we will calculate results for our system. For results we w ill be using three methods: (I) Accuracy, (II) Hamming loss and (III) Exact match.

heading: 6.1 Summary:
content: In this research, we have developed three novel computational linguistics analysis tools for Urdu language spell checker, hybrid POS tagger and text classifier. We have designed and developed these three tools completely. We have shown each and every phase  of the development process. These three tools were designed using rule-based, dictionary lookup, stochastic methods and hybrid methods. We have also developed benchmark corpus for these tools  and described the corpus generation process. As corpus generation was one of the main phase. We have also explained the methodology of these tools individually. The methodology include system diagram, user - interaction diagram, flowchart and the interface for our application. Then we have explained the techniques, appr oaches or models we are using. Finally, we have concluded our results. For improving our results, we have defined some rules. Our finalized results were very convincing. We have also concluded evaluation measures for our three text processing tools.

heading: 6.2 Conclusion:
content: In this paper, we have described a novel computational linguistics analysis tools of the Urdu language spell checker, hybrid POS tagger and text classifier. We have designed, develop ed, evaluated and tested tools. Text processing tools formulated around rule-based, dictionary lookup, and stochastic methods. Our results have shown state-of-the-art performance and thus can be used as a baseline for future improvements. In addition to developing the software tools, our second set of contributions are the design, collection, manual annotation and release of Urdu corpora to enable comparative evaluations to be performed in the future.

heading: 6.3 Future work
content: We would like to improve the performance of tools by employing state-of-the-art machine learning techniques. Increase the size of datasets. Develop other Urdu NLP tools. Create an automatic tool for the semantic analysis of Urdu text building on these important foundations.

heading: 2.6 Software development life cycle model
content: In our Final Year Project we have used Iterative model from Software development life cycle model. The iterative model focus on initialisation of the project. Moreover, in iterative model, the iterative process starts with a simple implementation of a small set of the software requirements, which iteratively enhances the evolving versions until the complete system is implemented and ready to be deployed. In iterative model requirements meet gradually during the development. The iterative model have different stages. i.e.

heading: 1. Planning and requirement:
content: The first step to start any project is planning. Planning needs to go through the initial planning and make documentation and to meet the requirements.

heading: 2. Analysis and design:
content: After the planning is completed we are required to analyse the program logics and database model of the project. In designing process we need to establish the technical requirements i.e. language, services, data layers, platform of programming etc.

heading: 3. Implementation
content: After the planning, requirements, analysis and design there is the implementation process. Implementation process is the part where we apply all our planning and analysis to shape our project. All the coding building is completed in implementation process.

heading: 4. Testing
content: After the development of the project it is tested in series to find the bugs and errors. Due to the iterative process if the bugs are found we remove the bugs gradually (implemented immediately) and test again.

heading: 5. Evaluation:
content: Once testing is done successfully and all the prior parts are done efficiently. Whole project is checked thoroughly in the presence of whole team, clients as well other third parties for better reviews and feedback. After the evaluation if any problem is found the whole process repeats again, move back to the stage remove the error and move to next step again. Advantages of Iterative model: i. The iterative model is rapid process ii. Easily adaptable for almost every kind of project iii. Advance planning, increases efficiency iv. Less time in documentation and more time in development (implementation). Disadvantages of Iterative model: i. It is costly. ii. More dependent on user feedback. iii. Wastage of time if errors are found.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: The background or idea of the application is to minimize the distance between the one who is currently looking  forward building something but does not have the estimated cost and information required regarding the construction of that building and the one who does have the necessary information i.e. constructor and raw material providers. One can be provided with the estimation of material required e.g. tiles required for per room etc. The aim is to create a link be tween these two entities to ensure innovativeness and uniqueness of the idea i.e. Constructor – one touch away from the client. We will create the  dataset for the two entities each having their unique IDs. A separate database for the client shall be made h aving all the essential information required from the client and for the client to help operate him/her throughout the application. The user can select the plot area for the building i.e. 5-marla, 10- marla etc. The application will provide the user with some samples of the buildings desired. Furthermore, the user can contact the contractor or material provider, lightening with desired information. The main purpose which is covered at the client -end is to enlighten him with the ongoing innovations and neces sities in the field of construction to help him out in building the desired structure with proper consultancy and requirements fulfilled by the contractor-end with the help of this application. The thought of constructing something without the hurdles of d aily hustle and bustle ensures the client to use the application for a bigger purpose securing his goodwill for the application. Now coming to the part of contractor end. The contact numbers and references to their respective offices or shops shall be provided by the application. One can contact or arrange a meeting with the working official of the contractor. A database shall be created to store the information regarding top contractors and their ratings (by general public). The client can contact directly  to the contractor providing him with professional guidance creating a wave of consistency in the constructions by minimizing all the errors which could occur if professional advice is lacked or neglected. The contractor gains ratings if the advice or material provided satisfies the client resulting in the bright future of the application and maximum number of users. The design of the application will be user friendly providing all categories of users to easily understand and operate the application. Every user must be registered to use the application. One can simply register by filling in the required anomalies. The required information will allow both the entities to maintain a certain relation and ensure security of the deal. Different views and perspect ive of the users shall be entertained through the categorization of buildings and contractors to choose from. The development shall be done by using the most renowned android application developer tools such Android Studio, SQL Server, Sketch, XAMPP etc. for the best production of the application. From this application the person who was looking for someone’s guide line can easily contact to the top ranked constructor and material provider and know all the estimates, rates and designs which are necessary for building his house, office or shop etc. From this easiness he will reduce his expenses rather than paying to a consultant or by giving all his time to visiting all the distributors he will directly set a meeting to constructor and will know all the estim ates on one click, he will also select all his desired products which will use in future construction of his house by opening the material provider portion in this application. Therefore this application will convert all the construction work in smarter way and everyone who will want to build his dream house belonging any life style use this application and fulfil his dreams. `

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: The objectives of our project are as follows:  We provide the user with the facility to construct his home according to his budget i.e. to select the desired map proportional to his plot size.  To provide the estimation of the material + construction cost of the building in accordance to the current market rates.  A list of contractors sorted according to user ratings, best contractor comes on the top of the list and vice versa, allowing the user to get a better understanding of the system and to explore better options.  In contrast to list of contractors, the top material providers (suppliers) updated information shall be provided for those who are interested in building their own homes.  A complete database is designed to keep track of all the records, this will surely enhance the user experien ce providing ease in access regarding the different functions/features of the application  We provide the available plots images along with their details with seller contact number so if someone is looking for a plot first then he/she check out the availabl e plots in their desired location and area. These information will added by our self in database at first stage.  We provide the structural designs of homes according to plot size.  For contact with contractors and distributors, we add massaging facility so the user will contact with contactor or distributor and set a meeting.

heading: Abstract:
content: As High spatial resolution (HSR) imagery becomes more and more easily available, the efforts to extract information out of these images more efficiently and autonomously becomes more important. In our project we aim to find an easier and more efficient method that focuses on extracting information from HSR images. In particular, we would like to p ropose a method that would get rid of the mathematically intensive numerical computations and come up with a more simpler method to identify regions of interest in urban areas. After coming up with a good approach to do so we hope to apply this knowledge to identify buildings and roads and separate them from other terrains. This will be done in order to provide a system that autonomously finds the best evacuation route in the case of an earthquake.

heading: 1.1 Introduction:
content: HSR images are very high-resolution aerial images of the earth taken from satellites. The branch of image processing that deals with the capturing, working and analysis of HSR images is known as remote sensing. In literal meaning Remote sensing is the process of gathering inf ormation about an object remotely i.e. without ever making physical contact with it. In Digital image processing remote sensing means to observe and analyse information of the earth via pictures taken using a satellite. Remote sensing is very useful mainly due to the fact that it helps us analyse the earth with a whole new perspective and from a point of view that is not attainable by regular photography. HSR images are used for a wide number of purposes in almost all fields of everyday life [1, 2]. One of the fields where aerial imaging is used is journalism. With the news media being one of the biggest industries in the world, they want to get better and innovative at how they are reporting their news. Aerial reporting is one thing that they are focusing on for this purpose. Also, in case of a dangerous situation where on field presence might put the journalist’s life in jeopardy, aerial photography can be of great help as coverage can be provided from the air. Another use for such imagery is in the field of precision agriculture  [3]. Precision agriculture means to better the production rate of crops using computerized methods. This methodology of farming utilizes satellite images to observe and analyse crops for better production, disease detection etc. Surveillance is also a field that has been eager to utilize aerial photography, but surveillance on low - resolution images wasn’t very reliable. HSR imagery can help get over this hurdle and make aerial imagery feasible for surveillance. Another use for HSR images is Cartography i.e. taking aerial images and using them to create digital maps. As digital maps are getting more and more accessible, efforts are being made to utilize them for more useful purposes. This includes gathering information about the landscapes of urban areas as well as construction planning on a small scale. Another use of such maps is the semantic labelling of images. This labelling can be used for a number of purposes s uch as disaster evaluation, deriving shore etc. Our FYP focuses on making this labelling more automated, easier and efficient. This project will be worked on the SpaceNet dataset [4] provided by AWS. It consists of 8 band tagg ed spatial imagery along with ground truths in geojson format.

heading: 10 of 57  02 January 2019
content: Figure 1: An 8-band image from the SpaceNet dataset From an application point of view, we are going to be making a tool that can provide us with the safest/fastest route in case of disaster i.e. an earthquake. As mentioned above our program will differentiate between buildings and other terrain as well as i dentify the roads on the map. Using this information, we will analyse what route will be the best if we want to evacuate people from any point of the map.

heading: 1.2 Objectives:
content: The following are the objectives of this final year project:

heading: 1.2.1 Objective 1:
content: Our first objective that will focuses more on the research part, specifically on making the processing on HSR images better and easier. • To speed up labelling of HSR images. • To make up HSR image labelling more efficient • To propose a method for labelling HSR images that doesn’t include intensive calculations.

heading: 1.2.2 Objective 2:
content: To make a working application that will help in finding the best route possible in case of an earthquake based on the geographical factors that can come into play.

heading: 11 of 57  02 January 2019
content: • To label the buildings and roads from other terrain. • Identify densely populated areas. • Decide which route would work best in case of an earthquake.

heading: 1.3 Problem Statement:
content: With HSR images being more and more easily available, the need to process these images more efficiently and autonomously is becoming more and more important. We aim to provide a method that does precisely this i.e. we are going to be providing a method that does the semantic labelling of HSR images in a more easy and efficient way. This can help in further processing of HSR images such as using them to find some routes etc. We are also going to be putting our new -found algorithm to use by developing an application for rescue officials that provides them with optimal routes in case of emergencies.

heading: 1.4.1 Constraints:
content: • There will be no connectivity i.e. the rescue official will not have internet services. • The user must have a cell phone with enough storage to store a small amount of HSR images.

heading: 1.4.2 Assumptions:
content: • The user understands how a navigation application works.

heading: 1.5 Motivation and Scope:
content: According to a paper presented by Roger Bilham of the University of Colorado in Boulder in an annual meeting of the Geological Society of America, the magnitude and frequency of earthquakes that the world will face in 2018 is going to increase significantly  [5]. According to the paper we can face up to 20 devastating earthquakes per year starting from 2018. We are not even facing half of these numbers at the moment and even now it is extremely difficult for us to combat the aftermaths of these disasters. Our project aims to help in such situations, specifically in evacuating people in case of such a disaster. One of the major problems that rescue officials face in such scenarios is that they are unable to reach the people that are in dire need of help. This is mainly due to three reasons. Number one, being that some of the buildings might have collapsed and are now hindering the way of rescuers that need to get through. Secondly because earthquakes cause a state of panic among the people and they rush to check the safety of their loved ones. This results in the streets getting jam -packed leaving no way for the rescuers to pass

heading: 12 of 57  02 January 2019
content: through and do their work. And the final reason being that most of the times in the event of a disaster we are unable to get any reception on our phones which means no online access to maps which ultimately results in the rescuers playing guessing games on what route would work the best with no factual knowledge. We will develop an offline mobile application that would help rescue officials in finding a route that will be best suited for them in such scenarios. This will save their time and hopefully a lot of lives as well.
