heading: 5.1 Problems faced and lessons learned
content: Completing this project has not been without its challenges. We had decided to develop an application software on a platform and a language unfamiliar to us. Whereas we could have worked on a web application where the platform and language would have been familiar. By making this choice we had already prepared ourselves for a challenge. The various modules of this project were new to us we had worked on them throughout the project and applying these to an application software were relatively a new experience to us. The first real issue we have faced was when deciding the scope of this application. When you are an active developer like ourselves, you always want the maximum important features in an application and we had a tough task of deciding on the scope of this application by keeping two very important things in mind: the time constraint and the user. This would not have been an issue if we were familiar with application development at that stage, we had no idea how much time it would take to finish a certain module so we had t o think long and hard before deciding on adding a feature to our application. Gathering requirements was another problem. This was only really a problem because of the extremely short list of stakeholders and at the stage where we are currently like being new to industry or market makes it more troublesome. There was no customer for whom this product was being developed from whom we could collect the most important requirements. The requirements mainly came from the developers, being us, and the potential users of this application. Developing use case models, diagrams and the software architecture to be used was another problem because as mentioned earlier doing these for an application was completely new to us. After doing a lot of research; reading article s and looking at samples and with guidance from our supervisor we managed to complete that. These were the major problems that we faced during this phase. We would refer to them as challenges rather than problems and we got to learn from them.

heading: 5.2 Project Summary
content: Developing desktop application is a bit different from developing websites or mobile applications. Using the knowledge and skills acquired over the course of seven semesters we have had to relate and find similarities between what we have b een taught and what goes into developing a desktop application. With the help of our corresponding teachers, project supervisor and assistant supervisor we have managed to complete this documentation. We have been quite privileged to have been taught courses like software engineering and advanced software engineering, which includes topics like requirement specification, software quality management, software design and architecture and software project management. Page 109 of 117  19 December 2018 These courses have gone a long way in helping us develop the models, gather requirements and construct related diagrams. Through this we have instructed in this document all the various techniques we will be using and what structure we would follow and the process by which different activities will be carried out. We have clearly defined the requirements, so we would have no issues of creeping requirements or missing out on any critical requirement during the development phase. We have come up  with the suitable architecture for this project, so we would have a more structured approach and the work we will produce will not be a disordered one. The software process model to be used has also been defined. By working on this document we have insure d that the development phase passes without any major trouble.

heading: Introduction
content: Our project has of multiple modules which provide different dimensions of facilitating Teacher regarding students major, modules of our project are

heading: 3. Quiz system
content: Attendance module Even though most of the Institutes are using Online Attendance System such as CU Online in case of COMSATS but still teacher faces the problem of manually marking the Attendance of each student present in the class on the spot. According to these traditional systems teachers has a list of registered students and they call the name of each student, present student must respond in loud voice to validate his/her presence, no response means absence of a student. On average 15 minutes are spend on marking attend ance of 40 students in the class. These 15 min could be made useful if included in lecture or one could conduct a quiz in this time. Now we see the trend of Smart phone possession has quite matured in our society and it is the most rear case to see anyone without smartphone especially in Academic domain. So, our project is intended to put smart phones as a mean to literally automate attendance systems. This could be achieved through using Geofencing via smart phones of students. Real geographical areas of e ach class room in a campus will be assigned virtual perimeters and when a device leaves or enter a certain perimeter resultantly a response would be generated. Here we will categorize the response into two type one will be generated when the student enters the university perimeter this type of alert response will be treated as notification to parents that a student has entered the university and other alert response will be generated this will mark his attendance automaticity when a student enters a room’s perimeter. Attendance marked will be stored in in a database.

heading: Notification Module
content: Aim of this module is make parents aware of their children’s activities when they are within University. Through this functionality guardians will be able to know that when their child has reached the university, if more specific they would also be able to know that which lecture have been attended or not by their child This module will provide the functionality of delivering mobile message alert to a guardian’s device when a student enters a university perimeter and even if he does not enter university perimeter at a certain time of day. pg. 6

heading: Quiz Conducting Module
content: Quizzes are very essential activity to be conducted in a class for the evaluation purpose as well as for the driving the students to study more. Quizzes are part of every educational institute. So, we see that the most common way of conducting the quiz is in hard form i.e. on paper. This overhead the teacher with distributing paper to individuals of class and lat er collecting these quizzes and above all is the checking and marking of a quiz for a single teacher. The module is developed to automated quiz system. This means that a teacher will write a quiz and its solution in the faculty facilitator app and then he/ she will make it available to student mobile phone, as the quiz is online time will start on the timer of each student, if quiz page is closes on the app then the quiz will be cancelled or ceased. Once all students have completed the quiz with in time, it will be evaluated against the solution result will be generated spontaneously. Marks will be uploaded in database and a notification of marks will be sent to parents

heading: Objectives
content: Major objective of this project is • Cross platform application for students with functionality to mark attendance based of location, Attend quiz and view reports in an automated fashion. Expected outcome: android application and an iOS application. Success criteria: ❖ no manual calling of student’s name for attendance ❖ no need for quizzes on papers ❖ auto generation of reports to view on mobile app • Cross platform application for teachers with functionality to validate and mark attendance for students, upload quizzes and view class reports of marks and attendance. Expected outcome:  android application and an iOS application. Success criteria: ❖ Elimination of writing and distribution of quiz among class students. ❖ Elimination of manual checking of quizzes ❖ No manual uploading of ❖ Automatic generation of student reports based on data from daily attendance and quizzes & assignments. • Web application that provides all functionality like mobile app Expected outcome: a web application Success criteria: ❖ All criteria like mobile application. • Design and implement a database to automate the manual record keeping system. pg. 7 Expected outcome: a ready to deploy database for the Institute. Success criteria ❖ Record repository of 30,000 students along with function required. ❖ After deployment of this database no paper work would be required. ❖ A reduction of up to 50 % in the Human Resources required by this institute to maintain records. Problem statement: Faculty member spend 10 to 15 minutes in marking attendance of students in Cu Online portal and faculty members attendance is manually marks during lectures, the aim of our “Smart Class System” is to automate the attendance of students using geo-fencing, so faculty member could more time on lecture delivering and manual marking of faculty member is automated. Creating quiz for students, distributing them in class, collecting quizzes from students when they are done with it and uploading the marks of a quiz is a hectic job. And in COMSATS university, minimum four quizzes are mandatory. For each assigned section, faculty member has a lot of work to do. Smart Class System will automate quiz process for both faculty members and students. Assumptions & constraints

heading: Abstract
content: “Kashif Spinning Mills” is a yarn manufacturing company. They import its raw material from several countries. Its raw material is acrylic tow and after applying several processes on it, they manufacture yarn. The company manages its records on note books, in which they face many difficulties because their entries are very enormous in number. That’s why we will computerize their records of stock products and daily production reports, maintain their clients’ accounts, and track their sales of raw materials an d manufactured products. Their raw materials are Acrylic Tow, Acrylic Tops, Fibre etc. Their manufactured products include yarn of different counts, varieties and colors. If we find time we will try to develop an online ordering system as well. The company  requires separate interfaces for manager and every other user. P a g e  | 4 Table of Contents

heading: Chapter 1 – Introduction
content: “Your career is your business. It’s time for you to manage it as a CEO.”

heading: –– Dorit Sher
content: Accounting exists in every field where there is some sort of selling or buying of goods. Every transaction is required to be recorded to keep track of the money and the products. Business is that field which cannot even exist without accounting. If the business coincides with the manufacturing procedure, the accounting becomes  more essential part of it. Every procedure is required to be noted down.

heading: Objectives
content: In our project, we will focus on computerizing the stock department, accounts report generation and tracking of product delivery till its sale. We will integrate the systems (soft-wares) of these departments so that manager can see the stock information, order details, account reports and customer statements. The software will be web based so its users will be able to access it online at any place where internet is available. Moreover, admin will have access to create user and grant permissions to them to use the software features except reports, because only admin will have access to see reports.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Kashif Spinning Mills has four departments which need to be computerized. First department handles the orders from customers. These orders are written on an order book. Their customers place orders on telephones, which can cause misunderstanding and someti mes results in a huge problem for both customer and manufacturer. Second department deals with the stock. They maintain stock records on stock book s. The company keeps the demand of its customers on priority. They manufacture the fresh yarn on order. They seldom keep manufactured yarn in stock, and to achieve this task they must keep the report of raw material stock updated, so that they would be aware of the available colour and quantity to issue it on time for manufacturing. Third department maintains the cash transactions made on daily basis. Fourth department maintains the records of delivering products to the customers against their orders. All the above departments maintain their records in handwritten form. They all face problem while matching previous records to prepare any report or while searching the records of previous dates. Another major issue is of security which we must cover on. The software will be web based, so we need to apply authentication o n admin and users. Admin will create user and restrict him/her to use specific portion of the software.

heading: Assumptions & Constraints
content: The following constraints were believed to possibly limit the development of the project: • The time for the project wa s limit ed. All modules of th e project we re required to be completed in nine months. • Project was expected to be functional by the end of the academic year. • Applying of proper accounting principles can cause the development difficult and slow. • Understanding and designing the software  exactly according to the working style of that factory can be difficult to attain. P a g e  | 8

heading: Project Scope
content: Our software will facilitate the factory  management, owner and accountants. The software will maintain the record of all purchases, orders, accounts and clients’ information. The customers will be facilitated by evincing their reports on a well formatted design with all details of their purchases and payments between any dates. Manager can get the report of stock at any time which will help him to take his managing decisions faster than before. Currently, the management of Kashif Spinning Mills follows the manual procedure of filling books to maintain their stock records, orders details, daily production records and gate passes. It is very difficult to maintain this procedure on higher level when a lot of entries are recorded per day. We are doing this project to unravel their problems of dealing with immense number of entries. The Owner/Manager will have authority to see the reports anytime at any place on web. The application will show all transactions, pending orders, make a new order and deliver them within specific period. Factory have four people on specific posts which will use this software.

heading: Chapter 2 – Requirements Analysis
content: “The word accounting comes from the word accountability. If you are going to be rich, you need to be accountable for your money.”

heading: –– Robert T. Kiyosaki
content: This chapter is the non -ambivalent description for the users, developers and stakeholders of our software. All the requirements, functional and non -functional both, will be notified and well explained in this chapter. The requirements will help the developers to organise, design and develop the software utterly according to the customer requirements.

heading: Literature Review
content: The accounting exists, since the business exists in this world. In the prehistoric periods, people traded by using barter system [5]. In barter system, people directly trade by  exchanging goods without using any medium like money etc. But some rules, regulations and agreements must exist while they trade. With the passage of time, trends started changing and ways of trading also affected with that change. People now started using mediums like money while exchanging goods and services. The concept of money instigates two new concepts in trading, credit and debit, which laid the basis of accounting. P a g e  | 9 Accounting, at its beginning, was performed on books which is known as “Bookkeeping”. When the transactions increased in numbers, it was very difficult for accountants to generate trial balance, balance sheets, income statements etc. When this issue was pr opagating, the technology of computer science was also broadening at its full sprint. Accounting soft wares provide the best solution for this issue. Computers can handle these enormous number of transactions and generate reports in very less time. All models of businesses require unique software which works according to their demands and requirements. Same software can never work for all models of businesses. Manufacturing process was never too arduous. But now the manufacturing procedures have expanded to a large scale that they also need computers to record the transaction of goods from one department to the other and generate reports. Here are some soft wares which are used for accounting purposes:

heading: • Gnu Cash [1]
content: o Gnu Cash is accounting software, which can merely perform simple book keeping task and it is ranked first in accounting soft wares. This software is for small businesses and cannot perform tasks which our client requires for his factory. • TurboCash [2] o This software is for small size businesses and is just for accounting purposes. It is a general software not for a specific industry. So, our client cannot use this software because it lacks resemblance with his business procedures. • Apache OpenOffice [3] o This software is for people who trade. A businessman with manufacturing plant cannot take any benefit from this software, because this software only records incoming and outgoing of goods with some small number of accounts.

heading: • Admin Soft Accounts [4]
content: o Admin Soft Accounts is simple application used to  keep records of money transactions. It doesn’t support the feature to add and manipulate data of goods and manufacturing processes. • QuickBooks [6] o Quick Books is an elegant application which provides best solutions for accounting problems. It is an online software. It also maintain s purchase invoices but still the company cannot use it because  it does not have feature of handling the records of manufacturing processes of the company.  Besides this, the company wants a specific software according to its own requirements which the QuickBooks doesn’t provide.

heading: Stakeholders List
content: Stake holders of this software are those who have to  interact with it for any reason, directly or indirectly. This software will provide an easy and efficient provision for the problems to the company that it can view statistics in the form of pie charts and other graphical formats. Reports will be generated and evinced to manager in a perfect methodical way so that the he will sense the professional texture in them. Stakeholders list is as follows: P a g e  | 10

heading: • Owner
content: This software means a lot to the owner (manager) of the factory, because they need a very specific and complete software, solely for their own factory. T hey have searched for the built-in soft wares online but they didn’t get any single software, which fulfils their requirements. That’s why they contacted us to develop a software solely for their company.

heading: • Accountants
content: Accountants are currently using a software which is not providing them facility to operate it on any PC. So, for the sake of privacy of secret accounts, the manager does not hand over the PC to any person accept data entry clerk . This leads to disaster for maintaining stock, because stock is maintained by other accountants to whom handing over PC is very risky. Our software will help them to cater the draw backs of their previous software and provide security of data by  giving the authority of a ccessing any feature of software to the accountants or any other user which will also be created by the admin . This software will be web based and they can access it everywhere through internet under their assigned privileges.

heading: • Customers
content: This software will help to handle the orders, order deliveries and customer accounts. This software will create a customer statement on which every transaction of customer is described in detail. Customers will find it leisure to get their statements with a proper professional theme.

heading: Software Architecture
content: We are doing this project as a real-time project for Kashif Spinning Mills located in Gujranwala. They asked us to develop a software which will automate their process of accounting also managing their stock, production and client’s orders as well. So, Purpose is to design and develop a product which will not only FYP but will be a working product that will be used by their accountants to manage their accounts and manufacturing processes. Previously developed software’s only manages the accounts but doesn’t provides the facility of managing the orders, stock and productions all in one place so this will be the unique thing in this project. P a g e  | 31 The software architecture is designed in this manner that both accountants and the manager have their own separate p anels which they can open simultaneously on different internet enabled devices. This software will not be like other congested soft wares, where every person must view, add or update entries on a single PC. In our case, for example Admin create s three accounts of users which need to do specific tasks on the software. Accountant 1 will handle all the work regarding to stock and order delivery on hi s own internet enabled device and can save the respective data. Accountant 2 will handle all the accounts which include customer account, supplier account, expense account, assets, liabilities, revenue etc., on his internet enabled device and can save the respective data. Manager can handle all the information regarding orders on his internet enabled device.  Every addition or updating of a new order will be saved. Manager can view reports  of various types of almost all accounts.

heading: Dorit Sher
content: Accounting exists in every field where there is some sort of selling or buying of goods. Every transaction is required to be recorded to keep track of the money and the products. Business is that field which cannot even exist without accounting. If the business coincides with the manufacturing procedure, the accounting becomes more essential part of it. Every procedure is required to be noted down. Objectives In our project, we will focus on computerizing the stock department, accounts report generation and tracking of product delivery till its sale. We will integrate the systems (soft-wares) of these departments so that manager can see the stock information, order details, account reports and customer statements. The software will be web based so its users will be able to access it online at any place where internet is available. Moreover, admin will have access to create user and grant permissions to them to use the software features except reports, because only admin will have access to see reports. Problem Statement Kashif Spinning Mills has four departments which need to be computerized. First department handles the orders from customers. These orders are written on an order book. Their customers place orders on telephones, which can cause misunderstanding and sometimes results in a huge problem for both customer and manufacturer. Second department deals with the stock. They maintain stock records on stock books. The company keeps the demand of its customers on priority. They manufacture the fresh yarn on order. They seldom keep manufactured yarn in stock, and to achieve this task they must keep the report of raw material stock updated, so that they would be aware of the available colour and quantity to issue it on time for manufacturing. Third department maintains the cash transactions made on daily basis. Fourth department maintains the records of delivering products to the customers against their orders. All the above departments maintain their records in handwritten form. They all face problem while matching previous records to prepare any report or while searching the records of previous dates. Another major issue is of security which we must cover on. The software will be web based, so we need to apply authentication on admin and users. Admin will create user and restrict him/her to use specific portion of the software.

content: This chapter is the non-ambivalent description for the users, developers and stakeholders of our software. All the requirements, functional and non-functional both, will be notified and well explained in this chapter. The requirements will help the developers to organise, design and develop the software utterly according to the customer requirements. Literature Review The accounting exists, since the business exists in this world. In the prehistoric periods, people traded by using barter system [5]. In barter system, people directly trade by exchanging goods without using any medium like money etc. But some rules, regulations and agreements must exist while they trade. With the passage of time, trends started changing and ways of trading also affected with that change. People now started using mediums like money while exchanging goods and services. The concept of money instigates two new concepts in trading, credit and debit, which laid the basis of accounting. Accounting, at its beginning, was performed on books which is known as “Bookkeeping”. When the transactions increased in numbers, it was very difficult for accountants to generate trial balance, balance sheets, income statements etc. When this issue was propagating, the technology of computer science was also broadening at its full sprint. Accounting soft wares provide the best solution for this issue. Computers can handle these enormous number of transactions and generate reports in very less time. All models of businesses require unique software which works according to their demands and requirements. Same software can never work for all models of businesses. Manufacturing process was never too arduous. But now the manufacturing procedures have expanded to a large scale that they also need computers to record the transaction of goods from one department to the other and generate reports. Here are some soft wares which are used for accounting purposes: ? Gnu Cash [1] o Gnu Cash is accounting software, which can merely perform simple book keeping task and it is ranked first in accounting soft wares. This software is for small businesses and cannot perform tasks which our client requires for his factory. ? TurboCash [2] o This software is for small size businesses and is just for accounting purposes. It is a general software not for a specific industry. So, our client cannot use this software because it lacks resemblance with his business procedures. ? Apache OpenOffice [3] o This software is for people who trade. A businessman with manufacturing plant cannot take any benefit from this software, because this software only records incoming and outgoing of goods with some small number of accounts. ? Admin Soft Accounts [4] o Admin Soft Accounts is simple application used to keep records of money transactions. It doesn’t support the feature to add and manipulate data of goods and manufacturing processes. ? QuickBooks [6] o Quick Books is an elegant application which provides best solutions for accounting problems. It is an online software. It also maintains purchase invoices but still the company cannot use it because it does not have feature of handling the records of manufacturing processes of the company. Besides this, the company wants a specific software according to its own requirements which the QuickBooks doesn’t provide. Stakeholders List Stake holders of this software are those who have to interact with it for any reason, directly or indirectly. This software will provide an easy and efficient provision for the problems to the company that it can view statistics in the form of pie charts and other graphical formats. Reports will be generated and evinced to manager in a perfect methodical way so that the he will sense the professional texture in them. Stakeholders list is as follows: ? Owner This software means a lot to the owner (manager) of the factory, because they need a very specific and complete software, solely for their own factory. They have searched for the built-in soft wares online but they didn’t get any single software, which fulfils their requirements. That’s why they contacted us to develop a software solely for their company. ? Accountants Accountants are currently using a software which is not providing them facility to operate it on any PC. So, for the sake of privacy of secret accounts, the manager does not hand over the PC to any person accept data entry clerk. This leads to disaster for maintaining stock, because stock is maintained by other accountants to whom handing over PC is very risky. Our software will help them to cater the draw backs of their previous software and provide security of data by giving the authority of accessing any feature of software to the accountants or any other user which will also be created by the admin. This software will be web based and they can access it everywhere through internet under their assigned privileges. ? Customers This software will help to handle the orders, order deliveries and customer accounts. heading: Abstract
content: The success towards the hope of having autonomous machines under the parasol of artificial intelligence depends on bio-inspired cognitive agents, machine consciousness and humanoid projects. Such advancements in the field motivate us to take initial steps toward the initialization of research activity with the objective to develop a basic platform to take further the research in mach ine social cognitive learning domain using machine consciousness paradigm. We intent to propose a  socio-cognitive communication module that can engage customers in social interaction; thereby leading towards friendlier and more comfortable customer relatio nship. It will recognize the customer’s preferences, provide relevant information of products with different natures  and will recommend the kind of product the customer can use, through social interaction.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: Recent trends in the development of social cognitive robots have led us to the realization of treating machines as co -workers (Moore n.d.) .These robots are the agents that are intelligent, socially interactive, communicate thro ugh dialog -based system, and learn models to recognize other agents, display particular identity and character; and may learn or create social abilities. Agents programmed with aforementioned features are referred as cognitive agents, for detail see (S. P. Franklin, A “Consciousness” -Based Architecture 2005),(Franklin and Ferkin 2006), (Gamez, The Development and Analysis of Conscious Machines 2008)  and (Qazi 2012) . The corresponding relationship between cognitive science and robotics defines the characteristics of cognitive robotics research, which focuses on giving robots with advanced cognitive abilities in order to observe, reason, and behave separately in a similar intelligent manner to humans. Social intelligence in robots has turned out to be progressively obvious that social and intelligent skills are vital prerequisites in many cognitive modelled AI -based application regions and context s where robots need to connect and work together with other agents (robots or humans) (Dautenhahn 2007 Feb 13) Such kinds of socio -cognitive robots and agents were discussed in BICA challenge (Samsonovich, On a roadmap for the BICA Challenge 2012), and the aforementioned idea of these kinds of co-worker robots can be rationalized on the premises of BICA challenge. The primary objective of BICA (DARPA Ends Brain Reverse Engineering Project, ref: (Samsonovich, Johannsdottir and Chella, Proceedings of the F. Amsterdam: IOS Press BV 2010)) and our development is to build a general-purpose artificially intelligent agent, that has (to some extent) computational skills equivalent to human brain, which will extend human society, and not replace us. According to BICA challenge and roadmap (Samsonovich, On a roadmap for the BICA Challenge 2012) , to achieve these goals the agent (robot) should fulfil following conditions. • Accept as partner • Believable behaviour • Co-presence • Domain expert • Episodic memory • Social and communicational capabilities

heading: 10 of 82  08 January 2018
content: Recently a number of attempts have been reported in literature within the domain of Chatbots, which addresses similar kind of features. Some prominent Chatbots in this regard are Google NOW, Siri, and Amazon Alexa. The development of these Chatbots has changed the trend of customer relationship, Customer satisfaction and interaction has improved. Moreover, similar kind of w ork has also been done using cognitive modelling techniques, for example IDA [ref], AgentX (Strain, Kugele and Franklin, CIHLI, 2014 IEEE Symposium 9-12 Dec. 2014) , Librarian Robot (Mikawa, et al. 13 November 2009) IBM Watson (watson n.d.) , Virtual Nurse (Timothy Bickmore n.d.) , last but not least, Virtual Agents as Daily Assistants for Elderly or Cognitively impaired People (Ramin Yaghoubzadeh n.d.). Although these systems have played a significant role in the advancement of the underlying technologies but with reference to BICA challenge, some other features are essentially required. The problem with these existing syst ems is that they have very limited infrastructure to retain and formulate their experiences. The reason is that they have limited cognition in their design therefore they don’t have the ability to comprehend, and to consider past experiences in the similar  situations. They cannot generate new kinds of responses. Indeed, these kinds of features are very complex to accomplish; this project is an attempt to address the problem of socio-cognitive interaction. The question arises that what kind of computational constructs are required, in which these features can be encapsulated and the project goals and objectives are achieved. Keeping in view the complexity of the problem, we will introduce a domain specific socio -cognitive infrastructure to model and implement a dialogue based agent. The purpose of the artefact will be to serve as a co-worker customer service bot in hypothetical retail store. We intend to achieve this goal by developing out bot using cognitive modelling techniques which involve cognitive architectures and utilization of relevant frameworks. According to literature, cognitive architectures are one of the underlined computational infrastructures that allow encapsulating these kinds of features. Cognitive architecture is a computational representation of cognitive processes which allows the execution of these processes. Cognitive architecture allows us the development of cognitive agent, where this agent chooses actions to be performed on the premises of complex processing which simulates different mental functionalities at a certain level to general insight, cognition and response under rule of cognitive cycle(s) (Franklin and Ferkin 2006) . Cognitive architectures are used in cognitive artificial systems which is able to  perform cognitive activities like learning, reasoning, knowledge organizations, perceiving etc. (Anderson 1983/2013). Cognitive Architectures are, at the same time, theoretical modelling for how many different cognitive proces ses interact with each other in order to sense, reason and act, and also software frameworks, which can be reused through different applications. Although significant work has been done in the development of these cognitive architectures/agents, but still there is a significant room for improvement. One of the underlined challenges in development of cognitive systems is the representation of knowledge and information. For this we have theoretical and computational cognitive sciences (Lieto 2014) . As cognitive tasks involve different brain activities and neural impulses, it is essential to describe the conceptual information representation. Moreover,

content: for the concept representations the proxy type theory of concepts (Prinz 2004)  can be combined with heterogeneity approach (Machery 2010)(Lieto 2014). Systematic flow of the cognitive process is summarized in literature review. On the basis of cognit ive architectures, many applications are under the development phase. There are some robots that have cognitive architectures. For instance, Amelia, iCub, LIDA Max Agent (i.e. a medical agent) (Strain, Kugele and Franklin 2014) , J ohi(Qazi 2012) are some examples of business agents. Over the past few years ,Artificial Intelligent Machine and Robotics group at Department of Computer Science, CIIT Lahore has been trying to develop cognitive agents and architectural framework. Till to date at undergraduate level following agents have been developed, Blue (Laila Pervez 2016) , Turk (Phase 1) (Mikaal Anwar 2016) , and currently ADIBO, an attention based socio-cognitive bot is under development, which intends to assist human in the admission process. The artefacts developed from these studies will be used as component, as and when required in the design of our socio- cognitive bot. The contribution of this  project as compared to previous attempts at CIIT is the development of a social cognitive agent which could serve as a co-worker in a retail shop, where its responsibility is to possess a comprehensive cognitive architecture with autobiographical and gene ral knowledge representation through episodic and semantic memories and processed using the construction of cognitive map in working memory/workspace. As mentioned previously that designing of such agent requires handling complex structures along with comp utation complexities. Therefore, the intelligent and cognitive capabilities will be used to develop a robot that will have a dialog based system. The robot should be able to serve and interact with people using this dialog based system, hence making business effective and encouraging. For this purpose we used AIML (discussed in literature review section 2.1.4) to give some general knowledge based and retail specific questions and their responses. OpenMary TTS (discussed in literature review section 2.1.1) is used to convert these responses from text to speech furthermore to maintain customers profiling we used SQL database (discussed in literature review section 2.1.5 ) that will record all the conversation between customer and our system. To suggest products to customers we used NEO4J (discussed in literature review section 2.1.3) in which we create/maintain the social network of customers for effectively handling their product related queries For speech to text we use Google Cloud Speech API that enables to convert Speech to Text by applying different neural network models, this API recognizes up-to 110 languages. heading: 2.1  Literature Review
content: This study aims to propose a social cognitive robot for a retail store to serve as an assistant. The design of this agent required the utilization of concepts, tools and techniques from various domains. Therefore, literature review is interdisciplinary. The main objective of the research in robotics and cognitive artificial intelligence is to make computat ionally equivalent human -like mind. Broadly speaking, cognitive computing is defined as the simulation of human manners of thinking in an automated model. The corresponding relationship between cognitive science and robotics defines the characteristics of cognitive robotics research, which focuses on giving robots with advanced cognitive abilities in order to observe, reason, and behave separately in a similar intelligent manner to humans A cognitive agent that chooses actions to be performed based on complex processing which simulates various mental functionalities at a certain level in order to general insight, cognition and reactions under regulation of cognitive cycle(s) (Franklin and Ferkin 2006). Cognitive architectures (Anderson 1983/2013) are used in the construction of cognitive artificial systems which can perform cognitive activities like knowledge organization, attention, learning, reasoning etc. The problem in cognitively inspired artificial systems is concept representation for this we have theoretical and computational cognitive sciences (Lieto 2014). As cognitive tasks involve different brain activities and neural impulses so it is important to describe the conceptual information representation. Moreover, for the concept representations the proxy type theory of concepts (Prinz 2004) can be combine with heterogeneity approach (Machery 2010) (Lieto 2014).

heading: 14 of 82  08 January 2018
content: In this regard BICA (Samsonovich, Johannsdottir and Chella 2010)  is very important to create humanoid cognitive agents that serve the humans , reduce their burden, solve complex problems and will be acknowledged as a member of a society. It will help to lessen the need to do massive programming and help to create general purpose cognitive agents that will interact with humans, acquire, learn knowledge and help them to fulfil the dream of a future where everyone can enjoy prosperity and economic and social justice and can refrain from severe loses (Samsonovich, On a roadmap for the BICA Challenge 2012). For this we have many cognitive architectures. They have many same an d distinguish factors. These factors include support for common components, learning algorithms, decision making etc. For detail, you can see (Comparative Table of Cognitive Architectures (started on October 27, 2009; last update: June 18, 2012) n.d.) Cognitive agents get better over time and helps to introduce better interactions with people, based on their preferences. Web interactions, loyalty program patterns, online medical records, and location data prove to be helpful in this regard. It also tries to find the details that have been impossible to detect, such as the tone of a person, their emotions, environmental conditions, and nature of an individual’s relationship. The main reason is to find out how to engage a customer , through structured and unstructured data. All these elements deliver greater value, making it natural and emotionally appropriate to improve and enhance cognitive abilities by extending the decision making capability and reducing conflicts among individuals and groups in an organization. The cognitive agents are modelled with certain level of independence which allows the agent to take sensory input from its environment and try to assign meanings to it; this is called perception phase. After assigning meaning it tries to understand the perception. The analysis and understanding of perception allows the agent to decide what actions are there to be performed. This process includes complex cyclic processes based on current goals. By design these agents can b e self-regulated by the agent itself (Riccardo and Vincenzo 2004), (Qazi 2012). Consider the perception of different colours in different agents. The nervous system of an agent constructs the sense of colour on the basis of cone classes (Franklin and Ferkin 2006) . The modules involved in cognition process are memory, attention etc. After perception, Attention is the next phase which acts as a filter of the perceived information. External or perceptual attention selects and modulates information incoming from various senses and internal attention modulates internally generated information, such as the contents of working memory or a set of possible behaviours in a given context. The episodic memory provides information based on past experiences and events, to the rest of cognition. The Attention codeless interacts with the episodic memory to recall episodes of similar perception and also encodes new patterns. Memory is an es sential part of any systems -level cognitive model, regardless of whether the model is being used for studying the human mind or for solving engineering problems. Similarly, perception is evolved after every cycle of similar episode, known as perceptual learning. On contrast, procedural memory is the memory of actions and behaviors of a

heading: 15 of 82  08 January 2018
content: system; it stores the procedures of learning behavior. Cognitive agents always either learn new behaviors or improve and evolve old ones. This procedural learning is defined as non- declarative memory, which refers to “how to” kind of information. It is a set of internal processes that changes the capability of the way to respond to sensory inputs on the basis of past experience and practices. Perception, procedural learning, and episodic learning are based on association of things. An object is associated with its features and categorization in perceptual learning. Agents recall events from episodic memory through associations with cues. Procedural learning can be improved by a ssociating the performance with the desired results. Therefore, attention also reinforces the procedural learning at every cycle. This reinforcement may be a result of positive or negative effect of the behaviour and performance (Franklin and Ferkin 2006). According to the Greg Trafton, cognitive architecture seems like typical controllers for robotic systems. Most of the robots having this architecture performs the limited sensing and reasoning capabilities and are highly task specific. According to the John Laird, robotic architecture which based on real time planning, path planning, hierarchical planning, the fusion of many types of knowledge having both symbolic and non -symbolic knowledge. As there are many challenges arise w hen considering the real-world perception and motor systems with cognitive architecture. First is interface between perception and cognition. Another is maintaining the performance when extend the knowledge to large scale. The critical part of this concept  is to develop the intelligent robots that have the ability to learn from humans. " Robotics technologies has progressed expressively over the past few decades and are already being used in the logistics and manufacturing. Now a day all countries across the globe has facing challenges of aging population, social robots can play a essential role in addressing the issues by becoming a personal assistance for elders and for kids at home and in future it can likewise serve as a platform for health care services" explained Prof Thalmann, an expert in virtual individuals and a faculty from NTU's School of Computer Engineering. According to Russell and Norvig artificial intelligence can be comprehended in four different ways which concludes that the systems can thi nk like humans, act like humans, think rationally and can act rationally. System can also be capable of learning from the results of problem space search (Sleeman et al.,1982), by observing behaviours of other agents or through behavioural cloning (Sammut, 1996) instead of direct instructions. To understand the mind, cognitive architectures are believed to be vital (Anderson 1983, Newell 1990, Sun 2002). Herbert Simon (1957) once assert that “AI can have two purposes. One is to use computer’s AI for understanding how humans think and second is to use computer’s power to augment human thinking.”

heading: 3 Conversational Agent
content: AIML stands for artificial intelligence markup language and is used to cr eate conversational systems using natural language based knowledge representation based as discussed earlier in above section. Aiml possess the following pros. • Simple to program • easy to understand • highly maintainable Knowledge base in AIML is further consists of following tags.

heading: Basic:
content: • <aiml>: this tag defines the beginning of AIML file. • <category>: it is a basic knowledge unit contains for input and output response along with optional context • <pattern>: here we define the pattern/question which user may ask. • <template>: it contains the response against the user queries.

heading: Recursion:
content: • <srai>:  It is used for 4 main reasons (i) Symbolic Reduction: It reduces the complex grammatical patterns into simpler ones. (ii)  Divide and Conquer: Sentences are reduced into sub-sentences and formed a common reply. (iii) Synonyms resolution: Helps the bot to reply in identical manner for similar words. (iv) Keywords Detection: Helps to reply a standard reply whenever that specific keyword occurred.

heading: CONTEXT:
content: • <that>: it is used to respond according to context.

heading: Abstract
content: We will provide the user with the facility that the user can do the customize search and will be able to extract comments, posts, and likes of different people according to the his/her desire. We will give the suggestions to the user with the help of which user can promote Facebook page and will know about the trends. Our user can compare his profile or page with his/her competitors and can track his/her post. we will analyze the data of the user so we can facilitate the user with different features like automated reply and scheduled posts.

heading: 1.1 Introduction
content: We will build such a platform which will provide the user with the following features:  The user will know about the trends means what kinds of posts are getting more likes and comments. The user will know that people are interested in what kind of things and can promote his/her page very easily as shown in table 1.  We will give the suggestion to the user because of his/her activity which will help the user to promote his/her page. e.g. what is the best time to get a response from people or what kind of posts will attract more audience as shown in table 1.  Page level comparison will be performed (b etween the client’s and competitors’ pages) in terms of posts, comments and/or likes as shown in table 1.  We will track the posts of the user; how much audience are getting engaged and how much people are interested in user’s posts. We will also track the posts and pages of the competitors and will inform the user about the progress of competitors as shown in table 1.  The user will be able to search specific posts or comments and will be able to deduct some result on the basis of his/her search as shown in table 1.  We will analyze the data of our user and will let him/her know that how many people are interested in buying your product and will provide the facility of auto reply on comments and scheduled posts of ours.  The comments on the user’s page/s will b e compared with competitor’s’ page/s for comparison of products based on comments/reviews from the fans.

heading: 1.2 Objectives
content: Our objective is to boost the social marketing of the product/services of our user so that maximum no of Facebook user can get benefit from the product/services of our user. We will not only help our user to improve social marketing skills of his product but also take care of the information (User engagements, Posts, Comments) related to competitors. Our objective is to develop such a pla tform in which the user can manage his/her multiple Facebook pages in such a way that maximum no of people on Facebook takes interests by liking, commenting or sharing the post not only that we will also provide such features to our user which will help hi m to get ahead of his competitor.

heading: 1.3 Problem statement
content: Facebook is becoming the main source in which people are grooming their business by getting attention of millions of Facebook users. Facebook is becoming the hub of social marketing in which almost every king of business is advertise. If someone eat some food from hotel or do some shopping from mall, peoples like to share their reviews or tag their friends with which they have spent their time. Now hundreds of thousands of pages are created for marketing purpose of a product or a business. Facebook don’t provide the facility to manage all your pages at a same time but you have to open each page to see the statistics of your posts. Suppose if some user have 20 different pages for some information or ne ws purposes now this user has to open twenty pages to see the performance of all of his product and not only that but also if this user wants to see how his competitor is doing or how is the response of Facebook on his posts or his competitors. People don’ t have time to do all these steps and they don’t have so much memory to remember all the results from their multiple pages so we will develop such a tool which will address all the issues mentioned above.

heading: 1.4 Assumptions & constraints
content: • We assume that our user has an active Facebook page. • We also assume that there will be some competitor Facebook page which will be related to our user. • We assume that there will Facebook Page ID or Post ID which will be used in Facebook’s Graph API to collect the data. • There are some posts on Facebook page which gets thousands of comments or likes now the problem is Facebook’s Graph API supports only limited amount of data (Comments, Likes, Reactions). Now it depends on our user that how much amount of data he/she wants to anal yse. Facebook’s API Graph also supports larger amount of data but it’s not free So, we will charge extra money for larger amount of data.

heading: 1.5 Project scope (what and what not to consider)
content: Nowadays social media has a great impact on human life and people spend a lot of their time on social media. Moreover, there are some things which social media does not provide. Our aim is to make such a product which will make sure that the time of the user is used effectively and efficiently. we will provide the inform ation to the user which is related to him i.e. comments and likes to the post of the user. The user can manage the things which are related to the user. we can't provide the information (date of birth, personal phone no) of the friends of the user. the use r can see the statistics of his multiple social pages but cannot control his social pages with the help of our product.

heading: Abstract:
content: This is an inter-campus parking and vehicle security automation system through “Radio Frequency Identification. This project is intended to ensure the security of entering and leaving vehicles from the parking area. This application will assist us to ensure if a student is leaving with the same vehicle, he initially entered with. Students and their vehicles will be given unique RFID’s upon registration. So, upon leaving, they will only be allowed to leave if their RFID’s matches. This project is also aligned with tracking of students and whether that student is present in the university or not.

heading: 1.1  Introduction:
content: This system is a parking, vehicle security, student tracking -assist application which will work on the basis of RFID. RFID stands for radio frequency identification. It allows wireless data transmission. There are two vital components in the implementation which includes RFID tags and RFID readers. These RFID tags work on the basis of unique id’s which are given to them. No two RFID tags have the same id. When the RFID tag and the reader are matched with the help of electromagnetic fields, they are identified and can be tracked. RFID will enhance the working of parking automation system. This whole system works in a way that the code is embedded in the RFID tags and as stated earlier, unique id is given to each RFID tag. Then the same id is assigned to the vehicle. So, only if the RFID tag and the vehicle’s id match with each other upon leaving the premises of the university, they will be allowed to depart. The data from this transaction will be updated in the database. The records and ids of the students will be saved there. Similarly, in case of student trackin g i t can avoid proxy attendance and refine and further automate the system of student’s attendance. If a student’s RFID is matched with the scanner, the teacher will know he or she is in the university. Our app has two modules i.e.; web portal (front end) for the interaction of user, and a desktop app. Our final product will include a desktop application for users of the campus, a Web portal and Rfid Reader/Writer software for Administration or Securit y Personnel. The administration will use the software to read/write the Rfid cards and view the data mapping on the web portal. The portal will also be used to add new students, cars etc. The web portal will represent the parking status, time table, alerts etc. Moreover, our system shall be aligned with LCAST android app which uses a beacon- based technology to for student navigation and attendance. The application features are discussed below:

heading: Application Features:
content: • The user shall be allowed to login with the rfid number assigned by the security management. • The application shall notify the user whether the user is allowed in the university or not after checking/matching the rfid number in the database. • The user shall not be allowed to enter the university premises if its rfid number doesn’t exist in the system database or for some reason revoked.

heading: 9 of 56  14 May 2018
content: • Upon leaving the university premises, the application shall match the rfid number assigned to the user and the vehicle which was given to user and his/her vehicle on entry. • Only the permitted administrator should be allowed to access the web portal using his/her username and password. • Administrator of the web portal shall be able to enter, delete or alter records of university personnel along with their vehicles • Moreover, the application shall also provide a way to the teacher to know whether the student is in the university or not. Steps of development: • Firstly, we will purchase the rfid chip and rfid  tag to do basic testing with the apparatus. • Since this application will be a hybrid of desktop and web so we will start making the module for the detection of rfid chips and tags. • Then, we shall design the database in which the records of rfid numbers are kept and to whom it is assigned to. • In the parallel timeframe, we shall start building the web portal which will allow us communicate and control with the back end of the application. • After the structure of the application is built, we shall start implem enting the advanced functionalities required which are Vehicle  Parking and Security Verification. • After the structure of the application is built and the required functionalities have been added, then we shall move towards testing and debugging phase. • After successful testing of the application, the last step would be deployment and installation of our application in the university.

heading: 1.2  Objectives:
content: • Our goal is to provide effective and efficient tools for the management of parking within University premises. • To provide automated solutions for better management and security system for the vehicles within the University. • To provide verification solutions for student attendance issues. • Keeping the track of no. of students entering the campuses and leavi ng the campus. • To prevent stealing of any vehicles from campus. • To check if a student or a teacher is present in the university or not based on the rfid status of entering and leaving the university.

heading: 1.3  Problem Statement:
content: As we see at present that there is a manual system for the overseeing of the vehicles at the campus. A number of security guards have to be always there to keep a watch of the vehicles and also a manual token system is used.  Moreover, the manual system of security is prone to fail, cause s tealing of vehicles and compromise security of the campus. Our application will automate all of these factors and there will be no need for any security guards or tokens. So keeping this in mind, our motive is to build a system that should be intelligent, efficient, easy to use and swift enough to maintain and manage the security of the vehicles and the students entering the campus.

heading: 1.4.1    Assumptions:
content: • This system shall be used by almost everyone in the university including students, teachers and staff members since all of them will be accessing parking space. • The users of the system will receive notifications about status of their parked vehicles. • This app will assist every incoming/outgoing vehicle hence improving security and integrity of the university. • Administrator shall use this application to check the whereabouts of the students.

heading: 1.4.2. Constraints:
content: • Parking Space Management module of the application w as difficult to implement because it is an advanced, less used and researched system. • Parking space management require s extra apparatus to assign every vehicle a different slot so it is not feasibly possible with the current financial resources. • This type of project is mostly used at a large scale, so implementation might be incomplete according to the resources offered. • Automation of security will require top-notch apparatus otherwise it is prone to fail. • As automation and internet of things is a new technology, so high user satisfaction shall be difficult to achieve.

heading: 1.5  Project Scope:
content: The core basis of our project is on the technology of RFID. The scope of RFIDs is really vast and is set to expand with time. RFIDs are expected to take over the barcode technology soon because the amount of information that can be stored on barcod es is really less as compared to the RFIDs. RFIDs can store as far as 1000 bytes of data and are specified to each item whereas barcodes are not. Other than that RFID is entering the fields of pharmaceuticals, healthcare, retail, banking and defence etc. RFID was not considered to be feasible because of the high cost factor involved for its implementation but now the companies are moving towards building of low cost RFIDs. Slowly the picture of RFID is the coming to view of all companies wanting to implemen t it. Looking at the different benefits it will provide for the businesses, the cost reduction, this will lead them to huge profit margins which is a necessity in today’s competitive and fast market world.

heading: 2.1  Literature Review:
content: Our motive is to build a system that should be intelligent, efficient, easy to use and swift enough to maintain and manage the security of the vehicles and the students entering the campus. A thorough study on the related applications of vehicle management and security has been done for the sake of gaining enough and necessary information about the development and designing of our app. These apps are on google play store. These apps are specified below: [1] DPM-Dynamic Parking Management permits to control and manage the parking of vehicles in real-time. This app is a lot like ours and provided meaningful inputs for future work. [2] Smart Parking Beta is a wireless parking system based on Zigbee technology for smart parking. Although this is a real time parking app but is inefficient, lacklustre in performance. This app is difficult for use for novice users and even perpetual intermediates. [3] Get My Parking is an IOT platform parking app. The problem with this app is that it is only limited to Delhi. Moreover, complains were found about the layout, promotional techniques etc. and as a result gaining minimum user satisfaction. [4] Park Indigo is a globally used parking app which can be used across 4000 locations in 7 countries. It is a different from us because of its scale but studying it provided useful information about our app. Although, this app lacks user friendliness and had bad reviews due to basic performance bugs. Our app will be based on the technology of Rfid, which at initial stages, will be designed for inter university parking and security thus focusing on maximum user friendliness and smooth performance.

heading: 4.3 INTEGRATION TESTING:
content: Integration testing is done to ensure the interactivity of the modules with each other. Following integrations are to be performed and tested to require approval. Testing will be performed by team members other than the assigned person. • Interface Integration: Each unit is to be integrated with its designated interface. Interface should be pixel perfect and all elements of interface have been properly integrated with the unit. • Unit Integration: Each unit must be check as whole after integration. All the tests performed in unit testing must be repeated. • Error Handling: Anomalies must be tested to ensure each error is being handled properly and a message is generated for the user. • Error Message: Error Messages are presented in a mannerly fashion and interface layout does not break or loses aesthetics because of error message. • Error Logging: Each incurred error is integrated with the error logging module and is being stored in the database for later review or probable fix. After developing the modules of the system, their integration is one of the main tasks. While integrating, there arise many errors which are not know at the time of integration but are available only when the system is tested thoroughly by integration testing. So , we performed integration testing when all the perspectives (units) were developed and tested.

heading: 4.4 ACCEPTANCE TESTING:
content: Acceptance test is a final test performed by the end users. This test will prove that system is in working condition, adaptable and sho uld or should not be implement widely. A questionnaire would be conducted through the system itself after 20 days of initial use. heading: Abstract
content: Many people want different services for their business purposes but the application they want cost a lot and not all of them can afford it or the application they have does not serve efficiently. We will provide a software as service (SAAS) web a pp that is based multi - tenant architecture. Multi tenancy refers to software architecture in which the software serves multiple tenants. Tenant means users who use the services. We propose a web application based on multi-tenant architecture which will provide several services. It’s on the user that for how long he will use our services so that when he don’t need the services the user can stop using it will also save the cost of the user .

heading: 1.1 INTRODUCTION
content: We will develop a software as service (SAAS) web application based on multi -tenant architecture. In multi-tenancy the application is installed on a single server and the user can use that services. The users will have the same view. The customization of the services will be changed as per their needs. The data of the user is also stored in the database of the web application. Each user can only see his data and not the data of other users. The web application will provide services that will help the user to do their daily tasks and to earn profit from their business. Our main focus is on the multi tenancy of the website as the multi -tenant architecture has many benefits. The followings are the benefits of multi-tenancy. • Cost: due to multi -tenancy a lot of cost can be saved as  there is only one instance of software running on one server and having a single database saves a lot of money. The software also uses less resources as only one instance of software is used by all the customers. • Data aggregation\data mining: data is stor ed in a single database instead of multiple databases with different schemas saves a lot cost as query cost and datamining and finding patterns is much simpler. • Easy updates: in multi tenancy as the software is stored in a single server any upgradation in a software will be easy as all the customers can access the upgraded services. • Easy customization: in multi tenancy each customer can customize the service as per the customer's need without effecting the other's customer customization. The web application will provide services that user can use for free. web application will have a gui interface which will be user friendly so that the user can easily customize the services as per the needs of the users. The services will be generic and flexible so that th e customization can be made of any type. The user don’t need any technical knowledge for the customization, only he will customize according to his needs. The database schema will be generated according to the customizations of the users. The web application will provide facilities just like others software so that it’s for every user and not restricted for the technical users only.

heading: Python (Django or FastAPI):
content: FastAPI is a software backend written in lightweight and high performance, which is asynchronous and also generates API documentation automatically. Django is a powerful framework with an administrative interface, security implementation as well as authentication. Although it is the first option we use, it is possible to resort to other programming languages and frameworks in case of the project need.

heading: AI, NLP & CV Libraries
content: NLP: spaCy, natural language text segmentation and classification. Transformers (Hugging Face): Introduced to fine models (headings, captions and references). Deep Learning Structures: PyTorch and TensorFlow in classification model training. Image Ethics Detection (Image Vision): Image ethics (or image decency) can be detected and filtered with help of OpenCV, CNNs using TensorFlow/Keras, or CLIP (the vision-language model used by OpenAI). Speech Recognition (Voice-to-command): Vosk (offline), Google Speech API and open AI Whisper to voice to voice command conversion. Command Interpretation: spaCy or Hugging Facebook Transformers to text of speech to formatting actions.

heading: Abstract:
content: The offered project, which will be called Report Formatter, presents an AI- and machine learning-based program that will be used to automate the process of report formatting based on the templates specified by the user or institutions. The system will include: Admin Panel: It allows administrators to post and control format regulations like font styles, margins, table formats and heading structures. A custom template can be done by each university. AI-Powered Content Classification: Detecting attributes (heading, subheading, tables, images, captions, references) and formats them accordingly Ethical Image Detection: The system incorporates an AI model, which is capable of differentiating between ethical and unethical images. In case of an inappropriate or unethical image posted, the system will make sure that it is not included in the report, thus making sure that one does not go against academic and professional standards. Voice-Enabled Formatting Requirements: The users and administrators will be able to set formatting requirements by speech recognition using a microphone. This natural language processing capability renders the system more usable and easy to use especially when the user finds it more comfortable or needs to use voice interactivity as opposed to using handwriting. Student Application: This will enable students to post raw data (Word, PDF or plain text) and get a well formatted report according to the template of their campus. Specialized: Grammar checking, plagiarism checking, table of contents auto-generated, audio and table numbering, section recognition, version control, collaboration, and multilingual. Security Measures: It has data security and privacy measures which have been incorporated in order to secure sensitive academic work with the use of encryption and local storage. There is also live preview, with students being able to see changes in formatting on the fly, just like on platforms like LaTeX like Overleaf. Combining all these features, the solution is expected to offer a complete platform that is not confined to mere formatting and can improve the academic writing overall.

heading: Proposed Solution
content: Final Year Project (FYP) reports are frequently a very tedious and professional writing where students have to adhere to specific guidelines of the institutions. Formatting by hand takes up precious time, and distracts the actual research, and often the issue of inconsistencies ensues. The current project suggests creating an AI-driven Report Formatter that will automate the process of formatting the reports, making sure they are formatted in accordance with the institution-specific template and protecting the academic integrity. The system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning to identify the elements of a document (headings, paragraphs, tables, figures and references) and uses these elements to apply formatting rules. An exclusive administration panel will enable the institutions to post and maintain their own templates to guarantee a high level of flexibility in the various universities. The innovations are AI-based with ethical vs. unethical image detection, which filters indecent or otherwise unacademic images, and a voice-activated formatting interface, which lets the user set formatting instructions by simply speaking to the computer and improving accessibility. Other functions provided are plagiarism and grammar check, absent section suggestions, and live preview. Word, PDF and LaTeX export options will be used to provide a high number of compatibility. The proposed solution alleviates the administrative workload of formatting, enhances academic integrity and increases accessibility in students by incorporating smart content classification and ethical protection as well as multi-modal interaction with users. In the end, the Report Formatter hopes to be a smart academic assistant that fills the gap between the creation of content and the presentation of the professional work, thus contributing to the high level of productivity and the quality of academic work in general.

heading: Motivation and Significance of the Project
content: The existing procedure of report creating is ineffective, prone to errors, and does not help the students to concentrate on their research quality. The vast majority of students do not have the technical knowledge to work with the more advanced formatting features of programs like Microsoft word or Latex. Consequently, they have to use manual adjustments that are quite repetitive and in most cases result in wastage of time, stress, and inconsistency of formatting. Moreover, the lack of an automated program that can address various institutional needs has presented a barrier to students who study in various academic settings. Another problem that keeps on reoccurring in a collaborative environment is the ability to merge various sections without losing formatting. Insufficiency of mechanisms used to guarantee ethical contents is another cause of concern. Learners will either add unprofessional images in their reports without knowing how, or they can do it deliberately, and this can result in both academic and professional punishment. Furthermore, the existing systems restrict the formatting to the manual mode of input and they do not consider innovations like speech-based instructions, which might make the process more user-friendly with people with varying needs. Therefore, an urgent demand is seen in the creation of the system that will be not only automated in formatting but also will make use of artificial intelligence to sort, arrange, and ethically control the material and promote various forms of interaction with the users.

heading: Problem Statement
content: The rationale of this project is the fact that students continuously struggle to create properly formatted scholarly reports, which meet the institutional requirements, do not lose their quality or ethical value. Hand formatting wastes precious time and could be used to conduct research and innovation and poses a hindrance to productivity and consistency in academic writing. Current software such as Microsoft word and LaTeX are highly technical and do not offer flexible and adaptive solutions to varying formatting capabilities which uses AI. Moreover, the existing systems do not consider accessibility, ethical protection like speech-based formatting and image detector of unacademic images. This project is important because it has the potential to combine Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to facilitate the formation of reports, make them more accessible, ethical, and academically honest. This project helps to improve the technology of education and enhance quality education in accordance with SDG Goal 4 (Quality Education) as it eliminates the divide between manual formatting and intelligent automation.

heading: Abstract:
content: Report writing is part and parcel of academic and professional work. In tertiary education, learners have to deliver reports, theses, and project documentation which has to be in perfect format according to the requirements that are given by their institutions of higher learning. Such formatting guidelines usually include font types, font size, headings hierarchy, margin requirements, table format, reference format and other organizational aspects. Although these standards are required to ensure uniformity and readability, the manual formatting is normally time consuming, difficult and cannot be done without errors. Students are often wasted in matching headings, numbering lists and the reference styles more than in the actual content of their work. The latter is even more difficult when the various institutions have varying formatting standards. As an example, one university might recommend using the APA style form of reference, and another one to use IEEE or Chicago style. Equally, the specifications on the appearance of the table, the position of the caption and the structure of the sections can be quite diverse. This is because the absence of a universal tool that can adapt to various formatting needs makes compliance quite challenging to the students, and in fact, unintentional non-compliance to institutional standards can be experienced. These difficulties are intensified in other group projects, where several contributors join their parts together in one document and in most instances the parts do not match. Moreover, in the contemporary digital reports, figures and images may occasionally be included. Nevertheless, uncontrolled insertion of unethical or unacceptable images may affect academic integrity. In this way, not only do the quality of the content have to be properly formatted, but also the possibility to avoid the incorporation of unethical content into the academic records. As automation, artificial intelligence, and natural language processing become increasingly more dependable, there is a high demand on a smart solution that can automatize formatting, comply with ethical standards, and offer an opportunity to allow the user to define the formatting needs in flexible ways.
