heading: Related Work
content: Document formatting automation is a new discipline that touches on Natural Language Processing (NLP), document layout analysis, and rule-based systems. Various commercial and academic solutions have tried to solve sections of this issue, but there exists little in the way of a widespread, template-driven, AI-assisted, academic report solution. Commercial word processors Powerful in their styling capabilities and templates, Microsoft Word and Google Docs need to be used manually. They are not smart enough to guess the framework of the unstructured academic text. Users have to apply formatting, which creates errors and inconsistency in longer reports. Overleaf and LaTeX In academia, Overleaf, a LaTeX cloud-based editor, is being widely used due to its strong typesetting features and active collaboration functionality [1]. Nevertheless, it involves the user learning how to use LaTeX, an important barrier to entry to many non-technical students. Although it is the best at generating well-structured reports, it does not offer AI flexibility in response to customer requirements. AI-driven text models GPT-based models, including ChatGPT, are able to produce and occasionally organize text but not be used to adhere to more complicated text formatting conventions, including margins, page breaks, or caption position. They also do not have a specific pipeline of analyzing document layout and adherence to formatting. Document Layout Analysis (DLA) DLA research is very relevant. Some projects like LayoutLM (Microsoft) [2] and DocBank [3] are based on deep learning to recognize textual and visual characteristics to understand the structure of the documents (titles, authors, paragraphs, etc.). These models are the basis of technology of our classification module but are research oriented as opposed to being implemented as end user academic tools. Content quality tools Grammatically and Turnitin are adjacent solutions. Grammarly prioritizes grammar, clarity, and tone recommendations [4] whereas Turnitin is the default plagiarism detection engine in the industry [5]. Nevertheless, both of them do not offer automatic formatting and adherence to institutional templates. Template engines Document creation systems such as Jinja or Apache POI are programmatic methods of document creation, where template documents are filled in with information. They are helpful with automation but not adaptive because they are unable to process unstructured academic material intelligently and correlate it with templates without human-defined rules. Automated format research A prototype of an NLP-based formatting system, which can be used to process documents and execute some rules automatically, was described by Islam & Rahman (2022) [6]. Although this is proof of its feasibility, the model is not extensible and fails to cover such sophisticated options as detecting ethics in images or speech-driven interaction. Ethical/unethical image detection Professional and academic integrity can be undermined by the uncontrolled incorporation of unethical or inappropriate pictures. Research in computer vision can be a good solution to this field. Image classification Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), ResNet, multimodal networks like CLIP [7] are examples of models that have been shown to have high precision in image classification tasks. Such systems are able to recognize inappropriate or irrelevant content and they are thus appropriate to be included in academic formatting software to maintain ethical standards. Speeches and voice interaction Speech recognition can be used to improve accessibility in formatting systems. The studies of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and intent classification, including Graves et al. (2006) [8], allow mapping natural speech to actions. New developments such as Google Speech-to-Text API and Whisper prove the accuracy of the transcription, and voice-powered formatting is possible and useful to the academic software with inclusivity. The project is expected to make an integration of all these disparate domains - DLA, NLP, template engines, computer vision, ASR and writing assistance tools into one user friendly application that is specifically tailored to an academic scenario, which currently there is a gap in the existing ecosystem of writing tools.

heading: Methodology
content: The report formatter is  developed with a structured pipeline to ensure that it is properly formatted and that the content of the reports is classified based on data AI to identify the essential elements of the report. The interconnecting modules constituting the architecture (Figure 1) are each with a unique purpose. 1. Admin Panel Module: This module defines formatting templates, such as margins, table styles, placement of captions, hierarchy of headings, font size, and style. The templates are stored in the Template Database. 2. User Module(Students): This module handles registration, logins and submission of reports by students. It provides file upload services of text, PDF, and word documents. 3. File Upload and Parsing Module: It receives uploaded files and removes their raw content (text, tables and figures) and converts the information into a structured format to enable AI to process it. 4. AI Content Classification Module: The NLP model marks the sections (Heading 1, Heading 2, paragraphs, tables, photos, captions, references, etc.) of the text. It provides the Formatting Engine with directed content. 5. Formatting Engine Module: It uses standards of the university template to a content that is categorised and controls captions, margins, spacing, numbering and styles of headers. A draft report is generated. 6. Other AI Services: Plagiarism and grammar checker ensure the accuracy and originality. AI recommendations provides recommendations to missing portions of the paper, including the Conclusion. 7. Table of Contents/ Numbering Module: This will automatically generate a list of figures, list of tables and table of contents. It perfectly places captions (under the pictures, on the top of the tables). 8. Collaboration & Version Control Module: It allows a number of different students to post and merge sections. The rollback version history is also maintained. 9. Live Preview Module: It provides a preview of the organized report live. Students can see changes immediately, as it works with Overleaf. 10. Image Ethics Detection Module: This recognizes ethical or unethical images uploaded and beforehand inserts them, based on pre-trained computer vision models (e.g. ResNet, CLIP or custom CNNs). The moracious pictures pass, the immoral row. 11. Voice to Command Module: Speech recognition engine converts the spoken instructions into actions (e.g. bold heading, insert caption). It uses commands to format actions relying on ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) and NLP intent-classification.

heading: Abstract
content: The offered project, which will be called Report Formatter, presents an AI- and machine learning-based program that will be used to automate the process of report formatting based on the templates specified by the user or institutions. The system will include: Admin Panel: It allows administrators to post and control format regulations like font styles, margins, table formats and heading structures. A custom template can be done by each university. AI-Powered Content Classification: Detecting attributes (heading, subheading, tables, images, captions, references) and formats them accordingly Ethical Image Detection: The system incorporates an AI model, which is capable of differentiating between ethical and unethical images. In case of an inappropriate or unethical image posted, the system will make sure that it is not included in the report, thus making sure that one does not go against academic and professional standards. Voice-Enabled Formatting Requirements: The users and administrators will be able to set formatting requirements by speech recognition using a microphone. This natural language processing capability renders the system more usable and easy to use especially when the user finds it more comfortable or needs to use voice interactivity as opposed to using handwriting. Student Application: This will enable students to post raw data (Word, PDF or plain text) and get a well formatted report according to the template of their campus. Specialized: Grammar checking, plagiarism checking, table of contents auto-generated, audio and table numbering, section recognition, version control, collaboration, and multilingual. Security Measures: It has data security and privacy measures which have been incorporated in order to secure sensitive academic work with the use of encryption and local storage. There is also live preview, with students being able to see changes in formatting on the fly, just like on platforms like LaTeX like Overleaf. Combining all these features, the solution is expected to offer a complete platform that is not confined to mere formatting and can improve the academic writing overall.

heading: Abstract
content: Final Year Project (FYP) reports are frequently a very tedious and professional writing where students have to adhere to specific guidelines of the institutions. Formatting by hand takes up precious time, and distracts the actual research, and often the issue of inconsistencies ensues. The current project suggests creating an AI-driven Report Formatter that will automate the process of formatting the reports, making sure they are formatted in accordance with the institution-specific template and protecting the academic integrity. The system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning to identify the elements of a document (headings, paragraphs, tables, figures and references) and uses these elements to apply formatting rules. An exclusive administration panel will enable the institutions to post and maintain their own templates to guarantee a high level of flexibility in the various universities. The innovations are AI-based with ethical vs. unethical image detection, which filters indecent or otherwise unacademic images, and a voice-activated formatting interface, which lets the user set formatting instructions by simply speaking to the computer and improving accessibility. Other functions provided are plagiarism and grammar check, absent section suggestions, and live preview. Word, PDF and LaTeX export options will be used to provide a high number of compatibility. The proposed solution alleviates the administrative workload of formatting, enhances academic integrity and increases accessibility in students by incorporating smart content classification and ethical protection as well as multi-modal interaction with users. In the end, the Report Formatter hopes to be a smart academic assistant that fills the gap between the creation of content and the presentation of the professional work, thus contributing to the high level of productivity and the quality of academic work in general.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Application of Report Formatter system should bring about some gains: Time Savings: The automation of the repetitive format process will save the students much time so that they can be able to spend the time on creating the content and conducting research. Consistency and Accuracy: With automated formatting, the problem of human error will be removed, and the strict adherence to the requirements of the institution will be ensured. Ethical Protections: The unethical image detection feature can be used to keep academic reports professional, ethical and devoid of unprofessional content. Increased Accessibility - Speech-based input should allow users to create formatting rules via the voice, which will make the system more inclusive and easier to use. Improved Quality: Grammar correction and plagiarism detector features will help in bettering the quality and originality of reports. Collaboration Support: Teamwork in academic projects will be simplified with such features as version control and collaboration between people. Flexibility and Adaptability: The system will support the different formatting rules and languages and therefore can be applicable across the various institutions and regions. Flexibility: Compatibility with other academic submissions platforms, such as Word, PDF, and LaTeX document export capabilities will make it flexible. Data Security: Vigorous privacy protocols will ensure that sensitive student reports are safe and they are not abused. The purpose of this Report Formatter is, finally, to become a smart assistant to the students, researchers and institutions by creating a linkage between the content development, ethical adherence and professionalism. Using artificial intelligence, the system will not only enhance effectiveness of report writing, but also establish new levels of academic productivity, inclusiveness, and quality.

heading: Expected Outcomes
content: The existing procedure of report creating is ineffective, prone to errors, and does not help the students to concentrate on their research quality. The vast majority of students do not have the technical knowledge to work with the more advanced formatting features of programs like Microsoft word or LaTeX. Consequently, they have to use manual adjustments that are quite repetitive and in most cases result in wastage of time, stress, and inconsistency of formatting. Moreover, the lack of an automated program that can address various institutional needs has presented a barrier to students who study in various academic settings. Another problem that keeps on reoccurring in a collaborative environment is the ability to merge various sections without losing formatting. Insufficiency of mechanisms used to guarantee ethical contents is another cause of concern. Learners will either add unprofessional images in their reports without knowing how, or they can do it deliberately, and this can result in both academic and professional punishment. Furthermore, the existing systems restrict the formatting to the manual mode of input and they do not consider innovations like speech-based instructions, which might make the process more user-friendly with people with varying needs. Therefore, an urgent demand is seen in the creation of the system that will be not only automated in formatting but also will make use of artificial intelligence to sort, arrange, and ethically control the material and promote various forms of interaction with the users.

heading: Introduction
content: Report writing is part and parcel of academic and professional work. In tertiary education, learners have to deliver reports, theses, and project documentation which has to be in perfect format according to the requirements that are given by their institutions of higher learning. Such formatting guidelines usually include font types, font size, headings hierarchy, margin requirements, table format, reference format and other organizational aspects. Although these standards are required to ensure uniformity and readability, the manual formatting is normally time consuming, difficult and cannot be done without errors. Students are often wasted in matching headings, numbering lists and the reference styles more than in the actual content of their work. The latter is even more difficult when the various institutions have varying formatting standards. As an example, one university might recommend using the APA style form of reference, and another one to use IEEE or Chicago style. Equally, the specifications on the appearance of the table, the position of the caption and the structure of the sections can be quite diverse. This is because the absence of a universal tool that can adapt to various formatting needs makes compliance quite challenging to the students, and in fact, unintentional non-compliance to institutional standards can be experienced. These difficulties are intensified in other group projects, where several contributors join their parts together in one document and in most instances the parts do not match. Moreover, in the contemporary digital reports, figures and images may occasionally be included. Nevertheless, uncontrolled insertion of unethical or unacceptable images may affect academic integrity. In this way, not only do the quality of the content have to be properly formatted, but also the possibility to avoid the incorporation of unethical content into the academic records. As automation, artificial intelligence, and natural language processing become increasingly more dependable, there is a high demand on a smart solution that can automatize formatting, comply with ethical standards, and offer an opportunity to allow the user to define the formatting needs in flexible ways.

heading: Abstract
content: The women still have to find their way in a world full of safety issues especially in societies where the patriarchal system is deeply entrenched. The continued fear of harassment, stalking, and assault is essentially a mobility tax in place which limits the ability of women to access education, professional prospects and social activities. In the present state of affairs, the safety information tends to be disjointed; women tend to use word-of-mouth or the anecdotal evidence as the formal reporting system is more likely to be slowed down by the social stigma and cultural friction barriers. The aim of this project is to eliminate these barriers through the creation of AI-powered Women Safety Intelligence System. The platform goes beyond binary safe or unsafe with the addition of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Rather, it comes up with Dynamic Area Risk Scores, an advanced measure based on real-time incidents reporting, time trends, and environmental aspects. Risk-based route suggestions or safe crowd density estimation are only a few examples of how this system will potentially change the raw data into actionable intelligence with prioritization on user privacy via secure and anonymous reporting and ethical implementation of AI.

heading: Background
content: The problem of women safety in cities is a complex systemic issue, which lies in the combination of urban plan, social dynamics and urban policy management. In the fast-developing societies, where the city lifestyle is highly urbanized, the gendered experience of the city is full of obstacles that are still not seen. As the physical infrastructure, roads, bridges, and transit system keep on growing, the digital and social infrastructure that allows navigation of these spaces safely has remained behind. Traditionally, the safety interventions used were reactive and carceral, with a focus on surveillance and reporting of incidents. Nevertheless, increasing the Internet of Things (IoT), omnipresent mobile sensing, and spatial analytics of high resolution is an opportunity that can change the world. We are leaving behind the un-animated maps and going to an animated, conscious urbanism. With the help of the citizen as a sensor, we will be able to gain the lived experience of the women, transforming qualitative experiences of unease into the quantitative data. This change enables us to shun the olden trends of the concept of hotspots mapping to the intricate, moving narrative of urban fluidity and danger. Motivation and Significance of the Project The motivation to this work comes as a result of the increasing disconnect between the increased criminal activities in the city and the inability of the centralized and old-fashioned platforms of safety. The tools that are used are often ineffective due to their capacity to operate in a vacuum and do not account for the cultural peculiarities of reporting or do not have the technical complexity to forecast risks prior to them occurring. The majority of navigation and safety applications consider the concept of risk as a fixed variable, and do not consider that urban settings are dynamic such that the safety profile of a street can change radically in a few minutes. The underlying reason behind this study is that there is a gap in the data that has to be filled with the help of high-fidelity, real-time analytics that transcend the limitations of official crime statistics, which tend to be delayed or under-reported because of social friction. The project is important in that it adds a key feature of the so-called Explainable AI (XAI) to personal safety; it does not simply declare a street to be dangerous, but explains why such an accident is possible, be it bad lighting, absence of eyes on the streets (low density of people), or historical trends that occur on a particular hour. This study fits into the establishment of genuinely inclusive cities by achieving Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality) and Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). It makes technology a proactive protection on the vulnerable, virtually reducing the mobility price that women pay and give urban planners the precise information necessary to implement structural modifications, like better lighting or more efficient patrol routes. Objectives and Scope of the Project The key goal of the present project will be the design of a versatile ecosystem of Safety Intelligence going beyond the constraints of conventional emergency apps. This includes designing a high-resolution risk-assessment engine that combines heterogeneous data, i.e. the text that users put in and GPS positions to time-varying trends and crowd density. The scope involves designing, development, and implementation of a cross-platform mobile application and a web central dashboard. The scope of the technology is, in particular, delimited by unstructured report analysis with the help of Natural Language Processing (NLP), predictive risk modeling with the help of Machine Learning (ML), route optimization and heatmap with the help of Geospatial Intelligence (GIS), and SOS and companion tracking with the help of Real-time Sync. Although the system considers a global architecture, the first implementation and data-model training will be in the Lahore cityscape, which will provide a local demonstration of the proof needs to be expanded to other urban settings in the future.

heading: Proposed Solution
content: The suggested solution is an advanced, multi-layer ecosystem that will help to bridge the disconnect between the uncivilized geospatial data and human-friendly security. The fundamental concept of the system is that it is based on a Microservices Architecture, which is driven by Python (FastAPI/Django) such that the NLP report processing, ML risk-scoring, and GIS routing engines can be scaled independently. The backend will use PostgreSQL database with PostGIS extensions that will enable complicated point-in-polygon queries that will be used to identify whether a user is entering a high-risk area or not in real-time. The frontend experience to be provided through a cross-platform mobile app (Flutter/React Native) will consist of an easy-to-use interface in the form of an in-car interface called the Safety HUD (Heads-Up Display) that depicts instant visual feedback regarding the risk profile of the surrounding environment. The system will include a Temporal-Spatial Risk Engine in order to make the intelligence explainable. This engine does not simply look at an area and then looks at the risk variance of the time of day, it also brings in live feeds of the crowd density and the street light data, where possible. One of the most important technical innovations is the Risk-Averse Routing Algorithm, which alters normal A* or Dijkstra pathfinding methods to incorporate so-called safety weights. This will make sure that the proposed route gives preference to well lit, populated, and historically low risk streets even though it may increase the overall duration of travel by some margin.

heading: Expected Outcomes
content: The technical deliverable will be a high-availability Women Safety Intelligence Platform with the first-ever implementation of the so-called Dynamic Area Risk Score of the city of Lahore. We will create an impeachable set of micro-incidents - harassment and environmental hazards - that do not show up on the radar of law enforcement. The project will result in a 40-60% improvement in the amount of safety data collected by reducing the cost of reporting an incident by using an anonymous interface with an NLP interface, which will create a map of urban risk much more resolute than ever before. The anticipated outcome of this project is a quantifiable decrease in "transit anxiety" in the eyes of the user. By administering pre-deployment and post-deployment survey, we seek to show that women would feel much more comfortable going through unexplored urban corridors with real time, explainable risk intelligence. Besides that, the project will lead to creation of a Centralized Web Dashboard to be used by stakeholders and urban planners, which will provide heatmaps and trend analytics that can help pinpoint where infrastructure failures (such as broken streetlights or absence of patrols) are leading to localized spikes in crime.

heading: Problem Statement
content: The present situation in the urban safety environment presents itself as a reactive-only model, in which digital technologies are applied to serve a digital siren instead of a digital shield. Although SOS buttons and location-sharing functionality are widespread, they have a critical weakness of being useless until the crisis happens. Moreover, current navigation and mapping applications are configured to minimize the path length or transit time without any consideration of the cost of safety of a route. This algorithmic apathy usually paves women along darkened lanes, rusticated industrial belts, or places where history has recorded a lot of incidents just because they are mathematically shorter. In addition to navigation, a serious lack of trust in current reporting systems is of a critical nature. The traditional systems tend to demand non-anonymous communication with authorities with a high degree of friction which dis-incentivizes reporting because of social stigma, fear of repercussions, or the bystander effect. This creates a gap in data of immense magnitude wherein the low-level harassment the antecedent to more illicit acts is not captured. Urban safety is a collection of anecdotes and not a verifiable science or actionable science that cannot be taken up without a system that can conduct real-time sentiment analysis of unstructured data within communities and exclude malicious, biased reports.

heading: Main Goal
content: The main objective of this project is to design and implement an AI-enhanced Women Safety Intelligence System, which uses time and space-varying information to anticipate, examine and represent safety risks real-time.

heading: Specific Objectives
content: To construct an algorithm based on a supervised machine learning to create a Dynamic Area Risk Scoring model. In order to deploy a secure, end-to-end encrypted feedback reporting module to provide anonymous feedback. To develop an NLP engine that will analyze and categorize incident reports. To create a risk-based route optimization navigation algorithm. To come up with time-aware risk prediction and facility-level safety indexing modules. In order to apply Isolation Forest algorithms to detect bias and false-reporting.

heading: Expected Impact
content: The systemic effect of such project is that it enables the measurement of the so-called mobility tax that women were forced to pay and give the means to regain the lost agency. The process of making the gendered experience of the city turn into a transparent data model changes the burden of safety on the individual to the community and the infrastructure. This forms a technological disincentive; the more people join the safety map the fewer blind spots there exist in the city and the more difficult it is to execute an offense under the pretense of invisibility. This is a direct catalyst of realizing the UN Sustainable Development Goal 5 of creating a society where physical mobility will cease to be a gender privilege. The economic aspect of the effect can be seen in greater economic involvement of women in work and education. Once the fear of the commute is addressed by the use of dependable risk-based routing and the companion track, the obstacles to late-shift work and evening education are reduced. The insights that will be produced by this system over time will be used as a blueprint to create Evidence-Based Urbanism that will enable city officials to distribute resources where they are most required. Finally, the project aims to shift the pivot of policing the city to designing a safe city, the urban power dynamic which is designed to the advantage of the vulnerable.

heading: Related Work
content: bSafe: Basic Functionality: This platform is focused on instant reaction by providing an SOS alert, live locations sharing with pre-established trusted individuals, and automatic audio/video recording when danger was detected. Weaknesses We Address: bSafe is reactively designed; bSafe logs the crime but does not assist the user to avoid the place where the crime is prone to the occurrence. This is achieved through our Dynamic Area Risk Scoring which allows its users to avoid high-risk areas and bypass them completely before having to use SOS at all.

heading: Noonlight
content: Key Features: It has a simplistic emergency interface, a press-and-hold SOS button, which, when released, sends automatic notification to professional emergency services, showing the exact location of the user. Weaknesses We Satisfy: Noonlight does not have any spatial risk intelligence. It will not inform a user that the street one is walking on is historically unsafe. To add the context in which a simple button cannot give, our project combines the Heatmaps of Harassment Zones and Time-Aware Risk Prediction. Safetipin / My SafetyPin Core Functionality: Safetipin is one of the limited platforms that have tried to do spatial analysis; it gives area safety scores, which are calculated using such parameters as GPS data, the density of people, street lighting, or the area density of transport. Weaknesses We Solve: Safetipin does not provide personalization based on AI and the advanced understanding of incidents via NLP, although it provides area audits. We go even further by recommending Adaptive Risk Personalization, that is, tailoring suggestions to the specifics of individual user behavior, and the use of NLP to classify the specifics of the localized harassment reports.

heading: Shake2Safety
content: Basic Operation: The application is aimed at core functionality where it enables one to activate a covert SOS signal and send emergency messages just by shaking their phone. Weaknesses We Address: The application is a one-purpose utility with no data-driven and community-driven validations. Our Community Validation System and Bias and False-Report Detection help us fill this gap, and is why we can provide the user with safety data that is not only verified, but is also not a random compilation of unverified warnings. UrSafe / Safe UP Core Functionality: These platforms provide a universal way of looking at safety such as planned safety checks, live streaming facilities as well as geo-located assistance services in various countries. Weaknesses We Address: though they have a wide range these do not yet incorporate a complete AI ecosystem of risk prediction. Our project fulfills this void by providing a dynamically changing risk level prediction solution using XGBoost and LSTM to complete a safety check instead of a fixed one. WanderSafe Beacon Core Functionality: This application is designed to address the needs of a solo traveler and offers location-based safety tips and sends notifications when a user gets to an unfamiliar territory or even a dangerous zone. Weaknesses We Satisfy: The advice can be generic and is not as precise as Risk-Based Route Recommendation. The algorithm we provide is a modified version of the Dijkstra algorithm, which offers the safest route of navigation, which the advisory-only version of WanderSafe does not have. MySIS & Zich Core Functionality: These applications offer a bundle of live location tracking and SOS alerts, that concentrate on audio and video evidence collection in an incident. Weaknesses that we satisfy: As with most others, these are not intelligence tools but evidence-gathering tools. Our system incorporates Safe Crowd Density Estimation, where real-time movement clustering is used to direct women to populated and well-lit locations before an incident happens and shift focus away on evidence to prevent. Proposed Methodology and Architecture

heading: Architecture
content: Safr - The Women Safety Intelligence System aims to be essentially a 5-level architecture that is highly complex to ensure reliability and fast response. It ensures that important safety measures such as the SOS button remain functional even during periods of hogging by the AI, by distributing the tasks between more than one layer.

heading: User Interface (Mobile Interface)
content: Flutter Mobile App: The primary access point is a cross-platform mobile app, which allows reporting an incident, getting directions and emergency alerts in real time. User Interactions: Users will be able to initiate several important workflows via the interface. Incident Reporting: Users should be able to provide text or media notifications of harassment or safety related incidents to the pipeline. SOS Activation: A fire-hose trigger, which contacts the emergency services immediately. Navigation & alerts: Receive a live notification and safe route suggestions depending on your current GPS location. API Gateway & Security Layer Efficient Request Routing: This layer will handle high-concurrent traffic between the back-end and the mobile app with the help of FastAPI and ensure that the data flows in the right direction. User Authentication & Privacy: Built in user authentication will shut the door, and a Zero-Knowledge encryption system will keep identities secret and not remove anonymous reporting. Intelligence Engine (AI Services Layer) NLP Analysis (BERT-based): Parses incident report unstructured text, identifies the type, identifies the severity, and excludes nasty language. Risk Scoring Engine (XGBoost): Risk scores based on the dynamic area will be generated and delivered in real-time, which is the potential risks using previous data and current data. Anomaly Detection (Isolation forest): Maintains the integrity of the community by identifying biased or coordinated fake reports. Business logic Layer (Backend Services) Route Navigation & Personalisation: Provides a risk-conscious Dijkstra routing algorithm, feeds into Google Maps API to provide graphics, and a personalisation engine to give you advice on how to make it safer to your personal preference. SOS Service & SMS Gateway: An SOS ring will call the SMS gateway to buzz emergency contacts as well as push alerts to other users or authorities in the vicinity. Facility Safety Indexing: This is a calculation of safety scores of locations such as bus stops or hospitals using community data.

heading: Storage Layer & Infrastructure Layer
content: PostgreSQL & PostGIS: Structured data, where risk predictions and risk reports have been parsed, are stored, and post-geo indexed queries (heat maps and routing) are run with PostGIS. Redis Cache: Provides a speed increase to personal information and popular look-up navigation. AWS Cloud Infrastructure: The entire stack will be on AWS, with scalable compute on AI and encrypted S3 buckets to protect data security.

heading: METHODOLOGY:
content: Dynamic Area Risk Scoring: This is the core of the system. It allocates risk scores (0-100) to geographic areas using supervised ML such as the Random Forest or XGBoost. The scores vary with incident frequency, severity, time of day, lighting, crowds, etc. and it is the reason why a zone received its rating. Type of incident: Data breach (anonymous and secure): To reduce the impact of culture, it provides a zero-knowledge configuration: end-to-end encryption, no data storage of personal IDs, and no metadata in the media to make you help the community without fear. NLP-Based Report Analysis: Converts textual content into structured information through a fined tuned BERT or DistilBERT. Fills out NER to extract places, tags incident type and severity and marks offensive or irrelevant content. Risk-Based Route Recommendation :The system does not attempt to find the quickest path using GPS, instead it manipulates the Dijkstra algorithm to give precedence to the safe parts. It allocates weights depending on the existing risk ratings and hence the route will exclude exposure to risk even at the expense of a few minutes. Time-Aware Risk Prediction :Risk chimes with time. It does this with the help of LSTM networks, which examine the patterns and forecast the change in the danger levels during night, or the change in seasons and provide proactive warnings before you have even moved. Facility Safety Index:Checks past the streets to assess such places as bus stops, hospitals, and shops. The weighted scoring model with Bayesian small-sample adjustments provides the user with a Safety Index that is up-to-date with community feedback. Heatmaps of Zones of Harassment:Visualization is key. Using Kernel Density Estimation, this app will overlay lively heatmaps on Mapbox or Google Maps and you can only see the so-called hotspots and swam through the complex grids of cities. SOS Button :One tap or trigger transmits your live GPS to emergency contacts and authorities through SMS and push in an emergency and has an auto-record audio feature to provide evidence. Safety Notifications and Alerts: Makes use of geofencing to monitor whether you have entered a high-risk area. When risk score goes high, a context-sensitive notification that can prompt you to watch out or switch route is activated. Validation System of the Community: Has a high Truth Score as it allows the users to either confirm or report. The credibility and historical background of the contributor is linked to the weight of a report, which creates a reputation-based system. Bias & False-Report Detection: One, to ensure that the system is not mangled by spam data or that somebody is attempting to hack it, we will implement an Isolation Forest anomaly detection algorithm. This will assist in trapping organized mass-reporting outbursts or malevolent efforts of undermining the status of particular spots or locations. Safe Crowds Density Estimation: Safety in numbers is usually better. We will collect real-time movement data in the form of anonymous information and allow the system to determine the level of congestion of a location. Unoccupied spots at night are marked as more dangerous, whereas busy areas are illustrated as less dangerous. Safety Companion Mode: This mode is more or less a virtual companion. You are able to share your live location with a known person. We set a clock and when you fail to arrive at your destination within the anticipated time or venture too much outside the intended path, there is an automatic alarm. Risk Personalization Adaptive Risk: Risk tolerance of everyone varies. With the reinforcement learning, the system will learn to avoid the routes that you tend to take off consistently and adjust future recommendations and risk weightings accordingly to your level of comfort.

heading: Success Criterion
content: The technical chops and user vibes will be used as measures of the success of this project. Technical Accuracy: The models should reach a 85-percent accuracy in incident classification and risk prediction. The risk-based routing algorithm must always select the paths whose aggregate risk score is significantly lower than the conventional route proposals of the fastest one. System Performance: The latency of delivering messages by SOS and real-time tracking should not exceed 2 seconds. High availability (99.9%) of the system should also be shown to ensure safety tools are available in times of an emergency. User Engagement & Integrity: It is also important that the Bias Detection module will have the capability to filter out at least 90 per cent of malicious or coordinated false reports to be successful. Qualitative Impact: Lastly, we will measure the success based on user feedback on the aspect of Perceived Safety, where we want to see an obvious rise in confidence in female users in their use of the app in walking into the public.

heading: Frontend
content: Mobile Application Development: The interface will be built on Flutter, the user-facing toolkit of Google to build natively compiled applications. This framework also allows us to maintain one codebase and run high-performance applications on Android as well as iOS meaning the UI remains the same and we save a lot of development time.

heading: Backend
content: Frameworks API Framework & AI Integration: Python and FastAPI will be used as the backend. The ability of FastAPI to scale to many connections simultaneously, the ease with which it can process asynchronous requests and a perfect integration with Python AI libraries is ideal in high-AI applications and a microservice. Real-Time WebSocket: To operate the most important real-time functions such as the SOS Emergency Button and the Safety Companion Mode (live location tracking), we are implementing WebSocks with FastAPI-SocketIO. This provides us with a stable, rock-bottom, two-way connection between the server and the mobile application.

heading: Database
content: Primary Relational Database: A PostgreSQL will be used as the primary DB to store the user profile, encrypted incident report, and system configuration data. It’s solid and keeps data safe. Geospatial Intelligence: We will then add on the PostGIS extension to PostgreSQL which is essential in rapid spatial queries. It allows us to perform geofencing, heat-map clustering and determine distances on our risk-based route recommendation engine as the map moves. Ephemeral Data Storage: Since the rapidly changing real-time data such as live GPS is required when there is an emergency, we shall use Firebase Realtime Database or Redis. And they are extremely fast, too, they will not overload our main relational DB.

heading: Additional Tools
content: AI and Machine Learning Models: The predictive engines, or Dynamic Area Risk Scoring and Community Validation System, will be developed using PyTorch, which is a deep learning framework, and scikit-learn, which is a traditional ML package. Language Processing, NLP: Hugging face Transformers library will assist us in analyzing unstructured incident reports that we can use the best models such as BERT or DistilBert to analyze their sentiment, severity, and possible incident classification. Mapping and GIS Visualization: To map and heat-map and route within the application we will use Mapbox GL SDK or the Google Maps Platform API. Infrastructure and Deployment: To ensure that the system can be scaled and reliable, all will be containerized using Docker to deploy it in a consistent way. We will be hosted on AWS, EC2 as the compute and S3 buckets with secure and encrypted storage of media files related to reports.

heading: Abstract:
content: The report formatter is developed with a structured pipeline to ensure that it is properly formatted and that the content of the reports is classified based on data AI to identify the essential elements of the report. The interconnecting modules constituting the architecture (Figure 1) are each with a unique purpose. 1. Admin Panel Module: This module defines formatting templates, such as margins, table styles, placement of captions, hierarchy of headings, font size, and style. The templates are stored in the Template Database. 2. User Module (Students): This module handles registration, logins and submission of reports by students. It provides file upload services of text, PDF, and word documents. 3. File Upload and Parsing Module: It receives uploaded files and removes their raw content (text, tables and figures) and converts the information into a structured format to enable AI to process it. 4. AI Content Classification Module: The NLP model marks the sections (Heading 1, Heading 2, paragraphs, tables, photos, captions, references, etc.) of the text. It provides the Formatting Engine with directed content. 5. Formatting Engine Module: It uses standards of the university template to a content that is categorized and controls captions, margins, spacing, numbering and styles of headers. A draft report is generated. 6. Other AI Services: Plagiarism and grammar checker ensure the accuracy and originality. AI recommendations provides recommendations to missing portions of the paper, including the Conclusion. 7. Table of Contents/ Numbering Module: This will automatically generate a list of figures, list of tables and table of contents. It perfectly places captions (under the pictures, on the top of the tables). 8. Collaboration & Version Control Module: It allows a number of different students to post and merge sections. The rollback version history is also maintained. 9. Live Preview Module: It provides a preview of the organized report live. Students can see changes immediately, as it works with Overleaf. 10. Image Ethics Detection Module: This recognizes ethical or unethical images uploaded and beforehand inserts them, based on pre-trained computer vision models (e.g. ResNet, CLIP or custom CNNs). The moraceous pictures pass, the immoral row. 11. Voice to Command Module: Speech recognition engine converts the spoken instructions into actions (e.g. bold heading, insert caption). It uses commands to format actions relying on ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) and NLP intent-classification.

heading: Methodology:
content: Final Year Project (FYP) reports are frequently a very tedious and professional writing where students have to adhere to specific guidelines of the institutions. Formatting by hand takes up precious time, and distracts the actual research, and often the issue of inconsistencies ensues. The current project suggests creating an AI-driven Report Formatter that will automate the process of formatting the reports, making sure they are formatted in accordance with the institution-specific template and protecting the academic integrity. The system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning to identify the elements of a document (headings, paragraphs, tables, figures and references) and uses these elements to apply formatting rules. An exclusive administration panel will enable the institutions to post and maintain their own templates to guarantee a high level of flexibility in the various universities. The innovations are AI-based with ethical vs. unethical image detection, which filters indecent or otherwise unacademic images, and a voice-activated formatting interface, which lets the user set formatting instructions by simply speaking to the computer and improving accessibility. Other functions provided are plagiarism and grammar check, absent section suggestions, and live preview. Word, PDF and LaTeX export options will be used to provide a high number of compatibility. The proposed solution alleviates the administrative workload of formatting, enhances academic integrity and increases accessibility in students by incorporating smart content classification and ethical protection as well as multi-modal interaction with users. In the end, the Report Formatter hopes to be a smart academic assistant that fills the gap between the creation of content and the presentation of the professional work, thus contributing to the high level of productivity and the quality of academic work in general.
